content:
Item 1 of 2 US President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, D.C., US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Evan Vucci

**[1/2]**US President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, D.C., US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Evan Vucci [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-donald-trump-and-chinas-president-xi-jinping-meet-at-the-white-house-in-washington-dc/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlJQTkFCWUc4QQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

WASHINGTON, Sept 30 (Reuters) - US President [Donald ​Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/donald-trump/) said on Wednesday he discussed the release of ‌political prisoners with Chinese President [Xi Jinping](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/) when the [two leaders met](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-plans-grand-spectacle-potentially-tense-xi-talks-2026-09-23/) last week.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Ftrump-says-he-discussed-release-political-prisoners-with-xi-2026-09-30%2F)

## DETAILS AND QUOTES:

*   "I did with President Xi. I did," Trump told reporters when asked if ​he brought up the cases of political prisoners like Myanmar ​scholar and US citizen Min Zin, who was arrested in ⁠June, and Hong Kong's most vocal China critic and media ​tycoon Jimmy Lai.

*   "We talked, and I think we had some very, very ​important discussions. Hopefully, fruitful discussions," Trump added.

*   The White House had said ahead of Xi's visit that Trump was expected to bring up cases of people wrongfully ​detained in China with the Chinese leader.

*   The White House did not ​say if Trump aimed to directly raise broader rights issues related to Tibet, the ‌Uyghur ⁠Muslim minority group, and China's new "ethnic unity" law.

*   Trump has made winning freedom for Americans held overseas a priority, including in China, even as he has largely avoided talking about China's treatment of Tibetans, Uyghurs ​and voices of ​dissent.

*   Lai's case [had sparked ⁠global concerns](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/trump-says-china-may-release-detained-pastor-tycoon-lai-is-tough-one-2026-05-15/) over the national security clampdown in Hong Kong, in part reflecting his prominence as founder ​of the now-shuttered Apple Daily newspaper. He was ​sentenced to ⁠20 years in jail in February on two counts of conspiracy to collude with foreign forces and one count of publishing seditious materials.

*   Washington designated ⁠Myanmar ​scholar and US citizen Min Zin as [wrongfully ​detained](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-designates-american-held-by-china-wrongfully-detained-2026-08-20/) in August after his arrest by Chinese authorities in June.

Updates with question asked to Trump, his response, background of Xi visit in bullets

Reporting by Gram Slattery ​and Kanishka Singh in Washington; Editing by Caitlin Webber and Michelle Nichols

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Gram Slattery is a White House correspondent in Washington, focusing on national security, intelligence and foreign affairs. His work covers how key U.S. foreign policy decisions are debated, shaped and executed. He was previously a national political correspondent, covering the 2024 presidential campaign. From 2015 to 2022, he held postings in Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo and Santiago, Chile, and he has reported extensively throughout Latin America.

Kanishka Singh is a breaking news reporter for Reuters in Washington DC, who primarily covers US politics and national affairs in his current role. His past breaking news coverage has spanned across a range of topics like the Black Lives Matter movement; the US elections; the 2021 Capitol riots and their follow up probes; the Brexit deal; US-China trade tensions; the NATO withdrawal from Afghanistan; the COVID-19 pandemic; and a 2019 Supreme Court verdict on a religious dispute site in his native India.

title: US Supreme Court sides with Tennessee to allow its first execution of a woman in 200 years
summary: * Summary * Christa Pike, 50, convicted of murder at age 18 * Failed clemency bid cited childhood sexual abuse, neglect * Pike diagnosed with bipolar, post-traumatic stress disorder Sept 30 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court ruled on Wednesda
content:
*   Summary

*   Christa Pike, 50, convicted of murder at age 18
*   Failed clemency bid cited childhood sexual abuse, neglect
*   Pike diagnosed with bipolar, post-traumatic stress disorder

Sept 30 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that [Tennessee](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/tennessee/) could proceed with its first execution of a woman in 200 years, clearing the way for ​Christa Pike to be put to death by lethal injection for murdering a schoolmate as an 18-year-old three decades ago.

The Tennessee Department of Correction said ‌in a statement to Reuters afterwards that it planned "to move forward with the execution today."

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fus%2Ftennessee-due-execute-woman-first-time-two-centuries-2026-09-30%2F)

Pike, 50, whose clemency petition highlighting childhood trauma and sexual abuse was denied by Governor Bill Lee on Monday, would also be the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager.

In an order decided by its 6-3 conservative majority, the Supreme ​Court lifted a stay of execution that was granted by a three-judge panel of the 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals one hour before Pike had ​been scheduled to be put to death.

The appellate panel voted 2-1 to order a "short stay" to allow time to weigh Pike's claim ⁠that evidence of her childhood sexual abuse was not adequately considered during her sentencing.

But the Tennessee attorney general's office immediately asked the US Supreme Court to vacate the stay. And ​the high court's decision siding with Tennessee marked the final word on whether the execution was permitted to go forward before her death warrant expires at midnight CDT (0500 GMT).

The state ​did not give a precise new time frame for the execution, which was set to take place at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital.

If the state were to run out of time to conduct the execution, it would need to obtain a new warrant from the Tennessee Supreme Court, according to Robin Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center.

## GRISLY KILLING

Pike was 18 ​in January 1995 when she, a 17-year-old boyfriend and a third companion lured 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a wooded area ​where they tortured and killed her.

The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim's chest and taking a chunk of her skull as ‌a souvenir ⁠of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time.

Trial testimony indicated that Pike viewed Slemmer as a rival for the affections of her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp.

Pike and Shipp both were convicted of first-degree murder. Pike was sentenced to death, while Shipp received a life sentence with the possibility of parole.

Their co-defendant, Shadolla Peterson, who was 18 at the time of the murder and acted as a lookout for the other two, testified for the prosecution and received probation.

Currently the only woman on Tennessee's death row, Pike was also convicted in ​August 2001 of attempted first-degree murder in an ​assault on another inmate, according to ⁠the Tennessee Department of Correction.

## TEEN WHO COMMITTED MURDER 'NO LONGER EXISTS'

In the 226-page petition asking the governor to commute her death penalty to a life sentence without the possibility of parole, Pike's lawyers documented her history as the childhood victim of violence, neglect and sexual abuse, ​including two rapes at ages 11 and 17. They also cited the diagnoses she received in prison for bipolar disorder and ​post-traumatic stress disorder.

Moreover, they ⁠pointed to evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for their client to control her impulses as a young person.

"The 18-year-old girl suffering from severe mental illness and near-debilitating trauma no longer exists," her lawyers wrote in response to Lee's denial of clemency. "Christa is a 50-year-old remorseful woman who understands her actions, receives proper ⁠treatment for ​her mental illness, and provides for and guides fellow incarcerated women."

Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, has spoken out in ​support of the execution.

Executions of female prison inmates are exceedingly rare in the US, with women accounting for just 18 of the 1,683 people put to death since the Supreme Court allowed capital punishment to resume in ​1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Before Wednesday, Tennessee had executed 17 people.

Adds background, details of the case, execution history, paragraphs 14-19

content:
伦敦 —

英国人权组织“西藏观察”(Tibet Watch)星期三(9月30日)发布调查报告称，中国当局正在西藏建立从警用无人机、自动机巢到反无人机设备的空中管控体系。报告也促使部分英国议员和人权人士呼吁英国政府，重新审查对中国无人机的相关采购。

这份75页的报告，题目为《高原上的眼睛》(Eyes Above the Plateau)分析查阅了2017年至2026年中国政府的采购公告、警方通报、培训记录和飞行管制文件。“西藏观察”指出，当局一方面把无人机用于巡逻、人群监测、边境管理和救援，另一方面采购无人机侦测和反制设备，并加强对民用无人机的管控。

**监控从地面延伸到空中**

报告发现，在西藏一些曾发生抗议的地区出现新的警用无人机部署。

四川德格县2024年曾发生反对岗托水电站建设的抗议。约15个月后，当地警方在川藏公路检查站升级项目中采购四套大疆自动机巢、四架无人机及调度系统，其中大疆核心设备价值约60.2万元人民币。

2013年曾发生抗议的西藏比如县，则拥有报告数据库中最大的县级警用无人机机队，共18架、涉及五种型号，用于日常巡逻。

日喀则桑珠孜区警方称，自2024年5月以来，无人机已执行5723次勤务，飞行超过2.27万公里，任务包括大型活动人流监测。

西藏观察组织发言人凯特·桑德斯(Kate Saunders)对美国之音说，中国安全部门在购买无人机、自动机巢和反无人机设备的同时，也限制其他人的飞行。西藏警方还将“维稳”列为无人机培训任务之一。

不过，桑德斯强调，采购地点与过去发生抗议的地区重合，并不能证明无人机曾被用于监控某次具体抗议。“没有任何文件显示，无人机曾飞越某一场具体抗议、节庆或某座寺院；我们的报告也没有这样声称。”她说。

报告也指出，无人机被用于搜救等正常警务工作，领导人访问的安保需要也可以解释部分临时飞行限制。

报告确认了12项涉及大疆设备的政府采购，买方包括西藏自治区公安厅反恐部门、拉萨城关警方、日喀则边境管理部门和武警西藏总队等。

报告所列12项采购的整个项目合同总额约2479万元人民币，但其中包括大量非大疆设备。报告还强调，大疆并不是这些采购合同中的直接卖方，设备均通过经销商或系统集成商提供，现有文件不能证明大疆知道最终用途或直接参与相关警务行动。

**英国采购受到质疑**

与此同时，报告援引2023年的数据称，当时37支英国警队拥有的337架无人机中，至少230架为大疆产品。

英国政府2022年要求各部门停止在敏感场所安装由中国生产的监控设备，并建议提前移除和更换已经部署的设备。英国政府2025年11月表示，最初识别出的相关敏感政府场所已经完成设备更换。

西藏观察呼吁英国政府将相关限制延伸至无人机。

英国上议院议员、议会人权联合委员会前主席戴维·奥尔顿勋爵(Lord David Alton)对美国之音说：“西藏人民如今被迫生活在乔治·奥威尔所设想的那种警察国家中。”他进一步表示,“除非英国限制警方使用中国制造的无人机，否则它将成为极权主义的合作者。”

国际人权组织“强化权利”(Fortify Rights)高级主任罗杰斯(Benedict Rogers)也对美国之音表示，这是一份“极为重要且令人担忧”的报告，揭示了他所称的中共在西藏广泛使用无人机监控，同时限制他人使用藏区空域的情况。

“这应当促使英国和其他民主国家政府质疑，采购中国制造的警用无人机是否明智、是否符合伦理和道德，”罗杰斯说。他将这类无人机称为“监控、镇压和间谍活动的工具”。

**报告证据的边界**

西藏观察强调，其数据库并非中国在藏区部署无人机的完整清单。系统性资料收集从2025年4月开始，2022年至2024年的资料仍在补充，青海和甘肃藏区也存在资料缺口。因此，报告明确没有声称无人机采购近年来出现加速。

报告也没有找到无人机针对某个具体藏人、某场抗议或某座寺院进行监控的直接记录。它所记录的是无人机和反无人机能力被部署到包括曾发生抗议、举行大型宗教活动以及边境在内的地区，而“维稳”和大型活动人流监测已成为警方公开列出的任务。

大疆此前否认参与侵犯人权活动，并表示其产品为民用及和平用途开发。

美国之音向英国政府、英国全国警察局长理事会、中国驻英国大使馆和大疆请求回应。但截至发稿前，均未收到回复。

# 韩国“习近平餐馆”遭中国人跨境喷漆袭击

图像来源，News1

图像加注文字，监控影片显示，一群蒙面男子在韩国京畿道城南市的这家餐厅内喷洒油漆。

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 黄思琪（Kelly Ng）

*   Published 2026年9月30日早上8点23分
*   阅读时间: 2 分钟

韩国警察表示，当地一家以中国国家主席习近平命名的餐厅遭一群中国籍人士破坏，而他们在施袭后立即逃离韩国，返回中国。

位于首尔以南京畿道城南市的这家餐厅的监控录像显示，9月24日凌晨，四名蒙面男子闯入店内，砸毁傢具并喷洒清漆。

餐厅老板向当地媒体表示，他之所以取名“习近平”，是因为他“希望它成为（韩国）最好的中餐馆”。他补充说：“没有任何政治意图。”

《朝鲜日报》报导称，这家餐厅已经营八年，但直到过去一年才开始收到要求更改店名的诉求。

End of content

去年8月，当有消息传出习近平将出席在韩国举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会时，老板表示，他接到了数十通与这些诉求有关的电话。他说，有些人甚至提出愿意付钱。

他向《朝鲜日报》表示：“一些自称在中国经营生意的人提出愿意给予大笔金额，只要我们改名。他们非常执着。”

今年4月，有人就餐厅菜单上一道名为“习近平特色炒饭”的菜式向韩国知识产权部门提出投诉，但该部门最终结案，认定不存在问题。

老板表示，上星期的袭击是他过去一年来遭遇过规模最大的一次。他告诉当地媒体，财物损失约为1,500万韩元（1.08万美元；7.2万元人民币；32.4万元新台币）。

习近平餐厅在袭击后关闭五天，并于星期二（9月29日）重新营业。老板表示，其团队现正考虑为餐厅更换新名称。

警方星期二表示，四名嫌疑人均为年龄介乎20至40岁的中国男子。据信他们在施袭后已逃往上海及山东烟台。

警方表示，计划为这四名男子申请国际刑警组织红色通报（Interpol Red Notice）。红色通报并非逮捕令，而是请求世界各地警方在引渡程序完成前拘留有关人士。

根据网上分享的截图，习近平餐厅供应种类广泛的中式菜肴，菜单中亦包括一些韩国菜式。Google用户给予该餐厅平均五星中的四星评分。

# 军情五处警告：中国资助英国研究，成果交予北京间谍机关

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，英国军情五处表示，一个曾资助英国研究项目的组织，一直在支援北京的间谍机关。

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 多米尼克·卡夏尼（Dominic Casciani）
    *   Role, BBC英国内政及法律事务记者

*   Published 2026年9月30日下午4点31分 最近更新： 1 小时前
*   阅读时间: 2 分钟

英国军情五处警告，中国透过一家为其情报及安全部门效力的掩护机构，取得超过100名与英国院校有联系的学者协助，用于针对英国的间谍活动，这些学者对此并不知情。

这个英国的国内安全情报机关罕有地公开[发出警告](https://www.mi5.gov.uk/mi5-issues-espionage-alert-cgtri-%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E9%80%9A%E7%94%A8%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF%E7%A0%94%E7%A9%B6%E9%99%A2)，提醒各大学和学者，如果继续与中国通用技术研究院（China General Technology Research Institute，简称CGTRI）保持联系，最终可能因协助外国而面临刑事检控。

英国安全事务国务大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）表示，军情五处的警告揭露了中国情报机构企图利用英国的学术研究，损害英国国家安全。

他表示，自己已致函所有大学校长，要求终止与该机构的关系。

今年6月，[英国军情五处与美国、加拿大、澳洲和新西兰的主要合作伙伴联合发出警告](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cj3pkgrzrd8o/trad)，指中国军事情报机关正以职业社交网站和网上求职平台为目标。

这次英国独立发出的最新警告更进一步，揭示军情五处所称正在英国学术机构内不断加剧的威胁。

军情五处表示，中国通用技术研究院——英文名称有时也译作China Academy of General Technology（简称CAGT）——与中国国家安全部有“非常密切的联系”。

警告说：“军情五处确认，中国通用技术研究院的主要目的，是资助能够直接提升中国国家安全部间谍技术能力的学术研究。”

警告又说：“超过100名与英国有联系的学者，曾参与由中国国家安全部透过中国通用技术研究院资助的项目。”军情五处补充，在部分个案中，研究人员可能并不知道这家掩护机构在其项目中所扮演的角色。

英国学者曾参与由中国通用技术研究院资助的项目，研究范畴包括人工智能、网络安全、隐蔽通讯系统和讯息隐写术。隐写术是指把秘密讯息或档案隐藏在普通讯息或物件之中。

军情五处说：“这些活动有助中国国家安全部进行间谍活动，对英国国家安全构成威胁。”

安全警告表示，许多学术机构和个人可能是“出于善意”与中国通用技术研究院合作，因为该机构与中国国家安全部的关系一直被“刻意掩饰”。

警告续称：“强烈建议英国学术机构立即检视任何正在进行或计划与中国通用技术研究院展开的合作，以确保中国国家安全部无法再从英国的大学或研究机构获益。”

这项公开警告意味，未有立即采取行动的英国学者，最终可能触犯法律。

该警告强调，英国在2023年通过、旨在打击国家间谍活动的重要法例《国家安全法》，订立了协助外国情报机关的新罪行，如果当事人按理应该知道自己的行为是在提供这类协助，便可能干犯该罪。

丹·贾维斯说：“这项警告揭露了中国情报机构企图暗中利用我国学者的专业知识和研究成果，从而损害英国及其盟友的国家安全。”

title: Exclusive: U.S. Lawmaker Warn South Korea’s Tilt Toward China Poses Risk
summary: Published 2026.09.30. 20:00 Updated 2026.09.30. 20:25 Republican John Moolenaar, chairman of the U.S. House of Representatives' U.S.-China Strategic Competition Special Committee. /Chosunilbo DB Republican Congressman John Moolenaar (John M
content:
Published 2026.09.30. 20:00 Updated 2026.09.30. 20:25

Republican John Moolenaar, chairman of the U.S. House of Representatives' U.S.-China Strategic Competition Special Committee. /Chosunilbo DB

Republican Congressman John Moolenaar (John Moolenaar), Chairman of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the 28th, stating, “South Korea’s shifting stance in economic, technological, and diplomatic areas toward the People’s Republic of China is posing a significant risk to U.S. interests.” Beyond the controversy over discrimination against U.S. digital companies like Coupang, the letter broadly addressed diplomatic and security issues, including President Lee Jae Myung’s position on the Taiwan issue and allegations of classified information leaks by Unification Minister Chung Dong-young. It argued that frictions between the U.S. and South Korea could lead to a “structural shift” in South Korea’s foreign policy and emphasized the need for close monitoring and joint measures.

The House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), established in January 2023, is a bipartisan body in the House of Representatives involving around 20 Republican and Democratic lawmakers, including Korean-American Young Kim and pro-Korea faction member Tom Suozzi. It analyzes economic, military, and technological threats from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and leads legislative and policy responses. Moolenaar, a six-term congressman, is a leading hawk in Congress who has criticized China’s military and economic coercion and urged unified action by allies, including South Korea, Japan, and the U.S. In the letter sent to Rubio, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, he stated, “The ROK-U.S. alliance remains indispensable,” but added, “Differences in views between allies on critical national interests cannot be taken lightly.”

Moolenaar referenced Rubio’s remarks in Congress in June that “South Korea’s elected leaders are taking positions contrary to U.S. national interests.” He evaluated that the pace of summits between South Korean and Chinese leaders over the past nine months, including Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to South Korea in October 2025 and President Lee Jae Myung’s state visit in January 2026, was unprecedented. Amid diplomatic conflicts between Japan and the People’s Republic of China over the Taiwan issue, he criticized Xi’s mention of Japan’s “sacrifices” against militarism 80 years ago as a “blatant attempt to drive a wedge between the U.S.’s two treaty allies.” Moolenaar also expressed concern that South Korea and the People’s Republic of China expanding export control and supply chain consultation channels could create a separate structure from the U.S. He further labeled Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix’s semiconductor factories in the People’s Republic of China as “leverage” for the CCP, stating, “The South Korean government may create commercial incentives to compromise with the People’s Republic of China.”

President Lee Jae Myung, left, and U.S. President Donald Trump meet for a summit on the 22nd during the UN General Assembly in New York. /News1

While acknowledging South Korea’s “progress” in sharing the U.S.’s burden, Moolenaar pointed out that achievements like increased defense spending and wartime operational control transfers are framed not as expanded contributions to the alliance but as reduced dependence on the U.S. He cited discord between the U.S. and South Korea over the U.S. Forces Korea’s sortie into the West Sea in February this year and the U.S. restricting intelligence sharing after allegations of classified leaks by the Unification Minister. He stated, “Seoul’s attitude toward regional emergencies is concerning.” Moolenaar also invoked President Lee’s past remarks, “What happens in the Taiwan Strait has nothing to do with us,” arguing, “The South Korean government seems to have effectively ruled out supporting potential regional responses to a Taiwan crisis triggered by the People’s Republic of China’s aggression.”

Moolenaar also highlighted the expansion of Chinese companies like AliExpress and Temu in the South Korean market and issues related to personal information and consumer protection. He claimed, “This contrasts sharply with immediate and repeated law enforcement actions against U.S. companies in South Korea.” He noted, “While South Korean regulators did not conduct an on-site investigation for four months after AliExpress concealed a platform hack, they launched an aggressive, multi-agency crackdown against Coupang over a low-sensitivity personal information leak, imposing a staggering $409 million fine.” The Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) imposed a record penalty of 624.681 billion Korean won on Coupang in June. The Coupang issue has acted as an obstacle in bilateral relations for nearly a year. Moolenaar requested the State Department to provide a follow-up briefing to the committee by October 31 on changes in South Korea–People’s Republic of China relations and the U.S. government’s response.

Republican John Moolenaar, chairman of the U.S. House of Representatives' U.S.-China Strategic Competition Special Committee, sends a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the 28th. /U.S. House of Representatives' U.S.-China Strategic Competition Special Committee

title: China carves new military presence in Southeast Asian neighbour
summary: * Summary * Satellite imagery shows Ban Keun airfield with paved runway and new buildings * Chinese military says facility will train air force pilots and is not directed against third parties * China's statement gives no details on personn
content:
*   Summary

*   Satellite imagery shows Ban Keun airfield with paved runway and new buildings
*   Chinese military says facility will train air force pilots and is not directed against third parties
*   China's statement gives no details on personnel, equipment or facilities to be based there

Sept 30 (Reuters) - China’s latest expansion of its overseas military footprint was carved from a patch of farmland in Laos over the past year, satellite imagery showed, as analysts said the ​new support centre could deepen Beijing's presence in Southeast Asia.

The China-Laos Joint Support and Training Center and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy are [now operational](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/china-opens-rare-joint-military-support-centre-laos-2026-09-29/) at an airport in Ban Keun, some 50 km (31 ‌miles) north of the Lao capital Vientiane, Beijing's Ministry of National Defence said on Tuesday.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fasia-pacific%2Fchina-carves-new-military-presence-southeast-asian-neighbour-2026-09-30%2F)

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

"The fact that this is a joint support and training centre suggests (China's People's Liberation Army) could be seeking persistent access to a logistics hub that can support forces rotating through Laos, perhaps with a small forward support element," said Rachel Vandenbrink, a senior analyst at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute.

Some records indicate the area was once used by the United States during its war in Laos and neighbouring Vietnam and Cambodia in the 1960s and 1970s. But commercial ​satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters shows the new construction goes far beyond the rough dirt strip visible until last year.

Work began on the new airfield in late 2025, according to the satellite imagery. As of ​early this month work was ongoing. In place of green fields, a large paved runway and a parallel taxiway and apron were visible, along with a number of new buildings.

The Laos ⁠Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not respond to questions, and China's statement did not provide details of what personnel, equipment or facilities would be based at the airport.

The facility will be used for training air force pilots and was "not ​directed against any third party," the Chinese defence ministry said.

China operates another joint training and support centre at Cambodia's Ream naval base on the Gulf of Thailand, and a logistics base in Djibouti. Cambodia says no Chinese personnel or warships are ​based permanently at Ream.

"Unlike Ream Naval Base, this military logistics base in Laos is more ostensibly similar to the one in Djibouti," Collin Koh, a security scholar at Singapore's S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, wrote in a post on the social media platform X. "It may not be wrong to conclude this is the first full-fledged PLA overseas base in Southeast Asia."

## DEEPER TIES

Laos, an impoverished one-party state ruled by the Lao People's Revolutionary Party, has a long and complex history with its fellow communist neighbours in China and Vietnam.

Its air force ​is small and operates a handful of aircraft designed by China and Russia.

Lao troops have typically needed to travel to Vietnam, Russia, and China for advanced training, but now some can be trained at home, said a diplomat from ​a Southeast Asian country who spoke on condition of anonymity.

China has been expanding its military presence across the region, the diplomat added, citing a [joint munitions factory](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-indonesia-ministers-meet-friday-discuss-security-economic-issues-2026-08-20/) in Indonesia.

Laos has carried out joint military exercises with China, including one aimed at humanitarian response this ‌month. In ⁠June, Lao President Thongloun Sisoulith visited Beijing for meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who called for a strategic dialogue on a number of issues including national defence.

The United States, which operates an expansive network of its own overseas bases, has watched Chinese moves with suspicion. Last year the Pentagon issued an annual report that listed 22 countries where Beijing had plans for military facilities, though Laos was not among them.

Thailand, a U.S. treaty ally that shares a long border with Laos, considers itself a close partner of both Laos and China and sees it as Vientiane's sovereign right to decide whether to grant permission for a Chinese base, said Rear Admiral Surasant Kongsiri, Thailand's Ministry of Defence spokesperson.

"Nevertheless, Thailand will ​continue to closely monitor developments and how the matter ​proceeds, particularly with regard to building mutual trust," he ⁠added.

Regional military attaches and analysts have long said China lacks an adequate network of military bases given its ongoing military modernisation and perceived need to project power to compete with the US.

Vandenbrink said it was unclear what military power China could project from Laos that it could not already do from its own southern province of Yunnan.

"At Ban Keun, ​the more immediate significance may be China's ability to establish a persistent military presence and deepen its institutional relationship with the Lao armed forces," she said.

## EXPANDING PRESENCE

China opened ​its Djibouti base in 2017 ⁠and has been gradually expanding its presence with extensive ship berthing and surveillance capabilities. The Pentagon has previously estimated it held 400 Marines.

Though extensive, the facility is surrounded by bases from other militaries, including Japan and the US.

Beyond Djibouti and Cambodia, China also has three island bases — complete with military-grade runways 3 km long — on Fiery Cross, Mischief and Subi reefs in the Spratly islands of the disputed South China Sea.

Developed since 2014, the facilities now contain wharves, extensive surveillance and air defence installations as well ⁠as housing.

Military attaches ​say the bases have allowed China to significantly expand its naval, coast guard and fishing militia deployments deep into the maritime heart of Southeast ​Asia. So far, however, it has yet to base jet fighters permanently in the Spratlys, possibly due to the harsh maritime environment.

Reuters in August and last month reported fresh work on what are expected to be extensive new bases in the Paracel archipelago further north, which is also ​claimed by Vietnam.

Reporting by Poppy McPherson and Josh Smith in Bangkok and Greg Torode in Hong Kong; Additional reporting by Panu Wongcha-um in Bangkok, Mei Mei Chu and Liz Lee in Beijing; Writing by Josh Smith; Editing by Kate Mayberry

title: Republican committee chair calls for scrutiny of Seoul's China ties
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung shake hands at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, China January 5, 2026. China Daily via REUTERS/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.r
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung shake hands at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, China January 5, 2026. China Daily via REUTERS/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/chinese-president-xi-jinping-and-south-korean-president-lee-jae-myung-in-beijing/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMllVSUEzWERPTQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Lawmaker's letter cites Taiwan issue in warning on Seoul
*   Warns frictions could develop into 'structural shift' in Seoul's alignment
*   Letter highlights technology ties, treatment of US firms

WASHINGTON, Sept 30 (Reuters) - The Republican chair of the congressional committee focused on China is calling on the Trump administration ​to scrutinize US ally South Korea's warming ties with China, which he said pose "significant risks" to the United States.

In a letter to Secretary ‌of State Marco Rubio, Representative John Moolenaar urged "heightened vigilance" about the relationship, citing deepening leader-level ties, South Korean semiconductor investment in China, and unfair treatment of American firms in South Korea compared with Chinese rivals.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Frepublican-committee-chair-calls-scrutiny-seouls-china-ties-2026-09-30%2F)

Report Ad![Image 2](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

Moolenaar described South Korea as "a major American ally," but warned of "the potential for frictions to develop into a structural shift in Seoul's alignment" requiring "close monitoring and, as necessary, concerted action."

South Korea's ​foreign ministry said it could not comment in detail on the contents of the letter, which was sent on Tuesday and had not been ​previously reported or made public.

It said that the US-South Korea alliance was the cornerstone of its foreign policy and that they were ⁠advancing the alliance across several areas.

The letter comes after a period of tensions in US-South Korea relations that has included some [sharp criticism of Seoul by President Donald Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-instructs-pentagon-reduce-military-exercises-with-south-korea-2026-08-16/).

The ​two countries have been allies since the 1950-53 Korean War, in which China backed North Korea, but differences have surfaced over trade, China policy and security issues, even ​as Trump has [worked to improve his own relations with Beijing.](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-xis-stalemate-summit-was-glitzy-gift-china-2026-09-28/)

On Tuesday, people familiar with the discussions told Reuters Trump could announce as soon as Wednesday that his administration intends to use South Korea's strategic investment fund [for several major US projects](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/trump-set-tout-korean-investment-alaska-lng-other-projects-2026-09-29/) including roughly $54 billion for a planned Alaska LNG facility.

Moolenaar called the ​pace of leader-level engagement between Seoul and Beijing unprecedented, citing Chinese President Xi Jinping's first visit to South Korea in 11 years in 2025 and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's ‌visit to ⁠China this year, the first by a South Korean president since 2019.

He said the "widening gulf" between South Korea and the US was especially troubling because Seoul had "effectively ruled out" supporting a regional response to any Chinese aggression against Taiwan, citing Lee's 2024 election campaign remark: "What does it matter to us what happens in the Taiwan Strait?"

In an interview with Japan's NHK broadcaster in January, Lee said that it would serve South Korea well to "avoid unnecessary involvement," saying it was in the national interest to respect ​others' positions.

This week, in a post ​on X mentioning South Korea's booming trade ⁠with China, Lee said: "In diplomacy, South Korea-US alliance is most important, but it is also important to manage relations with China."

Lee met with Trump [on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/south-koreas-lee-trump-welcome-progress-us-strategic-investment-projects-2026-09-23/) last week, two days before the US president's meeting with ​Chinese leader Xi.

On technology, Moolenaar argued that South Korea's semiconductor investments in China could leave key US supply chains vulnerable ​to Chinese pressure. He ⁠pointed to Samsung's chipmaking plant in Xi'an and SK Hynix's operations in Wuxi and Dalian, calling them potential points of leverage for Beijing over allied technology production.

Moolenaar also expressed concern over what he described as more lenient South Korean enforcement toward Chinese e-commerce platforms such as Alibaba's AliExpress and Temu when it came to alleged data privacy, consumer protection, ⁠cybersecurity and product ​safety violations compared with that faced by American firms such as Coupang.

The companies mentioned in the ​letter did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Coupang declined to comment. South Korea's foreign ministry said its regulatory authorities treat all companies operating in Korea fairly.

Moolenaar called for a State Department briefing on ​developments in South Korea-China relations by October 31.

Adds detail about the letter in paragraph four

Reporting by David Brunnstrom and Alexandra Alper; Additional reporting by Kyu-seok Shim in Seoul; Editing by Don Durfee and Michael Perry

title: Israeli officials say diverted flydubai incident may be attempted 'terror attack'
summary: * Summary * Companies * Plane landed safely at Tabuk airport, all passengers are accounted for, airline says * Flight transmitted general emergency signal, then possible unlawful interference signal, Flightradar24 says * Israeli official sa
content:
*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Plane landed safely at Tabuk airport, all passengers are accounted for, airline says
*   Flight transmitted general emergency signal, then possible unlawful interference signal, Flightradar24 says
*   Israeli official says pilots sent emergency signals after physical altercation with each other
*   Flightradar24 data showed aircraft plunged nearly 14,000 feet within 30 seconds

JERUSALEM, Sept 30 (Reuters) - The co-pilot of a flight ​from Dubai to Tel Aviv is believed to have stabbed the captain in a possible attempted "terror attack" on Wednesday, forcing the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia where it landed safely, ‌three Israeli officials said.

They said the cabin crew entered the cockpit and took control of flydubai flight FZ1073 from the United Arab Emirates to Israel, which diverted to Saudi Arabia as it flew over Jordanian airspace. One of the officials identified the attacker as an Omani national.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Fdiverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30%2F)

An Israeli official had earlier told Reuters the plane transmitted emergency signals after the pilots got into a physical altercation with each other.

The aircraft's data appeared to show that it had suddenly and rapidly descended by nearly 14,000 feet in less than ​30 seconds before a first emergency signal was sent, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24.

Around the time the plane landed in Saudi Arabia, Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister's office, told Reuters ​the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking, describing it as a "different incident".

He did not immediately respond to a further request for comment on whether Israel ⁠was treating it as a "terror incident".

The Israeli officials, speaking on the condition of anonymity to brief reporters, said Israel's current assessment is that the incident was an attempted "terror attack" and not related to any kind of mental ​health issue with either of the pilots.

Omani authorities and the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

## BOTH PILOTS HOSPITALISED, TABUK AIRPORT SAYS

In a video purportedly of an Israeli passenger on board ​the flydubai flight and carried widely by Israeli media, the passenger said one of pilots was seriously injured and the other was slightly injured, after one of the pilots was stabbed.

Saudi Arabia's Tabuk airport, where the plane landed, said that both pilots had been hospitalised after sustaining injuries. Neither the airport nor the purported Israeli passenger identified the attacker.

The flight transmitted a general emergency signal and then another emergency signal that indicated possible unlawful interference, according to Flightradar24.

The Boeing 737 plane, which Israeli media said had around ​150 Israeli passengers on board, then again transmitted the initial general emergency signal before later landing at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, the website said.

It was not immediately clear who transmitted the emergency signals.

The incident heightened ​security fears in Israel weeks before Israelis vote in the first election since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attacks, with Israel's security figuring prominently in the campaigning.

Responding to the incident on X, far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir wrote "terrorism is a devil with whom no ‌agreement must ⁠be reached".

## CONFLICTING REPORTS APPEAR IN MEDIA, ISRAEL HOLDS SECURITY CONSULTATIONS

Israeli media published conflicting reports on the incident, with some outlets reporting that a pilot had tried to crash the passenger plane in an alleged suicide attempt. Some Israeli media outlets identified the pilots as Omani and Emirati nationals, while others said they were Russian and Ukrainian.

The incident triggered national security consultations in Israel, which has no official diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, where the plane landed.

In an earlier statement, the Israeli prime minister's office said the situation was "under control" and that all measures were being taken to bring the Israeli passengers back to Israel.

Netanyahu who had held security consultations on the incident, has cleared his schedule ​for the rest of the day to manage the crisis, ​an Israeli official said.

Netanyahu on Sunday met with ⁠UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan during a a rare visit to the Gulf country. Israel and the UAE have forged close security, military and economic ties since establishing diplomatic ties in 2020.

Earlier this year, Israel provided the UAE with Iron Dome air-defence systems and Israeli personnel to operate them, helping defend against Iranian attacks ​launched after Israel and the United States began strikes on Iran.

The UAE has yet to comment on the incident, while the Dubai-owned airline has only said that the flight ​experienced an "incident" and diverted to ⁠Tabuk, where it landed safely, and that all passengers were safe and accounted for.

## PASSENGER REPORTEDLY WITNESSED PILOT FORCED TO THE FLOOR BY MAN HOLDING A KNIFE

Yasmin Abukasis said her daughter Miriam, who was among the passengers on the flight, had told her that she had heard screaming and that a man holding a knife had forced one of the pilots onto the floor, and that there was blood everywhere.

Israeli media published a photo purportedly taken from inside the plane, which appeared ⁠to show a ​passenger's blood-soaked shirt. Reuters could not immediately verify the image.

Flydubai operates daily return flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route that is ​popular among Israeli nationals. The flight path normally uses airspace over Saudi Arabia and Jordan.

It is not the first time a flight between Israel and the UAE has landed in Saudi Arabia. A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Riyadh ​in September 2025 due to a medical incident, Israeli media reported at the time.

Adds Israeli official identifying attacker as an Omani national in paragraph 2, political context in paragraphs 14-15

Reporting by Rami Ayyub, Alexander Cornwell, Rami Amichay, Federico Maccioni, Lina Obeid; Writing by Alexander Cornwell and Tom Perry; Editing by Andrew Heavens and Philippa Fletcher

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Alexander has over a decade of international reporting experience. He is currently a senior correspondent in Jerusalem covering Israel & the Palestinian Territories and was formerly in Dubai where he covered the Arabian Peninsula, including the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Yemen, often writing about foreign policy, security and economic-related issues.

content:
[BBC News, 中文](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/simp)[跳过此内容](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/c64grn5g7em2o/simp#content)

分类

# 中国人工智慧工具“教导”研究人员制造生物武器

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，学者指出国际监管不太可能跟上人工智慧的发展速度

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 克里斯·瓦兰斯（Chris Vallance）
    *   Role, BBC资深科技记者

*   Published 4 小时前
*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

中国人工智慧（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智能）开发商月之暗面（Moonshot）正在进行内部审查，因为有其他公司的研究人员成功说服其两款热门的 Kimi 模型讲解如何制造生物武器和执行暗杀任务。

测试 AI 系统安全性的 Mindgard 公司告诉BBC，该公司在今年7月发现 Kimi K2.6 和 K3Swarm 可以绕过开发者设定的安全限制。

问题是在被称为“越狱”（jailbreaking）的过程中出现。研究人员使用一系列复杂的指令来测试 AI 工具是否会忽略防护措施——Mindgard 表示，这本应阻止 Kimi 讨论令人担忧的话题。

月之暗面告诉BBC，它欢迎第三方意见，“这是建立更好、更安全的AI的关键支柱”。

## 网路攻击发动平台

Mindgard 尚未证明 Kimi 就相关问题提供的答案是否有效。

但这家研究机构指出，应该有相应的防护措施来阻止相关模型与使用者就此类主题进行讨论。

该机构还强调他们确信，越狱后的 Kimi 2.6 能让骇客在其运算资源上运行程式码并连接到网路，从而成为网路攻击的潜在跳板。

加拉汉先生为其公司公开讨论其破解月之暗面系统的决定辩护，称其已通知开发商，并且不会透露如何让该公司的模型无视防护措施的关键细节。

Mindgard 今年7月27日透过电子邮件通知月之暗面越狱漏洞，并在大约一周后跟进。

随后，该机构于9月12日发表了一篇关于此事的部落格文章。

但该公司表示，月之暗面是最近才联系他们的，此前BBC曾联系他们征求意见。

月之暗面在一封发给 Mindgard 的电子邮件中要求提供更多细节。月之暗面向BBC分享了该邮件，当中提到，其模型在内部评估中普遍显示“此类请求的拒绝率很高”。

## 防止越狱

这项研究结果出炉之际，人工智慧产业仍在争论封闭的专有模型——例如ChatGPT 和Anthropic 的 Claude 系统所使用的模型——还是开源工具才是最佳或最安全的发展方向。

Kimi 是一个开放权重模型，这意味着理论上任何人都可以获得该模型并在自己的计算基础设施上运行它。

英国萨里大学（Surrey Univesity）的艾伦·伍德沃德教授（Prof Alan Woodward）向BBC强调，开源模型存在落入坏人手中的风险，但它们也可以用于网路防御。

他举例，人工智慧公司 Hugging Face 使用了一个中国开源模型来理解一次骇客攻击，而该攻击[后来被证实是由 OpenAI 的代理执行的](https://bbc.com/news/articles/c3ek3gvdnj3o)。

伍德沃德教授解释，国际监管不太可能跟上人工智慧的发展速度，他说：“我们花了数十年才就电话号码的格式达成协议。”

与 Mindgard 创始人加拉汉教授一样，伍德沃德教授认为应该更加重视识别和起诉滥用人工智慧的人类。

# 特朗普排除美中合作开发人工智能

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，特朗普在 America.gov 网站的启动仪式上发表讲话。

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 小伯恩德·德布斯曼（Bernd Debusmann Jr）
    *   Role, BBC白宫记者

*   Published 2 小时前
*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）表示，不会考虑与中国合资发展人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧），认为这等同于把美国的技术机密交给主要经济竞争对手。

尽管美国民众对人工智能可能带来的风险越加关注，[特朗普周二（9月29日）在华盛顿出席一场活动时](https://bbc.com/news/articles/cme30dz5vkzko)，再次反对对人工智能发展加设限制，认为这些限制会妨碍这项技术未来的发展。

中国国家主席习近平上周访问白宫后，中美宣布成立新的人工智能对话机制，并计划在11月继续举行会谈。

两国亦设立新的沟通渠道，以避免人工智能相关事件引发误会。

特朗普周二出席利用人工智能，协助简化政府服务的新网站 America.gov 启动活动。特朗普认为美国在人工智慧领域“遥遥领先”，不想与潜在的竞争对手“混为一谈”。

“如果我们这样做，就等于把我们掌握的大量机密交给他们（中国），而他们当然会想得到这些东西，其他国家也会想得到。”

他又说：“坦白说，根本没有第三名⋯⋯现在就是我们和中国之间的竞争。”

特朗普表示，上周与习近平会面时也谈到人工智能，但他仍然反对中美共同发展这项技术。

“这样一来，他们就可以立即接触到一些我们知道、但他们还不知道的东西。”他又说：“我们现在领先中国，也领先其他所有国家，我希望保持这个优势。”

特朗普与习近平会面前，中国外交部曾警告，散播“威胁论”和采取对抗态度都会阻碍人工智能的治理。

特朗普之后在白宫与政府部门及科技公司代表共进午餐，出席者包括 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 的代表。他说在场人士“普遍认为人工智能应该受到大幅度的自我监管”。

会面后，特朗普向记者表示，与会的科技界领袖已签署一份具有“道德约束力”的文件，希望以此作为防范人工智能潜在危险的“一种保障”。

特朗普又说，政府很可能会在未来数日任命一名“超级智能沙皇”（Super Intelligence Czar）。他周二下午签署[行政命令](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/09/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-inaugurates-the-era-of-super-intelligence/)，正式把政府文件中的“人工智能”改称为“超级智能”（Super Intelligence）。

在美国国内，越来越多人担心人工智能可能带来的危险，也有人要求政府加强监管。

Politico 于9月底公布的一项民调显示，每三名美国人就有约两人认为，人工智能至少有“中等程度”的风险，可能最终摧毁人类。

在受访的特朗普支持者中，44%表示，他们宁愿暂停人工智能的发展。

不过，特朗普多次淡化外界对人工智能安全问题的忧虑，形容这些担忧是“骗局”，又把人工智能安全问题与他所称的“全球暖化骗局”相提并论，并声称这是由“激进左翼民主党人”策动的。

title: Xi in Washington and the Future of Sino-American Relations - The Institute for Peace and Diplomacy - l’Institut pour la paix et la diplomatie
summary: ## Strategic Foresight Brief Whether Washington and Beijing can translate their summit commitments into a more enduring basis for managing competition, or whether it represents another interval between crises, remains to be seen. Four month
content:
## Strategic Foresight Brief

Whether Washington and Beijing can translate their summit commitments into a more enduring basis for managing competition, or whether it represents another interval between crises, remains to be seen.

Four months after their Beijing meeting, Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping have renewed their efforts to stabilize U.S.-China relations. The Washington summit extended the trade truce and advanced arrangements for economic dialogue and managing AI risks. Yet disputes over Taiwan, technology and the wider strategic relationship remain unresolved.

The continuing war in Iran is also testing whether Washington and Beijing can cooperate to contain instability in the Middle East even as they disagree over its causes and resolution. The central question is whether sustained engagement can produce a more durable relationship, and whether the mechanisms emerging from these meetings can withstand the next serious disagreement.

Building on its May **[symposium](https://peacediplomacy.org/2026/05/13/trump-meets-xi-where-u-s-china-relations-go-next-and-where-they-take-the-world/)**, the Institute for Peace & Diplomacy brings together scholars and practitioners to assess what has changed and what remains uncertain. Contributors differ over the significance of the current rapprochement. Some see the beginnings of a more stable coexistence while others question whether diplomatic momentum reflects meaningful convergence or a temporary alignment of interests. These assessments also examine Beijing’s bargaining position, the impact of Washington’s involvement in the Iran war, the benefits and limitations of leader-level diplomacy, and the implications of closer great-power coordination for other countries.

Whether Washington and Beijing can translate their summit commitments into a more enduring basis for managing competition, or whether it represents another interval between crises, remains to be seen.

*    September 29, 2026

## The view from experts

## Sumantra Maitra

## Washington Fellow, Institute for Peace & Diplomacy

China and the U.S. have realized that they are peer powers, and given the war in Iran and over Ukraine, dialogue is beneficial to a trade war, but it somehow gives the impression that China is on the front foot in this equation and is waiting out the Trump administration to see what comes next.

The summit was high on symbolism and low on substantive progress. There was no mention of human rights, and the pomp clearly demonstrated that China is now a peer power of the United States, and Washington recognizes that. The truce was extended as a sign of American failure to coerce China, and major disputes over Taiwan, tariffs, technology, artificial intelligence, and the broader strategic relationship remained unresolved. At the same time, direct engagement is increasingly understood as necessary to prevent that competition from escalating into a crisis in Asia.

China and the U.S. have realized that they are peer powers, and given the war in Iran and over Ukraine, dialogue is beneficial to a trade war, but it somehow gives the impression that China is on the front foot in this equation and is waiting out the Trump administration to see what comes next.

## Mark Esposito

## Senior Fellow, Institute for Peace & Diplomacy; Professor, Northeastern University

With AI executives in the room alongside heads of state, Washington and Beijing are quietly conceding that the operators of these systems are now participants in their governance.

The Washington summit will be read as a thaw, but its significance is narrower and more interesting than that. What the two governments have built is not cooperation on AI. It is plumbing: a dialogue channel and a threat notification system that presume competition will continue and seek only to keep it from becoming an accident.

That is worth having. Frontier systems now fail in ways neither Washington nor Beijing can fully anticipate, and agentic deployment compresses the time available to interpret the other side’s behaviour. A hotline does not align interests; it buys minutes. In a domain where misread capability is as dangerous as misused capability, minutes matter.

The limits are structural. Chip access, distillation, and control over how advanced AI capabilities diffuse are distributional questions, and no notification protocol resolves those underlying conflicts. Expect the channel to hold on safety incidents and to fray wherever commercial advantage is implicated.

The deeper implication is institutional. With AI executives in the room alongside heads of state, Washington and Beijing are quietly conceding that the operators of these systems are now participants in their governance. That is the real shift the summit records, and the rest of the world, which has neither the models nor the seats, should notice.

## Stacie E. Goddard

## Arnold A. Saltzman Professor in War and Peace Studies; Director, Saltzman Institute for War and Peace Studies, Columbia University

Despite the lack of substantive outcomes, what the summit shows us is that Trump is far more interested in great power collusion than he is in great power competition.

The summit between President Trump and President Xi is unlikely to produce anything of substance. Surely the two leaders will discuss key issues of trade, AI, and the war in Iran. Chinese media [reports](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202609/25/content_WS6ab55a99c6d00ca5f9a0d724.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) that Xi used the occasion to ask Trump to act “prudently” towards Taiwan.

Despite the lack of substantive outcomes, what the summit shows us is that Trump is far more interested in great power collusion than he is in great power competition. This has been evident from the start of his second term in office. Within months of taking office, Trump signalled that he seeks a wide-ranging settlement with Xi. Early on, anonymous Trump advisers [told](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/19/business/economy/trump-china-trade-deal.html) The New York Times that Trump would like to sit down “man to man” with Xi to hammer out terms governing trade, investment, and nuclear arms.

It is striking that, in the same week that Trump has banned U.S. media from the White House, he welcomed Chinese media to record the pageantry surrounding Xi’s visit: the hundreds of U.S. military personnel on display, a 21-gun salute, a B-2 stealth bomber flyover, and a state dinner stacked with tech billionaires. While diplomatic engagement with great power rivals is necessary, this autocratic adulation undermines democratic interests.

## Xiao He

## Director, Foreign Policy Analysis, Institute of World Economic and Politics

[U.S.] resistance to overarching cooperative frameworks such as the new model of major-power relationship stemmed chiefly from geopolitical hubris rather than claimed cultural disparities.

The timely and successful convening of the Washington summit brings positive prospects for China-U.S. relations and the world. Following President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump’s Beijing meeting in May, bilateral ties have enjoyed unusual stability in both strategic and economic areas, which this summit further reinforces. It proves that the White House discarding Cold War mentalities allows China and the United States to overcome disruptions and move toward harmonious coexistence.

Both sides reaffirmed a constructive strategic-stability relationship. Washington once insisted on issue-based cooperation premised on China’s unilateral concessions. Its resistance to overarching cooperative frameworks such as the new model of major-power relationship stemmed chiefly from geopolitical hubris rather than claimed cultural disparities.

China principally seeks confidence in viable bilateral coexistence. It expects Washington to rein in anti-China sentiment and uphold a restrained, consistent China policy. China does not expect drastic U.S. policy adjustments amid unfinished domestic consensus, yet it urges continued U.S. strategic and economic goodwill to sustain improving bilateral dynamics.

## Paul J. Heer

## Senior Nonresident Fellow, Lester Crown Center on US Foreign Policy, Chicago Council on Global Affairs

The key obstacle to stabilizing US-China relations: both sides are still maneuvering for advantage in what each claims the other has made a zero-sum competition. And both sides think they have the balance of leverage and that time is on their side.

Pageantry overshadowed substance during Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington last week. Time for actual policy discussions was limited, but the two sides agreed to extend their “trade truce” for another two months, and spoke tentatively about establishing a dialogue on AI issues. Clearly, the primary purpose of the visit was to sustain the narrative of forward momentum in President Trump’s relationship with Xi, rather than to confront any troublesome bilateral issues in depth. In their public remarks, both leaders spoke about working together to forge a better future for both countries and for the globe.

But advancing that vision in the real world faces several fundamental challenges. At their Beijing summit in May, the two sides embraced the framework of pursuing “constructive strategic stability” in US-China relations. Since then, however, almost nothing has been done to define that goal or to develop a plan for proceeding toward it. Indeed, only Xi explicitly reaffirmed that goal in Washington, whereas many on the US side have tried to retreat from it rhetorically, or have characterized it as a Chinese trap. This underscores the key obstacle to stabilizing US-China relations: both sides are still maneuvering for advantage in what each claims the other has made a zero-sum competition. And both sides think they have the balance of leverage and that time is on their side. That is not a recipe for advancing “constructive strategic stability.”

## David C. Kang

## Principal, Pacific Research and Consulting

The few times Trump has talked about Taiwan directly in the past year, he has been either critical or ambiguous. This might be viewed positively in Beijing, but it is in fact decades-long U.S. policy to be ambiguous about Taiwan and to acknowledge but not support China’s position on the issue.

As expected, the summit between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump produced few surprises. Both leaders avoided the roughest parts of the US-China relationship, settling instead for atmospherics and symbolism.

The most substantive outcome was announced just before the summit, when the U.S. and China announced they had agreed to extend a truce on their trade wars into January 2027. This does not, however, mark any actual movement in the relationship, and the hoped-for reduction in tariffs has not occurred.

Perhaps most notable is what was not discussed publicly: Taiwan. Although Xi reportedly brought up Taiwan in their private discussions, urging Trump to “oppose Taiwanese independence,” Trump declined to say whether Taiwan had been discussed. In fact, Trump has recently been notably quiet about Taiwan, barely mentioning it at all in his social media posts. The few times Trump has talked about Taiwan directly in the past year, he has been either critical or ambiguous. This might be viewed positively in Beijing, but it is in fact decades-long U.S. policy to be ambiguous about Taiwan and to acknowledge but not support China’s position on the issue. That Trump downplayed Taiwan during the summit will not please the hawks in Washington, but it does continue this 2nd Trump administration’s relative lack of attention to that issue.

Given the lack of substantive movement on trade or tariffs, the pageantry of the summit is perhaps the best outcome that could be hoped for. In short, no surprises, but little progress, either.

title: 日中两国就《联合国宪章》的“敌国条款”再度交锋
summary: 华盛顿 — 星期二(9月29日)是《日中联合声明》签署、日中邦交实现正常化54周年的纪念日。此前一天，中日因《联合国宪章》中的“敌国条款”再次交锋。 在纽约举行的联合国大会一般性辩论中，针对日本首相高市早苗几天前呼吁“尽早删除”《联合国宪章》中的“敌国条款”，中国代表在行使答辩权表示，日本企图推动军国主义复活，并表示“坚决反对”，而日本代表反驳称日方“坚持专守防卫”。 高市早苗9月22日首次在联合国大会上发表讲话，呼吁联合国删除《联合国宪章》中关于“敌对国家”的表述。她郑重表
content:
华盛顿 —

星期二(9月29日)是《日中联合声明》签署、日中邦交实现正常化54周年的纪念日。此前一天，中日因《联合国宪章》中的“敌国条款”再次交锋。

在纽约举行的联合国大会一般性辩论中，针对日本首相高市早苗几天前呼吁“尽早删除”《联合国宪章》中的“敌国条款”，中国代表在行使答辩权表示，日本企图推动军国主义复活，并表示“坚决反对”，而日本代表反驳称日方“坚持专守防卫”。

高市早苗9月22日首次在联合国大会上发表讲话，呼吁联合国删除《联合国宪章》中关于“敌对国家”的表述。她郑重表明：“凭借日本过去70年来为联合国工作做出的重大贡献，我带着深刻的自豪感与敬意，强烈地提出这一点。”

《联合国宪章》中的“敌国”条款到底是什么？它为何被写入《联合国宪章》？高市早苗为何要求删除它？而中国又为何反对？

**联合国宪章有关“敌国”的三个条款**

“敌国”一词在《[联合国宪章](https://www.un.org/zh/about-us/un-charter/full-text)》的三个条款中均有提及：第53条、第77条和第107条。

《联合国宪章》起草于第二次世界大战末期，并于战后立即生效，即1945年10月24日。同盟国(美、英、中、苏、法)在宪章起草过程中发挥了关键作用，并随后占据了联合国安理会常任理事国席位。同盟国将宪章视为一种机制，旨在防止前轴心国(德、意、日)重新滋生军国主义或法西斯政治，而无需诉诸新成立的安理会。

联合国宪章第53条第一款规定：安全理事会对于职权内之执行行动，在适当情形下，应利用此项区域办法或区域机关。如无安全理事会之授权，不得依区域办法或由区域机关采取任何执行行动；但关于依第一百零七条之规定对付本条第二项所指之任何敌国之步骤，或在区域办法内所取防备此等国家再施其侵略政策之步骤，截至本组织经各关系政府之请求，对于此等国家之再次侵略，能担负防止责任时为止，不在此限。

第53条第二款说，本条第一项所称敌国系指第二次世界大战中为本宪章任何签字国之敌国而言。

第77条第二款的第二项涉及“托管制度”对“……因第二次世界大战而从敌国手中分离出来的领土”的适用。根据《联合国宪章》，联合国应建立“国际托管制度”，以管理和监督“托管领土”(第75条)，这些“托管领土”指的是“人民尚未获得完全自治的领土”(第73条)。当时共有11个这样的托管领土，分布在非洲和太平洋岛屿上。

第107条规定：本宪章并不取消或禁止负行动责任之政府对于在第二次世界大战中本宪章任何签字国之敌国因该次战争而采取或受权执行之行动。

简单来说，这三个条款赋予了二战同盟国在无需联合国安理会事先批准的情况下，对德、意、日等前敌国再次表现出侵略倾向时直接采取防范或军事打击行动的法律基础。

**日本：“敌国条款”过时，日本是爱好和平的国家**

在高市早苗在联大发表讲话后，日本外务省9月24日在X平台发帖再次表明了日本政府的立场，即这些条款已经过时，与日本在国际社会中的地位不符。

声明说，中国再次就《联合国宪章》中所谓的“敌对国家条款”发表声明，仿佛这些早已失效的条款仍然有效。这种声明与联合国已通过并由中国自身支持的相关决议相矛盾。

声明说，中国曾投票赞成1995年联合国大会决议，该决议明确承认《联合国宪章》中所谓的“敌国条款”已经过时，形同虚设。此外，中国也加入了2005年联合国大会决议的共识，该决议明确规定所有会员国国家元首和政府首脑决心从《联合国宪章》中删除“敌对国家”一词。作为联合国安理会常任理事国，中国理应尊重其所支持的这些决议。

声明还强调，日本自战后以来，“作为一个爱好和平的国家，始终为国际社会的和平与繁荣作出贡献。国际社会也普遍认可这一事实。”

声明说，正如高市首相在一般性辩论中所述，日本将继续坚定地阐明和宣传其立场和倡议。

**中国：日本再军事化，挑战战后国际秩序**

对高市早苗的言论，中国常驻联合国副代表孙磊9月28日行使答辩权，表达了坚决反对。他将这些条款与日本的历史责任及其当前的安保政策联系起来。

他指出，“敌国条款”是《联合国宪章》不可或缺的组成部分，在日方近年消极动向的背景下，时至今日仍具有重要现实意义，不容删改。

他还说，高市政府对历史罪行避而不谈，一边炮制周边威胁，一边持续大幅扩充军费、放宽杀伤性武器出口、推进修宪并试图突破“无核三原则”。中方单方面指责日本的“再军事化”已经成为地区乃至世界和平稳定的现实威胁，是对战后国际秩序的挑战。

值得一提的是，朝鲜代表也行使了答辩权，指出“日本正在推行军国主义政策”，并称呼吁删除敌国条款是“可耻之举”。

对此，日本代表行使答辩权，进行了反驳，强调日方“坚持专守防卫”，并表态日本会继续坚持“无核三原则”，“绝不会改变作为热爱和平的国家所走过的道路”。

9月23日，在高市早苗在联合国大会讲话的第二天，中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆在例行记者会上被问到如何看待日本的说法。

他也以同样的说辞指日本“美化战争罪行，还持续强军扩武，加速“再军事化”...公然挑战战后国际秩序，已成为威胁地区和平稳定的突出因素。”

日本媒体报道指出，《联合国宪章》的“敌国条款”为北京提供了向日本施压的助力。

**联合国大会的态度及修改宪章的难度**

高市早苗并不是第一位呼吁删除《联合国宪章》中“敌国条款”的日本首相。

1995年，联合国大会以155票赞成(包括中国在内)、0票反对、3票弃权通过了第50/52号决议，表示有意启动《联合国宪章》第108条规定的程序，删除“敌对国家条款”。

十年后，未经表决通过的2005年世界首脑会议成果文件再次宣布应删除“敌对国家条款”。然而，这一进程随后停滞不前，《联合国宪章》本身也从未被正式修订以删除这些条款。

但是，修改《联合国宪章》的程序极其繁琐.第108条规定的程序本身就是一个障碍。根据第108条，任何修正案都必须经联合国大会三分之二多数票通过，并由联合国会员国三分之二按照各自的宪法程序予以批准，其中包括安全理事会所有常任理事国。这意味着任何正式的修正案都不能绕过安全理事会常任理事国，包括中国和俄罗斯。

值得注意的是，高市在纽约联合国大会上的讲话呼吁删除“敌对国家”条款是她呼吁改革联合国，特别是安理会的更广泛诉求的一部分，她称安理会改革“至关重要”。

“安理会目前的架构，其职责是维护国际和平与安全，反映的是1945年的国际形势。我们需要立即将其改造为一个真正反映当前国际社会现实的架构，”高市早苗说，“为此，必须扩大安理会常任理事国和非常任理事国的数量，以确保安理会的合法性和代表性。”

**美国的立场**

美国尚未就日本首相高市早苗在联合国大会上呼吁删除《联合国宪章》“敌对国家”条款的讲话发表正式的官方声明。美国之音也向美国国务院发出问询，但是，截至美国之音发稿，还没有收到国务院的回复。

高市早苗在联大发表讲话前，与唐纳德·特朗普总统(Donald Trump)举行了一次简短的峰会。两位领导人主要讨论了美日同盟、经济安全以及涉及中国的区域合作。此次会晤的公开记录并未明确提及“敌对国家”条款。

特朗普总统在谈到高市时说：“她是我的朋友，正在取得非常出色的成就。她也将被历史铭记。”

值得一提的是，在中日关系陷入低谷的当下，中国外长王毅9月28日在会晤到访北京的日本前外相岩屋毅时呼吁中日关系正常化。

9月29日，中国驻日本大使馆再次在X上发帖说，1972年9月29日,中日两国政府正式签署《中日联合声明》。 “让我们共同重温两国关系的原点。”

title: Fortress Guam: The Environmental Cost of Preparing For War With China
summary: _Editor’s Note: This is the second part of a two-part investigation. Read the first story, [“The Pesticide Papers,” here.](https://thewarhorse.org/guam-military-pesticide-contamination/) CHamoru is the officially adopted spelling in Guam. T
content:
_Editor’s Note: This is the second part of a two-part investigation. Read the first story, [“The Pesticide Papers,” here.](https://thewarhorse.org/guam-military-pesticide-contamination/) CHamoru is the officially adopted spelling in Guam. This project was produced in collaboration with [The Margin](https://themargin.us/) and The War Horse._

Life felt peaceful when Robert Underwood was a child on Guam.

The small island in the western Pacific had survived three brutal years under Japanese occupation during World War II. But in the early 1950s, village life had a rhythm to it. Half the island’s population was still Indigenous CHamoru people, who trace their roots on the island back thousands of years. The U.S. military, which had been growing its presence on the island since American forces retook it from Japan in 1944, was there, too. But military folks had separate lives.

“They lived behind the fence. They shopped behind the fence,” Underwood said. “I grew up at a time when CHamoru was the language of the neighborhood.”

By the time Underwood—who would later serve as Guam’s delegate to Congress and as president of the University of Guam—graduated high school in 1965, things were changing. During his junior year at Tumon Junior-Senior High School—named for the district where it was located—the school became John F. Kennedy High School after the president’s assassination. The change reflected Guam’s growing connection to events unfolding thousands of miles away on the U.S. mainland.

Robert Underwood, Guam’s former congressional delegate, on the island this summer. Credit: Kent Velesrubio for The Margin

In the two decades after World War II, Guam’s population nearly quadrupled from prewar levels, driven in part by military personnel and Filipino construction workers who came to expand the island’s bases. In 1965, B-52 bombers began taking off from Guam on missions over Vietnam, and the island became a critical stop for refueling military ships and treating and transporting wounded service members evacuated from the war.

Guam has remained a military hub ever since, acting as a staging and refueling stop during wars in the Middle East. Thousands of service members and their families are permanently stationed there, and slowly but steadily, military activity became the primary force shaping the island.

“Whatever the military saw as threats became the guiding principle for life on Guam,” Underwood, who is now with the Pacific Center for Island Security, said.

Today, that threat is China—and the Pentagon is relying on Guam more than ever as a centerpiece of its Pacific strategy. The island is located 3,500 miles west of Hawaii, in range of Chinese missiles. Defense analysts say building up the island’s defensive—and increasingly, offensive—capabilities is critical preparation for a potential conflict. More than 5,000 Marines are expected to rotate to the island in the coming years, and last fall, the military signed off on constructing a new multilayered 360-degree missile defense system, spread across 16 sites on the island.

But activists and local leaders say Guam’s strained resources can’t support the surge in military activity without sustaining irreparable damage to the island’s fragile ecosystem. And while the military has promised to be mindful of local concerns, environmental advocates argue that decades of the Defense Department taking ancestral CHamoru land for its own use and leaving them with toxic Superfund sites have shown the Pentagon can’t be trusted to expand its presence there in a responsible way.

This article is the second in a two-part series, published by [_The War Horse_](https://thewarhorse.org/) and [_The Margin_](https://themargin.us/), examining how the U.S. military buildup on Guam is impacting the island’s environment, public health, Indigenous CHamoru communities, and military personnel. In part one, [we investigated the military’s legacy of toxic contamination on Guam](https://thewarhorse.org/guam-military-pesticide-contamination/). In this article, we examine the environmental impacts on the island as the military looks to counter China.

The Supreme Court in October will consider whether the Air Force complied with federal environmental law in a case centered on open-air detonation of munitions on Guam’s beaches. Through public records requests, _The War Horse_ and _The Margin_ have obtained previously unreleased letters and reports related to the Air Force’s open detonation practice in Guam and its relationship with environmental regulators.

Monaeka Flores—whose community organization, Prutehi Guåhan, is suing the Air Force in the case—says the case deals with only one of many environmental concerns related to the military.

“Now we have a firing range that’s going to be firing [millions of rounds] over our sole source aquifer,” she said. “We have the missile defense system, 16 sites identified, all of which have extensive, long-term military contamination that’s never been dealt with. All of these things are compounding.”

Guam is a U.S. territory, which means that its residents are American citizens but can’t vote for president, and its delegate to Congress cannot vote on the House floor. While billions of dollars in military funding flow to the island, Guam has struggled to maintain its power and water infrastructure. Roads and bridges, already strained by severe typhoons the island endures regularly, have been further damaged by heavy military trucks. The island faces a severe shortage of doctors and nurses. Although nearly 15% of Guam’s local population has served in the military—[Guam has the highest enlistment rate per capita in the United States](https://thewarhorse.org/military-veterans-from-us-territories-battle-for-va-benefits/)—veterans sometimes have to fly seven hours one-way to Hawaii to access care with the Department of Veterans Affairs. Local leaders have little leverage over the US military.

“Guam is politically always—not a junior partner, if a partner at all,” Underwood said. “It’s like you’re just somebody who gets the memo.”

## A Growing Military Footprint on Guam

The torpedo that sank the USS _Juneau_ was fired by a Japanese submarine.

It hit toward the back of the ship, throwing an enormous plume of water and debris high into the sky as the ship’s stern began to slip beneath the water. Not long after, the _Juneau_ came to rest on the ocean floor, 200 nautical miles off Guam’s coast.

The _Juneau_, an amphibious transport dock, had entered service in 1969, moving military equipment and forces during Vietnam and Desert Storm before retiring from the fleet in 2008. Her sinking came this summer during Operation Valiant Shield, a joint training exercise in the Pacific Ocean involving U.S., Japanese, and other allied forces.

The military touted the ship’s sinking—a SINKEX, in military parlance—as a valuable training exercise that brought together air, sea, and submarine assets to practice coordinated live-fire exercises in real-world conditions.

“This SINKEX provided an outstanding opportunity for our joint team to integrate capabilities across domains, honing the lethal precision and coordination essential for high-end maritime operations in the Pacific theater,” said Navy Rear Adm. Eric Anduze, then-commander of Carrier Strike Group 5, which took part in the exercise.

The USS Juneau lists after being hit by a torpedo in the Pacific Ocean during Operation Valiant Shield this summer. Credit: U.S. Navy photo by SN Anthony Vilardi

But for environmental advocates, the sinking was another instance of a military decision that quite literally shaped the landscape of their home without care for the long-term impact.

“They drop thousands of pounds of bombs and then they just let it sink,” Flores said. “And then they leave it there in the ocean.”

U.S. Pacific Command said the _Juneau_ was fully cleaned before the sinking, its toxic chemicals and petroleum residues removed, and that the site of the exercise was selected to minimize impacts to marine life. But Flores and others remain skeptical. And in any case, a massive joint military exercise like Operation Valiant Shield would be effectively impossible to stop—like so much of the military activity in the region.

“It’s so overwhelming,” Flores said. “You can feel so hopeless sometimes.”

The military has long shaped Guam, from its ecology and economy to the emotions of its inhabitants. Just hours after the Japanese attacked Pearl Harbor in 1941, warplanes took off from Saipan in the Northern Mariana Islands and began bombing Guam. Although the U.S. had been in control of the small Pacific island for more than 40 years after taking Guam from Spain in the Spanish-American War, it had done little to fortify its remote territory. The only military forces there at the dawn of America’s involvement in World War II were small Marine and naval units of just a few hundred people and a local CHamoru guard force. They were quickly overpowered by Japanese forces, which held the island for nearly three years.

A memorial with statues of American soldiers, sailors, and airmen, alongside Guam’s CHamoru Scouts and combat patrols. Credit: Kent Velesrubio for The Margin

After the U.S. military retook Guam in 1944, it was determined to never let anything similar happen again. Towards the war’s end, the Navy constructed massive airfields and supply depots, literally paving the way to a permanent militarization of the island.

Today, about a quarter of Guam is controlled by the military. Andersen Air Force Base and the Marine Corps’ Camp Blaz sit at the northern end of the island; Naval Base Guam is in the southwest. In between are scattered munitions and fuel storage facilities, communications stations, and military family housing.

“The reason that Guam was important in the 1600s for the Spanish was the same reason it was important for the United States when they got it from Spain in 1898, the same reason we fought so hard during the Marianas campaign to recapture Guam and support the strategic bombing effort in 1944, and it’s the reason that we really kind of prioritize it today,” said Carlton Haelig, a defense researcher at the Center for a New American Security.

“It is a logistics and forward deployment hub to project power from American territory deep into the Western Pacific,” he said.

That is increasingly true as military strategists look to China and the possibility that Beijing could move against Taiwan, the self-governing island it claims as its territory, potentially [this decade](https://media.defense.gov/2025/Apr/29/2003700710/-1/-1/1/FEATURE%20-%20MOORE%20DISCLAIMER.PDF). A conflict over Taiwan could draw in the United States, which has long provided the island with defensive weapons and maintained a strong relationship with Taipei. Taiwan is also an important trading partner with the U.S., which is committed to maintaining stability and open commerce across the Taiwan Strait.

In 2006, the Defense Department agreed to move 8,000 Marines from Okinawa, Japan, to Guam. The original impetus for the relocation was not particularly strategic—in 1995, three American service members kidnapped and raped a 12-year-old girl in Okinawa, unleashing a wave of popular anger, rooted in decades of protests over the American military presence, and pushing the Japanese government to demand a reduction in the U.S. footprint there.

But the Pentagon quickly realized that Guam offered benefits as China built up its military.

“It means that there will be Marines that are based on U.S. sovereign territory,” Haelig said. “We don’t have to do the political negotiations with allies and partners to put active fighting forces on their territory.”

But the Pentagon was unprepared for the local reaction when the military unveiled its plan to relocate Marines in 2009. Outrage on Guam was instantaneous. Locals worried about a potential rise in crime, echoing the frustration of Okinawa residents.

title: 香港人权组织在英国首相府前请愿 呼吁对BNO签证被拒港人特例处理
summary: 香港 — 多名香港人权组织成员星期一(9月28日)到英国首相府递交请愿信，呼吁英国当局协助因参与香港2019年反修例抗议遭定罪的香港人士，取得移居英国所需的签证。此前，有12名港人在申请英国国民海外护照BNO签证时遭到拒绝。 2020年《港版国安法》实施后，英国政府为香港的英国国民海外护照(BNO)持有人提供移民英国的途径，不过，过去两个月，至少有12名因参与2019年反修例运动被定罪的港人，遭到英国内政部拒绝批出BNO签证。 “蒲公英互助网络”(Dandelion Soli
content:
香港 —

多名香港人权组织成员星期一(9月28日)到英国首相府递交请愿信，呼吁英国当局协助因参与香港2019年反修例抗议遭定罪的香港人士，取得移居英国所需的签证。此前，有12名港人在申请英国国民海外护照BNO签证时遭到拒绝。

2020年《港版国安法》实施后，英国政府为香港的英国国民海外护照(BNO)持有人提供移民英国的途径，不过，过去两个月，至少有12名因参与2019年反修例运动被定罪的港人，遭到英国内政部拒绝批出BNO签证。

“蒲公英互助网络”(Dandelion Solidarity CIC)等多个港人劳工及人权组织，9月28日到英国伦敦唐宁街10号首相府递交请愿信。他们表示，受影响的港人是因为政治迫害而入狱，希望英国政府给予特例处理。

参与请愿的吴伟豪2019年因为在工作的仓库里藏有大量汽油，被以持有攻击性武器等罪名判刑五年，2023年获准假释。

去年6月，吴伟豪持英国国民(海外)护照(BNO)来到英国，寻求政治庇护，却遭到英国内政部拒绝。他在接受美国之音专访时回忆自己与内政部官员会晤的经历。

吴伟豪说：“(英国内政部)职员询问我被捕的经历，出狱后的生活，为何在香港受到迫害等等。他们的问题十分尖锐，似乎不相信我，似乎一直在推翻我受过的创伤。其实内政部可以从网路上搜寻到我的案子的资讯，完全没有必要重提这些我想避免的话题。”

**寻求庇护港人称不获英内政部信任**

吴伟豪说，他在香港监狱服刑期间曾多次被囚犯性侵，出狱后，每逢“六四”等敏感日子都受到身份不明人士严密监控，更一度尝试自寻短见。住院期间，香港惩教署人员曾扬言，若他无法适应社会，有可能会被安排重返监狱。他批评英国内政部在审批政治庇护申请时，没有充分考虑到他的遭遇。

吴伟豪说：“拒绝(政治庇护)的信中建议，假如我精神或心理状态出问题，可以到中国杭州的医院求医。我正申请上诉，若上诉失败，我会采取其他办法继续留在英国。我无法想象万一被遣返香港的后果，预计我会再次坐牢，这与送死没有分别。”

接受美国之音采访的“蒲公英互助网络”总监郭子健认为，吴伟豪申请政治庇护遭拒绝，反映英国当局并不理解香港的实况。

郭子健说：“英国内政部官员反复盘问这些受到政治迫害的人士，显示官员并不信任他们，让他们受到二次伤害。内政部必须认识到，不少在香港参与和平示威而无法获得公平审讯的人士都属于政治犯。现在的问题是，他们在香港坐了冤狱，到了英国仍要被行政部门阻挠。”

英媒《都市日报》(Metro)9月21日报道，自首相安迪伯纳姆今年7月上台以来，最少12名曾因参与2019年反修例示威而被香港法庭定罪判囚的港人，在申请BNO签证移居英国时，遭英国内政部拒绝。

**英国禁止向海外获刑一年以上人士发签证**

根据英国移民法的《适宜性条款》(Part Suitability)规定，若申请人在任何地区曾被判监或缓刑12个月以上，当局必须拒绝其签证申请，但相关规定不适用于在英国不构成犯罪行为的情况。

报道引述英国内政部回应说，无法评估这些不具名人士的说法是否属实，并提到，英国入境法例中涉及案底与其他有问题行为的规定，同样适用于BNO签证申请。

“蒲公英互助网络”总监郭子健表示，基于英国当局的规定，政治犯获批BNO签证几乎是不可能的事，而香港政治环境等因素往往被忽视。

郭子健说：“政治检控往往把暴动、非法集结、刑事毁坏、管有违禁品等不同罪名加诸当事人。即使当事人犯下与英国刑事法对应的罪名，并不代表香港的检控背景、证据基础与英国的情况相当。这往往牵涉到检控、定罪或判刑是否具有政治动机。”

英国内政部上月回复港人团体查询时表示，若申请人提出自身定罪涉及政治动机，审批人员会考虑相关证据及个案背景。

郭子健促请英国政府在审批签证、入籍的过程中，把涉及政治动机的定罪与真正的严重犯罪行为，区分开来,并设立专责审核及审查机制，以维持初衷，保护受政治迫害的港人。

美国之音向英国内政部发出电邮，查询当局会否把因反修例被定罪的港人视为特例？会否修订相关法规？对于无法使用BN0或其他正常途径入境的港人，会否另有人道安排？直到截稿为止，英国内政部尚未回复。

**学者：当局应专案处理**

英国自2023年底起，分阶段向享有免签证入境英国待遇的85个国家及地区民众推出ETA电子旅游许可制度。去年1月起，若没有有效居英签证，所有BNO和香港特区护照持有人都必须在入境英国前取得ETA电子旅游许可。有关政策实施两个月后，BNO护照持有人获得豁免。

身在英国的香港政治学者黄伟国对美国之音表示，不排除近期被拒发BNO签证的港人锐增，与英国扩大ETA的实施范围有关。

黄伟国说：“英国这项政策全面收紧有刑事案底人士的限制。任何人若有犯罪记录或曾经坐过牢，英国政府会直接拒绝他入境。ETA并非仅仅针对港人，而是面向全球多个国家。这很明显是英国国家安全或治安当局的要求。从最近一年多以来，香港涉及反修例人士申请BNO签证的审批情况看来，英国内政部似乎完全不清楚香港的情况。”

学者黄伟国说，BN0签证被视为港人的“救生艇”，英国当局有义务设立“专案”，确保政治犯也能顺利“上船”。

title: Spain plans stricter rules on asylum seekers in Ceuta, draft decree shows
