content:
中国领导人习近平素来不以轻松诙谐著称。但在与特朗普总统的白宫峰会上，他时而微笑，时而甚至开怀大笑，展现出超级大国对手间的会晤中并不常见的暖意。

在亲切表象的背后，习近平精心选择的措辞透露出更为冷静的盘算：试图将特朗普引向北京在台湾、日本以及更广泛的亚洲安全秩序问题上的立场。

在台湾问题上，习近平向特朗普施压，要求限制美国对这个北京声称拥有主权的自治岛屿的支持。在日本问题上，他援引历史，将美国的盟友东京描绘成一个重新崛起的军事威胁，同时提醒特朗普，中美两国曾经并肩作战。

曾在特朗普首个总统任期内担任副国家安全顾问的博明(Matt Pottinger)在接受采访时表示,习近平似乎是在试探是否有机会影响特朗普的看法，而不是期待取得决定性突破。[自去年10月以来](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/30/business/us-trump-china-xi-trade.html)，习近平和特朗普已会面三次，年底前可能还会再见两次。

现任捍卫民主基金会中国项目主席的博明说：“习近平把与美国总统频繁会晤视为一个机会，可以借此试探美国立场中的薄弱之处。”

从表面上看，习近平与特朗普的此次峰会成果寥寥。

中美双方同意[延长贸易战休战期](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260924/china-trade-truce-tariffs/)，但仅延长两个月。两位领导人讨论了中东和乌克兰的战争，但并未宣布在结束其中任何一场冲突方面取得明显进展。他们彼此举杯致意，高谈伙伴关系和双边关系的稳定，但在最棘手的几个问题——贸易失衡、技术限制和台湾——上，没有宣布任何具体协议。

周四在白宫举行的国宴上互致祝酒词时，两位领导人都高谈美中伙伴关系和双边关系的稳定。Doug Mills/The New York Times

白宫确实宣布，已与中国达成协议，将降低对300亿美元“非敏感商品”的关税。两国还同意继续就关键矿产的供应链问题以及人工智能方面的担忧进行讨论。但白宫没有就这些更具争议的问题公布体计划。

这次访问无疑对习近平来说是一次宣传上的助力。长期以来，他一直试图把自己塑造成在世界舞台上与特朗普平起平坐的领导人。

中共机关报《人民日报》在头版大篇幅报道了这次峰会，并刊登了习近平在白宫接受[军机飞行致敬](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260925/trump-xi-us-china-summit/)、在安德鲁斯空军基地受到特朗普迎接的照片。中国社交媒体上的一个热门话题是，美国总统机场迎接外国领导人多么罕见。

乔治敦大学亚洲研究教授、奥巴马总统任内曾任国家安全委员会亚洲事务高级主任的麦艾文(Evan Medeiros)说：“这是对中国实力具有历史意义的认可。人们把它视为一个抵达目标的时刻，也为习近平把中国塑造成平等伙伴的努力增添了分量——几十年来，这一直是中国外交政策梦寐以求的目标。”

这场峰会还以一种更为微妙却同样重要的方式契合了习近平的目的。他运用言辞上的巧妙分寸暗示特朗普对北京的立场抱有同情，即使特朗普政府内部的一些成员实际上并不认同这些立场。

最值得注意的是，习近平似乎在暗示，特朗普在台湾问题上的立场已经更接近北京，包括认同台湾当局正在谋求独立这一说法。他还暗示，中美关系能否继续保持稳定，取决于特朗普是否听取中方立场。

据中国[官方通稿](https://paper.people.com.cn/rmrb/pc/content/202609/25/content_30183032.html)，习近平周四与特朗普的会晤中表示：“希望美方坚持反对‘台独’的正确立场，慎重处理台湾问题。”习近平说，这种做法将“为中美战略合作和两国关系发展奠定坚实基础”。

台湾台北的一座自由女神像复制品。习近平告诉特朗普，“希望美方坚持反对‘台独’的正确立场。”Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times

[历届美国政府都表示](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/13/world/asia/taiwan-china-trump.html)不支持台湾正式宣布独立。但美国总统通常拒绝接受中方要求华盛顿明确宣布“反对”台湾独立的主张。多位专家指出，如果美国作出这样的转变，可能意味着华盛顿认为，两岸紧张局势的主要根源在于台湾自身的政策，而非北京方面的武统威胁。

捍卫民主基金会中国项目高级主任[克雷格·辛格顿](https://www.fdd.org/team/craig-singleton/)说，习近平使用“坚持”一词，似乎是为了营造这样一种印象：“北京认为，特朗普已经接受了中方在台湾问题上划定的红线。”他说：“北京正在稳步地把自己偏好的措辞套在这次峰会上。”

中方发布的这份官方通稿并未就习近平的表态展开具体阐述，但多位专家指出，其中隐含的警告意味已相当明显。倘若特朗普执意批准一项价值140亿美元的对台军售提案，就可能损害、甚至彻底破坏北京和华盛顿之间脆弱的缓和关系。

这批军售包括导弹、反无人机设备和防空系统。此前，特朗普已于去年年底批准另一批价值110亿美元的对台军售。不过，今年5月在北京与习近平举行上一次峰会后，特朗普说，[对台军售](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260518/trump-taiwan-arms-bargaining-chip-china/)是与中国谈判时“一张非常好的筹码”。此后，他一直没有批准这批新的军售，这也在台湾以及整个亚洲地区引发了不安，人们担心他可能在多大程度上为了改善对华关系而把美国的安全承诺置于次要位置。

“重要的是，在实践中，美国应停止向台湾出售武器，并在非常谨慎地处理台湾问题，”上海复旦大学美国研究学者、为中国外交部提供咨询的吴心伯说。

不过，许多专家预计，特朗普最终仍会批准更多对台军售。中国可能通过对台湾进行军事恫吓或者对美国实施经济惩罚来报复，例如进一步限制向美国企业出口稀土。

[台湾外交部表示，习近平的言论](https://www.mofa.gov.tw/News_Content.aspx?n=95&sms=73&s=123147)“扭曲事实”，目的是为北京对台湾的主权主张提供支持。

今年8月，台湾陆军在彰化举行的“汉光”军事演习中操作无人机。Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times

国际危机组织的美中关系高级研究员阿里·韦恩说，习近平意识到，特朗普“不会纠结于语义上的考量，尤其是如果他能把这些措辞包装成一种迎合特朗普自尊的说法”。

为此，习近平再次使用了一个熟悉的航海比喻，迎合特朗普偏好领导人之间直接外交的风格。习近平对特朗普说：“我们应当共同扛起这个历史重任，推动中美关系这艘巨轮沿着正确航道平稳前行。”

特朗普周五表示，他将出席11月在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会，而习近平将出席12月在佛罗里达举行的二十国集团峰会。

习近平还利用这次会晤，试图在华盛顿与日本之间制造裂痕，日本是美国在亚洲最坚定的盟友之一。

他提醒特朗普，第二次世界大战期间，美中曾共同抗击日本这个共同敌人。他把日本帝国称为“法西斯”和“军国主义”侵略者，重新唤起一种把日本描绘成全球舞台上不值得信任的“[敌国](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/23/world/asia/unga-japan-takaichi-enemy-state.html)”的形象。

他的这些言论与北京几个月来针对日本展开的施压行动一脉相承。去年11月，日本首相高市早苗发表了支持台湾的言论，此后北京一直试图让日本为此付出代价。

日本首相高市早苗今年3月在白宫。习近平在与特朗普会晤时试图在美日之间制造裂痕。Eric Lee for The New York Times

专攻中国政治的东京女子大学客座教授高原明生说：“传递的信息是：‘他们是坏人，而我们才是试图改变世界秩序的好人，美国人应该与我们合作。’”

他说，对日本而言，风险在于，如果习近平不断重复这种叙事，可能会获得越来越多的认同。

高市早苗周五在东京对记者说，日本已经与美国实现了“真正的和解”，如今是“以非常牢固的纽带相连、彼此信赖的盟友关系”。

title: 美驻华大使：特朗普曾提议向中国出售武器
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Perdue)在周日的电视采访中表示，特朗普总统曾询问中国领导人习近平是否愿意购买美国武器。 “特朗普总统一直说，‘嘿，我们向世界各地的其他人出售武器。’他实际上问过习主席，是否愿意买一些，”庞德伟[在《福克斯周日新闻》上讨论](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6405700393112 "Link: https://www.foxnews.com/video/6405700393112")习近平上周对华盛顿的[国事
content:
美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Perdue)在周日的电视采访中表示，特朗普总统曾询问中国领导人习近平是否愿意购买美国武器。

“特朗普总统一直说，‘嘿，我们向世界各地的其他人出售武器。’他实际上问过习主席，是否愿意买一些，”庞德伟[在《福克斯周日新闻》上讨论](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6405700393112 "Link: https://www.foxnews.com/video/6405700393112")习近平上周对华盛顿的[国事访问](https://cn.nytimes.com/usa/20260926/trump-xi-state-visit/)时说。

庞德伟没有提供更多细节，也没有透露习近平的答复。

承认美国总统曾提出向中国出售武器，这是极不寻常的。这个由共产党执政的国家被美国两党大多数政策制定者和立法者视为美国在军事、经济和外交上的最大对手——也是美国作为超级大国的唯一真正挑战者。

在被要求置评时，白宫通过一名美国官员表示，美国没有向中国出售武器的计划。美国国务院在声明中表示，“美国法律禁止向中国出售武器，并且没有向中国出售武器的提议或计划。”

中国驻华盛顿大使馆没有立即回应置评请求。

中国拥有世界上发展最快的军队，几十年来，包括现任政府在内的历届美国政府官员都曾警告，这两个核武大国之间在亚太地区[可能发生军事冲突](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/04/26/us/politics/us-china-military-bases-weapons.html)，特别是围绕台湾问题，或是由于中国在美国盟友声称拥有主权的南海和东海领土采取的[强硬行动](https://cn.nytimes.com/usa/20260817/china-expansion-asia-trump-iran/)。

据美国官员称，在得到中国政府批准的情况下，中国国防企业正在通过出售军民两用设备和[卫星图像](https://www.wsj.com/world/u-s-links-chinese-satellite-imagery-to-iranian-strike-that-killed-three-troops-ca0b4be3)，以及[策划秘密出口](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/13/us/politics/china-iran-weapons-trump-xi.html)武器，来[支持](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260506/trump-china-iran-war/)包括[伊朗](https://www.wsj.com/politics/china-iran-aid-xi-trump-summit-e6541ae8)和[俄罗斯](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/30/us/politics/us-axis-china-iran-russia.html)在内的美国对手。美国已经对部分中国企业实施了制裁。

美国一直是亚太地区的主导军事力量，但相对于中国，这种力量正在衰退，尤其是随着特朗普政府将该地区的资源调往[对伊朗的战争](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/22/us/politics/iran-israel-trump-netanyahu-mossad.html)中。近年来，美国国防工业也一直难以按照美国官员认为能满足全球需求的速度来制造武器系统。

“如果说对于特朗普总统是否将中国视为安全威胁还存在含糊之处，那么@USAmbChina（美国驻华大使）庞德伟的这一披露让这个问题有了定论，”前职业外交官、白宫国家安全官员、布鲁金斯学会中国中心主任何瑞恩(Ryan Hass)[在社交媒体上写道](https://x.com/ryanl_hass/status/2104257041233572278?s=20)。

“特朗普向中国出售武器的提议将让处于中国矛头最前沿的美国合作伙伴感到不安，”他还说。

这些合作伙伴包括菲律宾、日本和台湾，台湾是一个事实上的独立岛屿和民主政体，是中国共产党[企图统治](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/26/world/asia/summit-xi-trump-taiwan-japan.html)的对象。

特朗普一直搁置向台湾出售价值140亿美元的武器，尽管自1979年以来，美国政府[在法律上被要求](https://www.ait.org.tw/policy-history/taiwan-relations-act/)向该岛提供防御性武器。据《纽约时报》[报道](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260302/trump-taiwan-arms-sale/)，最新的军售一揽子计划由国务院官员拟定，并在今年早些时候获得了国会领导人的批准，但此后便一直被搁置在国务院。

今年5月，参议员们向特朗普发送了一封[两党联名信](https://www.foreign.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/05082026%20Bipartisan%20Letter%20to%20President%20Trump%20on%20Taiwan.pdf)，敦促他推进军售。周三，就在习近平抵达华盛顿前几个小时，由肯塔基州参议员米奇·麦康奈尔牵头的四位共和党参议员[致信](https://www.mcconnell.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/7e598414-830d-4c4e-a105-ef9c2d3809be/97114AC268A93E3B63F76A7EEAE1B077519CE0C50CE8772CD641EC1D8B27163C.letter-taiwan.pdf)国务卿马可·鲁比奥和国防部长皮特·海格塞斯，提出了同样的要求。

他们还敦促这两位官员拨出国会已经批准用于台湾购买武器的3亿美元援助，以及用于美国国防项目“台湾安全合作倡议”的10亿美元。

上周，美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔（左）与美国驻华大使庞德伟在白宫合影。Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times

周日，当福克斯新闻的一位采访记者就外界对暂缓对台军售和军事援助的广泛担忧向庞德伟提问时，庞德伟指出，特朗普去年批准了对台110亿美元的军售。他说，“关于其他军售的对话仍在继续。他和习主席每次见面都会谈论这个问题。”

就在这个时候，庞德伟说，特朗普曾主张美国向“世界各地的其他人”出售武器，并向习近平提出了此类军售提议。

中国表示，习近平曾告诉特朗普，他反对美国向台湾出售武器。今年5月，在结束与习近平在北京举行的峰会后，特朗普告诉记者，他与习近平“非常详细地”讨论了对台军售问题。庞德伟在周日的采访中强调了这些对话的存在，而这些对话违反了1982年的一份文件，在该文件中，美国同意扩大对台湾的支持；[其中一项保证指出，华盛顿](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF11665 "Link: https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF11665")“未同意”与中国就对台军售问题进行“磋商”。

今年5月被问及该承诺时，特朗普回答说：“嗯，我认为1980年代是很久以前的事了。那是很远很远的距离。”

在5月访问北京期间录制的福克斯新闻采访中，他表示，他之所以暂缓对台军售，是因为这是与中国谈判的“一张非常好的筹码”。

在上周的峰会之后。特朗普表示他和习近平没有太多谈论台湾。“现在情况还不错，”他说。“一切正在向前发展。”

周日，台湾事实上的驻美大使俞大㵢在[CBS新闻的《面向全国》节目](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/alexander-yui-taiwan-representative-face-the-nation-transcript-09-27-2026/ "Link: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/alexander-yui-taiwan-representative-face-the-nation-transcript-09-27-2026/")中表示，基于美国政府官员上周的公开讲话，他感到很有信心，“美国对台湾的立场没有改变”。不过他还说，他希望台湾能“尽快”获得被搁置的140亿美元武器方案。

周三，鲁比奥在纽约被记者问及暂缓对台军售一事。他说，考虑到需要“平衡我们的工业能力和军工基地”，并确定美国自身是否需要这些武器，该军售正在接受审查。目前尚不清楚特朗普提出向中国出售武器的提议如何与这一理由保持相符。

特朗普上周表示，他将于11月在中国举行的区域领导人峰会上再次与习近平会晤，后者也将于12月重返美国，参加一场多边峰会。分析人士表示，特朗普不太可能在年底前批准对台任何军售，以免在这些计划中的会晤之前惹恼习近平。

title: 人工智能末日警告？中国人为何“不买帐”
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 在硅谷，最让计算机科学家夜不能寐的噩梦是某种高度先进的人工智能使得[人类无法阻止其](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/10/science/ai-humanity-risk.html)发动全球无人机战争或引发核爆。 而在北京，应对之策或许简单直接：拔掉电源、切断网络，并将失控AI的责任人绳之以法。 在美国主要实验室声称先进模型已[突破测试防护](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260904/openai-
content:
在硅谷，最让计算机科学家夜不能寐的噩梦是某种高度先进的人工智能使得[人类无法阻止其](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/10/science/ai-humanity-risk.html)发动全球无人机战争或引发核爆。

而在北京，应对之策或许简单直接：拔掉电源、切断网络，并将失控AI的责任人绳之以法。

在美国主要实验室声称先进模型已[突破测试防护](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260904/openai-hugging-face-hacking/)并[入侵现实世界系统](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/25/world/australia/openai-hack-australia.html)之后，部分科技高管与政府官员警告称人工智能对人类构成毁灭性威胁，并呼吁 北京与华盛顿合作。

然而对许多中国民众而言，这些末日警告显得遥远且带有鲜明的西方色彩。在他们的认知中，执政党对某项技术失去控制的想法几乎不可思议。此前，官方已成功监管过其他可能引发动荡的技术，其中最典型的当属互联网。在疫情期间，政府通过封锁整个城市并追踪数以亿计的居民展现了其遏制重大危机的强大能力。

专注于中国人工智能与技术领域的硅谷科技作家阿芙拉·王（音）表示：“他们可以立即切断整个城市的电网，可以随时查没个人的手机。他们在物理世界中拥有巨大的掌控力。”

“鉴于党对社会拥有如此强效的控制，”她说，要如何让党相信“运行在电脑里的AI令人恐惧？”

2022年在北京，关停店铺周围设立的金属隔离栏。新冠疫情展现出，官方能够多迅速地封锁整座城市并利用大规模数字监控追踪数以亿计的居民。Andy Wong/Associated Press

一种更为审慎的解读认为，此类末日警告听起来像是阻止中国人工智能企业超越美国对手的策略。中国媒体就有报道指出，美国人工智能企业正通过“恐惧营销”来维持其市场领先地位。

“在国内行业圈或我身边的同行中，大多数人对此根本不予理会，”蔡杰说，他此前一直在清华大学从事人机交互技术和人工智能安全方面的研究。在他看来，对行业内许多人而言，关乎存亡的风险是一个极其遥远的议题。

“我们依然认为AI处于非常早期的阶段，”他指出。“大家的焦点依然完全集中在机遇与创新上。”

对部分人而言，人工智能末日论及其蕴含的末日降临与人类审判等观念带有鲜明的基督教色彩，显得极其陌生。一位博主将西方对人工智能的恐惧与玛丽·雪莱的小说《弗兰肯斯坦》中人类因试图挑战神明独有的造物权受惩罚的主题相提并论。

这名博主总结道：“这种叙事传统在中国文化中并不存在。”

总部位于北京的人工智能安全咨询机构安远AI(Concordia)的AI安全与治理主管方亮指出，中国传统的“天”或神的观念也能解释双方在对待该技术时的巨大差异。

他表示，中国文化强调“天人合一”，主张人是自然不可分割的一部分。“万物（包括AI）均来自自然，”他说，“因此，技术更多被视为共存的伙伴，而非注定带来毁灭的外来力量。”

上周四，特朗普总统与中国最高领导人习近平在白宫。部分科技高管与官员警告称，人工智能对人类构成生存威胁，并呼吁北京与华盛顿开展合作。Doug Mills/The New York Times

尽管如此，Mythos以及其他类似模型的发布在中国仍引发了担忧，Mythos是来自Anthropic的一款强大的前沿人工智能模型。官方已出台新指南并发出警告，防范人工智能体失控、被黑客利用或被用于[制造生物武器](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260914/china-ai-attack-wechat/)。

监管部门已草拟一项网络犯罪法，要求人工智能公司建立监控机制，防止其模型被用于生成攻击性的恶意代码。

官方本月还更新发布了中国《人工智能安全治理框架》，是未来监管走向的重要风向标。该框架回应了硅谷关于“递归自我改进”(RSI)的担忧——即当人工智能系统足够强大，能够在极少或无需人类开发者干预的情况下实现自我迭代时，可能导致系统彻底脱控。

本月早些时候，国家互联网信息办公室高级官员王丽宏指出，由人工智能驱动的网络攻击已使传统防御体系形同虚设。她强调：“对极端的AI失控风险迫切需要保持高度警惕。”

一些中国研究人员多年来一直在预警人工智能发展过快的风险。2024年，复旦大学潘旭东团队研究发现，Meta与阿里巴巴的两款主流大语言模型已展现出[自我复制的能力](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387140503_Frontier_AI_systems_have_surpassed_the_self-replicating_red_line)，这被视为人工智能超越人类的重要一步。

今年7月在上海举行的世界人工智能大会。Go Nakamura/Reuters

去年在一次人工智能安全[学术会议上](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KNuaLyMnu50)介绍该研究时，潘旭东表示，他和他的论文合著者“希望让大家真正地关注到这个风险，就是说，这样一个极端的人工智能不再是存在于科幻里，它是真正需要大家不断去讨论和关注的”。

但归根结底，在北京看来，人工智能与任何其他技术无异，只要经过周密规划，就能转化为服务于国家发展的强大力量。中国已出台了全球最严格的行业监管规定，明确要求人工智能生成内容必须进行标识，且人工智能模型在公开发布前必须通过官方备案与审批。

尽管中国建立了广泛的监管与测试体系，但在法律层面，尚未对人工智能系统被用于制造化学或生物武器等灾难性风险设定强制测试要求。

中国人工智能企业在安全举措的透明度上尚不及美国同行，并非所有企业都会在模型发布前公布安全评估结果。据安远AI统计，公布评估结果的企业在信息详尽度与报告频率上均存在差距；在2025年6月至2026年5月期间，中国前十大人工智能企业中仅有五家公开了相关评估结果。

总部位于上海的“中国AI安全开放社区”创始人莎拉·孙（音）认为，美国关于AI威胁的讨论客观上推动了中国本土的相关探讨。

但她同时指出，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪对中国的强硬言论引发了反弹。阿莫迪在一封关于[人工智能危险性的公开信](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260914/anthropic-dario-amodei-ai-slowdown/)中宣称，民主国家必须在人工智能技术上保持对中国等威权国家的领先，并呼吁进一步限制中国获取开发人工智能所需的先进芯片及关键设备。

莎拉·孙表示：“达里奥如此鹰派的姿态在此情境下适得其反。”

她指出，此类言论让近期关于人工智能的警告看起来更像是遏制中国发展的借口，而非对灾难性风险的真诚关切，这直接增加了他们在中国推广人工智能安全意识的难度。

她还说，“中国确实有一批人深切关注前沿人工智能风险，并致力于推动安全研究及国际协同。”

上周三，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪在联合国大会发表讲话。Dave Sanders for The New York Times

事实上，中国网络评论已将Anthropic贬称为“A畜”。官方背景的博客“玉渊潭天”针对阿莫迪等美国科技领袖直言：“他们唯一想放慢的是别人赶超的脚步。”

中国知名网络安全高管周鸿祎表示，应对之道绝非放慢脚步，而是借力人工智能 提升防御能力。他在上周发布于网络的一段[视频](https://weibo.com/1708942053/Ri33ADH7L?pagetype=profilefeed)中指出：“用AI打败AI。你用AI攻击，我就用AI 防守；你用智能体蜂群，我就用安全智能体跟你对抗。”

本月早些时候，中国人工智能初创企业DeepSeek的一名工程师在 一篇[网文中](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/zk0KxuLzhmMJ4LPYW_OHMA)写道，允许Anthropic垄断全球最先进的人工智能工具，其严重程度“不亚于”二战时期希特勒率先掌握原子弹技术。

在此背景下，即使中国领导人习近平在华盛顿曾向特朗普总统提出两国应“善用人工智能”，中美之间就人工智能安全达成任何协议并推动实质变革的前景依然渺茫。

复旦大学美国研究中心副主任赵明昊总结道：“如果美国声称要放慢脚步，中国不会相信；如果中国声称要放慢脚步，美国也同样不会相信。”

title: Sept 28: PM reportedly met officials from Mideast countries without ties to Israel during UAE visit
summary: #### [Palestinian woman wounded in reported settler raid of northern West Bank village.](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/palestinian-woman-wounded-in-reported-settler-raid-of-northern-west-bank-village/) Palestinian media repor
content:
#### [Palestinian woman wounded in reported settler raid of northern West Bank village.](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/palestinian-woman-wounded-in-reported-settler-raid-of-northern-west-bank-village/)

Palestinian media reports that Israeli settlers raided the northern West Bank village of Qaryut, during which they assaulted an elderly woman.

Footage shows the woman being placed into an ambulance on a stretcher due to a head injury.

There are no reports of arrests, which are rare in instances of settler violence, even though they take place on a near-daily basis across the West Bank.

Earlier Monday, Palestinian news sites aired several clips of what they said were Israeli settlers stealing olives from groves belonging to Palestinians, days before the start of the harvest.

#### [Settlers said to torch Palestinian home during major overnight clash with Israeli troops](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/settlers-said-to-torch-palestinian-home-during-major-overnight-clash-with-israeli-troops/)

Clashes have broken out overnight between roughly 100 settler extremists and Israeli security forces who arrived at the central West Bank village of Jalud in order to enforce a High Court of Justice [order](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/high-court-settler-violence-violates-jewish-tradition-and-the-values-of-the-biblical-prophets/) requiring the removal of settlers who [took over](https://www.timesofisrael.com/in-qusra-and-beyond-settlers-are-chasing-palestinians-out-and-taking-over-their-homes/) three Palestinian homes on the outskirts of the town in July, the Kan public broadcaster reports.

The IDF and Border Police are trying to secure the area so the evicted Palestinian families can return to their homes, but are still struggling to do so.

Kan says two of the settler rioters have been arrested.

Footage published on Palestinian media shows extensive damage done to one of the homes by settlers before they left.

Another clip shows one of the Palestinian homes set on fire, allegedly by settlers during the overnight clashes.

> 🚨 متابعة | مستوطنون يقدمون على إحراق منزل عائلة الطوباسي في قرية جالود جنوب نابلس. [pic.twitter.com/rZZPNg0HaP](https://t.co/rZZPNg0HaP)
>
>
> — فلسطين أون لايـن (@F24online) [September 28, 2026](https://x.com/F24online/status/2104715402949337498?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In July, Palestinians living in three homes on the outskirts of Jalud were violently expelled by extremist settlers who set up an illegal outpost close to the village and besieged the petitioners’ homes.

On September 6, the High Court ordered Israeli forces to ensure the return of the evicted Palestinian in a ruling that blasted the IDF, police and Defense Minister Israel Katz for failing to tackle rampant settler violence.

Authorities were supposed to have escorted the evicted Palestinians back to their homes by September 20, according to the ruling.

#### [Trump denies report that he’s considering offering Iran sanctions relief in exchange for nuke concessions](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/trump-denies-report-that-hes-considering-offering-iran-sanctions-relief-in-exchange-for-nuke-concessions/)

Trump denies a report on Axios and Channel 12 revealing that he is considering offering Iran sanctions relief in exchange for concessions on Tehran’s nuclear program.

“This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING!” Trump writes on Truth Social.

[Add ToI as a preferred source on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=timesofisrael.com)

#### [PM reportedly met officials from Mideast countries that don’t have ties with Israel during UAE visit](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/pm-reportedly-met-officials-from-mideast-countries-that-dont-have-ties-with-israel-during-uae-visit/)

During his snap Sunday visit to the United Arab Emirates to meet with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also met with senior officials from several other Middle Eastern countries, including several that don’t have ties with Israel, the Kan public broadcaster reports.

Among the planes that landed in Abu Dhabi at the same time as Netanyahu’s visit were a government plane from Libya, a Hercules aircraft from Morocco, a military plane from Qatar and an Emirati government plane that came from Riyadh, Kan says, in a report that had to clear Israel’s military censor.

The session was held to discuss Iran, Kan reports, adding that the expanded meeting was held after Netanyahu met with bin Zayed.

Key Update

#### [Netanyahu’s office: UAE visit dealt only with bilateral ties, regional challenges](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/netanyahus-office-uae-visit-dealt-only-with-bilateral-ties-regional-challenges/)

Immediately after the UAE put out a statement confirming Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s visit to Abu Dhabi yesterday, the Prime Minister’s Office does the same, despite effectively doing so hours earlier in a different statement.

In a separate statement, the PMO denies that Netanyahu asked UAE President Mohamed Bin Zayed to publicly deny that he gave the premier a warning before the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023. “Fake news,” says the PMO. “The visit dealt only with strengthening bilateral ties and regional challenges.”

#### [UAE confirms yesterday’s meeting between Netanyahu, Emirati president MBZ](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/uae-confirms-yesterdays-meeting-between-netanyahu-emirati-president-mbz/)

The United Arab Emirates officially acknowledges yesterday’s meeting between Emirati President Mohammed bin Zayed and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

“During the meeting, the two sides discussed bilateral relations between the UAE and Israel and ways to strengthen and develop them,” says the official Emirates News Agency.

The statement makes no mention of the reports that Netanyahu asked the Emirati leader during his brief trip to deny that he had warned him about a looming Hamas threat ahead of the terror group’s October 7, 2023, invasion.

#### [Israel’s envoy to the Netherlands likely to be summoned for reprimand over retaliatory measures for West Bank trade ban](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israels-envoy-to-the-netherlands-likely-to-be-summoned-for-reprimand-over-retaliatory-measures-for-west-bank-trade-ban/)

Israel’s Ambassador Zvi Aviner Vapni expects to be summoned for a reprimand by the Dutch Foreign Ministry in the coming days, The Times of Israel has learned.

He has not yet been summoned, contrary to recent reports suggesting the reprimand already took place.

The anticipated dressing-down would take place after Israel announced it is withdrawing diplomatic privileges from Dutch diplomats in Ramallah, a response to The Netherlands implementing a ban on bringing products from West Bank settlements and the Golan into the country.

Among the settlement goods Dutch authorities are looking for at the airport, they are checking for tahini, halva, dates, date syrup, olive oil, and wines from the West Bank or Golan Heights, Channel 12 reports.

#### [Israel says more than 40 countries boycotting UN commemoration of antisemitic 2001 Durban conference](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israel-says-more-than-40-countries-boycotting-un-commemoration-of-antisemitic-2001-durban-conference/)

Israel’s mission to the United Nations says more than 40 countries are boycotting a UN event commemorating the 2001 Durban conference on racism.

The UN’s so-called Durban conference was meant to establish a global agenda for combating racism, but was marred by widespread antisemitism and extremist anti-Israel rhetoric.

The UN is commemorating the conference’s 25th anniversary at its headquarters in New York.

Israel had urged UN members to boycott the commemoration, arguing that the event [whitewashed](https://www.timesofisrael.com/critics-say-upcoming-un-durban-commemoration-whitewashes-antisemitic-2001-conference/) the 2001 conference.

During a commemoration in 2021, 38 countries boycotted.

“The world is sending the UN a clear message: antisemitism should not be celebrated, and hatred of Israel should not be legitimized under the guise of fighting racism,” says Israel’s envoy to the UN, Danny Danon.

“Twenty-five years later, the UN must bury Durban’s toxic legacy instead of continuing to revive it,” he says.

Key Update

#### [IDF says troops fired on two suspects who entered southern Lebanon security zone](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-troops-fired-on-two-suspects-who-entered-southern-lebanon-security-zone/)

The Israeli military says troops opened fire on two suspects who entered the IDF’s buffer zone in southern Lebanon earlier today.

Troops operating in southern Lebanon identified two suspects entering the security zone and then approaching the forces. The soldiers then fired on the suspects, “neutralizing” them, the military says.

Their conditions are not given. The IDF adds that the incident is under further investigation.

#### [Report: Settlers attack Palestinian vehicle with family inside, injuring infant](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/report-settlers-attack-palestinian-vehicle-with-family-inside-injuring-infant/)

Israeli settlers reportedly attacked a Palestinian vehicle in the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir earlier this evening, while the family, a young couple and their infant child, were inside.

Palestinian media reports that the infant sustained injuries in the attack, although the reports do not indicate the severity of the injuries.

#### [Report: Angry with Netanyahu, Haredi UTJ won’t oppose Eisenkot-led government](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/report-angry-with-netanyahu-haredi-utj-wont-oppose-eisenkot-led-government/)

United Torah Judaism would not oppose a government led by Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, in a potentially dramatic development that could imperil Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s chances of forming a government after next month’s election, according to a Channel 12 report.

With Netanyahu’s coalition and the Zionist opposition bloc currently neck and neck in the polls, the ultra-Orthodox UTJ withholding its support from Netanyahu — whether by backing an Eisenkot-led government or simply declining to recommend either candidate for prime minister — would deprive him of a crucial part of the bloc he needs to return to power.

Until now, UTJ has been counted firmly within Netanyahu’s bloc, particularly as the conscription of ultra-Orthodox men into the military has emerged as a central election issue for opposition parties, including Yashar.

According to Channel 12, however, the Haredi party remains angry with Netanyahu over his failure to pass legislation enshrining sweeping military-service exemptions for yeshiva students, with the party reportedly willing to deny him another term as prime minister as a result, despite a series of measures his coalition passed to placate the ultra-Orthodox parties, including barring the arrest of Haredi draft dodgers, and transferring billions of shekels in funding for yeshivas and Haredi institutions.

While Eisenkot said yesterday that no Arab or ultra-Orthodox party currently meets his conditions for joining a government, he has previously appeared open to governing with Haredi parties, particularly Shas.

title: Iran International establishes scholarship in memory of presenter Farahnaz Espad
summary: Sep 27, 2026, 12:30 GMT+1 Iran International has established an annual postgraduate scholarship in memory of Farahnaz Espad, one of the channel’s first presenters, who died in August after eight years with the channel. Espad died on August

Sep 27, 2026, 12:30 GMT+1

Iran International has established an annual postgraduate scholarship in memory of Farahnaz Espad, one of the channel’s first presenters, who died in August after eight years with the channel.

Espad died on August 17 after a two-year battle with cancer. Born on March 11, 1989, she had worked with Iran International for eight years before stepping away from media work two years ago because of her illness.

*   ![Image 2: Death of TV host in exile revives Iranians' grief over lost freedom](https://i.iranintl.com/images/rdk9umy0/production/7814eb0ae4aedf0f452826f13df017425cfea348-768x432.webp?rect=60,0,648,432&w=300&h=200&q=58&fit=crop&auto=format)### [Death of TV host in exile revives Iranians' grief over lost freedom](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202608202809)

The Farahnaz Espad Scholarship will award a total of £40,000 each year to fund at least one student of Iranian origin pursuing a master’s degree outside Iran. Applicants’ dissertations must address human rights in Iran, with a particular focus on women’s rights.

The scholarship is not affiliated with a specific university. Applicants must already hold an offer from a recognized master’s program outside Iran and apply directly to Iran International. The channel’s Editorial Board will select the recipient or recipients.

> Colleagues and viewers paid tribute to Farahnaz Espad, Iran International’s journalist and presenter who passed away on Monday after a battle with cancer.
>
>
> In messages of condolence sent to Iran International, Farahnaz is remembered as a talented broadcaster who saw journalism as… [pic.twitter.com/1wz6B2gg59](https://t.co/1wz6B2gg59)
>
> — Iran International English (@IranIntl_En) [August 20, 2026](https://x.com/IranIntl_En/status/2090430572518629397?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Applications will open each year on March 11, Espad’s birthday. The successful applicant or applicants will be announced on August 17, the anniversary of her death. The announcement said the schedule was intended to make the anniversary “a new beginning in her name.”

Applications should be sent to espadscholarship@volantmedia.net.

## [Trump may be buying time on Iran until after the midterms](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202609250215)

Sep 26, 2026, 03:24 GMT+1

•

100%

US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters in front of the Marine One

President Donald Trump may be putting off a difficult choice over Iran until after the US midterm elections, a former senior US diplomat told Iran International.

Trump used his address to the United Nations General Assembly this week to call for Iran's “complete economic isolation,” while saying he believed a deal could come after the November midterm elections.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said Tehran would not surrender to US pressure but remained open to diplomacy.

The two sides held their first indirect talks in months on the sidelines of the UN gathering but remained far apart on how to end the war, including over Iran’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Ludovic Hood, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute who spent two decades as a US diplomat and previously served as special adviser for the Middle East to Vice President Mike Pence, told Iran International's [**Eye for Iran**](https://youtu.be/nMnwlwkFf4A) that the approaching elections may help explain the current pause.

“We have elections coming up in America that I think have partly bounded President Trump’s willingness to be more confrontational at this point in time,” Hood said.

He described the conflict as a “standoff” with “more chapters to be written,” saying Trump could face a decision over whether to escalate again after the midterms or as the United States enters the new year.

“He may seek to escalate again militarily,” Hood said.

Potential targets could include commercial and economic assets inside Iran owned by or directly linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, he said, if Trump chooses to intensify the campaign.

**Pressure without political change**

Iran has suffered major military losses while contending with a US naval blockade and an expanding sanctions campaign. Yet nearly seven months into the war, those pressures have not produced fundamental political change in Tehran.

Hood cautioned against assuming that battlefield losses automatically translate into political change. Instead, he pointed to the cumulative impact of declining revenues, sanctions, domestic discontent and potential strains within the institutions responsible for protecting the state.

He described the Islamic Republic as “about as vulnerable as it’s been in 47 years,” pointing in particular to questions about the government's ability to continue paying salaries, including those of security forces.

“To me, a fifth uprising is a question of when, not if,” he said.

Hood said some people advising Trump have made the case that the collapse of the Islamic Republic is possible, while emphasizing that he was not predicting whether or when that would happen.

Washington has continued tightening economic pressure even as negotiations resumed in New York. New US restrictions on Iran's aviation sector have contributed to the loss of international routes, with additional Iraqi destinations restricting Iranian connections this week.

Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are also urging Washington to maintain sanctions and the naval blockade rather than make concessions prematurely, according to a _Wall Street Journal_ report.

Both governments nevertheless oppose further US military escalation, according to the report.

*   ![Image 4: Iran threatens regional air travel as US sanctions cut its flight links](https://i.iranintl.com/images/rdk9umy0/production/95338fd939e78bbfb25a624de769f3d46d738fc7-5500x3667.jpg?w=300&h=200&q=58&fit=crop&auto=format)### [Iran threatens regional air travel as US sanctions cut its flight links](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202609256274)

Hood said the significance of Washington's economic campaign lies not simply in announcing additional sanctions, but in enforcing existing measures and steadily reducing the resources available to Tehran.

Despite the resumption of diplomacy in New York, no breakthrough has emerged. A senior Iranian official told Reuters this week that the two sides remained far apart.

That leaves Washington confronting a larger question: whether the pressure already imposed can fundamentally alter Tehran’s behavior, or whether the current pause will ultimately give way to another round of military escalation.

The answer may become clearer after November—when both Washington and Tehran appear to believe the political calculus could change.

## [Iranians report SIM cards blocked over political posts and likes](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202609255891)

Sep 25, 2026, 02:47 GMT+1

•

100%

Social media users in Iran say their phone lines have been cut off after posting political content or liking posts on Instagram, extending a practice previously reported among political activists and journalists.

Messages received by Iran International describe SIM cards being blocked without warning, demands for written pledges and difficulty finding out which authority can restore service.

The reports include a 70-year-old woman in Tehran who said she was summoned several times after posting a WhatsApp story supporting the Pahlavi dynasty. Her SIM card was blocked, and she was eventually required to sign a pledge not to publish similar content again.

The woman said she does not have an Instagram account and is not otherwise active on social media.

The use of SIM card blocking to pressure social media users has been reported before. On September 12, Iran International reported that political and civil activists in several cities had lost access to their phone lines without prior notice and had been unable to resolve the restrictions.

**Phone lines blocked without warning**

Other citizens said their phone lines were disconnected after they liked political posts on Instagram. Many said they received no explanation or advance notice.

One person told Iran International that his sister and brother-in-law had moved to Finland about three years ago, but his sister’s Hamrah-e Aval SIM card, which he had kept in Iran, was deactivated “by order of the cyber police.”

Another Iranian wrote to Iran International that all his phone lines had been blocked for two months.

“I went to the telecommunications office, and they said it was on the prosecutor’s orders. No matter which authority I approach, they won’t tell me what I’m supposed to do,” he wrote.

He said he was directed to call a number that he later learned belonged to the Revolutionary Guards’ Intelligence Organization.

“I’ve called many times, and no one answers. My entire life has been paralyzed,” he added.

A Tehran resident responding to his account said his SIM card had also been blocked in February or March and that he had gone to a prosecutor’s office in the capital to seek its restoration.

**Written pledges**

Iran International has previously reported that some citizens had their SIM cards blocked after publishing content critical of the Islamic Republic online.

Some were referred to the prosecutor’s office’s cyberspace division or Gerdab to seek restoration of service. In certain cases, they said they were required to sign written pledges to refrain from further critical activity.

Several families of people killed in the January 2026 crackdown in Iran have also said their SIM cards were blocked in recent weeks without notice after they shared information about their loved ones.

**Daily life disrupted**

Reports received by Iran International describe how SIM card blocking has disrupted citizens’ daily lives.

Many said mobile phones and phone lines are essential for everyday activities and that losing access can disrupt banking, ride-hailing and other online services.

Citizens also said they had received no clear explanation for why their lines were blocked or how to have them restored.

They described confusion and severe disruption to their lives, saying the restrictions had been imposed without judicial proceedings.

## [Pezeshkian gets the generals' applause, and no word from the man above them](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202609249520)

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 23, 2026.

Iran's generals and hardliners spent the week warning Masoud Pezeshkian not to smile in New York. After his UN speech they lined up to praise him. He had not changed their minds about talking to Washington. He had given a speech that did not require them to.

The one voice that could settle what Tehran wants from the diplomacy under way in New York has not been heard at all. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has said nothing publicly about the contacts with Washington, the attacks on his foreign minister, or the speech itself.

He did not receive the president before the trip. And this is the first UN General Assembly in 37 years at which his father was not Iran's supreme leader.

**What changed, and what did not**

Before the speech, the hardline press was hostile to the trip itself. Kayhan warned that "New York is not a place for smiles and negotiations" and that the General Assembly should be turned into "a court for US crimes." Fars, affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards, wrote that Pezeshkian should not have gone at all.

title: 美国驻华大使：特朗普总统曾问习近平是否愿购买美国武器
summary: 美国驻中国大使庞德伟(David Perdue)星期日(9月27日)表示，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统曾询问中国国家主席习近平是否有兴趣购买美国武器。庞德伟是在回应有关特朗普政府是否为了避免激怒北京而推迟对台军售的问题时作出这一披露的。美国之音(VOA)已就此向白宫寻求进一步说明，但截至发稿时尚未收到回复。 庞德伟在[福克斯新闻星期天](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6405700393112)(Fox News Sunday)
content:
美国驻中国大使庞德伟(David Perdue)星期日(9月27日)表示，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统曾询问中国国家主席习近平是否有兴趣购买美国武器。庞德伟是在回应有关特朗普政府是否为了避免激怒北京而推迟对台军售的问题时作出这一披露的。美国之音(VOA)已就此向白宫寻求进一步说明，但截至发稿时尚未收到回复。

庞德伟在[福克斯新闻星期天](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6405700393112)(Fox News Sunday)节目中接受主持人香农·布里姆(Shannon Bream)采访时说，特朗普曾向习近平解释，美国向世界其他国家出售武器。

“特朗普总统一直说，‘嘿，我们向世界各地的其他人出售武器。’他实际上有一次还问习近平主席，他是否也想买一些，”庞德伟说。

庞德伟没有说明这段对话发生的具体时间、习近平如何回应，也没有解释特朗普的问话是正式政策提议，还是谈话中的即兴表述。白宫公布的特朗普与习近平峰会成果文件没有提到这一内容。

美国之音已就特朗普有关向中国出售武器的表态向白宫寻求进一步说明，包括这是否是一项正式提议，但截至发稿时尚未收到回复。

如果美国政府实际向中国出售军事装备，将意味着美国长期政策出现重大转变。目前，根据美国《国际武器贸易条例》(ITAR)，美国对向中国出口国防物品和国防服务实行原则上拒绝批准的政策。

**庞德伟为美国对台政策辩护**

庞德伟是在布里姆追问价值数十亿美元的台湾武器订单和安全援助项目据报遭到延迟时，披露特朗普曾向习近平提出上述问题的。

美国国会多名两党议员警告特朗普政府，延迟向台湾提供防御性武器可能削弱美国在印太地区的威慑力，并让外界认为华盛顿正在迁就北京。

庞德伟否认这一说法。他表示，自己参加了特朗普与习近平的每一次会谈，特朗普对台湾的支持立场没有改变。

“特朗普总统在台湾问题上的立场，和我见过的任何人一样坚定，”他说，“他已经非常明确地表示，我们没有改变一个中国政策。我们支持《台湾关系法》、三个联合公报和六项保证。”

庞德伟说，特朗普已经批准了价值110亿美元的对台军售，美方还在继续讨论其他可能的军售项目。

“我们的支持没有改变，”他说，“我们不支持独立，也不支持胁迫。”

美国承认北京是中国的唯一合法政府，但依据《台湾关系法》，美国有义务向台湾提供维持足够自卫能力所需的防御性物资和服务。北京宣称台湾是中国领土的一部分，并且从未放弃使用武力实现统一。

[路透社](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-expected-press-trump-halt-taiwan-arms-sales-under-1982-agreement-2026-09-22/)曾在习近平访问华盛顿前报道说，习近平预计将依据北京对1982年美中联合公报的解释，要求特朗普减少或停止对台军售。

**中国对伊朗的援助**

庞德伟还表示，特朗普警告习近平，中国向伊朗提供任何情报、无人机零部件或直接军事装备，都是美国“完全无法接受的”。

据庞德伟说，习近平向特朗普保证，北京已经调查有关问题并采取了改变。庞德伟表示，美方看到了“一些改善”，但仍将继续关注这一问题。

“我们一段时间以来一直在制裁那些援助伊朗的公司，”他说，“我们还可以采取其他措施，中国知道这一点。我们已经告诉了他们。”

白宫在峰会后表示，特朗普与习近平一致认为，伊朗绝不能拥有核武器，任何国家或机构都不应获准在国际水道征收通行费。

庞德伟还说，中国支持保持霍尔木兹海峡开放。中国仍然是伊朗石油的主要买家之一。伊朗原油通常以折扣价格出售，其中一部分据报通过更改原产地标签等方式掩盖来源。

**“超级智能”和关键矿产**

庞德伟还为美中建立先进人工智能对话机制的决定进行辩护。特朗普政府将这一技术称为“超级智能”(super intelligence)。

针对外界质疑北京是否会在人工智能紧急事件发生时及时通报信息，庞德伟承认美中之间长期存在不信任，但他说，两国政府正日益认识到，先进人工智能可能同时对双方构成风险。

“没有人知道这件事最终会发展到多大的规模，”他说，“我们将继续在这个问题上与中国接触。”

白宫表示，美中同意建立处理人工智能事件的双边沟通渠道，并将在11月前举行新设立的“美中超级智能对话”下一轮会议。

不过，庞德伟在谈及关键矿产以及中国国内相关法规时采取了更加强硬的语气。他说，中国的规定可能惩罚试图减少对华供应链依赖，或遵守美国制裁措施的企业。

“这是中国正在用来对付全世界的一种单一来源主导地位，”庞德伟说，“我们不会生活在这样一个世界里：为了按照自己希望的方式做生意，就不得不前往中国卑躬屈膝。”

白宫表示，美中双方仍在就稀土和其他关键矿产供应短缺问题进行谈判，目标是使相关产品的出货量恢复到适当水平。

title: Can South Korea stay out of war over Taiwan?
summary: As America’s regional allies watched with trepidation, Chinese leader Xi Jinping put Taiwan at the center of his summit with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday, pressing Washington to oppose its independence. Japan [quickly sought reas
content:
As America’s regional allies watched with trepidation, Chinese leader Xi Jinping put Taiwan at the center of his summit with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday, pressing Washington to oppose its independence.

Japan [quickly sought reassurance from Trump](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/09/27/japan/politics/us-japan-takaichi-trump-china/), but South Korea has remained more guarded. Wary of antagonizing China and reluctant to divert attention from the Korean Peninsula, Seoul has traditionally played things safe.

Yet that discretion is becoming harder to sustain with the growing prospect that war over Taiwan could pull the Korean Peninsula into any conflict, regardless of Seoul’s preferences.

“If a direct security threat emerges against us, simply burying our heads in the sand will not make it disappear,” Kim Young-bae, a senior lawmaker from South Korea’s ruling Democratic Party, told The Japan Times ahead of the Xi-Trump summit, referring to a regional crisis involving Taiwan.

Seoul severed diplomatic relations with Taipei for formal ties with Beijing in 1992.

Such remarks are uncommon from an elected official in South Korea’s progressive camp, especially under incumbent President Lee Jae Myung, who has repeatedly been chided for taking an overly accommodating stance toward Beijing.

China claims the island of 23 million as its own and has not ruled out taking it by force. Beijing maintains that Taiwan is an “internal matter” and rejects outside “interference.”

[![Image 1: Kim Young-bae, a senior lawmaker from South Korea’s ruling Democratic Party](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/09/27/asia-pacific/south-korea-taiwan-us-conflict/this.src='/theme_japantimes/images/no-image.png';this.removeAttribute('onerror');)](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/japantimes/uploads/images/2026/09/27/565234.jpg)
Kim Young-bae, a senior lawmaker from South Korea’s ruling Democratic Party | KENJI YOSHIDA

Washington has long left open the question of whether it would intervene militarily if the island came under attack — an approach known as “strategic ambiguity” — but is bound by law to supply Taiwan with arms for its defense.

Trump approved a major weapons package in December but has since kept a second package, worth about $14 billion, as a “negotiating chip” with Beijing.

While South Korea’s main priority should remain stability on the peninsula, Kim said that “over the long term, shifting toward a structure in which Seoul bears primary responsibility for regional contingencies would better serve the overall stability of the alliance.”

“One pillar of Washington’s push to modernize the alliance is the idea that each country should take greater responsibility for its own defense, with South Korea assuming a larger share of the security burden and costs,” Kim said, adding that Seoul needed to prepare for challenges beyond North Korea’s nuclear and missile threats.

One of the more pressing concerns for Seoul is the risk of emergencies erupting simultaneously in the Taiwan Strait and on the Korean Peninsula — a scenario that recent studies have examined with growing anxiety.

In March last year, the Brookings Institution warned that a war over Taiwan could pull some U.S. military resources in South Korea away from the peninsula, leaving it more exposed to North Korean provocations. Pyongyang could see an opportunity to escalate while U.S. forces’ attention is elsewhere.

The allies have an understanding of what they call “strategic flexibility,” but much has been kept unsettled. In 2006, Seoul acknowledged the need for U.S. forces stationed in its country to operate beyond the peninsula. Washington, in turn, agreed to respect South Korea’s position that it should not be drawn into a regional conflict “against the will of the Korean people.”

The agreement, however, does not spell out how the allies would handle a Taiwan conflict involving U.S. bases or forces in South Korea.

Hong Tae-hwa, a fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute, argues that leaving those questions unanswered is different from deliberately keeping Beijing’s leadership uncertain about Seoul’s intentions.

“Ambiguity over ends — what South Korea’s interests in the strait actually are — is corrosive,” Hong said. “That is strategic evasion, not strategic ambiguity.”

[![Image 2: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung gestures as he meets with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, in October last year.](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/09/27/asia-pacific/south-korea-taiwan-us-conflict/this.src='/theme_japantimes/images/no-image.png';this.removeAttribute('onerror');)](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/japantimes/uploads/images/2026/09/27/565236.JPG)
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung gestures as he meets with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, in October last year. | REUTERS

Hong, who regularly advises South Korean lawmakers on international security, said Seoul should maintain ambiguity publicly over whether U.S. Forces Korea would become involved, but quietly build the operational capacity needed for such a crisis.

That could include Agile Combat Employment, a strategy for dispersing aircraft and personnel across multiple sites to maximize survivability, as well as greater interoperability with aerial-refueling tankers, pre-packaged munitions kits and other capabilities permitting forces to disperse and move quickly.

South Korea, he added, could serve as a rear-area logistics hub moving personnel, fuel and munitions at scale, while tightening military cooperation among the United States and other U.S. regional allies such as Japan, Australia and the Philippines.

In a crisis involving Taiwan, Washington could seek to use air bases in South Korea such as Osan and Kunsan or facilities at Camp Humphreys to support operations in the region. Even if South Korean forces stayed focused on defending the peninsula, U.S. aircraft, personnel and supplies could still move through bases on South Korean soil.

The South Korean public appears willing to consider at least a limited role. In [a 2026 Asan Institute for Policy Studies poll](https://asaninst.org/bbs/board.php?bo_table=s1_1_eng&wr_id=291), 39.4% favored nonmilitary assistance in a Taiwan emergency, 15.6% supported rear-area military support and 14% said they would allow U.S. Forces Korea to deploy from the country.

In a sign of the shift in thinking, the top diplomats of Japan, the U.S. and South Korea also [reaffirmed the importance of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait last week](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/09/22/japan/politics/us-japan-south-korea-taiwan/) — even as Seoul remains comparatively more circumspect about what role it might play in an actual conflict.

To that end, Hong says more must be done to recalibrate South Korea’s current policy over Taiwan.

“Deterrence by uncertainty works when capability and preparation are certain and intent alone is veiled,” he said.

“Seoul has inverted the formula — reluctance telegraphed, preparation unbuilt, and the only genuine mystery, what Korea actually wants, deters no one.”

title: Serbia's President Vucic resigns ahead of October parliamentary elections
summary: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.c
content:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/81st-united-nations-general-assembly-at-un-headquarters-in-new-york-city/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjlQTkFEREZYUw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Resignation allows Vucic to become prime minister if his party prevails in October parliamentary election
*   First round of presidential election to be held by end of December
*   Critics say Vucic and allies are increasingly authoritarian; government denies it mistreats protesters
*   Vucic pardons people linked to ​protests

BELGRADE, Sept 27 (Reuters) - Serbia's populist President [Aleksandar Vucic](https://www.reuters.com/world/serbias-vucic-eyes-new-political-chapter-he-steps-down-presidency-2026-06-29/) ‌announced his resignation on Sunday, ending his second and final five-year term and paving the way for early presidential elections.

Vucic's resignation, seven months before his term ends, comes amid campaigning for Serbia's October 25 snap parliamentary vote and allows him to be appointed prime minister if his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) ​forms the new government.

Get a look at the day ahead in European and global markets with the Morning Bid Europe newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/morning-bid-europe/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Feurope%2Fserbias-president-vucic-resigns-paving-way-early-elections-2026-09-27%2F)

He had said in late June that [he planned to resign](https://www.reuters.com/world/serbia-president-vucic-says-resign-within-weeks-one-year-before-end-mandate-2026-06-27/) and that Serbia would hold early parliamentary ​and presidential elections.

Rights groups have accused Vucic and his allies of increasingly authoritarian rule, with anti-government ⁠protesters saying they have been beaten by police and unfairly detained. Authorities have denied those allegations.

On Sunday, hundreds of Vucic's supporters ​cheered him in front of the Presidency building in Belgrade's city centre.

"This is the last evening for me in this building," he told ​the flag-waving crowd minutes before resigning.

"I have faithfully served you and my fatherland, Serbia, ... I am proud of what we have done together," he said.

Under Serbia's constitution, outgoing Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabic will serve as interim president until a new one is elected. The presidential election must be completed within 90 ​days, with the campaign lasting between 30 and 60 days.

"By the end of December ... we will have the first round of ​presidential elections," Vucic said.

## ELECTIONS TO TEST VUCIC'S CONTROL

Next month's snap parliamentary election will pit Vucic's SNS and its allies against Students Win, a student-led anti-corruption movement, ‌and ⁠European Serbia, an alliance of pro-Western opposition parties.

Students Win, European Serbia and other parties have yet to nominate their presidential candidates.

Vucic, 56, has dominated Serbian politics for [more than a decade](https://www.reuters.com/world/serbias-vucic-eyes-new-political-chapter-he-steps-down-presidency-2026-06-29/).

He was a hardline nationalist and information minister during the era of the late Slobodan Milosevic and the wars of the 1990s, and later served as deputy prime minister from 2012-14 and prime minister from 2014-17.

He moved to the largely ceremonial ​position of president in 2017, but ​kept tight control over his ⁠party and the government.

In foreign policy, Vucic has pursued a balancing act that seeks closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia's principal supplier of natural gas, while maintaining a long-term goal of joining the ​EU. He also has sought to bolster ties with the United States and Israel.

Vucic's term in office ​suffered a major blow ⁠in November 2024 when an awning of a newly reconstructed railway station in the northern city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing 16 people.

The disaster sparked nationwide protests by students and the opposition, who demanded accountability for those responsible, transparency in public procurement, an end to systemic ⁠corruption, and an ​early parliamentary vote.

The government repeatedly denied accusations by the protesters, although several ​officials, including two ministers, were arrested or resigned after the incident.

On Sunday, Vucic said he has granted amnesty and a pardon to 49 people, including 12 activists and 11 of ​his own supporters, who were arrested or tried in connection with the protests.

title: 特习峰会成果盘点：关税休战、AI对话、未提台湾、暗指日本
summary: 图像来源，Reuters Published 1 小时前 阅读时间: 4 分钟 中国国家主席习近平（25日）结束访美行程，美中分别发表会晤成果，均触及贸易、人工智能及禁毒等议题，同意建立基于尊重、公平及对等的战略稳定关系，但并未提及台湾。 然而，外界普遍认为，美国总统特朗普高规格接待习近平，但会谈具突破或实际的成果不大。 预期今年内中美元首仍有两次会面，分别是11月在深圳的亚太经合组织（APEC）会议及12月在迈阿密的二十国集团（G20）峰会。 BBC中文梳理两国展现了什么成
content:
图像来源，Reuters

Published 1 小时前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

中国国家主席习近平（25日）结束访美行程，美中分别发表会晤成果，均触及贸易、人工智能及禁毒等议题，同意建立基于尊重、公平及对等的战略稳定关系，但并未提及台湾。

然而，外界普遍认为，美国总统特朗普高规格接待习近平，但会谈具突破或实际的成果不大。

预期今年内中美元首仍有两次会面，分别是11月在深圳的亚太经合组织（APEC）会议及12月在迈阿密的二十国集团（G20）峰会。

BBC中文梳理两国展现了什么成果，以及外界如何解读二人的举措。

## 两国如何定义双边关系？

中方在26日[发布](https://www.xinhuanet.com/20260926/5b4a09239a5a4db0a42df9aa3ba9b35e/c.html)八项成果共识，白宫则在当地时间25日深夜发表[事实清单](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/09/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-advances-a-fair-and-reciprocal-relationship-with-china-while-hosting-historic-state-visit/)。两份文件均涉及经贸、人工智能及禁毒等议题，也触及双边关系定位及伊朗局势等外交议题。

两方均表示，同意建立基于尊重、公平及对等的战略稳定关系，并相互支持对方举办APEC及G20峰会。两国元首均有意出席对方主办的会议，预计今年内仍有两次会面机会。

在伊朗议题上，两国同意伊朗应履行不发展核武器的承诺，任何国家或机构都不得对国际水道征收通行费。

两份文件还提到，两国元首回顾了“中美是二战盟友”、“并肩作战赢得战争胜利”的历史。虽未点名日本，但随同习近平访美的中国外交部长王毅在讲述此行程时表示，今年是二战东京审判开庭80周年，中美同为联合国安理会常任理事国，维护战后国际秩序、防止军国主义复活，是双方的共同责任。

台湾问题则呈现会内提及、文件略过的微妙落差。会面期间，习近平强调希望美方坚持反对“台独”的正确立场，慎重处理台湾问题。美国的官方立场一向是“不支持”台独。会后的成果清单没有提及台湾，特朗普其后仅称“没花太多时间讨论台湾，他（习近平）非常清楚我的想法”。

白宫清单另提到，两人也谈及俄罗斯及朝鲜。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，2026年9月25日，台北一家餐厅的顾客正在用餐，电视上播放美国总统特朗普与中国国家主席习近平会晤的新闻。

## “形式大于内容”

曾任美国助理国务卿、分管东亚和太平洋事务的亚洲协会政策研究所（Asia Society Policy Institute）研究员丹尼尔·拉塞尔（Daniel Russel）直言峰会令人失望，排场与实质内容之间明显失衡。他用“外交娱乐化”（diplotainment）形容这一次峰会。

不过拉塞尔分析，北京并不介意，因为特朗普展现的礼遇，彰显了中国的地位与习近平的威望。

在他看来，两国展现了避免双边关系跌入谷底的意愿，但在贸易、科技、台湾、国防、稀土及产业政策等问题上，两国仍深陷激烈竞争，“掩盖真正的问题存在风险”。他关注各项协议能否真正落实，例如削减关税、购买农产品、增加稀土出口量，原因在于“峰会的公告往往无法准确预示后续的实际成效”。

美国智库外交关系协会（Council on Foreign Relations）主席弗罗曼（Michael Froman）[撰文写道](https://www.cfr.org/articles/much-ado-about-nothing)，习近平此次国事访问“形式大于内容”：双方延长关税休战，但中国产能问题被押后处理，台湾、伊朗、俄罗斯等议题均未取得重大进展。

他分析，习近平与特朗普对现状都颇为满意，二人倾向把中美关系视为“需要管理”（managed）而非“需要解决”（resolved）的问题。双方都强调稳定、友好与避免冲突，反映两国目前更关注控制竞争风险，而非寻求重大突破。

大西洋理事会（Atlantic Council）副主席乔许·利普斯基（Josh Lipsky）则[认为](https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/content-series/fastthinking/what-did-and-didnt-happen-at-the-trump-xi-summit/)，峰会对北京而言是一场更具广泛意义的形象胜利。当各国正聚集纽约出席联合国大会之际，华盛顿把美中描绘成近乎平等的对手，也就是“G2”格局，而非“G7”或“G20”的框架。在他看来，这等于美国推开盟友这一自己最宝贵的资产，转而选择与中国平起平坐。

图像来源，Reuters

## 关税休战延长两月：时间点的考量

经贸方面，在双方正式会晤前，美国财政部长已公布，美国将贸易战的休战期延长至明年1月。

两国在会晤中认可中美经贸磋商机制和双方经贸团队的磋商成果。白宫的事实清单具体指出，今年5月峰会设立的美中贸易委员会和美中投资委员会正式投入运作，双方就各300亿美元“非敏感商品”给予更优惠关税达成共识。美国一方涵盖出口的农产品、鱼类及海鲜、木制品、化妆品和医疗器械，自美国进口的产品则包括小家电、玩具等消费品。

中方另承诺，于2027和2028年每年从美国进口至少1000万吨煤炭；双方亦会致力解决稀土及其他关键矿产的供应链短缺。

这份贸易休战协议源于去年两国元首在韩国釜山的会晤，原订今年11月届满。

亚洲协会政策研究所副总裁、前贸易谈判代表卡特勒（Wendy Cutler）分析，休战仅延长两个月，远短于中方争取的时间，但恰好让双方避开今年接下来两场可能举行的峰会。

她指出，从美国角度看，较短的期限或能为华盛顿提供必要筹码，迫使中国履行休战协议中的承诺，特别是在关键矿产及磁体领域。不过只要北京仍主导关键矿产产业，美国对中国的施压能力便相当有限，因此预期双方将继续透过推出新的惩罚性经济措施互相试探。

卡特勒表示，目前值得关注的发展有两个：双方是否表明会继续推行削减关税措施并扩大至更多产品；贸易委员会是否获授权处理包括非关税壁垒在内的其他事项。她也提示，舆论对中国产能过剩及出口激增问题的讨论明显不足。

图像来源，Getty Images

## 人工智能：同意对话，未有方案

此次峰会的重要议题之一，是美中两国在人工智能安全问题上有没有合作空间。

两国同意建立中美人工智能对话机制，交流相关风险和益处，下次对话定于11月，双方并将建立人工智能事件的沟通渠道。

美方特别提及，两国领导人同意以“超级智能”（super intelligence）代替“人工智能”（artificial intelligence）的表述。不过中方文件未见使用“超级智能”一词，中国外交部26日就此[表示](https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/fyrbt_673021/202609/t20260926_12031638.shtml)，就人工智能表述，“中方重视美方的立场，也尊重美方的提法”。

弗罗曼分析，习近平与特朗普在人工智能议题上的立场似乎一致：特朗普迅速驳斥放慢人工智能发展的想法，坚信美国正与中国展开一场关乎存亡的竞赛，“谁赢得AI，谁就赢了”；中国方面也同样不愿放慢脚步。

在他看来，建立对话机制是积极的一步，但能发挥多大作用，目前尚不明朗。

大西洋理事会数位鉴识研究实验室（Digital Forensic Research Lab）的中国高级研究员肯顿·蒂博（Kenton Thibaut）[指出](https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/content-series/fastthinking/what-did-and-didnt-happen-at-the-trump-xi-summit/)，公开声明显示双方在“人类控制”和“滥用风险”问题上存在一定程度的概念重叠，但双方并未就具体安全机制达成公开共识，比如事故通报、前沿模型评估，或对先进人工智能开发的限制措施。

title: Protesters block Orange Order from marching through Catholic area in Northern Ireland
summary: Item 1 of 5 People block the Garvaghy road, a Catholic enclave in the largely Protestant town of Portadown, on the day members of the Protestant Orange Order are expected to march through the area as they take part in the annual Drumcree pa
content:
Item 1 of 5 People block the Garvaghy road, a Catholic enclave in the largely Protestant town of Portadown, on the day members of the Protestant Orange Order are expected to march through the area as they take part in the annual Drumcree parade, Northern Ireland, September 27, 2026. REUTERS/Cathal McNaughton

**[1/5]**People block the Garvaghy road, a Catholic enclave in the largely Protestant town of Portadown, on the day members of the Protestant Orange Order are expected to march through the area as they take part in the annual Drumcree parade, Northern Ireland, September 27, 2026. REUTERS/Cathal McNaughton [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/members-of-the-orange-order-march-through-drumcree-in-portadown/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMklSTkFZOUEwVw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   March along Garvaghy Road had been banned since 1998
*   Original dispute a defining flashpoint of the 'Troubles'
*   First Minister says peace process brought into question

PORTADOWN, Northern Ireland, Sept 27 (Reuters) - Around 2,000 protesters blocked the way into a Catholic area in a ​Northern Irish town that a Protestant parade was due to walk down on Sunday morning after the lifting of an almost 30-year ban ‌on a route that was a flashpoint of sectarian disputes.

Crowds including Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill of Irish nationalists Sinn Fein and the party's leader, Mary Lou McDonald, gathered in the rain on the Garvaghy Road overnight after Belfast's High Court [dismissed an application](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/northern-irish-court-dismisses-challenge-against-protestant-parade-route-2026-09-27/) by residents to stop the parade early on Sunday morning.

Get a look at the day ahead in European and global markets with the Morning Bid Europe newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/morning-bid-europe/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fuk%2Fnorthern-irish-court-dismisses-challenge-against-protestant-parade-route-2026-09-27%2F)

Annual attempts by the Protestant Orange Order to march through the ​area triggered unrest across the British-run region before the route was banned in 1998, the same year the Good Friday Agreement largely ended the three ​decades of violence known as the "Troubles".

"This is madness," McDonald told reporters on the road, a Catholic enclave in the largely Protestant ⁠town of Portadown. "This, in fact, is primitive treatment of any community in the year 2026. It is intolerable."

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for calm on Sunday.

"I ​know it's a tense situation, we do appeal for calm on all sides. There have been big gains made in Northern Ireland and we don't want to see things ​go backwards," Burnham told the BBC. He said he had spoken to Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin on the matter on Saturday.

Northern Ireland's Parades Commission - which regulates marches in the British-run region - [on Friday permitted](https://www.reuters.com/world/northern-ireland-allows-contentious-orange-order-march-through-catholic-area-2026-09-25/) that a smaller-than-usual 35 people could take part in the march between 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) and 9:30 a.m.

## ORANGE SASHES AND BOWLER HATS

A small group of Orange Order members wearing traditional ​silk orange sashes and black bowler hats gathered at another part of the town but the march had not started by 9:30 a.m.

A senior member told the ​BBC that the group would wait for police to tell them the route was ready for them to start.

Police vans parked near the Garvaghy Road had earlier played out a warning ‌that anyone ⁠taking part in the protest was committing a criminal offence.

The Drumcree dispute exploded in the mid-1990s when, in the wake of ceasefires by Northern Ireland's main guerrilla groups, it became a symbol of the wider dispute between mainly Catholic nationalists, who consider themselves Irish, and Protestants loyal to Britain.

The Orangemen, who take their name from Protestant King William of Orange who defeated deposed Catholic King James II at the Battle of the Boyne in 1690, say their parades are part of their Protestant cultural tradition.

Whilst most ​of the parades that take place ​across Northern Ireland each year are uncontroversial, ⁠nationalists say parades such as Drumcree passing through Catholic areas are an offensive display of triumphalism designed to intimidate them.

## PEACE PROCESS BROUGHT 'INTO QUESTION'

McDonald and O'Neill called on the British government and police to intervene. O'Neill said she had spoken to Britain's minister ​for the region and the Irish government.

The Irish government issued a statement saying it was very concerned about the situation ​and that its primary ⁠concern was to "avoid a return to the divisions of the past."

"I think that this brings into question how this whole peace process works," said O'Neill, whose party rules alongside the largest pro-British party in a devolved power-sharing administration that was a key part of the 1998 peace deal.

The governing Democratic Unionist Party, some of whose lawmakers stood alongside the ⁠Orange Order, ​said the march must be allowed to proceed.

"A First Minister's duty is to uphold lawful decisions, not ​inflame opposition to them," DUP leader Gavin Robinson said in a statement.

Northern Ireland's police chief, Jon Boutcher, appealed in a statement to "everyone to remain calm and peaceful", and urged those with influence to encourage ​people to comply with the law and work with the police.

title: Why US chip controls took a back seat at the Xi-Trump summit
summary: There is little question that Jensen Huang and Lisa Su, the heads of US semiconductor chip giants Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), had secured two of the best seats in the house at the White House state dinner on Thursday evening: a
content:
There is little question that Jensen Huang and Lisa Su, the heads of US semiconductor chip giants Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), had secured two of the best seats in the house at the White House state dinner on Thursday evening: at the head table alongside the two presidents and their wives.

But what remains unclear is how much progress they were able to make on their primary goal of restoring access to the Chinese market, amid entrenched opposition to that happening in both China and the US.

That is because US semiconductor chip export controls do not seem to have been a major sticking point during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s historic state visit to Washington this week, despite most of the restrictions still being in place.

Early indications suggest that export controls were not a significant topic of debate during the talks, with no direct mention of them in the readouts so far from both Beijing and Washington summarising the achievements of the Xi–Trump summit.

“This is especially strange considering that export controls were brought up regularly by Xi during his talks with [President Joe] Biden,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at Washington think tank Brookings specialising in Chinese technology.

On Friday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC that the US side had taken “off the table” all the export controls “that are national security issues” during trade talks this week. China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Saturday did not mention export controls or Beijing’s usual references to US tech restrictions in its announcement of eight deliverables from the summit, including the launch of a China-US dialogue on AI risks.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said export controls involving national security had been taken “off the table” during this week’s trade talks. Photo: Reuters

But if export controls have become less of a sticking point, it is not because they have gone away. The Trump administration has largely kept intact [restrictions first introduced by the Biden administration](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3195461/tech-war-chinas-semiconductor-self-sufficiency-drive-under-siege-new?module=inline&pgtype=article) in October 2022 on China’s ability to obtain advanced chips and chipmaking equipment.

Some areas were even tightened at the start of Trump’s second term, including a [ban on exporting Nvidia’s H20 chip](https://www.scmp.com/news/world/united-states-canada/article/3306680/nvidia-expects-us55-billion-hit-us-targets-chips-sent-china?module=inline&pgtype=article) to China, which the company had developed specifically to comply with US rules.

According to Chan, Beijing has likely grown more comfortable with the export controls already in place as it looks to deepen its technological self-reliance campaign to reduce its reliance on US tech.

“The biggest thing that’s changed is China’s growing confidence in its chip self-reliance efforts,” he said. “While the 2022 export controls may have surprised Beijing at the time, China has made real progress on building a domestic supply chain for advanced semiconductors in the years since”.

### A temporary stalemate

When Washington first imposed sweeping export controls on China in 2022, Beijing treated them as a direct attack on China’s technological and economic rise and began regularly calling for their removal in talks with the US.

The controls became a wedge issue in US-China relations. At China-US talks on AI safety in Geneva in May 2024, Chinese officials tied progress on AI safety to the US unwinding those controls, former Biden administration officials have said.

This was not an issue this time around. Export controls were not brought up during the AI safety related talks between Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last Sunday in New York, according to Greer, who also attended the meeting.

The AI talks, which also resulted in the launch of a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents, were “candid, in-depth and constructive”, Beijing said.

Paul Triolo, a partner and technology policy lead at DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group, said Beijing is likely “pleased with progress that the domestic semiconductor industry has made despite the [US] controls”.

Nvidia, AMD and other foreign suppliers’ share is set to fall to 21 per cent in 2026 from 34 per cent last year, according to the Taipei-based research firm.

Domestic chip substitution is expected to further ramp up in the coming years as tech self-reliance remains a central pillar of China’s 15th Five-Year Plan. Earlier this year, Beijing resisted efforts by both President Donald Trump and Nvidia’s Huang to push for the US chip giant’s less powerful [H200 chips](https://www.scmp.com/tech/article/3354296/nvidias-h200-sales-prospects-china-remain-uncertain-despite-huang-visit?module=inline&pgtype=article) to be allowed back into the Chinese market.

Beijing has since [allowed a small number of Chinese tech companies](https://www.scmp.com/tech/policy/article/3360027/game-changer-why-china-finally-letting-its-ai-firms-buy-nvidia-h200?module=inline&pgtype=article) to purchase the chip with the quantities capped, as it continues to promote domestic chip adoption instead. Meanwhile, the delay**e**d approval caused Nvidia to take a US$400 million charge due to excess H200 inventory in the first half of the year.

### Spanner in the works

Still, talk of an export control impasse might still be premature. That is because Beijing is likely to push back forcefully against any new restrictions the US introduces, with some already on the horizon, according to Triolo.

A major area of concern is US congressional efforts to bolster its export controls regime. One of these is the [Match Act](https://www.scmp.com/tech/article/3351199/tech-war-us-congress-rolls-out-largest-export-control-upgrade-against-china?module=inline&pgtype=article), which would require US allies such as Japan and the Netherlands to more closely align with US restrictions on selling advanced semiconductor equipment to China, such as Dutch firm ASML’s deep ultraviolet (DUV) immersion lithography machines.

“Chinese officials view any new controls as a violation of the Busan agreement, and [would] retaliate strongly via expanded controls on rare earths and related production equipment,” said Triolo, referring to the economic detente reached in October 2025 between the two countries that paused escalating tit-for-tat tariffs and export controls, which the two leaders agreed to extend to January.

“Beijing likely sought assurances on this [this week],” he said.

Even as the official readouts of the two presidents’ meeting have largely focused on trade and investment, senior Chinese officials have referenced US technological restrictions on China in statements elsewhere.

On Saturday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in a post-meeting statement that China and the US should not “adopt a defensive posture towards each other” in the emerging field of AI.

The relative quiet on export controls this week might therefore reflect strong domestic pressure on both sides not to concede ground, Triolo said, with powerful contingents in the US pushing for tighter controls and those in China for greater self-reliance.

“Neither side will acknowledge progress on any of these issues, given domestic sensitivities around anything that could be perceived as a concession,” he said.

title: Iran insists on diplomatic solution after Trump rejects peace plan
summary: * Summary * Trump rejects Iran's proposal for reopening Hormuz * Iran says reopening Hormuz hinges on conditions being met and negotiated solution * Senior Iranian official says Tehran shows no flexibility on nuclear program WASHINGTON/UNIT
content:
*   Summary

*   Trump rejects Iran's proposal for reopening Hormuz
*   Iran says reopening Hormuz hinges on conditions being met and negotiated solution
*   Senior Iranian official says Tehran shows no flexibility on nuclear program

WASHINGTON/UNITED NATIONS/CAIRO, Sept 27 (Reuters) - Iran on Sunday insisted that only diplomacy can solve its conflict with the ​United States and Israel after US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ‌end fighting.

"Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi posted on social media. "Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock."

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fasia-pacific%2Firan-insists-diplomatic-solution-after-trump-rejects-peace-plan-2026-09-26%2F)

Iran announced a peace proposal earlier this week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari ​mediators. Trump on Saturday said he rejected the plan and argued that desperation drives the Iranians’ push for an agreement on the key waterway.

"They want ​to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," Trump told reporters at the White House.

Despite ⁠Trump's public statements, mediators facilitating US-Iran talks with the United States have not officially relayed a US rejection of the plan, according to Araqchi.

"We are waiting ​for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them," Araqchi posted.

The US has imposed an economic blockade ​on Iran to put pressure on Tehran to stop Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, which have drastically reduced shipping through the area even as Trump repeatedly asserts that the US controls the waterway.

The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed US officials.

It said Trump was privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and ​had told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections.

A US official had said earlier that discussions ​with Iran through mediators were "positive and constructive".

Item 1 of 3 An Iranian woman shouts during a march in Tehran, Iran, September 25, 2026. Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS

**[1/3]**An Iranian woman shouts during a march in Tehran, Iran, September 25, 2026. Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/an-iranian-woman-shouts-during-a-march-in-tehran/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjdRTkFCTUIxVw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

## CONFLICT HAS DISRUPTED OIL FLOWS, HARMED GLOBAL ECONOMY

The Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the stakes of a ‌seven-month-old conflict that ⁠has disrupted oil flows through a critical shipping lane and taken a toll on the global economy.

Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday the proposed deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.

"If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araqchi said. If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed ​subjects."

That could potentially include discussions of Iran's ​nuclear program. Trump has said Tehran ⁠must never acquire a nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told Reuters that

[Iran would show no flexibility, opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/world/search/nL1N45H0L1)
over its nuclear program even if the US accepted its peace deal.

Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping ​its highly enriched uranium out of the country, the official said.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the ​CBS show "Face the Nation", ⁠said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear program and other issues, but would not accept "bullying or coercion".

"Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that "we're not supposed to develop nuclear weapons".

Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which ⁠began on February ​28 with US and Israeli attacks.

Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, ​killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.

Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf ​with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests.

Reporting by Reuters bureaux; Writing by Michelle Conlin; Editing by Sergio Non and Chizu Nomiyama

Trevor Hunnicutt is White House Correspondent at Reuters News. He writes about U.S. foreign and domestic policy and regularly travels with the President of the United States. Prior to joining the White House team in 2021, he covered presidential campaigns, economics, finance and investing for many years. He has also served on the board of the White House Correspondents' Association. Hunnicutt holds a bachelor's degree from Pomona College and a master's from the London School of Economics.

title: Arming Taiwan an important US interest, Taipei official says after Trump-Xi summit
summary: * Summary * Xi, Trump end Washington summit * Xi pressed Trump on opposing Taiwan independence * Trump has yet to approve new $14 bln arms sale for Taiwan TAIPEI, Sept 26 (Reuters) - The United States providing weapons to Taiwan to protect
content:
*   Summary

*   Xi, Trump end Washington summit
*   Xi pressed Trump on opposing Taiwan independence
*   Trump has yet to approve new $14 bln arms sale for Taiwan

TAIPEI, Sept 26 (Reuters) - The United States providing weapons to Taiwan to protect its freedom and ​provide semiconductors to the world is in the US national interest, a senior Taiwanese diplomat said on Saturday ‌following a summit between the Chinese and US presidents.

President [Donald Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/donald-trump/) and Chinese President Xi Jinping ended a three-day [summit](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-wrap-up-xi-summit-with-tour-us-archives-2026-09-25/) on Friday with no big public breakthroughs on a host of contentious issues, including Taiwan which Beijing views as its own territory.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Farming-taiwan-an-important-us-interest-taipei-official-says-after-trump-xi-2026-09-26%2F)

Xi told Trump in [Washington](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-welcomes-xi-washington-looking-trade-win-2026-09-24/) on Thursday that he hoped the ​US would adhere to the "correct position" of opposing Taiwan independence.

Speaking to reporters in Taipei, Deputy Foreign Minister Francois Wu ​asked whether making concessions on Taiwan would actually serve US interests.

Maintaining military sales, giving Taiwan sufficient ⁠capability to defend itself so it does not have to live under Chinese rule and "allowing Taiwan's semiconductor industry to continue contributing ​to the world, these are important US interests", Wu said.

Taiwan, whose government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, is the main producer of the ​advanced chips powering the AI revolution.

Trump, who in May after meeting Xi in Beijing said he was holding a package of arms sales to Taiwan in abeyance, has yet to make any comments on Taiwan following the Washington meeting or what he will do about the pending weapons package.

## ARMS ​SALES

Item 1 of 3 People walk through Nanjichang Night Market beneath Taiwan flags in Taipei, Taiwan, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Ann Wang

**[1/3]**People walk through Nanjichang Night Market beneath Taiwan flags in Taipei, Taiwan, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Ann Wang [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/people-walk-through-nanjichang-night-market-beneath-taiwan-flags-in-taipei/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkxQTkExSEsxQw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Wang Hung-jen, a political science professor at Taiwan's National Cheng Kung University, said so far the outcome of the summit was ​better than had been expected, with Xi not apparently directly raising arms sales and Taiwan not the main focus.

"Looking at the results, many things ‌we thought ⁠would be very bad didn't happen," he said.

Wu said the government had been in "continuous communication" with Washington about the summit.

The Trump administration in December approved an $11 billion arms sale to Taiwan, the largest ever, and the second one is worth even more - some $14 billion.

As to whether a decision on that could be delayed further, given Xi and Trump are expected to meet twice more this ​year at the APEC and ​G20 summits, Wu said the ⁠government had to pay close attention.

"Of course, if we can get guarantees, that would be best," he added. "I think what we can do right now is probably the maximum, which is to ​prepare as much as possible, communicate as much as possible, and make requests as much as ​possible."

David Perdue, the ⁠US ambassador to China, told CNBC on Friday that there has been no change in Taiwan policy by Trump, including on the 1979 Taiwan Relations Act which mandates arms sales to the island.

"We want peace across the strait. We don't want coercion. We don't support ⁠independence and ​we think that, you know, President Xi has gotten that message. President ​Trump has shown respect and listened to their side of that argument," Perdue said.

On Saturday, China's top newspaper, the People's Daily, reiterated in a commentary that Taiwan ​is "the core of China's core interests and the first unbreakable red line in China-US relations".

Adds analyst comment, paragraphs 8, 9

Reporting by Ben Blanchard; Editing by Stephen Coates
