Ben joined Reuters as a company news reporter in Shanghai in 2003 before moving to Beijing in 2005 to cover Chinese politics and diplomacy. In 2019 Ben was appointed the Taiwan bureau chief covering everything from elections and entertainment to semiconductors.

title: Iran awaits US move after WSJ report says Trump rejects peace plan
summary: * Summary * Iranian proposal would open strait, end fighting in 7 days * Wall Street Journal report says Trump rejects offer * Saudi allies show support amid continued attacks by Houthis CAIRO/UNITED NATIONS, Sept 26 (Reuters) - Iran on Sat
content:
*   Summary

*   Iranian proposal would open strait, end fighting in 7 days
*   Wall Street Journal report says Trump rejects offer
*   Saudi allies show support amid continued attacks by Houthis

CAIRO/UNITED NATIONS, Sept 26 (Reuters) - Iran on Saturday awaited an official US response to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the wider Middle East war after the Wall Street Journal ​reported that US President Donald Trump had rejected the deal.

Iran raised the diplomatic initiative at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, saying it had been ‌transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Firan-awaits-us-move-after-wsj-report-says-trump-rejects-peace-plan-2026-09-26%2F)

The Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the strait, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through one of the world's most critical shipping lanes and taken a toll on the global economy.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday the deal ​would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.

"If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen ​the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araqchi said.

If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects," ⁠Araqchi said.

That could potentially include discussions of Iran's nuclear program. Trump has vowed that Tehran will never acquire a nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told Reuters that [Iran will show no ​flexibility](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-will-make-no-nuclear-concessions-iranian-official-says-2026-09-25/) over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its peace deal.

Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the ​country, the official said.

Even so, Iran had put forward a plan that would halt hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon. The plan in turn would require the United States to lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds, and waive its oil sanctions, Araqchi said.

A US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, had previously called discussions through mediators "positive and constructive."

But Trump was privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands, the Journal report said, ​and he told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely.

Reuters could not immediately confirm the Journal report.

Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/members-of-iranian-militia-forces-basij-ride-on-motorcycles-as-they-participate-in-a-march-in-tehran/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjdRTkEwNTE2Ug%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

## SAUDI ALLIES UNITE

Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, ​which began on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks.

Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.

Iran and its allies ‌have retaliated by ⁠extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran, which controls the strait along with Oman, has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests. Iranian-aligned militias in Iraq were blamed for a pipeline attack that temporarily took more Saudi oil off the market. All the while, Iranian-backed Hezbollah has been engaged with Israeli forces in Lebanon.

Araqchi briefed his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan on the understanding between Iran and Oman regarding safe shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's foreign ministry said early Saturday.

The war's widening toll ​has also united Saudi Arabia's allies to shore up ​the kingdom's defenses.

The Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Yemeni ⁠government has come under assault from Iran-linked Houthi fighters, with Houthi missiles striking inside the kingdom.

Yemen's Saudi-led coalition said early Saturday it intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital Riyadh in addition to intercepting a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward Khamis Mushait.

The Houthis, ​who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have launched attacks against Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade ​against Riyadh in July, ⁠with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.

The attacks have targeted Saudi cities, energy infrastructure and shipping, adding to pressures on global oil supplies caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran and putting at risk the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked.

Defense officials of Turkey and Pakistan, both partners in a joint defense pact with Saudi Arabia, met ⁠in Riyadh ​on Friday to review the security situation and discuss intelligence cooperation, military coordination, and integrating forces, the Saudi defense ministry ​said in a statement.

The statement came a day after Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met within the framework of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement.

The violence in Yemen has prompted a new [humanitarian crisis,](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/child-malnutrition-rises-yemen-fighting-intensifies-says-unicef-2026-09-25/) the United Nations children's agency said on ​Friday, reporting a rise in acute malnutrition among children.

title: 特习华盛顿峰会在贸易、台湾、AI和伊朗问题到底取得哪些进展？
summary: 中国领导人习近平星期五(9月25日)结束了为期两天半的访美之行。唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统和习近平都表示此次会晤很成功。那么，在外界最为关注的经贸、人工智能、台湾问题上，美中首脑峰会到底取得了哪些成果？ **贸易休战延期两个月，更多细节下星期一见** 特朗普和习近平能否将两人在2025年10月在韩国釜山达成的脆弱贸易协议延期是本次会晤关注的焦点。这个协议11月10日到期。在美中关税一度突破100%后，特朗普和习近平在韩国釜山达成了初步协议。特朗普同意削减关
content:
中国领导人习近平星期五(9月25日)结束了为期两天半的访美之行。唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统和习近平都表示此次会晤很成功。那么，在外界最为关注的经贸、人工智能、台湾问题上，美中首脑峰会到底取得了哪些成果？

**贸易休战延期两个月，更多细节下星期一见**

特朗普和习近平能否将两人在2025年10月在韩国釜山达成的脆弱贸易协议延期是本次会晤关注的焦点。这个协议11月10日到期。在美中关税一度突破100%后，特朗普和习近平在韩国釜山达成了初步协议。特朗普同意削减关税，以换取北京方面打击芬太尼前体、恢复购买大豆以及暂停稀土出口管制。这项协议成功遏制了关税持续升级的态势。

星期三(9月23日)晚间，在习近平抵达华盛顿后几个小时，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)宣布，美中两国已同意将贸易贸易休战期延长两个月。

贝森特在接受福克斯新闻“特别报道”节目采访时表示：“休战期限将延长至1月10日，以便我们有更多时间探讨在经济领域可以采取哪些措施。”他还补充说，两国仍在努力达成一项可能规模更大的协议。

美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)星期五告诉美国媒体CNBC，预计将于星期一公布美中贸易谈判的细节。

在美中领导人会晤前，两国的贸易代表团9月20日开始在纽约和华盛顿已经展开了连续几天的会晤。会谈后格里尔告诉媒体，美中已经启动“贸易委员会”机制，该机制能够“为双边关系提供某种稳定”。

贸易委员会机制是特朗普和习近平在北京峰会上宣布的重要的成果之一。这一机制旨在为双方各自价值约300亿美元的非敏感商品削减关税与贸易壁垒。

格里尔说：“会存在这样一种局面：美中两国有一小部分商品可以进行平衡贸易，这些商品属于非敏感商品，未来在贸易谈判中，我们可以将它们作为一个独立的类别来考虑。”

特朗普总统在美国东部时间星期五上午在白宫与习近平会晤时表示，美国的农民应该会开心。

“美国的农民肯定对这一次的国事访问的成果非常的满意，因为可以说很多正面的一些事情已经发生了。”特朗普说。

欧道明大学国际商业讲座教授李少民告诉美国之音，将贸易休战期延长对双方都有利，中国尤其能够获利。他说：“因为中国国内经济非常不好，所以它现在唯一能靠的就是外贸，因为它毕竟有产品价格低的优势。另外它有举国模式，国家可以帮助。”

**AI管控**

特朗普总统星期四上午在真相(Truth Social)社交平台上发文称，人工智能(AI)将是他与习近平会晤时的重要议题。

美中两国近几周在AI议题上交锋激烈，美国人工智能行业的数位高管纷纷呼吁放缓AI技术研发步伐，以确保公共安全。中国政府则称这一提议不公平，并指责这种呼吁制定安全规则的做法意在遏制中国方面的竞争。

美中两国间能否通过此次峰会，建立或达成一个监管机制来管控AI技术，成了外界关注的重中之重。

习近平在星期四上午的讲话中对人工智能方面有一些表述，他说，中美两国“有能力也有责任发展好、管控好人工智能，确保人工智能发展始终受控于人、造福于民。”

也是在特习峰会前，美国财政贝森特说，双方同意建立AI对话机制，旨在就AI的目标和威胁达成共识。双方计划再次会晤。

对于习近平的表态，美国智库亚洲协会政策研究所的中国政治专家牛犇(Neil Thomas)在X上发文提问：“我对此持怀疑态度。特朗普与习近平能在人工智能问题上找到基本共同点吗？”

**台湾和美国对台军售**

在特朗普与习近平在白宫举行闭门会晤后，中国官方新华社发布的通稿则表示，习近平在会谈中敦促美国“慎重处理台湾问题”，并希望美方反对“台独”。到美国之音截稿时为止，白宫还没有公布会谈纪要。

分析人士普遍认为，此次峰会对台湾问题的影响有限，峰会后美中双方在台湾问题上不会有重大改变。

布鲁金斯学会约翰·桑顿中国中心主任瑞安·哈斯(Ryan Hass)在X上发帖，表示此次峰会在台湾问题上并非旨在达成某种“大交易”。哈斯写道：“我不认为特朗普在台海问题上维持现状(不统、不独、不战)的倾向会发生重大改变”。

美国西密歇根大学政治系教授王元纲在接受美国之音(VOA)采访时表示，台湾对美国来说有很高的战略价值，美国不会轻易放弃。他说：“台湾的地理位置在关键的第一岛链，左右东亚的海上运输线，对中美两国的海权较劲有着重要战略价值。”

王元纲表示，中方希望美国明确表明“反对”台独，但目前没有迹象显示美方会接受中方立场。他说：“接下来观察的重点是今年延宕已久的美国140亿美元军售是否会放行。”

美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)星期三(9月23日)重申，美国对台军售仍在审查之中，并表示美国必须在权衡此类决定与自身需求之间做出取舍。

“人们认为……我们看待军售的角度过于局限，只关注某一特定地区。但实际上，这其中也涉及到平衡我们的工业产能和军事工业基础。”卢比奥在纽约对记者做出上述表示。卢比奥同时担任特朗普总统的国家安全顾问。

**持续警告中国对伊朗的帮助**

特朗普总统星期五在和习近平一同参观国家档案馆时亲自向媒体证实，两人谈到了伊朗问题。但总统没有给出细节。

美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Perdue)星期五对CNBC说，华盛顿几星期前就告诉北京，任何对伊朗的帮助都是“完全不可接受的”。庞德伟说：“特朗普总统昨天再次明确表达了这一点。这是持续不断的警告。”

中国对俄罗斯与伊朗的支持是美国政界长期关注的问题。

新罕布什尔州民主党参议员珍妮·沙欣(Jeanne Shaheen)是参议院外交关系委员会的首席民主党议员，她星期四在X上写道：“我们知道伊朗人正在利用来自中国和俄罗斯的目标信息来帮助他们打击美国的资产。令人难以置信的是，我们没有竭尽全力去追究弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)的责任，没有去追究中国的责任，没有去阻止他们对美国男女的袭击。”

德克萨斯州共和党参议员约翰·科宁(John Cornyn)星期五援引《华尔街日报》在X上的一篇报道写道，“伊朗海关数据显示，中国实体已运送了几千批用于无人机和导弹的零部件。”

曾在特朗普总统第一任政府任职的哈德逊研究所中国中心主任余茂春在接受美国之音采访时表示，美国近年来通过包括“二级制裁”在内的政策，对与俄罗斯、伊朗等国开展相关活动的国家施加压力，因此中国与这些国家的经贸关系可能成为美方关注的对象。

他认为，特朗普政府可能会继续要求北京在相关问题上作出更加具体的承诺，而美国最终是否采取进一步措施，则取决于北京的实际行动。

**美中“建设性战略稳定关系”“拓展了”内涵**

美中共建“建设性战略稳定关系”是习近平的愿景。在白宫的欢迎仪式上以及星期五的茶叙中，习近平都提到了“建设性战略稳定关系”。 “建设性战略稳定关系”是中国在北京峰会后一再强调的成果。

在星期五茶叙时，习近平提到了“建设性战略稳定关系”拓展了内涵。他说：“我们定位呢，中美关系是相互尊重、公平、 对等的建设性战略稳定关系。”

“公平和对等或互惠”应该是来自美国的理念。

美国国会下属的美中经济与安全审查委员会(USCC)主席共和党委员薛瑞福(Randall Schriver)和民主党委员克里斯·斯莱文(Chris Slevin)在习近平的华盛顿访问前曾接受美国之音(VOA)访问，谈到了美中“建设性战略稳定关系”。

薛瑞福说：“在我看来，他们似乎在将美国和中国描绘成两个地位平等的伟大国家，势均力敌。他们还表示，双方有机会建立一种能够共同应对区域和全球挑战的关系。他们谈到了战略稳定的框架。美国会加上基于公平和互惠，但中国没有加。”

斯莱文说**，“**如果你听听，如果你和政府官员谈谈，我们在这里重申了这一点，那就是要建立一个基于公平和互惠的战略框架。我认为这对于构建对话框架，以及我们希望从峰会中达成的目标，都是一个重要的补充。”

**被拘美国人尚无公开结果**

习近平访美前，被美国政府认定遭中国错误拘押的华裔地震学家陈友麟和缅甸问题学者敏辛(Min Zin)的家属呼吁特朗普要求中方释放两人。

白宫此前表示，特朗普预计会在峰会中提出这些案件。不过，白宫星期五发表的访问总结和中国公布的会谈纪要都没有说明两人的案件是否被讨论，或中方是否作出回应。

**大熊猫和欢迎10万美国青少年**

在此次美中峰会上，习近平再次启动了“熊猫外交”。他在星期四白宫欢迎仪式上致辞时宣布，中国将向亚特兰大动物园赠送两只大熊猫，并表示，未来五年邀请十万名美国青少年去华交流学习。

这也是本次峰会宣布的最具体的成果。

但美国欧道明大学国际商业讲座教授李少民表示，大熊猫和未来五年邀请十万名美国青少年去华交流学习，表面看，这是习近平向美国伸出的两根引人注目的“橄榄枝”、是慷慨友好的姿态，但实际上它恰恰是美中关系走向根本性决裂的信号。

李少民告诉美国之音：“这两个在我看来已经是很不祥的预示，预示着中美关系又退回到多少年前。中国现在又得用这种中国文化来打动美国了，所以看起来挺失败的”。

**专家看峰会成果**

对于此次峰会的成果，许多分析人士持认为，峰会象征性意义高，实质成果少。

华盛顿智库战略与国际研究中心中国商业问题专家甘思德(Scott Kennedy)在X上发文说，他认为迄今为止，此次峰会的表现甚至未能达到人们最初的低预期。

甘思德写道：“结果很可能仅仅是贸易与出口管制休战期延长两个月，特朗普总统对开展实质性人工智能对话兴致寥寥、几只大熊猫、参观直升机停机坪，以及中国对台湾施加更大压力”。

甘思德认为，双方在做出让步方面都进展缓慢，目前也尚无关于“以300亿美元关税减让换取300亿美元采购”或伊朗问题的消息。

美国西密歇根大学政治系教授王元纲在接受美国之音(VOA)采访时指出，美中之所以希望保持稳定是因为美国受伊朗战争和国内诸多问题困扰，不希望在东亚节外生枝；而中国也因国内经济问题希望美中之间能保持战略稳定。

他强调，长期来看，中国崛起挑战了美国的世界领导地位，美中之间存在难以化解的结构性的矛盾，元首外交能发挥的功能有限。王元纲告诉美国之音：“未来美中关系的安全竞争只会增强，不会减少。”

白宫星期五公布的类似会谈纪要的声明的最后一点似乎应证了王元纲的说法。 声明说，这次国事访问彰显了美国的实力，促进了美国的经济利益，并明确揭示了一点：当美国凭借实力地位发挥领导作用时，和平与繁荣才能最为稳固。

title: ‘Xi, You’re Not Welcome’: As Trump Hosts China’s Leader, Thousands Protest in Washington
summary: On September 24, more than 3,000 Tibetans gathered in Washington to protest Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House, in what organizers described as the largest-ever Tibetan rally in North America. The rally was organized by
content:
On September 24, more than 3,000 Tibetans gathered in Washington to protest Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House, in what organizers described as the largest-ever Tibetan rally in North America. The rally was organized by [Tibetan Youth Congress](https://www.tibetanyouthcongress.org/) (TYC) and supported by other Tibetan activist organizations.

The protesters came with demands that they said should be part of the China-U.S. relationship: that Trump raise human rights with Xi, that China release [political and religious prisoners](https://thediplomat.com/2025/03/chinas-system-of-mass-arbitrary-detention/), and that Tibetans be allowed to preserve their language and culture. The group also demanded the repeal of China’s new [Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law](https://thediplomat.com/2026/07/whither-an-international-response-to-chinas-ethnic-unity-law/), which took effect in July and promotes what Beijing calls a shared sense of identity among China’s 56 ethnic groups. Tibetan activists say the law further advances Beijing’s efforts to [assimilate](https://savetibet.org/new-prc-ethnic-unity-and-progress-law/) Tibetans into Chinese identity. Chinese authorities say the law protects minority rights while promoting ethnic unity.

“Human rights should not be left outside of their talks,” said Tencho Gyatso, president of the International Campaign for Tibet. “The Tibetans, the Uyghurs, the Hong Kongers, the Taiwanese, we want to make sure our voices are also heard there.”

The demonstration unfolded as Xi made his first state visit to Washington in more than a decade. U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed him to the White House for talks that touched on AI, trade, and other issues, while the two governments were also dealing with disputes over Taiwan, Iran and rare earths. Trump hosted Xi at a state dinner on the evening of September 24.

Outside, Tibetan protesters marched through the capital carrying Tibetan flags and signs reading “Xi Jinping is guilty of genocide” and “Tibet was never a part of China.” By the end of the day, the demonstration had expanded into a coalition that included Uyghur, Southern Mongolian, Chinese democracy, Taiwanese, Burmese, Falun Gong, and Chinese Christian groups, all people that have suffered under the Chinese Communist Party.

Protesters holds signs criticizing Chinese President Xi Jinping during a demonstration in Washington, D.C., on September 24, 2026. Photo by Tsering Dolka Gurung

The rally began at about 9 a.m. outside the Chinese Embassy, where protesters gathered before marching toward the U.S. Capitol. Police were deployed around the demonstration as the crowd assembled. The protesters then moved through Washington, with Connecticut Avenue closed to accommodate the march. The crowd passed through Dupont Circle before arriving at the Capitol, where several speakers addressed the demonstrators.

Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and Rep. Jim McGovern, a Massachusetts Democrat, joined the rally. McGovern called for human rights to be included in Trump’s discussions with Xi.

“No Xi in D.C. without human rights,” McGovern told the crowd.

He also criticized Republican lawmakers, who he said had declined to join efforts urging the administration to press China on human rights. “Are they afraid of Donald Trump? Are they afraid he’ll be offended if they ask him to ask Xi to release prisoners of conscience?” McGovern said.

U.S. Rep. Jim McGovern speaks at a rally outside the U.S. Capitol during a demonstration against Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., on September 24, 2026. Photo by Tsering Dolka Gurung.

Pelosi also spoke in support of the protesters, calling attention to human rights in Tibet and urging the release of prisoners of conscience.

For many Tibetan protesters, Thursday’s demonstration was also shaped by the death of Lobga Rangzen, a longtime Tibetan independence activist who died after [self-immolating](https://thediplomat.com/2026/07/why-a-tibetan-protester-set-himself-on-fire-outside-the-united-nations/) outside the United Nations in New York on July 2. Rangzen, 52, had called for Tibetan independence and unity in a final message before setting himself on fire.

Jigme Ugen, president of the Tibetan National Congress, said the size of the demonstration showed that the Tibetan independence movement remained active.

“This is the biggest gathering, as such, to not just protest Xi Jinping, but also to tell the world and the U.S. government that the Tibetan movement, and the call for Tibetan independence, is still very much alive,” Ugen said.

Tsering Chomphel, president of the Tibetan Youth Congress, who traveled from India for the protest, said people had come from New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Philadelphia, Boston, Chicago, Vermont, and Toronto. “This is the first-ever mass gathering in North America. Whenever Xi Jinping or a Chinese delegation visits, TYC will be there to make sure our voices are heard.”

Tibetan protesters hold flags outside the U.S. Capitol during a demonstration against Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., on September 24, 2026.
Photo by Tsering Dolka Gurung.

Seventeen Tibetans had set off on foot from the United Nations headquarters in New York on September 17, walking through Philadelphia before reaching Washington on the evening of September 23 – the same day Xi arrived. Rangzen Dolkar, one of the walkers, said the journey was meant to raise awareness about Tibet and _Pawo_ Lobga Rangzen’s death.

Pawo is an honorary title given to any individual who has sacrificed their lives through self-immolation to bring attention to Tibet’s situation.

“I am a mother of two kids, and I left my kids home. We all took off from work and left on this journey,” she said. “People stop us on the way and ask us what we’re doing because they see the flag. It gives us an opportunity to speak about Tibet and what Pawo Lobga Rangzen sacrificed his life for.”

After the rally at the Capitol, the protestors marched to Franklin Park, half a mile from the White House, where speakers from the Uyghur, Taiwanese, Burmese, and Hong Kong communities addressed the crowd.

Misran Dolan, president of the Uyghur American Association, framed the gathering as a common demand for political and religious freedom. “Free the [Uyghurs](https://thediplomat.com/2023/03/as-survivors-of-chinas-genocide-we-must-bear-witness/). Free the Tibetans. Keep Taiwan free. Keep Hong Kong free. Keep China free,” Dolan told the crowd.

“All of us here have moved away from our homelands,” he said. “And now we’re here in the United States … to exercise those rights – freedom of speech, freedom of expression, freedom of religion.” About 200 members of the Uyghur community attended, according to Dolan.

Protesters hold Taiwanese, Tibetan, and Uyghur flags and signs during a demonstration against Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., on September 24, 2026. Photo by Tsering Dolka Gurung.

The gathering also included Chinese democracy activists. About 50 members of the Democratic Party of China traveled from Los Angeles, according to Zheng Zhou, a member of the group.

“We want Xi Jinping to stop persecuting people. We want him to free Jimmy Lai, Ding Jiaxi,” said Zhou. Lai, the billionaire founder of Apple Daily, Hong Kong’s most prominent pro-democracy newspaper, and a vocal critic of the Chinese Communist Party was sentenced to 20 years in prison earlier this February after being convicted of conspiracy to commit sedition and collusion with foreign forces. Marco Rubio, the U.S. secretary of state, had urged the CCP to grant him humanitarian parole calling the sentence [unjust and tragic](https://www.state.gov/releases/office-of-the-spokesperson/2026/02/sentencing-in-jimmy-lai-case),

Daniel Zhou, a Chinese Christian affiliated with an [underground church](https://thediplomat.com/2026/03/despite-growing-crackdown-independent-religious-groups-defy-chinas-communist-party/) – churches that operate outside China’s state-controlled religious system and whose members can face detention and other restrictions from authorities – spoke about the persecution of Christians in China.

“Our church leaders have to stay in Chinese jails, leaving their families praying and crying at home, just because they wanted to practice their religion peacefully in China,” Zhou said.

Cynthia Sun, a senior researcher at the Falun Dafa Information Center, said her friends from the United States had family members killed in Chinese prison through forced organ harvesting. “When they went to see their dead parents at the mortuary, their bodies were split open, there were stitches, and they were missing a heart or a kidney,” she said.

Falun Gong is a spiritual practice that emerged in China in the 1990s and was banned by Chinese authorities in 1999. The Chinese government has been accused of forcibly harvesting organs from imprisoned Falun Gong practitioners. In 2019, the[China Tribunal](https://www.bmj.com/content/365/bmj.l4287), an independent people’s tribunal, concluded that forced organ harvesting has occurred in China on a significant scale and that Falun Gong practitioners were likely the main source of organs.

Sun described the persecution of Falun Gong practitioners as something that had followed her throughout her life.

“I was born in July 1999, the month and year that the persecution began,” she said. “When I graduated high school, I thought the persecution would end by the time I got to college. But now I’m in grad school. I’m engaged, I’m getting married, and the persecution is still going on.”

“I don’t want this to be the [burden](https://thediplomat.com/2024/08/first-known-survivor-of-chinas-forced-organ-harvesting-speaks-out/) of my children, my grandchildren,” she said.

For the Tibetan organizers, the rally was not simply a call for another statement from Washington.

“Tibetans are not looking for a statement at this point,” Ugen said. “The U.S. government already has enough laws that have been passed by Congress, and all they need to do is to actually stand on those.” In 2020, Trump signed the Tibetan Policy and Support Act of 2020 into law, which strengthened U.S. policy on Tibet.

Later in the evening, protesters marched toward the White House.

Police had erected barricades near 14th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue, separating the demonstrators from another group of people carrying Chinese flags and supporting Xi. The two groups shouted at each other from opposite sides of the barricades. Tibetan protesters waved Tibetan flags and chanted as the other group shouted back across the street. The confrontation grew increasingly loud, but there was no physical altercation.

Xi Jinping supporters gather behind police barricades during demonstrations surrounding Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington, D.C., on September 24, 2026. Metropolitan Police Officers stand between the groups. Photo by Tsering Dolka Gurung.

Inside the White House, Xi was attending the state dinner hosted by Trump. Outside, the opposing groups remained separated by police barricades.

For Ugen, the demonstration was ultimately about making sure Tibet was not left out of the China-U.S. conversation.

“The basics of the conversation is beyond Taiwan, AI, trade,” Ugen said. “We are telling the world that if there’s justice in the world, it should come through Tibet.”

title: China & Taiwan Update, September 25, 2026
summary: ## Toplines **Chinese Communist Party (CCP) General Secretary Xi Jinping met with US President Donald Trump in Washington, DC, from September 22 through 24. The People’s Republic of China (PRC) and the United States agreed to an extended tr
content:
## Toplines

**Chinese Communist Party (CCP) General Secretary Xi Jinping met with US President Donald Trump in Washington, DC, from September 22 through 24. The People’s Republic of China (PRC) and the United States agreed to an extended trade truce, with both sides praising positive US-PRC relations.**US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with PRC Vice Premier He Lifeng on September 23.[1] The United States and the PRC agreed to extend the trade truce two months beyond the original November 10 end date.[2] Bessent also reported that the United States may be open to considering a more comprehensive US-PRC trade deal.[3] Bessent stated that the PRC was meeting its commitments on purchasing US soybeans, but had yet to commit fully to the originally agreed-upon purchases of other agricultural goods.[4]

Bessent and He previously met to discuss other bilateral concerns, including artificial intelligence (AI) safeguards and establishing a bilateral dialogue on AI security, on September 20.[5] Xi similarly emphasized the importance of bilateral cooperation on AI security during his summit with Trump. Xi said that the United States and PRC should ensure that the development of AI technology remains “under human control” and serves the interests of the people.[6] Xi stated that the United States and PRC have “intertwined interests” and benefit from cooperation, rhetoric consistent with that of the last Xi-Trump meeting in May 2026.[7]

The PRC appears to have taken a more conciliatory approach toward certain areas of significant US concern prior to the summit, announcing a new set of regulations surrounding illegal drug components — a significant component of US-PRC relations amid the US fentanyl crisis.[8] The PRC announced on September 22 that it would require permits to ship two precursor chemicals to the United States, Mexico, and Canada, supplementing similar legislation from 2025.[9] Xi also called for 100,000 American students to visit the PRC over the next five years.[10] Xi similarly announced the delivery of two new pandas to the United States, consistent with past instances of “panda diplomacy” meant to showcase positive PRC bilateral relations with the recipient nation.[11] Xi’s statements also referenced the “Thucydides trap” — the notion that a rising power inevitably clashes with an existing one — when calling for increased bilateral cooperation to reduce the risk of future conflict.[12]

Xi’s rhetoric emphasized bilateral cooperation and highlighted the common goals of the United States and PRC, likely in an attempt to highlight similarities between the two states and suggest that the two share common strategic interests. Xi’s September 24 speech highlighted the US and PRC’s dual role as great powers and emphasized that both must maintain a “constructive and stable relationship.”[13] Xi stated that the resolution of global issues hinges on US-PRC cooperation and that the international community supported a positive US-PRC relationship.[14] Xi confirmed Trump’s invitation to an APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in the PRC in November.[15] Xi’s September 24 dinner address echoed these themes, emphasizing the shared history between the United States and PRC, including their alliance against Japan in World War II.[16] Xi drew a connection between Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement and the PRC’s push for national rejuvenation, stating that both movements could “complement” one another.[17]

**The PRC may take advantage of seemingly warming US-PRC ties to attempt to influence US policy on Taiwan.** Xi warned Trump on September 24 to “oppose” “Taiwan independence,” the first time he has used such direct phrasing.[18] The PRC typically warns the United States not to “support” “Taiwan independence.” This wording change, while minor, could represent a renewed PRC effort to change US policy on Taiwan.

The Xi-Trump talks did not produce any changes in the US’ Taiwan policy. The PRC could perceive US openness to continued dialogue as an opportunity to extract concessions on Taiwan in the future, however. The United States has already delayed an arms sale to Taiwan worth $14 billion.[19] Trump has previously called arms sales to Taiwan a “negotiating chip” in reference to dialogue with the PRC.[20] US officials have blamed Taiwanese arms sale delays on supply chain constraints imposed by other conflicts.[21] US Secretary of State Marco Rubio referenced supply chain challenges when asked about arms deliveries to Taiwan on September 23.[22] Taiwanese Ministry of National Defense deputy spokesperson Chiao Fu-chun said on September 23 that Taiwan would maintain “close contact” with the United States to receive updates on the status of these arms sales.[23]

US arms sales to Taiwan are authorized under the 1979 Taiwan Relations Act (TRA), which stipulates that the United States will provide Taiwan with defense articles that enable Taiwan to “maintain a sufficient self-defense capability.”[24] US arms sales to Taiwan receive bipartisan support from the US Congress. Four Republican senators called on Trump on September 23 to release Taiwan’s security funding.[25] Delays in arms shipments to Taiwan pose an ongoing threat to Taiwan’s defense and risk fueling PRC information operations aimed at undermining US-Taiwan ties.

## Key Takeaways

1.   **US-PRC Relations:**US President Donald Trump and Chinese Communist Party (CCP) General Secretary Xi Jinping held a summit in Washington, DC, from September 22 to 24. The United States and People’s Republic of China (PRC) agreed to increase cooperation in a number of sectors and extend the US-PRC trade truce another two months. The PRC could view increased US-PRC cooperation as an opportunity to influence the US’ Taiwan policy.

## Cross-Strait Relations

### Taiwan

**Taiwanese Minister of Labor Hung Sun-han attended the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Nanjing, PRC, on September 21 — the first official trip to the PRC by a ministry head within the William Lai Ching-te administration. Hung’s presence at APEC represents the maintenance of the status quo for Cross-Strait relations, given Taiwan’s long-standing attendance at APEC.**Hung and the Taiwanese delegation participated in the meeting under the name “Chinese Taipei.” Hung stated upon his return to Taiwan that the delegation was able to fully participate in the forum and receive the same treatment as other member economies without being “bullied.”[26] The meeting centered on the development of human resources during ongoing labor market disruptions caused by AI and technological and demographic changes. Hung spoke at the summit on AI guidelines and risk management to prevent a negative impact on workers’ rights.[27] Taiwan’s previous trade representative and minister-without-portfolio Yang Jen-ni also attended a May 2026 APEC meeting of commerce ministers in Suzhou without incident.[28]

Hung’s participation in the meeting did not represent a significant change in the status quo for Taiwan’s international position or Cross-Strait relations. Taiwan’s designation as “Chinese Taipei” at APEC meetings has remained since Taiwan joined APEC in 1991.[29] The PRC has not altered its stance on Taiwan’s participation in APEC despite its rhetoric towards the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), which it views as a party of “separatists.” Hung is a former DPP legislator with a record of speaking out on issues politically sensitive to the PRC.[30] Hung stated that the summit was an important element of Taiwanese international participation. Hung also clarified that the delegation’s visit to the PRC was a representation of the importance of the forum, rather than a signal of warming cross-Strait relations.[31] The PRC’s engagement with DPP delegations at APEC appears to be an exception to its typical assertion that cross-Strait engagement must align with the 1992 Consensus. The 1992 Consensus is a semi-official agreement between the CCP and the Kuomintang (KMT) based on an agreement that there is “One China,” but disagreeing on what “China” means. The DPP does not officially accept the 1992 consensus.

### China

**Former US Army soldier Ruoyu Duan pled guilty to conspiring to spy for the PRC on September 16**. **The PRC seeks to acquire information on US and allied military units and systems that could impede a future PRC invasion of Taiwan.** Duan recruited two active-duty soldiers to gather US military secrets for the PRC from 2021 to 2025, including technical manuals on high mobility artillery rocket systems (HIMARS), information on Bradley and Stryker fighting vehicles, and information on US military readiness for a potential conflict with the PRC.[32] The soldiers also stole several classified hard drives and an encryption-capable computer to sell to the PRC. US authorities arrested and charged the three co-conspirators in March 2025.[33]

PRC espionage operations seek to acquire US military secrets and advanced technology, likely to improve the People’s Liberation Army (PLA)’s military capabilities and discover vulnerabilities in US and allied forces that the PRC could exploit to defeat potential US and allied intervention in a future Taiwan conflict.[34] US, Australian, and Taiwanese armed forces currently field HIMARS, and Japan, the Philippines, and South Korea have hosted US-operated HIMARS during combined training exercises.[35] Taiwan is planning forward deployment of HIMARS to its outlying islands, allowing Taiwan to strike PLA Navy (PLAN) bases along the PRC’s east coast and stationary PLA amphibious landing ships during an invasion, significantly degrading the invading PLA force.[36] US and allied forces can also rapidly forward-deploy HIMARS directly from transport aircraft to aid in a Taiwan scenario.[37]

## Southeast Asia

### Philippines

**The Philippines and Taiwan are likely expanding bilateral cooperation in ways that could improve their ability to combat PRC coercion. The PRC likely views enhanced Philippine-Taiwan ties as a threat to its regional ambitions.**Taiwanese media reported on September 22 that an unnamed source confirmed reports that the Taiwanese Coast Guard Administration (CGA) had transferred a decommissioned patrol vessel to the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG).[38] The vessel is a 500-ton patrol ship that was in service with the CGA since 2008.[39] Taiwan typically only transfers decommissioned vessels to states that officially recognize Taiwan’s statehood, which the Philippines does not.[40] Taiwan’s CGA also plans to visit the Philippines in 2027, the first such visit since the Philippines switched its recognition from Taiwan to the PRC in 1975.[41] Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung also announced on September 15 that Taiwan would establish its second Philippine representative office in Cebu.[42] These developments may indicate that the Philippines and Taiwan are enhancing their bilateral relations, despite the Philippines’ recognition of the PRC.

Taiwan and the Philippines face a common coercive threat from the PRC that cooperation, particularly between coast guards, could help address. The China Coast Guard (CCG) and PLAN frequently operate around the Philippines and Taiwan’s sovereign territory and claimed exclusive economic zones (EEZ).[43] The CCG often uses its vessels’ numerical and size advantage over CGA and PCG vessels to attempt to support the PRC’s territorial claims and aggressive maritime exercises.[44] Enhanced CGA-PCG cooperation could allow Taiwan and the Philippines to coordinate effective responses to PRC coercive activity in the South China Sea and Taiwan Strait.

# Philippines accuses China of obstructing resupply mission in South China Sea

## Manila cites violations of international law in latest South China Sea standoff

September 25, 2026 at 11:43 am

[](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=timeslive.co.za "Make us a preferred source")[](https://news.google.com/search?q=timeslive.co.za "Follow us on Google News")

Share current article via Email Share current article via Facebook Share current article via Twitter Share current article via LinkedIn

## [Reuters](https://www.timeslive.co.za/author/reuters-agency)
News Agency

Enter fullscreen mode displaying this image.Expand

The Philippines called on China to stop interfering with its lawful resupply missions. Picture: (PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD)

The Philippines Coast Guard (PCG) accused China on Friday of obstructing a resupply mission for troops on board a grounded World War 2-era warship in the South China Sea, saying the action “put Filipino personnel at risk”.

The PCG said the China Coast Guard and the People’s Liberation Army Navy on Thursday “obstructed a legitimate humanitarian and sustainment operation” to Second Thomas Shoal.

It said China’s actions were inconsistent with international law and a 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated Beijing’s sweeping claims in the South China Sea.

The Philippines called on China to stop interfering with the resupply missions.

The PCG said it would continue its lawful operations in the South China Sea and exercise Manila’s sovereign rights and jurisdiction in the waterway.

The Chinese embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In 2024 Manila and Beijing reached a provisional arrangement on resupply missions to Second Thomas Shoal, which the Philippines’ foreign ministry has said helped prevent confrontations between the two sides.

In July Manila accused the China Coast Guard of firing a water cannon at government vessels near Scarborough Shoal and striking a Philippines Navy staff member with a wooden baton during a separate encounter near Second Thomas Shoal.

**Reuters**

content:
华盛顿 —

唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统在结束接待中国国家主席习近平对美国进行的三天国事访问之际表示，美国展示了实力以及与中国的友谊。这次在华盛顿举行的美中元首峰会在星期五(9月25日)结束。特朗普宣布今年还会与习近平有两次会晤。他的助理指出，美中双方在化解在贸易和技术问题的紧张关系方面取得了进展。

在习近平和夫人彭丽媛启程离开美国不久，特朗普在真相社交(Truth Social)的一则帖文中写道：“这次会晤对中国和美国来说都是友谊、实力和成功的会晤。我们将于11月在中国再次会晤，然后又于12月在佛罗里达州迈阿密的20国集团会议上会晤。”

白宫在星期五晚些时候发表的[声明](https://www.voachinese.com/a/white-house-readout-on-xi-state-visit-conclusion-20260925/8204460.html)中说，这次国事访问“彰显了美国的实力地位，促进了美国的经济利益，并明确揭示了一点：当美国凭借实力地位发挥领导作用时，和平与繁荣才最为稳固。”

这是中国长期领导人习近平2015年以来首次对美国进行国事访问，在此之前，两位元首今年5月举行了一次峰会，那次是习近平在北京接待特朗普。在本星期的峰会期间，特朗普总统给予了习近平夫妇隆重礼遇，在习近平夫妇抵达安德鲁斯联合基地时亲赴机场迎接，这是美国总统对来访外国领导人的罕见友好姿态。他还在白宫举行了盛大的欢迎仪式，展示美军实力，并在白宫东厅举办国宴。

特朗普总统夫妇与习近平主席夫妇参观美国国家档案馆。(2026年9月25日)

星期五，特朗普总统在引导习近平和彭丽媛短暂参观国家档案馆时说，他和习近平进行了“很棒的会晤”，他预计将会有对美国农民和“每个人”都“很棒”的结果。参观国家档案馆是此次国事访问的最后一站。

两位星期五接受美国各电视网采访谈论这次峰会的特朗普助理说，美国在减少与中国的贸易逆差方面取得了进展，在管控与北京的人工智能开发竞争方面也取得了进展。美国在人工智能方面是全球领军者。

特朗普总统本星期说，他将把人工智能(AI)的名称改为超级智能(SI)，他说，SI对这种技术来说是更为准确的名称。

美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)对CNBC说，特朗普政府星期一将公布“有关我们在过去几周与中方谈判期间所取得的成就的更多细节”。

资料照片：美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特和美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔在纽约与中国副总理何立峰会晤后与媒体交谈。(2026年9月20日)

他预览了这些细节并表示，峰会达成的一项协议是美国和中国将保护“非敏感”贸易不受未来纠纷所产生的任何关税措施的影响。

他说，这类非敏感贸易将包括美国向中国出口的农产品和医疗设备以及中国向美国出口的消费产品。

蒙塔纳州共和党籍联邦参议员史蒂夫·戴恩斯(Steve Daines)星期四在X平台写道，拥有中国的市场准入对美国农民和牧民来说是“关键”。

财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)星期三在接受媒体采访时宣布把美中关税休战延长两个月。美国贸易代表格里尔说，这项休战将作为“合规期”，美国在此期间将密切关注中国先前做出的购买更多美国大豆并解除稀土矿物出口限制的承诺。稀土对美国制造业来说至关重要。

美中2025年达成的关税休战把美国和中国去年对彼此征收的关税封顶。贝森特已表示，休战将从11月10日延长到2027年1月10日。

此外，格里尔说，与中国在贸易方面取得的进展使美国走上今年把贸易逆差从2025年的2020亿美元减少到1400亿美元的轨道上。

美国驻中国大使庞德伟(David Perdue)对福克斯新闻(Fox News)说，双方在管控AI/SI竞争方面取得一项“突破”。他说，美国和中国同意建立一个“危机机制”，就AI/SI开发构成的危险进行对话。

摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙(左)与美国驻华大使庞德伟在进入白宫出席为中国国家主席习近平举办的国宴前与执法人员交谈。（2026年9月24日）

“如果不就这一问题与中国--这是世界第二大经济体，同时也堪称拥有世界第二大军事力量的国家--进行接触，那将是不负责任的，”庞德伟对CNBC说。“因此，令我感到鼓舞的是，我们在合作方面至少取得了一些进展，并且至少开始探讨如何就此共同努力。”

格里尔告诉哥伦比亚广播公司(CBS)说，美中之间将在“未来一个月左右”就AI/SI举行另一次会晤。

格里尔对CNBC表示，特朗普与习近平的会晤并未谈判美国对先进计算机芯片及半导体技术的对华出口限制问题，这些是推动美国在AI/SI领域取得进展的关键技术。他指出，此类芯片是美国技术“皇冠上的明珠”，而针对它们的出口管制属于国家安全议题，华盛顿方面已明确将这个议题“排除出桌面”。

马萨诸塞州的民主党籍联邦参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦(Elizabeth Warren)星期三在X平台上写道：“中国不应获取我们的先进技术。”

title: ICT joins Tibetans, rights groups, Congressional partners in urging Trump to put Tibet and human rights on the agenda during Xi visit
summary: As Chinese President Xi Jinping traveled to Washington for a state visit Sep. 23-25, the International Campaign for Tibet (ICT) joined Tibetan organizations, Tibet supporters, human rights groups and members of the U.S. Congress in a coordi
content:
As Chinese President Xi Jinping traveled to Washington for a state visit Sep. 23-25, the International Campaign for Tibet (ICT) joined Tibetan organizations, Tibet supporters, human rights groups and members of the U.S. Congress in a coordinated campaign calling for Tibet and human rights to be prioritized both during Xi’s visit and in the broader U.S.-China relationship.

Through advocacy with policymakers, coalition initiatives and participation in protests, rallies, press conferences and other public actions, ICT worked alongside partners to highlight Tibetan political prisoners, the disappearance of the 11th Panchen Lama, Chinese government interference in Tibetan Buddhist succession, coercive assimilation, transnational repression and China’s repressive new so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law.”

Hundreds of Tibetans from across North America gathered at Washington D.C. on Sep. 24 to protest Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit. (ICT)

The campaigns culminated in a day-long mobilization on Sep. 24 by Tibetans and Tibet supporters that brought together over 2,000 Tibetan Americans from across North America, including Toronto, Minnesota, New York, Indiana, and many other locales. ICT joined the Tibetan-led protests outside the Chinese embassy and the peaceful march to the U.S. Capitol, where protestors were joined by congressional and human rights supporters. The Tibetan Youth Congress and Capital Area Tibetan Association led the Tibetan American mobilization, with participation and support from ICT, Students for a Free Tibet, Tibetan National Congress and other Tibetan organizations.

ICT also participated alongside Uyghurs, Hong Kongers, Taiwanese, Southern Mongolians and Chinese democracy activists and dissidents in broader coalition protests during Xi’s visit, with a candlelight vigil at Franklin Park.

The public mobilization was part of a broader advocacy effort before and during Xi’s visit. Ahead of Xi’s arrival on September 23, [ICT called on President Donald Trump to make Tibet and human rights central to his discussions with X](https://savetibet.org/ict-calls-on-president-trump-to-publicly-press-xi-on-tibet-the-panchen-lama-and-human-rights/)i and to raise these issues both privately and publicly. ICT urged renewed substantive dialogue between Chinese authorities and Tibetan representatives, the release of the Panchen Lama, Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, and a repeal of the so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” (EUPL) and other policies threatening Tibetan religion, language, culture and identity.

On Sep. 24, Rep. Jim McGovern addresses hundreds of Tibetans gathered outside the U.S. Capitol to protest Xi’s visit to Washington. (ICT)

ICT simultaneously worked through broader coalitions. [On Sep. 16, it joined a coalition of 30 human rights, democracy and religious-freedom organizations in an open letter calling on Xi](https://www.nchrd.org/2026/09/an-open-letter-to-chinese-communist-party-general-secretary-xi-jinping/) to release prisoners of conscience, end transnational repression and undertake legal reforms. The coalition included International Tibet Network, Campaign for Uyghurs, Uyghur Human Rights Project, Human Rights Foundation, Freedom House, Amnesty International USA, Hong Kong Watch, ChinaAid, Reporters Without Borders and the Committee to Protect Journalists, among others.

ICT also participated in a [Religious Freedom Institute and International Religious Freedom Summit event on CCP repression](https://religiousfreedominstitute.org/events/ccp-oppression-in-america-and-china/). ICT Executive Director Ryan Fioresi and Head of Research and Monitoring Bhuchung K. Tsering spoke alongside former U.S. Ambassador-at-Large for International Religious Freedom Sam Brownback and representatives of other affected communities. Speakers addressed imprisonment, surveillance, forced labor, family retaliation and pressure reaching people outside China.

Fioresi focused on restrictions on Tibetan Buddhism, and said restrictions have entered “the most intimate spaces of religious conviction,” affecting who may pursue monastic life, how teachings are transmitted and how Tibetan communities practice their faith. Fioresi also addressed Chinese government interference in religious succession, citing the case of Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, who was disappeared by the Chinese authorities after he was recognized by the Dalai Lama as the 11th Panchen Lama.

Fioresi argued that the case offers a warning about how Chinese authorities could seek to influence the eventual succession of the Dalai Lama. “Those decisions belong to Tibetan Buddhists themselves,” he said.

At the U.S. Capitol grounds on Sep. 24, Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi and Rep. Jim McGovern join hundreds of Tibetan protesting Xi’s visit to Washington. (ICT)

ICT Head of Research and Monitoring Bhuchung K. Tsering focused on the concerns around the new EUPL and emphasized that the legislation codifies Sinicization and coercive assimilation and “further undermines Tibetans’ fundamental freedom to preserve their unique culture, religion and way of life.”

Tsering said policies implemented in Tibetan areas over more than a decade helped test an approach later incorporated into national legislation. His remarks highlighted four areas of concern: increased emphasis on a single Chinese national identity and Mandarin-language education; the treatment of ethnic affairs through a national-security framework; ideological influence extending into family life; and the law’s reach beyond China’s borders through Article 63.

Tsering called on Trump to urge Xi to repeal the new law, protect Tibetan cultural and religious rights and seek the release of, or independent access to, the Panchen Lama.

As Xi arrived in Washington, ICT President Tencho Gyatso also participated in a campaign organized by the Human Rights Foundation to call for the release of the 11the Panchen Lama. The campaign formed part of the broader human rights mobilization surrounding the visit and followed the joint call by ICT and other organizations for the release of prisoners of conscience, including Gedhun Choekyi Nyima.

### **Congressional partners amplify calls on Tibet and human rights**

Members of Congress amplified these concerns as Xi arrived in Washington.

A [joint congressional letter signed by 37 members of the House of Representatives](https://savetibet.org/dozens-of-house-representatives-urge-trump-to-press-xi-to-repeal-chinas-repressive-ethnic-unity-law/) urged President Trump to raise the EUPL directly with Xi during their meetings and to press for its repeal. In the Sep. 23 letter — led by Jamie Raskin (D-MD), Jim McGovern (D-MA) and Gregory Meeks (D-NY) — lawmakers cited concerns about the [EUPL’s implications for Tibetans, Uyghurs, other ethnic and religious communities](https://savetibet.org/ict-joins-tibetans-in-protests-urging-global-action-against-chinas-new-ethnic-unity-law/), human rights advocates and critics of the Chinese government living outside China.

On Sep. 23, Rep. Jim McGovern also convened a press conference with representatives of Tibetan, Uyghur, Hong Kong and Chinese communities. McGovern called on the administration to raise political prisoners, fundamental freedoms and other human rights issues directly with Xi and specifically criticized the EUPL, arguing that it threatens the distinct cultural and linguistic identities of non-Chinese communities.

“Our call today is ‘no Xi in DC without human rights’,” McGovern said. “Our call must also be ‘no US foreign policy without human rights’.”

Tibetans protest Xi visit to Washington on Sep. 24 (ICT)

ICT President Tencho Gyatso joined McGovern at the press conference, urging the administration to raise Tibetan political prisoners, the Panchen Lama, the forced assimilation of Tibetan children and the need to resume meaningful dialogue on Tibet. Her message ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting was direct: “Put human rights on the agenda. Put Tibet on the agenda and ask where is the Panchen Lama?”

Gyatso also spoke personally about carrying a connection to Tibet despite never having seen her homeland, saying the issues at stake concern whether Tibetan language, religion, culture and identity will survive.

Gyatso connected the Panchen Lama’s disappearance to the broader question of who has the right to determine Tibetan Buddhist leadership, including the eventual succession of the Dalai Lama. She also warned that repression increasingly reaches beyond China through technology, surveillance and transnational pressure against people exercising their rights in the United States.

Congressional support was also visible at the Sep. 24 Capitol rally, where Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi and Congressman McGovern stood with Tibetan leaders, activists and representatives of other communities.

Pelosi emphasized the preservation of Tibetan identity, religion, language and culture, and on following the message and example of His Holiness the Dalai Lama to continue striving for Tibet. “We have to demand and insist,” she said, “that the religion, the language, the faith, the community, the sense of community, in Tibet be respected.”

Rep. McGovern reiterated four priorities: freeing prisoners of conscience, countering transnational repression, rejecting the EUPL, and ensuring that Tibetans, Uyghurs and others are not deported to China.

### **A day of Tibetan and coalition protest**

The Sep. 24 mobilization extended across Washington. After gathering outside the Chinese Embassy, Tibetan protesters marched toward the Capitol for the afternoon rally. Participants in the Rangzen Walk, organized by Tibetan National Congress New York/New Jersey, joined the mobilization after walking from New York to Washington. Students for a Free Tibet organized additional protest actions, including demonstrations outside the Waldorf Astoria and at Joint Base Andrews, ensuring that Tibetan voices were visible at multiple locations associated with Xi’s visit.

On Sep. 24, ICT President Tencho Gyatso addresses hundreds of Tibetans gathered outside the U.S. Capitol to protest Xi’s visit to Washington. (ICT)

At the Capitol rally, Capital Area Tibetan Association President Tenzing Norbu emphasized both Tibetan resilience and solidarity with other affected communities. Uyghur Human Rights Project Executive Director Omer Kanat highlighted parallels between Tibetan and Uyghur experiences and the transnational pressure faced by diaspora communities, while Hong Kong democracy advocate Frances Hui urged policymakers not to allow political prisoners and human rights to disappear behind discussions of trade.

Together, the speeches underscored one of the central themes of this week’s mobilization: Tibetans were not advocating in isolation, but in solidarity with other communities who have been impacted by Beijing’s repression. Through all of the actions this week, these collective voices highlighted the urgency of placing human rights and fundamental freedoms at the center of the U.S.-China relationship.

title: As Trump hosts Xi, protests over Chinese acts in Tibet, Xinjiang rage next door to White House
summary: As President Donald Trump hosts Chinese leader Xi Jinping, a host of protesters gathered next door to the Whtie House to decry Chinese ethnic cleansing in Xinjiang and Tibet, the stifling of civil and political liberties in Hong Kong, and m
content:
As President Donald Trump hosts Chinese leader Xi Jinping, a host of protesters gathered next door to the Whtie House to decry Chinese ethnic cleansing in Xinjiang and Tibet, the stifling of civil and political liberties in Hong Kong, and minorities across China.

Pro-Tibet independence protestors demonstrate near the US Capitol while China's President Xi Jinping visits the White House on September 24, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: Allison Robbert/AP)

As President Donald Trump hailed "the truly great friendship" with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, a host of protesters gathered next door to the White House to decry Chinese ethnic cleansing in Xinjiang and Tibet and stifling of democracy in Hong Kong.

These protesters joined [Congress members from across party lines to remind Trump that the leader whom he is appeasing presides over a totalitarian regime that has no space for religious, ethnic, or linguistic minorities](https://www.firstpost.com/world/as-trump-courts-xi-congress-sounds-alarm-over-china-on-iran-ai-and-indo-pacific-14048070.html) — one of the first decisions that the Communist Party of China (CPC) took after conquering the country was to invade Tibet, subjugate the populace, and embark on a campaign of ethnic cleansing and cultural erasure that continues to this day.

In a rare break from Trump, Republican lawmakers took the lead in calling out Xi and his regime's record, with Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker reminding Trump that Xi is a "brutal, unelected, and oppressive dictator" and should be treated as such.

The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party said in a video that Xi has presided over "some of the world's worst human rights abuses".

The committee said that China had "dismantled the democracy in Hong Kong, committed genocide in Xinjiang, used forced labour, jailed and persecuted people of faith, and targeted dissidents in and out of China, and implemented mass surveillance measures" during Xi's tenure.

Pro-Tibet independence protestors demonstrate near the US Capitol while China's President Xi Jinping visits the White House on September 24, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: Allison Robbert/AP)

While [Mao Zedong presided over the cultural erasure in Tibet](https://www.firstpost.com/world/why-tibet-and-dalai-lama-make-china-nervous-13903895.html), Xi stepped up similar efforts in Xinjiang. The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (UNHCR) in 2022 concluded that the Chinese regime has likely committed "crimes against humanity" in Xinjiang against Uyghur Muslims. The situation of Tibet is well known: China drove their spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, into exile and has effectively barred the teaching of Tibetan language and culture.

## **'Xi Jinping has to go', 'Shame on Xi Jinping', 'Unwelcome Xi'**

Protesters gathered behind a fence along the Lafayette Park with flags and placards. They chanted slogans on loudspeakers and their voice carried across the park to the White House's North Portico, where an honour guard and a red carpet awaited guests attending the state dinner, according to The Associated Press.

Protesters chanted "Xi Jinping has got to go" and "Shame! Shame on Xi Jinping!" and chants grew louder throughout the ceremony.

**ALSO READ — [From East Turkestan to Tibet: 76 years of China’s colonial domination](https://www.firstpost.com/opinion/from-east-turkestan-to-tibet-75-years-of-chinas-colonial-domination-13938753.html)**

Protesters also gathered outside the Chinese embassy and at other spots near the White House to hold protests against Xi.

Pro-Tibet independence protestors demonstrate near the US Capitol while China's President Xi Jinping visits the White House on September 24, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: Allison Robbert/AP)

Protesters waved 'Free Tibet' flags and flags bearing "freedom" and "democracy" in Mandarin along with placards reading "Keep Taiwan Free" and "Liberate Hong Kong, revolution of our times", a slogan associated with the city's 2019 uprising against the CPC.

Anjali Tenzin Sonn, 17, joined a mostly Tibetan group and called for a free Tibet outside the US Capitol. She told the AP that she felt compelled to participate after growing up hearing stories about her mother fleeing Tibet on foot and her grandfather suffering as a political prisoner.

Another protester, 31-year-old Zhang Na, said, "I hope Emperor Xi won't remain in power. I hope he can give Chinese people real freedom — freedom of speech and religion."

Yang Fan, a 39-year-old Christian, who joined the protest with his wife and daughter, held a handwritten sign calling for "freedom of religion" and an "end to dictatorship". He told the news agency that he wanted to stand up for Christians in China and hoped Xi would release those imprisoned for their religious beliefs.

title: Brazil's Lula bans online betting, unveils debt relief plan as reelection race tightens

content:
Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva speaks during a ceremony of social welfare program "Bolsa Familia" (Family Allowance) at the Planalto Palace in Brasilia, Brazil, March 2, 2023. REUTERS/Adriano Machado/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/brazils-president-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-speaks-during-a-ceremony-of-social-welfare-program-bolsa-familia-family-allowance-at-the-planalto-palace-in-brasilia/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6bmV3c21sX1JDMlJMWjlTUzVRNA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Executive order bans online betting operations in Brazil
*   Measure comes as polls show tight presidential election
*   Bolsonaro calls betting ban "politically motivated"
*   Lula also unveils initiative aimed at reducing household debt

SAO PAULO, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Friday announced a ban on online betting operations in Latin ‌America's largest economy and unveiled a new debt relief program aimed at households, the latest in a [series](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazils-lula-raises-welfare-benefit-ahead-october-election-2026-09-17/) of measures introduced ahead of next month's election.

[Opinion polls](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/lula-holds-lead-over-flavio-bolsonaro-ahead-brazil-election-datafolha-poll-shows-2026-09-24/) have shown Lula locked in a tight race with right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, ahead of the October 4 first-round vote.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Famericas%2Fbrazils-lula-bans-online-betting-operations-reelection-race-tightens-2026-09-25%2F)

Report Ad![Image 2](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

The executive order bans online betting operations in Brazil, less than two years after the ​government kicked off a legal framework allowing the industry to operate. It takes immediate effect but must be approved by Congress within 120 days ​to remain in force.

The crackdown reflects growing concern within the government that rising spending on gambling has drained household budgets and ⁠contributed to record levels of indebtedness. Recent surveys showed roughly three-quarters of Brazilians support a complete ban on online betting.

"We are facing a public health issue ​involving online betting. It is a serious problem," said Finance Minister Dario Durigan during the announcement.

Durigan said that betting firms' websites will remain available for users to claim ​remaining funds until October 5. App stores and network providers will be required to block these websites on October 6, he added.

Senator Bolsonaro called the measure "populist, hypocritical and politically motivated" during a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro on Friday.

Online betting was legalized in Brazil in 2018 under former President Michel Temer but remained largely unregulated throughout Jair Bolsonaro's administration. Lula signed legislation ​in 2023 establishing rules and explicitly authorizing online casino games in addition to sports betting.

Licensed operators have been allowed to offer services nationwide since January 2025 after ​paying concession fees and meeting regulatory requirements.

Officials have argued that betting losses have fueled public dissatisfaction with the economy, despite record-low unemployment and relatively subdued inflation in the country.

The Finance ‌Ministry estimates ⁠Brazilian households spend around 60 billion reais ($11.57 billion) annually on online betting, generating roughly 10 billion reais in tax revenue.

JPMorgan said listed companies most exposed to Brazil include Evolution

, which derives about 9% of sales from the country, Allwyn

, whose Betano business contributes 6% to 7% of EBITDA, Entain and Flutter.

ANJL, an association representing the betting sector, said in a statement that the measure would push more than 30 million gamblers into illegal websites, adding it disrespects investments made in compliance with ​the law.

## DEBT RELIEF PROGRAM

Lula also announced ​a new initiative aimed at reducing ⁠the burden of household debt, only months after relaunching a broad federally backed consumer debt renegotiation program known as "Desenrola," which was unveiled in 2023.

The government said it will hold an auction in November to buy and restructure household debt, spending ​15 billion reais to acquire up to 150 billion reais of delinquent loans at discounts of at least 90%. ​The program is expected ⁠to cover about half of the debt stock deemed eligible.

Households would then be able to clear overdue obligations at the discounted value, with the full benefit of the write-down passed through to borrowers.

The initiative targets debts that have been overdue for two to 4.5 years, mainly credit card balances and unsecured personal loans. Planning Minister Bruno Moretti ⁠said the ​auction will cover debts of up to 10,000 reais.

"This is a better Desenrola than the previous ​versions," Lula said. "In the earlier Desenrola, people had to approach banks individually. Now the government will purchase the debt and settle it on behalf of borrowers."

The measure had already been [flagged](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazils-lula-raises-welfare-benefit-ahead-october-election-2026-09-17/) by the government ​last week as part of Lula's election-year economic agenda.

($1 = 5.1856 reais)

title: Venezuela's promised elections face long delays, sources say
summary: Item 1 of 3 A woman holding a Venezuelan flag looks on as protesters demonstrate against the visit of Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez to New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), and to demand elections outside t
content:
Item 1 of 3 A woman holding a Venezuelan flag looks on as protesters demonstrate against the visit of Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez to New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), and to demand elections outside the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) office in Caracas, Venezuela, September 22, 2026. REUTERS/Gaby Oraa/File Photo

**[1/3]**A woman holding a Venezuelan flag looks on as protesters demonstrate against the visit of Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez to New York for the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), and to demand elections outside the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) office in Caracas,... [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/protest-against-venezuelan-interim-president-delcy-rodriguezs-visit-to-new-york-in-caracas/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkZPTkFBS0wwMw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)Read more

*   Summary

*   Vote unlikely before end of next year, two political sources say
*   Talks in Caracas focused on reforming courts, electoral body
*   US says economic, social stability needed for political transition
*   Rodriguez told UNGA state preparing for elections but gave no timeline

CARACAS, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Venezuela's long-awaited vote may not happen for a year or more due to planned overhauls of the courts and electoral ‌authorities, according to five political sources and analysts, despite Acting President Delcy Rodriguez's [promise of a transition](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelas-rodriguez-promises-elections-2026-09-23/) to "full democracy".

Rodriguez, who [took power](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/delcy-rodriguez-formally-sworn-venezuelas-interim-president-2026-01-05/) after a US raid [captured then-President Nicolas Maduro](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/venezuelas-maduro-test-us-courts-reluctance-apply-international-law-criminal-2026-09-01/) in January, told the [UN General Assembly](https://www.reuters.com/world/united-nations/) on Wednesday that state institutions were preparing for elections. She said her government had opened talks with the opposition and would guarantee ​full participation, but gave no timetable.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Famericas%2Fvenezuelas-promised-elections-face-long-delays-sources-say-2026-09-25%2F)

Five sources, including from parties close to the government and opposition, as well as analysts said ​that major obstacles remain, such as difficult institutional reforms and little apparent urgency in Washington for a prompt ⁠vote.

Two of the sources told Reuters that an election was unlikely before the end of next year.

## TRICKY REFORMS

At the center of the delay is ​the planned replacement of all 32 Supreme Court judges and the five directors of the National Electoral Council, the top electoral body. Opposition groups and ​international rights observers have [long said](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/opposition-seeks-voting-tallies-contested-venezuela-presidential-race-2024-07-29/) that both bodies lack independence, and that Maduro's 2018 and 2024 re-elections were fraudulent.

Institutional reform is under discussion in [US-backed talks](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-backed-venezuela-talks-begin-without-opposition-leader-machado-2026-07-31/) between Rodriguez's interim government and a faction of the opposition.

But even after a new electoral council is installed, authorities would still need to update voter rolls, ensure that all parties can compete and ​resolve basic operational questions such as whether voting would be manual or electronic, said Oswaldo Martinez, of the Caracas-based consultancy ORC.

That process alone could take up ​to a year, according to two of the sources close to the talks.

## US CALL FOR STABILITY

US officials have also said that any political transition must be accompanied by [economic and ‌social stability](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/trump-venezuelas-rodriguez-discuss-debt-restructuring-rubio-says-2026-09-23/), raising ⁠more potential questions on the electoral timeline.

"What would threaten an enduring republic in Venezuela would be that someone is elected and they inherit a complete catastrophe, economic and social, and then the whole project is endangered," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said this week.

Some critics of this position say Washington has [sidelined the country's opposition](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuela-acting-president-opposition-leader-navigate-new-relations-with-trump-2026-01-16/) and reduced the urgency for free elections in favor of [oil and investment deals](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelan-delegation-led-by-rodriguez-discuss-debt-energy-us-sources-say-2026-09-21/) with the interim government.

Last month, President ​Donald Trump announced an unprecedented US ​push to [take control of a fifth ⁠of Venezuela's vast oil reserves](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/us-enters-into-oil-agreement-with-venezuela-trump-says-2026-08-28/).

"The Trump administration is currently prioritizing economic stability and oil-related deals under Delcy, with little apparent urgency to move toward a fresh vote," said Risa Grais-Targow, Latin America director at political ​risk consultancy Eurasia Group.

"That, along with some of the required institutional changes, suggests new elections won't be ​held until late ⁠2027 at the earliest, with a possibility that it takes longer."

## COMPETING PRIORITIES

Maria Corina Machado, Venezuela's best-known opposition leader and exiled [Nobel Peace Prize laureate](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nobel-peace-prize-laureate-machado-says-will-bring-award-back-venezuela-2025-12-11/), has been notably absent from the talks with the interim government as her [efforts to re-enter the country](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelan-opposition-leader-machado-fails-return-attempts-rodriguez-meets-trump-2026-09-23/) have been stymied.

Some US lawmakers have [called for elections](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/seven-months-after-trump-intervention-us-senators-seek-venezuela-elections-2026-08-04/) and say that Washington ⁠has not ​secured meaningful democratic concessions from Rodriguez's government.

"Stability and economic normalization centered heavily on US commercial ​participation remain the priorities," said Nicholas Watson of consultancy Teneo, adding that Washington and Caracas are treating the need for political transition as a "longer-term" and "open-ended" process.

"Neither is taking decisive steps ​toward an electoral process," Watson said.

Reporting by Vivian Sequera and Mayela Armas in Caracas and Anthony Esposito in New York; Editing by Jonathan Spicer

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Vivian reports on politics and general news from Venezuela's capital, Caracas. She is interested in reporting on how Venezuela's long economic crisis, with its rampant inflation, has affected human rights, health and the Venezuelan people, among other topics. She previously worked for the Associated Press in Venezuela, Colombia, Cuba and Brazil.

Since 2018 Mayela has reported for Reuters on Venezuela’s economy and general news from capital Caracas. She is particularly interested in covering the effects of Venezuela’s economic crisis and high inflation, especially concerning the effects this has on the day-to-day lives of people and families. She also writes about how the country’s finances are managed, as well as Venezuela’s main industries. Before she joined Reuters Mayela worked at local media outlets.

*   Tehran presents Washington with plan to end hostilities within 7 days

*   Allies of Saudi Arabia show support for kingdom amid Houthi attacks

WASHINGTON/UNITED NATIONS, Sept 25 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping turned to ​the Middle East war at their summit on Friday, as Iran pressed Washington to accept a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting.

China is highly ‌dependent on the flow of Middle Eastern oil, which has been disrupted by Iranian threats on tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz and the advance of Iranian-allied Houthis along chokepoints in the Red Sea.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Fallies-unite-behind-saudi-arabia-houthis-step-up-attacks-2026-09-25%2F)

Xi urged the United States and Iran to return to the June framework agreement that led to a short-lived ceasefire and continue negotiations toward a broader settlement, according to China's state news agency Xinhua.

Trump, meanwhile, [warned Xi](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-told-xi-that-china-helping-iran-is-unacceptable-us-ambassador-says-2026-09-25/) against providing support to Iran and received assurances that China would not do so, ​the US ambassador to China said on Friday, the final day of Xi's three-day state visit.

The flurry of diplomacy underscored the global stakes of the seven-month-old conflict, which has disrupted oil flows through ​one of the world's most critical shipping lanes and drawn in regional and world powers.

Xi's visit coincided with the United Nations General Assembly, where Iran and ⁠the US engaged in diplomacy through Qatari mediators.

Iran welcomed Xi's push for a return to the June framework, but also placed renewed emphasis on its peace proposal, formally unveiled on Thursday.

"Iran has conveyed to the United States through ​Qatar a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, a normal maritime passage restored within seven days. The choice now rests with the United States," Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas ​Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday.

"The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan," he said.

Washington has yet to publicly respond to the Iranian offer, but a US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said, "We are having positive and constructive discussions through the mediators, and we continue to discuss the nuclear issues."

If the US agrees, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects," Araqchi said. Tehran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and hostilities ​would end on all fronts, including Lebanon. The plan in turn requires the United States to lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds, and waive its oil sanctions.

But separately, a senior Iranian ​official told Reuters that [Iran will show no flexibility](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-will-make-no-nuclear-concessions-iranian-official-says-2026-09-25/) over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its peace deal. Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of ‌the country, ⁠the official said.

Trump has vowed Iran will never develop nuclear weapons.

## RETURN TO DIPLOMACY?

The Iranian seven-day proposal comes after previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes.

Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.

Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests. Iranian-aligned militias in Iraq were blamed for a pipeline attack that temporarily took more Saudi ​oil off the market. All the while, Iranian-backed Hezbollah ​has been engaged with Israeli forces in Lebanon.

## WARNING ⁠TO CHINA

The US warning to China came amid reports that China had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired air-defense missile launchers and that Tehran had found ways to evade sanctions on its oil sales with Chinese help.

David Perdue, Trump's ambassador to Beijing, said in a CNBC interview that Trump reiterated to Xi that direct or indirect ​support for Iran was "totally unacceptable."

Asked separately on Fox News if that meant China would stop assisting Iran, Perdue said, "They assured us yesterday they're not doing that."

The ​war's widening toll was also ⁠visible on the Arabian Peninsula, where Saudi Arabia's allies moved to shore up the kingdom's defenses.

With the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Yemeni government under assault from Iran-linked Houthi fighters, and Houthi missiles striking inside Saudi Arabia, allies of the kingdom have united to show support.

Defense officials of Turkey and Pakistan, both partners in a joint defense pact with Saudi Arabia, met in Riyadh on Friday to review the security situation and discuss intelligence cooperation, military coordination, and integrating ⁠forces, the Saudi ​defense ministry said in a statement.

The statement came a day after Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met within the framework ​of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement.

The violence in Yemen has prompted a new [humanitarian crisis,](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/child-malnutrition-rises-yemen-fighting-intensifies-says-unicef-2026-09-25/) the United Nations children's agency said on Friday, reporting a rise in acute malnutrition among children.

content:
中国国家主席习近平为期三天的访美行程9月25日落下帷幕。美国总统特朗普在白宫以高规格国事访问礼遇接待了习近平，两人参加国宴并举行会谈，涉及贸易、超级智能、台湾以及中东等重要国际议题。

纵观中国官方媒体与西方媒体这三天的报道，它们使用了两种不同的尺子在衡量这场峰会。中方报道更倾向于把习近平此次访美放进一个更宏大的叙事，也就是“美中两个大国未来应该如何相处”之中，强调关系的稳定、合作的延续以及双方如何管控分歧。

相比起来，美国媒体则把峰会拆解成一场具体的战略博弈，追问双方究竟拿到了什么、哪些问题暂时搁置、谁手里握有更多筹码，以及这场盛大的外交仪式背后究竟有没有产生足够实质的成果。

**报道框架：合作稳定v.s.战略竞争**

中国官方媒体近期对美国总统特朗普和中国主席习近平峰会的报道，明显将稳定美中关系作为核心框架。特习会被放在更大的美中关系、国际格局和大国相处的框架里。关键词包括“战略稳定”“合作”“管控分歧”“新愿景”“长期发展”等。

新华社9月23日发表题为《推动中美关系大船平稳前行》的文章，文中写道，“元首外交引领中美关系这艘大船驶向前方...只要两国元首共同领好航、掌好舵，中美关系这艘大船就能不偏航、不失速。”

美国之音记者利平现场报道特朗普夫妇陪同习近平夫妇参观国家档案馆后下台阶

9月24日特朗普和习近平会面之后，新华社的“第一观察”发表题为《从习主席抵美书面讲话中感悟大国胸怀担当》，其中的关键词包括”大国胸怀”，“责任担当”，“中美关系大方向”等等。

文章指出，在元首外交引领下，双方在各方面的关系有所缓和。“这一稳定态势来之不易，需要在相向而行、良性互动中不断巩固。”新华社的文章说。

与此同时，中方的报道聚焦于习近平国事访问的规格和历史意义。把特朗普的机场迎接、21响礼炮、军乐团、儿童献花等仪式性元素放在显著位置。

美国媒体当然也对各种仪式进行报道，但仪式不是重点。美媒的切入点大多是：两个大国如何在竞争中避免失控？

包括路透社、美联社、华盛顿邮报、福克斯新闻等西方媒体以美中战略竞争为主线，将习近平此次的国事访问视为双方进行利益交换和战略博弈的平台，重点关注贸易、稀土、人工智能等具体议题，以及双方手中的谈判筹码。

西方媒体关键词包括“筹码”(leverage)，“协定”(deal)，“让步”(concessions)，“没有突破”(no breakthrough), 报道的切入点通常是具体的问题，比如贸易休战能维持多久？特朗普希望中国在伊朗问题上做什么？中国能否从美国获得什么？台湾、人工智能、稀土、关税等问题上双方各自有什么筹码？最终有没有实质性突破？

例如《华盛顿邮报》在9月23日的[报道](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/09/23/trump-greets-xi-jinping-airport-rare-gesture-summit-starts/)，在关注特朗普罕见地亲自到机场迎接习近平后，立即将注意力转向安排背后的外交意义，以及双方关注的人工智能、投资、贸易等问题。

另一篇[报道](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/as-trump-meets-xi-rare-earths-give-china-a-powerful-hand/ar-AA2cSjfX?ocid=BingNewsSerp)的题目是《特习会之际，稀土成为中国的底牌》(As Trump meets Xi, rare earths give China a powerful hand)，则以中国在稀土领域的优势成为谈判筹码为核心，把特习会形容成一场力量和杠杆的较量。

[路透社](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/trump-xi-summit-in-washington-begins-with-great-fanfare-but-low-expectations/ar-AA2cV03g?ocid=BingNewsSerp)9月24日发表的文章题为《特习会在盛大声势中拉开帷幕，但外界预期不高》(Trump-Xi summit in Washington begins with great fanfare but low expectations)。开篇就指出两国领导人希望展示稳定关系，但双方仍存在包括人工智能、贸易、台湾和伊朗战争在内的一系列棘手问题。文章随后把访问放进美中长期竞争和具体利益谈判的框架中。

也就是说，同一场峰会，中国官媒看到的是一艘需要共同掌舵的“大船”；而西方媒体看到的，则更像一张摆满筹码的谈判桌。

**成功与否？西方媒体更谨慎**

习近平在周五(9月25日)结束了三天的访美行程，启程返回北京。

周五登录中国的搜索引擎百度，置顶的三个热搜分别是：“中美建设性战略稳定关系”，“习近平圆满结束对美国的国事访问”，以及“进一步丰富中美关系定位的内涵。”

新华社在习近平结束访问时发表文章，题为《习近平圆满结束对美国的国事访问》，奠定所有官媒的整体报道基调。成功被大致定义为把双方的关系稳住，也就是两国元首将保持沟通，美中关系扩大合作、管控分歧。

在2026年9月24日举办的国宴上，美国总统特朗普与中国国家主席习近平握手。(美联社）

《人民日报》周五发表题为《习近平同美国总统特朗普会谈》的文章，其中强调“中美两国元首在不到半年时间里实现互访，在中美关系史上是前所未有的。”

人民日报海外版则在特朗普为习近平设国宴之后发表名为《引领中美关系这艘大船行稳致远》的文章，其中指出，元首外交取得积极成果, 并引用学者的话说“可预期性本身就是一种全球公共产品”。

中方还特别强调习近平在讲话中宣布的文化交流层面的具体举措，即在未来5年，中国将邀请10万名美国青少年赴中国学习。

新华社题为《“5年10万”，习近平主席向美国青少年发出新邀约》的文章，表述美中关系的稳定从政府层面延伸到人民层面。

相比之下，西方媒体的总体评价则更加谨慎。他们普遍的总结是此次峰会成果有限。

美国[哥伦比亚广播公司](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/trump-china-xi-jinping-state-visit-dinner-tariffs-ai/)周五发表题为《特习会结束 但公布成果有限》(Trump-Xi visit wraps up with few achievements announced)的文章，其中写道:“白宫没有透露周四和周五的峰会取得了什么成果…特朗普说他与习近平进行了一次‘很棒的会晤’，但没有回答有关会谈实质内容的问题。”

[路透社](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/four-takeaways-from-trumps-summit-with-xi-in-washington/ar-AA2cUKLB?ocid=BingNewsSerp)9月24日发表的文章题为《特习会的四个要点》(Four takeaways from Trump's summit with Xi in Washington)。文章写道，此次双方会面最重要的实质成就就是美国财政部长贝森特宣布，双方的贸易战休战期限延长两个月。但路透社马上指出，延期并未促成一项持久协议，而是“将关税、中国采购、稀土供应和技术限制推迟到了下一轮的磋商中。”

美国[全国公共广播电台](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/24/nx-s1-5973112/long-agenda-short-meeting-trump-and-xi-meet)(NPR)形容特习会是“议程繁重，会议简短“(Long agenda, short meeting)。该台记者冯哲芸说，“如果习近平在访问中能显示他与美国一样强大，那对中国来说他们认为就是一场胜利。”

**中国、台湾民众如何看“习特会”？专家如何解读峰会成果？**

Published 3 小时前

中国国家主席习近平时隔11年再次访美进行国是访问，与美国总统特朗普举行今年第二次会晤。今次“习特会”有哪些成果？中国及台湾民众又如何看待？

两位专家分析，今次会谈虽未有在部分重大议题上取得具体突破，但特朗普对习近平的高规格接待，以及两国领导人之间的互动，仍具有一定象征意义。有分析认为，中美关系正逐渐呈现更加平起平坐的态势。

不过，在台湾、人工智能及技术出口管制等问题上，中美仍存在分歧。专家指，随着两国领导人今年稍后预计再次会面，没有那么容易达成的细节就“可以慢慢来谈”。
