## 数百艘中国渔船出现在越南外海，北京想要什么？

图像来源，Getty/BBC

图像加注文字，2026年8月16日中国一年一度的单方面禁渔期结束后，超过3,400艘渔船从阳江港出发，另外超过3,000艘渔船分别从北海、钦州和防城港等城市出海。

*       *   Author, 黎爱（Thuong Le）
    *   Role, BBC越南语记者

*   Published 5 小时前

*   阅读时间: 6 分钟

8月中旬，中国一年一度的单方面禁渔期结束后，超过6,000艘中国渔船大规模出海，分散驶向广阔海域。

这一幕令人想起赤壁之战，当时曹操率领数以千计战船在江面列阵，与孙权和刘备联军对峙。

不同的是，这些渔船并非驶往一场海战，而是分散前往不同渔场，其中包括越南专属经济区内、中南部沿海省份广义省对开海域。海事研究人员称，近年出现在这片水域的中国渔船数量显著增加。

昔日看似只是季节性的捕鱼活动，如今反映出一个更大的问题：海洋资源的争夺、渔民的生计，以及围绕南海控制权的更广泛战略盘算。

美国史丹福大学戈尔迪之结国家安全创新中心（Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation）旗下SeaLight项目的研究人员发现，大批中国渔船聚集在越南海岸附近。

他们引述海事数据称，这支船队约有100艘船，大部分从广西港口出发，自2024年起一直在越南广义省外海作业，距离李山岛最近只有28海里，即接近52公里。

SeaLight项目主任鲍威尔（Ray Powell）对BBC越南语表示：“我们查看了2024年至2026年的数据，发现2026年每天都有超过40艘船，远多于以往数据所见，而且数字仍在上升。”

“情况并没有真正稳定下来，所以这个问题看来只会持续下去。”

视频加注文字，南中国海渔船活动轨迹

## 季节性的规律

SeaLight提供的数据显示，每年某些时段，中国渔船会出现在非常接近越南海岸的地方。

曾直接参与分析海事数据的SeaLight实习生格雷斯·加布里埃利（Grace Gabrielli）说：“从它们的活动模式来看，它们往返不同港口，在广义省一带停留，然后返回港口，这是渔船常见的活动模式。”

数据显示，这支船队在2025年底以及2026年最初几个月尤其活跃，2026年2月则是例外。

澳洲新南威尔士大学教授卡尔·塞耶（Carl Thayer）表示，这种规律一定程度上可以由中国每年的单方面禁渔期解释。禁渔期由5月1日持续至8月16日中午。

他解释：“年初有农历新年，你会看到一些原本在那里的船只返回中国过年。之后它们再回来，3月至5月期间会大量聚集。到了4月底，它们开始撤走，包括一些护航船只。到了8月中捕鱼季重新开始后，它们又回来。”

## 船队中有政府和军事船只

曾任美国空军驻越南武官的鲍威尔对BBC表示，这一带大部分中国船只的活动都与一般渔船相似，确实在从事捕鱼。不过，船队中也包括政府船只和海上民兵船只。

值得注意的是，SeaLight发现一艘中国政府船只，在同一季节性活动期间与渔船船队一同行动，而SeaLight将其辨识为军事船只。

鲍威尔说：“我们发现的那艘政府船被归类为军事船只，悬挂中国国旗，记录中的捕鱼活动是零，而它出现的时间也跟船队的季节性规律一致。换句话说，它就像跟着整支船队来回移动。”

他表示，这显示政府船只正在伴随渔船船队行动，而这种模式“与海上民兵船只的活动高度吻合”。

他说：“当一艘被明确归类为政府船只的船混在其中时，我们看到的是在越南近海进行、获中国政府认可的捕鱼活动。”

鲍威尔认为，中国“不能声称，而且实际上也不希望声称，这只是一群自行其是的渔船”。

他解释：“中国希望越南知道，它正在监察并认可这些活动；如果越南对这些捕鱼活动构成重大挑战，中国已准备好保护它们。”

他补充：“中国也在向越南传递一个地缘政治讯息，即它可以在自己声索范围内任何地方活动，而越南能够阻止它的手段非常有限。”

塞耶同样认为，这支船队的活动很可能得到中国政府支持。

他说：“中国不会只是派一些没有武装的渔船到南海捕鱼赚钱，然后回家。他们需要保护这些船，因为他们会说，这是我们的地方，我们必须威吓其他人，把他们赶出去。”

不过，塞耶警告，不应对渔民本身的身份作出假设。

他说：“我们没有确切的照片证据。有些分析人士称他们为‘小蓝人’，意思是这一刻他们还在捕鱼，下一刻进入船舱，再出来时已经穿上蓝色制服，成为海上民兵。”

因此，他认为这支船队可能由多种人员和船只组成，包括商业渔民、获政府补贴的民兵，以及更大型的海上执法船只，其中部分属民兵类型，另外还有中国海警船。

## 为什么是广义省？

广义省位于越南中部，渔场丰富，海洋资源充裕。

它的海域广阔，自然条件有利，栖息着多种鱼类和海产，包括吞拿鱼、鲭鱼、竹筴鱼、鳀鱼、鱿鱼和虾。

捕鱼长久以来都是沿岸社区生活的重要部分，尤其是在岛屿和沿海地区。每一次出海不仅带回大量食物，也提供就业机会，并为当地经济带来收入。

据越南通讯社报道，截至2026年5月，广义省渔船管理系统内有接近5,000艘注册渔船。当地渔民亦长期在西沙群岛及南沙群岛一带渔场作业，经验丰富。

然而，在西沙和南沙群岛周边海域，越南渔船经常遭中国方面驱赶、袭击，渔民被殴打，财物亦曾遭扣押或没收。

2024年9月29日，广义省渔船QNg 95739 TS遭中国方面人员袭击。船上渔民表示，他们被殴打，渔网、设备以及“数吨鱼获”遭取走。至少10名越南渔民受伤。

路透社2024年10月1日报道，中国外交部表示，越南渔船“未经中国政府批准，非法进入中国西沙群岛海域捕鱼，中国有关部门依法采取措施予以制止”。不过，北京并未直接提及9月29日的袭击事件。

2024年10月2日，越南渔业协会向农业与农村发展部、外交部及越共中央对外部发出公文，“抗议中国阻挠作业、掠夺财物及袭击渔民，并建议加强对出海作业渔民的支援”。

再早之前，2020年4月，越南媒体报道，一艘广义省渔船在永兴岛附近被一艘“外国船只”撞沉，中国其后交还船上的八名渔民。

图像来源，CTV

图像加注文字，2024年9月30日，越南渔船QNg 95739 TS抵达沙圻港后，船员黄进功被送院接受治疗。

鲍威尔表示，中国渔船到这片水域活动，最简单的解释就是这里鱼产丰富。不过他强调，这些活动同时服务于北京的战略和地缘政治目标。

他说：“这些渔船每年有数个月出现在那里，而且当然没有征求越南许可，这本身就是目的，而不是意外。因为这有助中国宣示自己对这些水域享有权利的主张，即使按照国际法，情况并非如此。”

SeaLight实习生加布里埃利补充：“当地对专属经济区的执法有限，而且渔场非常丰富。我认为中国近年发现这里资源丰富而执法有限，所以正在充分利用这个情况。”

## 对越南渔民意味什么？

曾两度前往广义省研究当地渔民生活的塞耶教授表示，渔民经常在夜间出海，前往西沙群岛附近水域，他们“愿意承受风险”，因为那里可以捕到最值钱、收益最高的海产。

他指出，根据SeaLight数据，中国在2024及2025年曾以大量海上民兵和海上执法船只形成一道大型“屏障”，阻止越南渔民前往相关水域。

他表示，结果是广义省渔民曾告诉他，他们被迫转到其他地方作业，例如北部湾（Gulf of Tonkin；东京湾），或印尼纳土纳群岛周边水域。

他说：“他们的确会向媒体，包括外国媒体投诉，即使他们求助，也无法立即得到援助。他们会被丢下不管。他们出海时，当地巡逻不足，有时甚至完全没有巡逻。”

因此，塞耶认为这些渔民十分脆弱。

他忆述：“中国有钢壳的民兵船，海警船也曾使用水炮。所以渔民说，当他们看到船只靠近时，由于中国船只速度快得多，他们会尝试逃走，但由于距离等原因，有时仍会被追上。”

他表示，结果是这一带供越南渔民作业的渔场愈来愈受限制。

对广义省沿海社区来说，这并不只是一个关于渔场的故事，也关乎一代又一代依海而生家庭的生计。

2024年1月，越南渔业协会主席及岘港渔业协会主席曾向BBC越南语表示，当时渔民为避免遭中国海上民兵及执法船只威胁，不得不与西沙群岛渔场保持数十海里的距离。

岘港渔业协会主席陈文岭亦根据当地渔民转述，形容有大批中国海上民兵船只出没。

陈文岭说：“他们是以一轮一轮行动的方式出现。禁渔期一结束，他们便大批涌入越南海域。我们的渔民看到他们会害怕，因为数量实在太多，可以有数百甚至数千艘船，非常强势地横扫我们的渔场。”

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，数以千计越南渔民的生计持续受到来自中国的压力。

## 越南和中国的回应

对于有关中国渔船在广义省外海活动的报告，BBC已向越南外交部发送电邮寻求官方回应，但未有即时收到答复。

BBC亦曾联络越南渔业协会，希望取得回应及更多资料，但未获回覆。

中国自1999年起，每年实施为期三个半月的单方面禁渔令，越南多年来一直提出反对。

今年5月5日，越南外交部发言人范秋姮在例行记者会上表示：“越南对中国在南海实施禁渔令的立场是一贯的，多年来亦已明确重申。”

范秋姮又表示，越南已要求中国根据国际法，尤其是1982年《联合国海洋法公约》，尊重越南渔民在越南水域以及国家管辖范围以外海域合法作业的权利。

塞耶表示，虽然越南政府和越南渔业协会均曾提出抗议，但这些行动主要停留在口头层面，而越南在相关海域亦没有显著的力量部署。

他说：“从某种意义上说，这些抗议没有作用。问题在于，如果采取实际行动，某程度上也是徒劳，因为无论是船只数量还是船只吨位，中国都占有压倒性优势。越南不会因此得到甚么，只会被推回去。”

不过他指出，两国高层领导人会面时，越南肯定会提出这些问题。他表示，双方一般都认为双边关系应继续发展，而南海紧张局势不应盖过两国之间更广泛的关系。

鲍威尔也有类似看法。他表示，中越关系一直受到非常谨慎的管理，以至双方都不容易公开发表对对方非常负面的言论。

鲍威尔表示，尽管双方存在他形容为“非常、非常尖锐”的分歧，特别是在南海、西沙群岛以及更靠近越南海岸的水域问题上，但两国仍在努力维持稳定关系。

最近一次争议发生在2026年9月初。越南“坚决反对”所有外国在南海西沙群岛的活动后不到一星期，中国外交部表示越南无权评论。

中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆9月3日对记者表示：“西沙群岛是中国固有领土，不存在任何争议。中国在自己的领土上开展必要建设是主权范围内的事，越方无权说三道四。”

河内的声明和北京的强硬回应，正值8月中旬有报告指，中国正在鸭公岛进行新的建设活动。鸭公岛位于羚羊礁东北约14公里。

安全专家表示，目前判断有关设施用途仍为时尚早，但它可能是预警雷达设施的初期工程，用以支援中国预计在羚羊礁建造的设施。羚羊礁正逐渐成为南沙和西沙群岛范围内规模最大的人工岛之一。

越南近年亦加快在南沙群岛进行填海造岛。观察人士表示：“中国肯定不会对此感到高兴”。

鲍威尔表示，中国并没有骚扰越南的挖泥船或采取类似行动。换言之，北京选择不直接回应，而是透过其他方式展示力量，其中之一就是在广义省外海进行捕鱼活动。

他说：“它可以藉此提醒越南，谁才是这里势力最大的一方，同时又不需要向全世界大肆宣扬这件事。”

## 涉及台湾的战略考量

塞耶教授表示，中国渔船在广义省外海的活动，不只是出于眼前的商业或政治利益。他认为，“更大的原因”在于中国在南海的整体战略。

他说，中国一直逐步在西沙群岛兴建设施和基地，尤其是在永乐群岛一带，包括中建岛和羚羊礁所在的区域，为涉及台湾的不同情境作准备。

在这项战略之中，渔船扮演的角色并不限于捕捞海洋资源，也有助维持中国在海上的存在。这些船只在不同水域活动期间，也可能提供它们观察到的活动和海况资讯。

除了越南之外，亦有报道指中国渔船、执法船及勘测船在菲律宾专属经济区内活动。近年北京与马尼拉之间的紧张局势有所升温。

北京似乎尤其关注菲律宾，部分原因是菲律宾是美国的盟友，而中国非常希望削弱美国在东亚的影响力。

菲律宾亦采取了一项所谓的“透明度倡议”，包括拍摄双方在海上的接触，并公开相关影像和影片，希望藉此公开曝光中国的行动。

视频加注文字，中菲船只在仁爱礁附近海域发生冲突。

相比之下，越南通常较为谨慎，不太容许涉及中国的海上对峙和事故影像公开，包括渔民在海上遇袭的个案。

除非外交部或渔业协会的官方发言人公开回应，或外国记者能够前往当地直接与渔民交谈，否则相关事件的资讯很难在媒体找到。

观察人士因此表示，大部分公众并不知道越南专属经济区内正在发生甚么。

鲍威尔表示，越南这种做法让河内可以避免与北京直接对抗，使紧张局势保持在低度状态，而不像中国与菲律宾之间那样升级。

但他亦表示，这种做法的缺点是，中国采取了一套逐步、系统而持续的策略。长年累月之下，涉及越南声索和主权权利的中国活动愈来愈多。

他举例说：“2023年，我们曾追踪到越南南部海岸外的一次勘测活动。他们基本上花了一个月时间，让勘测船按照中文字‘中’的形状航行。”

“他们整整一个月都让勘测船、中国海警和海上民兵以这种轨迹航行。这是一件相当惊人的事，中国这样做非常高调而大胆。”

鲍威尔表示，这宗事件是在提醒越南，中国从未缩减其主张，“这是在提醒越南，中国的声索从来不会倒退。他们从来不会声索得更少，只会愈来愈多。”

中国渔船在越南专属经济区内活动，多年来一直有纪录。不过鲍威尔表示，大约过去四年间，相关活动持续增加，而今年5月更达到尤其高的水平，这一趋势特别值得注意。

他总结说：“长远来看，只可能有愈来愈多这类活动逐步向南扩展。”

_**图像制作：阿格尼亚·阿兹基亚（Aghnia Adzkia）、阿尔文·苏普里亚迪（Arvin Supriyadi）**_

## 特习会：习近平促特朗普“反对台独”，北京措辞升级要的是什么？

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，外界认为，北京正寻求美方在官方表述中更明确反映其反对“台独”的立场。

*       *   Author, 蒋宜婷
    *   Role, BBC中文记者
    *   Reporting from, 台北

*   Published 2026年9月25日上午10点01分

最近更新： 2 小时前
*   阅读时间: 6 分钟

中国国家主席习近平在白宫与美国总统特朗普会面，两人对“台湾问题”的表述引发关注。

据中国官媒新华社报导，习近平在会中表示，中方维护国家统一和领土完整的立场十分明确，并希望美方“坚持反对‘台独’的正确立场，慎重处理台湾问题”。

特朗普对此是否作出回应尚不明确。会后，特朗普形容双方进行了一场“很棒的会议”。面对媒体追问会谈是否涉及台湾及人工智慧（AI）等议题，两位领导人均未作回应。

政治学者向BBC中文表示，相较于前次美中领导人会晤，北京此次在台湾议题上的表述更为直接，并争取美方不仅在口头上承诺，还在政策文件或官方表述中更明确表达反对“台独”立场。

分析也指出，北京试图掌握峰会后的叙事主导权，若这种“先声夺人”的趋势持续，而台美高层互动又受到更多限制，台湾在美中台三角关系中的角色可能进一步被“边缘化”。

未来几天，外界将持续关注华府如何回应相关说法，及美中双方公开声明是否提及台湾。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2026年9月24日，中国国家主席习近平在白宫椭圆形办公室与美国总统特朗普进行约两小时的同席会晤。

## 北京促美方“反对台独”表述更直接

特朗普与习近平于美东时间周四（9月24日）在白宫举行会谈。

这是两人今年第二次会晤。上一次面对面会谈是在今年5月特朗普访问中国期间。当时，台湾议题已是外界关注焦点；此次峰会中，美中双方将如何处理相关问题，同样受到密切关注。

台湾成功大学政治学系教授王宏仁接受BBC中文访问时表示，相较于前次美中领导人会晤，北京此次在台湾议题上的表述更为直接。

他分析，中方诉求已从强调“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要、最敏感的问题”，以及警告处理不当可能冲击两国关系，进一步转向要求美方在政策层面作出更明确表态。

“北京希望美方在正式公报或官方文件中作出更具体的表述，而不只是由川普（特朗普）口头表态。”

王宏仁表示，中方向特朗普提出相关要求，本身就具有一定的政治效果；至于影响能有多大，仍取决于美方后续如何回应。他认为，美方未必会接受这项要求，但若华府因此调整既有对台政策，对台湾而言将是值得警惕的发展。

中国政府主张台湾是其领土的一部分，并将台湾问题列为对美关系中的核心议题之一，但多数台湾民众认同台湾拥有自己的主权，并希望两岸维持现状，即不与中国统一，也不正式宣布独立。

台湾政治大学选举研究中心“台湾民众统独立场趋势分布”今年6月发布的民调显示，台湾近六成民众倾向维持现状，倾向独立的占26.1％，倾向统一的占7.9%。

美国与台湾没有正式外交关系，但维持稳固的非官方关系，并依据《台湾关系法》提供台湾自我防卫所需能力。华府历来表示“不支持”台湾正式独立，但从未在其长期政策表述中明确宣示“反对台独”。

美国对台政策的主要基础包括《台湾关系法》（Taiwan Relations Act）、美中三个联合公报，以及“六项保证”（Six Assurances）。

台湾外交部周四（9月25日）下午回应，“这是中方一贯透过扭曲事实，单方面传达其立场与主张的手法”，并指中华民国台湾与中华人民共和国互不隶属，台湾未来只能由台湾人民以民主方式共同决定。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，9月24日，中国国家主席习近平与美国总统特朗普会面，美国副总统范斯（JD Vance）、国务卿鲁比奥（Marco Rubio）、财政部长贝森特（Scott Bessent）及中方代表团成员在场陪同。

## 华府未表态，增加台湾焦虑感

相较于北京明确阐述其在台湾议题上的立场，外界仍不清楚特朗普是否在会中作出回应。白宫尚未公布会谈成果，而新华社发布的会谈纪录亦未显示特朗普曾回应相关表述。

多名政治学者向BBC中文表示，在白宫尚未公布会谈内容前，北京率先公开相关讯息，有助于中方率先界定此次峰会的讨论重点，并可能影响外界对会谈成果的理解。

非营利智库国际危机组织（International Crisis Group）东北亚资深分析师杨晧暐（William Yang）向BBC中文表示，中方在峰会结束后迅速公布会谈内容，除了重申其对台立场，也意在塑造外界对峰会成果的认知。

他认为，北京希望营造一种印象：“中美接下来慢慢会形成一种共管台湾的形势，美方现在已经渐渐把自己的立场调整成中国希望美方所采取的立场。”

前次美中会晤后，特朗普接受福斯新闻访问时提出“我不希望有人走向独立”，就曾被部分观察人士解读为采纳了北京惯用的部分论述。此前，特朗普也曾公开质疑部分美国长期对台政策基础的框架。

杨晧暐分析，特朗普一向不愿受美国传统外交政策框架约束，其对外政策立场经常带有高度个人色彩与不确定性，而北京正是利用这种不确定性推进自身叙事；若华府未能及时透过官方渠道说明自身立场，可能加深台湾社会对美国对台政策走向的疑虑，进而增加焦虑感。

图像来源，台灣總統府

图像加注文字，近期美国对台军售的核心焦点，集中在一笔总额约140亿美元的关键武器进度上。 这笔军售正处于白宫暂缓并列入“评估与审查”的卡关状态。

## 对台军售有变数吗？

值得关注的是，特朗普对相关议题的任何表态，即使只是细微的措辞调整，外界都可能解读为美国对台政策变化的讯号，进而影响各界对华府安全承诺及对台军售政策的预期。

路透社9月22日报导，有消息指出习近平访美期间，将向特朗普施压，要求依1982年《八一七公报》停止对台军售。

《八一七公报》全称《中美就解决美国向台出售武器问题的公告》。公报中，美方表示将逐步减少对台军售，并期待台湾问题最终以和平方式解决。

中方长期批评美国未落实相关承诺。美国则指出，时任总统雷根在随后提出的对台政策文件中已表明，美方是否减少对台军售，取决于中国是否持续以和平方式处理两岸分歧；台湾的防卫需求，仍将是美方考量的重要因素。

在前次美中会晤中，特朗普表示他即将向台湾出售价值140亿美元的武器，作为与中国领导人谈判的筹码，称其为“非常好的谈判筹码”。

特朗普政府去年12月批准一项约110亿美元的对台军售案，创下历来最大规模；另一项约140亿美元的军售案则已搁置数月。

美国国务卿鲁比欧（Marco Rubio）日前向媒体表示，美国对台湾的军售进度之所以延宕，部分原因是受到华府在世界其他地区的潜在军事需求，还有本土国防工业产能的限制。

台湾国防部日前表示，将持续与美战争部保持密切协调联系，推动对台军售按计画执行。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，此次特习会被认为外交排场十足。从军事基地举行的隆重欢迎仪式，抵达白宫时接受仪仗队迎接，美国总统特朗普都为这位中国国家主席习近平铺上红地毯。

## 分析：台湾“已经被边缘化”

智库专家杨晧暐表示，台湾对美中互动的影响力始终有限，包括对台军售何时推进、以及美中如何处理台湾议题，台北都缺乏足够杠杆加以左右。

他指出，北京近年在历次美中峰会中持续采取“先声夺人”的策略，尝试率先界定台湾议题的讨论框架及论述方向。若这种趋势持续，而台美高层互动又受到更多限制，台湾在美中台三角关系中的角色可能进一步被边缘化。

美国德州山姆休士顿州立大学政治学系副教授翁履中向BBC中文表示，从对台军售到台湾主权议题，特朗普近期向北京释出的讯号整体较为友善。他观察，在特朗普第二任期内，台湾在美中关系中的战略重要性相较过去有所下降，甚至可说“已经被边缘化”。

翁履中指出，美国国会、行政部门及多个智库近年持续强调台湾的重要性，并呼吁白宫不要将台湾视为与北京谈判的筹码。然而，从特朗普重返白宫以来的政策与公开言论来看，台湾并未成为其外交议程中的优先事项。

路透社9月25日报导，美国参议院19名民主党议员批评这场峰会过于注重形式而忽视实质问题，并呼吁特朗普兑现国会已批准的对台超过150亿美元安全援助，包括13亿美元资金和140亿美元军售。

此前，多名共和党参议员也呼吁尽快解冻这笔对台安全援助。

翁履中认为，未来几天特朗普如何谈论台湾，将是观察此次特习会影响的重要指标。他表示，若特朗普之后再次提及台湾，尤其是公开批评台湾在国防投入或安全责任方面做得不足，外界可能会解读为美中在峰会期间已就台湾议题形成某种程度的共识。

“北京要的未必是美国直接宣布放弃台湾，”翁履中说，“中方更希望美国释出一些讯号，让台湾社会逐渐对华府的支持产生疑虑，进而削弱外界对美国安全承诺的信心。”

此次特习会为期三天，接续主要行程包含白宫红厅茶叙、参观美国国家档案馆等。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，台湾方面对特习会可能涉及台湾的议题相当关注。

## 台湾社会反应

在台湾，相关发展也引发高度关注。在野党国民党日前呼吁赖清德总统立即召开国安高层会议，全面掌握特习会可能涉及台湾的议题，并向民众公开说明。

台湾总统赖清德在周三（9月23日）一场公开活动表示，台湾的自由与繁荣不仅关乎2300万人民的未来，也攸关印太地区乃至全球的和平与稳定。台湾行政院长卓荣泰则表示，政府正密切关注川习会相关发展。

美国智库大西洋理事会（Atlantic Council）中国研究员宋文笛向BBC中文表示，作为美中台三角关系中的第三方，台湾难免担心自己是否会从“牌桌边”被推上“餐桌”。

不过，他认为无需过度解读此次特习会对台湾的直接影响，“台湾议题并非此次峰会的核心重点”。

宋文笛指出，特朗普当前更关注经贸成果，希望争取中国增加采购并在打击芬太尼等毒品问题上扩大合作，以回应美国国内政治需求；对习近平而言，重点则在于延续中美“建设性战略稳定关系”的论述，并在人工智慧等科技议题上争取更多合作空间。

“无论是川普（特朗普）还是习近平，目前都有比台湾更迫切、也更容易取得成果的议题需要处理。”

政治学者王宏仁则指出，尽管美方此次以高规格礼遇接待习近平，从表面上看，中美关系似乎已暂时稳定下来，但若检视具体成果，双方至今仍未取得显著突破。

他表示，目前较为明确的进展，是美中原定为期一年的贸易“休战”将再延长两个月，但这仍未完全符合北京的期待。此外，双方在稀土出口、大豆采购等议题上尚未达成具体成果。

王宏仁也指出，从此次国宴及相关活动的出席安排来看，中方商界人士的参与仍受到一定限制，显示华府虽希望稳定双边关系，但仍将中国视为涉及国家安全的重要竞争对手，美中之间的竞争与战略戒备并未消失。

BBC中文记者余美霞、江颖怡对本文亦有贡献

title: Explainer: What has turned the Afghan Taliban and Pakistan from partners to foes?
summary: * Summary * Chinese-mediated talks produced ceasefire in March * Hundreds were killed in clashes this year * Attacks in Pakistan killed at least 30 people last week * Pakistan launched air strikes on multiple Afghan targets this week * Paki
content:
*   Summary

*   Chinese-mediated talks produced ceasefire in March
*   Hundreds were killed in clashes this year
*   Attacks in Pakistan killed at least 30 people last week
*   Pakistan launched air strikes on multiple Afghan targets this week
*   Pakistan initially welcomed Taliban return in 2021

ISLAMABAD, September 25 - Pakistan's air force [struck 10 locations in Afghanistan](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-says-it-launched-air-strikes-afghanistan-over-drone-attacks-2026-09-24/) on Thursday, its second round of strikes in four days after three months of relative ​quiet along the two countries' 2,600-km (1,600-mile) border.

Islamabad said it struck militant hideouts in retaliation for drones launched from Afghanistan. Kabul denied sending the drones and ‌said the seven Afghan fatalities in strikes this week were all civilians.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fasia-pacific%2Fwhat-has-turned-afghan-taliban-pakistan-partners-foes-2026-09-25%2F)

Here is what is driving the latest escalation, and why previous attempts to contain it have failed.

## WHY HAVE THE FORMER ALLIES TURNED ON EACH OTHER?

Islamabad initially viewed the Taliban government as a potential ally when it returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021. Then-Prime Minister Imran Khan applauded the Taliban's return, saying Afghans had "broken the shackles of slavery."

Pakistani frustration soon mounted, however, as ​militants launched widening insurgencies in Pakistan's southwest and northwest.

Pakistan has since accused its archrival India and the Taliban-run government in Kabul of providing the militants with funds and ​weapons as well as a safe haven in Afghanistan. The Afghan Taliban and the Indian government deny these allegations.

Frustration in Islamabad spilled into ⁠cross-border fighting last year when Pakistan carried out an air strike on the Afghan capital Kabul in October, targeting the head of the Pakistani Taliban militant group, Pakistani security officials said ​at the time.

The Pakistani Taliban, a group that operates separately from the Afghan Taliban that run the government in Kabul, later said their leader survived the strike.

Pakistan has also accused the Afghan ​Taliban of hosting Baloch insurgents, a secular armed movement seeking independence for the southwestern province of Balochistan.

## HOW DID PRIOR ESCALATION SPIRALS END?

A first ceasefire, signed in Doha in October, soon faltered. Clashes reached a peak in intensity this spring when hundreds were killed in shelling and air strikes.

In the deadliest incident, more than 400 people were killed in one of the [Pakistani air strikes on Kabul](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-bombs-fuel-depot-private-airline-near-kandahar-airport-afghan-taliban-2026-03-13/), which the Afghan Taliban said hit a drug ​rehabilitation centre. Islamabad defended the strikes as having "precisely targeted military installations and terrorist support infrastructure."

Chinese-mediated talks produced a ceasefire in March that quelled the fighting but again postponed a resolution of ​the underlying dispute.

Item 1 of 2 A member of the Taliban security forces inspects metal debris at the site of a partially damaged house following what Taliban officials say was a Pakistani airstrike in Gurbuz district, Khost province, Afghanistan, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer/File Photo

**[1/2]**A member of the Taliban security forces inspects metal debris at the site of a partially damaged house following what Taliban officials say was a Pakistani airstrike in Gurbuz district, Khost province, Afghanistan, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/a-member-of-the-taliban-security-forces-inspects-metal-debris-at-the-site-of-a-partially-damaged-house-in-gurbuz/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkpQTkFNUUVGMQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

## WHAT TRIGGERED THE LATEST ESCALATION?

Nearly three months of relative quiet ended last week with two major militant attacks in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 30 people, including 15 police officials and 6 soldiers.

At ‌least 8 ⁠militants, including suicide bombers, killed 24 people, including 15 police officials, at a police facility in northwestern Kohat district last Friday. An Islamist militant group - Shura Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen led by militant commander Hafiz Gul Bahadur - claimed the attack.

Two days later, on Sunday, an exchange of fire with militants killed 4 soldiers and 2 officers in adjacent Hangu district.

## WHAT ARE THE MAIN MILITANT GROUPS IN THE NORTHWEST?

Pakistan's widening insurgencies are waged by competing groups with different support bases and ideologies but a common enemy in the Pakistani state.

Most recent attacks by militants in northwestern Pakistan have been attributed ​to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), commonly known as the Pakistani ​Taliban.

It was formed in 2007 by a ⁠group of Islamist outfits from the Pashtun ethnic group operating in northwestern Pakistan, which borders Afghanistan.

The TTP was modelled on the Afghan Taliban, the predominantly ethnic Pashtun movement that conquered Afghanistan in the 1990s before being ousted by a US-led invasion in 2001.

TTP fighters also fought alongside ​the Afghan Taliban in Afghanistan and sheltered Afghan fighters in Pakistan, forging a close bond over the Afghan Taliban's 20-year insurgency.

Pakistan mounted a ​series of military operations ⁠against the TTP on its own soil, with limited success.

In recent years, the group's attacks have primarily targeted Pakistani security forces rather than civilians, allowing it to make inroads into local communities.

The leader of the Shura Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen group that claimed responsibility for last week's attack in Kohat - Hafiz Gul Bahadur - once hosted al Qaeda and Arab Islamist fighters in the bordering region, said Abdul Basit, an analyst at ⁠Singapore's S. ​Rajaratnam School of International Studies.

The group initially focused attacks on US and NATO forces in Afghanistan, but turned against ​Pakistan after its military conducted a major offensive around 2015 targeting a safe haven of the group in North Waziristan district, Basit said. That pushed the group's fighters into Afghanistan.

The long-term repercussions of that shift are still playing out ​today, said Basit, as Bahadur's group has become "an umbrella of different militant groups where al Qaeda is the architect and Gul Bahadur is the face."

Reporting by Asif Shahzad; Editing by Rick Noack

He primarily reports out of Pakistan, Afghanistan regions, with a great interest and an extensive knowledge of Asia. He also reports on politics, economy, finance, business, commodities, Islamist militancy, human rights

*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Russia steps up air attacks on Ukrainian industry
*   ArcelorMittal says it can't operate Kryvyi Rih plant safely
*   Company to take impairment charge of around $1 billion

KYIV, Sept 25 (Reuters) - Steelmaker ArcelorMittal said on Friday it could not restart production at Ukraine's ​largest steel plant after a series of missile strikes, the latest economic setback from Russia's escalating air campaign.

The Luxembourg-based firm ‌said it had informed the Ukrainian government that "safe and sustainable" operations were not possible after four strikes in five weeks caused extensive damage and killed five workers at the southeastern plant.

Its shutdown is another blow to Ukraine's steel sector, a key industry that accounts for 15% of the country's exports but has come under pressure from ​Russian attacks and [restrictions from the EU](https://www.reuters.com/business/ukraines-war-hit-steel-industry-faces-new-obstacle-eu-rules-2026-08-14/), its top trading partner.

"It is with deep regret that we have concluded that we are ​no longer able to safely operate ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih," subsidiary CEO Mauro Longobardo said in a statement.

## ESCALATING AIR WAR

Russia ⁠has intensified attacks across Ukraine in recent months using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones that Kyiv's military lacks the resources to intercept.

Targets have included ​businesses, logistics networks, Black Sea port facilities and civilian infrastructure.

A drone strike on central Kyiv on Friday killed a 14-year-old boy in an attack ​President Volodymyr Zelenskiy described as "absolutely savage and sickening".

Zelenskiy said a separate strike killed one person at a postal facility in the Black Sea port of Odesa, while a medical clinic in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia was hit while people were inside.

Russia denies deliberately targeting civilians [in the war](https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraine-russia-war/), triggered by its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in ​2022.

The United Nations said on Friday its monitoring mission in Ukraine had recorded at least 200 civilian deaths in September from attacks that also ​damaged "homes, hospitals, shops and workplaces".

Russia's defence ministry said its forces had carried out overnight drone strikes on Ukrainian defence industry facilities, logistics centres and vessels used by Kyiv's ‌armed forces.

Ukraine ⁠has also stepped up attacks on Russia, targeting defence and energy facilities as well as major online retailers in an effort to undermine revenues and support for Moscow's war effort.

## SUFFERING STEEL INDUSTRY

ArcelorMittal, whose Kryvyi Rih plant produced 1.7 million metric tons of steel in 2025, said it expected to book a non-cash impairment charge of around $1 billion.

The plant's operations also include iron ore mines, which produced 7.6 million tons of iron ore in 2025, ​according to the company's annual report.

"We ​are discussing the future of ⁠the plant with the Government of Ukraine and will focus on preserving the infrastructure, so when peace finally returns, options for restarting production remain available," said Longobardo.

ArcelorMittal shares were up 2.2% at 1021 GMT, outperforming a 0.6% ​rise in the pan-European STOXX 600 index

.

Ukrainian steelmaker Metinvest, owned by the country's richest person, has also ​been repeatedly targeted by ⁠Russian attacks.

Earlier this month, a ballistic missile strike on its Kamet pig iron and steel plant in the eastern Dnipropetrovsk region forced a halt to operations.

Zaporizhstal, its nearly century-old mill, [temporarily closed](https://www.reuters.com/world/russian-attack-kyiv-triggers-fires-officials-say-2026-08-10/) in August after a strike that killed seven workers.

The impact of the shutdown on ArcelorMittal and global steel markets is likely ⁠to be limited ​because the Kryvyi Rih plant had already been operating at significantly reduced capacity since ​2022, a Kepler Cheuvreux analyst told Reuters.

Investors appeared to have anticipated the decision after recent strikes, while the $1 billion impairment charge was relatively modest for a company of ArcelorMittal's size, ​equivalent to roughly 2% of its market capitalisation, the analyst said.

title: 特朗普为何送习近平一座白头海鵰？国礼背后的外交玄机
summary: ## 为何特朗普在国宴上送习近平一座华丽的白头海鵰雕像？ 图像来源，EPA 图像加注文字，特朗普称，他与第一夫人梅拉尼娅一同参与了雕像的设计。 * * Author, 布兰登‧德雷农（Brandon Drenon）、萨琳·哈贝什安（Sareen Habeshian） * Published 1 小时前 * 阅读时间: 3 分钟 美国总统特朗普在华盛顿一场盛大的国宴上，向中国国家主席习近平赠送了一座白头海鵰雕像。这种鸟类原生于北美，也是美国的国家象征。 这份礼物在星期四的国宴上
content:
## 为何特朗普在国宴上送习近平一座华丽的白头海鵰雕像？

图像来源，EPA

图像加注文字，特朗普称，他与第一夫人梅拉尼娅一同参与了雕像的设计。

*       *   Author, 布兰登‧德雷农（Brandon Drenon）、萨琳·哈贝什安（Sareen Habeshian）

*   Published 1 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

美国总统特朗普在华盛顿一场盛大的国宴上，向中国国家主席习近平赠送了一座白头海鵰雕像。这种鸟类原生于北美，也是美国的国家象征。

这份礼物在星期四的国宴上，于一众贵宾面前亮相。特朗普说，它体现了“美国自由翱翔的精神”。

他表示，自己和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普都有参与雕像的设计。

这座雕像亦反映了国际外交中一个珍贵但有时相当棘手的环节：送礼。

此类礼物虽只是小小心意，却别具意义，也呼应习近平与特朗普三天峰会的一项更宏大目标——在两个全球超级大国的领导人之间建立私人情谊。

美商亚洲集团（The Asia Group）合夥人康达（Daniel Kritenbrink）说：“他们要讨论所有这些复杂的问题，但说到底，他们仍然是两个人。”

他说：“所以，这种私人关系是有意义的。我认为交换礼物是其中一个重要部分。”

康达曾任美国外交官超过30年，大部分时间在亚洲工作。他说，对习近平而言，私人关系尤其重要。

他认为，特朗普与习近平之间直接建立的关系，是维系“全球最复杂、影响最深远的双边关系”的黏合剂。

康达形容这种“领袖层级外交”，他认为特朗普同样重视。

送礼在特朗普的总统任期内一直占有独特的位置。

这位美国总统曾经收到豪华大型客机、刻字金条、镶满钻石和宝石的金戒指等礼物。

挪威国际事务研究所（Norwegian Institute of International Affairs）的奥勒·雅各布·森丁（Ole Jacob Sending）说：“如果从这个角度理解特朗普的总统任期，我认为广义而言，送礼确实是他行事方式的一部分。”

星期四早上，习近平宣布向亚特兰大一间动物园赠送两只中国大熊猫，同时推出一项新的学生交流计划，未来五年将接待10万名美国学生到中国留学。

习近平说：“大熊猫一直是中美人民友谊的使者。几天后，两只大熊猫‘平平’和‘福双’将来到亚特兰大动物园的新家，与美国人民见面。”

目前尚不清楚习近平是否还赠送了其他礼物。BBC已就此联络白宫。

如今，赠送豪华礼物的外交传统，主要仍见于海湾国家和威权政府。

莫滕·斯库姆斯鲁德·安德森（Morten Skumsrud Anderson）曾与森丁共同研究外交与送礼文化。他说：“中国等威权国家会赠送昂贵得多的礼物。”

安德森说，在西方，这项传统已受到民主制度的制衡和限制，重要性因而有所降低。

例如，美国宪法中的“薪酬条款”限制总统可以从外国政府收取的礼物价值。

目前上限是525美元（397英镑）。如果礼物价值高于这个金额，便会成为联邦政府财产，除非总统选择自掏腰包将它买下。

同样，美国总统如果要送出价值超过特定金额的礼物，一般也要经过国会程序，除非由总统本人付款。

森丁说：“这里涉及大量规则和礼宾程序。要仔细考虑送甚么礼物、在哪里交换礼物、以甚么方式进行，以及甚么时候进行。”

他说：“所有这些事情都是经过高度编排的，而且较低层级的人员会提前几个星期反复磋商。”

安德森补充：“这可不是在机场临时买的礼物。”

2013年习近平对美国进行国事访问期间，时任总统奥巴马送给他一张刻有文字的长椅，以加州原生的红杉木制成。两人当时正是在加州会面，之后更一同坐在长椅上，微笑让传媒拍照。

相比之下，2009年的一次礼物交换就没有那么成功。

当时英国首相戈登·布朗（Gordon Brown）送给奥巴马一个装饰用的书桌笔座，以一艘历史悠久的反奴隶贸易船只木材制成；奥巴马回赠戈登·布朗的则是一套DVD，据报却无法在英国的DVD播放器上播放。

森丁说：“这算是一次颇尴尬的礼物交换。”

幸好，戈登·布朗和奥巴马是盟友领导人，而不是要设法解决看似难以化解分歧的深层竞争对手。

森丁说：“你可不想把事情搞砸。”他补充，一份不恰当的礼物，甚至有可能破坏更大的外交目标。

而在特朗普与习近平这次会面中，潜在利害尤其重大。

这是特朗普第二个总统任期开始以来，两人第三次面对面会晤。两国正竞逐迅速发展的人工智能产业主导地位，而外界对人工智能可能带来末日式灾难的忧虑也日益增加。

此次峰会亦是在一场激烈的中美贸易战之后举行。双方目前只是以临时休战暂时化解争端，并在这次访问期间延长休战期限。

所以，康达说，那就安排军机飞越上空、准备表演、把酒杯斟满，再交换礼物吧。

他说：“礼宾、场面和交换礼物，全部都只是达成一个目标的手段，那就是维持稳定的美中关系。”

“无论哪一天，要我在脆弱的休战和白热化的贸易战之间选，我都会选前者。”

## 习近平获特朗普红地毡迎接，但并非事事如愿

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，特朗普与习近平出席白宫国宴。

*       *   Author, 碧嘉兰（Laura Bicker）
    *   Role,  BBC驻中国记者

*   Published 2026年9月25日凌晨4点24分

最近更新： 1 小时前
*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

习近平与特朗普举行峰会，有一个很清楚的目标。

中国认为，美国正试图遏制中国崛起成为超级大国，因此希望华盛顿不要阻碍中国，尤其是在贸易、科技和台湾议题上。

不过，这次访问期间，尽管特朗普以红地毡隆重迎接习近平，这名中国领导人并未得到所有他想要的东西。

中美此前暂停互相加征关税，避免贸易战进一步升级。这次双方只同意把贸易休战延长几个月，由11月延至明年1月。

北京原本希望至少延长一年，让习近平可以在特朗普余下任期内继续维持这种局面。

这意味关税、中国在稀土供应方面的主导地位，以及中国取得美国先进晶片等主要争议，只是再次被推迟到下一轮谈判处理。

对习近平而言，一个令人不太舒服的现实是，中国国内经济正面对困难。

中国向世界各地出口的商品数量创下纪录，但国内消费者仍然不愿增加开支。青年失业率持续高企，而在约八成人拥有自置居所的中国，楼价亦大幅下跌。

贸易正协助支撑经济增长，因此中国能否进入海外市场，比以往任何时候都更加重要。习近平需要保护中国出口，避免再次受到美国去年实施的高额关税重创。

在台湾议题上，习近平再次明确表示，美国对台军售是中国的红线。

根据美国法律，美国有义务向这个实行自治的岛屿提供自我防卫所需的手段。

今年5月，习近平曾警告特朗普，如果处理台湾问题不当，两国就会“碰撞甚至冲突”。

特朗普其后延迟批准一项总值140亿美元的对台军售案，并形容这是与北京谈判时“非常好的筹码”。

习近平可能在这次会谈中利用这个突破口，并很可能主张，限制对台湾的支持可以减低爆发冲突的风险。

他星期四再次表示，希望美国坚持反对“台独”的“正确立场”。

不过，特朗普正面对来自民主、共和两党要求继续支持台湾的压力，而他至今仍未公开回应习近平这番说话。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，贸易正协助支撑中国经济增长

两名领导人至少有讨论人工智能，但目前仍不清楚双方是否就任何安全保障措施达成共识。

外界一直关注两人会否就人工智能作出任何具体决定，例如同意举行人工智能峰会。

此前，人工智能公司Anthropic行政总裁达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）发表文章，呼吁放慢人工智能发展速度，以提高安全性。该公司一名顶尖安全研究员亦曾警告，人工智能导致人类灭绝的机率“高于10%”。

不过，除了习近平谈到确保人工智能“始终处于人类控制之下”的重要性之外，双方并没有公布太多其他内容。

特朗普近期则把人工智能可能导致人类灭绝的忧虑斥为“骗局”。

当然，也别忘了大熊猫。中国在4月首次宣布向亚特兰大赠送“平平”和“福双”，习近平如今表示，牠们将在数天内抵达，标志着中国的“熊猫外交”重新展开。

随着两人在星期五准备茶叙和参观美国国家档案馆，可能还会有更多宣布。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，大熊猫长期在中国外交中扮演重要角色

但至少到目前为止，这场峰会给北京带来的其中一项最大收获，可能是场面和观感。

豪华的接待、特朗普亲自到机场迎接，以及以芝麻脆皮鲈鱼和烩小白菜入馔的国宴，都受到不少中国民众欢迎。这有助进一步巩固习近平在国内与特朗普平起平坐的形象。

中国社交媒体上广泛流传把两名领导人作对比的网络迷因。其中一张热门图片显示，轰炸机从上空飞过时，特朗普皱起脸来，习近平则神情不变。

习近平似乎已找到一套与这名全球最难预测的领导人之一打交道的方法。

但特朗普谈论的是两人“真正伟大的友谊”，习近平关注的却是更大的目标：确保中国能够与美国并列，取得超级大国的地位。

大熊猫、隆重仪式和友好言辞或许有助令两国关系变得顺畅一些。

但在这些华丽场面之下，全球两个最强大国家之间的竞争，仍然一如以往激烈。

content:
## 习近平访美：白宫国宴谁出席、谁缺席？意味了什么？

图像来源，Reuters

Published 2026年9月25日凌晨5点03分

最近更新： 44 分钟前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

美国总统特朗普于美东时间周四（9月24日）晚上，在白宫东厅设国宴欢迎中国国家主席习近平。

多名美国科技和金融界巨头出席，部份人士更与两国领导人同桌。但近日高调警告人工智能风险的企业Anthropic代表未有露面。

有分析认为访问行程至今未见重大突破，外界持续关注中美两国就人工智能发展及台湾等议题的表态。

两国元首周五将在白宫共进下午茶，并前往美国国家档案馆（National Archives）参观，其后习近平将启程离开美国。

## 国宴前致辞的不同侧重点

两国元首在国宴开始前发表致辞，特朗普赞扬美中关系的悠久历史，感谢习近平专程从中国远道访美，并表示：“我们之间的关系从未像现在这样好。”

他一度提及正兴建宴会厅，预计一年后才会完工；又指作为一项“特别礼遇”，习近平及夫人可成为首批进入白宫新宴会厅的人士。

特朗普向习近平赠送一座白头海鵰雕塑，他与第一夫人梅拉尼娅均有参与设计。

白头海鵰原生于北美洲，并被定为美国的官方国鸟。特朗普表示，这座雕塑体现“美国自由翱翔的精神”，“我们希望它能在北京找到一个美好而合适的位置。这是属于你的荣誉”。

习近平则在致辞中，感谢特朗普与梅拉尼娅的“热情接待和周到安排”，令他和夫人“有宾至如归的感觉”。

与特朗普的发言相比，习近平的讲话内容明显更着重历史层面，特别提及两国在第二次世界大战期间“抗击日本军国主义侵略者”，形容“血与火锻造的友谊必将世代相传。”

他回顾特朗普今年5月访华，“我们同意构建中美建设性战略稳定关系”。他又表示，双方今日进行“坦诚深入的交流”，“为中美关系提供了新的战略指引。”

图像来源，Reuters

视频加注文字，白宫晚宴 习近平特朗普伉俪再亮相

## 谁出席国宴？

多名美国科技和金融界巨头齐聚白宫，部份人士更与两国领导人同桌，包括：

*   辉达行政总裁黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）及其妻子洛丽·黄（Lori Huang）
*   苹果执行董事长蒂姆·库克（Tim Cook）
*   特斯拉行政总裁伊隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）
*   超微半导体公司（AMD）行政总裁苏姿丰（Lisa Su）及其丈夫丹尼尔·林（Daniel Lin）

出席者还包括来自OpenAI、亚马逊及谷歌等公司的多位科技界重量级人物。

值得留意的是，逾130人的宾客名单中，据报只有19人属于中国代表团，但没有企业界人士。

今年5月特朗普访问北京期间，当时国宴主桌上的中方席位主要由政府官员组成。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，2026年9月24日，美国总统特朗普与中国国家主席习近平在美国华盛顿特区白宫举行的国宴上并肩而坐，同桌还有多名科技业界巨头。

此次峰会其中一个重要议题，正是美中两国未来是否有可能在人工智能安全相关问题上展开合作。

然而，Anthropic代表未有出席国宴。该公司是全球规模最大、估值最高的人工智能企业之一。BBC记者曾向Anthropic查询是不被获邀还是自行决定不出席，但至今仍未收到回覆。

Anthropic向来对人工智能及中国问题持较强硬立场。该公司不仅多次警告人工智能若缺乏监管可能带来的风险，亦曾就中国议题提出警示。

其行政总裁达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）曾在一篇文章中警告，若中国在人工智能竞赛中取得领先地位，将对美国及全球构成“严重危险”。中方则强烈反驳有关说法。

中国外交部表示，将中国描绘成“威胁”的论调，只会干扰人工智能治理进程。

中国《环球时报》（Global Times）英文版在习近平展开访美行程后，发表多篇评论文章，呼吁中美两国成为“伙伴，而非对手”。其中多篇文章提到人工智能（AI），并认为人工智能“应成为拓展中美合作的新领域”。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，特斯拉行政总裁伊隆·马斯克。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，辉达行政总裁黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）及其妻子洛丽·黄（Lori Huang）

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，OpenAI首席执行官山姆·阿尔特曼（Sam Altman；奥特曼）与Meta行政总裁马克·朱克伯格

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，亚马逊创办人杰夫·贝佐斯（Jeff Bezos）及妻子萝伦·桑切斯（Lauren Sanchez）

食物方面，国宴选用世酿伯格酒庄的气泡酒，有向历史致敬意味。

1972年，时任美国总统尼克逊访华，曾与中国时任总理周恩来举行著名的“和平祝酒”（Toast to Peace）时，所使用的正是来自同一酒庄的葡萄酒。

按梅拉尼娅办公室公布国宴菜单，当中包括：前菜黄南瓜浓汤、主菜芝麻脆皮鲈鱼，配搭炖白菜（bok choy）及烤茄子，以及香草奶油冻配酸樱桃蜜饯和核桃杏仁奶油作为甜点；办公室称其旨在展现“美国食材，并融入细腻的中国风味”。

## 三家美国新闻机构被禁止采访国宴

美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）、《政治》（Politico） 和MS NOW（前身为MSNBC）三间媒体的记者早前表示，法官已裁定必须恢复他们进入白宫园区采访的权利，但他们仍被拒绝进入采访白宫国宴。

特朗普自上周六起禁止这三家美国传媒进入白宫，并指责它们发布“假新闻”。

在一名联邦法官于周四凌晨裁定该禁令可能违反宪法，并要求政府恢复其采访权后，三家媒体的记者于周四上午获准再次进入白宫园区。

不过，这些机构当晚表示，他们被禁止采访国宴活动。

## 峰会至今释放的讯号

部分民主党议员批评峰会过于着重“排场”，而非实质成果。至今仍未见到在贸易、人工智能、对台军售以及关键矿产等重大分歧议题上取得突破。

路透社取得的一份声明显示，47名民主党党团成员中有19人联署，敦促总统立即向台湾提供数十亿美元的资金及军售，并要求中国释放被错误拘留的美国公民。

这些民主党议员亦批评特朗普放宽对中国出口高端晶片的限制。

北京与华盛顿已同意将贸易休战期延长两个月，以争取时间磋商一项更大规模的协议。

Saxo Markets投资策略师洛芙·查纳纳（Charu Chanana）表示，目前企业对于未来数月将在何种营商环境下运作，所面对的不确定性与之前相差不大。

企业关注的是一些实际讯号，例如“已公布的关税调整”、稀土出口安排、农产品采购，以及美国晶片出口规则的变化。

查纳纳表示：“与峰会展现出的友好气氛相比，这些因素更为重要。”

“我的解读是，这是一场旨在维持稳定的峰会，而非一场实现突破的峰会。”

## 华盛顿多地现示威活动

习近平访美期间，首都华盛顿多地出现示威活动。

有一批示威者抗议中国政府对新疆维吾尔族穆斯林的待遇。

人权组织认为，中国近年来违背其意愿，将超过100万名维吾尔人拘留于所谓的“再教育营”内。

来自维珍尼亚州的示威者阿齐兹·苏莱曼（Aziz Sulayman）向路透社表示，其兄长阿利姆·苏莱曼（Alim Sulayman）是一名牙医，于10年前被捕。

他说：“我不知道他现在身在何处。据我所知，他被判监17年，没有经过任何法庭审讯，也没有任何正当法律程序。他是无辜的。他是一名年轻的维吾尔男子。我们希望他能够获得自由。”

视频加注文字，白宫习特会登场 亲华反华团体华府示威

另一名在白宫外示威的人士海德尔·詹（Haider Jan）向路透社表示，就针对维吾尔人及中国其他少数民族的人权侵害问题，“特朗普总统必须质询习近平。”

中国政府一直否认所有在新疆的人权侵犯行为指控。

要求结束中国对西藏控制的示威者穿过华盛顿市区游行，其后在美国国会大厦外集结。

自中国政府于1950年代将西藏纳入管治范围以来，西藏一直是中国高度敏感的议题。当地长期以来要求获得更大的自治权。

北京视西藏为中国不可分割的一部分，但西藏领袖表示，中国派驻当地的军队和官员有所增加，削弱其宗教信仰及传统文化。

华盛顿部分政界人士一直支持西藏独立运动。民主党重量级人物佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）到场探访这批示威者。

外间也关注特朗普会否再度向习近平提出释放黎智英。

title: What is 'Taiwan independence' and is Taiwan already independent?
summary: TAIPEI, September 25 - China's [Xi Jinping](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-welcomes-xi-washington-looking-trade-win-2026-09-24/) told President Donald Trump on Thursday that he hoped the US will adhere to the "correct position" o
content:
TAIPEI, September 25 - China's [Xi Jinping](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-welcomes-xi-washington-looking-trade-win-2026-09-24/) told President Donald Trump on Thursday that he hoped the US will adhere to the "correct position" of opposing Taiwan independence, and that the Chinese stance on "reunification" is clear-cut.

Below are some questions and answers about what is meant by the term "Taiwan independence" and the positions of the Chinese, US and Taiwanese governments.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fwhat-is-taiwan-independence-is-taiwan-already-independent-2026-09-25%2F)

## WHAT IS TAIWAN'S HISTORY ​AND FORMAL NAME TODAY?

The Qing dynasty incorporated Taiwan as part of Fujian province in 1684 and only declared it a separate Chinese province in ‌1885.

Following the Qing's defeat in a war with Japan, it became a Japanese colony in 1895. In 1945, it was handed over to the Republic of China government at the end of World War Two.

In 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong's Communist forces, the Republic of China government fled and moved its capital to Taiwan, and Republic of China remains the island's formal name.

Mao set up the People's Republic ​of China, and claimed it was the only legitimate Chinese government for the whole of China, including Taiwan, as the Republic of China's successor state.

## WHAT IS TAIWAN'S ​INTERNATIONAL STATUS AND CHINA'S POSITION?

For decades, the Republic of China in Taipei also claimed to be the legitimate Chinese government, but in 1971 ⁠Beijing took over the China seat at the United Nations from Taipei.

Most major Western countries and US allies maintain close unofficial ties with Taiwan by recognising the Republic of ​China passport and having de facto embassies in each other's capitals.

China says it will not renounce the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control. Beijing has [offered Taiwan](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-again-touts-benefits-union-with-taiwan-taipei-rebuffs-2026-04-29/) a "one country, ​two systems" model similar to Hong Kong, which promised the city a high degree of autonomy, although no major political party in Taiwan supports that.

## WHAT IS THE US POSITION?

Any change in official US wording on Taiwan would upend decades of policy set by both Republican and Democratic presidents.

The US severed official ties with Taipei in favour of Beijing in 1979 but is bound by the Taiwan Relations Act to ​provide the island with the means to defend itself. The US officially takes no position on Taiwan's sovereignty under Washington's "One China" policy.

Item 1 of 3 A person rides a bike past Taiwan flags, above the entrance to Nanjichang Night Market, in Taipei, Taiwan, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Ann Wang

**[1/3]**A person rides a bike past Taiwan flags, above the entrance to Nanjichang Night Market, in Taipei, Taiwan, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Ann Wang [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/a-person-rides-a-bike-past-taiwan-flags-above-the-entrance-to-nanjichang-night-market-in-taipei/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkxQTkFKOEw5VA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

In 2022, the State Department also added wording ​on the Six Assurances, referring to six Reagan-era security assurances given to Taiwan, which the United States declassified in 2020.

Among the assurances made in 1982, but never previously formally made public, are statements that ‌the US ⁠has not set a date for ending arms sales to Taiwan, nor agreed to prior consultation with Beijing on such sales, or to revise the Taiwan Relations Act that underpins US policy towards the island.

China has repeatedly demanded that the US [end arms sales](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-expected-press-trump-halt-taiwan-arms-sales-under-1982-agreement-2026-09-22/) to Taiwan.

In May after meeting Xi in Beijing, Trump said he was still considering whether to go ahead with new weapons sales and that the US was "not looking to have somebody say, 'Let's go [independent](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-open-direct-talks-between-trump-lai-amid-concerns-after-beijing-summit-2026-05-18/) because the United States is backing us'."

The US ended its formal defence alliance with Taiwan in ​1979 and has since then had a ​policy of "strategic ambiguity" on whether it would ⁠come to Taipei's defence should Beijing attack.

## IS TAIWAN ALREADY AN INDEPENDENT COUNTRY?

Taiwan, whose people elect their own leaders and whose government controls a defined area of territory with its own military, passport and currency, enjoys de facto independence even if that is not formally recognised ​by most countries.

Taiwan's government says the Republic of China is a sovereign state and that Beijing has no right to speak ​for or represent it given ⁠the People's Republic of China has no say in how it chooses its leaders and has never ruled Taiwan.

## COULD TAIPEI DECLARE A "REPUBLIC OF TAIWAN"?

It would be very difficult and require parliamentary approval of a constitutional amendment and then a referendum, rather than a simple declaration by President Lai Ching-te.

At least 75% of lawmakers would need to pass that amendment, and the ruling Democratic Progressive ⁠Party and ​main opposition party the Kuomintang (KMT) currently have an equal number of seats.

The DPP, which has been in power ​since 2016, has not made an attempt to change the constitution. The KMT strongly opposes any attempts to change the name Republic of China.

## WHAT DOES TAIWAN'S PRESIDENT SAY ABOUT INDEPENDENCE?

China detests Lai and calls him a "separatist". Before ​Lai was elected president he made comments about being a "practical worker for Taiwan independence". Lai maintains he simply meant Taiwan is already [an independent country](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-independence-means-we-dont-belong-beijing-president-says-2026-05-17/).

Reporting by Ben Blanchard; Editing by Michael Perry

title: Trump to wrap up Xi summit with a tour of US archives
summary: * Summary * Trump, Xi tout stability but few big summit breakthroughs * Taiwan looms as Trump takes Xi on National Archives tour * Focus will be Trump's post-summit comments on Taiwan WASHINGTON, Sept 25 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trum
content:
*   Summary

*   Trump, Xi tout stability but few big summit breakthroughs
*   Taiwan looms as Trump takes Xi on National Archives tour
*   Focus will be Trump's post-summit comments on Taiwan

WASHINGTON, Sept 25 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump will follow up his summit with Xi Jinping by taking the Chinese leader ​on Friday to the US National Archives, where they are expected to stress views about the history and direction of ‌ties between their countries.

Thursday's lavish state summit at the White House appeared [heavy on symbolism but light on substance](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-welcomes-xi-washington-looking-trade-win-2026-09-24/), with no sign of major breakthroughs between the world's biggest economies.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Ftrump-wrap-up-xi-summit-with-tour-us-archives-2026-09-25%2F)

Still, Trump [highlighted progress](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/four-takeaways-trumps-summit-with-xi-washington-2026-09-24/) under a bilateral trade mechanism, citing what he described as increased market access for US farmers and ranchers, while both leaders identified artificial intelligence as an area ​for cooperation.

Trump said in remarks welcoming Xi they would see some of the greatest treasures of US history at the National Archives, ​including the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights.

They would also see "artifacts testifying to ⁠the long and cherished relationship" between China and the United States and their "cultural exchanges," he said.

"Just as our ancestors reached across the ocean centuries ago ​to trade, to learn, and to build a better world, our two countries do really the same thing, and we're very proud of it and ​the relationship," Trump said.

China has not commented on the visit to the archives, but analysts say Xi may be keen to see records relating to the US switch of recognition [to communist China from Taiwan](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-expected-press-trump-halt-taiwan-arms-sales-under-1982-agreement-2026-09-22/) in 1979.

## CHINA PRESSES ON TAIWAN

China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own and Xi has long sought to persuade Trump to state publicly that ​the United States opposes Taiwan's independence, rather than saying only that it does not support independence, which has been Washington's formulation for decades.

He is ​also keen to get the US to halt arms sales to the island.

Item 1 of 3 US President Donald Trump holds a binder as he stands next to Chinese President Xi Jinping before Xi delivers a speech during a state dinner at the White House in Washington, D.C., US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein

**[1/3]**US President Donald Trump holds a binder as he stands next to Chinese President Xi Jinping before Xi delivers a speech during a state dinner at the White House in Washington, D.C., US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-donald-trump-hosts-state-dinner-for-chinas-president-xi-jinping-at-the-white-house-in-washington-dc/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjBRTkE0WEE4Nw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

As expected, Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan on Thursday, saying he hoped the United States would "handle ‌the Taiwan ⁠question with prudence." China's state news agency also reported that Xi "hopes the US side will adhere to the correct position of opposing 'Taiwan independence'."

While the United States, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic relations with Taipei, Washington is its most important international backer and is bound by US law to provide it with the means to defend itself.

America's Asian allies will watch closely to see how Trump talks about Taiwan following Xi's visit.

After his May summit with ​Xi, Trump, whose administration in December ​approved an $11 billion arms sale ⁠package to Taiwan, said he was holding a second package, worth some $14 billion, in abeyance and described it as a "very good negotiating chip."

Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies think tank said Beijing may believe it ​has established a new baseline on Taiwan with Trump.

He said Xi's use of the word "adhere" was revealing because "it ​implies Beijing believes Washington ⁠is already behaving in ways it wants."

"In the context of the current standdown on Taiwan arms sales, China may increasingly view that restraint as a new baseline rather than a temporary pause," he said.

"Beijing's objective is to get Trump to absorb Chinese red lines into his own definition of a stable relationship."

On ⁠Thursday, Senate Democrats ​criticized the summit, saying Trump had failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on ​trade, security, artificial intelligence or human rights.

They also criticized Trump for failing to publicly address China's military pressure on Taiwan and called for the immediate delivery of approved military aid and ​arms sales to the island.

Reporting by David Brunnstrom and Trevor Hunnicutt; additional reporting by Patricia Zengerle and Simon Lewis; Editing by Don Durfee and Stephen Coates

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Trevor Hunnicutt is White House Correspondent at Reuters News. He writes about U.S. foreign and domestic policy and regularly travels with the President of the United States. Prior to joining the White House team in 2021, he covered presidential campaigns, economics, finance and investing for many years. He has also served on the board of the White House Correspondents' Association. Hunnicutt holds a bachelor's degree from Pomona College and a master's from the London School of Economics.

title: How Trump's diplomatic week exposed the limits of his power
summary: * Summary * Trump's foreign policy agenda appears stalled heading into November midterms * Iran stalemate looms large * Some world leaders push back against Trump * US-China summit heavy on pomp, papering over differences WASHINGTON, Sept 2
content:
*   Summary

*   Trump's foreign policy agenda appears stalled heading into November midterms
*   Iran stalemate looms large
*   Some world leaders push back against Trump
*   US-China summit heavy on pomp, papering over differences

WASHINGTON, Sept 25 (Reuters) - From his high-profile address to the UN General Assembly to his high-stakes White House summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump this week was looking to reassert himself on the world stage.

But Trump’s diplomatic flurry has done little to dispel the view among many analysts of a president beset by problems at home and ​abroad. Those include a widening Iran war that has driven up US gasoline prices and cratered his approval ratings, while his relations with allies worsen and the AI challenge from China intensifies.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fhow-trumps-diplomatic-week-exposed-limits-his-power-2026-09-25%2F)

With the limits of his ‌power exposed, Trump has begun facing pushback from world leaders on issues ranging from the crisis in the Middle East to Russia's war in Ukraine, leaving the impression of a foreign policy agenda that has stalled. This comes as Trump's Republican Party faces midterm elections in November that could further constrain him politically.

Even so, Trump’s speech to the United Nations on Tuesday was a stark reminder of how, since returning to the White House last year, he has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped to create from the ashes of World War Two.

Standing atop the rostrum of a world body dedicated ​to peacemaking, he issued a fresh threat to “annihilate” Iran if it did not agree to a deal, defended his coercive approach to OPEC member Venezuela by asserting “to the victor belong the spoils,” and signaled he may not be done deploying ​the US military to achieve his international aims.

Despite that strident stance, Trump’s talks with Xi on Thursday put the US president up against a Chinese counterpart who appeared to be in stronger position, ⁠overseeing a surge in his country’s trade with the world while the US grapples with the economic fallout from the Iran conflict.

## LIMITED RESULTS FROM XI SUMMIT

That was the backdrop for a state visit by Xi that was heavy on pomp and ceremony but light ​on substance, despite a host of thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and Iran. The most tangible outcome appeared limited to a two-month extension of a trade truce, originally due to expire in November, between the world’s two biggest economies.

While Trump showed little interest ​in publicly airing any differences between the two powers, Chinese state media reported that behind closed doors Xi urged him to oppose independence for Taiwan. The democratically governed island claimed by China remains the most contentious topic in relations between Washington and Beijing.

Trump's seemingly non-confrontational attitude was a far cry from his previously hawkish, tariffs-driven approach, which has been tempered by Beijing's control over rare earth minerals, a key input for technology and auto manufacturing that Beijing has shown the ability to withhold in retaliation.

"Trump sees himself taking us back to a world where might makes right," said Brett Bruen, who was ​a foreign policy adviser in the Obama administration and now heads the Global Situation Room strategic consultancy. "But it’s noteworthy that he goes all wobbly when it comes to Xi Jinping and ascendant Chinese power."

Responding to Reuters questions, a White House official rejected the notion that ​Trump's foreign policy had hit a wall and said his UN remarks "highlighted his various wins in advancing US interests around the world," including preventing Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. Tehran has always said its nuclear program is for peaceful purposes.

## IRAN WAR STALEMATE

Looming over Trump’s packed week of ‌diplomacy was the ⁠war with Iran, which he started alongside Israel on February 28.

It has dragged on for nearly seven months, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region — most recently to Yemen and the Red Sea shipping corridor.

Iran’s defiance, despite the economic and military beating it has taken, has become the most intractable foreign policy challenge of Trump’s second term.

Item 1 of 2 US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping stand inside the White House ahead of a state dinner in Washington, D.C., US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

**[1/2]**US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping stand inside the White House ahead of a state dinner in Washington, D.C., US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS/Kylie Cooper [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-trump-hosts-state-dinner-for-chinese-president-xi-jinping-in-washington/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlpQTkE5N1ROTQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Trump used his address at the UN to defend his attack on Iran and to declare that “America is back,” stronger than ever.

But after a string of early foreign policy achievements, including a Gaza ceasefire and the capture of Venezuela's leader, Trump's record in his second term in office is increasingly defined by stalemates.

With the Iran war deeply unpopular and dividing Trump’s political base, he could pay a price in the midterm congressional elections when his Republican Party’s ​control of Congress is at risk.

World leaders appear to be preparing ​for a time when the US president's influence could ⁠begin to wane following the midterms, and with less than two-and-a-half years left in office.

Most European and Asian allies have already spurned Trump's demands for assistance in an Iran conflict he launched without consulting them.

At this year’s UN gathering, some US partners took aim at Trump, though mostly without mentioning him by name.

France's President Emmanuel Macron warned against a global "return to the law of the jungle," saying countries ​faced a choice between a world governed by power and coercion, and a "civilized international society."

In a rebuke to Trump, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva decried foreign interference in his ​country’s October election and insisted that "we ⁠do not need aircraft carriers patrolling our waters, we need cooperation to stem the flow of weapons and money that fuel crime.”

The White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that Trump was "not concerned with posturing but about results" and that some leaders' public comments did not match what they told the president in private.

## RESISTING TRUMP

In another sign of diminished clout, Trump's effort to pressure Ukraine and Russia to agree to even a limited energy ceasefire failed to gain much traction.

And while Trump touted a deal with Denmark and Greenland for an expanded US military ⁠presence in the ​vast Arctic island, it fell short of his initial demand to “own” the territory and his threat, if necessary, to take it by force from a fellow NATO ​member.

“A year ago, few countries dared cross Trump,” Ian Bremmer, president of the Eurasia Group, wrote on X. “Now Canada, Europe, China, Iran, Russia and others are all more willing to say no.”

At one point, Trump himself seemed to wonder how much international sway he actually possessed.

In his speech, he told world leaders he wanted to ​rebrand AI as “super intelligence.”

“Let’s see if I have any power,” he said. “Maybe I do and maybe I don’t. We’re going to find out pretty soon.”

Reporting and writing by Matt Spetalnick; additional reporting by Antoni Slodkowski in New York; Editing by Don Durfee and Edmund Klamann

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

【大紀元2026年09月25日訊】（大紀元記者伊鈴多倫多報導）9月24日，多倫多部分法輪功學員在領館前集會，抗議中共跨國鎮壓，呼籲逮捕一名兩天前在中領館前向法輪功學員發出死亡威脅、並實施仇恨犯罪襲擊的肇事者。

9月22日上午9時20分左右，2位法輪功學員正在領事館外的公共人行道上進行和平抗議。現場視頻顯示：一名身穿印有中共國旗圖案黑外套的男子衝過來，拔掉法輪功學員豎立的幾條橫幅，其中一條被拖走，並推搡試圖取回橫幅的法輪功學員李娜，推搡過程中，導致李娜臉部受傷。（[大紀元報導1](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/26/9/23/n14855701.htm)）（[大紀元報導2](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/26/9/24/n14856699.htm)）

[![Image 19](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856890-DSC_2942.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856890-DSC_2942.jpg)

2026年9月24日，受害人李娜（右）和耿凌寰（左）詳細講述事件發生過程，並呼籲停止跨國鎮壓。（伊鈴/大紀元）

[![Image 20](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856888-be6da002e2dc81216d9d2c1b.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856888-be6da002e2dc81216d9d2c1b.jpg)

這名男子還踢踹正在拍攝事件過程的另一位法輪功學員耿凌寰，並對法輪功學員大吼： 「這是大使館門口……這是中國領土，你知不知道？」還說，按照中共法律中的「反分裂國家法」， 「我可以槍斃你，你知不知道？」

這名男子在和法輪功學員爭奪抗議橫幅時，威脅李娜： 「滾開！摔死你，信不信？槍斃你，信不信？這是中國領土，知道吧？」法輪功學員耿凌寰拍攝了整個過程。

目前，多倫多警局已確認，該事件正在調查中。

法輪功（又稱法輪大法）是一種基於「真、善、忍」原則的修煉功法。自1999年7月以來，在中國一直遭受中國共產黨的迫害。

## 譴責暴力襲擊

當天，數百法輪功學員來到現場，拉開大型橫幅，抗議中共跨國鎮壓。加拿大政界及社區人士也到場聲援，譴責暴力襲擊。

[![Image 23](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856893-DSC_2958.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856893-DSC_2958.jpg)

2026年9月24日，前國會議員李宗（Ted Lizon）譴責暴力襲擊，要求追究肇事者。（伊鈴/大紀元）

前國會議員李宗（Ted Lizon）說：「這是加拿大，這樣暴力事件不可接受。沒有人有權利這樣做，這個人應該被拘捕，並追究。」他認為，政府應該要求王家騎警及情報局（CSIS）介入調查，追究肇事者的責任。

[![Image 24](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856892-DSC_2953.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856892-DSC_2953.jpg)

2026年9月24日，中國民主黨加拿大主席餘厚強（左）和民陣加拿大副祕書長侯世軍譴責暴力襲擊，要求追究肇事者。（伊鈴/大紀元）

中國民主黨加拿大主席餘厚強表示，加拿大是世界上自由、民主、人權做的最好的地方，竟然發生這樣的暴力事件，顯然不是一個簡單事情，無論是指派的、還是自發的，都是犯罪行為，建議加拿大警方調查。

民陣加拿大副祕書長侯世軍在發言中譴責暴力襲擊，要求警察調查，追究暴徒的責任。

法輪功人權組織主席瑪麗亞·張（Maria Chung）對大紀元說：「在光天化日之下，暴徒對法輪功學員進行暴行，這是加拿大絕對不允許的。」

她表示，現在加拿大已經出臺了一個C70法案，法案的第二部分是針對外國干涉和外國鎮壓的暴行，包括恐嚇、威脅和破壞。在加拿大領土上，暴徒引用中共的分裂法來進行恐嚇和死亡威脅，這是非常嚴峻的刑事犯罪，它對法輪功學員這樣做，也可以對其它任何一個團體進行這樣的打壓。這是絕對不允許，絕對不能接受的。

她呼籲，加拿大政府要重視跨國鎮壓，依法逮捕肇事者，並繩之以法。

## 籲停止跨國鎮壓

在當天的新聞會上，受害人李娜和耿凌寰詳細講述事件發生過程，並呼籲停止跨國鎮壓。

李娜說：「在加拿大的自由社會，光天化日之下打砸搶，還用死亡威脅我們，這是對加拿大自由民主的挑釁，是赤裸裸的跨國鎮壓，我要求政府將行兇者繩之以法，維護加拿大的民主自由。」

耿凌寰在發言中表示，要求停止跨國鎮壓，逮捕肇事者，維護加拿大的自由和民主。

中領館真相點協調人潘學鋒表示，她在真相點長期受到不明人士的騷擾、破壞，她呼籲加拿大政府應該重視跨國鎮壓，保護法輪功學員的安全。

[![Image 27](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856889-DSC_2936.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856889-DSC_2936.jpg)

2026年9月24日，加拿大法輪功社區聯絡人李卓夫（Jeff Lee）在集會上發言，譴責暴力襲擊，要求逮捕肇事者。（伊鈴/大紀元）

法輪功社區聯絡人李卓夫（Jeff Lee）說，自1999年中共打壓法輪功開始，在多倫多對法輪功學員的騷擾、襲擊達數百次，大多是快閃式騷擾事件。但這次攻擊持續時間較長，施暴者行為囂張，竟然對和平的法輪功學員施以暴力攻擊和死亡威脅，甚至要求同夥拍攝全過程。這些情況令人有理由相信，事件是經過事先策劃，受到幕後組織的指使。

「我們要求加拿大執法機構徹底調查，查明施暴者的身分，以及參與策劃、指使或協助此次攻擊的幕後黑手。」他說，「 如果調查發現有外國政府或其代理人參與，就必須依法追究相關人員的責任，絕不能讓加拿大成為外國政權實施跨國鎮壓的場所。」

自1999年以來，法輪功學員已經堅持了27年的和平抗議。李卓夫說：「面對長期的恐嚇、騷擾和威脅，我們從未退縮。我們始終堅持以和平、理性的方式，維護信仰自由，揭露迫害，呼籲良知。」

他說，這起暴力事件，向加拿大政府和人民發出警示： 跨國鎮壓正在威脅加拿大社會。他呼籲加拿大政府：徹底調查9月22日發生的暴力攻擊事件，依法追究施暴者的刑事責任。調查事件背後的策劃、指使、資助或協助者，必須依法採取進一步行動。

他呼籲加拿大政府加強對法輪功學員及其他受迫害社群的保護，確保他們能夠安全、自由地行使加拿大法律所保障的基本權利；採取切實有效的措施，同時也呼籲加拿大各級民選代表、社會各界和廣大民眾，共同關注這起事件，維護加拿大的法治、自由與尊嚴。

## 誰是幕後主使者？

[![Image 28](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856896-DSC_2998.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14856896-DSC_2998.jpg)

2026年9月24日，上海移民葛開英到場聲援，譴責幕後指使者。（伊鈴/大紀元）

現場一位上海移民葛開英每天都到中領館前抗議。她因拆遷、上訪與維權經歷，遭遇中共當局打壓與強制關押。當聽到餘厚強在發言中提到該暴力事件是否與中領館有關時，她立刻呼應。

她告訴大紀元，她天天來中領館前抗議，看到有人打法輪功學員，她就拍攝視頻發到X上。她因此被中領館找去談話2次，第一次要了她的電話，第二次要她拿護照來，還要她不要幫助法輪功學員。

今年上半年，一位男子天天來騷擾她。有一天，那位男子離開時，她跟著後面拍攝，走到拐彎處，從中領館後面出來一個人，從口袋掏錢準備付給那位男子。她看到後大喊：原來你付錢讓小粉紅來騷擾我？那人看到她後，趕快把手縮回去。

她說，因為之前被中領館找去談話，在裡面見過這個人，知道他是中領館的人。

2025年，加拿大法輪大法學會發布的一份報告（長達130頁）《針對加拿大法輪功的外國干擾和打壓》，詳細地揭示了中共政權如何將迫害延伸至加拿大，對異見團體實施恐嚇與監視、威脅，網絡攻擊、死亡威脅以及炸彈威脅，對身在中國的家屬註銷或拒發護照等。

## Lawmakers battle National Archives over plans to move historical Asian American records

Reporting from San Bruno, Calif.

Rep. Kevin Mullin, D-Calif., rallies on Aug. 24 with Asian American and tribal leaders and other community members in opposition to the planned closure of the National Archives facility in San Bruno, Calif. The Office of Rep. Kevin Mullin

Democratic lawmakers and local activists are scrambling to stop the [closure of a National Archives and Records Administration](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trump-closing-national-archives-burying-history-rcna592187) facility here, which houses more than 750,000 federal immigration, genealogical and Alcatraz penitentiary records.

They include culturally sensitive archival material treasured by the Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander community: records related to the Chinese Exclusion Act, Angel Island Immigration Station and Japanese American mass incarceration during World War II, as well as Native American census records.

[_**Read the full story here.**_](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/lawmakers-battle-national-archives-plans-move-historical-asian-america-rcna599402)

22h ago / 11:03 PM EDT

## Florida attorney general says 20 people charged with voter fraud

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier.Joe Raedle / Getty Images file

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier and Gov. Ron DeSantis announced today that 20 people in Florida have been charged with voter fraud.

Twelve of the 20 people charged had been arrested as of this afternoon in a statewide election integrity operation that is "targeting illegal voting in Florida elections, including the 2024 General Election."

Most of the 20 cases involve noncitizens who registered to vote and attested to be U.S. citizens, according to Uthmeier. Four of them are convicted felons who registered and voted while still on probation, he said.

His office said additional charges and arrests are expected.

“These defendants swore they were qualified electors, cast ballots in our elections, and later confirmed they were never eligible to vote,” Uthmeier said in a news release.

DeSantis [signed a bill](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/desantis-signs-bill-creating-election-police-unit-florida-rcna25941) in 2022 creating a police force dedicated to pursuing voter fraud and other election crimes via an Office of Election Crimes and Security, which operates under the Florida State Department, reviewing fraud allegations and conducting preliminary investigations.

The first charges stemming from the unit tasked with the prosecutions occurred [later that year.](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/desantis-election-police-charged-20-voter-fraud-advocates-say-story-rcna45895)

"We will not tolerate attempts to undermine the integrity of our electoral process, and we will hold accountable those who violate our laws," DeSantis [said on X](https://x.com/GovRonDeSantis/status/2103262748591239676).

23h ago / 10:44 PM EDT

## Marjorie Taylor Greene says MAGA is 'dead,' strikes out at House Speaker Johnson

Tasos Katopodis / Getty Images file

Former Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene drew a stark contrast between herself and what she called the MAGA “cult” at an event at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, throwing fiery accusations at both Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La.

“So, is it fair to say that MAGA is not just a movement but that it’s also a cult?” asked Robert Draper, a New York Times author and moderator of the conversation.

“I would say yes,” Greene said. “When you vote for someone, not only are you supporting them, but you’re holding them accountable, and if they can’t be truthful and hold him accountable to his campaign promises that affect the entire country, then they’re liars and they’re hypocrites and they’re in a cult.”

Greene, who represented a Georgia district in the House, doubled down by saying the MAGA movement she once supported is "dead."

Greene spent much of her near-hourlong conversation with Draper criticizing Trump, including his opposition to releasing files relating to the late Jeffrey Epstein. Greene said she[and Trump clashed](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/-america-first-marjorie-taylor-greene-knocks-trump-not-focusing-domest-rcna247869) over her backing a House resolution forcing the release of the files.

Trump “had a 100% lock on this is not going to be released,” Greene said. “I mean, he had a tight leash on [former Attorney General] Pam Bondi. This was not going to be released. He had a tight leash on Speaker Johnson, [Senate Republican] Leader John Thune. These are not going to be released. Shut it down.”

Greene said that after she refused to step back from her support for releasing the files, Trump began posting about her on Truth Social, calling her “Marjorie Traitor Greene.” Those posts, according to Greene, spurred backlash and death threats, including [against her son](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/rep-marjorie-taylor-greene-blasts-trump-vicious-unwarranted-attacks-re-rcna244351).

Greene homed in on Johnson, as well, calling him “the biggest liar in Congress” and saying that when Trump was attacking her, he did nothing to stand in her defense.

Draper asked whether she ever planned to run for office again, to which she responded, “Oh, my God, Robert, no.”

“I think it’s safe to say, and I’ll pick on myself — I made probably the worst mistakes of my life,” Greene said of her time in Congress. “I learned the biggest lessons of my life, and I did all of that on a national stage, even a world stage, while serving in Congress.”

23h ago / 10:02 PM EDT

## N.J. Gov. Mikie Sherrill calls on Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell to resign over ethics, sexual harassment violations

Julian Leshay Guadalupe / USA Today Network via Reuters file

New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill said tonight that she was giving Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell until tomorrow to resign after an internal investigation found he had violated state ethics and harassment policy.

"Today, I’m announcing the conclusion and findings of an independent investigation into allegations regarding Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell," Sherrill [wrote on X](https://x.com/GovSherrillNJ/status/2103267032540078234?s=20). "The investigation found that the Lieutenant Governor engaged in serious, repeated violations of state policy and failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office. I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so."

The state of New Jersey [said this month](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/new-jersey/new-jersey-dale-caldwell-investigation/6544406/)that it had hired a law firm to investigate allegations that Caldwell, who was elected on the ticket with Sherrill last year, had behaved inappropriately toward women.

Sherrill said Caldwell's "ethical lapses persisted despite multiple warnings and trainings."

"The substantiated finding of sexual harassment is extremely troubling. I’ve seen firsthand how a hostile culture can undermine everyone’s ability to succeed. It’s insidious and ruptures the trust within an organization," she said.

Sherrill said that the investigation "fully examined the evidence, followed the facts, and protected everyone’s privacy" and that Caldwell's resignation "is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents."

Lawyers for Caldwell said in a statement tonight that they "strongly disputed the three findings in the investigation into allegations concerning his conduct," as its conclusions "go further than the evidence supports."

“This unnecessarily protracted and one-sided process lacked the requisite due process that should be afforded every citizen of this state,” said Thomas Calcagni, a lawyer for Caldwell.

Calcagni said Caldwell was “not provided a meaningful opportunity to address each of these anonymous allegations or offer readily identifiable witnesses who possessed more pertinent, first-hand knowledge of the events in question."

The 61-page report, which was [published by the New Jersey Globe,](https://newjerseyglobe.com/governor/sherrill-caldwell-report/) found that Caldwell sexually harassed a young female staffer and her friend. Caldwell was also found to have violated state ethics rules for using his office to try to promote a state employee whom he had a romantic relationship with, without disclosing the relationship.

He also violated ethics rules by making a practice of taking personal guests to ticketed events without providing payment or reimbursement for the tickets, the report said.

title: China's Transnational Repression Examined as Trump Hosts Xi Summit
summary: ## **Why It Matters** A hearing held by the East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee of the House Foreign Affairs Committee on September 16, explored China's coercion beyond its borders and the continued human rights crisis in North Korea, while
content:
## **Why It Matters**

A hearing held by the East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee of the House Foreign Affairs Committee on September 16, explored China's coercion beyond its borders and the continued human rights crisis in North Korea, while lawmakers raised concerns about Trump administration cuts to programs intended to advance human rights interests. The hearing, titled "Lives, Not Leverage: The Long Arm of China and North Korea's Repression," put a personal face on the stakes: Sylvia Zin, whose husband remains wrongfully detained in China, [made a direct plea to President Trump to secure his release](https://www.berkeleyside.org/2026/09/17/wife-of-uc-berkeley-scholar-detained-in-china-asks-trump-for-help) during the upcoming Xi Jinping summit.

The East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee convened at [on September 16](https://app.legis1.com/hearings/detail?id=31451#summary) at the just days before Trump's scheduled meeting with Xi on September 24. The timing highlighted an uncomfortable tension as lawmakers were sounding alarms about Chinese coercion tactics targeting Americans while the administration prepared to prioritize trade, Taiwan, and artificial intelligence over human rights concerns.

## **The Big Picture**

China's transnational repression has expanded beyond its borders, according to U.S. lawmakers, human rights organizations and researchers. The administration's May summit with Xi focused heavily on trade and strategic issues, while human rights advocates have pressed the administration to put China's treatment of dissidents, religious minorities and other groups on the bilateral agenda.

China also enacted a Law on the Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress in March. Human rights groups have criticized the law as part of Beijing's broader efforts to strengthen ideological and cultural assimilation and have raised concerns about its potential application to Uyghurs, Tibetans and other ethnic minority communities.

The hearing examined two intersecting issues, China's coercive tactics targeting dissidents and diaspora communities outside its borders and North Korea's human rights abuses. Lawmakers also discussed Radio Free Asia, which suspended all remaining news production in October 2025 amid a federal government shutdown and uncertainty over future U.S. funding after the Trump administration had earlier sought to cut funding for U.S.-supported international broadcasters.

Myanmar-born U.S. citizen and UC Berkeley doctoral student Min Zin was detained in Yunnan on June 3 after traveling to China for an academic conference at the invitation of the Chinese government. Chinese authorities have said he is suspected of espionage and activities endangering national security. Secretary of State Marco Rubio subsequently designated Min Zin as wrongfully detained, making his release a priority for the U.S. government. China disputes the U.S. characterization and says its judicial authorities are handling the case according to Chinese law.

## **What They're Saying**

The hearing highlighted disagreements over how the United States should respond to repression by Beijing and Pyongyang.

Deborah Choi, a human rights activist who escaped North Korea in 2004, recounted being trafficked and sexually abused after fleeing to China. Peter Mattis, president of the Jamestown Foundation, called for targeted measures including [sanctions against state-owned enterprises and disclosure of CCP leaders' foreign assets](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/north-korean-defector-recounts-trafficking-sexual-abuse-in-china-in-us-congressional-hearing/12880019). Victor Cha, president and Korea Chair of the Geopolitics and Foreign Policy Department at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, testified about China's forced repatriation of North Korean refugees and cooperation between China and North Korea that facilitates repression.

But the hearing's most personal moment came when Sylvia Zin, wife of the detained scholar, testified directly. She cited Trump's record of securing the release of wrongfully detained Americans and urged him to raise her husband's case with Xi. Zin described concerns about her husband enduring repeated interrogations, isolation and harsh detention conditions since his detention in June.

Rep. Young Kim (R-CA), the subcommittee chair, framed the hearing around expanding Chinese coercion and wrongful detention. She also cited the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri of Zion Church, who was released from Chinese custody after Trump raised his detention directly with Xi during their May meeting. Jin was released in July and reunited with his family in the United States.

Rep. Ami Bera (D-CA), the subcommittee's ranking member, raised concerns about Radio Free Asia and the administration's decision to scale back the Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercise with South Korea. Bera and other Democratic lawmakers have argued that reducing military exercises without reciprocal concessions could weaken U.S. leverage with North Korea as Trump seeks renewed leader-level talks with Kim Jong Un.

## **Political Stakes**

The hearing came as lawmakers and human rights advocates questioned the Trump administration's approach to human rights in Asia. The administration sought major reductions to U.S.-funded international broadcasting, including Radio Free Asia, and the position of special envoy for North Korean human rights issues has remained vacant since former envoy Julie Turner left the post in January 2025.

For lawmakers including Bera and Kim, who have worked on legislation addressing Uyghur human rights and Chinese harassment of diaspora communities, the hearing represented an effort to keep human rights and wrongful detention on the agenda before Xi's visit.

The Transnational Repression Policy Act was introduced in the 119th Congress to address transnational repression by foreign governments against private individuals. The Senate measure, S.2525, was introduced by Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR), with Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-AK) as an original cosponsor and Sen. Tim Kaine (D-VA) later joining as a cosponsor. An identical House measure, H.R.4829, was introduced by Rep. Christopher Smith (R-NJ).

Congress has also considered legislation that would establish a framework for designating foreign countries as state sponsors of unlawful or wrongful detention. H.R.4179 would require the State Department to brief Congress on whether several countries, including China, should receive such a designation.

Advocacy efforts have also increased ahead of Xi's Washington visit, with human rights organizations calling on Trump to raise individual detention cases and China's repression of dissidents. The Human Rights Foundation launched a Toolkit to Counter the Chinese Communist Party's Transnational Repression as a direct product of its Beyond Borders workshop. Freedom House [published a brief timed to Xi's visit](https://freedomhouse.org/article/xi-jinping-washington-dc-countering-beijings-efforts-undermine-free-speech-beyond-its) urging the administration to take countermeasures against CCP efforts to repress free expression on American soil.

## **The Other Side**

The Trump administration has emphasized strategic competition with China, including trade, technology and Indo-Pacific security. The [National Defense Strategy](https://humanrightscommission.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/humanrightscommission.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/20260428-tlhrc-hearing-koreas-jpm-opening-remarks.pdf) identifies homeland defense and the Western Hemisphere as priority areas, with deterring China in the Indo-Pacific as another central strategic priority.

China rejects U.S. allegations that Min Zin and other Americans have been wrongfully detained. Beijing has said Min Zin is suspected of activities that endangered China's national security and maintains that Chinese judicial authorities are handling his case according to law.

Some analysts have [cautioned against narrowly focusing on physical overseas police stations](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/chinas-overseas-police-stations-an-imminent-security-threat/) as the sole mechanism of Chinese transnational repression. Researchers have identified a broader range of tactics, including surveillance, online harassment, threats against family members, coercion and efforts to influence diaspora communities.

## **The Bottom Line**

The Trump-Xi summit begins September 24. [No legislative outcomes](https://www.congress.gov/119/meeting/house/119561/witnesses/HHRG-119-FA05-Wstate-ChoiD-20260916.pdf) have emerged from the hearing, and no associated legislation has been formally introduced. However, the Transnational Repression Policy Act and the proposal to designate China as a "State Sponsor of Wrongful Detention" remain vehicles for institutionalizing government responses to wrongful detention cases. Senators Kaine and Sullivan reintroduced a companion Senate bill on June 25, 2026.

Whether Trump raises Min Zin's case, or any of the wrongfully detained Americans and residents highlighted at Wednesday's hearing, will signal whether human rights have any place in his administration's China strategy.
