title: America’s AI push in Southeast Asia faces a China problem
summary: Capitol Hill is scrambling to stifle chip smuggling to China, despite industry warnings. By [Brian Dabbs](https://www.politico.com/staff/brian-dabbs) 09/24/2026 05:00 AM EDT|Updated:09/24/2026 10:51 AM EDT SINGAPORE — America’s campaign to
content:
Capitol Hill is scrambling to stifle chip smuggling to China, despite industry warnings.

By [Brian Dabbs](https://www.politico.com/staff/brian-dabbs)

09/24/2026 05:00 AM EDT|Updated:09/24/2026 10:51 AM EDT

SINGAPORE — America’s campaign to dominate the global AI market has collided with an uncomfortable reality here in Southeast Asia: The same investments that extend the reach of U.S. technology could also help China evade Washington’s controls and catch up in the AI sprint.

Every advanced chip shipped to the region and every U.S.-powered data center expands the market for American artificial intelligence. But the investments also create another potential route for Chinese companies to obtain computing power the U.S. wants to deny them.

That spiraling conflict will loom over talks as President Donald Trump meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday in Washington. Meanwhile, the issue is driving a new bipartisan push in Congress for tougher controls on chip shipments and access to U.S. data centers, despite industry warnings that further restrictions could cost American companies business and push Southeast Asian governments closer to Beijing.

The stakes are growing as U.S. tech giants pour billions of dollars into a region that is rapidly becoming a global data-center hub. Washington wants U.S. companies to supply Southeast Asia’s booming digital economies, fearing China could otherwise capture the market as it did during the global build-out of 5G telecommunications networks.

But experts say the illegal smuggling of chips to banned Chinese companies — and Chinese access to servers in Southeast Asia that use advanced chips — are undercutting U.S. export controls, even as governments across the region step up enforcement.

“The demand for smuggling is, if anything, growing,” said Chris Miller, author of “Chip War” and a professor at Tufts University’s Fletcher School. “AI chips are absolutely critical for the future of AI and therefore the future of national power.”

AI is set to play a major role in the Trump-Xi summit, with top U.S. AI leaders including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang [planning to attend](https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2026/09/ai-titans-invited-to-trump-xi-dinner-01083068?site=pro&prod=alert&prodname=alertmail&linktype=headline&source=email) a state dinner. And the Trump administration is ramping up coordination with Southeast Asian governments to stem smuggling of chips. The U.S. co-hosted a summit in Jakarta, Indonesia, last week focused on AI, semiconductors and supply chain security.

However, the White House didn’t comment on the fresh legislative push or whether chip smuggling would come up at the Trump-Xi summit but defended the United States’ export control regime as strong.

Rapid advancements in AI mean the U.S. needs to stay ahead in competition with China, according to policymakers and U.S. industry. While AI can be used to advance life-saving medical innovation and other arguably beneficial causes, its power can also be unleashed for nefarious ends, leading many experts, including [some at top U.S. AI labs](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/12/anthropic-ceo-dario-amodei-seeks-immediate-slowdown-artificial-intelligence-01073519), to spell out doomsday scenarios.

Now, lawmakers are scrambling to tighten U.S. controls and prevent China from obtaining the most sophisticated chips. [The Chip Security Act](https://legislation.politicopro.com/bill/US_119_S_1705), which would crack down on smuggling by requiring advanced chips to contain location-verification and tracking mechanisms, is likely to be included in the Senate’s defense authorization legislation that lawmakers aim to pass by the end of the year.

Sen. Tom Cotton, author of the Chip Security Act and chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said the bill would “ensure our advanced chips don’t fall into the hands of those who seek to do America harm.”

“Communist China continues to lie, cheat, and steal in order to undermine American AI innovation,” the Arkansas Republican said in a statement to POLITICO. “Recent events demonstrate the stakes for economic and national security if China were to develop frontier capabilities that match America’s.”

The bill is also supported by top Democrats.

“China has always been desperate to get our AI chips. They’ve set up elaborate ways to smuggle them,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, a co-sponsor of the Chip Security Act, [said at a press conference Wednesday](https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2026/09/schumer-presses-thune-for-vote-on-chip-export-bills-01089760). “We can and must both maintain our lead on AI by restricting China’s access to our technology.”

Vivek Chilukuri, a senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security and a former Capitol Hill staffer, said there’s “strong bipartisan consensus in Congress that we should not be allowing Chinese companies or entities to buy American chips or access American chips.”

Chilukuri said Congress has been “really important for building pressure on the administration” to address smuggling. But U.S. export controls [did not surface](https://url4763.email.politicopro.com/ls/click?upn=u001.Q6ij-2B6lCBUOmLoIECmNeyasVlxItr2fdP9GFDpe8m4oi88lXFGXei52n966MomgQ91HXgboQFHZvL8tSTtmIDo-2BGyykbIhy-2BcuC0KivFgomR1eJPVSCQv50vT7AvsGjMww3ISkhWULCVgZBMVeuU4nhOb6AtQrTjjU-2B1bVS7I0Iqw5nPq0dYMure-2BkV98eXT5X2ZolIl-2Bl1g6LZmWF-2FMX9DTTsDui-2Bq8ocVKZISgalD4zEvNWeLnVrfXsE8Ay8QsUiARO0-2FVE2TW9Yjj9pAgHqNF4gnFCMg5S-2FK2DuEXIRE-3DivcJ_PFF6-2BZ7iHtC6sYNiivjNEHeUJrOAGDIOuOfFh-2BoduvJByh4EWdI0U0vrfVt-2Bb-2FGDIJpLyZpsQ1WYpnOzuXauRDSSdMRkeT7cxlYikaGd-2FA0-2F5XT-2FLGirQeOYKSNJTCakN6rbfHx3YCnkCM9N6lAJrgRfDSdLmRYhKhAvoAAyG1dhB7SHdac6t8Gf72dI94pdgXACR7Ks2cNWlIcMlBvUVsW71DSmiJ-2Fkq3o-2FaTHhuyqw478kN3O3HJ8Euo2IT6o8qOv2kGdY-2BXNuBd1jkudGzDg6Y3L-2Fy-2BnoPZjAVzolEJxomz6JY4qAEcwifWx1AFIM5BrB8aXAob4yrykTY41SZUl5tQDhH-2Fa-2F8zXxqeWU6kyHGC2nQce1tnrJpRIdYjSJpLvY-2BeVJxpHhkCrMxw-2FjEJJ8jOSwCAFabPBcX0vtDxrkCcMgssykG0XuWKYTWaZo4LC9afgbSWOY1YG-2Fcx6AGyjeS1i287U3yDRk8DOlv23iZYHk1sCXh79X7hI-2BuI3UVdtx-2F12M5n8Qj2YdTGHYaQX0kzND8nYdldaPkeZGN948vNbWhbIEMWhaMwmM5Bv5CPD0gPFZXtcJ5LgiO90WpQ-3D-3D) in preliminary negotiations this weekend, according to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

On the Senate floor last Thursday, Schumer called for export control measures in the defense bill, saying Trump “is the biggest barrier standing in the way.”

## ‘A strategic resource’

Also known as semiconductors or integrated circuits, chips are small silicon-based devices that house advanced processors containing millions or billions of microscopic transistors. Widely regarded as some of the most advanced technology in human history, they’re used to build servers in data centers, where large language AI models like ChatGPT are trained and AI programs are deployed to businesses and the public.

Since the Cold War, the U.S. has battled to stay ahead globally in the chip business. And in 2022, the Biden administration imposed sweeping export controls on advanced chips. Even though the U.S. still restricts [advanced chip exports to China](https://www.bis.gov/media/documents/bis-guidance-may-31-2026.pdf), the Trump administration halted a last-minute Biden administration regulation, called the AI Diffusion Rule, that capped chip shipments to countries in Southeast Asia and elsewhere across the globe.

Southeast Asia is cracking down on smuggling — at least ostensibly. As part of a series of law enforcement operations over recent months, Malaysia seized [millions of dollars worth of AI chips](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-customs-seizes-ai-chips-worth-16-7-million-at-kuala-lumpur-airport). Singapore [seized a luxury villa](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2d9y18g73o) tied to smuggling. And U.S. prosecutors suspect a firm in Thailand is [linked to smuggling](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-08/us-said-to-suspect-nvidia-chips-smuggled-to-alibaba-via-thailand), according to Bloomberg.

Authorities in Taiwan are also prosecuting illegal shipments, most recently [charging a ring of people](https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202608240023) in late August that included employees of Nvidia and Supermicro. The most powerful chips are designed by California-based Nvidia and produced in Taiwan.

The operations follow a handful of high-profile U.S. Justice Department prosecutions over chip smuggling since 2025. Still, experts say the efforts are not enough to keep China at bay in the epic battle over AI supremacy.

“There’s no point where you restrict China’s access to compute enough,” said Erich Grunewald, a Berlin-based researcher at the Washington-headquartered Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, referring to the computational power needed to train and deploy AI models.

“It’s better to think of compute as a strategic resource, like oil or steel production in the past,” he said.

U.S. hyperscalers Amazon, Microsoft and Google, along with cloud provider Oracle, are expanding big in the region, while other American companies like CoreWeave seek entry. The region’s data centers are set to hit 9.4 GW by 2035, which is more power capacity than nine U.S. nuclear power plants, the consultancy Wood Mackenzie said in a [recent report](https://www.woodmac.com/press-releases/data-centre-boom-drive-structural-lng-demand-in-southeast-asia/).

Southeast Asia is attracting investment because of its rapidly-growing economies, cheap land and other resources, as well as access to undersea cables, which are laid on the ocean floor to facilitate internet traffic and are critical for the data transfers needed for AI.

High-powered chips are continuing to flood into the region. On top of U.S. hyperscaler projects, Singapore-founded Aolani will deploy 22,000 controlled Nvidia chips at sites in Malaysia and the Philippines, according to an announcement Monday. Zankore, a Singaporean firm operating in Indonesia, also announced progress [earlier this month](https://zankore.com/zankore-expands-southeast-asias-ai-compute-infrastructure-with-nvidia) in plans to build a data center and cloud service that will use controlled Nvidia chips.

China is also pushing full throttle on tech infrastructure in the region to strengthen already tight economic ties. Meanwhile, Chinese companies like Alibaba, Moonshot and [Z.ai](http://z.ai/) are producing AI models [that compete](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models) with Anthropic and OpenAI in sophistication. But Chinese firms are far behind in designing and manufacturing chips.

That, on top of the enforcement operations, is leading experts to conclude that smuggling — largely through Southeast Asia — is playing a critical role in Chinese innovation. In July, Michael Kratsios, director of the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy, said that Chinese company Moonshot [“acquired” servers](https://x.com/mkratsios47/status/2079933645888880708) equipped with high-powered, highly restricted Nvidia chips, “likely to train its AI models.”

“China is six or seven years behind the cutting edge in Taiwan, and it’s actually fallen further behind TSMC, the Taiwanese leader, over the last 24 months in terms of both the quality of chips it produces and its share of the market,” said Miller, referring to the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

The Washington-based nonprofit C4ADS released a report earlier this month identifying 50 shipments of Nvidia GPUs diverted through Vietnam, Malaysia and India to China and Hong Kong between 2023 and 2025, totaling $13.4 million.

“Some actors may avoid detection entirely, moving chips through fishing boats or other channels that bypass legal reporting mechanisms,” [the report said](https://c4ads.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Covert-Compute-C4ADS.pdf). “Others may relabel products as goods from unrelated sectors and move them through regular shipping channels.”

## 习近平访美排场十足，但迄今进展甚微

图像来源，Yuri Gripas/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images

*       *   Author, 安东尼‧泽克尔（Anthony Zurcher）
    *   Role, BBC驻北美记者

*   Published 54 分钟前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

至少到目前为止，中国国家主席习近平访问华盛顿可谓排场十足，但在迫切议题上未见多少明显进展。

从周三（9月23日）在军事基地举行的隆重欢迎仪式，到（美东时间）今天早上抵达白宫时接受仪仗队迎接，美国总统特朗普都为这位中国领导人铺上了红地毡，无论从字面还是象征意义上都是如此。

两位领导人的公开发言充满友好措辞和外交辞令。习近平在今天正式会谈前发表声明，宣布将向美国赠送中国大熊猫，并推出新的学生交流计划。

他说：“让我们秉持人民情怀、展现历史主动，不断推进中美两国人民友好事业，携手共建一个更加美好的世界”

特朗普则列出两人在会谈中计划讨论的一些议题，包括“涉及安全、科技和超级智能的迫切问题”。他所说的“超级智能”，是他惯常用来谈及人工智能的说法。

特朗普说：“我们今天在这些领域作出的决定，可以在未来数十年推动和平与繁荣。”

不过，周四的军乐队表演和军机飞越，至少对特朗普而言，可能还有更大的目的。

彭博经济研究首席地缘经济分析师珍妮弗·韦尔奇（Jennifer Welch）对BBC说：“这些有一点刻意安排的盛大场面，是为了营造峰会的正面气氛。”

“这很符合特朗普总统看待这次峰会，以及他自己在美中关系中所扮演角色的方式，也就是充当提供稳定的压舱石。”

不过，她指出，习近平的一些言论仍然带有一定的警示意味。

习近平在白宫发言时再次提到“修昔底德陷阱”。这一理论认为，全球权力格局发生变化时，崛起中的国家与相对衰落的国家之间往往容易爆发冲突。

习近平说：“中美两国国情不同，通过坦诚、深入、持续的对话能够增进理解、求同存异、积累互信。”

然而，中美两国要达成任何实质协议，仍面对重大障碍。

特朗普与习近平今年5月在北京会面时，两人同意成立贸易和投资委员会，以监督两国经济往来，但除此以外成果有限。

美国财政部长贝森特（Scott Bessent）周三表示，中美两国为期一年的贸易“休战”将再延长两个月。这项安排一直令双方的关税维持在较低水平。

金融分析师预期，由于双方都不希望去年的贸易战重演，本周峰会结束前，这项安排可能会进一步延长。

至于其他议题，包括美国与伊朗的战争、乌克兰战争和人工智能规管，取得进展的前景就黯淡得多。

中国未有履行增加购买美国农产品，以及向美国出售更多稀土矿产的承诺，也令前景更加不明朗。

与此同时，中国正观望特朗普会否落实一项拟议中的对台军售。这项出售美国武器给台湾的计划已经搁置数月。

视频加注文字，习近平访美晤特朗普：中美竞赛谁领先？美国民众怎么看

伦敦国王学院政治经济学教授罗宾·克林格勒-维德拉（Robyn Klingler-Vidra）对BBC表示，在人工智能议题上，中美两国对于任何有关这场科技竞赛的协议，都抱有非常不同的目标。

她说：“美国这边关注的是生存风险，以及是否可能要放慢人工智能发展。”

“而在中国，重点则是加快发展，或许要在人工智能科技竞赛中取胜，以及把人工智能应用到实体经济。”

多名美国主要人工智能企业高层计划出席今晚在白宫举行的正式国宴。许多人认为，美方希望藉此展示其目前在科技领域的优势。

除了展示实力之外，更多盛大的外交排场，以及维持稳定的承诺，最终或许就是习近平此次访问的主要成果，即使在他周五下午离开前，两位领导人还会有更多时间面对面交流。

特朗普第一任期内，曾担任时任国务卿蓬佩奥（Mike Pompeo）首席中国政策规划顾问及策略师的余茂春对BBC说：“中国谈的是形而上和抽象的东西，美国则希望解决具体问题。”

“这两种不同的方式不会带来任何结果。”

title: Flush with allies, Tigray's leaders face internal discord in new Ethiopia war
summary: * Summary * Experts say federal forces hold manpower and technology advantage over opponents * Postwar grievances sparked protests over hunger, displacement and unpaid compensation * TPLF alliance with other Ethiopian armed groups could bol
content:
*   Summary

*   Experts say federal forces hold manpower and technology advantage over opponents
*   Postwar grievances sparked protests over hunger, displacement and unpaid compensation
*   TPLF alliance with other Ethiopian armed groups could bolster its fight

NAIROBI, Sept 24 (Reuters) - The last time the Tigray People's Liberation Front went to war with the Ethiopian federal government in 2020, it compensated for its isolation amid a sea of enemies with internal cohesion.

As the biggest political party in northern Ethiopia's ​Tigray region [enters a new conflict](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopian-airlines-suspends-flights-tigray-region-2026-01-07/) with Addis Ababa following the outbreak of fighting on Wednesday, that dynamic has been turned on its head.

The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/daily-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fafrica%2Fflush-with-allies-tigrays-leaders-face-internal-discord-new-ethiopia-war-2026-09-24%2F)

This time, the TPLF has no shortage of ‌allies. On Sunday, it [announced an alliance](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/seven-ethiopian-armed-groups-announce-anti-government-alliance-2026-09-21/) with six other Ethiopian armed groups aimed at overthrowing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government. Regional experts also widely believe it is receiving support from neighbouring Eritrea. Asmara denies this.

On the home front, however, the TPLF’s grip over Tigrayan society has weakened significantly. Since the end of the last war in 2022, it has faced protests over dire economic conditions, increasing competition from rival parties and defections of leading members.

Overnight, armed men detained four veteran military leaders who had expressed ​doubts about the new war, including the commander-in-chief of Tigrayan forces during the last war, Tadesse Werede, a member of Tadesse's family told Reuters.

"Previously, TPLF had very large support within the region, within ​the country, as well as from outside of the country, the diaspora. And they also managed to mobilize the local people to join TDF (Tigray Defense Forces)," said ⁠Jalale Getachew Birru, East Africa regional expert for the non-profit Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project.

"But this time... we don't see all these things."

Abiy's spokesperson declined to comment. A spokesperson for the TPLF did not respond to ​a request for comment.

## 'PATRIOTS' AND 'TRAITORS'

Wednesday's developments, in which Tigrayan forces seized control of the region's main airports and attacked federal forces in two neighbouring regions as part of what they called a defensive war in response to ​federal government aggression, shattered the four-year-old peace deal that ended one of the century's deadliest civil wars.

In that conflict, TPLF faced enemies on all fronts, including the federal government, Eritrea to the north and fighters from the Amhara region to the south and Afar to the east.

The former guerrilla movement, which had dominated Ethiopian national politics for more than three decades until Abiy was appointed prime minister in 2018, was able to harness widespread animosity across Tigray towards the federal government.

That allowed it to ​weather swift early advances by federal forces and contest a grinding, two-year war, although the federal government ultimately gained the upper hand on the battlefield before the African Union-mediated Pretoria Agreement was signed in November 2022.

After the ​war, political unity in Tigray frayed. Many Tigrayans criticised the TPLF-led authorities for failing to address continuing hunger and displacement. War veterans staged public protests, demanding compensation.

And TPLF hardliners clashed with more moderate party members, leading to high-profile defections and ‌the creation of ⁠a rival armed force by former TDF generals.

Item 1 of 2 Members of the Tigrayan forces sit along a street as they patrol as tensions intensify after the forces launched a major offensive against the federal government in multiple locations, in Mekelle, Tigray Region, Ethiopia, September 24, 2026. Obtained by REUTERS

**[1/2]**Members of the Tigrayan forces sit along a street as they patrol as tensions intensify after the forces launched a major offensive against the federal government in multiple locations, in Mekelle, Tigray Region, Ethiopia, September 24, 2026. Obtained by REUTERS [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/members-of-the-tigrayan-forces-sit-along-a-street-as-they-patrol-as-tensions-intensify-after-the-forces-launched-a-major-offensive-against-the-federal-government-in-multiple-locations-in-mekelle-tigray-region/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMktQTkE5NDA3Rg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

In recent months, Tigrayan authorities have turned to forcibly recruiting young men into the defence forces, according to local and international human rights groups, opposition parties and multiple Tigray residents.

The TPLF has denied conducting forced recruitment.

As the new conflict got underway, the mood in Mekelle was very different from in 2020, three residents told Reuters.

"At the beginning of the previous war, despite political disagreements, there was a strong sense of collective mobilization around the defence of Tigray," said one of the residents.

"Today that social cohesion has been severely weakened. Tigray is politically polarized, and people are increasingly being divided into categories of 'patriots' and 'traitors.'"

## OLD FOES UNITE ​AGAINST FEDERAL GOVERNMENT

Tigray's leaders have taken heart from their ​new alliance, which includes its former foe the ⁠Amhara Fano National Movement.

Since Wednesday, they have been fighting together in Amhara, where Fano, a coalition of armed groups, has been waging an insurgency since 2023, security sources told Reuters.

The federal government has accused Eritrea, which won its independence from Ethiopia in 1993, of providing financial support to the TPLF and other armed groups - claims that ​many Ethiopia experts say they believe.

Eritrea has repeatedly denied supporting armed groups in Ethiopia.

But the alliance's real-world effectiveness remains in doubt. Its members have diffuse – and ​sometimes directly contradictory – interests. The ⁠TPLF and Fano, for example, continue to stake competing claims to land Amhara captured from Tigray during the last war.

"The only issue joining them is their opposition to (Abiy's) Prosperity Party rule," said Kjetil Tronvoll, a professor of peace and conflict studies at Oslo New University College.

The federal government, for its part, has major tactical advantages over its opponents. In the last war, its widespread deployment of foreign-made drones helped turn the tide of the conflict after the TPLF ⁠advanced into Amhara.

Since ​then, it has bolstered its stocks of drones, including by starting domestic production, while the TPLF surrendered weaponry as part of the ​Pretoria Agreement.

It faces its own challenges, however. Prolonged fighting has strained morale and resources, while frequent drone strikes have not been enough to suppress the insurgency in Amhara, analysts say.

"The TPLF look weaker than previously as their forces are depleted since the end of the last ​war," said Magnus Taylor, a Horn of Africa analyst at the International Crisis Group think tank. "However, the alliances with other opposition groups, plus support from other regional states ... could offset this to some degree."

Editing by Alex Richardson

title: Netanyahu expected to berate New York's Mamdani in 'campaign speech' at UN
summary: * Summary * Netanyahu takes Israeli election campaign to UN stage * No Trump meeting planned five weeks before Israeli vote * Growing diplomatic isolation hangs over UN visit UNITED NATIONS, Sept 24 (Reuters) - Benjamin Netanyahu is expecte
content:
*   Summary

*   Netanyahu takes Israeli election campaign to UN stage
*   No Trump meeting planned five weeks before Israeli vote
*   Growing diplomatic isolation hangs over UN visit

UNITED NATIONS, Sept 24 (Reuters) - Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to use his UN address on Thursday to berate New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani for calling him a war criminal, a [feud](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/netanyahu-says-will-tell-truth-israels-actions-united-nations-2026-09-22/) that highlights the Israeli leader's growing isolation ahead of ​elections at home that [he may lose](https://www.reuters.com/graphics/ISRAEL-ELECTION/POLLS/lgvdbwrakvo/).

Addressing the mayor directly in a video statement this week, Netanyahu said he was going to New York "to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers" and "to tell ‌the truth about you." He falsely accused Mamdani of supporting Hamas militants.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Fnetanyahu-expected-berate-new-yorks-mamdani-campaign-speech-un-address-2026-09-24%2F)

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

Mamdani campaigned for office on a promise to have Netanyahu arrested for alleged war crimes should he visit the largest US city but later said he [determined](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/why-new-yorks-mamdani-cannot-have-israels-netanyahu-arrested-2026-07-22/) he lacked the legal authority to do so. This week, Mamdani described Netanyahu as "the architect of a horrific genocide against Palestinians."

Netanyahu, who rejects war crimes allegations, will be making his first visit to New York since Mamdani took office in January. Israelis opposed to Netanyahu's right-wing government are planning to protest in New York.

Ahead ​of his speech, Netanyahu's government paid to place 500 pro-Israel and anti-Iran billboards and dozens of trucks carrying messages in support of Israel across Manhattan, Netanyahu's office said in a statement.

"Freedom doesn't defend itself. ​America and Israel stand together against terror," one of the billboards states. Under it appears the subtext: "Paid for by the State of Israel".

Anti-Israel protesters took to the New ⁠York City streets.

Several hundred anti-Israel protesters gathered near the United Nations, with dozens blocking traffic and chanting: "Stop arming Israel, let Gaza live" and "Stop arming Israel, let Iran live." Police detained them.

## NETANYAHU ADDRESS TO RESEMBLE 'CAMPAIGN SPEECH'

Israel holds a general ​election in five weeks that opinion polls suggest could end Netanyahu's long hold on power.

The campaign is unfolding amid mounting criticism of Israel's Gaza war and without a planned meeting with US President Donald Trump.

"He's not really speaking to the ​UN, he's speaking to the Israeli public," said former Israeli Ambassador Michael Oren, who expects Netanyahu's address to resemble a "campaign speech."

"Maybe he's thinking, 'If I can attack Mamdani and attack the Iranians, somebody who was wavering between voting for me and voting for (Gadi) Eisenkot may decide to vote for me,'" Oren said, referring to former military chief Eisenkot, Netanyahu's leading rival.

On Thursday morning, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN General Assembly – via video after the US [denied](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-allows-palestinian-president-again-speak-via-video-after-us-denies-visa-2026-09-17/) him a visa for the second year in a row – and [reaffirmed](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/abbas-pledges-first-palestinian-parliamentary-vote-20-years-doubts-mount-2026-09-24/) plans ​to hold legislative elections on November 28, the first such vote in 20 years, despite serious domestic doubts it will go ahead, as he seeks to advance internationally backed reforms.

## NETANYAHU NOT EXPECTED TO MEET TRUMP

Netanyahu is making ​an unusually short visit to the US for his UN address. He arrived in New York around 9 a.m. ET (1300 GMT) and is expected to fly back the same day after delivering his speech in the afternoon.

The Israeli leader is to meet ‌with the presidents ⁠of Argentina, Bolivia, Ethiopia, Panama and Paraguay and the vice president of Colombia, and with the prime ministers of Greece, Papua New Guinea and Slovenia, Netanyahu's office said. His office did not say if meetings were planned with US officials.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, two Israeli officials earlier said Netanyahu's team was discussing potentially holding meetings with senior US officials including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, though nothing had been set.

Netanyahu is not expected to meet Trump. The two men jointly launched a war on Iran on February 28, but they found themselves on a [collision course](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/netanyahu-trump-collision-course-us-iran-agree-halt-war-2026-06-15/) after the US and Iran agreed to an interim ceasefire that Netanyahu opposed.

Many Israelis were angered by that deal, and opinion polls ​showed they questioned Trump's commitment to Israeli security, even as ​his administration proceeds with billions of dollars in ⁠arms sales to Israel's government.

"A lack of any encounter with the president, a month before an Israeli election, will indicate that Trump is keeping a distance from him and will be negative for Netanyahu's campaign," said Nimrod Goren, president of Mitvim, an Israeli think tank focused on the country's foreign policy.

The election is scheduled for October 27.

## ISRAEL ​CONFRONTS INTERNATIONAL CRITICISM

Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Netanyahu has in the past made a visual spectacle of his UN appearances, using charts, diagrams and props to warn of ​Iran's nuclear program, which Tehran says ⁠is for civilian purposes.

Last year several delegations walked out as Netanyahu approached the lectern while supporters in the gallery cheered.

Goren said Netanyahu's speech would likely follow a familiar script: defending Israel, confronting its critics and warning about Iran while arguing that Israel's opposition to Tehran serves the interests of the wider international community.

He will also likely tout what he sees as his own achievements and close ties to Trump and the US, Goren said.

Israel has faced deepening diplomatic isolation since launching its ⁠war in Gaza ​in response to the Hamas-led attacks on Israel nearly three years ago.

Netanyahu is unable to travel to many countries because of an International ​Criminal Court arrest warrant, issued against him and his former defense minister as well as the then-military commander of Hamas in 2024.

Earlier this month, once-steadfast allies Britain, France and Canada announced [sanctions](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-sanctions-networks-enabling-settler-violence-west-bank-2026-06-09/) targeting Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which drew a muted response from Washington.

Updates with New York protests and Abbas remarks paragraphs 7-8 and 13

Reporting by Antoni Slodkowski at the United Nations and Maria Tsvetkova in New York; Additional reporting by Alexander Cornwell and Emily Rose in Tel Aviv; Editing by Rami Ayyub and Howard Goller

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Antoni Slodkowski is Reuters Chief Politics & General News Correspondent for China, based in Beijing, where he leads coverage of Chinese politics, society, and its relations with global counterparts. He has won two Pulitzer Prizes with Reuters colleagues: in Investigative Reporting in 2025 for uncovering fentanyl supply chains, and in International Reporting in 2019 for exposing the persecution of Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar. Previously Japan Deputy Bureau Chief and Myanmar Bureau Chief at Reuters, Antoni also reported from Tokyo for the Financial Times and was a Knight-Wallace Fellow at the University of Michigan. He began his journalism career as a teenager, hosting a children's TV show for Poland's largest public broadcaster.

Maria Tsvetkova is an investigative journalist originally from Moscow who focuses on Russia’s invasion of Ukraine as part of an international team of reporters. She has reported from the conflict zones in Ukraine and Nagorno-Karabakh, as well as doing reporting stints in Armenia, Turkey and Iraq.

title: 关于人工智能安全，中国真正在乎的是什么
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 如果要说谁 代表了中国人工智能的前沿，那就是[唐杰](https://keg.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn/jietang/)。 这位文质彬彬的数据工程师是中国顶尖人工智能实验室智谱AI(Z.ai)的联合创始人、首席科学家兼最大个人股东。智谱AI旗下模型的性能已[跃升](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/glm-5-3/)至中国第一梯队，也让唐杰成为了中国人工智能生态系统的领军人物。 在某种程度上，唐杰关于人工智能的表态似乎与达
content:
如果要说谁 代表了中国人工智能的前沿，那就是[唐杰](https://keg.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn/jietang/)。

这位文质彬彬的数据工程师是中国顶尖人工智能实验室智谱AI(Z.ai)的联合创始人、首席科学家兼最大个人股东。智谱AI旗下模型的性能已[跃升](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/glm-5-3/)至中国第一梯队，也让唐杰成为了中国人工智能生态系统的领军人物。

在某种程度上，唐杰关于人工智能的表态似乎与达里奥·阿莫迪遥相呼应。阿莫迪是Claude背后的美国公司Anthropic的联合创始人兼首席执行官，也是行业内既赞美人工智能前景又警告其风险的代表性人物。唐杰将一种近乎乌托邦式的热情与他所称的“极致安全治理”这一“最重的责任”结合在了一起。

“当一项技术抵达足以改变文明进程的力量量级时，安全就不再是附属品，而是技术得以存续与被允许应用的根本前提，”唐杰在7月曝光的一封[致员工的信](https://finance.sina.com.cn/wm/2026-07-12/doc-inihqetv4464441.shtml)中这样写道。

这些话听起来或许与美国顶尖人工智能实验室发出的预警惊人地相似。但若结合中国国家主席习近平的语境来理解，其含义会更加清晰——对习近平而言，人工智能“安全”归根结底指向一个核心关切：中国共产党政权的安全。

西方[多国政府](https://www.government.nl/documents/2026/09/22/a-call-for-control-of-frontier-ai-models)将辩论焦点放在人工智能对社会构成的危险上，中国最关切的则是其对国家政权构成的威胁。中国模型因过滤或规避政治敏感信息以契合国家审查制度而广为人知。但像唐杰这样的开发者正走得更远，他们致力于将执政党意识形态深刻植入模型底层，这对中国人工智能系统所携带的价值观及其潜在脆弱性具有深远影响。

认清对这项将塑造下个世纪的关键技术的理念分歧对于设定特朗普与习近平周四在白宫会谈的预期至关重要。两国领导人准备讨论如何规避人工智能风险。然而，要达成实质性合作将极其困难，甚至难以实现，因为太平洋两岸对于“人工智能安全”的理解完全是两套互不相干的语境。

这背后的影响可能是巨大的。唐杰和他的同事正向模型注入特定价值观，从而塑造模型理解世界与做出回应的方式。随着中国人工智能系统在全球范围内得到越来越广泛的应用，这些价值观也可能随之传播，悄然将执政党的世界观带到远超中国本土的地方。

**在唐杰发表致智谱员工信六天后**，习近平于7月17日在上海出席年度世界人工智能大会时，展现了他的思考方向。在 由 官方媒体[翻译成英文](https://au.china-mission.gov.cn/eng/zgyw_3/202607/t20260717_11984910.htm)的表述中，习近平表示“China lays great emphasis on safety and security in A.I.”（中国高度重视人工智能的安全和保障），并致力于确保其“safe, secure and controllable”（安全、稳固和可控）。在与特朗普预定的会谈前夕，这似乎释放出了一个令人放心的信号。

然而，中国官方媒体在翻译领导人讲话时，往往会面向外国受众软化其政治含义。习近平中文讲话的原话是：中国坚持“发展和安全”并重，确保“人工智能安全、可靠、可控”。

这在翻译上或许看似只是微小的差别。但在习近平的语汇体系中，“安全”与“控制”等词汇归根结底指的是执政党的政治安全。他多次明确强调，确保中国的社会主义制度在快速变化的世界中稳固长久是他施政的核心议题。

如今的硅谷先行者成长于自由民主社会，从小接触的科幻作品多描绘人类怀着建设乌托邦的本意，却创造了 可能最终毁灭人类的机器。在今年1月发表的关于人工智能风险的文章[《技术的青春期》](https://darioamodei.com/essay/the-adolescence-of-technology)中，阿莫迪开篇引用了他最喜欢的电影之一《超时空接触》(Contact)的场景：由朱迪·福斯特饰演的女主角被问及，她想对来自外太空并建立起无线电联系的高级智慧生命说些什么。

她回答道：“你们是怎么做到的？你们是如何演化的？你们是如何度过这个技术青春期而没有毁灭自己的？”

该文详细阐述了如何管理阿莫迪参与构建的技术所固有的灾难性风险，其中包括将安全原则融入人工智能，使其与模型本身密不可分。这种被称为“宪制人工智能”(constitutional A.I.)的方法，试图在性格、价值观和品格层面教授这项技术何为“合格的人工智能”——“就像一个正在形成自身认同的孩子，”阿莫迪写道。

Anthropic注入其模型中的价值观借鉴了《世界人权宣言》，高度侧重于信息获取、法治、政治自由、自决权和个人自由。

无独有偶，Google DeepMind联合创始人兼主席德米斯·哈萨比斯也制定了一套明确锚定于自由民主价值观的人工智能原则，并[主张](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/responsible-ai-2024-report-ongoing-work/)民主国家应当在“自由、平等和尊重人权等核心价值观的指引下”引领人工智能的发展。

中国的新一代科技领袖则成长于截然不同的环境——在一个威权体系中，自由主义价值观被标记为对华敌对，技术的开发与管控完全服务于执政党的利益。

习近平任命的国家安全部部长陈一新在本月发表的一篇关于人工智能风险的[文章](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/jsc97cKVYOcHuI_WisvOxw "Link: https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/jsc97cKVYOcHuI_WisvOxw")中清晰阐明了这一点。陈一新完全没有提及困扰美国人工智能领军人物的生存威胁，即人工智能失控反噬人类的恐惧。相反，他强调中国必须加强防御敌对势力，防止其利用这一强大工具“直接威胁我政治安全、制度安全、意识形态安全”。

在陈一新的论述中，人工智能的安全在于大力推进中国人工智能的发展，以防落后于美国，他暗示这种落后才是该技术对中国构成的最大危险。中国[不断完善的人工智能监管体系](https://www.cac.gov.cn/rootimages/uploadimg/1791137114683961/1791137114683961.pdf)也将对社会主义价值观、国家权力和政治稳定的威胁列为政府的核心安全关切。

**外界对极少公开发言的唐杰个人信息知之甚少。**他联合北京名校清华大学的知识工程实验室其他成员共同创立了智谱AI。该团队曾开发出用于分析社交网络和信息流的[先进工具](https://keg.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn/jietang/publications/ICDM07-Tang-et-al-Academic-Network-Extraction.pdf)，包括用于对国内外研究人员进行画像、定位及绘制关系图谱的系统，它们被定位为人才招聘工具。

唐杰在 7月的一封信中，拒绝了对人工智能采取“外挂式”安全补丁的做法，而是主张必须将行为准则植入公司模型的底层架构中，包括将国家法律、战略与安全关切——换言之，即执政党的政治利益——写入人工智能的基础基因。8月，唐杰更进一步，发表了一篇[评论文章](https://epaper.gmw.cn/gmrb/html/content/202608/10/content_21750.html)，主张通过立法对中国人工智能产业强制实施意识形态的一致性。

上个月，他的公司[发布](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-zai-says-new-model-nears-anthropics-mythos-5-cyber-defence-tests-2026-08-14/)了中国最强大的AI模型之一GLM-5.3。智谱AI将其定位为一款廉价、易获取且功能强大的开源权重网络防御工具，其性能已接近Anthropic强大的网络安全模型Mythos 5。用户可以下载并修改开源权重模型，针对特定任务进行微调，尽管其中深度嵌入的行为可能难以彻底清除。智谱AI主张将这类先进工具向全球开发者和网络安全团队开放，这一路线与Anthropic和OpenAI严格保密的闭源专有模型形成了鲜明对比。

尽管唐杰高调宣传开放，智谱AI在模型训练和评估方式方面却几乎没有透明度。此外，中国公民、企业及其他实体均须遵守《国家情报法》，该法规定他们有义务在接到要求时配合国家情报工作。智谱AI的[财务报告](https://cdn.financialreports.eu/financialreports/media/filings/50642/2026/RNS/50642_rns_2026-08-31_dccaa9af-2a08-44d5-84e0-53f7f75c190d.pdf)显示，其模型发现的安全漏洞会提交给中国当局，包括收集和分析网络安全缺陷信息的国家安全漏洞数据库。而该数据库正是由陈一新主管的国家安全部负责管理。

这引发了一个令人不安的疑问，尤其是在中国开放式模型在海外广泛应用的背景下：如果智谱AI发现一个危险的安全漏洞，究竟谁会首先获知——是需要修复该漏洞的公司，还是中国政府？

美国顶尖人工智能实验室的研究人员，以及[美国](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-2e2025.pdf)与[盟友国家](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/research/poisoning-attacks-on-llms-require-a-near-constant-number-of-poison-samples)的政府机构，已经对“[潜伏特工](https://www.anthropic.com/research/sleeper-agents-training-deceptive-llms-that-persist-through-safety-training)”(sleeper agents)带来的潜在威胁表达日益强烈的担忧。这类恶意隐藏指令可以预先植入人工智能模型中，保持潜伏状态，直至被特定条件触发，极难被检测或清除。而随着具有更高自主权限、可直接访问计算机系统的“智能体式”人工智能的发展，这种危险被进一步放大。

所有这一切都凸显出美中两国在人工智能领域寻求共识的紧迫性——但同时也说明了为什么达成共识将极其困难。

中共执着于在与美国的竞争中取得优势，并将政权安全置于首位，这令双方几乎没有就人工智能的灾难性风险达成共识的空间。而特朗普似乎也认为，战略竞争的重要性超过了不受约束的人工智能发展所带来的危险，他最近在公开讲话中和社交媒体上均对监管的必要性持否定态度。

特朗普这种自由市场的态度忽视了正在形成的更大博弈。围绕人工智能的竞赛已不仅仅关乎技术领先地位，更是双方关于自由、安全以及国家角色等理念的角逐。胜出的理念将被融入日益深刻地塑造社会思维方式、决策过程和权力运作方式的强大系统之中。

# 特朗普为何亲赴机场，超规格接待习近平？

图像来源，Reuters

Published 2026年9月24日上午10点12分

最近更新： 2 小时前

阅读时间: 3 分钟

中国国家主席习近平在美东时间9月23日傍晚抵达华盛顿，展开国事访问。美国总统特朗普亲赴机场迎接，是相隔超过60年来，再次有美国总统亲自迎接除教宗外的他国元首到访。

这也是习近平时隔11年再度对美国进行国事访问，上一次国事访问，还是在奥巴马总统任内。不仅是时间尺度上的难得，特朗普给出的超规格礼遇，也引发外界关注。

有学者向BBC中文分析，特朗普的举动既是向中方“做生意打交道”的姿态，也是在向美国民众展示自己处理大国关系的能力。

在中美围绕稀土、人工智能等议题角力加剧的背景下，这次访问被视为两国关系的重要风向标。接待规格、谈判筹码与双方盘算，成为分析焦点。

## 反映双方“位阶”或已出现变化

美国德州山姆休士顿州立大学政治系副教授翁履中向BBC中文指出，在国际政治上，外交互动所释放的讯号十分重要。

他分析，特朗普打破60年来的惯例，高规格接待习近平，是向全世界宣布“美国现在看待中国跟其他的国家都不一样，而且觉得中国是必须要非常非常尊重”。

他指出，在过去中美竞争之下，外界普遍认为美国综合国力“比较强势、占上风”，但如今特朗普亲自接机，反映双方“位阶”或已出现变化，“现在的中国手上确实握有一些筹码，是美国必须要取得的”。

当中，稀土与人工智能问题尤其关键。他认为美国感到压力，希望能与中国“好好坐下来谈、友善地谈”。

香港大学哲学系助理教授、当代中国与世界研究中心研究员黄裕舜也分析，美国目前最迫切的问题，是在关键战略资源出口、供应链角色等贸易议题上，与中国取得共识。

## 商人性格：亲自接机的个人盘算

黄裕舜强调，特朗普是“一个生意人”。从生意角度来看，以高规格接待是在给贸易伙伴“优待和厚待”，本质上也是在“做生意打交道”。

从个人层面而言，黄裕舜指出，特朗普十分欣赏习近平的手腕，“特朗普还蛮用心希望能够跟北京，尤其是习近平搞好关系”。

翁履中也认为，这种做法与特朗普的商人背景有关。

“他是非常交易导向和目标导向的，”翁履中分析，作为传统政治人物，要打破60多年的惯例，必然受到建制派或政治文化历史的制肘，但特朗普不同，“简单的示弱，如果可以换来真正的交易，特朗普会觉得这非常划算”。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，美东时间9月23日傍晚，习近平抵达美国展开国事访问，获特朗普亲赴机场迎接。

## 试图展示大国关系处理能力

今年5月特朗普访华时，在机场迎接他的是中国国家副主席、前中共中央政治局常委韩正。现场有仪仗队、军乐队，还有约300名中国青年挥舞中美两国国旗，高喊“欢迎！欢迎！热烈欢迎！”。

这一次，特朗普超过了中方给予的礼遇，不仅有仪仗队、礼砲和飞行表演，而且还和第一夫人一起赴机场迎接。

不过在美国国内，这种接待规格引发共和党反弹。

共和党参议员罗杰·威克（Roger Wicker）指出，美国与习近平及中国共产党之间存在“种种令人忧虑的问题”，批评特朗普根本不应邀请习近平到访。

共和党策略师布雷特·马森（Barrett Marson）接受美国政治媒体Politico访问时则表示，习近平此行是“特朗普的讯息与共和党立场并不一致的又一例证”。

不过翁履中分析，特朗普的做法除了向中方示好，其实也是在向国内民众展示自己处理大国关系的能力，“他做到的事情，是拜登做不到、也是之前的美国总统都做不到的”。

“（特朗普想展示）只有他能够同时处理中国，也可以处理俄罗斯的普京，甚至是可以在中国的协助之下再跟金正恩见面。”

## 中方怎么看：接机本身已可宣称“胜利”

根据新华社报导，习近平抵达美国后发表书面声明，表示“两国应该成为伙伴而不是对手”，并相信访问将“取得丰硕成果，为两国人民增进福祉，为世界和平增添希望”。

“对中国来说，光是接机已经可以宣称‘胜利’了，”翁履中分析，特朗普打破惯例的做法，已能让中方宣称“习近平带领的中国，让美国必须尊敬”。

澳洲前总理、亚洲协会全球总裁陆克文（Kevin Rudd）在回覆BBC中文的邮件中表示，对中国高层官员而言，这次访问的头号优先事项，是避免在美国首都停留期间出现任何个人尴尬，更不用说羞辱，哪怕是最轻微的礼仪失误，也要力求所有成果都经过安排、尽可能四平八稳。

陆克文认为，对习近平的国内观众来说，能在白宫受到恰如其分的礼遇且全程不出意外，就代表“任务完成”。这对中国共产党向国内和世界传递的信息同样重要，那就是中国如今被视为与美国平起平坐。他形容，“访问本身就是信息”，与访问可能产生的实质成果是两回事。

在习近平下机之际，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）宣布，中美贸易战的休战期将延长至明年1月。翁履中形容，这个开局“是一个好的结果”，但休战只是大方向，细节仍有待双方“慢慢来谈”。

黄裕舜则认为，美方的举动反映其对会面的重视，但中方体制对美方早已没有“抱有任何幻想”，中美关系不会因为特朗普的客气或尊重就“长期往好方面走”。

不过他同时指出，就短中期而言，“特朗普的急功近利”或能促成一段战略休息期，对缓和双边关系、让两国经济复苏与稳定，有一定帮助。

title: US Democrats tee up pre-election war powers vote as some Republicans break with Trump on Iran
summary: Flags are held by Iranian Americans and supporters of the National Council of Resistance of Iran during a march near the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., U.S., May 16, 2026. REUTERS/Ken Cedeno/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens n
content:
Flags are held by Iranian Americans and supporters of the National Council of Resistance of Iran during a march near the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., U.S., May 16, 2026. REUTERS/Ken Cedeno/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/demonstrators-rally-in-support-of-iran-in-washington-dc/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkZBTEFLWTA4Nw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Aides say vote as soon as Thursday, six weeks before midterms
*   Democrats see votes as way to push Republicans on unpopular war
*   Republicans in tight races breaking from Trump on Iran
*   Polls show war deeply unpopular as ​fuel prices rise

WASHINGTON, Sept 24 (Reuters) - The US Senate could vote as soon as ‌Thursday to tell President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran or get Congress' authorization to continue it, as Democrats tee up a vote on the unpopular conflict before November's midterm elections.

With polls showing Trump's Republicans struggling to keep their slim congressional ​majorities on November 3, more of them have been edging away from the war, which has [pushed ​up fuel prices.](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/global-diesel-prices-hit-record-highs-further-rises-possible-2026-09-21/) Democrats are pushing for a vote to put Republicans on the ⁠record. Only 34% of respondents in a [Reuters/Ipsos poll this week](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-approval-falls-career-low-32-high-costs-bite-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-09-21/) said they approved of the strikes on ​Iran.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fus%2Fus-democrats-tee-up-pre-election-war-powers-vote-some-republicans-break-with-2026-09-24%2F)

Senate leaders had said they expected a nonbinding vote on a war-powers resolution before leaving Washington this week or next ​to return to their districts to campaign. Senate aides said it could take place as soon as Thursday.

The Senate has voted on [Iran war powers resolutions](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-house-votes-curb-trumps-iran-war-powers-senate-backs-president-2026-07-23/) 13 times -- two times in favor -- since US and Israeli forces began bombing Iran on February ​28. The House has held six votes, with three in favor of ending the conflict.

They have been ​largely symbolic. Only one has passed both the House and Senate, and the White House has ignored the result.

## SHIFTS IN TIGHT RACES

Two Republican ‌Senate candidates [called ⁠on Monday](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/two-republican-senate-candidates-call-swift-end-iran-war-diverging-trump-2026-09-21/) for a swift end to the war in Iran, the latest sign that vulnerable candidates are trying to put some distance between themselves and Trump.

Both Mike Rogers in Michigan and Ashley Hinson in Iowa had previously backed Trump's authority to strike Tehran.

In the House of Representatives, seven Republicans voted with Democrats to pass ​a war powers resolution last ​week. Three of the ⁠seven -- Zach Nunn and Marjorie Miller-Meeks of Iowa and Nancy Mace of South Carolina -- voted against party leaders on the issue for the first time.

Nunn and ​Miller-Meeks face competitive re-election races in November, when all 435 House seats and 35 of 100 ​Senate seats are ⁠up for grabs. Mace is not seeking re-election after a failed campaign for South Carolina's governor.

Representative Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the House's Democratic leader, accused Republicans on Wednesday of not being serious about ending the war as he noted a recent ⁠shift ​in attitudes.

"It's interesting to me that several of them who are ​in tight races and on the verge of losing, including in places like Iowa or Michigan or Wisconsin, are all now starting ​to say the war needs to end," he said.

Reporting by Patricia Zengerle; editing by Andy Sullivan and David Gregorio
