title: 中美AI竞赛：美国在哪些领域领先、哪些领域落后？
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 特朗普总统将在周三晚间起迎接中国国家主席习近平进行国事访问，届时将有很多问题需要讨论，包括伊朗战争、台湾和关税问题。 但在最近几周，没有任何话题比双方能否[就人工智能的发展速度达成共识](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260923/us-china-ai-competition/)更令全球关注。关于人工智能风险快速变化的辩论已彻底席卷硅谷和华盛顿，近日波及联合国，以至于一些观察家将此次美中峰会比作核军备竞赛期间的冷战一对一会谈。 尽管有人
content:
特朗普总统将在周三晚间起迎接中国国家主席习近平进行国事访问，届时将有很多问题需要讨论，包括伊朗战争、台湾和关税问题。

但在最近几周，没有任何话题比双方能否[就人工智能的发展速度达成共识](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260923/us-china-ai-competition/)更令全球关注。关于人工智能风险快速变化的辩论已彻底席卷硅谷和华盛顿，近日波及联合国，以至于一些观察家将此次美中峰会比作核军备竞赛期间的冷战一对一会谈。

尽管有人认为本周的博弈[事关文明存亡](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/10/science/ai-humanity-risk.html)，但人们对达成任何实质性协议的期望依然很低。外交政策分析人士表示，两国正陷入人工智能竞赛，双方都认为这场竞赛将决定谁能在军事、技术和经济上占据上风，而且双方的相互猜疑根深蒂固。

西方专家普遍估计，在人工智能竞赛中，就领先模型而言，美国[领先中国约六个月左右](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260626/zai-china-artificial-intelligence-models/)。但这个数字掩盖了两国之间复杂的关系，进一步增加了就应对人工智能安全风险达成共识的难度。

以下是美国在人工智能领域相对于中国的优势所在，以及落后于其头号地缘政治对手的领域。

历届美国政府都实施了出口管制措施，限制了中国获得高性能芯片的渠道，其中包括英伟达生产的芯片。Max A. Cherney/Reuters

**获取顶级计算机芯片至关重要。**

相对于中国，美国有一个不可否认的优势：计算机芯片。[用于构建和运行人工智能技术的大多数专用芯片](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/03/16/technology/ai-data-centers.html)都是由美国公司设计的，其中包括现在全球市值最高的公司——硅谷芯片制造商英伟达。

“制造出最快芯片的人在这里，”[硅谷芯片制造商Cerebras](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/17/technology/cerebras-public-offering-ai.html)的首席执行官安德鲁·费尔德曼说。“他们不在中国。”

过去十年里，三届美国政府都[实施了出口管制](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20250613/washington-china-export-controls-tech-huawei/)，限制中国获取强大的芯片。尽管中国努力规避这些管制，但中国的人工智能研究人员经常表示，芯片短缺是他们面临的最大障碍。

中国领先企业已经花费数亿美元来[获取所需芯片](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260728/china-ai-alibaba-bytedance/)。为了绕过美国的出口管制，他们经常购买对中国境外数据中心的远程访问权限。过去一年里，这使得中国[缩小了其系统与美国领先技术之间的性能差距](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260626/zai-china-artificial-intelligence-models/)。

与此同时，中国正在努力建立自己的芯片制造产业。但引领这一努力的电信和电子公司华为也承认，距离生产出性能可与英伟达当前产品媲美的芯片[仍需数年时间](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260225/china-chips-nvidia-huawei/)。

中国人工智能公司表示，他们已经在使用华为的芯片，但这些芯片不太可能为构建尖端技术提供太多帮助。性能较弱的芯片通常用于通过互联网向用户提供技术服务。

即使有华为的帮助，像月之暗面这样的中国人工智能公司仍难以[找到满足需求的额外芯片](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260225/china-chips-nvidia-huawei/)。

**美国人对人工智能日益感到反感，中国在政治上面临的阻力较小。**

美国的民意调查显示，人工智能在过去一年里变得越来越不受欢迎——以至于它现在已成为中期选举的一个关键议题。许多美国人担心人工智能会威胁他们的工作、破坏教育，而最近更担心它会对人类构成威胁。[皮尤研究中心本周的一项民调](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/09/22/americans-views-of-data-centers-have-turned-more-negative/)发现，60%的美国人对新建本地数据中心感到不安。

尽管特朗普将放缓人工智能发展的呼吁斥为“骗局”，但在有关失控的人工智能智能体黑客入侵其他公司的事件曝光后，越来越多的共和党及民主党议员、州长以及[2028年总统大选的有望参选者](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/21/us/politics/2028-presidential-race-artificial-intelligence.html)，正争先恐后地提出各种提案，试图对这项技术进行监管。

由于中国实行集中式管理体制，因此无需面对是否以及如何限制人工智能的激烈公众辩论。而且，尽管中国的民意调查可能值得怀疑，但各项调查始终显示，公众对采用人工智能的态度更为积极。

中国公民似乎普遍[对人工智能要乐观得多](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260305/china-ai-enthusiasm/)——事实上，根据毕马威去年对47个国家进行的一项[调查](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/xx/pdf/2025/05/trust-attitudes-and-use-of-ai-global-report.pdf)，他们是全世界对该技术抱有最大希望的人群之一。约69%的中国人表示，这项技术的好处大于风险，相比之下，持相同观点的美国人仅占35%。这项技术也更多地融入了日常生活，包括酒店和餐厅的服务机器人，以及医院的医疗聊天机器人。

**到目前为止，美国经济在面对人工智能领域的巨额投资时表现出了更强的韧性。**

美国的另一个优势是，在人工智能热潮期间，其经济更具韧性。股票指数接近历史高点，对人工智能泡沫的担忧迄今也未成为现实。尽管这项技术正在美国企业界广泛普及，但由此引发的失业担忧尚未在经济数据中真正显现。

有一些迹象表明，人工智能正在导致受其影响最大的行业的[工资增长放缓](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/16/business/ai-raises-hiring.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/16/business/ai-raises-hiring.html")，职位空缺减少，尤其对年轻求职者而言更是如此。此外，由于人工智能被用于撰写简历或筛选申请人，求职过程变得更加艰难，尤其是对初级职位的求职者而言。但总体而言，与人工智能直接相关的经济困境远小于许多经济学家的预测。

在中国，[情况则有所不同](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260921/china-ai-economy/)。其经济困境——包括青年高失业率、消费者削减开支和通货紧缩螺旋——有可能削弱北京在人工智能领域的巨额投资。中国经济学家最近发出警告称，经济本就脆弱，且可能因为以人工智能为中心的财政支出配置而变得更加岌岌可危。

周二，在北京举办的面向信息技术行业的展会中国国际信息通信展上，一款机器人成为焦点。Kevin Frayer/Getty Images

**美中两国人工智能模型的性质截然不同。**

在美国， OpenAI和Anthropic等领先人工智能公司对其技术的使用方式实施严格管控。它们建立了周密的防护机制，希望防止用户[传播虚假信息](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/08/16/technology/openai-chatgpt-iran-misinformation.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2024/08/16/technology/openai-chatgpt-iran-misinformation.html")或[入侵计算机网络](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/technology/anthropic-claude-mythos.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/technology/anthropic-claude-mythos.html")。

随着对人工智能风险担忧的加剧，这些公司呼吁制定联邦法规，以强化这种做法。他们表示，政府应在人工智能技术发布前进行审查查，以确保适当的防护措施到位——许多政策制定者、立法者和专家对此表示同意。

但中国领先的公司采取不同的立场。像深度求索、月之暗面和智谱AI这样的公司通常将其最强大的技术“开源”，这意味着任何人都可以自由地根据需要使用和修改这些系统。

几十年来，开源一直推动着计算机软件、互联网和人工智能的发展。其理念是，当计算机代码可供任何人自由查阅、使用和改进时，技术进步会更快。

通过开源其技术，中国企业实际上可以整合其资源，加速研发进程。而且，如果美国监管机构扼杀美国开源项目的进展——正如一些立法者建议的那样——中国可能会获得重大优势。

许多专家认为，如果最好的开源系统来自中国，全球各地的开发者将基于中国技术进行开发。这种情况已经开始发生，[甚至在硅谷也是如此](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20260626/zai-china-artificial-intelligence-models/)。

“这些模型在细节上仍显粗糙，但在某些任务上，它们与领先的美国系统不相上下，”硅谷初创公司alphaXiv的联合创始人雷汉·艾哈迈德说，他在过去几个月里一直在使用最新的中国技术。

任何人都可以将这些开源技术用于恶意目的，其中最引人注目的是网络攻击。但安全专家表示，另一种现象抵消了这一风险：任何人都可以使用相同的技术来[防御恶意攻击](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/technology/anthropic-claude-mythos.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/technology/anthropic-claude-mythos.html")。

**中国在电力领域可能取得领先。**

一些人认为，如果中国能建立起一个可行的芯片产业，它可能会超越美国，因为它在另一个领域发展了优势：电力。

成千上万的领先芯片密集部署在巨型数据中心内，消耗着巨大的电能。它们需要的电力如此之多，以至于美国大公司无法从现有的电网中获得所需的一切。它们日益转向风能或核能，甚至在数据中心旁边安装燃气轮机。

“从根本上说，科技行业正试图将电力转化为智能，”Cerebras首席执行官费尔德曼说。“这就像一台苏斯博士笔下的机器。一边输入芯片和电力，另一边输出智能。”

费尔德曼表示，尽管美国在芯片方面拥有显著优势，但他认为中国有可能后来居上，因为它花了数年时间重建电网。“这将是一笔巨大的资产，”他说。“我们的电网还是20世纪50年代的技术。”

**中国在培养人工智能人才方面处于领先地位。**

早在2024年，[研究就表明](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20240322/in-one-key-ai-metric-china-pulls-ahead-of-the-us-talent/ "Link: https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20240322/in-one-key-ai-metric-china-pulls-ahead-of-the-us-talent/")，按照某些指标，中国已经超过美国，成为最大的人工智能人才出产国，培养了世界上近一半的领先研究人员。相比之下，只有约18%来自美国。

出生在中国、并在中国接受教育的研究人员多年来一直在美国顶尖的人工智能实验室中发挥着重要作用。较新的研究表明，他们继续[推动着整个美国工业界和学术界的重要人工智能研究](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20251120/ai-research-chinese-talent/)。但如今，他们当中越来越多的人选择留在中国，为月之暗面、智谱AI和深度求索等公司工作。

title: 特朗普为何淡化中美竞争、“讨好”习近平
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览
summary: 在特朗普总统周三晚间于华盛顿迎接中国国家主席习近平之前的几周里，北京被指在多个方面损害美国的国家利益。 今年夏天，特朗普指责中国在2020年大选中进行了“险恶的选举干预”，他认为这一行为造成的破坏具有历史意义，因此[在黄金时段发表讲话](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/07/16/us/trump-speech-election)，公布了相关指控。自对伊朗战争开始以来，据多名美国官员称，中国企业向德黑兰提供了卫星图像以及一颗间谍卫星的使用权
content:
在特朗普总统周三晚间于华盛顿迎接中国国家主席习近平之前的几周里，北京被指在多个方面损害美国的国家利益。

今年夏天，特朗普指责中国在2020年大选中进行了“险恶的选举干预”，他认为这一行为造成的破坏具有历史意义，因此[在黄金时段发表讲话](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/07/16/us/trump-speech-election)，公布了相关指控。自对伊朗战争开始以来，据多名美国官员称，中国企业向德黑兰提供了卫星图像以及一颗间谍卫星的使用权限，伊朗军方利用这些资源在该地区发动多次袭击。而且，面对美国试图切断德黑兰经济命脉的行动，北京没有表现出任何要停止[与伊朗商业往来](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/china-iran-us-sanctions-banks-cips.html)的迹象。

但随着与习近平会晤的临近，特朗普却一再设法对他网开一面。尽管双方在全球影响力、贸易、人工智能等诸多问题上存在重大竞争，他却更多地把习近平描绘成自己的私人朋友，而非地缘政治竞争对手。

数周来，特朗普一直在为习近平的到访造势，将其宣传为美国的一件大事；提前对白宫进行了一番修缮布置，并筹划了一场国事访问，开场将是他罕见地亲赴安德鲁斯空军基地举行迎接仪式。

就连特朗普的坚定盟友也对这些安排颇有微词。

参议员罗杰·威克表示，他希望特朗普就“中国大规模扩军的目的，以及中国对伊朗的明显支持”向习近平施压。Maxim Shemetov/Reuters

周二，密西西比州共和党参议员、参议院军事委员会主席罗杰·威克[在参议院发表讲话](https://www.wicker.senate.gov/2026/09/22/chairman-wicker-delivers-senate-floor-speech-on-china-and-xi-jinping/)说，如果征求他的意见，他会[建议不要邀请](https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2026/09/22/senate-armed-services-committee-chair-criticizes-trump-xi-meeting/)这位“残暴、未经选举产生、实行压迫统治的独裁者；此人企图称霸邻国，其庞大的军事武库直接瞄准美利坚合众国”。

威克说，他希望特朗普就“中国大规模扩军的目的，以及中国对伊朗的明显支持”向习近平施压。

针对威克的言论，国务卿鲁比奥回应称，此次访问体现出特朗普认识到，尽管双方存在分歧，中国仍是世界上最大的经济与军事力量之一。

“美中关系将定义21世纪，美中关系将决定21世纪，决定这个世纪会发生什么，”鲁比奥说，“认为我们不应在最高层级上与他们互动，这种想法是不负责任的，是荒谬的。我们必须这样做。”

外交政策专家表示，即便对于一位以个人外交为傲的总统来说，特朗普的姿态也格外引人注目。

“特朗普对习近平表现出了非同寻常的顺从，”研究美中关系史的哥伦比亚大学学者朱利安·格维茨说。“他给予中国领导人极高礼遇，同时淡化对美国利益的威胁。北京方面几乎不可能遇到一个更迁就自己的东道主了。”

格维茨曾在拜登总统任内担任白宫和国务院负责中国事务的官员。他说，过去通常是北京方面寻求进行国事访问，而这一次，双方的态势似乎反了过来。特朗普从这一系列引人注目的场面中究竟能收获什么，将是对他那套强调私人关系的外交风格的考验。

“华盛顿过去常常利用象征性的礼遇，来换取北京方面在实质问题上的让步，”他说。“所以问题很简单：特朗普用这一整套隆重礼遇究竟为美国换来了什么？”

在与记者的电话吹风会上，白宫官员表示，此次与习近平的会谈议程将涉及人工智能、芬太尼以及即将到期的贸易休战协议等议题。

当被问及总统是否打算提出他此前关于中国干预2020年大选的指控时，白宫没有发表评论。

一名要求匿名的白宫官员指出，美国已采取多项措施对中国经济造成了影响，包括对美出口显著下降。Gilles Sabrie for The New York Times

另一名白宫官员则反驳了特朗普对习近平过于迁就的说法。这名官员列举了美国采取的多项[影响中国经济](https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20260922/trump-xi-china-trade/)的措施，其中包括中国对美出口的明显下降。

这名官员说，美国已对部分被查实支持伊朗的实体实施了制裁——不过其中没有大型银行——此外还有其他措施正在幕后推进，尚未公布。

由于是在访问开始前讨论相关情况，这些官员均要求匿名。

（上个月，当特朗普被问到为什么没有像通常针对加拿大等盟友那样针对中国的银行时，他厉声反驳道：“谁说我没有？你问为什么没有。我的意思是，谁说我没有？你又不知道我有没有这么做。我没必要什么事都公之于众，对吧？”）

财政部一名发言人随后在电子邮件中表示，牵头[所谓“经济放逐行动”](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260825/trump-bessent-iran-economic-d-day/)的财政部长斯科特·贝森特已经向中国明确表示，对于中国在经济上支持伊朗，美国会毫不犹豫地追究其责任。

最近几周，当被追问中国的行为时，特朗普有好几次似乎都在替习近平开脱。

本月在白宫椭圆形办公室的一场活动上，特朗普称伊朗战争是“小事一桩”，并暗示由于他亲自出面提出了请求，中国对伊朗的援助微不足道。

“我对习近平主席说，请不要介入——我和他关系非常好，”特朗普说。“他们实际上没有怎么介入。中国介入得非常少。中国本来可以大举介入。他们有50%的石油要经过霍尔木兹海峡。”

中国没有表现出任何要减少与伊朗商业往来的迹象，公然无视美国在全球范围内切断德黑兰经济命脉的行动。Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times

当月晚些时候，当被问及有关中国实体可能向伊朗提供卫星图像、帮助伊朗发动造成驻约旦美军死亡的袭击的报道时，[特朗普再次避而不答](https://x.com/jimsciutto/status/2099328672654131373?s=4)。

“基本上他们做的和我们一样，”他说。

“习近平来访时，你会向他提出这件事吗？”一名记者问。

“我认为他的表现还算不错，我们的表现也还算不错，”特朗普说。“你知道，当他们说中国刺探我们的情报时，我会说，你说得对，我们也刺探他们的情报。你知道，我们也刺探他们的情报。”

在接受福克斯新闻采访、被问及习近平可能希望从此次访问中得到什么时，特朗普再次搬出了他一贯的说辞：“你知道，他和我处得非常好。”

多名外交政策分析人士指出，这次访问恰逢特朗普连续数周[不断升级对美国盟友的攻击言论](https://cn.nytimes.com/usa/20260819/trumps-upside-down-world/)之际，两相对照，形成了尤其强烈的反差。

“国际政治有一条美国历任总统通常都会遵循的规则：对盟友的态度理应好于对对手的态度，”拜登政府时期的美国驻华大使尼古拉斯·伯恩斯说。“我们不希望让盟友产生这样的印象：相比与他们的关系，我们其实更重视与习近平的关系。我认为，总统对中国如此不加批评正在给人造成这种印象。”

伯恩斯还说，特朗普的这套策略不太可能在中国身上奏效，因为在他看来，中国只会对实力做出回应。

“他们务实、强硬，对美国抱有怀疑，”伯恩斯说。“我认为，他们会根据我们有多强大以及在必要时的反击力度来判断我们。我认为中国人理解实力和威慑。相比奉承，美国采取强硬立场更能影响到他们。”

分析人士说，如果以过去的峰会为参照，特朗普试图以盛大排场和奉承给习近平留下深刻印象，不会产生多大作用。例如，[两人去年在韩国会晤、试图缓和激烈的贸易战时](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/30/us/politics/trump-xi-trade-meeting.html)，大部分时间都是特朗普在讲话，习近平基本保持沉默。特朗普称习近平是“我的朋友”，还说他是“强有力的领导人”。习近平则以谨慎而强硬的态度参加会晤。在讲话中，他把中美关系比作一艘需要双方稳健共同掌舵的“大船”。

曾在中央情报局从事中国政治分析工作、现为布鲁金斯学会研究员的秦江南(Jonathan A. Czin)表示，两位领导人此次在美国举行峰会所处的形势可谓截然不同。

习近平[占据时间上的优势](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260922/xi-trump-meeting-china-summit/)，他希望借此为自己争取更多喘息空间，以缓解来自美方的压力——毕竟他正在为即将到来的第四个任期做准备，这将使他继续执掌大权五年之久。特朗普则将在几周后面临中期选举，由于他的一些政策，其所在政党面临一场艰难的选战。

“习近平走进这场会晤时，会非常清楚地意识到一个事实：再过几个星期，特朗普很可能最好的结果是成为一名跛脚鸭总统；最坏的情况下，他在国内政治上将遭受重创，还不得不面对一个分裂的政府，” 秦江南说。

他接着说：“习近平已经在思考，‘我怎样才能让与美国达成的这项君子协定继续维持下去’，从而争取时间；而且他已经在考虑特朗普卸任之后的局面该如何应对。”

特朗普向来对威权领导人抱有好感。他时常炫耀自己与俄罗斯总统普京的关系。今年夏天,他还大肆宣扬自己与朝鲜独裁者金正恩之间所谓的良好关系。同时却[取消了与美国盟友韩国之间由来已久的联合军事演习](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/20/us/politics/trumps-order-military-exercises-risks.html)。

纽约大学研究法西斯主义与威权主义的历史学家露丝·本-吉亚特表示，特朗普一直以来都很欣赏习近平，因为后者拥有他所渴求的那种权力。

她指出，特朗普上个月曾发出末日般的警告，称“共产主义是我国历史上面临的最大威胁”，但这丝毫没有影响特朗普对一个强大共产党国家领导人的“奉承讨好”。

她还提到，上周有记者提出中国是全球对新闻记者压制最为严厉的国家之一时，特朗普再度为中国政府进行了辩护。特朗普打断了那名记者的提问，回应道：“这个嘛，我倒不这么认为。我觉得我们自己也挺压制的。”（就在同一天，他宣布禁止他不满其报道内容的新闻机构进入白宫区域。）

本-吉亚特说，“这次国家元首会晤的重要性在于它所制造出的视觉效果——两位强大的铁腕人物以对等身份会面，至少在特朗普看来是如此。此外还在于以不透明方式达成交易的可能性。”

title: 习近平访美首日看点：谁同行？第一夫人角色？高规格接待引反弹？
summary: ## 习近平访美首日看点：谁同行？第一夫人角色？高规格接待引反弹？ 图像来源，Reuters 图像加注文字，2026年9月23日，美国总统特朗普迎接中国国家主席习近平。 Published 1 小时前 阅读时间: 4 分钟 随着中国国家主席习近平的专机抵达美国首都华盛顿，三天访美行程正式开始。 这是他时隔11年再次国事访问美国，美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）亲自迎接，若不计算罗马天主教教宗，属美国总统超过60年来首次以此方式迎接他国元首到访。 话题预计将包括
content:
## 习近平访美首日看点：谁同行？第一夫人角色？高规格接待引反弹？

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，2026年9月23日，美国总统特朗普迎接中国国家主席习近平。

Published 1 小时前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

随着中国国家主席习近平的专机抵达美国首都华盛顿，三天访美行程正式开始。

这是他时隔11年再次国事访问美国，美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）亲自迎接，若不计算罗马天主教教宗，属美国总统超过60年来首次以此方式迎接他国元首到访。

话题预计将包括中美两国人工智能竞争、台湾问题、关税与伊朗局势等；与此同时，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）宣布，美国和中国将把两国贸易战的休战期延长至明年1月。

BBC中文整理，习近平抵达华盛顿一刻，外界关注的重点看点：谁是习近平访美团成员？美国共和党及人民对中国的态度为何？

## 习近平出访团成员有谁？

习近平的专机在周三（9月23日）美东夏令时间约17:40（格林尼治标准时间21:40；北京时间24日周五05:40）降落位于华盛顿市郊的安德鲁斯联合基地。

除了习近平夫人彭丽媛随行外，乘坐同一班专机抵达的，包括被视为习近平重要亲信的中共中央政治局常委蔡奇，以及外交部长王毅。

另外，亦有官员较早前已抵达美国，包括中国国务院副总理何立峰。他在峰会举行前于纽约会见美国财政部长贝森特（Scott Bessent）。中国驻美国大使谢锋亦在机场迎接。

中国官方新华社报道，习近平在一份书面声明中表示，“两国应该成为伙伴而不是对手”，又指相信此次访问将“取得丰硕成果，为两国人民增进福祉，为世界和平增添希望”。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，中国国家主席习近平与夫人彭丽媛抵达美国马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地，准备进行国事访问；两人走下飞机时挥手致意。

目前尚不清楚有哪些商界高层会随习近平一同出访。

如果多名美国人工智能（AI）企业行政总裁出席国宴，而中国人工智能企业行政总裁却似乎无人现身，这将形成鲜明对比。尤其是在特朗普今年5月访问北京时，曾带同企业行政总裁同行。

但习近平作出这样的安排并不令人意外。

BBC驻中国记者劳拉·比克尔（Laura Bicker）分析，习近平可能认为这对北京而言存在风险，因这类活动可以迅速演变成媒体高度关注的场合，而中国领导人最不希望看到的，就是有企业行政总裁在任何时候发表与其讯息不一致的言论。

带同中国企业赴美，亦可能引发外界对中国商业运作方式、政府补贴及产能过剩等问题的质疑。这些议题都可能招致比习近平或中国共产党所愿承受更多的批评和提问。

今年5月，特朗普访华期间，美国大型科技企业高层组成的代表团随行，包括苹果的库克（Tim Cook）、特斯拉的马斯克（Elon Musk）和辉达的黄仁勋等。

《南华早报》早前报道，习近平计划仿效华府去年5月派出的代表团安排，意味代表团预计将由来自科技、金融、电动车等商业领袖组成。

## 习近平乘搭什么专机？

美国总统出访时会乘坐“空军一号”（Air Force One），这是全球最广为人知的飞机之一。

当习近平的专机出现在安德鲁斯联合基地上空时，可以发现它在许多方面与“空军一号”相似。它几乎总是一架波音747客机，配备中国领导人出访所需的各项设施。但相较之下，它较少为外界所知，原因是它并非固定使用同一架飞机。

与美国不同，中国政府并没有专门供国家元首公务出访使用的飞机。习近平使用的是中国国际航空（Air China）机队中的一架波音747客机。

中国官员曾向传媒表示，这项安排旨在善用现有飞机，以减少浪费。

根据中国媒体报道，中国空军会检查并改装飞机，以符合国家主席的需要，包括拆除部分座位，腾出空间安装沙发和睡床。

除此之外，外界对这架飞机所知不多。但人们通常可以看到，在中国领导人下机的舱门附近，会悬挂官方旗帜。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，美国马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地，中国国家主席习近平抵达准备进行国事访问，美国总统川普与习近平一同走在红毯上。

## 梅拉尼娅：“每个细节我都有参与”

美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅（Melania Trump）表示，她深度参与中国代表团此次访问行程的规划工作。

她在接受福克斯新闻（Fox News；霍士新闻）访问时表示：“每一个细节，我都有参与。”

她称，特朗普决定亲自到机场迎接习近平，是因为“他们关系非常好”，而她则参与了包括国宴在内的其他主要访问安排。

她说：“整个规划涉及大量细节，亦有必须遵循的礼宾程序。”

除了白宫的欢迎仪式，梅拉尼娅亦安排与彭丽媛一同参观史密森尼国立亚洲艺术博物馆（Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art），以展示美中两国之间的文化联系。

白宫表示，此次访问将以一项具有历史象征意义的行程作结。

两对夫妇将前往美国国家档案馆（National Archives），参观重要国家档案，其中包括一些“对美中关系具有重要意义”的历史纪录。

图像来源，Reuters

## 高规格接待引共和党反弹？

白宫数月来一直大力宣传习近平访问华盛顿，而特朗普总统本人亦经常提到自己与这位中国领导人之间的“极佳”关系。

白宫官员和幕僚显然认为，这次访问，以及特朗普今年5月访华之行，可能是他第二个总统任期中最具影响力的两项外交活动。

但多年来，特朗普的“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）支持者普遍对中国抱持怀疑态度。如今，特朗普为身兼中国共产党总书记的习近平铺设红地毯欢迎，已引起共和党内部分人士的关注。

毕竟，特朗普一再提出共产主义逐步蔓延的威胁，认为这对美国构成危险。

共和党参议员罗杰·威克（Roger Wicker）周二发表演说时，批评习近平获得“隆重欢迎”。作为参议院军事委员会主席的他表示，鉴于“我们与习近平主席及中国共产党之间存在的种种令人忧虑问题”，特朗普本应审慎考虑是否邀请习近平访美。

共和党策略师布雷特·马森（Barrett Marson）接受Politico访问时则表示，习近平此行是“特朗普的讯息与共和党立场不一致的又一例证”。

马森说：“在这个选举周期，共和党最直接的论点之一，就是民主党想把社会主义或共产主义带到美国。”

“而特朗普热情拥抱两位最直言不讳支持这些意识形态的领导人之一，令这项讯息更难引起选民共鸣。”

## 美国人对华态度回温吗？

在美国，无论是在政府内还是政府外的不少知名人士，都经常将中国描绘成对手甚至潜在敌人。

但特朗普对习近平的高规格接待，正值美国民众对中国的观感似乎有所回暖之际。

中美峰会前夕，芝加哥全球事务委员会（Chicago Council on Global Affairs）发布最新民调显示，41%的美国人认为中国的领土野心对美国构成威胁。但这一比例较2022年的52%有所下降。

超过半数美国人（57%），认为美国应与北京合作并保持接触。

值得注意的是，这一看法横跨美国不同政治光谱。

不认同“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）的共和党人当中，有57%支持合作；大多数民主党人，无论属温和派还是自由派，也持相同看法。

大多数MAGA共和党人，即63%，则支持限制美国与中国的关系。这意味着特朗普最忠实的支持群体，在对华政策上与他致力拉近与习近平关系的做法存在分歧。

视频加注文字，习近平访美晤特朗普：中美竞赛谁领先？美国民众怎么看

title: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington looking for a trade win
summary: * Summary * Companies * Trump rolls out red carpet as leaders seek stability despite deep tensions * Trade truce extension envisaged, but major breakthroughs not expected * Xi enters summit with stronger hand given trade surge and rare-eart
content:
*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Trump rolls out red carpet as leaders seek stability despite deep tensions
*   Trade truce extension envisaged, but major breakthroughs not expected
*   Xi enters summit with stronger hand given trade surge and rare-earth dominance

WASHINGTON, Sept 24 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday for a lavish state summit expected to be heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with ​both leaders keen to showcase stable ties despite a deep underlying rivalry.

It will be the year's second meeting of the leaders of the two biggest economies, but Xi's first ‌visit to Washington in more than a decade.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Ftrump-welcomes-xi-washington-looking-trade-win-2026-09-24%2F)

Trump greeted Xi on arrival on Wednesday evening, the first time a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews in 11 years, when President Barack Obama welcomed Pope Francis in 2015, according to C-SPAN, which tracks presidential events.

In a statement on arrival carried by China's Xinhua news agency, Xi voiced hope for a more stable relationship with the United States, saying Beijing and Washington should be "partners, not rivals" and that the "historical logic ​of peaceful coexistence" between the two countries had not changed.

For Trump, who relishes ceremony and prizes his ties with powerful leaders, the visit is as much a matter of national prestige as ​an opportunity for high-stakes diplomacy.

The US president aims to reciprocate the grand welcome he received [in China in May](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-xi-set-second-day-talks-after-taiwan-warning-2026-05-14/) and impress Xi with a ceremony spanning the ⁠White House South Lawn, State Floor and Rose Garden.

Major breakthroughs are not expected.

Analysts say tangible outcomes are likely to be limited to an extension of a trade truce expiring in November and an agreement to ​examine threats posed by artificial intelligence.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that [they had agreed to extend until January 10](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-china-agree-extend-the-busan-agreement-until-january-bessent-says-2026-09-23/) an agreement that paused a ​trade war that saw mutual tariffs top 100%.

People familiar with the plans say the talks could also yield deals to lower some tariffs, combat drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue, while Trump is expected to seek the release of Americans and others detained in China.

Former Deputy Secretary of State Kurt Campbell said the summit was less about substantive negotiations than a chance for two forceful leaders to project strength.

"This is really the historical reincarnation of what we often referred to in ​antiquity as single combat - really powerful guys, each representing their civilizations, kind of measuring and going toe to toe," said Campbell.

## KEEPING TIES STABLE

Xi [appears to be in a stronger position](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/xi-rolls-into-trump-summit-with-chinas-trade-engine-roaring-2026-09-21/), having overseen a surge in China's ​trade and controlling supplies of rare earth minerals that give him a powerful source of leverage.

Item 1 of 2 US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping react as Xi arrives ahead of a state visit at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst

**[1/2]**US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping react as Xi arrives ahead of a state visit at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-donald-trump-welcomes-chinas-president-xi-jinping-at-joint-base-andrews/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkFQTkE5V0w2Rw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Both leaders see advantages in keeping relations stable, with Trump mired in the unpopular Iran war and Xi grappling with domestic economic challenges.

But beneath ‌the surface are ⁠challenges that could reignite tensions, including disputes over Taiwan, export controls and AI.

Taiwan, a democratically governed island claimed by China, is the most contentious of these.

US allies in Asia are concerned Trump may be tempted to soften Washington's support for Taipei to lock in economic wins with China.

Xi is expected to press Trump to halt Taiwan [arms sales](https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/four-us-republicans-call-trump-release-taiwan-security-funds-2026-09-23/) and could do this during a [planned visit by the two to the US National Archives on Friday](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-expected-press-trump-halt-taiwan-arms-sales-under-1982-agreement-2026-09-22/), sources briefed told Reuters. In return, China is offering help to put pressure on Iran, the sources added.

After the May summit, Trump said he was holding in abeyance an arms package worth some $14 billion ​and called it a "very good negotiating chip."

The leaders will ​likely discuss the [Iran war](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran/), but there has ⁠been little sign Beijing is willing to exert pressure on its ally to yield to US demands, despite the disruption the conflict has caused to energy supplies and trade.

## TRADE DEALS POSSIBLE

Trade is more promising.

Trump is seeking trade wins ahead of the midterms and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said this month the countries will ​make "some announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers."

Greer said on Monday China is making progress on a commitment to buy 200 Boeing

aircraft, but gave no ​indication that any additional orders ⁠are near.

Analysts say AI could be an area for cooperation, given its implications for national security, economic competitiveness and military capabilities, and shared US and Chinese concerns about misuse.

Bessent [discussed AI with He Lifeng at the weekend](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/us-treasurys-bessent-chinas-he-launch-talks-ai-trade-critical-minerals-2026-09-20/), and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was nascent thinking about "the equivalent of a hotline that we had during the Cold War" to avoid dangerous incidents that "could impact economies or societies and even lead to a conflict ⁠between nation-states."

However, analysts ​say intense competition in AI is likely to limit the scope for anything beyond symbolic agreements.

The guest list for Thursday's state ​dinner includes CEOs like Apple's Tim Cook, Amazon's Jeff Bezos, Alphabet's Sundar Pichai, Open AI's Sam Altman, Tesla's Elon Musk and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, but despite such an array, people familiar with US plans say Trump is likely to maintain firm export controls on ​US tech Xi wants loosened.

Reporting by David Brunnstrom, Andrea Shalal, David Lawder and Trevor Hunnicutt in Washington; Ben Blanchard and Yimou Lee in Taipei, and Joe Cash in Beijing; Editing by Don Durfee and Stephen Coates

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Trevor Hunnicutt is White House Correspondent at Reuters News. He writes about U.S. foreign and domestic policy and regularly travels with the President of the United States. Prior to joining the White House team in 2021, he covered presidential campaigns, economics, finance and investing for many years. He has also served on the board of the White House Correspondents' Association. Hunnicutt holds a bachelor's degree from Pomona College and a master's from the London School of Economics.

title: A diplomatic split screen as Trump and Xi meet
summary: * Summary * Trump-Xi meeting overshadows UN gathering * Absences fuel questions about UN relevance * Financial woes and gridlock cloud UN future * Diplomats say UN remains an indispensable forum UNITED NATIONS, Sept 24 (Reuters) - While wor
content:
*   Summary

*   Trump-Xi meeting overshadows UN gathering
*   Absences fuel questions about UN relevance
*   Financial woes and gridlock cloud UN future
*   Diplomats say UN remains an indispensable forum

UNITED NATIONS, Sept 24 (Reuters) - While world leaders gather at the [United Nations](https://www.reuters.com/world/united-nations/) for their annual diplomatic ritual, the two biggest power brokers in global politics will sit down in a different venue on Thursday: the White House.

US President Donald Trump and Chinese ​leader Xi Jinping will meet for the second time this year, hoping to keep the world's most consequential bilateral relationship steady as both leaders grapple with a host of ‌domestic and global issues.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fdiplomatic-split-screen-trump-xi-meet-2026-09-24%2F)

The split-screen moment highlights an existential question for the UN: does the world body, established after the calamity of two world wars, still matter?

While UN delegates discuss "multilateralism" and hold panels on the world's conflicts, Trump and Xi – what the US president calls the "G2" – will talk AI, trade and defense.

"It's pretty notable that Xi Jinping is coming to Washington in the same week as the General Assembly, but does not feel bothered to come up to New York," said Richard ​Gowan of the International Crisis Group.

"I think a lot of people will say, 'Where is the real center of decision-making?'"

Xi rarely travels to New York for the General Assembly.

The questions about the UN's ​role are hardly new, but have acquired fresh urgency as the organization struggles with deep financial problems, divisions among major powers and limited influence over conflicts ⁠from Ukraine to the Middle East.

Those concerns have gained new relevance since Trump's return to office last year. The US leader has pulled the US out of dozens of UN agencies and slashed Washington's ​budgetary contributions to the organization, [pushing it](https://www.reuters.com/world/un-chief-guterres-warns-imminent-financial-collapse-2026-01-30/) to the brink of bankruptcy.

In his speech on Tuesday, Trump accused the UN of "imposing the far-left agenda of globalist bureaucrats who nobody ever elected."

## DEEPENING WOES

The UN has a persistent budget ​shortfall, forcing it to cut the budget of its Secretariat by 9.2% for 2026. It laid off thousands of staff, sent peacekeepers home and cut back on humanitarian and human rights work.

The United States, which has for years withheld much of its dues, is part of that problem.

The Trump administration last week [paid](https://www.reuters.com/world/us-pays-725-million-un-easing-its-debt-dispute-with-world-body-2026-09-16/) $725 million for the regular budget, preserving its vote at the assembly, but still owes $1.3 billion to the regular budget and $2.9 billion for peacekeeping operations, the UN said.

The organization's problems ​extend beyond money, however.

Item 1 of 3 US President Donald Trump shows the way to Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrives ahead of a state visit at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst

**[1/3]**US President Donald Trump shows the way to Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrives ahead of a state visit at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-donald-trump-welcomes-chinas-president-xi-jinping-at-joint-base-andrews/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkJQTkFEM09ZOA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Gridlock has long defined the UN Security Council, where five veto powers including China, Russia and the US rarely agree on anything substantive.

"There are two main challenges that the UN faces today: ​the first is its dire financial situation," said Eugene Chen, a former UN official.

"This is linked to a second, broader, challenge – the fact that member states no longer agree on what the form or function of the UN ought ‌to be at ⁠a time of mounting global challenges," he said.

Outgoing Secretary-General Antonio Guterres launched a reform task force last year, known as

[UN80, opens new tab](https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/statements/2026-09-03/secretary-generals-remarks-the-general-assembly-the-un80-initiative)
, which seeks to cut costs, remove duplication, move jobs to locations cheaper than New York and Geneva and improve efficiency.

It includes a 21% reduction in posts at the Secretariat and a review of more than 600 series of mandated Secretary-General's reports, aiming to reduce reporting by about 700,000 words in 2026.

## 'CRAVEN HYPOCRITES'

Unlike in 2025, Trump did not use his Tuesday speech to complain about escalators or teleprompters and largely stuck to a script that focused on defending his record in the war with Iran and on the US ​economy.

Still, he inveighed against the "craven hypocrites" of the ​UN's Human Rights Council who "want America to open ⁠our borders to gangs and criminals from the world’s most dangerous places," and zeroed in on UNESCO, saying "these globalists are actively destroying the greatest cultures and most extraordinary heritage in history."

The UN has defended culture and education agency UNESCO's work as "unanimously acclaimed by major specialized organizations,” and the Human Rights Council as playing "a ​very important role in the promotion and protection of human rights worldwide."

Xi has sought to capitalize on Trump's often bellicose rhetoric by presenting China as ​a reliable partner on the ⁠global stage, especially for developing nations, and by using the UN as a platform to advance that message.

## 1,000 MEETINGS

For all the criticism of the UN, its annual meeting remains a forum for high-volume diplomacy. This week, member states planned

[more than 1,000 bilateral meetings, opens new tab](https://press.un.org/en/2026/db260918.doc.htm)
, according to UN data.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner [communicated through mediators](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/hope-progress-after-us-iran-hold-first-shuttle-talks-months-2026-09-23/) on the sidelines on Tuesday, the first such contacts since an interim ceasefire agreement collapsed ⁠in July.

The ​European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters the UN remained relevant, but she too criticized the organization for being "paralyzed ​when it comes to preventing or ending conflicts."

Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy [used the venue](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/zelenskiy-meet-trump-un-push-energy-truce-with-russia-2026-09-22/) to hold talks with Trump on ending the war with Russia, including a potential ceasefire on energy-related targets.

He was asked by a journalist whether years of meetings at the UN have ​brought any concrete results. He answered in English: "Today it helps us to meet. Maybe it's not too much, but it's something."

Reporting by Antoni Slodkowski, John Irish and Tom Balmforth; Editing by Don Durfee and Howard Goller

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Antoni Slodkowski is Reuters Chief Politics & General News Correspondent for China, based in Beijing, where he leads coverage of Chinese politics, society, and its relations with global counterparts. He has won two Pulitzer Prizes with Reuters colleagues: in Investigative Reporting in 2025 for uncovering fentanyl supply chains, and in International Reporting in 2019 for exposing the persecution of Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar. Previously Japan Deputy Bureau Chief and Myanmar Bureau Chief at Reuters, Antoni also reported from Tokyo for the Financial Times and was a Knight-Wallace Fellow at the University of Michigan. He began his journalism career as a teenager, hosting a children's TV show for Poland's largest public broadcaster.

title: The US Is Badly Losing Its Trade War with China
summary: Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House on Thursday will be the first Chinese state visit to the United States [since 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_state_visit_by_Xi_Jinping_to_the_United_States). It thus makes for the perfect ti
content:
Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House on Thursday will be the first Chinese state visit to the United States [since 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_state_visit_by_Xi_Jinping_to_the_United_States). It thus makes for the perfect time to judge the radical changes to US-China trade policy that President Donald Trump unleashed in 2018. After eight years of historically high tariffs, export controls, industrial policy, and more, we can conclude the policy has been a failure by its own objectives.

In March 2018, the US’s opening [tariff salvo](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2018-03-27/pdf/2018-06304.pdf) – implemented via Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 – [aimed to roll back](https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2018/march/section-301-report-chinas-acts) Chinese industrial policy and blunt Beijing’s push for dominance in advanced manufacturing. Subsequent tariffs and export controls [added more goals](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/RL33536): shrink China’s trade surplus and policy-driven overcapacity, reduce US dependence on Chinese goods, slow China’s technological advance, and weaken Beijing’s geopolitical position.

Granted, there have been a few superficial victories. Between 2017 and 2025, direct [imports from China declined](https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/balance/c5700.html) from about 21.6% of US goods imports in 2017 to roughly 9% by 2025, a level not seen since China joined the World Trade Organization in 2001. Export restrictions have denied Chinese companies easy access to Nvidia Corp.’s best chips and ASML Holding NV’s best chipmaking equipment. And American firms such as Apple Inc. shifted production capacity from China to India, Vietnam, Mexico, and other low-wage alternatives.

Beneath the surface, however, there’s little for trade hawks to cheer. New [research](https://www.hbs.edu/ris/Publication%20Files/AC_TradeReallocation_Mar2026_0006a539-9531-4298-9e9d-92cf2262bf06.pdf)[finds](https://www.piie.com/research/piie-charts/2026/years-us-tariffs-china-have-largely-failed-reduce-dependence-chinese) that Chinese _content_ – either directly or lawfully embedded in third-country goods – has been entering the US at levels only modestly below those in 2017, confirming the [anecdotal evidence](https://www.cato.org/commentary/what-most-people-dont-understand-about-us-china-decoupling). Illegal transshipment and [customs fraud](https://x.com/scottlincicome/status/2032464737984758177?s=20) have also increased – another [predictable result](https://www.cato.org/commentary/republicans-cant-pay-their-tax-cuts-fantasy-revenue-sources) of high and complex US tariffs. The 2025–26 drop in [China’s import share](https://www.piie.com/publications/working-papers/2026/how-did-trumps-2025-trade-war-affect-decoupling-us-china-supply), meanwhile, is mainly owed to surging AI inputs from Mexico and Taiwan – goods that were never made in China to begin with.

Outside the US, China’s trade position has never been stronger. Its trade surplus in goods [rose to a record](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/14/china-trade-data-surplus-exports-imports-december-tariffs-tensions.html) $1.19 trillion last year and is [on pace to meet or exceed](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-09-08/china-s-trade-surplus) that total in 2026, with [substantial export gains](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/05/in-what-ways-has-u-s-trade-with-china-changed/) in non-US markets and in advanced industries like electronic vehicles. China also [remains the world’s top manufacturing nation](https://rbaldwin.substack.com/p/is-china-still-the-worlds-sole-manufacturing) and the largest producer and exporter of intermediate goods – both by large margins. Chinese firms have [ramped up](https://www.economist.com/interactive/business/2026/08/19/chinese-firms-are-wrapping-their-supply-chains-around-the-globe?taid=6ab07385b2348200012c4d31&utm_campaign=editorial-social&utm_content=discovery.content&utm_medium=social-media.content.np&utm_source=twitter) both sales to and outbound investment in third-country production hubs facing lower US tariffs. Overall, Chinese exporters responded to new trade barriers not by shrinking but simply going around them.

China’s state capitalist economic model is also unchanged and may have been further entrenched by the US’s confrontational approach. In 2021, Beijing responded to US tariffs with a [five-year plan](https://merics.org/en/comment/chinas-14th-five-year-plan-strengthening-domestic-base-become-superpower) that doubled down on industrial policy and technological self-reliance. According to the US-China Business Council, Beijing’s [latest (15th) plan](https://www.uschina.org/articles/chinas-industrial-policy-in-the-15th-five-year-plan-everything-beyond-subsidies-june-3/) “suggests that industrial policy is no longer just one policy area among many but rather an organizing logic for the whole economy.”

Today, policymakers in Europe and elsewhere worry aloud about a destabilizing wave of Chinese exports – a “China Shock 2.0” – fueled by [massive Chinese subsidies](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2026/05/oecd-magic-database-of-industrial-subsidies_3d51d749/ce94f33b-en.pdf). State-owned enterprises, meanwhile, continue to play a large role in China’s economy and trade. Per [the Peterson Institute](https://www.piie.com/research/piie-charts/2026/chinas-private-sector-rebound-continued-2025-fueled-new-economy), companies with full or substantial government ownership still accounted for 60% of the combined market value of China’s top 100 listed firms. American farm export targets in the most recent US-China trade deal [perversely depend](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-12/china-pledge-on-us-soybeans-tested-as-private-crushers-hold-back) on state-owned Sinograin and COFCO.

American policy has proven ineffective – if not counterproductive – in other ways, too. Following the shock of US tariffs and export restrictions during Trump’s first term, Beijing worked to reduce its vulnerability to economic pressure from Washington and to [develop asymmetric countermeasures](https://www.iiss.org/online-analysis/charting-china/2025/02/chinas-use-of-export-controls/) should US coercion reemerge. This deepened Beijing’s involvement in China’s economy, led [Chinese companies](https://www.ft.com/content/c99d86f0-2d17-49d0-8dc6-9662ed34c831) to [look inward](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3367792/us-sanctions-boost-chinas-science-driven-innovation-over-70-study-finds) for technology and innovation, and gave the CCP new leverage – most notably over the rare earth minerals that US [firms depend on](https://www.ft.com/content/201a86a6-3597-4efb-b575-39172c729fe1?syn-25a6b1a6=1) – in bilateral talks. The moves help to explain why the 2018 wave of US tariffs produced a “Phase One” deal that (superficially, at least) favored Washington, while Trump’s second-term escalation has produced a stalemate.

Today, the US-China détente has, along with other Trump tariffs on non-China goods, so narrowed the gap between tariffs on Chinese imports and those on China alternative nations that some [supply chains](https://www.cato.org/blog/trumps-tariffs-push-us-companies-back-china) are [now moving](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/companies-left-china-dodge-tariffs-now-some-are-heading-back-2026-09-14/)_back_[into China](https://www.autonews.com/stellantis/jeep/an-stellantis-jeep-returns-to-china-starts-ev-exports-with-dongfeng-0825/). German firms are [boosting their China investments](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/german-firms-lift-china-investment-us-outlays-fall-iw-study-shows-2026-09-13/) while cutting US outlays. India has [engaged with China](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/india-china-ties-how-trump-s-trade-war-is-bringing-modi-xi-closer-together) after years of tension. And polls find China is viewed more favorably than the US in [numerous countries](https://www.pewresearch.org/global/2026/07/15/views-of-china-and-xi-are-improving-globally/) for the first time.

American export controls and sanctions have also proven leaky. Research firm [Epoch AI estimated](https://epoch.ai/publications/chip-smuggling) that by the end of 2025 hundreds of thousands of Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips had reached China in violation of US export controls. Washington has [relented on advanced chip sales](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/ball-games-over-the-us-is-out-of-the-ai-chip-market-in-china/) to China, but no one there is buying because US restrictions prodded Chinese chipmakers to build passable alternatives. American firms, the [Brookings Institute concluded](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/ball-games-over-the-us-is-out-of-the-ai-chip-market-in-china/) in June, are now “shut out of the high end of the world’s largest chip market.”

These US policy failures don’t mean that China is an unstoppable hegemon in waiting. Beijing has set its [lowest growth target in decades](https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/04/business/china-npc-gdp-economy-intl-hnk). Chinese technology [still lags behind](https://www.cato.org/commentary/chinese-industrial-policy-anchor-not-engine) in certain advanced manufacturing industries, including top-end semiconductors. And the Chinese economy faces long-term headwinds – pervasive capital misallocation, sub-frontier productivity, smothering debt, and a rapidly aging population – that no amount of exports can fix.

But that’s very much the point. The problems in China’s economy are owed to factors beyond Washington’s control, and US trade restrictions since 2018 have done little to alter China’s trajectory while imposing a significant cost on American companies and consumers.

After eight years of failed unilateralism, Trump officials [still don’t](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-08-11/us-moves-past-tariffs-to-focus-on-supply-chain-revamps-in-china-trade-policy) seem [to understand](https://ep.ft.com/permalink/emails/eyJlbWFpbCI6ImNlNWUwMDkwNjdlOTQzZjk5OTc2ZjU2MjljMjQyZjVjZmUiLCAidHJhbnNhY3Rpb25JZCI6IjViZDliN2VmLTk3MzUtNGYyYS1hZjJkLTUzZjFhZDQ1ZDY5YiIsICJiYXRjaElkIjoiMDgwN2U4OGMtM2FiNy00MTM2LThkMjQtMzY0MWZiZmVkZGM2In0=) that Washington can’t fundamentally change how the Chinese government organizes its economy, and that it’s [better to focus](https://www.cato.org/policy-analysis/course-correction) US government efforts on a narrow set of real Chinese threats, on deepening non-China alliances, and on fixing _American_ economic competitiveness across a range of issue areas.

Dramatic changes to _Chinese policy_ must come from _Chinese officials_. Washington unfortunately keeps giving them reasons not to change.

title: 专家：数据显示北京对日本的旅游抵制未产生显著影响
summary: 华盛顿 — 日本首相高市早苗在唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统星期四(9月24日)在白宫与中国国家主席习近平举行峰会之前，与特朗普会面，并寻求他对日本与中国关系的帮助。日中关系因高市早苗早前有关台湾的言论而陷于低潮，日本也正承受中国各种包括经济胁迫在内的报复行动。不过，一个最新的报告说，中国的经济筹码未必有效。 路透社报道，高市早苗星期三表示，她希望美中关系有利于国际稳定，两人也同意进一步强化彼此的经济安全关系。自高市早苗去年说过关于台湾受攻击可能构成日本依法行
content:
华盛顿 —

日本首相高市早苗在唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统星期四(9月24日)在白宫与中国国家主席习近平举行峰会之前，与特朗普会面，并寻求他对日本与中国关系的帮助。日中关系因高市早苗早前有关台湾的言论而陷于低潮，日本也正承受中国各种包括经济胁迫在内的报复行动。不过，一个最新的报告说，中国的经济筹码未必有效。

路透社报道，高市早苗星期三表示，她希望美中关系有利于国际稳定，两人也同意进一步强化彼此的经济安全关系。自高市早苗去年说过关于台湾受攻击可能构成日本依法行使集体自卫权事态后，日本与中国的关系急转直下，中国以多种措施，包括警告中国公民避免前往日本旅游作为报复。

不过一个新报告说，日本以分散市场的做法减低了中国游客大量减少对日本的经济冲击，其他也遭受中国同样待遇的亚洲邻国也可以思考如何以自己的强项来降低中国的经济胁迫。

**中国经济筹码未必有效**

澳大利亚洛伊研究所近期一篇文章援引日本国家旅游局数据说，北京对日本的旅游抵制显示，经济杠杆并不能保证经济控制。

文章说，尽管中国游客大幅减少，但今年前半年外国游客对日本的经济贡献为4.9万亿日圆，约为304亿美元，而今年7月访问日本的游客也达到破纪录的340万人，其中来自中国的游客只有42万8千200人，占所有访客的12.4%，与去年7月同比减少了56.1%，但日本旅游业仍然维持水平，“从数据来看，中国游客的衰退对日本更广泛的旅游业并没有多少影响。”

日中关系自2025年11月以来急剧恶化。高市早苗当时在日本国会质询时表示，如果中国对台湾使用武力并对日本的生存构成威胁，可能符合日本安全保障法制所规定的“存亡危机事态”，日本自卫队不排除进行武力干预，依法有限行使集体自卫权。

尽管民主自治的台湾政府称，中华民国与中华人民共和国“互不隶属”，但北京当局视民主自治的台湾为中国领土一部分，从未放弃以武力实现统一，也一贯反对外部势力干预中国内政，因此指责高市的言论暗示日本可能军事介入台海，随后采取多项报复措施，包括限制军民两用物项对日出口、鼓励中国公民不要赴日旅游等反制措施，并以核污水争端为由冻结进口日本海产品，还加强了对稀土、石墨等战略物资的出口管制。

文章作者，美国曼斯菲尔德(Mansfield)基金会研究员、海军中校安德鲁·奥查得(Commander Andrew Orchard)说，中国对日本的经济筹码是来自于传统上中国游客对日本旅游市场的庞大数量。在2019年，来自中国的游客达到960万人，占了所有外国游客的将近三分之一，但今年前7个月，中国游客只占整个市场的10.2%。

奥查得指出，中国对日本的做法与它对帕劳、韩国一样，航空公司和旅游业者因此而减少了前往日本的游客数量，而较受中国游客欢迎的旅游市场也受到较大影响，例如今年6月，大阪的每日平均旅馆订房率就与去年同比减少了18.8%。

“不过日本原本就不需要去弥补每一个中国游客带来的缺口，”奥查得说，“它需要做的是填补2025年中国游客贡献的大约2万亿日圆(约127亿美元)消费，而答案就在于通常每趟旅游人均消费较高的远程游客。”他说。

他说，数据显示，去年每一位中国游客在日本的消费为24万6千日圆，远低于美国游客平均每人消费的34万1千日圆，以及德国游客平均每人消费的39万3千日圆，因此“日本能以弥补中国游客贡献的收益的方式来吸收其人数的大量减少，而不是去填补游客的总数。”

**日本旅游业仍保持韧性**

至于日本的旅游市场数据是否表示日本已经可以不受中国经济报复的影响，奥查得中校在接受美国之音采访时说，他个人的评估是，尽管中国游客大量减少，但日本旅游经济仍然保持相当韧性，那表示日本已经变得较不依赖中国作为主要游客来源所带来的营收。

“不过，我不会错误地把这个认为是中国旅游不再重要的信号。部分日本旅游经济仍然严重依赖中国游客，而那些生意很可能已经收到重大影响。这包括以中国旅游团为主要客源的业者。对他们来说，日本更广泛的分散市场并没有带来立即的缓解。”他说。

仍然是现役军人的奥查得特别表明，他在采访中所表达的是他个人的看法和意见，并不一定代表美国防务研究所、曼斯菲尔德基金会、美国国防部、美国海军部或美国政府的看法。

他说，最近发布的8月数据还是支持他对日本旅游业仍具韧性的看法。根据日本国家旅游局，虽然国际游客与去年同比减少了9.6%，但来自其他几个远程市场，包括法国、美国和墨西哥等国家的游客，数字都在持续增加，平均每趟消费金额也都比中国游客来得高。以法国游客为例，8月就增加了8.4%，达到4万多人，2026年第二季法国游客平均每人消费为42万3千日圆(约2,700美元)。对比远程旅游，8月到日本的中国游客与去年同比减少了59%，比7月减少2.38%，今年第二季平均每人消费为26万6千日圆。

奥查得指出，同比数据显示，与2025年相比，日本的中国旅游依然处于严重低迷状态；而环比降幅可能表明，这一下滑趋势正开始趋于稳定，不过在得出确切结论前还需要更多数据来加以佐证。

**市场多元化抵消冲击**

奥查得认为，更广泛的观点是，如果其他游客能停留更久一点或消费更多一些，日本并不需要填补每一个流失的中国游客。“正如我在文章里提到的，日本旅游市场的组成元素，与整体访客人数一样重要。”

展望未来，奥查得强调，远程旅游市场的增长将提供另一个日本如何有效抵消中国游客减少的指标，而冬季旅游在这方面尤其重要，包括北海道新雪谷町和长野县白马谷，都已成为国际滑雪游客的主要目的地，许多人会停留更久，并且在住宿、装备、餐饮和地方商品上消费更多，那些消费将有助于抵消中国旅游团的减少，虽然这两种市场贡献日本经济不同部分，也不一定可以互换。

除了远程市场外，奥查得说，另外还有一个条件也支持了这种变化，那就是日圆的汇率。2026年美元与日币的兑换大约维持在155-162日币兑换1美元左右，那支持了一个重要的高消费市场群体，但这种优势并不是能保证的，未来日圆汇率的浮动都可能影响远程游客的消费并带来另一种不确定性。

他说，2026年另一个值得注意的因素是日本正在改变的免税购物制度。这个即将实施的改革将取消每日50万日圆消耗品的限额，并将退税流程改为在机场办理，目的是要遏制批量采购和转售行为，但这种改变可能对高消费国际游客造成意想不到的结果，他们可能必须在离境前办理退税，如果没有正确完成这个程序，他们有可能失去退税。

“所以我会将这种更广泛的转变形容为是日本在改变对中国的风险敞口，而不是终止那种依赖。中国依然是一个重要的市场来源，一些商业仍然高度依赖中国游客。改变的是日本吸纳那个市场衰退的能力，同时仍然能维持强劲的整体旅游消费，”奥查得说，日币越来越学习到来自不同国际游客的价值，尤其是那些能停留更久、消费更多的群体。

**日本经验可参考**

至于除了奥查得在文章里提到也同样受到中国经济报复的帕劳和韩国，另一个亚洲邻居台湾也经常面对北京当局各种不同的压力，他们是否也能以类似日本透过不同市场来抵消中国的经济胁迫，奥查得告诉美国之音，他认为其他邻居也能通过分散旅游市场来减少对中国经济胁迫的脆弱性，“但是没有一个单一模式能适用于所有人。每一个邻居都必须从它吸引国际游客的基础来构建，并从这些强项开展一个更广大的客源。”

他以菲律宾为例表示，菲律宾可以持续通过建设其度假村、海滩及其强大的酒店服务，持续吸引来自全世界的游客；韩国有不同优势，例如其美容和娱乐业；泰国已在医疗旅游方面确立了一个稳固的地位；台湾也能采取类似的策略，利用其美食、自然环境及独特的文化来吸引更多游客。

“日本的经验显示，多元化并不意味着要排除中国游客。它的意思是要确保中国游客的减少不会自动成为一个更广泛的经济冲击。如果一个国家的旅游业已不同原因吸引更多不同市场的游客，它就有更多空间来吸纳任何一个市场突然的减少。”他说。

奥查得最后表示，旅游业只是整个策略的一部分，旅游业更大的韧性不一定能减少其他经济领域上对中国依赖的脆弱性，因此旅游业的多元化应该被视为是更广泛韧性策略的一部分。

“目标未必是要摆脱对中国的依赖，而是要避免在任何单一市场上的过度依赖，以至于一旦在那个市场发生动荡就产生不成比例的经济影响。”他说。

中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆上星期在北京再次表示，高市早苗的“涉台错误言行”是当前中日关系面临困难的最大症结。他要求日方遵守日中四个政治文件精神，为两国关系重回正轨创造条件。

# 中国希望伊朗战争结束，但不是以特朗普想要的方式

图像来源，BBC / Getty Images

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 萨伊德·贾法里（Saeed Jafari）
    *   Role, BBC政治分析员

     和
    *   Author, WSL Global Journalism

*   Published 2026年9月23日 最近更新： 7 小时前
*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

在中国国家主席习近平对美国进行备受瞩目的访问前几天，北京接待了伊朗外长阿巴斯·阿拉格齐（Abbas Araghchi），这也提醒外界，中国对德黑兰具有一定影响力。

预料伊朗战争将是周四特朗普与习近平会晤时的主要议题之一。

自伊朗战争七个月前爆发以来，中国一直维持一贯立场。北京谴责美国和以色列对伊朗的攻击，以及华盛顿对德黑兰实施的制裁。与此同时，中方亦多次呼吁结束战争，尤其要求重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。

凭藉庞大的石油储备和能源多元化策略，中国至今相当顺利地抵御了伊朗战争带来的冲击。

英国埃克塞特大学（University of Exeter）中国与中东问题专家李安风（Andrea Ghiselli）表示，中国可以在目前的处境下维持更长时间，但经济成本只会愈来愈高。

不过他说，中国既希望战争结束，也需要在这一利益与其他地缘政治考量之间取得平衡。

“中国不希望这场冲突成为中美关系中的一个麻烦因素”，但同时也“不会损害伊朗的核心利益和诉求”，李安风博士说。

他解释：“伊朗和中国的立场大致一致，双方都认为，美国和以色列的侵略性行动是这场冲突爆发并持续至今的原因。”

## 能源与经济

国际危机组织（International Crisis Group）的哈米德雷扎·阿齐兹（Hamidreza Azizi）表示，作为能源消费国，中国会因战争持续而“受到损害”。

根据美国能源信息署2025年的一份报告，石油约占中国能源消耗总量的五分之一，但其中超过70%依赖进口。

中国去年每日进口约140万桶伊朗石油，只占其原油进口量的12%。相比之下，中东其他地区占42%，远高于伊朗。

中国已经能够以俄罗斯、巴西和其他出口国的供应，取代部分原本来自伊朗和其他海湾产油国的石油。不过，要替代从该地区购入的天然气，就困难得多。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，中国希望霍尔木兹海峡重新开放，因为战争前中国高度依赖来自中东的石油。

中国庞大的石油储备协助其承受战争造成的能源冲击。中国的石油储备规模仍属国家机密，但外界估计，2025年的储量介乎10亿至14亿桶。

美国哥伦比亚大学（Columbia University）中国能源研究员邓丽嘉（Erica Downs）说：“如果中国在战争开始时约有14亿桶石油库存，按照2025年的水平计算，足以应付254天从中东进口的石油。”

她补充，由于战争期间仍有部分中东石油运抵中国，中国的石油储备实际上可能可以维持得更久。

不过，路透社亚洲大宗商品专栏作家克莱德·拉塞尔（Clyde Russell）的数据显示，过去四个月中，中国有三个月需要动用石油储备，当中包括8月。

邓丽嘉博士说：“北京大概希望早一点而不是迟一点停止动用库存，从而保留相当规模的缓冲空间。”

如果获伊朗支持的胡塞武装加强对沙特阿拉伯的攻击，并进一步控制曼德海峡，全球能源市场可能变得更加波动。

伊朗战争带来的经济困境甚至可能引发全球经济危机，这对依赖出口的中国经济而言将是坏消息。

自2019年以来，中国经济增长一直放缓。这个全球第二大经济体正面对房地产危机、与西方的贸易摩擦，以及地方政府债务上升等问题。

因此，根据总部位于华盛顿的智库战略与国际研究中心（Center for Strategic and International Studies）的数据，去年净出口占中国国内生产总值增长的32.7%，是1997年以来最高水平。由于国内消费仍然疲弱，出口已成为推动经济增长的主要引擎。

## 制裁、海上封锁和谈判

随着战争陷入僵局，特朗普政府继续加大对德黑兰的经济压力。华盛顿警告，支持伊朗经济的企业、银行和国家可能面临次级制裁。

到目前为止，尽管美国已制裁数间中国公司和实体，但仍没有对中国主要银行采取行动。在美中贸易紧张关系仍然高企之际，华盛顿在这方面一直保持审慎。

北京并未公开同意华盛顿要求其加入对伊朗金融施压行动的要求。中方表示反对“非法单边制裁”，并称中国与伊朗的合作是在国际法框架内进行。

图像来源，Handout/Houthi Military Media Centre via EPA

图像加注文字，伊朗支持的胡塞武装正在加强对曼德海峡的控制，这是另一个重要的全球航运通道。

伊朗问题分析员阿齐兹表示，中国不太可能因为美国施压而停止购买伊朗石油。

他说：“中国人不希望开创一个先例，让美国可以透过施压，迫使中国企业和银行执行美国的政策。”

不过，美国的海上封锁已严重限制伊朗向中国买家输送石油的能力。

路透社报道，伊朗3月每日出口200万桶石油，但到8月已跌至每日22万至25.5万桶。自美国7月14日恢复海上封锁后，再没有伊朗原油成功穿越霍尔木兹海峡并抵达中国。

美国乔治华盛顿大学（George Washington University）伊朗问题专家穆罕默德·盖迪（Mohammad Ghaedi）表示，如果封锁持续，伊朗与中国之间的贸易将愈来愈局限于陆路运输，但陆路运输成本更高，出口能力也远低于海运。

中国希望减轻金融制裁所造成的影响，并不代表它有能力或有意愿挑战海上封锁。突破这类封锁可能令北京与华盛顿陷入程度截然不同的对抗。目前没有迹象显示中国领导层准备承受这种代价。

李安风博士说，中国已清楚表明“倾向透过谈判结束战争”，并补充指，中国很可能会阻止伊朗进一步升级冲突。

他说：“中国有能力，也可能协助重启谈判。它甚至可能向伊朗施压，要求作出一些让步，令特朗普总统能够宣称取得某种胜利，并以此作为结束战争的理由。”

不过他说，中国会要求协议为其伙伴伊朗带来实质利益，例如解除制裁、重新取得被冻结的资金，以及停止军事攻击。

## 特朗普迎接习近平开展对美国事访问 贝森特宣布两国贸易战继续“停火”

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，习近平时隔11年的首次对美国事访问实际将逗留不到两天。

Published 2026年9月23日

最近更新： 3 小时前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）亲自迎接中国国家主席习近平，象征习近平三天访美行程开始。

习近平的中国国际航空公司专机星期三（9月23日）美东夏令时间约17:40（格林尼治标准时间21:40；北京时间24日星期五05:40）降落位于美国首都华盛顿市郊的安德鲁斯联合基地（Joint Base Andrews）。

特朗普与夫人梅拉尼娅（Melania Trump）迎接习近平与彭丽媛伉俪下机。现场先后由美军仪仗队演奏中美两国国歌，并鸣放礼炮。一架B-1轰炸机飞越上空。

视频加注文字，直播回放：特朗普迎接习近平抵达华盛顿

视频加注文字，习近平访美晤特朗普：中美竞赛谁领先？美国民众怎么看？

中国官方新华社报导，[习近平抵达后发表“书面讲话”](https://www.xinhuanet.com/politics/leaders/20260924/ac4faf2186f54d6fa24cce7c41318195/c.html)，提到中美两国“应该成为伙伴而不是对手，实现中华民族伟大复兴和让美国再次伟大，完全可以并行不悖、相互成就、造福世界”。

习近平说：“中美双方应该相向而行，推动形成合作为主、竞争有度、分歧可控、和平可期的稳定关系，走出一条新时代中美两个大国正确相处之道。我对此抱有信心。”

据美方公布行程，特朗普将于星期四（24日）早上在白宫给习近平举行正式欢迎仪式，两人将紧接举行会谈，话题预计将包括中美两国人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）竞争、台湾问题、关税与伊朗局势等。

特朗普还将为习近平一行设宴，习近平一行将在星期五（25日）参观美国国家档案馆（National Archives）后结束访美返华。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，空军基地的简单欢迎仪式上，一架B-1轰炸机飞越上空。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，一些关注中国人权团体成员到习近平下塌酒店外抗议。

图像来源，China News Service

图像加注文字，中国官方媒体称，习近平受到美国华侨华人和留学生代表“热烈欢迎”。

视频加注文字，白宫“特习会”上演在即，外界则关注北京是否改变中美互动形式，对台军售已成为美中博弈下的交易筹码？

就在习近平一行下机之际，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）宣布，美国和中国将把两国贸易战的休战期延长至明年1月。

贝森特在与中国国务院副总理何立峰会面后接受福克斯新闻（Fox News；霍士新闻）访问时表示，双方已同意延长所谓的“釜山协议”，彼此降低对对方征收的关税，而该协议原定于11月10日到期。

他表示，双方还讨论了两国最终是否能达成一项更具实质性的贸易协议。

他说：“我不知道是否能达成一项更大的协议。我不知道我们是否只会延续目前的协议。”

## 白宫习特会，排场会否盖过实质内容？

**BBC北美编辑莎拉·史密斯（Sarah Smith）**

图像来源，Reuters

特朗普给习近平铺上了红地毯——无论是字面上还是象征意义上都是如此。白宫已为他的到访重新粉饰，行程还将包括一场盛大的国宴。

这次峰会有可能场面胜过实质内容。

习近平将要求特朗普进一步推迟向台湾出售价值数十亿美元武器的计划。

双方都希望延长贸易战休战期，以避免重回极高的贸易关税。但中国似乎未有履行增加购买美国农产品及向美国出售更多稀土矿物的承诺。

当然，最有可能主导讨论的议题是人工智能。尽管业界近期曾就 AI 的潜在风险发出警告，但双方不太可能同意制定新的规则或保障措施，以减缓这项技术的发展。

特朗普总统已将这些忧虑斥为“骗局”，而两国正竞相争取在这个领域取得主导地位。

但双方可能会同意建立一套机制，以便在这项技术失控时向对方发出警告。

结尾 Instagram 帖子

## “贸易战休战”——习特会前的好消息

**BBC商业记者彼得·霍斯金斯（Peter Hoskins）**

图像来源，Reuters

即使特朗普与习近平之间的峰会尚未正式展开，美国财长贝森特已为他的上司带来一些初步的好消息——我们得知双方已达成协议，延长贸易战休战安排。

这项协议于去年生效，原定于11月到期，现将至少延长至1月10日。

此前，中国国务院副总理何立峰于周末在纽约，以及星期三在华盛顿，与美方进行了长时间会谈。

为了实际上只是将问题押后处理而耗费如此长时间，这正在证明全球两大经济体之间的谈判极为棘手。

特朗普于2025年升级与北京的贸易战，似乎相信自己握有胜算，因此推出一连串关税措施。

但中国随后采取一系列反制措施，包括限制关键稀土出口，造成重大冲击，使两国陷入僵局。

如今的问题是，当两位领导人于星期四坐下来会谈时，是否能取得任何真正的进展。

summary: 在中国国家主席习近平抵达华盛顿，对美国进行国事访问之际，美国众议院两个委员会致函行政部门，要求对与中国共产党(CCP)有关联的多个非盈利组织展开调查。 众议院中国问题特设委员会主席，共和党众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)和同为共和党籍的众议院筹款委员会主席杰森·史密斯(Jason Smith)星期二(9月22日)[联名致信](https://files.constantcontact.com/f0eecb46901/2e1ce56f-1f5d-4719-b
content:
在中国国家主席习近平抵达华盛顿，对美国进行国事访问之际，美国众议院两个委员会致函行政部门，要求对与中国共产党(CCP)有关联的多个非盈利组织展开调查。

众议院中国问题特设委员会主席，共和党众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)和同为共和党籍的众议院筹款委员会主席杰森·史密斯(Jason Smith)星期二(9月22日)[联名致信](https://files.constantcontact.com/f0eecb46901/2e1ce56f-1f5d-4719-ba15-50bd6836b061.pdf)美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)和国税局(IRS)局长弗兰克·比西尼亚诺(Frank Bisignano)，要求两个部门采取行动，制止中共破坏美国的行动。

“我们致函对中国共产党正开展一项旨在破坏美国人工智能基础设施建设的影响力行动表达关切，”联名信说。

“随着人工智能在全球范围内加速发展，美国必须继续保持其作为该技术投资与开发首选地的地位。部署人工智能基础设施的竞争具有重大的经济和军事影响。我们绝不能允许对手——同时也是我们在人工智能基础设施领域最主要的竞争对手——将我们的税收法规武器化，从而损害美国这一新兴产业，”联名信又指出。

众议院筹款委员会今年2月曾就外国势力对美国免税部门的影响举行了听证会。委员会主席史密斯同时致函“人民论坛”(The People's Forum)、“突破新闻”(BreakThrough News)及“三大陆社会研究所”(Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research)，要求这些组织提供相关文件，并对它们在美国的免税资格提出了严重质疑。

这些组织被指属于一个由一位居住在中国、并与中国共产党关系密切的美国科技大亨内维尔·罗伊·辛格姆(Neville Roy Singham)资助、并与中国共产党有关联的非营利组织网络。

美国发展人工智能，需要在全国各地建造许多数据中心，但这却是一个争议性极强的问题。许多数据中心选址附近的居民对新建数据中心持强烈反对的态度。有传言说，在反对兴建数据中心的声浪背后，就有这些与中共相关非盈利组织的资助和支持。

众院筹款委员会与特别委员会今年4月初就曾联名致函美国财政部和国税局，要求对那些代表中国共产党干预美国选举和政治、从而违反《国内税收法》关于禁止干预政治竞选之规定的免税组织展开调查。

“中国共产党一贯锁定我国国内引发公众热议的政治议题，并试图扭曲相关讨论。中共不仅企图左右这些议题的走向，使其结果有利于削弱美国相对于中国的实力，还力图加剧美国民众的分歧并破坏我们的公民议事进程，”穆勒纳尔和史密斯的联名信指出。

联名信指出，近期有报道披露了中国试图干预，且部分已成功干预美国数据中心建设相关讨论的证据，这并不令人意外。OpenAI发现两批源自中国，极有可能是“机器人农场”或自动化账号群的ChatGPT账号，这些账号因针对美国人工智能政策辩论开展隐蔽影响力行动而被封禁。

第一场抹黑行动被 OpenAI 称为“数据中心跟风潮”(Data Center Bandwagon)，其生成的社交媒体评论和图像声称数据中心建设推高了电价。第二场行动被称为“科技与关税”(Tech and Tariffs)行动，其生成的评论和图像批评美国的关税政策，称其意在主导科技竞争。

X平台今年8月宣布，约200个疑似来自中国机器人农场的账号一直在试图影响美国民众，挑动他们反对数据中心建设。

联名信援引比特币政策研究所(BPI)的一份独立报告显示，“社会主义与解放党”(PSL)在14个州发起了21项运动，导致了10项针对数据中心的暂停令、一项永久性禁令，以及4个数据中心项目被否决或取消。

PSL的背后是总部位于中国且与中国共产党立场一致的内维尔·罗伊·辛格姆所建立的非营利组织网络。他利用国会为鼓励美国慈善事业而设立的免税机制，通过空壳公司和一个匿名的“捐赠者建议基金”(donor-advised fund)，向美国的倡导团体输送了2.78亿美元资金。

“我们的税法不应成为外国资金针对美国人工智能基础设施发动虚假信息战的掩护。这是又一个令人震惊且危险的例证，展示了恶意外国行为体如何向美国输送资金，以推进中国共产党的利益，”联名信指出。

联名信说，美国民众有权知晓，哪些敌视美国的行为体正试图通过资助政策倡导活动和散布虚假信息，来破坏这些决策过程并左右基础设施的发展走向。

“因此，我们呼吁财政部及国税局展开调查，核实支持该网络的免税组织是否违反了其免税资格的相关规定，……其运作是处于真正的慈善目的，还是为了服务于亲外国势力的私人或政治利益。”

特朗普总统星期四将与来访的习近平展开会谈。特朗普表示，他将与习近平讨论人工智能，并表示美国目前在人工智能竞争中领先中国，但必须保持这一优势。

title: Trump pledges 'unmatched military might' against drug cartels at UNGA
summary: By REUTERS SEPTEMBER 23, 2026 01:17 US President Donald Trump vowed on Tuesday to reassert US dominance in the Western Hemisphere and to use "unmatched military might" against threats in the region as he gathered allies behind an expanding
content:
By REUTERS SEPTEMBER 23, 2026 01:17
US President Donald Trump vowed on Tuesday to reassert US dominance in the Western Hemisphere and to use "unmatched military might" against threats in the region as he gathered allies behind an expanding campaign against drug cartels.

Speaking to world leaders at the [UN General Assembly](https://www.jpost.com/international/internationalrussia-ukraine-war/article-909346), Trump cast drug cartels as "the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere" and urged a tougher response to transnational crime.

Later at UN headquarters, [Trump](https://www.jpost.com/american-politics/article-909341) met with leaders and foreign ministers from 14 Latin American and Caribbean countries that have signed up to the Shield of the Americas, an anti-cartel coalition launched by his administration. He called on the group to join the US in designating 24 narcotrafficking groups as threats to stability and impose sanctions on them.

The countries later issued a statement pledging to take steps toward such joint sanctions.

The US raid that captured Venezuelan leader [Nicolas Maduro](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-905225) and a subsequent oil deal with the interim government underscored the US willingness to act in the region, Trump told world leaders at the General Assembly.

US President Donald Trump participates in a Shield of the Americas event on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York City, US, September 22, 2026. (credit: Reuters/Kylie Cooper)

“Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, and if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States,” he said.

### **Trump revamps Monroe Doctrine**

Trump's National Security Strategy late last year set out plans for a revamped Monroe Doctrine, the 19th-century policy asserting US primacy across the Americas that critics have long associated with decades of American intervention. Trump himself has taken to calling it the "Donroe Doctrine," a play on his own name, after the phrase gained currency in conservative media.

Trump has also spoken, often in vague terms, of retaking the Panama Canal and annexing Greenland and Canada. On Tuesday, he signed an agreement on Greenland that stops short of his demand that the island become US territory to head off the growing Arctic presence of Russia and China.

Still, Trump's focus on the Western Hemisphere has raised concerns of a neo-colonial project.

[Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-904625) in his UN speech bristled at the approach, warning Latin America and the Caribbean countries of "renewed hegemonic temptations." "Brazil is nobody's backyard," Lula said.

### **Shield of the Americas**

The Shield of the Americas gathering was the latest US effort to rally Latin American nations behind a more aggressive approach that has included US military strikes on drug boats since last fall and greater cooperation with Latin American countries.

Trump launched the group in March, gathering more than a dozen regional leaders in Florida.

The coalition includes governments closely aligned with Trump, including countries like Argentina, Ecuador and El Salvador whose leaders Trump has either praised or endorsed as candidates. Colombia and Peru joined after Trump-aligned presidents took power in recent months.

Brazil and Mexico are among the countries that have not joined.

Since returning to power early last year, Trump has designated drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations and launched dozens of deadly strikes on boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that US officials say are carrying narcotics bound for the US. Rights groups have said the strikes, which have killed more than 220 people, amount to extrajudicial killings.

"For decades, other administrations allowed much of this region to be dominated by vicious gangs and bloodthirsty drug cartels, destabilized by uncontrolled migration, and infiltrated by hostile foreign adversaries – foreign sick, demented adversaries – but not anymore," Trump told the UN, adding that he was "reasserting American power" to make the region safer by taking out cartels.

“Like ISIS, they should be killed, exiled or detained as enemy combatants without the possibility of release,” Trump said, “which is what we're doing.”

Trump also touted his administration’s pressure campaign on Communist-run Cuba, accused its leaders of seeding “subversive and radical” left-wing groups in the United States, and said Secretary of State Marco Rubio was “deep into negotiations with Cuba.”

Drug cartels controlling territory in US neighbor Mexico were “unacceptable,” he said, insisting that the government there “must reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity.”

title: As Xi lands in Washington, Uyghurs and Tibetans press Trump for human rights showdown
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping Wednesday arrived in Washington as diasporic minority communities urged U.S. President Donald Trump to press him on human rights and religious freedom during their three-day summit. Trump's rare welcome for Xi (
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping Wednesday arrived in Washington as diasporic minority communities urged U.S. President Donald Trump to press him on human rights and religious freedom during their three-day summit.

Trump's rare welcome for Xi (RFA Video)

President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump met Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan on the tarmac [at Joint Base Andrews](https://www.rfa.org/english/china/2026/09/23/trump-xi-jinping-arrival-pictures/ "https://www.rfa.org/english/china/2026/09/23/trump-xi-jinping-arrival-pictures/") in Maryland. After their brief greeting, which included a military honor guard, the two leaders parted ways to make last minute preparations for a full slate of events scheduled for Thursday.

Experts expect that Trump will try to work with Xi on a variety of issues, with economic friction over tariffs, U.S. soybean exports, and supply chains taking center stage.

But minority advocacy groups have been calling on Trump to use the summit to spotlight Chinese government policies that they say perpetuate human rights abuses and genocide.

**Genocide unresolved**

Toward the end of Trump’s first term, the United States classified China’s actions and policies in Xinjiang – where over a million Uyghurs and other minorities have been subject to mass internment and forced labor – as a genocide. This designation was upheld during the Biden administration and into Trump’s second term.

The summit presents an opportunity for Trump and the U.S. government to raise the Uyghur genocide both publicly and in private, the World Uyghur Congress, or WUC, an exile group based in Munich, said in a statement.

“Xi’s visit to Washington is a strategic moment to move beyond words of condemnation on the Uyghur genocide,” said WUC President Turgunjan Alawdun in the statement. “The United States has been a strong and vocal ally to the Uyghur people, and Donald Trump has to use this opportunity to continue proving it.”

uyghur protest washington People hold up flags and signs during a protest in Washington, Feb. 5, 2023. The U.S. formally declared China's actions towards the Uyghurs as genocide in 2021. (Andrew Caballero Reynolds/AFP)

The East Turkestan Government-in-Exile, or ETGE, a Washington-based group that advocates for the independence of the Uyghur region, said in a statement that Trump should push Xi to end the genocide. East Turkestan is the preferred name for the region for diaspora and exile organizations.

President Trump “should make clear to Xi Jinping that genocide, colonial occupation, and the exploitation of our homeland cannot be separated from the strategic challenge China poses to the United States,” said ETGE President Mamtimin Ala in the statement. “Ending the genocide requires confronting the occupation that sustains it and supporting the restoration of East Turkistan’s national independence.”

**Cultural erasure**

Tibetan exile activists, meanwhile, urged Trump to raise the issue of Chinese authorities’ erasure of Tibetan culture.

“Since the two presidents are going to hold talks, I am appealing to President Trump, as the leader of a powerful country, to discuss with Chinese President Xi Jinping the strategies being pursued to infiltrate Tibet’s religion, culture, and language,” Lobsang Shastri, a Tibetan scholar, told RFA.

free-tibet-us-capitol Protesters unfurled a "Free Tibet" banner near the U.S. Capitol building in Washington on Sept. 22, 2026, ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's arrival on the 23rd. (Students for Free Tibet)

“I am appealing to President Trump to raise the issue of resuming dialogue between China and Tibet,” Nyima Lhamo, the niece of renowned Tibetan Buddhist leader and political prisoner Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, who died in Chinese custody in 2015, told RFA.

“I call for an end to the ongoing destruction of Tibet’s religion and culture, and urge the release of all political prisoners, including the Panchen Rinpoche,” she said, referring to the Panchen Lama, the second most important figure in Tibetan Buddhism.

The current Panchen Lama recognized by Tibetans is Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, who was at the age of six forcibly disappeared by Chinese authorities in 1995. His whereabouts remain unknown.

Following his disappearance, the Chinese government installed their own Panchen Lama, and this represents a “terrible violation against all of Tibetan Buddhism,” Asif Mahmood, the Chair of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom, or USCIRF, told RFA.

An RFA cartoonist's rendition of what the 11th Panchen Lama, last seen in 1995 when he was six years old, might look like on his 30th birthday, April 25, 2019. (RFA)

Tibetan Buddhists “should have, under international standards, the religious freedom to select their own leaders, free from the interference of the Chinese Communist Party,” said Mahmood. “This terrible situation facing the disappeared Panchen Lama, and indeed all Tibetan Buddhists, is why USCIRF has urged President Trump to directly advocate for freedom for Gedhun Choekyi Nyima and his family.”

**Breaking with precedent**

During previous visits of Chinese leaders to Washington, the U.S. President’s formal welcome had traditionally happened at the White House. That Trump is going to Andrews to meet Xi upon arrival is an indication of the high level of importance of U.S.-China relations to the administration.

Both leaders believe that a stable relationship between the two countries is a priority, Bonnie S. Glaser, a U.S.-China-Taiwan relations scholar and director of the German Marshall Fund, told RFA.

“They don’t want to see a rupture that could have negative consequences for their respective countries,” she said. “Both of them want to see that the problems in the relationship are managed, that things don’t spin out of control.”

china-usa President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping shake hands at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, China, Nov. 9, 2017. (Damir Sagolj /Reuters)

The summit will kick into high gear Thursday where the two leaders are expected to discuss artificial intelligence governance and security issues, including arms sales to Taiwan, and, Glaser said, they will likely discuss extending a trade truce – a temporary halt to escalating tariffs by Trump and retaliatory moves by Beijing – which they negotiated during a meeting in South Korea last year.

“The truce does not expire until November. So it remains unclear whether the two sides will actually announce an extension at this upcoming summit,” she said. “However, it has been reported that the United States wants a six-month extension of the truce and that China would like to extend it through the end of the Trump administration.”

Following the summit meeting, a state dinner is on the schedule for Thursday evening, and Xi will return to China on Friday.

_**Edited by Eugene Whong. Additional reporting from Washington by RFA Uyghur, RFA Tibetan and RFA Mandarin.**_

title: Trump to raise detainees with Xi, but other rights issues may not come up
summary: * Summary * Rights groups, Democrats press Trump to raise Tibet, Uyghur rights * White House says Trump will discuss detainees but does not say whether human rights will come up * China warns discussion of democracy, human rights are a 'red
content:
*   Summary

*   Rights groups, Democrats press Trump to raise Tibet, Uyghur rights
*   White House says Trump will discuss detainees but does not say whether human rights will come up
*   China warns discussion of democracy, human rights are a 'red line'

WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - President [Donald Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/donald-trump/) ​is expected to press Chinese leader [Xi Jinping](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/xi-jinping/) to free two US citizens held by China, but it is not clear whether other ‌human-rights issues will get similar attention during this week's summit.

In a preview of Xi's visit last Friday, a US official said Trump is likely to bring up cases of people wrongfully detained in China with Xi. However, the White House has not said whether Trump will directly raise broader rights issues related to Tibet, the Uyghur Muslim minority group, and the ​country's new "ethnic unity" law.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fus%2Ftrump-raise-detainees-with-xi-other-rights-issues-may-not-come-up-2026-09-23%2F)

Trump has made winning freedom for Americans held overseas a priority, including in China, advocates say.

But the Republican leader has largely ​avoided talking about China's rights record, and has not publicly [brought up](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-welcome-saudi-crown-prince-with-offer-fighter-jets-business-deals-2025-11-18/) rights issues when meeting other world leaders like Israeli ⁠Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Trump will ask Xi to free Youlin Chen, a Chinese-born expert ​on North Korean nuclear tests who has been imprisoned since late 2024, and Min Zin, a scholar arrested in June, [according](https://www.reuters.com/3fec1b0a85a0/world/china/wife-us-seismologist-held-china-says-trump-will-ask-xi-free-him-2026-09-23/) to Chen's wife, Yufang Rong. Both ​are US citizens. Trump raised Chen's case when he met Xi in Beijing in May but nothing has happened since then, she said.

"We hope to see Dr. Chen and Zin come home after this meeting," said Elizabeth Richards, research director of the James Foley Foundation, a hostage advocacy group.

Human rights groups and Democratic lawmakers say Trump must also press Xi on ​China's treatment of Tibetans and Uyghurs and speak up for Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters.

Democrats in Congress say Trump is soft-pedaling human rights concerns and taking a ​transactional approach to international affairs.

"We cannot abandon human rights in our foreign policy," Democratic Representative Jim McGovern of Massachusetts said on Wednesday. "China's record is beyond debate and it is atrocious."

Item 1 of 2 U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping react as they hold a bilateral meeting at Gimhae International Airport, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, in Busan, South Korea, October 30, 2025. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein/File Photo

**[1/2]**U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping react as they hold a bilateral meeting at Gimhae International Airport, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, in Busan, South Korea, October 30, 2025. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-donald-trump-meets-with-chinese-president-xi-jinping-on-the-sidelines-of-the-apec-summit-in-busan/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX1JDMjRNSEFPSEVVOA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Beijing has ‌signaled that ⁠the topic will be off limits. The country's ambassador to the US warned on Wednesday that democracy and human rights are ["red lines"](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-us-ambassador-warns-red-lines-ahead-trump-xi-meeting-2026-09-23/) that cannot be crossed.

Human rights groups say China has [detained Uyghurs](https://www.reuters.com/article/world/un-calls-on-china-to-free-uighurs-from-alleged-re-education-camps-idUSKCN1LF1EP/) on the pretext of countering extremism and confined them in re-education camps. US secretaries of state from both parties have labeled the [treatment of Uyghurs as genocide](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-responsible-uyghur-genocide-unofficial-tribunal-says-2021-12-10/).

"Xi's visit to Washington is a strategic moment to move beyond words of condemnation on the Uyghur genocide," World Uyghur Congress President Turgunjan Alawdun ​said.

China's embassy in Washington did not ​respond to a request for comment. ⁠Beijing says it has established "vocational training centers" to curb extremism and denies abuse allegations.

Rights groups and exiles also routinely describe China's rule in Tibet as "oppressive," an accusation that Beijing rejects. China has exerted greater control over the region since Xi ​became chief of the Communist Party in 2012.

Beijing says Washington should stop using "Tibet-related issues to interfere in China's internal ​affairs."

The International Campaign for ⁠Tibet called on Trump to ask Xi "to resume substantive dialogue without preconditions" with the [Dalai Lama](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-reiterates-backing-tibetan-aspirations-preserve-culture-after-man-set-himself-2026-07-08/), the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhists and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate. The State Department reiterated calls for such dialogue when a Tibetan American [died](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/tibetan-man-dies-after-setting-himself-fire-near-un-headquarters-activists-say-2026-07-03/) after setting himself on fire in July.

China passed a [law](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-set-pass-new-ethnic-minority-law-prioritise-use-mandarin-language-2026-03-12/) this year to create a shared national identity ⁠among the ​country's 55 ethnic minority groups, which includes penalties for people outside the country for "inciting ethnic separatism."

The ​State Department calls the law problematic. Katie LaRoque, director for policy and advocacy at Freedom House, urged Trump to condemn the legislation himself.

"President Trump must make clear that Beijing’s domestic law has no ​jurisdiction over those exercising their fundamental freedoms on US soil," she said.

Reporting by Kanishka Singh, Jonathan Landay and Patricia Zengerle; editing by Andy Sullivan and Alistair Bell

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Kanishka Singh is a breaking news reporter for Reuters in Washington DC, who primarily covers US politics and national affairs in his current role. His past breaking news coverage has spanned across a range of topics like the Black Lives Matter movement; the US elections; the 2021 Capitol riots and their follow up probes; the Brexit deal; US-China trade tensions; the NATO withdrawal from Afghanistan; the COVID-19 pandemic; and a 2019 Supreme Court verdict on a religious dispute site in his native India.

Patricia Zengerle has reported from more than 20 countries, including Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and China. An award-winning Washington-based national security and foreign policy reporter who also has worked as an editor, Patricia has appeared on NPR, C-Span and other programs, spoken at the National Press Club and attended the Hoover Institution Media Roundtable. She is a recipient of the Edwin M. Hood Award for Diplomatic Correspondence.

title: US drafted a memo condemning UK over West Bank sanctions. It was never released
summary: WASHINGTON/JERUSALEM, Sept 23 (Reuters) - In early September, US officials in Jerusalem and Washington prepared a draft statement attributed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemning plans by the UK, France and Canada to block imports fr
content:
WASHINGTON/JERUSALEM, Sept 23 (Reuters) - In early September, US officials in Jerusalem and Washington prepared a draft statement attributed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemning plans by the UK, France and Canada to block imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The September 8 dated document, previously unreported and which two sources ​said was driven by David Milstein, an influential aide to US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, proposed that Rubio describe the countries' [actions](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-announce-trade-ban-israeli-west-bank-goods-2026-09-08/) as a ‌series of hostile measures against Israel that contribute to antisemitism.

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

"These tactics unacceptably draw from the playbook of the antisemitic boycotts, divestments and sanctions movement," the draft document, reviewed by Reuters, said.

The statement was never released.

According to three people familiar with the matter, the statement was not supported by the White House and the State Department's senior leadership.

The people spoke on condition of anonymity.

Instead, speaking to reporters on September ​8 in Florida before traveling to Latin America, Rubio refrained from outright criticism of the decision or any particular country.

"Obviously, we’re not going to do what the ​UK did. We saw their announcement today, but I don’t have any comment on it right now," Rubio said.

The episode illustrates a ⁠widening divide between the White House and Trump's senior diplomats in Israel about how best to respond to the expansion of Israeli settlements under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing ​government.

It also highlights a growing ideological split within the American right over support for Israel, with polling showing younger Republicans holding an increasingly unfavorable opinion of Washington's closest Middle East ​ally.

President Donald Trump earlier this year expressed his opposition to settlement expansion, a growing source of friction with Israel's Arab neighbors, but his administration has put little pressure on Israel to change its policy.

That has at times put him at odds with Huckabee, a Baptist minister who is a staunch supporter of settlements and who refers to the West Bank by its biblical name, Judea and Samaria, ​a term used by the Israeli government but not formally adopted by the US.

Huckabee's aide Milstein last year advocated that the US impose sanctions on the entire International Criminal ​Court to convince it to drop war crimes charges against Israeli leaders over the Gaza war - a measure the Trump administration has yet to deploy.

In response to questions from Reuters, a senior US ‌official said ⁠the draft statement was not prepared in consultation with the State Department or White House.

The US embassy referred questions, including requests for comment from Huckabee and Milstein, to the State Department.

The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

## US PUBLIC SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL QUESTIONED

US public backing for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats. A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48% of voters and 66% of Democrats believe the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 16% and 20% when ​the question was first asked in 2017.

While ​large majorities of Republicans aged 50 and ⁠older view Israel positively, younger conservative Americans have grown more critical, a Pew Research Center poll from late March showed. Some 57% of Republicans aged 18-49 have an unfavorable opinion of Israel, up from 50% a year previously.

In December last year, Trump said that ​he and Netanyahu, whose government has overseen a rapid expansion of settlements, [did not](https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-says-he-netanyahu-dont-fully-agree-west-bank-2025-12-29/) fully agree on the West Bank following a ​meeting with the Israeli leader. ⁠That September, Trump said he would

[not allow, opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/nMT1ALTL2N3VC11Q1)
Israel to annex the territory.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since the 1967 Arab-Israeli War. The United Nations and most countries consider settlements to be illegal under international law governing military occupation. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.

Violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the territory has risen sharply this year, ⁠some of them ​emboldened by support from Netanyahu's right-wing government, which includes ministers who are themselves settlers.

Huckabee has publicly [condemned](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-envoy-huckabee-tells-israeli-settlers-not-take-palestinian-americans-land-2026-08-20/) the ​violence and called for perpetrators to be prosecuted. He has also said violent settlers were a minority and do not represent the wider settler community.

Some 500,000 Israeli settlers and 3 million Palestinians live in the West Bank, ​territory Palestinians have long sought for a future state, along with Gaza and East Jerusalem.
