Humeyra Pamuk is a senior foreign policy correspondent based in Washington DC. She covers the U.S. State Department, regularly traveling with U.S. Secretary of State. During her 20 years with Reuters, she has had postings in London, Dubai, Cairo and Turkey, covering everything from the Arab Spring and Syria's civil war to numerous Turkish elections and the Kurdish insurgency in the southeast. In 2017, she won the Knight-Bagehot fellowship program at Columbia University’s School of Journalism. She holds a BA in International Relations and an MA on European Union studies.

Alexander has over a decade of international reporting experience. He is currently a senior correspondent in Jerusalem covering Israel & the Palestinian Territories and was formerly in Dubai where he covered the Arabian Peninsula, including the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Yemen, often writing about foreign policy, security and economic-related issues.

title: 美中峰会之际，参院共和党人敦促特朗普政府加速对台军援
summary: 国会山 — 美中领导人峰会即将举行之际，多位美国国会共和党参议员敦促特朗普政府尽快提供数十亿美元对台安全援助。与此同时，多位国会两党议员对美国之音(VOA)表示，美国对台政策目前并未改变，支持台湾维持自身防卫能力仍是华盛顿的重要议题。 来自肯塔基州的资深共和党联邦参议员米奇·麦康奈尔(Mitch McConnell)率领多名参议院共和党议员，于9月23日[致函](https://www.mcconnell.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/7e59
content:
国会山 —

美中领导人峰会即将举行之际，多位美国国会共和党参议员敦促特朗普政府尽快提供数十亿美元对台安全援助。与此同时，多位国会两党议员对美国之音(VOA)表示，美国对台政策目前并未改变，支持台湾维持自身防卫能力仍是华盛顿的重要议题。

来自肯塔基州的资深共和党联邦参议员米奇·麦康奈尔(Mitch McConnell)率领多名参议院共和党议员，于9月23日[致函](https://www.mcconnell.senate.gov/public/_cache/files/7e598414-830d-4c4e-a105-ef9c2d3809be/97114AC268A93E3B63F76A7EEAE1B077519CE0C50CE8772CD641EC1D8B27163C.letter-taiwan.pdf)国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)和战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)，呼吁行政部门尽快释放数十亿美元对台外国军事融资（Foreign Military Financing，FMF）。参与联署的共和党参议员包括来自德克萨斯州的约翰·科宁(John Cornyn)、来自阿拉斯加州的丽莎·穆尔科斯基(Lisa Murkowski)和来自北卡罗莱纳州的汤姆·蒂利斯(Thom Tillis)等。

“我们谨致函，表达我们对以下事项的关切：国务院拟不动用国会在2026财年为台湾拨付的3亿美元对外军事融资(FMF)资金；国防部未能动用2026财年为‘台湾安全合作倡议’(TSCI)拨付的10亿美元资金；以及本届行政当局决定暂缓批准一项总额140亿美元对台湾的对外军事销售(FMS)方案，”议员们在两页的信中说。

现年84岁的麦康奈尔为参议院拨款委员会国防小组委员会主席。议员们在信中对特朗普总统今年早些时候将台湾形容为“一个非常好的谈判筹码”一事表示担忧。唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)今年5月与中国国家主席习近平会面后，曾表示台湾问题涉及美中之间的谈判；目前，一项总额140亿美元的对台军售方案仍处于等待批准状态。

“很难想象，如果为了维持外交表面上的体面，就不得不拒绝向我们的伙伴提供关键的威慑能力，美国还能如何可信地在印度—太平洋地区投射影响力。”议员们在信中说。他们还提及，拜登政府曾在2021年与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)举行峰会前冻结一项原定向乌克兰提供的援助方案，并以此提醒特朗普政府考虑类似决定可能产生的后果。

议员们还表示，“单独来看，这些援助遭到延迟或拒绝的实例，正在考验我们之间的安全伙伴关系的牢固程度--而你们曾将这种伙伴关系形容为至关重要。”

“综合来看，尽管你们今年早些时候曾保证，在特朗普总统与习近平主席的会谈中台湾议题不在讨论之列，但这依然让我们对美国对亚洲及全球关键伙伴和盟友承诺的坚定程度产生了严重关切。”

国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)星期三在联合国大会期间接受媒体采访时表示，美国对台军售在一定程度上受到美国在世界其他地区的潜在军事需求以及国防工业基础的制约。

“人们认为……我们是在一个有限的视角下，仅仅从某一个特定地区来看待武器销售问题。实际上，其中很大一部分还涉及如何平衡我们的工业产能和国防工业基础，”卢比奥说。

“这并不是专门针对台湾而言的，而是说，当我们出售某种装备时，就意味着我们手头已经没有了，”卢比奥说。“我们未来可以补充，但目前手中没有。”

“所以，无论我们进行任何军售--不只是对台湾，而是对任何方面，我们始终都会权衡，一是我们自己在世界不同地区的军事需求，二是我们是否有能力出售某种装备，因为我们自己可能需要这些装备。因此，目前正在进行的就是这样一个评估过程，”卢比奥说。

随着美中领导人峰会临近，华盛顿对台政策是否会出现变化受到各界关注。对此，多位国会两党议员对美国之音表示，他们认为美国对台政策并未改变，对台湾的防卫支持依然十分重要，并已形成跨党派共识。

国会众议院台湾连线(Taiwan Caucus)共同主席、来自佛罗里达州的共和党联邦众议员马里奥·迪亚兹-巴拉特(Mario Diaz-Balart)星期二接受美国之音专访时表示，尽管美国国会内部存在诸多党派分歧，但在台湾议题上，两党始终保持着强有力的跨党派支持。

“美国与台湾之间的这种特殊关系，很大程度上建立在美国国会与台湾的关系之上，”迪亚兹-巴拉特议员说，“国会内部确实存在很多党派分歧，但在台湾问题上，两党一直拥有非常强有力的支持。我认为，这种两党支持是我们必须继续保持的重要基础。”

来自佛罗里达州的共和党联邦参议员里克·斯科特(Rick Scott)对美国之音表示，他认为特朗普政府的对台政策没有发生变化，并呼吁特朗普总统在与习近平会晤时明确重申华盛顿的立场。

“我们必须明确表示，我们将捍卫台湾的独立，”斯科特说。

众议院中国问题特设委员会主席、来自密歇根州的共和党联邦众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)对美国之音表示，特朗普总统目前对台湾提供的军事支持已经超过拜登政府任内的水平，美国对台政策并未发生改变。

“(对台政策)没有任何改变，就是维持台湾海峡的现状。我们，特朗普总统在其任期内提供的军事支持，比乔·拜登整个四年任期内提供的还要多。因此，从这个角度来看，他采取的行动极大地支持了台湾的自卫能力。而我们的政策正是为了确保台湾海峡的和平与航行安全。”

穆勒纳尔本月早些时候在一封致特朗普总统的信中，要求他拒绝中国干预美国对台武器出口以及美国与盟友安全合作的企图，同时肯定特朗普任内对台军售，并呼吁继续强化对中国的威慑。

“我对您的两次任期内向台湾出售美国军事装备创下历史纪录表示赞赏，并随时准备支持您继续努力，遏制中共煽动可能摧毁全球经济的军事灾难。”他写道。

除目前正在审议的140亿美元对台军售案外，特朗普政府去年12月还批准了一批总值约110亿美元的对台军售案。

来自纽约州的共和党联邦众议员麦克·劳勒(Mike Lawler)也认为，特朗普政府并没有改变美国长期以来的对台政策。

“不，我认为情况没有发生任何变化。我认为台湾显然是一个至关重要的合作伙伴。它是我们的第四大贸易伙伴。全球90%以上的先进半导体都是在台湾岛上制造的，”劳勒对美国之音说，“因此，我们要确保台湾的安全。我们要击退中国任何干涉台湾的企图。”

来自马里兰州的民主党联邦众议员约翰·奥尔谢夫斯基(John Olszewski)在接受美国之音采访时也表示，特朗普总统应该借着美中峰会的机会向中国表明美国不接受中国在印太地区咄咄逼人的军事行为。

“最近，中国对台湾采取了一系列令人担忧的侵略行为。我认为美国必须与我们的朋友站在一起，并向习主席明确表示，我们绝不会接受这些侵略行为，这些行为是不可接受的，”奥尔谢夫斯基说。

title: VOA专访遭中国“非法拘押”的华裔科学家陈友麟妻子：“有很多人在帮助你，你很快就能回来”

content:
被中国关押的美籍华裔地震学家陈友麟的妻子荣玉仿星期三(9月23日)在接受美国之音(VOA)专访时透露，白宫告诉她，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统将在本星期与中国国家主席习近平会面时提起她丈夫的案子。陈友麟在中国被拘押了600多天，目前面临间谍罪指控。美国政府认定他遭到非法拘押。

美中首脑峰会前夕，陈友麟(Youlin Chen)的妻子、同为地震科学家的荣玉仿(Yufang Rong)来到首都华盛顿，连日天来奔走于白宫、国务院以及国会等诸多机构，会晤这些机构的高层官员，呼吁他们进一步帮助陈友麟获释。

就在中国国家主席习近平抵达美国的几个小时前，荣玉仿接受了美国之音(VOA)专访。她表示，她的首要目标是希望特朗普总统第二次向习近平提起这个案件。

荣玉仿说：“我得到的保证是，他们(白宫)会再次提及此事。我们希望，随着他的名字再次被列出，两位元首能找到办法把这件事情解决。”

美国政府认定在美籍华裔科学家陈友麟在中国遭非法拘押，陈友麟的妻子荣玉仿到白宫与高层官员会面，呼吁中国释放丈夫。(照片摄于2026年9月22日，由荣玉仿提供)

今年5月，特朗普总统在访华期间，曾经跟习近平提起过陈友麟的案件。一直致力于帮助陈友麟获释的美国非营利组织Global Reach(意为“全球触及”)首席调查官、联邦调查局(FBI)前助理局长基兰·拉姆齐(Kieran Ramsey)7月中旬告诉美国之音，美国国务院一直在幕后悄然致力于解决此案，但是案件几个月来一直毫无进展。

荣玉仿告诉美国之音，她此行在与国会相关人士会谈时，他们也告诉她，陈友麟的案件是国会工作的“重中之重”。

荣玉仿强调，除了白宫和国会的支持外，国务院也向她传达了同样的信息。她说：“这些会面之后，我感觉挺有希望的。”

**陈友麟被拘押的原因可能与核探测工作有关**

陈友麟是一位居住马萨诸塞州波士顿的美国地震学家，曾和中国学者联合进行由美国政府资助、主要探测朝鲜地下核试验地震信号的公开研究项目。

2024年10月，陈友麟前往中国探亲。11月5日，陈友麟在准备飞回美国前，在北京首都国际机场被北京市国家安全局人员逮捕；中国在2025年5月1日正式指控他从事间谍活动。

荣玉仿表示，得知陈友麟的罪名时，她极度震惊。她告诉美国之音，在陈友麟长达二20多年的职业生涯中，他一直致力于对地球、地球波动及地震波进行公开透明的研究。他与世界各地的地震学家，尤其是中国的同行开展了广泛的合作。

荣玉仿说：“他的部分项目涉及利用地震数据探测核试验，例如如何分析地震仪接收到的波形，并区分信号究竟源自天然地震还是核试验。他不仅在国际期刊上发表了相关研究成果，还在国际会议上展示过。他从事这类研究已超过20年，此前从未有过任何迹象显示这项工作会给他带来麻烦。”

荣玉仿告诉记者，陈友麟经常往返于美中两国，他几乎每年都会参加许多中国的研讨会或学术会议，中国的同行们很喜欢邀请他去交流研究成果，而他也乐于与同行们分享研究成果。

荣玉仿透露说，他们怀疑导致陈友麟被拘押的原因是他从事的核探测相关工作。

Global Reach首席调查官拉姆齐7月中告诉美国之音，陈友麟的专长之一是通过分析地震数据来探测核试验，他的研究成果已公开发表，且“他从未隐瞒自己为此项工作接受了美国政府资助的事实”。

拉姆齐透露，美国政府指责中国利用了所谓的“解耦”(decoupling)技术(即在地下大型空腔中引爆装置，以掩盖核试验产生的地震波信号), 违反了《全面禁止核试验条约》(Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty)。

拉姆齐表示，陈友麟正是利用中国公开的数据揭示了朝鲜进行核试验的情况。但是，陈友麟却因此“身陷囹圄，面临着中国指控其为间谍的境遇”。

**遭拘押的第一年多时间里，陈友麟被审讯了100多次**

2026年3月，美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)将陈友麟认定为被非法拘押(Wrongfully Detained)的人员。目前美国有两位被国务院正式认定为遭中国非法拘押的学者，另外一位是[美籍缅甸裔学者敏辛](https://www.voachinese.com/a/voa-exclusive-interview-with-aung-maw-zin-about-min-zin-20260825/8190274.html)(Min Zin)。

Global React首席战略官、美国前国安官员埃里克·莱布森(Eric Lebson)星期三和荣玉仿同时接受美国之音采访时透露，截至2026年9月23日，陈友麟已经被中国政府拘押了686天，其家人至今还未能与陈友麟说上话。

莱布森告诉美国之音，在最初的434天里，陈友麟甚至不允许会见律师。在一年多的时间里，陈友麟因工作问题被审讯了100多次。

莱布森透露，陈友麟现在每个月得以与大使馆人员会面一次，时间大约半小时；妻子荣玉仿会给他写信，信先送到美国驻华大使馆，再由使馆人员会面时读给陈友麟听。

莱布森说，美国使馆人员朗读家人信件时，中国官员一直在场；之后，陈友麟可以口述回复内容，由使馆人员记录下来；但由于有中国官员在场，有些话陈友麟是不能说的。

莱布森说，陈友麟在信中“完全不能谈论他的案子”，也不得对妻子帮他聘请的中国律师、或者大使馆官员，及其他任何人透露案情。

**国会两院两党议员谴责中国非法拘押陈友麟和敏辛**

荣玉仿告诉美国之音，她最开始获知陈友麟被拘押的消息后，极度震惊，更是不愿接受现实。除了兼顾一份全职工作及其它志愿者工作外，荣玉仿家里还有一个高龄老母亲要照顾。

更糟糕的是，各项日常生活也受到极大影响。荣玉仿说：“我甚至无法登录银行账户或支付水电费、房贷等账单，因为这些账户都绑定了他的手机号码，而他的手机被中国政府没收了。”

她说：“随后我意识到必须采取行动，必须寻求帮助。”

除了联系Global Reach组织寻求帮助外，荣玉仿还联系了她所在州马萨诸塞州民主党籍联邦参议员爱德华·马基(Edward Markey)的办公室。她说：“马基参议员的办公室提供了很大帮助。”

马萨诸塞州民主党籍联邦参议员爱德华·马基(Edward Markey)在办公室与美籍华裔科学家陈友麟的妻子荣玉仿会面。(照片摄于2026年9月22日，由荣玉仿提供)

马基参议员7月14日在其官网发表[声明](https://www.markey.senate.gov/news/press-releases/senator-markey-statement-on-the-wrongful-detention-of-dr-youlin-chen)，指出陈友麟自2024年11月以来，“一直遭到中国政府的非法拘押”。

马基参议员称陈友麟是“一位杰出的地震学家，多年来一直与中国同行开展合作，其工作备受推崇”。

马基参议员强调陈友麟的“工作性质公开透明且属于学术范畴，相关成果均已公开发表并明确署名”，中国政府对待陈友麟的方式“不仅损害了(美中两国学者和研究人员)的伙伴关系，还可能阻碍其他学者与中国同行进行交流合作。”

另外，9月17日，马基参议员牵头，联袂北卡罗来纳州共和党籍联邦参议员泰德·巴德(Ted Budd)与犹他州共和党籍联邦参议员匡希恒(John Curtis)以及加利福尼亚州民主党籍联邦参议员亚当·希夫(Adam Schiff)[推出决议案](https://www.voachinese.com/a/bicameral-bipartisan-resolution-calls-for-release-of-americans-wrongfully-detained-by-china-20260918/8201601.html)，谴责中国共产党政府非法拘押美国学者，并敦促美国政府把包括陈友麟和敏辛在内的所有被中国非法拘押的美国公民平安返回当作优先事项。

该[决议](https://files.constantcontact.com/f0eecb46901/179d48cd-1178-4ed7-aafe-23d51b88511e.pdf)的众议院版本则由众议院中国问题特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)联袂马萨诸塞州民主党籍联邦众议员斯蒂芬·林奇(Stephen Lynch)、加利福尼亚州共和党联邦众议员金映玉(Young Kim)推出。

荣玉仿表示，她对决议案的提出深表感激。她说：“这种两党共识对我丈夫意义重大。这意味着尽管共和党和民主党在许多其它问题上存在分歧，但在‘美国公民不应在海外被非法拘押’这一特定问题上，双方立场一致。”

**妻子最担心陈友麟的健康问题**

荣玉仿告诉美国之音，美国大使馆官员在9月18日的探视后告诉她，陈友麟这个月大约瘦了30到40磅，“他吃不到有营养的食物。而且他有糖尿病、高血压和高胆固醇等健康问题”。

荣玉仿透露，美国领事官员转达陈友麟的话说，针对他的健康问题和失眠问题，监狱方面有为他提供药物，但是陈友麟不知道那些都是些什么药物。

当被问及是否有话要告诉特朗普总统，荣玉仿说，她和家人要感谢特朗普总统5月份在和习近平会晤时提到了陈友麟的名字。

她说：“我们知道，只要他亲自过问这类案件，美国公民就能平安回家。他上任以来已经让110多名美国公民重获自由。我对此深表感激。我非常希望能把友麟接回来。”

荣玉仿告诉美国之音，陈友麟遭拘押时，他们的儿子还是一名大学新生，如今儿子已经大三了，至今未能与父亲通上一次话。

荣玉仿鼓励陈友麟“要坚强、乐观，多锻炼身体，不必挂念家里”。

荣玉仿希望借美国之音的平台告诉丈夫：“我们正在为他的事全力奔走。有很多人在帮助他，他总有一天会回来的，而且很快就会回来。我们都很想念他！”

title: 特习会前瞻：双方致力稳定战略竞争关系，缓解贸易、科技和国际冲突分歧

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期四(9月24日)将与中国国家主席习近平在白宫举行峰会，并给予他国事访问的礼遇。此次峰会旨在管控这两大世界强国在贸易、科技以及全球冲突应对方式等领域激烈的竞争关系。

习近平将于星期三抵达华盛顿。这将是他自2013年出任中国国家主席以来第六次访美，也是自2015年以来首次对白宫进行国事访问。

特朗普在此次峰会上最重要的议题包括美国长期以来的对华贸易逆差，以及他力求在人工智能和半导体技术领域保持美国对华优势的努力。

白宫表示，特朗普将在习近平抵达安德鲁斯联合基地时亲自前往迎接他，随后将于星期四在白宫南草坪为他举行国事欢迎仪式。届时将有479名美军人员组成的仪仗队列队接受检阅，B-2“幽灵”轰炸机和F-22“猛禽”战斗机也将进行空中飞越表演。

两位领导人星期四举行的峰会结束后，特朗普总统与第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普(Melania Trump)将在白宫东厅为习近平及其夫人彭丽媛设国宴款待，随后于星期五上午在白宫红厅举行茶叙。此次访问将以两对夫妇参观华盛顿国家档案馆、阅览有关美中关系历史相关文件的方式结束。

特朗普上周五在白宫对记者发表讲话时表示，他预计与中国领导人的会晤将会“非常好”。他说，“我们与中国的关系进展顺利，习近平主席与我之间关系良好。”

美国礼宾司司长莫妮卡·克劳利(Monica Crowley)大使告诉《纽约邮报》，这场为期三天的盛会“彰显了我们双边关系的重要性，以及影响两国乃至全世界的战略议题”。

习近平稍早于5月在北京接待了特朗普，举行了两位领导人的上一次峰会。那次峰会展现了两位领导人融洽的个人关系，同时表达了建立“建设性的战略稳定关系”的愿望，尽管双方的主要分歧和紧张关系的根源仍未得到解决。

特朗普去年对中国进口商品加征关税，促使美国对华贸易逆差降至2020亿美元，创下2004年以来的最低水平。中国则采取反制措施，对美国进口商品加征关税。

美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)星期一在接受美国消费者新闻与商业频道(CNBC)采访时表示，2025年10月达成并将于今年11月10日到期的美中关税“休战”协议是他前一天在纽约与中国国务院副总理何立峰会晤时的“焦点”议题。这项休战协议使双方对彼此出口商品征收关税的水平受到限制，目前尚无有关该协议是否会延期的消息。

贝森特在谈及关税休战时表示，“自去年秋季以来，双方关系一直保持着极大的稳定性。我认为我们将继续维持这种状态。”

贝森特还表示，美中双方在星期日的会谈中同意将人工智能对话机制化，并“很可能”于两个月后在中国深圳就该议题再次举行会晤。

作为该对话的一部分，他表示美方希望与中国建立沟通渠道，以应对人工智能相关事件，并力求就人工智能带来的主要危险达成共识——“无论是失控的(人工智能)智能体……(还是)掌握生物武器的网络非国家行为体”。

一同出席周日会谈的美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)会后告诉记者，美方并未讨论针对向中国出口先进人工智能(AI)芯片及半导体制造设备的管制措施。

北京呼吁放宽美国的这些管制措施，同时也对中国出口至美国的稀土矿物实施了管制。这些矿物是工业制造的关键原材料。中国主导着这些矿物的全球供应链，而美国一直敦促北京放宽相关管制。

贝森特在接受采访时表示，他还与中方谈及了中国与伊朗伊斯兰共和国的密切关系。自今年2月与以色列联手针对该恐怖政权发起攻势以来，美国一直对伊朗实施严厉制裁。

特朗普7月在“真相社交”(Truth Social)平台发布的一则帖文中表示，习近平曾在5月的峰会上承诺，“在任何情况下”都不会向德黑兰提供或出售武器。次月，特朗普再次发帖警告称，向伊朗提供“任何形式的生命线”的“任何”国家，都将面临“巨大的经济后果”。尽管他未点名提及中国，但中国长期以来一直是伊朗石油的最大买家，而石油贸易正是该政权的主要收入来源。

对习近平而言，双边关系中最重要的分歧在于美国向台湾出售武器。台湾是一个自治的民主政体，也是美国的伙伴，但北京将其视为一个叛离省份。

中国长期以来一直要求美国停止对台湾不时进行的对台军售。特朗普在5月的峰会后告诉美国福克斯新闻台(Fox News)，他将一项拟议中价值140亿美元的对台军售案“暂时搁置”。他补充道，“这取决于中国。坦率地说，这对我们来说是一个非常好的谈判筹码。”

特朗普和习近平今年可能还有两次会晤机会：中国将于11月在深圳主办亚太经合组织(APEC)领导人会议，而美国将于12月在迈阿密主办二十国集团(G20)峰会。

title: 特朗普联合国演说五个要点：古巴垮台、摧毁伊朗、格陵兰基地，以及把AI改名SI

content:
视频加注文字，观看：特朗普威胁称，若无法达成协议，将把伊朗“彻底摧毁”

Published 2026年9月23日凌晨4点24分

阅读时间: 3 分钟

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）周二再次登上联合国（United Nations）的讲台，在世界各国领导人面前宣扬其政府的政策，并向在座的一些国家发出尖锐的威胁。

这篇冗长的演讲涉及面很广，涵盖伊朗战争、人工智能（AI）、古巴以及美国军队的角色等多重议题。

BBC采访这场演说的记者整理出当中五个尤其引人注目的关键时刻。

## 1. 特朗普大力宣扬美国实力

**_作者：北美编辑莎拉·史密斯（Sarah Smith），现场报道_**

美国总统对联合国并无太大敬意，他指责联合国推行极左议程，但他确实乐于利用这个全球性平台。

他利用周二的演说宣扬自己的政绩，并自称为和平缔造者，同时也发出多项尖锐威胁。

伊朗可能遭到彻底摧毁；针对涉嫌走私毒品的小型船只的致命打击将持续进行；古巴政权甚至可能被推翻。

他传达的信息十分明确：只要特朗普认为有必要维护美国国家利益，美国仍准备动用其军事力量。

特朗普表示，他正在“重振美国实力”，并展示他所称的美国“无可匹敌的军事力量”。

他说：“美国将不再容许任何对美国构成威胁的势力在西半球任何地方站稳脚跟。”

特朗普再一次向世界高调宣示“美国优先”。

## 2. 特朗普称古巴为“失败国家”，古巴代表离席抗议

**_作者：白宫记者伯恩德·德布斯曼（Bernd Debusmann Jr），现场报道_**

特朗普把矛头指向美国最接近的邻国之一古巴，称其为“一个彻底失败的国家”，并表示其政府一直在推动“从根本上改变古巴的局势”。

“它将会垮台，”他说。

随着特朗普继续发言，古巴代表团离开会场以示抗议。

过去一年来，这位美国总统对古巴共产主义政府的批评愈发强烈。周二，他表示该政权正承受“巨大压力”，并且“以前所未有的程度走向失败”。

然而，他并未详细说明古巴的变革将以何种形式呈现。

古巴外交部长对特朗普的言论作出愤怒回应，指责这位美国总统散播“谎言”。

布鲁诺·罗德里格斯（Bruno Rodriguez）在X平台上写道：“美国政府无法接受古巴是一个、并且有权成为一个完全主权和独立的国家的事实。”

视频加注文字，观看：古巴代表团在特朗普联合国演说期间离席抗议

## 3. 直接威胁“歼灭”伊朗

**_作者：BBC波斯语部驻华盛顿记者哈沙亚尔·乔内迪（Khashayar Joneidi）_**

特朗普在联合国大会上向伊朗提出一个严峻的选择：与华盛顿达成协议并重建国家，或面对伊斯兰共和国被迅速“彻底摧毁”的命运。

他随后再次预测，结束这场战争的协议很可能会在11月美国中期选举后达成。

他的言论展现出特朗普一贯的强制外交策略：在保持谈判大门敞开的同时，也以压倒性的武力相威胁。

但他的措辞模糊了摧毁政治体制与威胁伊朗国家本身之间的界线。

国际法专家此前曾对美国官员使用的、他们所称的“令人警惕的言论”表示忧虑，其中包括特朗普本人。他曾发文表示，美国可能会“彻底摧毁”伊朗的发电厂。

周二演讲中提到让伊朗“没有生存机会”、让其后代“没有希望”的说法，很可能引起类似的警觉。更具讽刺意味的是，这番警告是在联合国发表的，而这个组织正是为了使后代免受战争之害而成立。

然而，这场演说并非宣告外交努力已经失败。

相反，这是一次试图界定未来可能谈判条件的发言：美国仍准备达成协议，但前提是在生存威胁的阴影之下进行。

## 4. 特朗普盛赞新的格陵兰安全协议

**_作者：白宫记者伯恩德·德布斯曼（Bernd Debusmann Jr）在现场报道_**

特朗普还盛赞与格陵兰（Greenland）达成的一项新协议，他表示，根据该协议，美国将在这片北极领土上建设两座军事基地。

谈及这项协议时，他表示：“我们将完全有能力采取一切必要措施，保卫美洲大陆，同时也保卫欧洲。”这项协议是他于上周五首次公布的。

他补充说，这项协议将“大大加强”北大西洋公约组织（Nato，北约）这一防务联盟。

在特朗普发表演说后不久，美国、丹麦和格陵兰在联合国举行了联合签署仪式。

虽然格陵兰是一个享有高度自治的领土，但它仍属于丹麦王国的一部分，其外交政策主要由丹麦负责。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，特朗普在签署安全协议前与丹麦首相梅特·弗雷泽里克森（Mette Frederiksen）握手。

特朗普政府官员已将这项协议誉为一项能以最低成本提升美国安全、同时维持良好关系的成果。

然而，丹麦和格陵兰政府则希望，这项协议能够终结由来已久的争议。这场争议始于特朗普曾威胁以武力夺取格陵兰。

这项威胁曾动摇北约联盟，并严重考验美丹关系。

鉴于特朗普此前数月一直试图购买或吞并这个享有高度自治的领土，一些分析人士将这项协议视为外交斡旋的一次低调胜利。

视频加注文字，Watch: Moment Trump rebrands Artificial Intelligence to Super Intelligence

## 5. 人工智能的重命名尝试

**_作者：纳达·陶菲克（Nada Tawfik），驻联合国纽约记者_**

特朗普一向擅长品牌包装。在这次演讲中，他为人工智能（AI）取了一个新名字：“超级智能”（Super Intelligence）。

他说：“‘人工’（artificial）这个词听起来像是假的。但它并不假，实际上非常了不起。不过我们必须小心。”

“欢迎来到超级智能——SI——的新世界。”他补充道。

特朗普过去曾主张，美国必须在人工智能发展竞赛中占据领先地位。他上周曾表示：“谁赢得 AI，谁就赢得未来。”

这位总统坚决反对政府监管或设立新的安全护栏，而这一立场令他与许多出席联合国大会的人士意见相左。

对那些呼吁加强监管的人而言，问题在于外交协商和国际规范制定的步伐相对缓慢，是否能赶得上AI技术迅速发展的速度。

title: Race to evacuate war-damaged Gaza buildings after deadly apartment block collapse
summary: * Summary * Collapse of building in Gaza City left 21 dead * Evacuation order issued for 255 other buildings * Officials say risk increases as winter nears GAZA/CAIRO, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Officials in Gaza say plans to evacuate people from
content:
*   Summary

*   Collapse of building in Gaza City left 21 dead
*   Evacuation order issued for 255 other buildings
*   Officials say risk increases as winter nears

GAZA/CAIRO, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Officials in Gaza say plans to evacuate people from war-damaged buildings after the deadly collapse of an apartment block last week face major challenges, including a lack of demolition equipment and limited land to relocate residents.

Nearly a year since ​a ceasefire ended major fighting between [Israel and Hamas](https://www.reuters.com/world/israel-hamas/), officials say tens of thousands of people, with few options for shelter, are living in buildings damaged during Israel's military campaign, despite ‌repeated warnings that they should leave.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Frace-evacuate-war-damaged-gaza-buildings-after-deadly-apartment-block-collapse-2026-09-23%2F)

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

In the early hours of September 16, the danger became clear when the Al-Saada building in Gaza City's Al-Rimal neighbourhood [collapsed](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/war-damaged-gaza-building-collapses-killing-12-people-seeking-shelter-inside-2026-09-16/), killing 21 people. At least 45 survivors were rescued from the rubble.

Gaza officials say more than 2,000 buildings have been classified as being at risk. Other war-damaged buildings have [previously collapsed](https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/society-equity/gaza-struggles-pull-bodies-rubble-storms-rock-damaged-buildings-2025-12-15/), causing casualties, including amid winter storms.

"These buildings now represent ticking time bombs for residents and displaced people in many places," said Husni Muhanna, spokesperson for the Gaza City ​municipality, adding that this presented a "real danger" with the weather set to deteriorate into the winter.

On Sunday, Gaza authorities announced an emergency plan to evacuate people from 255 buildings most at risk of ​collapse and demolish them.

An Egyptian-led relief body had offered to provide transport to move those evacuated to designated shelters, said Ismail Al-Thawabta, head of the Hamas-run ⁠Gaza government's media office.

But he said the plan faced major obstacles, "including some families refusing to evacuate unsafe buildings despite the warnings, severe funding shortages, a lack of heavy equipment needed for safe demolition, and limited safe ​land available to relocate displaced people."

## SHORTAGE OF EQUIPMENT

Large-scale reconstruction in Gaza has yet to begin, with [US-brokered efforts](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/gaza-board-peace-official-says-plan-is-still-operative-2026-08-10/) to get Hamas to disarm and Israeli forces to withdraw largely stalled. A population of more than 2 million ​lives confined to about a third of the enclave, mainly housed in makeshift tents or overcrowded rooms in damaged buildings. Deadly [Israeli airstrikes](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-fire-kills-two-people-gaza-medics-say-2026-09-23/), which Israel says target militants, have continued.

Most of Gaza's buildings were destroyed by airstrikes or bulldozed by Israeli forces, and almost all others have suffered damage.

Palestinian and UN officials blame Israel's restrictions on Gaza for the lack of heavy machinery to clear rubble and materials and equipment to rebuild homes.

In response to a request for comment, Israel's military said it was ​committed to minimising harm to civilians and that any activities, including against "terrorist infrastructure", were carried out based on operational necessity.

Item 1 of 2 Palestinian children watch from a damaged house as rescuers work at the site of a nearby residential building that had been damaged in an earlier Israeli strike during the war and collapsed on Wednesday, in Gaza City, September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Mahmoud Issa

**[1/2]**Palestinian children watch from a damaged house as rescuers work at the site of a nearby residential building that had been damaged in an earlier Israeli strike during the war and collapsed on Wednesday, in Gaza City, September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Mahmoud Issa [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/war-damaged-building-collapses-in-gaza-city/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjhLTkFKQUNPSg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said entry of heavy equipment and reconstruction materials ​would not be authorised until Hamas disarmed. It said Hamas exploited humanitarian aid, something the Palestinian militant group denies.

Alessandro Mrakic, head of the United Nations Development Programme office in Gaza, said a shortage of equipment meant people had to dig ‌through the ⁠rubble with their hands when the Al-Saada building collapsed, and that oil and spare parts were needed to keep the machinery already in Gaza in service.

He estimated the number of buildings at risk of collapse at 400. "We know that these buildings will collapse, especially now with the upcoming winter," he said. "We are running against time."

## RESIDENTS SAY THEY HAVE NOWHERE ELSE TO GO

The Al-Saada building was in an area that was hit by Israeli bombardment two days after a Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, triggered Israel's offensive in Gaza. Israel launched heavy airstrikes followed by a ground campaign which it said were aimed at destroying Hamas and its ​underground [network of tunnels](https://www.reuters.com/graphics/ISRAEL-PALESTINIANS/GAZA-TUNNELS/gkvldmzorvb/).

Mohammad Arafa, head of the Gaza Engineers ​Association, said that based on assessments by fellow ⁠engineers who inspected the Al-Saada building over the past year, its collapse resulted from structural weakness after bombardment damaged several concrete pillars supporting its foundations.

But people had sheltered there because they had nowhere else to go, said Feryal Abu Ghanem, whose daughter-in-law was staying with her family when the building collapsed and was among ​those killed.

Bassam Naseer, a displaced man living in another damaged building nearby, said he feared the same thing would happen there. "No one is looking after us. ​The conditions are very difficult," ⁠he said.

After the Al-Saada's collapse, the Israel Defense Forces said in a social media post that it had not struck the building during the war. It did not respond to questions about residents saying it had struck the building, or about whether the building had been damaged by strikes on the surrounding area.

Eyad Azzam, who lost his pregnant wife and a 3-year-old son in the Al-Saada building's collapse, showed a video on his mobile phone of another ⁠son, Abdel-Rahman, trapped ​in the wreckage of the building before he was pulled to safety.

Abdel-Rahman, 7, had reached towards his mother, hoping to protect ​her from fallen rock, his father said. "He put out his hand and it wasn't a rock that had fallen, it was the entire ceiling."

People continued to live under damaged ceilings or columns for lack of other options, Azzam said.

"Today people say, 'This is a dangerous ​place to live in.' But where shall I go?" he said. "Even in the street there's no place."

Reporting by Nidal al-Mughrabi, Mohammad Salem, Dawoud Abu Alkas and Mahmoud Issa; Additional reporting by Steve Scheer; Editing by Aidan Lewis

title: New Zealand says China is its most persistent state-backed cyber threat
summary: A hand is seen on a laptop with binary codes displayed in front of the Chinese flag in this illustration taken, August 19, 2022. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/ File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconne
content:
A hand is seen on a laptop with binary codes displayed in front of the Chinese flag in this illustration taken, August 19, 2022. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/ File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/a-hand-is-seen-on-a-laptop-with-binary-codes-displayed-in-front-of-the-chinese-flag/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjI6bmV3c21sX1JDMkpaVjlGNlRURQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

WELLINGTON, Sept 24 (Reuters) - New Zealand's cyber security agency said China was the country's most persistent and capable state-backed cyber threat, as foreign actors targeted government ​agencies and organisations in sectors including health, education and information technology.

The National ‌Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), part of the New Zealand intelligence community, said it had identified activity suspected to originate from foreign state actors that put sensitive New Zealand information at risk.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fnew-zealand-says-china-is-its-most-persistent-state-backed-cyber-threat-2026-09-23%2F)

It linked suspected state-sponsored ​cyber activity to actors from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, according ​to its annual Cyber Threat Report released on Thursday.

"Of these nations ⁠the People's Republic of China is the most persistent and capable state actor ​undertaking cyber activity in New Zealand," the report said.

The assessment is the latest warning ​from a Western-aligned intelligence agency over alleged Chinese cyber espionage, which Beijing has routinely denied. It follows [a report from New Zealand’s security agency](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinese-state-linked-observatory-sought-nz-site-spy-agency-says-2026-08-13/) in August that said that China was the only ​country New Zealand had detected conducting espionage "at scale."

The Cyber Security report said 86 of ​369 cyber incidents deemed to be of potential national significance in the year to June 2026 ‌had ⁠suspected links to state-sponsored actors. The incidents included activity targeting government agencies, health and education organisations, and IT managed-service providers.

The agency warned that geopolitical competition was increasingly playing out in the South Pacific, where it was aware of state-backed cyber espionage targeting ​governments and infrastructure.

New ​Zealand has close ⁠family, cultural, political and economic ties across the Pacific, and such activity could affect citizens, businesses and civic institutions, it said.

State-backed ​actors were likely to target organisations that operate infrastructure or networks, ​provide essential ⁠public services, or hold information that could offer a strategic advantage, the NCSC said.

It warned that cyber espionage can be difficult to detect, with actors conducting reconnaissance and ⁠positioning access ​in systems over months or years before using ​it for intelligence gathering or disruption.

Long-running intrusions could lead to the compromise of operational technology and the loss ​of corporate and personal data, it said.

Reporting by Lucy Craymer; Editing by Kim Coghill

title: “你有五年规划，我有移民计划”：一份香港未来发展蓝图，为何引发一些年轻人的离港焦虑？

content:
## “你有五年规划，我有移民计划”：一份香港未来发展蓝图，为何引发一些年轻人的离港焦虑？

图像来源，Getty Images

Published 2026年9月23日上午9点36分

最近更新： 45 分钟前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

9月16日，香港特首李家超发表香港首个五年规划文件，以及年度施政报告。

李家超说，这份规划是香港未来五年经济和社会发展的蓝图。教育局局长蔡若莲则[形容](https://www.wenweipo.com/a/202609/21/AP6ab0c7b7e4b01d54a2842847.html)，青年在五年规划实施中担当重要角色，“既是发展的受益者，亦是建设者与接班人”。

但在网络上，部分年轻人却开始讨论如何离开香港。他们对规划中的措施感到担忧，在社交平台上发问：“最少需要储多少钱”、“有冇师兄师姐帮初级大人分析点部署”。有人表示，“我知而家先谂（计划）太迟，但迟总好过等死”。

当中，有网民发布一张从飞机拍摄地面的照片，配文写上：“你有你五年规划，我有我移民计划”。该帖文获得超过一万个赞好。

BBC中文访问三位香港年轻人，了解他们对五年规划及香港未来的看法。有人表示担心未来在香港变“二等公民”；也有人认为措施不如网友所言般令人担忧，但随着讨论发酵，也开始想像离开。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，9月16日，香港特首李家超发表香港首个五年规划文件，以及年度施政报告。

## “我不觉得我有被考虑进去”

今年25岁的Claudia（化名）在公营机构任职文员，过去她甚少主动关注施政报告，但这次五年规划出台之后，她的第一感受是不安、担心，以及“少少愤怒”。

从用词、内容到实践，她都对规划文件抱有疑问。

“香港一直是一个自由市场、（走）资本主义，‘五年规划’的出现已经让我好困惑”。文件出台后，她曾和朋友研究，发现当中存在不少“中国用语”：优化、当家人、第一责任人、顶层设计。

Claudia觉得报告的风格跟中国越来越像，“很不舒服、好碍眼”，“每一只字都睇得明，但又不知道它实际想讲什么。”

BBC中文使用检索工具，发现在约6万字的文件中，“深化”使用了101次、“优化”97次、“协同”则有61个，另外也有了30次“对接”。

但令Claudia真正感到不安的，是规划的具体内容。

她留意到，政府首次提出推动“以人民币支付政府开支”的措施。她表示2019年社会运动后，已有一些外资企业撤出香港。她忧虑若日后港元或与美金脱鈎、被人民币取替，“将来个经济发展会是怎样呢？”

根据五年规划文件，当局在合适情景下探索增加以人民币结算政府开支。不过，该文件未有提出改变联系汇率制度或以人民币取代港元。

除此之外，Claudia认为政府并无回应年轻人最担心的就业问题。Claudia在2024年毕业，形容自己“很幸运”，一毕业就找到工作。但她说身边有朋友大半年前离职后，至今仍未找到工作。

根据政府统计处[数字](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202608/20/P2026082000323.htm)，今年6至8月整体失业率为3.8%，20至29岁青年失业率则达9.1%。

在五年规划中，政府提到运用AI等工具加强就业配对，并表示会在保障本地劳工的前提下，因应社会及经济实际需要适度输入外劳。此外，政府联同商界推出为期两年的“三万青年职位及实习计划”。

Claudia认为，相关政策空泛，“没有一个实质改善的政策”。而在越发与中国大陆接轨的未来，她质疑政府措施最终能惠及多少市民，“有职位空缺是否香港人优先？”

Claudia说，在政府眼中，五年规划是香港未来发展的蓝图，但“我不觉得我（年轻人）有被考虑进去” 。

她坦言，早在国安法生效后，她已有60分的移民意欲；读完五年规划后，想法升到“150分”。她担心若继续留在香港，自己日后可能会变成“二等公民”。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，根据政府统计处数字，今年6至8月，整体失业率为3.8%，20至29岁青年失业率则达9.1%。

## 担心或只是一种“情绪”

在五年规划公布后当晚，社交平台Threads涌现不少移民帖文，当中不少自称“00后”，发文寻求移民意见。

18岁的家晴是求意见的其中一人。但与Claudia不同，她认为措施并不如大家所形容的那么令人担忧。

她起初对五年规划并不感兴趣，但随着社交平台被移民贴文“洗版”，她发现“大家都好焦虑”，才开始了解其内容。

阅读过后，她认为年轻人的担心更多是一种“情绪”。她记得，去年港府进一步放宽八间资助大学非本地生比例至五成，当时政策也引发身边同学不安，担心要和内地生争学位。但家晴对此反应淡定，认为中港越发融合是“无可避免、一定会发生”。

在中学六年生涯里，她亲历不少变化：通识科变成公社科、学生一定要出席内地考察团、每天都要升旗。“现在街上多了好多国旗，其实比大陆还夸张。”

对于五年规划内容，她认为还是要等到落地实践，才足以看到影响。

不过，网络上有关移民的讨论仍然影响了她。2019年社会运动爆发时，家晴刚升读中一，其后移民潮出现，身边陆续有朋友退学离开。家晴开始向往外国生活，认为“会比较舒服、比较开心”。

目前，家晴最焦虑的是没有BNO护照。她加入网上讨论，发问还有什么方法离开香港。有人留言：“后生就是本钱”、“移民不是讲有没有钱，取决于你有多大决心”。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，18岁的家晴感慨，中港越发融合是“无可避免、一定会发生”。

## “香港好似不再是香港”

今年27岁的阿瓜（化名）早些年曾有过移民念头，但计划最终因为要照顾家人而搁置。

她现于社福界别工作。打开五年规划文件之后，她越读越担心，“（感觉）慢慢......香港好似不再是香港”。

李家超的任期仅余一年。阿瓜说，自己本来抱着期望，认为若李家超不连任，新任特首或许作风会不同。她笑自己这个“不切实际”的想法，而现在看来“应该会一步一步向中国靠近、慢慢地规格可能也越来越大陆。”

除了人民币相关措施，最令阿瓜担心的是规划提出两地专业资格互认。规划提到，建造业将是先行先试的行业。政府亦会推动两地医疗服务衔接及规则对接，并鼓励香港法律界人士参加大湾区律师执业试。

阿瓜担心未来互认的资格会逐步扩展，她认为过去政府已有不少政策逐步开放大陆人来港工作，形容那时是“温水煮青蛙”，但当五年规划出台，阿瓜感觉就是用“热水烫”——香港未来的发展方向，似乎已愈来愈清晰。

阿瓜理解网络的情绪。她看到有人再提起电影《十年》。这是一套于2015年上映的香港电影，电影剧情分别讲述香港未来自由法治、语言文化受到大陆冲击的情况。

阿瓜曾思考过生育下一代，但她无法接受小朋友日后只会讲普通话，因而一度考虑移民。如今移民计划搁置，也让她再次思考生育的问题。

对于香港未来五年发展，阿瓜坦言没有期望，但她也在为自己作打算：先进修、考车牌，为未来留后路。

“不排除可能突然有一天，真的没有办法好想离开时，这些‘揸拿’（让自己有底气的东西）都可以在外国搵到食。”

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2019年社运后，香港曾爆发移民潮。

## 夹在中间的香港Z世代

过去，在香港网民常言1997年出生的人是“被选中的一代”：幼儿园毕业时碰上沙士、小学毕业则是猪流感，到大学毕业又碰上社会运动以及新冠疫情。

五年规划公布后，有网友发文慨叹：“总觉得我们00后这代好惨，没有见过最美好的香港，但见过没有最差只有更差的香港”。

Claudia有同样感受。她觉得自己一代人像被夹在中间——2020年国安法通过时，自己刚上大学，没有钱，“想走都走不到”。到现在毕业工作两三年，未有足够的时间规划移民和金钱，但不少国家已经在收紧移民政策。

今年8月31日，加拿大为港人推出的“救生艇计划”停止接受申请。澳洲亦于今月[宣布](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cx24jdd1j59po/trad)收紧移民政策。

“我们好像在跟时间竞赛这样，”Claudia感慨。对于未来五年，Claudia没太大的信心能成功移民，但她说会用未来五年“装备好自己”——希望能够升职、储钱，收获不同技能，先去工作假期，再想思考去留。

针对五年规划，香港青年发展委员会[表示](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202609/16/P2026091600437.htm)热烈欢迎。该会副主席梁毓伟认为，规划“高度重视青年发展”，措施“方向清晰、措施务实”。

全国政协委员杨政龙则[表示](https://www.orangenews.hk/hongkong/VVSMxsF/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E4%BA%94%E5%B9%B4%E8%A6%8F%E5%8A%83-%E6%A5%8A%E6%94%BF%E9%BE%8D-%E5%96%9C%E8%BF%8E%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E7%AC%AC%E4%B8%80%E5%80%8B%E4%BA%94%E5%B9%B4%E8%A8%88%E5%8A%83-%E7%B9%AA%E6%93%98%E8%97%8D%E5%9C%96%E8%BF%8E%E8%88%AA%E6%96%B0%E7%AF%87.shtml)，五年规划及施政报告“处处重视、关心及支持青年”，称为青年成长成才创造条件。

民政及青年事务局回覆BBC中文表示，指规划强调“开拓青年发展空间”，构建多元交流实践平台，支持青年更好把握国家发展机遇，重点培育“能服务国家所需、发挥香港所长的人才”。

另外为呼应五年规划，民青局指施政报告推出“支持青年发展”措施，对青年在就业、发展及长远生活规划等方面均有正面影响。

就年轻人表达的担忧，政制及内地事务局回覆BBC中文，表示自规划公布以来，特首及各官员展开解说工作，有关工作将延续，称望让年轻一代“真切体会”规划措施都与“他们的发展机会及职业生涯规划息息相关”。

局方亦表示规划建立了“跨越任期、重在连续”的执行机制，强调不会受年度政府换届、人事更替的不确定性所影响。

另外局方指出，香港市民“普遍支持”香港首次编制五年规划，指行公众咨询期间共收到超过1.7万份意见，而规划发表后，“总体反应也是正面的”。

# 习近平即将抵达华盛顿，美国学者、政客怎么看？

图像来源，Getty Images

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 布兰登‧德雷农（Brandon Drenon）
    *   Reporting from, 华盛顿特区

*   Published 4 小时前
*   阅读时间: 2 分钟

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将于本周在华盛顿接待中国领导人习近平，从人工智能到贸易，再到台湾问题，都将出现在这两位全球大国领导人的议程上。

预计习近平周三抵达安德鲁斯空军基地（Andrews Air Force Base）时，将由特朗普亲自迎接；周四则将在白宫举行欢迎仪式，包括军机飞越上空，以及近500名军人参加的检阅。

这是习近平十多年来首次对美国进行国事访问，也是自特朗普开始第二个总统任期以来，两人的第三次会面。

令这场高规格国事访问更添紧张的是，美中去年达成的贸易协议将于11月到期。

这份贸易休战协议于2025年10月达成——当时特朗普与习近平在韩国会晤——内容包括华盛顿暂停对中国商品大幅加征关税，而北京则放宽了对制造业至关重要的稀土出口限制。

专家表示，他们将关注此次国事访问期间，双方是否会发表某种关于延长该协议的声明。

习近平的华盛顿之行将于周五结束，行程排场十足、仪式隆重，包括豪华晚宴、私人参观和文艺演出。

美国外交关系委员会（Council on Foreign Relations）亚洲研究研究员戴维·萨克斯（David Sacks）形容，特朗普计划中的隆重欢迎“实属前所未有”。

“从亲自到安德鲁斯空军基地迎接习近平，到为习近平安排军机飞越表演，这是任何美国盟友都从未获得的待遇，”萨克斯说，“更不用说像中国这样的对手了。”

“这实在令人大为惊讶，”他继续说。

预计特朗普在会见习近平时将提出多项议题，尤其是关税和贸易问题。

这位美国总统长期批评本国对华贸易逆差。根据美国人口普查局（US Census Bureau）的最新数据，目前逆差超过910亿美元（682亿英镑）。

此外，尽管去年10月达成了协议，但中国对美国的稀土出口仍在下降。

多位消息人士告诉BBC，美中官员周二在联合国大会会议间隙举行了贸易会谈，但未能在习近平访问之前取得实质性进展。

据熟悉白宫想法的消息人士透露，会谈重点是围绕非关税贸易问题和农产品出口寻找共识。

预计周三习近平抵达后，美方谈判代表将在华盛顿继续与中方代表磋商。

特朗普与习近平之间另一个可能的议题是人工智能。布什中国基金会（Bush China Foundation）的方大伟（David Firestein）表示，在此次访问前夕，这一议题已“迅速攀升至议程前列”。

中美正展开一场被形容为“人工智能军备竞赛”的角逐。但近期接连发生的多起涉及这项新兴技术的瞩目安全事件，令特朗普政府面临越来越大的压力，要求其对人工智能进行监管并放缓发展步伐。

参议员伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）本周在X上写道：“为了全人类，特朗普和习近平必须立即谈判达成条约，暂停人工智能开发，并在为时已晚之前禁止超级智能。”

特朗普的前白宫顾问史蒂夫·班农（Steve Bannon）以及一些共和党国会议员也对人工智能的危险发出警告。

这位总统视人工智能技术为美国经济的命脉，也是全球权力角逐的战场，因此一直不情愿踩下刹车。

他视在人工智能竞赛中击败中国为首要目标。“谁赢得人工智能，谁就赢得一切，”特朗普曾说。

方大伟告诉BBC，他预计特朗普与习近平将讨论双方在人工智能领域合作的方式。

周日，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）与中国国务院副总理何立峰（He Lifeng）会面，并表示双方就贸易与人工智能进行了“非常成功”的会谈。

视频加注文字，观看：桑德斯呼吁美国和中国合作禁止人工智慧超级智能

接受BBC采访的专家表示，本周安排的多场“习特会”期间，双方不太可能在人工智能或其他议题上取得重大突破。

此外还有台湾问题——这始终是一个持续存在的外交麻烦。

美国国会已批准一项价值数十亿美元的对台军售案，目前只待特朗普签字。但他暂时按兵不动，视之为与中国讨价还价的筹码。

中国长期以来誓言要与实行自治的台湾“统一”，且不排除动用武力。

方大伟表示，他预计习近平将寻求特朗普承诺延长军售案搁置的时间，或者想方设法彻底避免这笔军售。

与特朗普一样，习近平也面临国内经济逆风，预计他将利用此次访问的机会，讨论如何深化美中贸易。

但这对特朗普而言可能带来政治难题。他的一些内阁成员和支持者对中国抱持深切怀疑。

美国运输部长肖恩·达菲（Sean Duffy）9月致信福特汽车公司（Ford Motor Company），以国家安全和保护美国就业为由，敦促该公司切断与中国的联系。

无论达成任何新的美中协议前还有哪些明显障碍，有一点很清楚：特朗普认为，与习近平的个人接触对这一进程至关重要。

“特朗普已经下定决心：无论如何，我们都需要避免与中国陷入对抗关系，”美中关系全国委员会（National Committee on US-China Relations）主席斯蒂芬·奥林斯（Stephen Orlins）说。

“他相信，他与习近平主席见面的次数越多，两国关系的对抗性就越低，”奥林斯继续说，“而他是对的。”

（BBC驻华盛顿记者丹尼尔·布什（Daniel Bush）补充报道）

## 习特会前瞻：特朗普会再度争取“释放黎智英”吗？

图像来源，STR/AFP via Getty Images

Published 2026年9月23日上午9点17分

最近更新： 1 小时前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

中国国家主席习近平即将访问美国，与总统特朗普（Donald Trump）会面。外界关注，继今年5月访华之后，特朗普会否再度当面向习近平提出“释放黎智英”。

香港《壹传媒》创办人黎智英2020年底被捕，还押超过五年。他2025年12月被裁定《香港国安法》下“串谋勾结外国势力”等罪名成立，今年2月被判囚20年。78岁的他近年一直被单独囚禁，家人称其健康欠佳，港府官员则指控有人“捏造”其健康状况。

特朗普5月访华时曾向习近平点名提及黎智英，事后形容对方反应“并不正面”，称这是“棘手的事情”。同获点名的中国地下教会牧师金明日，今年7月获释赴美，外界视为特朗普直接促成的结果。

学者向BBC中文分析，特朗普“百分之百”会在今次会面再提黎智英案，此时若中方放人，正是展现软实力的合适时机。但综合专家判断，习近平点头放人的机率微乎其微。

## 元首外交的前例：金明日案

特朗普早于2024年竞选总统时已表示，若重返白宫，会确保黎智英获释。

2025年10月，特朗普与习近平在韩国釜山会晤。同年12月黎智英被裁定罪名成立后，特朗普透露曾向习近平提出释放请求，指黎年纪大、身体不好，但未有披露双方具体谈话内容。

今年5月，特朗普结束访华后在空军一号专机上表示，曾向习近平点名提及黎智英和金明日。就黎智英案，特朗普引述对方说：“他告诉我这是一个棘手的事情。”（He told me that would be a tough one.）他形容对方反应“并不正面”（not positive），对释放前景并不乐观。

金明日是锡安教会创办人，该教会属基督新教，是中国规模最大的地下教会之一。他去年被捕，今年7月获释，其后被安排送往美国。外界视此为特朗普直接促成的结果，但中美双方均没有就事件正面回应。

金明日案显示，元首直接介入，确实能改变个别在囚人士的命运。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，2026年5月，特朗普访华，期间曾向习近平提及黎智英及金明日个案。

## “芬太尼虽然敏感，但黎智英案让气氛降至冰点”

美国智库太平洋论坛（Pacific Forum）兼任高级研究员蓝若思（Elizabeth Larus）向BBC中文分析，今次会谈的核心议题集中在人工智能、双边贸易、关键矿物供应链，也包括美国对台军售，以及中方争取特朗普公开表明反对台湾独立等。

但她认为，特朗普“百分之百”会在会面期间再次提及黎智英案，因为该案是美国政府最高层级关注的议题之一，目前由白宫直接处理，也是令二人会面陷入僵局的议题。蓝若思说：“芬太尼、贸易及在华美国公民等问题虽然敏感，但黎智英议题似乎特别令双方气氛降至冰点。”

美国乔治城大学亚洲法律中心（Georgetown Center for Asian Law）高级研究员黎恩灏博士则指出，争取释放黎智英在美国政坛是跨党派共识，民间组织亦持续向美国政府施压；加上特朗普在金明日事件上获得正面支持，这些诱因都会令特朗普及其政府继续提出黎智英议题。

## 北京放人的机率有多大？

蓝若思预计，特朗普今次会尝试进一步施压，并可能以人道理由切入，包括黎智英健康状况欠佳、其女儿正接受癌症治疗。

“若习近平希望展现中国的软实力，现时或许是一个合适时机，展现其宽宏大量，透过医疗假释安排释放黎智英，让他离港赴美治疗，”她补充，相关安排可规定黎智英若返港须履行余下刑期。

黎恩灏则认为，即使黎智英案被形容为“棘手的事情”，“目前为止，看不到任何信号是北京完全会拒绝释放黎智英，或拒绝讨论黎智英的问题”。

蓝若思亦估计，特朗普可能一并提出数名被扣押在中国的美国公民案件，此同属美国政府的优先事项。她分析，美国经常就中国政治犯问题提出交涉，而且不限于高知名个案，问题在于此类议题对双边关系有多大实际影响。

图像来源，Getty Images

北京为何不愿妥协？

金明日与黎智英同获特朗普点名，前者已获释赴美，后者被判囚20年。从北京的公开表态看，两案的分量并不相同。

黎智英被判刑后，中国外交部驻香港公署形容美国、英国等“叫嚣释放黎智英”，称黎智英“所作所为严重冲击‘一国两制’原则底线，严重危害国家安全，严重损害香港的繁荣稳定和市民的福祉，理应受到法律的严惩”。香港特区政府亦形容黎智英犯下“罪证纍纍的滔天罪行”。

相比之下，中国官方回覆金明日案则颇为低调，仅称，中国依法管理宗教事务，并“我们坚决反对以所谓宗教问题干涉中国内政”

蓝若思提醒，“中共喜欢以‘一国两制’的说辞来掩饰其在香港治理上的立场，但习近平只要说一句话，事情就会开始朝着好的方向发展。”

但她认为，这种可能性微乎其微。

## 香港政府“没有角色”

不过，黎恩灏分析，即使港府过去就黎智英案态度强硬，但“风向是可以转的”。释放黎智英与否是一个政治决定，议题已上升至中美元首会谈层面，“香港政府是没有角色”，只能够执行相关决定。

他解释，香港具备相应的法律基础。《基本法》第48条第12款订明，行政长官的职权包括赦免刑事罪犯或减轻其刑罚，条文没有明文规定如何行使，反映特首有很大酌情权。

特区保安局2017年曾回覆立法会称，特首可根据“长期监禁刑罚复核委员会”的建议，或医生向惩教署署长提出的建议减刑，在囚人士也可提出呈请。

不过，2024年3月通过的《维护国家安全条例》（即俗称“23条立法”）赋权惩教署署长裁定释放某囚犯会否不利于中国国家安全，对“不利国安”者不予减刑。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，黎崇恩到各地游说，争取释放其父黎智英。

图像来源，CLAIRE LAI

图像加注文字，黎崇恩在英国陪伴妹妹黎采抗癌。

## “我也不知道他还能等多久”

黎智英家人早前表示，他被单独囚禁后体重下降10公斤，牙齿腐烂、指甲脱落。黎崇恩向BBC中文透露，父亲“早阵子需要有人帮他才能起身”，身体“差了很多”：“说真的，我也不知道他还能等多久。”

妹妹黎采早前证实患癌，9月接受英国《泰晤士报》访问时说，父亲入狱以来对一切处之泰然，惟独获悉女儿患癌后痛哭，“那是他唯一一次真正崩溃大哭”。黎崇恩目前主力在英国照顾妹妹：“爸爸不在妹妹身边，让我妹妹失去父亲。”

香港保安局局长邓炳强今年2月[公开反驳](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202602/09/P2026020900668.htm)，称单独囚禁是黎智英自行提出，批评者“捏造黎智英健康不佳”，刻意塑造悲情形象“卖惨”，要求特区政府以健康和年纪理由放人。

9月16日，黎崇恩出席美国国会及行政当局中国委员会（CECC）听证会，称父亲“不构成任何威胁”，“囚禁他会使其成为不公义的象征”，并感谢特朗普政府支持。委员会同日提出跨党派法案，要求国务院调查有否因虐待、医疗疏忽导致政治犯死亡，确定责任人后制裁涉案的中国及香港官员。

中国香港特区政府随后[发声明严厉谴责](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202609/17/P2026091700533.htm)，反对美国政客与“反中乱港份子”勾结、就黎智英案作失实言论，“妄图恫吓维护国家安全的有关特区人员”；声明又指黎智英已选择不就定罪及判刑上诉，惩教署一直按规定确保羁押环境安全、人道、合适和健康。

黎崇恩说，难以估算中方会如何回应，但父亲在囚近六年、健康欠佳，已承受惩罚，释放他对各方有利：“我认为释放他是对多边关系发出的一个极佳讯号。这表明中国和香港愿意履行对国际社会的承诺，特别是对英国的承诺；这亦显示香港愿意朝着恢复法治的方向跨出正确的一步。”

Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan pauses as he speaks with Reuters during an interview, in Lahore, Pakistan March 17, 2023. REUTERS/Akhtar Soomro/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/former-pakistani-pm-imran-khan-speaks-with-reuters-during-an-intervew-in-lahore/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6bmV3c21sX1JDMlpWWjlWWThVOA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Nearly 35,000 more security personnel deployed, Interior Ministry official says
*   Authorities detained hundreds of party activists in recent days
*   Two major highways closed, authorities say

ISLAMABAD, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Pakistan curbed access on Wednesday to its capital, ​Islamabad, ahead of a march planned by supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, blocking major highways ‌with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces.

The show of force is the starkest sign in years of how [divisions between Khan's](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-ex-pm-imran-khan-taken-back-prison-hospital-party-spokesman-says-2026-08-21/) Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party and the military-backed government have polarised the South Asian nation of 240 million.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fasia-pacific%2Fpakistan-tightens-security-ahead-march-planned-by-imran-khans-party-2026-09-23%2F)

Ahead of Sunday's planned march, authorities detained three of Khan's sisters ​and hundreds of party activists in recent days, citing a need to maintain public order.

The PTI's last large-scale protest ​two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.

## SECURITY STEPPED UP, TWO HIGHWAYS SHUT

Nearly 35,000 additional ⁠police and paramilitary personnel have been stationed in and around the capital, an Interior Ministry official said on Wednesday, speaking on ​condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak publicly.

More have been deployed in other parts of the country where ​protesters may gather.

Two major highways linking Islamabad to the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, governed by Khan's party, have also been closed until further notice, the National Highway Authority said.

Shipping containers were seen being placed in recent days to barricade Islamabad's government district, home to parliament, the prime minister's residence, ​and foreign embassies.

Khan, 73, a former cricket star ousted by parliament in a 2022 no-confidence vote, has claimed to be a ​political prisoner.

Before his 2023 arrest, he had fallen out with the military, which is seen as the ultimate arbiter of politics in the nuclear-armed ‌nation. The ⁠military denies his claim to be a political prisoner.

On Monday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi warned that police were told to respond forcefully if the march turned violent, adding, "It is not like that they come and they fire shots and you do nothing."

## KHAN'S PARTY SAYS MARCH WILL PROCEED

PTI party chairman Gohar Khan said the march would proceed despite the blockade.

It comes more than a month after the ​government defied a court order and ​refused Khan treatment in a ⁠private hospital, despite mounting concerns over [his health](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-top-court-orders-ex-pm-imran-khan-be-moved-hospital-jail-local-media-2026-08-18/).

The protest also coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters.

"There should be freedom of expression and ​freedom of speech," said Muhammad Asad ul Asaf, a student. "The government has created a full atmosphere ​of fear." Muhammad Zeeshan, ⁠an unemployed mechanical engineer, said the curbs in Islamabad were piling pressure on an already-burdened public. "Businesses face problems and people face difficulties in commuting," he said, while "inflation is increasing day by day."

Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military ⁠in unprecedented ​ways when protesters stormed military installations.

Cases against him ranged from concerns over state ​gifts to instigating violent attacks on military and state installations, and an accusation of an unlawful marriage.

All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with ​appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.

Reporting by Asif Shahzad; Additional reporting by Sala Uddin; Editing by Rick Noack, Clarence Fernandez and Gareth Jones

Shahzad is an accomplished media professional, with over two decades of experience. He primarily reports out of Pakistan, Afghanistan regions, with a great interest and an extensive knowledge of Asia. He also reports on politics, economy, finance, business, commodities, Islamist militancy, human rights

title: German state election losses risk snarling Merz's reform agenda
summary: * Summary * Heavy defeats in eastern German states create pressure to rethink reforms * SPD paper sees "open questions" on proposed early retirement changes in pension package * Merz recognizes need to address issues of fairness and equity
content:
*   Summary

*   Heavy defeats in eastern German states create pressure to rethink reforms
*   SPD paper sees "open questions" on proposed early retirement changes in pension package
*   Merz recognizes need to address issues of fairness and equity

BERLIN, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Chancellor Friedrich Merz may have survived the triumph of the far right in this month's state elections in eastern Germany and Berlin but the shock to his coalition could force ​him to water down his promised reform agenda.

Merz took the unusual step of announcing immediately after exit polls showed his conservatives were on course for their [worst-ever defeat](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/merz-under-pressure-two-more-german-states-go-polls-2026-09-20/) that ‌he would stay in office to get a raft of reforms to the [tax, pensions and health](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/germanys-merz-unveils-pension-tax-labour-reforms-2026-07-02/) systems through parliament.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fgerman-state-election-losses-risk-snarling-merzs-reform-agenda-2026-09-23%2F)

His partners in the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD), who also lost heavily in elections in [Saxony-Anhalt](https://www.reuters.com/world/germanys-far-right-afd-seeks-landmark-state-victory-saxony-anhalt-votes-2026-09-06/) and [Berlin](https://www.reuters.com/world/far-left-party-wins-berlin-election-pledging-nationalise-housing-2026-09-20/) while holding on in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, also pledged to continue their alliance with his Christian Democrats (CDU). But there has been increasing pressure from within the coalition for the government to do something to reflect the votes.

"There can't be a simple carrying on as normal after the state ​elections," an SPD strategy document circulated this week said, calling for a "German 'New Deal' that doesn't leave people alone in a period of transition".

It said a special party meeting would be ​called in December where the leadership would issue new policy proposals.

Despite stronger-than-expected growth in the first half of the year, surveys showed Sunday's election ⁠results were heavily influenced by squeezed living standards and voter worries over economic issues, notably rising [inflation.](https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/german-inflation-accelerates-august-2026-08-31/)

Aware of the mood of the electorate, two days before Sunday's votes in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Merz ​announced a €2.5 billion [tax cut](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/germany-plans-cut-energy-tax-lower-petrol-prices-bild-reports-2026-09-18/) and plans for a price cap to help motorists deal with fuel prices sent soaring by the [Iran war](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran/).

There has also been pressure from his partners to change sections of the reform ​package that have drained support for the ruling parties in the eastern German states which voted this month, including plans to change the rules on retiring early.

The SPD letter said there were "open questions" about the proposed scrapping of the option for people to retire on a full pension at the age of 63 as long as they had paid contributions for at least 45 years.

The measure was recommended by a government-appointed pension commission as part of ​a [package of measures](https://www.reuters.com/sports/german-pension-commission-proposes-shift-swedish-style-fund-2026-06-23/) that included adding a capital markets element to public pensions to keep the system affordable as the population ages.

But many in the east, where people typically have lower savings than ​in the west and lots went through long spells of unemployment in the wake of German reunification in 1990, feel such a change would hit them disproportionately hard.

Eastern state premiers from both the CDU and SPD ‌have already ⁠called for the proposed change to be scrapped and the SPD letter said the proposals had caused "enormous uncertainty" among both workers and employers.

Surveys after the elections in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania showed many voters feared for their personal economic security and mistrusted Merz, whose ratings have hit historic lows.

Manuela Schwesig, the SPD state premier in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, who has argued strongly against changing the early retirement rules, said this week Merz needed to regain the trust of voters. "I don't know if he will succeed," she said.

## REFORM PLEDGES

In the wake of the defeats, Merz himself recognized that the government needed to acknowledge that many ​voters did not feel it was being "fair" in ​its reform plans.

But already there have been ⁠warnings that picking apart reform plans agreed over the summer would undermine confidence in German policy planning just as Europe's largest economy looks like achieving [modest growth](https://www.reuters.com/business/german-institutes-raise-2026-2027-economic-growth-forecasts-sources-say-2026-09-22/) after years of recession.

"If we start this whole process again now, it just delays these reforms and we need them," said Martin Jacob, a ​professor at Spain's IESE Business School and a member of the German finance ministry's scientific advisory board.

"And this matters, because international investors, German ​investors, companies in Germany need ⁠to know what policy environment they're in," he said.

However, opinion polls this week showing the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party with almost 30% support across the country underline the political realities facing the government.

Merz, an instinctive pro-business fiscal conservative, came to power in 2025, pledging [broad reforms](https://www.reuters.com/business/merzs-reforms-have-potential-eventually-boost-german-growth-2026-07-02/) to revive a German economy which has seen its industrial base steadily eroded by relentless competition from China and by the abrupt loss of ⁠cheap oil ​and gas from Russia due to the Ukraine war.

Turning his back on years of German fiscal orthodoxy, he unleashed a €500 ​billion spending package to rebuild Germany's creaking infrastructure and its shrunken armed forces and, after months of wrangling, approved the reform package in July.

But the political crisis laid bare by this month's elections could now put those reforms at risk, said Carsten ​Brzeski, global head of macro at ING.

"Years of economic stagnation helped produce that fragmentation. Now the fragmentation will make the stagnation harder to escape," he said.

Additional reporting by Maria Martinez; Editing by Toby Chopra

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

title: Trump plans grand spectacle for potentially tense Xi talks
summary: * Summary * Companies * First Xi visit to US in nearly three years * Low expectations for a breakthrough * Trade, technology, Tehran and Taiwan top agenda WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - US President [Donald Trump](https://www.reuters.com/w
content:
*   Summary
*   Companies

*   First Xi visit to US in nearly three years
*   Low expectations for a breakthrough
*   Trade, technology, Tehran and Taiwan top agenda

WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - US President [Donald Trump](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/donald-trump/) welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit where the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Tehran will play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony.

For the Chinese leader's first trip to the US ​in nearly three years, Trump will greet Xi and his wife on the tarmac when they arrive Wednesday evening at the Maryland military base that hosts Air Force ‌One.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Ftrump-plans-grand-spectacle-potentially-tense-xi-talks-2026-09-23%2F)

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

The fanfare was due to include a state dinner with tech luminaries, a White House military ceremony including jet flyovers and a visit to the National Archives where the original Declaration of Independence and Constitution are housed.

Despite their deep disagreements, both sides pressed ahead with the summit, which analysts said seeks to project stability between the world’s biggest factory and its biggest consumer.

Expectations for a breakthrough during Xi's visit were slim.

The countries' 11-month trade truce sunsets in November, ​but the two sides are at odds on issues ranging from Taiwan to narcotics and rare-earth minerals.

People familiar with the plans said Xi was likely to forcefully raise Beijing's claim ​to Taiwan, a topic Washington would prefer to avoid, while Trump was likely to maintain firm US export controls despite Xi’s objections.

But talks set for ⁠Thursday could nonetheless yield deals to lower tariffs in specific sectors, cooperate on drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue.

Trump is expected to seek the release of some Americans and others detained in China, according ​to the people.

The two countries could also agree to talk more on AI, where they are in fierce competition but mindful of growing dangers.

The meeting comes at a difficult moment for Trump, who faces [falling ​approval numbers](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-approval-falls-career-low-32-high-costs-bite-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-09-21/) as public discontent with his war on Iran grows. Xi, while also facing challenges at home, arrives in a seemingly stronger position, with his country's trade engine [roaring](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/xi-rolls-into-trump-summit-with-chinas-trade-engine-roaring-2026-09-21/).

The leaders themselves may not feel they need to compromise, analysts said.

White House personnel and a U.S. military honor guard rehearse an arrival ceremony ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit next week with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/preparations-ahead-of-chinese-president-xis-meeting-with-us-president-trump-at-the-white-house-in-washington/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkRLTkFVVjVQSw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

"The president very much believes that over time the US economy is going to grow, the US will get stronger," said Edgard Kagan, a former White House official now with Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies. "I think ​when Xi Jinping sits down with Donald Trump, he very much believes the US is in hurtling decline, and that time is on China's side."

## STATE DINNER WITH AI CHIEFS

A state dinner on Thursday is ​expected to bring together chiefs of companies important in both markets like Apple's

Tim Cook, Nvidia's

Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman.

As in their prior two meetings since 2025, the leaders are planning a highly scripted public ‌spectacle. Instead ⁠of a joint press conference or statement at the end, the countries are expected to issue dueling announcements highlighting what each side hopes to convey to a domestic audience.

For Trump, the trip caps a week of diplomacy that began with a two-day stay in New York for the [United Nations General Assembly](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-eyes-busy-week-meetings-un-general-assembly-gathers-2026-09-20/). Nearly seven months of war with Iran have spiked energy prices in the US, and the president's Republican Party faces tough prospects in November’s congressional elections.

Xi has overseen a surge in China's foreign trade but faces weak household spending and a property market downturn. Sweeping corruption and discipline crackdowns in the military have ​helped cement Xi’s power but also raised questions ​about the People's Liberation Army's readiness.

Another meeting ⁠between Trump and Xi is seen as likely this year, potentially on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China in November or the Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

## AREAS OF TENSION INCLUDE IRAN, ELECTIONS, TAIWAN

After imposing [triple-digit tariffs](https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/how-trump-xi-went-tariff-war-trade-truce-2026-09-21/) on Chinese imports last year, Trump has relaxed ​policy and rhetoric towards China. One recent exception was a prime-time address in July when Trump [renewed accusations](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-alleges-china-committed-2020-election-fraud-2026-07-17/), which China denies, that Beijing meddles in ​US elections.

Iran is likely to ⁠feature in the discussions. Beijing has maintained close ties with Tehran, but it's unclear whether it will help Trump break a stalemate in the conflict. Washington thinks Beijing could use its influence over Tehran, but Trump has said he sees no need to seek China's help.

Beijing, the world's biggest oil importer, helped stabilize crude prices after the war started by cutting demand and releasing strategic stockpiles. After promising to unleash "economic D-Day" on ⁠countries doing business ​with Iran, the Trump administration [withheld secondary sanctions](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-treasury-broaden-scope-secondary-sanctions-iran-source-says-2026-08-24/) on major banks in China, Tehran’s largest trading partner.

Xi is also expected to ​push Trump to decrease arms sales to Taiwan after doing so at the last meeting in Beijing. In December, the Trump administration approved an

[$11 billion, opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/search/nL1N3XN16Z)
arms sale to Taiwan, the largest ever. But a second package, worth some

[$14 billion, opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/search/nL1N41S025)
, has been on ​hold for months. Trump has described the arms sales as a “very good negotiating chip.”

Reporting by Trevor Hunnicutt; additional reporting by David Brunnstrom, Yimou Lee and Ben Blanchard; Editing by Don Durfee and Cynthia Osterman

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Trevor Hunnicutt is White House Correspondent at Reuters News. He writes about U.S. foreign and domestic policy and regularly travels with the President of the United States. Prior to joining the White House team in 2021, he covered presidential campaigns, economics, finance and investing for many years. He has also served on the board of the White House Correspondents' Association. Hunnicutt holds a bachelor's degree from Pomona College and a master's from the London School of Economics.

title: “习特会”最棘手议题之一：中国稀土出口管制

content:
随着特朗普总统和中国国家主席习近平准备于本周举行会晤，中国对关键稀土金属和稀土磁铁的出口限制依然是最棘手的未决问题之一。

几个月来，美国、欧洲、日本和印度的制造商一直抱怨难以从中国获取足够的稀土金属，而中国主导着全球稀土生产。这些材料对于制造汽车、风力涡轮机、半导体、电脑显示器以及军事装备等各类产品至关重要。

2025年4月，中国对七种稀土及由其制成的磁铁实施了出口管制。随后，中国宣布了一项范围更广的限制措施，目前定于11月10日生效。此外，在一场政治争端中，中国大幅削减了对日本的稀土和磁铁出口，扰乱了同样服务于美国制造商的供应链。

所有这三个问题——现行的管制、11月10日生效的限制措施以及对日本的出口限制——预计都将笼罩在特朗普与作为中国最高领导人的习近平的会晤之上。迄今为止，几乎没有迹象表明这些问题将如何得到解决。

2025年4月，特朗普对中国及数十个其他国家征收高额关税。两天后，北京出台了出口许可规定，自此稀土便成为两国间的关键贸易问题。中国的稀土出口量锐减，其他地区的一些制造商也不得不削减其产品产量。

去年的经历彰显了中国凭借其对这些重要材料生产近乎垄断的地位所获得的影响力。

白宫表示，中国并未完全落实先前关于发放更多出口许可证的讨论。一位美国高级官员在周五的简报会上说，交付情况“未达到我们的预期标准，我确信，这将成为一个讨论话题”。

美国和欧洲商业团体表示，货物经常延误、数量不足或根本没有运达。中国商务部对每一份出口申请都会进行审查。

包头的稀土冶炼厂。The New York Times

中国美国商会会长何迈可(Michael Hart)表示：“虽然我们大多数的成员报称获得了他们所需的大部分稀土供应，但围绕该行业的限制让许多人担心，还能不能将中国视为可靠的长期供应链合作伙伴。”

中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆周一表示，北京方面仍致力于维护关键矿物供应链的稳定与安全。

定于11月10日生效的限制措施构成了另一项挑战。现任和前任美国官员表示，中美两国曾讨论过推迟实施这些规定，但未能就延期多长时间达成一致。由于外交敏感性，他们要求匿名。

官员们表示，美国提议推迟六个月至一年，作为对美国关税及其他贸易行动更广泛冻结计划的一部分。

此类协议将把重燃的贸易紧张局势推迟到美国中期选举之后，同时为特朗普政府在2028年总统大选前留出时间，以就贸易顺差、进口限制及工业补贴等问题向北京施压。

但北京有自己的政治日程。中国共产党预计将于明年秋季举行五年一次的全国代表大会，届时将选出该国的最高领导层。中国通常会在大会召开前尽量减少争端，这意味着一项为期六个月或一年的协议可能会在一个尴尬的节点到期。

现任及前任美国官员表示，中国转而寻求美国在特朗普剩余总统任期内停止实施进一步的关税和其他贸易行动。中国官员拒绝证实这一立场，并声称出口管制的目的是防止稀土被用于军事装备。

郭嘉昆周一拒绝讨论可能推迟11月10日规定的事宜。

这些新规将对包括铒在内的另外五种稀土元素实施出口管制。铒对人工智能数据中心和跨洋电缆的光纤通信至关重要。行业专家表示，甚至在规定生效之前，中国似乎就已经在限制或推迟铒的出口。

国家博物馆内展出的磁性材料。Maxim Shemetov/Reuters

伦敦大宗商品定价机构阿格斯的金属主管埃莉·萨克拉特瓦拉表示：“几个中国港口已经出现积压的情况。”

最棘手的争端或许是中国大幅减少了对日本的稀土磁铁出口，并几乎暂停了一些尤为重要的稀土供应，其中包括镝。镝被广泛应用于汽车磁铁及最先进的芯片中。

去年12月，在日本首相[高市早苗](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/21/world/asia/sanae-takaichi-japan-prime-minister.html)表示如果中国“入侵”，她的国家可协助[保卫台湾](https://cn.nytimes.com/asia-pacific/20251127/japan-china-taiwan-takaichi-dispute/https://cn.nytimes.com/asia-pacific/20251127/japan-china-taiwan-takaichi-dispute/ "Link: https://cn.nytimes.com/asia-pacific/20251127/japan-china-taiwan-takaichi-dispute/https://cn.nytimes.com/asia-pacific/20251127/japan-china-taiwan-takaichi-dispute/")之后，中国开始实施这些限制措施。台湾是一个实行民主制度的岛屿，北京将其视为自身领土的一部分。

中国在稀土销售上通常对各国区分对待，目前尚不清楚习近平是否会与特朗普讨论针对日本的限制措施。当周一被问及对日出口时，中国政府发言人郭嘉昆表示，中国禁止向日本出口用于军事的两用物项，以及其他可能增强其军事实力的物项。

中国在这一行业的主导地位赋予了其巨大的影响力。中国的精炼厂生产了四种稀土元素约90%的全球供应，这四种元素——镧、铈、钕和镨——广泛应用于石油炼制、玻璃抛光及低端磁铁。北京尚未限制这四种元素的出口。

中国还生产从半导体、激光器到风力涡轮机和机器人等一系列产品所需的另外十几种稀土元素的几乎全部全球供应。自2025年4月起，其中七种的出口已需获得特殊许可证，而11月10日生效的新规要求对另外五种实施出口许可制度。

北京表示，其稀土管制旨在防止武器扩散，而非施加经济压力。然而，军事用途仅占全球稀土消耗量的一小部分。

美国国防部2024年估计，美国军事需求仅占全球稀土需求的0.1%。但这一数字偏低，因为它涵盖了大量用于石油炼制和玻璃抛光等民用领域的普通稀土。

即使将比较范围限定在对武器生产最为重要的稀缺稀土上，行业估算也表明，军事用途约占总体需求的2%至5%。

title: Wife of US seismologist held in China says Trump will ask Xi to free him
summary: * Summary * Trump to ask Xi to free detained US seismologist, his wife tells Reuters * Chen worked on detection of North Korean nuclear tests * Chen's US-funded research publicly available, never classified WASHINGTON, Sept 22 (Reuters) - T
content:
*   Summary

*   Trump to ask Xi to free detained US seismologist, his wife tells Reuters
*   Chen worked on detection of North Korean nuclear tests
*   Chen's US-funded research publicly available, never classified

WASHINGTON, Sept 22 (Reuters) - The wife of a US expert on North Korean nuclear tests who has been imprisoned in China since late ​2024 said on Tuesday the White House has assured her that President Donald Trump will ask Chinese leader Xi Jinping to ‌free her husband when the pair meet this week.

Yufang Rong said she feared that Beijing planned to try her Chinese-born husband, Youlin Chen, on fabricated espionage charges even though his US-funded research was openly published, used publicly available data and was done in collaboration with Chinese scientists.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fwife-us-seismologist-held-china-says-trump-will-ask-xi-free-him-2026-09-23%2F)

Trump will welcome Xi on Wednesday for their second meeting since May as the ​leaders of the world's leading powers seek stability amid tensions ranging from [trade](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/xi-rolls-into-trump-summit-with-chinas-trade-engine-roaring-2026-09-21/)to [Iran](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-dismisses-report-china-entities-helped-iran-before-attack-that-killed-us-2026-09-14/)and [Taiwan](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-expected-press-trump-halt-taiwan-arms-sales-under-1982-agreement-2026-09-22/).

Rong said she was assured during a Tuesday meeting at the ​White House with officials from the State Department and National Security Council that Trump would ask Xi to free her ⁠husband.

Chen, 54, is one of two Americans held by Beijing that the US has designated as "wrongfully detained," making their release a top priority. The [other](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-designates-american-held-by-china-wrongfully-detained-2026-08-20/) is ​Min Zin, a scholar arrested in June.

Rong said she was told that Trump also would press Xi to release Zin.

Trump raised Chen's case with Xi during ​a visit to Beijing in May, but it produced no action, Rong said.

"Resolving the wrongful detentions of US citizens is always a top priority for the president," a senior US official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters.

The Chinese embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Chinese foreign ministry said in ​July that the country's judiciary deals with cases according to the law "and there is no so-called wrongful detention."

## 'BE STRONG'

U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping react as they hold a bilateral meeting at Gimhae International Airport, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, in Busan, South Korea, October 30, 2025. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/us-president-donald-trump-meets-with-chinese-president-xi-jinping-on-the-sidelines-of-the-apec-summit-in-busan/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX1JDMjRNSEE4NE1COA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Chen, whose detention was [revealed](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/china-detains-us-seismologist-who-has-studied-north-korean-nuclear-tests-2026-07-13/) by Reuters in ​July, is a seismologist with a US government contractor. His work detecting shockwaves from North Korean underground nuclear tests has been openly funded by the State Department and ‌the US ⁠Air Force Research Laboratory.

He became a US citizen in 2011 and settled in the Boston area.

He was arrested by Chinese state security officers on November 5, 2024, at Beijing International Airport as he prepared to fly home after visiting family and lecturing at two universities. Rong said her husband had been interrogated more than 100 times.

"I can't imagine how hard his life is there every day," she said.

She believes that China wants to use her husband's expertise to ​improve its ability to conceal nuclear tests ​using decoupling, a technique in which ⁠a device is detonated inside a large underground chamber to reduce the size of the shockwaves.

The US has [accused](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-reveals-new-details-alleged-chinese-nuclear-test-2026-02-17/) China of using decoupling to try to mask a low-yield nuclear test blast on June 22, 2020. China, which like ​the US has signed but not ratified a 1996 international ban on nuclear tests, denies conducting the test.

US embassy ​officials had been ⁠allowed to visit Chen for about 30 minutes once a month, always in the presence of Chinese officials, Rong said. They read out letters she had written to him and he dictated his replies.

"They record his appearance, his mental status, and just anything that they observe," she recounted, adding that Chen's Chinese lawyer was not ⁠allowed to ​discuss his visits with her.

Rong is concerned about the conditions of her husband's confinement, where ​she said he received substandard medical care and food. He suffered from high blood pressure and diabetes.

Asked what she would say to her husband if she could see him, Rong replied: "'Be strong. ​Be optimistic. There are a lot of people helping you. You will come back for sure.'"

Reporting by Jonathan Landay; Editing by Jesse Mesner-Hage and Stephen Coates

[Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/catalan-separatists-rally-against-far-right-party-ahead-of-national-day/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkhHTkE5MlM0RQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)Read more

*   Summary

*   Far-right Aliança Catalana polls second in the region
*   Message focused on curbing immigration
*   Its appeal cuts across traditional political divides
*   Traditional separatists refuse pacts with party

BARCELONA, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Almost a decade after Catalonia's failed [independence bid](https://www.reuters.com/article/world/catalan-leader-opens-door-to-secession-from-spain-after-vote-idUSKCN1C60Y5/), a growing number of voters are shifting their focus from secession to issues such as immigration and crime, fuelling the rise of the far-right separatist Aliança ​Catalana.

The party, which draws much of its support from working- and middle-class voters in rural areas outside Barcelona, has surged in the polls and now ‌trails only Spain's ruling Socialists ahead of Catalonia's next election in 2028.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fcatalonias-far-right-surge-divides-independence-camp-migration-fears-grow-2026-09-23%2F)

While Aliança says it would seek to break away from Madrid unilaterally if it won power in the wealthy northeastern region, its message is focused far more on curbing immigration and improving public safety.

Its growing influence is reshaping Catalan politics. Earlier this month, riot police prevented violent clashes between Aliança supporters and left-wing separatists in Barcelona, overshadowing Catalonia's September 11 national ​day celebrations, which have historically drawn large pro-independence crowds.

The episode highlighted divisions within [the separatist movement](https://www.reuters.com/world/eus-top-court-upholds-spains-amnesty-law-catalan-separatists-2026-07-16/), potentially complicating efforts to form a coalition to unseat the region's ruling ​Socialist Party. Traditional pro-independence parties have ruled out governing agreements with Aliança.

As its support has grown, other separatist parties have adopted more conservative ⁠positions, including lobbying Madrid to let the region restrict migration.

The party's appeal cuts across Catalonia's traditional political divides. Much of its support comes from voters who previously backed the separatist ​centre-right Junts or the far-right, staunchly anti-independence Vox, according to a Catalan government survey published in July.

## STRAIGHT-TALKING LEADER

Aliança's rise has been driven largely by its outspoken leader, Silvia Orriols, 41, who ​studied to become a librarian and comes from a middle-class farming family.

Orriols told Reuters her party was tapping into frustration with established politicians and concerns that immigration was diluting Catalan identity.

"People have regained hope and drive to fight for the restoration of the Catalan state, to implement policies aimed at preserving our identity," said Orriols, who frequently invokes Catalonia's history in her speeches.

She said far-right Alternative for Germany's [victory](https://www.reuters.com/world/germanys-far-right-afd-seeks-landmark-state-victory-saxony-anhalt-votes-2026-09-06/) in Saxony-Anhalt state ​earlier this month showed that "Europe is awakening".

"We Europeans are shielding ourselves in order to survive," she said.

Aliança rose to prominence in 2023 after Orriols won a local election in Ripoll. ​Her anti-Muslim message gained traction in the mountainous town where most of the Moroccan-born perpetrators of the [2017 Barcelona terror attacks](https://www.reuters.com/article/world/why-no-barriers-barcelona-attack-reignites-row-over-securing-streets-idUSKCN1AY18Y/) had lived.

The party entered Catalonia's parliament a year later with two seats. Since then, ‌it has grown ⁠from 3.8% to 16.7% of voter intentions for the next regional election, according to a poll published by El Mundo newspaper this month. It was 2.6 percentage points ahead of fellow separatist party ERC.

Eloi Radovan, whose family traditionally backed left-wing pro-independence parties like ERC, is among those who have shifted their support to Aliança.

"I feel betrayed," said Radovan, 19, referring to how parties like ERC and Junts failed to follow through on the [2017 referendum](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/key-dates-catalonias-independence-bid-subsequent-events-2021-09-24/) in which Catalans voted in favour of independence. He also criticised their cooperation with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

He ​supports Aliança's call for a total ban on ​migration because, he said, "Catalonia is increasingly becoming ⁠less Catalan".

Junts is seeking to counter Aliança's appeal by presenting itself as a more pragmatic centrist alternative while offering its own proposals on migration and security. Two senior Junts officials told Reuters they viewed Aliança's plans as unrealistic and discriminatory.

## CHANGING CONCERNS

The party's gains have coincided with ​shifting priorities among Catalan voters.

Affordable housing, migration and crime topped the list of concerns in the July survey. Two years earlier, political ​dissatisfaction and Catalonia's relationship ⁠with the rest of Spain ranked highest.

"The (2017) independence push was driven by economic anxiety, whereas Aliança responds to demographic anxiety," said historian Joan Esculies.

Aliança's rise is "an expression of frustration at the lack of a viable path towards independence and a cry born of fear as new waves of immigration pose a greater threat to (Catalan) language," he said.

Yet support for independence has remained resilient despite divisions within ⁠the movement ​and the loss of the regional presidency in 2024 after a decade in power. The July survey showed 45% ​backing independence, down from a peak of 49% in 2017.

Critics say Aliança is exploiting those frustrations rather than offering solutions.

The party offers no real solutions and other separatists must combat its "xenophobic, racist discourse of exclusion," said left-wing separatist ​Hug Lucchetti, 45, during this month's protests.

"The independence movement is alive," he said. "New ranks of activists continue to emerge."

Reporting by Joan Faus, Editing by Aislinn Laing, Charlie Devereux and Ros Russell

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Joan is a Barcelona-based correspondent reporting on politics, economics and social issues, such as migration and the car industry’s green transition, and also conducting investigative pieces. With over 15 years of experience, Joan previously worked as Washington correspondent for Spain’s leading newspaper EL PAÍS, closely covering the Obama and Trump administrations, electoral campaigns and major news; at Spanish newspapers Ara and Público in Madrid, and at EFE news agency in Buenos Aires and Barcelona. He is a journalism graduate from Barcelona’s Autonomous University, including an exchange program in Amsterdam and New York, and holds a business executive degree from IESE Business School

title: Taiwan, human rights are 'red lines' for China, ambassador says ahead of Trump, Xi meeting
summary: Item 1 of 2 Members of a U.S. military honor guard roll up a Chinese flag after rehearsing for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit next week with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., September 16,
content:
Item 1 of 2 Members of a U.S. military honor guard roll up a Chinese flag after rehearsing for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit next week with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst

**[1/2]**Members of a U.S. military honor guard roll up a Chinese flag after rehearsing for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit next week with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/preparations-ahead-of-chinese-president-xis-meeting-with-us-president-trump-at-the-white-house-in-washington/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkZLTkFOMlJROA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Presidents Xi and Trump to meet in Washington this week
*   China has repeatedly called for end to US arms sales to Taiwan
*   US has yet to approve new $14 bln arms package for Taiwan
*   People's Daily says US has 'erroneous' perceptions of China

BEIJING/TAIPEI, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Taiwan and human ​rights are "red lines" for China that cannot be crossed, the country's ambassador to the US warned on Wednesday, striking a firm tone ahead ‌of this week's leadership summit in Washington.

Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit Washington for a summit with President Donald Trump, as both sides look to bring stability to ties overshadowed by arguments over everything from [trade](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/xi-rolls-into-trump-summit-with-chinas-trade-engine-roaring-2026-09-21/) to [Taiwan](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinas-xi-expected-press-trump-halt-taiwan-arms-sales-under-1982-agreement-2026-09-22/).

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fchinas-us-ambassador-warns-red-lines-ahead-trump-xi-meeting-2026-09-23%2F)

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

Writing in the ruling Communist Party's official People's Daily on the day Xi is due to leave, Ambassador Xie Feng said managing differences hinges on good faith, and the ​US should stop "fabricating pretexts" such as national security, economic imbalances and forced labour to try to and constrain China.

When China and the US cooperate, both ​benefit, but when they confront each other, both suffer, he added.

"China's sovereignty, security, and development interests cannot be violated, and ⁠four red lines — the Taiwan question, democracy and human rights, development paths and systems, and development rights — cannot be challenged," Xie said.

"China is committed to pursuing peaceful development ​and hopes the US will move toward this as well."

China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite the objections of the government in Taipei.

## TAIWAN TENSIONS

The US ​is Taiwan's most important arms supplier and international backer, and China has repeatedly demanded weapons sales to Taiwan end.

After a May summit in Beijing with Xi, Trump said he was holding a [new arms package](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-thanks-us-support-ahead-further-trump-xi-talks-2026-05-15/), worth around $14 billion, in abeyance and described it as a "very good negotiating chip".

A senior Taiwan security official told reporters that Beijing views any delay in US arms transfers as ​a direct way to slow Taiwan's military build up, giving China more room to expand pressure around Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines.

China could use a package of ​inducements, including purchases of US goods or gestures on Middle East tensions, to convince Trump that reduced US military commitments in the region could buy broader cooperation from Beijing, the official ‌said, speaking ⁠on condition of anonymity.

China's military has significantly increased the number of naval, coast guard and research ships around Taiwan, in the South and East China Seas, and collecting data on things like undersea cables that could be useful for war, the official said.

China's defence ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

China's foreign ministry reiterated its "resolute opposition" to US arms sales, saying the Taiwan issue was its "core of core interests" and the political foundation of Sino-US ties.

China has never renounced the use of force to ​bring Taiwan under its control, though ​says it would prefer "peaceful reunification".

In Beijing, ⁠a spokesperson for Taiwan Affairs Office said it was Taiwan that was "deliberately" escalating confrontation.

"Scheming for independence is the primary culprit in destroying peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait and undermining the status quo," spokesperson Zhu Fenglian said.

## 'ERRONEOUS' US PERCEPTIONS

A separate commentary ​on Wednesday in the People's Daily said Washington's "erroneous" perceptions of China and its inability to let go of the notion ​of strategic competition are ⁠the basic causes of their difficult relationship.

"In recent years, the tortuous path China-US relations have travelled clearly shows the US's erroneous perceptions of China and its unwillingness to let go of the notion of 'strategic competition' are the fundamental cause of recurring difficulties," said the commentary, without offering details.

Both sides should cherish the favourable momentum that has come at "great cost, ⁠maintain the ​right direction, and eliminate interference", said the article, published under the pen name "Zhong Sheng", meaning "Voice of ​China" and used to give views on foreign policy.

"The US side, in particular, needs to maintain continuity and stability in its policies, honour its commitments, and inject certainty into bilateral relations," it added.

Reporting by Liz Lee and Yimou Lee; Additional reporting and writing by Ben Blanchard in Taipei; Editing by Michael Perry and Stephen Coates

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Liz Lee covers an extensive range of China-related stories from Beijing, including diplomacy, policy, economic data and extreme weather events. She has reported on breaking news and enterprise stories from when she joined Reuters in Malaysia. She previously focused on corporate deals and news in Kuala Lumpur, from IPOs to labour issues. Liz is a fellow at the International Strategic Forum and is part of the Oxford Climate Journalism Network. Her work also contributed to a story picked as a Pulitzer finalist looking into scam centres in Southeast Asia.

Yimou Lee is a Senior Correspondent for Reuters covering everything from Taiwan, including sensitive Taiwan-China relations, China's military aggression and Taiwan's key role as a global semiconductor powerhouse. A three-time SOPA award winner, his reporting from Hong Kong, China, Myanmar and Taiwan over the past decade includes Myanmar's crackdown on Rohingya Muslims, Hong Kong protests and Taiwan's battle against China's multifront campaigns to absorb the island.

title: 悉尼國際器官移植大會 法輪功揭中共活摘罪行
