He went on to serve as a vice chairman of the CPPCC until 2023.

Two business leaders, industrialist Ann Tse-kai and tycoon Henry Fok, who both served as vice chairs of the CPPCC, were given state funerals in 2000 and 2006, respectively.

Chinese state media described Tung as a “renowned patriot”, while his successor, Tsang, called him “an easy-going, gentle and refined man with a broad-minded outlook and far-reaching vision”.

Critics recalled his tenure as marked by governance struggles and public discontent that never fully recovered after the financial crisis.

title: Merz under pressure as two more German states go to the polls
summary: Item 1 of 3 German Chancellor and Christian Democratic Union (CDU) leader Friedrich Merz speaks during a CDU election campaign rally for his party's top candidate Stefan Evers before state elections in Berlin, Germany, September 17, 2026. R
content:
Item 1 of 3 German Chancellor and Christian Democratic Union (CDU) leader Friedrich Merz speaks during a CDU election campaign rally for his party's top candidate Stefan Evers before state elections in Berlin, Germany, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Fabrizio Bensch

**[1/3]**German Chancellor and Christian Democratic Union (CDU) leader Friedrich Merz speaks during a CDU election campaign rally for his party's top candidate Stefan Evers before state elections in Berlin, Germany, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Fabrizio Bensch [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/germanys-merz-rallies-for-his-partys-berlin-state-elections-top-candidate-stefan-evers-in-berlin/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjNMTkFGWkNRWg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Elections in Berlin and eastern German state set to pile more pressure on unpopular chancellor
*   Far-right AfD expected to make strong gains but no repeat of Saxony-Anhalt triumph
*   Latest polls show centre-left ahead in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
*   Berlin polls show far-left overtaking Merz's conservatives

BERLIN, Sept 20 (Reuters) - German voters go to the polls on Sunday in two state elections ​that look likely to heap more pressure on struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose future has been [in the balance](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/merzs-fate-balance-second-eastern-german-state-goes-polls-2026-09-16/) since the far right's triumph ‌in another regional vote this month.

The elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in the formerly communist east, and the capital Berlin follow the [September 6 election](https://www.reuters.com/world/germanys-far-right-afd-seeks-landmark-state-victory-saxony-anhalt-votes-2026-09-06/) in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came close to the rare feat of winning an absolute majority.

Get a look at the day ahead in European and global markets with the Morning Bid Europe newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/morning-bid-europe/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Feurope%2Fmerz-under-pressure-two-more-german-states-go-polls-2026-09-20%2F)

Regional elections would not usually draw much interest outside Germany, but the AfD's success in Saxony-Anhalt, which it sees as the ​first step towards winning federal elections due in 2029, has sent shock waves through Europe.

In just over a decade, the party, which wants to take tough ​action to deport foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, has ⁠transformed itself from a fringe eurosceptic movement to the country's most popular party.

Opinion polls indicate it is unlikely to repeat its victory in Saxony-Anhalt in either of Sunday's ​votes. But they are both expected to underscore the huge advances it has made in recent years and raise fresh questions over the so-called "firewall" strategy, under which the other ​main parties refuse to enter coalition agreements with it.

For Merz, whose approval ratings have plunged as low as 14%, according to the latest polls, the result was the latest in a series of blows that have raised growing doubts in his own conservative Christian Democratic Union party about whether he can continue to lead.

In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU looks likely to suffer its worst-ever election ​result, with the most recent opinion poll by the Forschungsgruppe Wahlen on Friday putting it at just 6% and at risk of failing to clear the minimum threshold ​to enter the state parliament.

## MERZ HAS STRUGGLED

Elected last year on a promise of ambitious reforms to return Germany's stagnant economy to growth, Merz has struggled to win over sceptical voters, compounding resentment ‌over unpopular ⁠pension, tax and healthcare reforms with a stream of gaffes and communication missteps.

For the moment at least, [senior figures in the CDU](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/german-conservative-state-premiers-back-embattled-merz-joint-statement-2026-09-16/) have rallied behind him, aware that replacing the chancellor - which would in any case be difficult on constitutional grounds - would leave any successor facing the same deep economic problems.

But disillusion with his government has hung over the campaigns in both Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, where voters have focused on issues including soaring energy and housing costs.

Surging fuel prices, felt acutely in a state like Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania ​where many rely on cars for transport, ​have put pressure on Merz to ⁠agree relief measures with his Social Democrat coalition partners.

On Friday, [he presented](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/germany-plans-cut-energy-tax-lower-petrol-prices-bild-reports-2026-09-18/) a relief package that included tax cuts on gas and diesel.

In the rural state, polls have shown the race narrowing over recent weeks as the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) have centred their campaign ​around popular [state premier Manuela Schwesig](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/merzs-fate-balance-second-eastern-german-state-goes-polls-2026-09-16/). The Wahlen poll on Friday showed the SPD edging in front of the AfD for the ​first time in months.

The ⁠poll put the SPD on 37%, the AfD on 36%, the far-left Left Party on 9% and the environmental Greens on 5%, just at the threshold for entering parliament. Both parties would be potential coalition partners for Schwesig.

In Berlin, the Wahlen poll showed the far-left Left Party moving ahead of the CDU, threatening the conservative hold on the mayor's office ⁠in a campaign ​that has focused heavily on housing affordability. Even in liberal Berlin, however, the AfD has made strong ​gains, moving into third place.

The latest poll puts the Left Party on 22%, the CDU on 20%, the Greens on 15% and the SPD on 12%. The AfD sits on 18%, while the far-left BSW, ​the only party that has said it might agree to work with the AfD, is just under the parliamentary threshold on 4%.

Reporting by James Mackenzie; Editing by Ros Russell

title: China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenario
summary: When reporters asked Donald Trump this week if he supported calls to slow down the development of artificial intelligence out of growing fears for cybersecurity, public safety and the fate of humanity, he said no. His argument: [China](http
content:
When reporters asked Donald Trump this week if he supported calls to slow down the development of artificial intelligence out of growing fears for cybersecurity, public safety and the fate of humanity, he said no. His argument: [China](https://www.theguardian.com/world/china).

“We’re leading China in AI,” Trump said. “We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to ⁠keep it that way, because whoever wins AI, wins.”

Trump was echoing a message the AI industry has put out for years. The US is in a heated technological race with China, companies including Anthropic and [OpenAI have argued](https://www.axios.com/2025/03/25/chris-lehane-openai-china-copyright), and any regulation that would cede the contest risks incalculable economic and political harm.

Even as Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s CEO, [led an industry-wide call this week](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/sep/14/ai-ceo-safety-slowdown) to “pace the frontier”, he declared that the US could only slow down to the point where China could not catch up.

“If we greatly restrain our AI capabilities in the belief that China will do the same, and then China defects, AI could be so powerful that such a defection could lead to their geopolitical dominance,” Amodei warned.

The AI industry’s concerns about China may come with self-serving economic incentives, but they also reflect a strain of hawkish foreign policy toward Beijing that has become entrenched in tech.

In recent years, parts of Silicon Valley have positioned themselves as the vanguard in a new cold war with China, arguing fiercely that the industry’s technological advancements are essential to both US hegemony and the liberal world order. This view has taken hold across tech’s different ideological camps, creating strange bedfellows of AI safety advocates, techno-militarists and neoconservatives, all of them fearful of Beijing.

AI companies have hired former top US government staffers from both the Biden and Trump administrations to shape public strategy and analyze geopolitical risk, setting up in-house policy teams. Influential tech leaders have meanwhile written essays and policy documents calling for efforts to deter and degrade China’s AI capabilities, sometimes advocating for threatening armed conflict if necessary, in an attempt to influence foreign policy.

As public calls for reining in the AI industry intensify and the risks associated with the technology increase, various industry forces are trying to ensure they are the ones with the answer to the question “what about China?”.

Anthropic and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment for this article.

## **Amodei’s worst China fears**

Few have been more vocal about the threat of Chinese state-controlled artificial intelligence than Amodei. The Anthropic CEO has argued for years that one of the reasons he’s so animated to advance AI is to ensure that the technology falls into the hands of Democratic governments and not oppressive regimes such as China.

Amodei’s position has made him one of Silicon Valley’s most vocal critics of China’s tech industry, separating him from fellow AI leaders such as OpenAI CEO [Sam Altman](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/sam-altman) or Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg, who frame the competition more in corporate or economic terms; and people such as Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s CEO, who have encouraged the use of Chinese AI models. Demis Hassabis, the leader of Google Deepmind, has made few public remarks on China in comparison with his peers.

“Sam Altman doesn’t have especially strong views when it comes to China. Anthropic is a totally different story,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution. “Amodei is really, really focused on a particular view of the risk from AI and what he frames as basically a struggle between a world dominated by authoritarian AI versus democratic AI”.

Amodei’s argument, which he has laid out over a series of essays, is that China acquiring superpowered AI is one of the most severe threats posed by the technology. He believes humanity is approaching the creation of an ultra-advanced AI, and that such a tool would give an authoritarian state the ability to create a “swarm of millions or billions of fully automated armed drones” that would be “capable of both defeating any military in the world and suppressing dissent within a country by following around every citizen”.

“There are a number of possible arguments against the severity of these threats, and I wish I believed them, because AI-enabled authoritarianism terrifies me,” Amodei wrote in January in an essay called The Adolescence of Technology.

Amodei has long asserted that in order to stop China’s advancement, the US and its allies should take aggressive action to limit Chinese AI companies’ growth – most notably blocking the sale of advanced semiconductor chips and manufacturing equipment necessary for improving AI. (Huang of Nvidia has bristled at this position, [calling export controls a failure](https://www.wsj.com/world/asia/nvidias-huang-calls-u-s-export-controls-a-failure-praises-trump-060940b5) and urging Trump to ease restrictions.)

But Amodei’s position was perhaps most on display last weekend, in his response to warnings from a young Anthropic researcher who resigned, predicting human extinction by the end of the decade at the digital hands of AI. The apocalyptic string of tweets by Jacob Coxon did not mention China. But the specter across the Pacific looms so large in the Anthropic CEO’s mind that, when outlining how to prevent human extinction, beating Beijing was paramount.

Amodei has built a team that shares his views. He for example hired Tarun Chhabra, former Biden-era national security council staffer, as Anthropic’s head of national security policy. Chhabra has campaigned against the sale of chips to China and has called for a full-scale government effort to curb the Chinese Communist party’s AI advancements.

“The CCP does not seek complementarity or coexistence or comparative advantage with the United States or our allies. Instead, the CCP seeks run-the-table dominance and control of the most critical technologies and supply chains,” Chhabra told a Senate hearing last year, adding that he believed the Biden administration did not take decisive or rapid enough action to maintain the US lead against China.

Dario Amodei speaks at Dreamforce 2026 summit in San Francisco, California, in September.  Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters

Amodei’s concern over export controls has also placed him in the company of other influential China hawks. He wrote an op-ed for the Wall Street Journal last year with Matt Pottinger, the architect of Trump’s first-term China policy, urging the administration to clamp down on chip exports. Pottinger, a visiting fellow at the conservative Hoover Institution and author of a book on how to defend Taiwan against a Chinese attack, argued in 2024 that the US and China were in the “foothills of a great-power hot war”.

Anthropic and Amodei’s stance on China puts the company in strange tension with its own domestic policy. The company has spent millions lobbying for increased government oversight and safety measures. At the same time as Anthropic advocates for more safeguards, it has made clear that it will aggressively oppose any policy it perceives as giving China the chance to overtake the US.

“There’s something that’s really important that everyone hears from Anthropic,” Sarah Heck, the company’s head of public policy, said at [a Politico event](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/16/anthropic-policy-chief-says-winning-ai-race-key-for-safety-01078981) on Wednesday. “The United States needs to stay in the lead on AI and you cannot do safety from second place.”

Understanding the beliefs of AI companies and CEOs such as Amodei is particularly important, experts say, because the Trump administration’s laissez faire policy towards the AI industry has meant that private companies are the primary actors in shaping public policy.

“It would be akin to having the entire pharmaceutical industry be just completely unregulated,” Chan said. “It’s kind of amazing and ultimately boils down to one thing, which is Trump has been very reluctant to want to regulate because he doesn’t want to slow down the AI boom and the effect that it’s having on the economy.”

Anthropic is not the only company to hire and align with former top policy staffers, with [OpenAI](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/openai) hiring the author of Trump’s AI action plan Dean Ball as “head of strategic futures” earlier this year. While Ball has criticized Amodei’s framing of the competition with China,, he has expressed a similar pessimism on US-China cooperation.

“There was a time when it was possible to believe we could each pursue our strengths, enrich our respective economies, and grow together. Alas, such harmony now appears impossible,” Ball wrote of China last year. “We are locked into a structural conflict.”

## **Silicon Valley’s China****hawks**

Although Amodei is the AI industry’s most prominent voice on China, fears of Beijing gaining advanced AI capabilities and using them for global domination run through Silicon Valley.

Several of the tech figures focused on China have connections, like Amodei himself, to the effective altruism movement – a quasi-utilitarian idea that society should focus on projects that maximize the good and reduce the most harm for humanity. The movement tends to overlap with AI safety advocates who worry about the longterm, existential risks of the technology.

Leopold Aschenbrenner, a 25-year-old former OpenAI researcher, founder of an influential AI hedge fund, and husband to Amodei’s chief of staff, called for a government-led effort to reach super-intelligent AI before China in a 165-page paper.

“Super-intelligence will give a decisive economic and military advantage. China isn’t at all out of the game yet. In the race to AGI, the free world’s very survival will be at stake,” Aschenbrenner wrote in 2024.

The position of Aschenbrenner, who made headlines earlier this year when his hedge fund lost $35bn in less than a month, was echoed in Washington. When the typically hawkish US-China cconomic and security review commission issued its annual report to Congress a few months after Aschenbrenner’s manifesto, the congressional advisory committee’s number one suggestion was to “establish and fund a Manhattan Project-like program dedicated to racing to and acquiring an Artificial General Intelligence”.

Grand strategy proposals from the AI industry on China are not solely contained within the effective altruist movement. In 2025, Google co-founder Eric Schmidt, Alexander Wang, Scale AI founder (now head of AI at Meta), and Dan Hendrycks, Center for AI Safety director, wrote a wide-ranging strategic deterrence doctrine called Mutual Assured AI Malfunction (Maim). Their paper applies the cold war framework of Mutually Assured Destruction (Mad) with nuclear weapons and applies it to AI, proposing that the US and China could achieve geopolitical stability through threatening espionage, cyberattacks and potential military strikes against each other if either state pursues a monopoly on AI.

“A nation with sole possession of super-intelligence might be as overwhelming as the Conquistadors were to the Aztecs,” the paper warns.

## **Nuclear considered an option**

Some leading AI thinkers have argued for extreme measures to deal with AI advancement from nations such as China. Eliezer Yudkowsky, one of the earliest and loudest voices of the AI safety movement, has argued that the US should be willing to carry out airstrikes against foreign data centers and risk nuclear war in order to make rival states comply with a global AI moratorium.

content:
华盛顿 —

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期二(9月29日)与美国主要科技企业高管举行白宫会议后表示，美国在超级智能竞赛中遥遥领先中国，不愿同中国共同推进相关技术，以免中方迅速获得美国企业掌握而中国尚不掌握的技术。

“我们处于领先地位。既然如此，我为什么还要做任何事情？”特朗普说。他认为，与中国合作可能把美国公司开发的机密交出去。

不过，白宫没有宣布取消习近平访问华盛顿后公布的相关安排。[白宫](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/09/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-advances-a-fair-and-reciprocal-relationship-with-china-while-hosting-historic-state-visit/)和中国外交部都表示，两国将于11月再次举行超级智能/人工智能(SI/AI)对话，就这项技术的风险和惠益交换意见，并建立人工智能事件双边沟通渠道。

特朗普总统的此番言论揭示了这些安排背后的核心矛盾：世界上两个主要超级智能/人工智能大国都希望防止意外或网络事件升级，但双方也都把技术领先地位视为不应与对手分享的战略和经济资产。

就在同一天，特朗普总统签署[行政命令](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/09/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence/)，要求行政部门在不涉及法定措辞的官方沟通中，以“超级智能”(super intelligence，简称SI)取代“人工智能”。行政命令仍沿用现有的人工智能法律定义，并要求白宫科技政策负责人在60天内提出“超级智能”的联邦定义。

华盛顿把新的双边机制称为“美中超级智能对话”，北京发布的声明则称之为“中美人工智能对话”。

专家说，比名称更重要的问题是：两国政府能否界定什么构成需要通报的事件、由谁负责报告，以及在不暴露国家安全能力或企业知识产权的情况下可以分享多少技术信息。

美中科技问题专家在接受美国之音(VOA)采访时认为，鉴于特朗普总统反对美中合作开发SI/AI，而且反对过度监管，主张超级智能企业自律并以美国法律为护栏，拟议中的美中沟通渠道短期内不太可能带来联合研发、对模型能力的实质限制或更广泛的安全协议，但是可能帮助两国政府就自主AI/SI智能体的危险行为或其他跨境事件相互通报。

**哪些事件会启动沟通机制？**

专门研究中国和科技政策的DGA-奥尔布赖特石桥集团合伙人保罗·特廖洛(Paul Triolo)说，最可能启动这一渠道的情况，是失控AI智能体未经授权进入美国或中国的网站及其他互联网资源。

近期事件使这种风险不再只是理论设想。据路透社报道，在一次安全测试中，近700个使用OpenAI模型构建的自主智能体侵入人工智能平台Hugging Face，并试图伪造日志以掩盖行动。澳大利亚随后表示，一个OpenAI智能体侵入了政府医疗数据门户，OpenAI已为此道歉。最新披露的加拿大事件又增加了一个案例，不过加拿大没有发现系统遭到入侵，事件归属也仍不确定。

这些事件引发了一个问题：一旦智能体离开受控测试环境，模型开发商是否还能持续掌握它们的行为？

特廖洛说，两国政府首先需要建立机制，要求主要人工智能企业在国内报告严重事件；随后还要商定一个共同门槛，决定什么情况下事件严重到需要通知对方政府。

“可能需要一些技术人员专门投入这一职能，”他对美国之音说。这些人员可以在国家级人工智能安全机构或新的监管部门内工作。

布鲁金斯学会约翰·桑顿中国中心研究员陈凯新(Kyle Chan)说，启动门槛可以包括造成严重人身伤害或经济损失的事件。例如，AI意外发动网络攻击，导致医院系统瘫痪。

乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心(CSET)研究员萨姆·布雷斯尼克(Sam Bresnick)也认为，自主网络活动是最可能启动这一渠道的事件。美国或中国实验室开发的智能体可能未经授权进入医院、供水系统或其他关键网络。他说，两国政府尚未说明，这一渠道是否也涵盖军事事件，例如无人机或无人潜航器发生碰撞。

布鲁金斯学会(Brookings Institution)史卓卜·塔尔博特安全、战略与技术中心高级研究员梅拉妮·W·西森(Melanie W. Sisson)则把问题分为两大类：一类是企业或实验室研发过程中出现的意外和不可预期行为；另一类是利用人工智能发动的蓄意攻击。

她说，如果事件涉及核指挥控制系统或可能产生同样严重后果的关键基础设施，沟通不应停留在较低层级，而应迅速上升到两国领导人层面。

SI/AI事件发生后的最初几个小时内，官员可能无法判断它究竟是意外、犯罪行为还是由国家指使。西森说，有效的沟通渠道应当减少各方仓促归责和报复的压力。布雷斯尼克则警告，实验室可能要几周甚至几个月后才发现智能体的活动，技术调查和归责还可能需要更长时间。

“从事情发生，到启动通报机制，两者之间必然会有时间差，”布雷斯尼克说。

他表示，视事件性质而定，双方可以交换有关攻击基本性质、系统如何绕过安全措施以及可能影响的信息；也可以交流测试和防御方面的经验，而不披露源代码、模型权重或其他专有技术细节。

这一区分至关重要。事件通报并不等同于技术合作。沟通渠道可以让一方说明某个危险系统已经失控、确定受到影响的网络并协调遏制行动，而不要求任何一方帮助对方开发能力更强的模型。

这一渠道也可能降低误判风险。布雷斯尼克说，一国政府可以利用它向另一方说明，某项恶意活动虽然源自一家人工智能实验室，但并非国家有意发动的攻击。西森说，两国可以从原则性的声明开始，承认双方都可能受到灾难性的SI/AI智能故障威胁，并负有防止此类事件引发常规冲突或核冲突的责任。

**类似对手间的军控谈判？**

美国外交关系协会(CFR)中国与新兴技术高级研究员、前白宫国家安全委员会官员克里斯·麦奎尔(Chris McGuire)认为，美中峰会取得的有限成果，可能已经接近当前两国关系所能承受的上限。

他说，美国在前沿人工智能领域仍然领先，但中国距离美国足够近，仍相信自己能够赶上。这造成了一个不稳定的谈判环境：华盛顿不愿牺牲领先地位，北京也没有多少动力接受可能固化其劣势的限制。

“在这种情况下，这两个国家进行军控谈判，其实没有任何历史先例，”麦奎尔在一场由美国之音查阅的[CFR讨论](https://www.cfr.org/event/media-briefing-unpacking-the-trump-xi-summit)中说。

他认为，对话可以帮助两国政府对先进系统可能给双方造成的伤害形成共同理解，基本的事件沟通渠道也可以发挥建立互信的作用。但当两国政府都把人工智能领先视为国家优先事项时，要求双方共同放慢发展速度并不现实。

麦奎尔在那次讨论中说，现阶段，对话应聚焦共同风险，而不是寻求一项包罗万象的交易。

**沟通渠道能否承受政治压力？**

特廖洛说，一个设计得当的事件通报机制可能在双边关系紧张时期继续运作。不过，它能否持久，将取决于通过这一渠道传递哪些信息，以及如何保护这些信息。

有用的通报可能需要主要实验室提供技术细节，而这些细节可能暴露系统漏洞或具有商业敏感性的数据，从而引发美国国会议员的质疑。他们担心安全合作可能帮助中国企业缩小差距。

“在人工智能相关问题上建立两国之间的互信与合作，将是一个长期而复杂的过程，”特廖洛说。

布雷斯尼克的看法更为谨慎。他指出，在双边关系紧张时期，中国过去经常不使用已经建立的军事危机沟通渠道。因此，他认为各方应当对新的人工智能渠道能发挥多大作用抱有“审慎的预期”。

这一沟通渠道还将与先进半导体、出口管制、涉嫌模型蒸馏以及中国开放权重系统等争端并行存在。

**11月会谈能有什么成果？**

陈凯新说，两国11月会谈取得有意义的进展并不需要一项范围广泛的协议。双方如果能初步交换安全做法和近期事件的基本信息，就足以表明两国都在认真对待这一机制。

对布雷斯尼克来说，近期最现实的议程甚至更为有限：双方交换对人工智能风险的认知，并讨论各自政府能够在本国体系内采取哪些降低风险的措施。

“短期内，最容易取得进展的是这场风险讨论，”他说。他补充说，只要华盛顿仍担心帮助竞争对手、北京仍怀疑美国的安全提议是另一种技术遏制，更深入的合作在近期内就不现实。

布鲁金斯学会的西森说，她对于11月会议能否取得重大进展并不乐观，但仍希望双方哪怕只迈出渐进的一小步，也能建立一个可以继续发展的基础。在一段由竞争定义的关系中，这或许是衡量成功最现实的标准。

title: Israel: Start-up Nation and Soup Kitchen Nation

content:
**_K_.: How did a French immigrant living in Israel come to found _Latet_? What in your personal journey led you to establish this organization?**

**Gilles Darmon:**When I arrived in Israel, my suitcase contained three T-shirts, a cassette player, and all my childhood memories, and I wondered what I could do for this country. It wasn’t a matter of saying, “I’m here now; I’m Israeli; I’m going to forget my French identity.”

My conception of humanitarian action is deeply tied to my French identity. I grew up in the 1980s, a time that was, in a way, the golden age of civil society in France: the founding of Restos du Cœur, the considerable influence of Doctors Without Borders… These initiatives embodied a form of commitment that extended political action through other means. When I arrived in Israel, I told myself that we needed to develop something comparable here, because it was missing. _Latet_ is based on a model that didn’t exist in Israel: conceiving of humanitarian action as a mobilization of civil society around major issues that institutional policies neglect. It’s a transfer of French civic culture to Israel. It is therefore no coincidence that it was a Frenchman who spearheaded it.

**_K._****: When you arrived in Israel, did you already intend to work on poverty and what is now called “food insecurity”?**

**G.D.**: The term “food insecurity” emerged later, but the idea of taking a fresh approach to poverty was already there. We wanted to engage in the public debate by asserting that we could not allow the state to have a monopoly on measuring poverty while also being solely responsible for addressing it. Why poverty, then? For two reasons. The first is personal. As a Jewish and Zionist activist in France, one is condemned to engage with society solely through the prism of Israel: Is this good for Jews? Is this bad for Jews? Is something antisemitic, or not? By making my _aliyah_, I wanted to become a full-fledged citizen, capable of taking an interest in retirees, poverty, or any other issue without reducing everything to the triad of Jews-Israel-antisemitism. Poverty struck me as a universal issue, free from any identity-based lens, in a society that still had yet to be built. The second reason was strategic. We had to choose a topic that would allow us to say to Israelis: “Here is a major issue, and it’s up to you to take it on.” We had to stop systematically turning to the Diaspora for funding and expecting everything from the government. Poverty had to be a matter of civic responsibility that we needed to place at the heart of the Israeli consensus.

**_K._****: Was the situation really that serious?**

**G.D.**: When we first started, poverty hadn’t yet reached such proportions. The real breakdown—marked by a sharp rise in inequality—occurred in the 2000s. When _Latet_ was officially founded in 1996, the situation was still relatively contained. But between 2000 and 2010, the poverty rate rose sharply. Since then, it has stabilized at a very high level—over 20 percent—placing Israel among the developed countries most affected by poverty. The decision to take on this fight arose from a combination of personal motivation and an intuition about the evolution of Israeli society.

**_K_****.: In France, the creation of Restos du Cœur and other similar organizations coincided with a sense of crisis in politics in general—and on the left in particular—which were seen as incapable of addressing social issues. Did this line of thinking play a role in your decision?**

**G.D.:** To be completely honest, I didn’t have a political stance when I founded _Latet_. It wasn’t about filling an ideological void or denouncing the shortcomings of a segment of the Israeli political scene. That’s not what sparked my commitment. However, this dimension became central when poverty rose sharply and we had to ask the fundamental questions: Who is responsible? How did we get here? How can we reverse the trend? What role should the state play? And what place does the Zionist project accord to social issues? Faced with the scale of the phenomenon, our position thus became clearer: we had to remind people that social justice and the fight against poverty are an essential dimension of the Zionist project. Yet they have become the blind spot in both public debate and the state’s budgetary decisions. On paper, Israel is a welfare state. All the necessary mechanisms are in place (minimum income programs, old-age benefits, unemployment benefits, etc.). But as soon as one examines their duration and amount, it becomes clear that the state is not effective enough to bring about a lasting reduction in poverty.

> **“[Israeli economic policy] has generated wealth, but not trickle-down effects.”**

Since the reform of the Israeli economy that began in the 1980s, all governments—both right-wing and left-wing—have followed the same course: a liberal policy inspired by the Chicago School and trickle-down theory. Taxes are cut, the deficit is strictly controlled, and it is hoped that the wealth created by entrepreneurs will eventually benefit the poorest segments of the population. The result is clear: this policy has generated value, but no trickle-down effect. Israel’s growth over the past thirty years has been exceptional. These were, in a sense, our “Glorious Thirty.” Excluding the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic, growth averaged around 4 percent, reaching 7 percent in some years. With the exception of China and a few other countries, few economies have experienced such momentum over such a long period. It is a true economic miracle. But the economic model that made this miracle possible came at a price: rising poverty. Today, depending on the method of calculation, between 2 and 2.8 million people live below the poverty line in Israel.

Based on OECD figures, Israel is the second-most poverty-stricken country within the organization, just behind Costa Rica. Two realities coexist there: the “Start-up Nation” and the “Soup Kitchen Nation.”

Credit: Latet

From the very beginning, we sought to anchor our approach within the Israeli public discourse in order to shift the conversation and ensure this issue remained at the heart of political concerns for the long term. It took time and significant effort to make our voice heard and to shed light on the issue of poverty in a country grappling with numerous conflicts and existential challenges. Today, after 30 years on the ground, _Latet_ has succeeded in bringing this issue to life by conveying a message of hope and commitment rather than one that is unnecessarily alarmist and guilt-inducing. We still have a long way to go before making the issue of poverty a central concern for Israelis.

**_K_****. : Isn’t rising poverty one of Israelis’ major concerns?**

**G.D.**: For the past twenty years, we’ve asked the same question every year: What do Israelis consider to be the most important problem facing society? We hoped to see poverty gradually rise in the rankings. But depending on the period, it’s education, corruption, security, or even political polarization that tops the list. The place of poverty among Israelis’ concerns is actually inversely proportional to the security situation. With every new crisis, security immediately rises to the top of the list, while poverty almost entirely disappears from the debate. It then slowly rises again, until the next shock, which relegates it once more to the background.

> **_“Poverty’s place among Israelis’ concerns is, in fact, inversely proportional to the security situation.”_**

Unfortunately, we have not succeeded in making poverty a lasting top priority for Israelis. On the other hand, we have succeeded in more strongly promoting the idea of a duty of solidarity, as well as issues of resilience and social capital.

In the weeks following October 7, the concerns of the majority of Israelis turned almost exclusively toward the war and the fate of the hostages. It was virtually impossible to raise other issues that, nevertheless, had not disappeared. On the contrary: the war has only exacerbated the situation of poverty; as is always the case in times of crisis, the vulnerable become even more vulnerable and are the first to pay the price of the crisis.

**_K_****: Let’s talk specifically about those who are getting involved, starting with the volunteers. According to your 2025 report,****_Latet_****has mobilized approximately 46,000 of them. What is their profile? Has it changed since October 7, in the context of the widespread mobilization of Israeli civil society?**

**G.D.**: Among our tens of thousands of volunteers, we have a core group of about 2,000 volunteers whom we know well and with whom we communicate regularly. Most are between the ages of 35 and 55, which is quite unusual.

Volunteering generally attracts many teenagers and retirees; we, for our part, have succeeded in engaging people in the prime of their working lives who choose to devote part of their time to social action. Has their profile changed since October 7? No. What has changed is their number: many more people have wanted to get involved. This phenomenon, however, remains cyclical. After October 7, participation reached an exceptional level: it is estimated that nearly 40% of Israelis volunteered or made a donation—that is, almost one in two Israelis. Since then, this figure has declined, but it remains at a relatively high level.

**_K_****: Are the beneficiaries mostly people from the Jewish population? Is aid provided regardless of background?****_Latet_****—does it operate throughout the country? I ask because when reading the word “Israeli,” some people—sometimes in bad faith—might wonder whether your work also reaches the Arab population, the Bedouins, and residents of the outskirts.**

**G.D.:** Our criterion is vulnerability, not community affiliation. We work in all sectors of Israeli society, and—to answer your question—we devote a great deal of energy to separating our work from the political and national debate that all too often clouds public discourse in Israel. A response that’s too specific risks assigning us to one side or the other, which I refuse to do. I don’t want to fall into the trap of saying, “We do this; we don’t do that.” I prefer to stick to a clear principle: _Latet_ has a humanitarian mission and a humanist vision to help, within the scope of its mission, people who are suffering. While Israeli identity is central to _Latet_, universalism and the deeply diverse nature of Israeli society are also part of our perspective.

We therefore help both the residents of Tel Aviv as well as Bedouins in the Negev, economically vulnerable ultra-Orthodox Jews as well as Arabs in the Galilee. Anyone who is part of the tapestry that is Israeli society can benefit from our assistance. Just like _Bituah Leum_ i, Israel’s social security system, we assist anyone in need both within and on the margins of Israeli society.

**_K._****: I’ll try to clarify my question, because the “ambiguity” you claim is itself highly political. Thirty years ago, when****_Latet_****was founded, the term “Israeli identity” did not encompass the same realities as it does today. Since then, society has become deeply divided, to the point where it sometimes feels as though we are on the brink of civil war. And this polarization centers precisely on two questions: What is Israeli identity? What is Zionism? The Israeli identity to which you refer remains, in part, an abstraction, even as conflicts—both in Israel and in the diaspora—crystallize around its definition.**

**I understand your approach: it is necessary and strategic, since you must bring together as broad a coalition as possible and make solidarity a shared responsibility. content:
**BERLIN, September 30, 2026** — Germany's Federal Foreign [Office updated](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/de/service/laender/china-node/chinasicherheit-200466) its China travel and security advisory on 29 September, reiterating that German ordinary-passport holders may enter China visa-free for stays of up to 30 days until 31 December 2026, while adding warnings that foreigners involved in civil or criminal proceedings may be barred from leaving the country.

[![Image 1: Germany China travel advisory visa-free 2026 infographic showing 30-day visa-free stays until 31 December 2026, 24-hour private accommodation registration requirement, four online registration channels, exit ban risks for civil or criminal proceedings, and entry bans of one to five years for false information. ](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/db814b_3160d286bffa46b99814de7383c71fc5~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_740,h_416,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/db814b_3160d286bffa46b99814de7383c71fc5~mv2.jpg)](https://www.visasupdate.com/post/germany-china-travel-advisory-visa-free-2026)

Germany updates China travel advisory confirming visa-free entry to end of 2026 with new exit ban warnings

## **Visa-Free Policy: Confirmed Through Year-End**

China has extended its unilateral visa-waiver arrangement for Germany and 48 other countries until **31 December 2026, 24:00**. German ordinary passport holders travelling for business, tourism, family visits, exchange programmes, or transit may enter without a visa for stays not exceeding 30 days.

Sweden was added to the scheme effective 10 November 2025, also valid until 31 December 2026. Russia's arrangement has been extended to **31 December 2027**.

Travellers who do not meet the visa-free conditions must still obtain a visa before entering China.

## **Private Accommodation: 24-Hour Registration Still Required**

The updated advisory emphasises that foreigners staying in accommodation other than hotels — such as private residences or homestays — must still complete local police registration **within 24 hours of arrival**.

According to Article 39 of China's Exit and Entry Administration Law, hotels must register foreign guests and report them to public security authorities. In cases of non-hotel accommodation, the foreign guest or their host is required to register with the local public security bureau within 24 hours.

Notably, the National Immigration Administration launched a **nationwide online accommodation registration service** on **21 September 2026**. Foreigners can now register through:

**Online Registration Channels**
NIA Government Service Platform website
"NIA 12367" mobile app
"NIA 12367" WeChat mini programme
Alipay mini programme

Registering online has the **same legal significance** as registering in person. Not registering could lead to a **warning and fine** for the foreigner or their host.

## **Exit Ban Warnings Added**

The German advisory now includes specific warnings about exit bans. Under the new Exit and Entry Regulations that took effect on **15 September 2026**, foreigners involved in **civil or criminal proceedings** may be prohibited from leaving China.

A significant expansion concerns **export control and technology import/export violations**. Chinese citizens who breach export control regulations may be deemed to endanger national industrial or technological security and barred from leaving the country. The duration of such restrictions is **not specified in the regulations**.

For foreign travellers, providing false information in a visa application or making misleading statements at the border may trigger **entry bans of one to five years**.

## **Compliance Guidance for Employers**

For German companies with substantial China operations — particularly in automotive and chemicals — the visa-free arrangement removes administrative lead time and cost for short business trips.

Mobility managers should remind employees that:

**Consideration****Detail**
**Visa-free does not permit work**Business visits only; paid employment requires a work permit
**Overstay risks**Exceeding permitted stay may trigger exit bans
**Legal dispute screening**Companies should vet whether staff face unresolved legal disputes in China before travel
**Registration and data compliance**Registration, data security, and audit-trail requirements remain in force

title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 28, 2026
summary: **CCTV: President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the U.S. last week drew close international attention. Can you share more information on this visit?** Guo Jiakun: From September 23 to 25, at the invitation of President Trump, President Xi Jin
content:
**CCTV: President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the U.S. last week drew close international attention. Can you share more information on this visit?**

Guo Jiakun: From September 23 to 25, at the invitation of President Trump, President Xi Jinping paid a successful state visit to the U.S. The two presidents had in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and world peace and development. They reached a number of important common understandings on building “a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.” Both sides agreed to support each other in successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and G20 Summit this year. China stands ready to work with the U.S. to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents and promote the steady, sound and sustainable development of China-U.S. relations.

**Xinhua News Agency: A few days ago, China successfully hosted the High-level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) at the UN headquarters in New York. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to event. Vice President Han Zheng attended the event and delivered remarks. The event was also attended by many state leaders, ministers, and heads of international organizations. Could you tell us more about the high-level dialogue?**

Guo Jiakun: On September 25, the High-level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative was successfully held at the UN headquarters in New York. More than 300 guests, including leaders and ministerial officials from member states of the Group of Friends of the GDI and heads of international organizations, attended the event. In his congratulatory letter, President Xi Jinping noted that the GDI was proposed to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, cooperation projects under the initiative have taken root and yielded outcomes in more than 120 countries. China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy and strive for more substantive progress in implementing the GDI.

Vice President Han Zheng attended the high-level dialogue. In his remarks, he elaborated on the great significance of the GDI and put forward four proposals: First, we should strengthen solidarity and coordination to fully implement the SDGs. China will continue to support the UN in strengthening the development pillar. Second, we should stay action-oriented and actively pursue development that benefits the people. China will train 10,000 engineers for developing countries over the next five years. Third, we should expand cooperation in priority areas and accelerate empowerment-driven development. China is ready to work with all parties to implement flagship projects under the GDI, including “Digital South” and “Clean Stove.” Fourth, we should strengthen partnerships to promote interconnected development. China will conduct extensive cooperation through relevant bilateral, trilateral and multilateral mechanisms to create synergy.

The substantive actions and fruitful outcomes of the GDI over the past five years speak volumes about China’s commitment to human progress and world harmony, as well as its efforts to offer China’s solutions and make China’s contributions to the common development for all countries. China stands ready to work with all parties to continuously turn the vision of the SDGs into tangible reality and to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.

**Anadolu Agency: One of the outcomes of the U.S.-China summit was that the two sides agreed on establishing an artificial intelligence dialogue. Do you think this bilateral mechanism will be a sufficient framework for global AI governance?**

Guo Jiakun: China takes a constructive and responsible part in global AI governance and acts as a solution contributor to the process. China stands for upholding the UN’s role as the main channel and building a fair and equitable global AI governance system. We are willing to maintain communication and exchanges with the U.S. through inter-governmental dialogue on AI and other channels. This is both an important pathway towards AI for good and for all, and integral to the vision of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.

**Prensa Latina: Today marks the 66th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Cuba and China. How does China view its relationship with Cuba nowadays amid turbulent international situations, even though both countries have always maintained strong bonds of friendship?**

Guo Jiakun: Since China and Cuba established the diplomatic relations 66 years ago, the two countries have maintained a deep friendship from generation to generation. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, sustained and steady progress has been made in building a community with a shared future between China and Cuba. No matter how the international landscape evolves, China will firmly support Cuba in exploring the socialist development path suited to its national conditions and in safeguarding national sovereignty and opposing external interference.

**Yonhap News Agency: The Chinese side said in a readout that Chinese and U.S. presidents exchanged views on the Korean Peninsula issue in their meetings. Could you elaborate on that?**

Guo Jiakun: During the visit, the two presidents exchanged views on major international and regional issues of mutual interest. China’s position and policy on the Korean Peninsula issue maintains consistency and continuity.

**Bloomberg: Scott Bessent said that China came up with the idea, proposed a bigger deal between the two countries, and that the U.S. was willing to entertain that bigger deal or continue on with the Busan arrangement. Can you confirm that China did indeed offer or propose a bigger deal and maybe describe what that bigger deal might entertain?**

Guo Jiakun: Competent authorities have shared information on the eighth round of China-U.S. economic and trade consultations. I’d refer you to them for more details.

**Global Times: Several permanent missions to the UN have told the media that China is weighing whether to support UNCTAD Secretary-General and former Vice President of Costa Rica Rebeca Grynspan or Guyana’s Permanent Representative to the UN Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett in the vote for the new UN Secretary-General. Can you confirm this? Which candidate is China considering supporting?**

Guo Jiakun: The election of UN Secretary-General bears on the reform and development of the UN and the vital interests of member states. China supports the selection in accordance with the UN Charter of a new Secretary-General who observes the UN Charter, shows outstanding competence, is impartial and upright, and fulfills responsibilities with dedication. China will work with all relevant parties to participate in the election process in a responsible manner.

**DPA: The German federal government commissioner for culture and the media said that on TikTok, Europe should “follow the American example,” it is dangerous to Europe’s democracy if other countries have the sensitive information, and TikTok’s European business should be “in European hands.” What is the foreign ministry’s comment?**

Guo Jiakun: China’s position on TikTok is consistent and clear.

A senior Taiwanese diplomat stated that the United States understands Taiwan’s defense needs and the military threat from China. Taiwan has been waiting for President Trump to approve a $14 billion arms sales package, following a previous $11 billion deal.

After meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Trump put the new arms package on hold and has not mentioned it since. Taiwan’s Deputy Foreign Minister, Chen Ming-chi, highlighted comments from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about careful consideration of military sales. Chen noted the severe situation in the Taiwan Strait, where China continues to build its military despite a declining economy. He emphasized that the US recognizes Taiwan’s determination to invest in its defense.

The US is legally required to support Taiwan’s self-defense, while China seeks to halt military sales. Ambassador David Perdue confirmed that US policy towards Taiwan has not changed, and Taiwan’s government asserts that only its people can decide its future amidst China’s claims of sovereignty.

content:
【大紀元2026年09月27日訊】（大紀元記者文清揚澳洲悉尼報導）「願所有良知未泯的中國人都竭盡所能，支持法輪功學員發起的拯救中國人靈魂的運動，那就是退出中國共產黨及其附屬組織」；「退出中共不是一場政治運動。恰恰相反，是人民渴望回歸正常生活、追求自由、安全與民主的呼聲。」這是9月26日在悉尼聲援三退集會上，發言嘉賓道出的心聲，發出的呼籲。

9月26日中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行集會，慶祝退黨、退團、退隊（共產黨、共青團、少先隊，簡稱三退）人數突破4. 66億這一歷史性的里程碑。

2004年11月19日，大紀元報社發表《九評共產黨》系列社論，深刻剖析了中共的邪靈本質，引發了華夏兒女精神覺醒的三退大潮。

26日中午12點，集會在嘹亮激昂的天國樂團鼓樂聲中拉開帷幕。多位發言嘉賓呼籲更多中國人選擇良知，拋棄中共。

## **中國問題專家：法輪功「真、善、忍」理念促道德覺醒**

長年關注中國人權議題的中國問題專家、悉尼科技大學（UTS）馮崇義副教授表示，法輪功學員多年來的堅持與抗爭，讓世界更多人認識中共政權的本質，並促使越來越多人拋棄中共，轉而擁抱法輪大法所提倡的普世價值。

[![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858182-f0a632fef7ecdd53b13ba13a2d442990-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858182-f0a632fef7ecdd53b13ba13a2d442990.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為悉尼科技大學（UTS）馮崇義副教授在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

馮崇義表示非常崇敬法輪功所倡導的「真、善、忍」理念，稱這是一種提升道德標準的理念，但在中共統治下，法輪功倡導的這一理念卻被視為對政權的威脅。

他以中國傳統文化中的「匹夫無罪，懷璧其罪」作比喻，點明中共對法輪功的持續迫害，本質上是極權政權對更高道德標準的恐懼。

「在中共眼中，修煉者唯一的『罪行』，就是堅持『真、善、忍』、努力提升整個民族的道德水準。」他說。

他強調，中共是一個依賴暴力、恐懼與殘暴來維持統治的極權政權。當前中共對法輪功學員的迫害，恰恰暴露了這個邪惡政權的「末日瘋狂」。

他特別提到，正因法輪功學員的勇氣、堅持與巨大努力，全世界逐步認清中共政權的殘暴與邪惡本質。

「正因如此，許多曾經加入中國共產黨、共青團和少先隊的人，如今選擇退出這些組織，轉而擁抱普世價值，以及法輪大法所倡導的新的道德理念。」他說。

他最後表示，只要越來越多的人覺醒，認識到中共政權的邪惡本質，中共必將倒臺。

## 袁紅冰教授：三退超越政治切割 是靈魂救贖

旅居澳洲的著名法學家、原北京大學法律系教授袁紅冰在集會上直言，對中國人而言，三退不僅是與中共作政治切割，更是在「拯救中國人的靈魂」。

[![Image 2](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858183-5cc2ba5c5581bd75430d57ea23fac2db-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858183-5cc2ba5c5581bd75430d57ea23fac2db.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為原北京大學法律系教授袁紅冰在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

「退黨運動不僅僅是一場要號召中國人和共產黨進行政治決裂的運動，不僅僅是希望中國人走出作為中國共產黨政治奴隸的悲慘的、屈辱的命運，更重要之處在於退出中國共產黨及其附屬組織，實際上是在拯救中國人的靈魂。」他說。

袁紅冰進一步表示，現在已經有數億人加入三退大潮。他們通過退出中共及其附屬組織的實際行動，表達與中共政權「進行徹底的政治決裂」的意願。

他堅信，當越來越多中國人選擇三退，表達希望成為「自由人」的信心和勇氣時，這種精神上的選擇將對中國未來產生影響。

在他看來，這場精神與政治覺醒並非偶然，而與法輪功學員長期向中國民眾及國際社會講述真相密切相關。他強調，「正是法輪功學員堅持了將近二十多年的不斷講真相活動，深刻揭露了中共暴政的邪惡本質，才促進了越來越多中國人的精神覺醒、政治覺醒」。

最後，袁紅冰呼籲所有「良知未泯」的中國人支持法輪功學員所發起的「拯救中國人靈魂」的運動，退出中共及其附屬組織。

## 中國民主進步聯盟代表分享自我三退經歷

中國民主進步聯盟代表紀懿宸分享了自己三退的經歷。他表示，對他而言，退出中共及其附屬組織，不只是一次聲明，更是一次按照自己意願做出選擇的經歷。

[![Image 3](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858184-dcc0e2988a411a8765e1206b80790917-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858184-dcc0e2988a411a8765e1206b80790917.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為中國民主進步聯盟代表紀懿宸在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

回顧自己的成長經歷，紀懿宸說，他很小的時候便知道法輪功，也了解到法輪大法所倡導的「真、善、忍」普世價值，很早便做了三退。

他回憶，小學時，學校要求學生加入少先隊。當時年紀尚小的他，並不了解政治，也沒有真正的選擇機會。到了初中，學校又要求他加入共青團，這件事甚至讓他與當時的班主任發生爭執。

「我從小接觸互聯網比較早，也會主動去看官方媒體之外的信息。」紀懿宸說，他當時在網上接觸到一些關於法輪功受迫害以及被活摘器官的相關報導。這些信息給他帶來衝擊，但令他更加確定的是，他不願意在沒有自由選擇的情況下，被要求加入任何政治組織。

儘管仍在學校壓力下他不得以加入了共青團。但加入後不久，他便登錄大紀元網站，公開聲明退出共青團和少先隊。

「對當時的我來說，這不僅僅是一個『三退』的聲明，更是我第一次真正按照自己的意願與中共暴政劃清界限。」他說。

他感慨道，「三退不是一句口號，而是一種態度——是對自由、良知和人格尊嚴的堅持。」

紀懿宸還分享了家人的經歷。他說，祖父年輕時曾參軍、上過戰場並負過傷，曾經為中共付出過鮮血。然而到了晚年，因家鄉發生洪水等原因，其檔案遺失，原本應有的身分和待遇長期未能落實。他表示，這些家庭經歷使他從小便開始思考，一個政權應該如何對待曾經為它付出的人，以及應該如何對待普通人的權利與尊嚴。

「也正因為這些家庭經歷和我自己的成長經歷，我逐漸形成了反對中共一黨專政的政治立場。」他說。

他表示，無論一個人是不是法輪功學員，也無論其政治立場如何，信仰自由、言論自由以及人的基本尊嚴都應該得到尊重。他呼籲更多人為信仰自由和人權發聲。

## 悉尼退黨中心代表：三退是和平覺醒運動

悉尼退黨中心代表楊裔飛發言表示，三退運動是「最大規模的和平、非暴力草根抵抗中共暴政運動」。

[![Image 4](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858210-944766372b0c8325a3a6cf13-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858210-944766372b0c8325a3a6cf13.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為中悉尼退黨中心代表楊裔飛在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

楊女士表示，許多中國人從兒童時期開始，就被納入中共所建立的組織體系，先加入少先隊，之後加入共青團，部分人在成年後再加入中共。

「在入黨儀式上，他們被迫舉起拳頭，宣誓將自己的一切，包括生命，都獻給黨。通過這種宣誓，中共對中國人的身心控制貫穿他們的一生。」她說。

她表示，通過公開聲明退出中共及其附屬組織，中國人擺脫了中共的灌輸和控制。

「中國不是中共，中國人民也不是中共。」她強調，三退並非一場以奪取政權為目的的政治運動，而是以和平方式表達對自由、安全及正常生活的追求。

澳洲法輪大法學會發言人約翰·戴樂（John Deller）也表示，三退是中國人覺醒的表現。他以安徒生童話《皇帝的新裝》的故事作比喻，指在一個人人都不敢說真話的環境中，最先站出來指出真相的人，就像故事中說出「皇帝沒有穿衣服」的孩子。他認為，法輪功學員多年來在中國反迫害、講真相的行動，以及三退運動，正是在幫助更多中國人打破對中共的恐懼與信息控制。

[![Image 5](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858186-JOHN-DELLER-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858186-JOHN-DELLER.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為澳洲法輪大法學會發言人約翰·戴樂（John Deller）在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

「那個說出真相、讓人們醒悟的天真孩子，就是中共制度下的法輪功學員。」他說。

戴樂表示，2004年11月《大紀元時報》發表的《九評共產黨》，猶如孩子喊出的那句真話，為中國人認識自身歷史真相奠定基礎。他表示，中國人自幼接受黨化教育，從少先隊、共青團到入黨，長期處於封閉的中共洗腦宣傳中，而三退運動正是中國人覺醒後的選擇。

## 前聯邦大選候選人：三退是正確道路

澳洲社會活動人士、企業家及前聯邦大選候選人加內什·洛克（Ganesh Loke）表示，面對中共暴政，長期推動三退運動及反抗中共的行動並不容易，但勇氣、決心與毅力終將帶來改變。他向數億選擇退出中共及其附屬組織的勇士表示祝賀，並鼓勵更多人繼續選擇這條正確道路。

[![Image 6](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858188-8979f301272f782d51932efbff470387-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858188-8979f301272f782d51932efbff470387.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為前聯邦大選候選人加內什·洛克（Ganesh Loke）在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

他說，自己一直支持法輪功學員，也十分敬佩法輪功學員多年來持續舉行的傳播真相的集會和抗議活動。他表示，這「這並不容易」，但他相信，參與者所付出的努力、勇氣和堅持最終會產生影響。

洛克在演講中以印度獨立運動領袖甘地（Mahatma Gandhi）的故事，回應人們對「中共如此強大，如何可能改變」的疑問。

他說，1927年，曾有人問甘地，面對強大的大英帝國，印度如何能夠取得自由。按照洛克的轉述，甘地回答說，他擁有堅持、勇氣和決心，相信在20年內可以使英國政府離開印度。洛克表示，20年後的1947年，印度獲得獨立。他以此強調，當面對看似強大的力量時，持續的努力和堅持仍然可能帶來歷史性的變化。

「沒有什麼是不可能的。」洛克說。他鼓勵現場參與者相信自己的行動，並表示大家可以一起努力、一起創造改變。

## 維吾爾團體代表：呼籲更多中國人加入三退大潮

澳洲維吾爾人協會（Australian Uyghur Association）祕書兼發言人穆罕默德·塞勒普西（Mehmet Celepci）表示，「三退」運動所代表的，是個人基於良知和對自由的追求，與中共及其附屬組織切割的一種選擇。

[![Image 7](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858192-035a4484f58ee0d2124ed87c37ae1637-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858192-035a4484f58ee0d2124ed87c37ae1637.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為澳洲維吾爾人協會（Australian Uyghur Association）祕書兼發言人穆罕默德·塞勒普西（Mehmet Celepci）在集會上發言。（文清揚／大紀元）

他強調，共產主義是「不適合人性的非人道制度」，而「三退」正是中國人試圖切斷與共產主義聯繫的努力。他表示，對於生活在中共政治體制下的人而言，退出中共及其附屬組織，不只是形式上的退出，更涉及個人如何看待自己的良知、自由與未來。

塞勒普西向選擇三退的數億人表示祝賀，並呼籲更多人們選擇三退。

演講中，他特別譴責中共7月1日出臺的《民族團結進步促進法》。他坦言，真正的團結不能通過強制建立，而應建立在對多元文化的尊重之上。不同民族、不同文化和不同身分都應得到尊重，人們也應有權按照自己的意願選擇自己的信仰、文化和生活方式。

「我們將繼續以和平、合法而無畏的方式，為那些聲音被壓制的人發聲。」塞勒普西說。他呼籲更多人思考自己與共產主義之間的關係，加入三退大潮。

當日集會，除了嘉賓演講，法輪功學員還帶來的樂團、腰鼓、舞蹈和歌唱表演，為集會增添了祥和而歡快的氣氛。

[![Image 8](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858194-IMG_2216-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858194-IMG_2216.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為天國樂團表演。（文清揚／大紀元）

[![Image 9](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858195-8e2a3a09e205c15103abc19ab9eefc2d-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858195-8e2a3a09e205c15103abc19ab9eefc2d.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為腰鼓隊表演。（文清揚／大紀元）

[![Image 10](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858200-871b5daf691430d881c4fd7d368162aa-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/09/id14858200-871b5daf691430d881c4fd7d368162aa.jpg)

2026年9月26中午，悉尼退黨服務中心在市政廳（Town Hall）舉行三退集會。圖為悉尼法輪功舞蹈隊表演。（文清揚／大紀元）

title: How Taiwan’s ‘silicon shield’ has kept it safe from China, indispensable to US in age of AI
summary: Trump, Xi and Taiwan sit at the centre of a global semiconductor race, with the island producing most of the world’s advanced chips The latest meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping has once again put Tai
content:
Trump, Xi and Taiwan sit at the centre of a global semiconductor race, with the island producing most of the world’s advanced chips

The latest meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping has once again put Taiwan at the centre of the world's most consequential geopolitical and technology rivalry.Xi pressed Trump during their Washington talks to adopt what Beijing calls the "correct position" of opposing Taiwan independence, according to a Chinese readout. Taiwan rejected the demand, saying Beijing had no right to determine the island's future. The exchange came as Washington continues to balance its longstanding support for Taiwan with its broader effort to manage relations with Beijing.The Taiwan question, however, is about more than territory, military power or competing political claims.

It is also about one of the most important foundations of the modern global economy: semiconductors.Taiwan produces the overwhelming majority of the world's most advanced chips, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, at the centre of that ecosystem. These chips power smartphones, artificial intelligence systems, high-performance computers, data centres, automobiles and increasingly sophisticated military technologies.

As Stanford University Hoover fellow Eyck Freymann told Rest of World, “The economic shock from a serious Taiwan disruption would dwarf anything we’ve seen in the postwar period.”The question is therefore not simply what would happen if China and Taiwan entered a military confrontation. It is why Taiwan became so important to the global chip industry, why TSMC is so difficult to replace, why the company depends on technology and suppliers across several countries, and why the US, China and India are all trying to reshape the semiconductor supply chain.

The world’s top semiconductor manufacturers powering everything from smartphones to AI data centres

The island that became a semiconductor chokepoint Semiconductors are the building blocks of modern electronics. They allow computers to process information, smartphones to function, vehicles to operate sophisticated electronic systems and AI data centres to perform enormous numbers of calculations.But semiconductor manufacturing is not concentrated in one country. The supply chain is divided among economies with different strengths.The US has major capabilities in chip design, software and electronic design automation. Taiwan dominates advanced manufacturing. South Korea is a major force in memory. Japan is important for semiconductor materials and equipment. The Netherlands is home to ASML, the key supplier of advanced lithography systems.

EUV lithography is at the heart of the race to control the world’s most advanced chips

Taiwan's importance comes from the concentration of advanced manufacturing on the island. Government data says Taiwan accounts for more than 60% of global chip production and nearly 90% of advanced chips.

TSMC is at the centre of that ecosystem.TSMC's scale illustrates why it is difficult to replace. In 2025, the company manufactured 12,682 products using 305 process technologies for 534 customers. Its chips served sectors including high-performance computing, smartphones, automobiles, the Internet of Things and consumer electronics. Its manufacturing capacity exceeded 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers during the year.The company therefore sits between some of the world's largest technology companies and the physical production of their chips.

TSMC sits at the centre of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem and the global advanced-chip supply chain

### How Taiwan built its semiconductor advantage

Taiwan's position was built over decades.In the 1970s, Taiwanese policymakers recognised that the island could not immediately compete with the US and Japan across the entire technology industry. Instead, it focused on specialised manufacturing capabilities and technology transfer.The Industrial Technology Research Institute, or ITRI, was established in 1973. Taiwan subsequently acquired semiconductor technology from the US through licensing arrangements and trained engineers overseas. The development of the Hsinchu Science Park, established in 1980, added another crucial component.Hsinchu brought together semiconductor companies, research institutions, universities, engineers and suppliers.

Over time, this geographic concentration created an ecosystem in which companies could access skilled workers, equipment, suppliers and technical expertise.The decisive change came in 1987, when Morris Chang founded TSMC.Chang's idea was to separate chip design from chip manufacturing. Instead of designing and selling its own branded chips, TSMC would manufacture chips designed by other companies.The model became known as the pure-play foundry model.TSMC's business model allowed companies such as Nvidia and Qualcomm to concentrate on chip architecture and design without having to build and operate their own advanced fabs. At the same time, TSMC could focus entirely on manufacturing.The model also reduced concerns among customers that their manufacturing partner would compete with them in the chip market. TSMC says its exclusive focus on manufacturing customers' products was central to the pure-play foundry model.That division of labour helped create the modern fabless semiconductor industry and made TSMC a central manufacturing partner for some of the world's most valuable technology companies.

### Why TSMC is so difficult to replace

TSMC's advantage is not simply the buildings containing its fabs.A leading-edge semiconductor facility requires enormous capital investment, but a modern fab also depends on years of accumulated process knowledge, engineering expertise, equipment suppliers, chemicals, gases, utilities, logistics and specialist workers.Taiwan developed these capabilities around TSMC over several decades.The result is a dense industrial ecosystem that is difficult to reproduce simply by spending money on a new factory.TSMC is expanding outside Taiwan. It operates manufacturing facilities in Japan and China, has expanded its Arizona operations and is developing a specialty technology fab in Dresden, Germany. But the company continues to invest heavily in Taiwan, including multiple 2nm facilities and advanced packaging capacity.That is why governments seeking greater semiconductor security are generally trying to create additional capacity rather than assuming that Taiwan's entire ecosystem can quickly be recreated elsewhere.

### Taiwan's 'silicon shield'

Taiwan's semiconductor dominance has also acquired a geopolitical dimension.The idea of a "silicon shield" was explicitly described by former Taiwanese president Tsai Ing-wen in a 2021 Foreign Affairs article.

The basic argument is that Taiwan's importance to the global economy creates a form of mutual dependence.A major conflict that disrupted Taiwan's chip industry would not hurt Taiwan alone. It would affect economies and companies that rely on its semiconductor output.But the shield is not an absolute guarantee of security.Eyck Freymann, author of Defending Taiwan: A Strategy to Prevent War With China, has argued that the concept can be overstated.

China would not necessarily need to seize TSMC's factories to disrupt the semiconductor supply chain.

An EUV machine combines precision optics, lasers, mirrors, vacuum systems and thousands of specialised components

A blockade, quarantine or other form of coercion could interfere with the movement of chips out of Taiwan even if the factories themselves continued operating.That distinction is important. Semiconductor production depends not only on fabs but also on electricity, water, equipment, chemicals, logistics, shipping routes and international workers and suppliers.A disruption to those systems could therefore affect output without physically destroying a fab.

### China wants semiconductor self-reliance

China's semiconductor strategy is closely linked to its broader technology and national-security objectives.Beijing has invested heavily in reducing dependence on foreign semiconductor technology, while Washington has imposed restrictions on China's access to advanced chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.Chinese companies including Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation and Huawei have developed domestic capabilities, while Beijing has pushed for greater self-sufficiency across the semiconductor value chain.China has made progress, particularly in mature and increasingly advanced manufacturing, but the leading edge remains difficult because of restrictions on advanced equipment and technology.The contest is particularly important because the most advanced chips depend on highly specialised manufacturing equipment that China has historically had limited access to.

### The EUV bottleneck

At the centre of the advanced-chip race is extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, lithography.EUV systems use light with a wavelength of 13.5 nanometres to print extremely small patterns on semiconductor wafers. The technology is critical to producing some of the most advanced generations of chips.This is where the Netherlands enters the semiconductor story.Dutch company ASML is the world's key supplier of EUV lithography systems. ASML does not manufacture chips. It makes the machines used by chipmakers to manufacture them.A modern EUV system combines precision optics, lasers, vacuum systems, mirrors, sensors and thousands of components supplied through a highly specialised international network.

German company Carl Zeiss is central to the optical systems, while suppliers in the US, Japan and elsewhere contribute other components and materials.The result is a semiconductor supply chain in which no single country controls every critical technology.Taiwan provides leading-edge manufacturing. The Netherlands provides critical lithography equipment. The US has major strengths in chip design and related technologies.

Japan supplies important materials and equipment. South Korea dominates parts of the memory market.ASML and TSMC are already working on the next generation of EUV technology. In September 2026, the companies announced an initiative to transition the industry towards 12-inch photomasks for High NA EUV. TSMC intends to use ASML's High NA technology in high-volume manufacturing for advanced nodes from 2030, while the initiative targets a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031 and advanced-node production readiness by 2033.That relationship shows how difficult it is for any one country to become completely independent in semiconductor technology.

EUV uses 13.5-nanometre light to print incredibly small patterns needed for advanced semiconductor production.

### China's EUV challenge

China's attempt to develop its own EUV capability has therefore become one of the most closely watched parts of the semiconductor race.Reuters reported in December 2025 that China had developed a prototype EUV lithography machine at a secure facility in Shenzhen. The machine was reportedly capable of generating EUV light but was not yet capable of producing advanced chips.

Reuters also reported that former ASML engineers had been recruited and that China had used components obtained from older systems and secondary markets.The distinction is important. Producing EUV light is not the same as developing a commercially viable EUV system capable of manufacturing advanced chips reliably and at scale.ASML's position was built over decades of research, engineering and collaboration with a vast supplier network.

China therefore faces the additional challenge of converting research breakthroughs into reliable industrial production.But the effort demonstrates why export controls cannot be viewed simply as a permanent technological barrier. They can restrict access to critical technologies while also encouraging efforts to develop alternatives.
