content:
华盛顿 —

美国国会共和党联邦众议员马里奥·迪亚兹-巴拉特(Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart)星期二(9月22日)在接受美国之音(VOA)专访时表示，美国的外交政策必须以国家安全为核心，面对强大的中国，美中必须打交道。针对即将到来的美中元首峰会，他认为若能在人工智能(AI)领域取得突破将是重大成果，但对于与北京达成的任何协议都必须抱持“不信任、但要核实”的态度。

同一天，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump) 在联合国大会发表演说时严厉批评古巴，称该国共产主义政权正面临有史以来最大的压力，并直言其“注定会失败”，这番言论引发古巴常驻联合国代表团当场离席。

作为国会中少数古巴裔美国议员之一，迪亚兹-巴拉特对美国之音表示，他认为哈瓦那政府将无法熬过特朗普政府接下来的任期，并严厉批评社会主义和共产主义政策给古巴人民带来了“苦难、物资匮乏与最终的压迫”。

谈到星期四即将在白宫登场的美中元首峰会，迪亚兹-巴拉特指出，鉴于AI发展已不可逆转，华盛顿应寻求与中国达成可核实的管控协议，并防范中国利用AI进行危险活动。

“当我想到中国时，我会说，‘不信任，但要核实’。所以，我们能否与中国达成一项可以得到核实的协议？如果能够做到这一点，那将是一项重大成果，” 迪亚兹-巴拉特众议员说。

身为佛罗里达州联邦众议员的迪亚兹-巴拉特也是“国会台湾连线”共同主席，他在访谈中强调，尽管美国国会内部存在诸多党派分歧，但在台湾议题上，两党始终保持着非常强有力的跨党派支持。

迪亚兹-巴拉特同时担任众议院拨款委员会国务院、对外运作和相关项目小组委员会主席。该小组委员会负责审议美国国务院、国际发展署、全球媒体总署、美国在台协会(AIT)以及美国国会暨行政当局中国委员会(CECC)等重要涉外机构的财政拨款。

**以下是这次专访中文翻译。为求语句流畅，部分文字稍有删减：**

**VOA：**我想先从第1490号众议院决议案(H. Res. 1490)谈起，该法案谴责一切形式的社会主义。今天上午在联合国大会上，特朗普总统就古巴发表了非常强硬的言论。他称古巴为一个失败的国家，并表示共产主义绝不会降临美国，但自由终将降临古巴。您认为总统的这番言论，与众议院最近刚刚通过的该决议案的宗旨是一致的吗？

**迪亚兹-巴拉特议员：**社会主义每一次、在每一个尝试过它的地方，都带来了破坏性的后果。你知道，共产主义者自己一直都说，社会主义只是通往共产主义的第一步。再说一次，无论称之为社会主义还是共产主义，无论你想给它贴上什么标签，这些政策从未奏效，它们带来的只有苦难、物资匮乏，以及最终的压迫。因此，这种制度已经被反复尝试过。在不同的时代、不同的国家，人们一次又一次地尝试过，结果却始终相同。这也正是为什么我们必须警惕社会主义进入美国。但如果有人想知道社会主义究竟是如何运作的，或者说它为什么行不通，那么他们可以看看委内瑞拉，也可以看看古巴。然后他们可能会说：“但那不是我们想要实行的社会主义。” 好吧，问题恰恰就在这里：凡是尝试过社会主义的地方，无一例外，最终都走向了完全相同的结局，那就是苦难、暴政、物资匮乏和贫困。

**VOA：**您是否支持政府采取措施促进古巴的政治变革？您希望看到美国采取哪些具体行动？

**迪亚兹-巴拉特议员：**我实际上确信，哈瓦那的那个政权——那个恐怖主义政权——撑不过特朗普政府接下来的两年。我之所以这么说，是因为美国政府一直在推行的政策，美国如今对这个反美政权所采取的“不再容忍”政策。他们(哈瓦那)政权派遣军队前往俄罗斯，为普京作战；它一直是西半球的一颗毒瘤，是美国的毒瘤，而且不仅危害西半球，也危害非洲。

再者，甚至根据乌克兰情报部门的消息，实际上有古巴特工在乌克兰为普京作战。这是一个破产的小国，它将得到的每一美元、每一欧元，不是用来帮助古巴人民，而是用来伤害自己的人民和世界各地。而这位总统不愿接受这一点。你已经看到了施压政策，不仅针对该政权，还针对那些协助和扶持该政权的人。这正在产生效果。

关键点在于，这属于公开信息，目前该政权坐拥 180亿到200亿美元的硬通货。然而，古巴人民甚至连水、电和基本生活必需品都没有，这并不是因为他们没有钱，而是因为该政权多年来获取并持续得到的每一美元、每一欧元，都被用来镇压自己的人民并在全球作恶。(美国)本届政府不愿接受这一点。他们对该政权的所作所为有着清醒的认识，不愿对此姑息。这对古巴人民是件好事，对西半球是件好事，归根结底，这也非常有益于美国的国家安全利益。

**VOA：**说到古巴和共产主义政府，人们自然而然会想到中国。为什么美国对中国采取的方法，与对古巴采取的方法会有所不同呢？

**迪亚兹-巴拉特议员：**每个案例都不相同，处理不同案例的方式也必须有所区别。外交政策绝不是一种‘一刀切’的政策，也不能是。然而，外交政策首先必须以美国的国家安全利益为优先来主导。就中国而言，无论我们愿不愿意，他们拥有核武器、庞大的军队，而且是一个非常、非常庞大的经济体。因此，你无法忽视这一现实。就古巴而言，我们面对的是一个距离美国仅90英里、且支持恐怖主义的国家。因此，假装这些差异不存在，就是脱离现实。正如美国过去对苏联帝国采取了不同的应对方式一样，正如美国对不同国家采取了不同的处理方式一样，你必须根据各个国家的具体情况来进行处理。

但关键在于，你必须清楚自己面对的是谁。所以说，中国体量庞大、实力雄厚，还拥有非常庞大的军队。但他们不是我们的盟友，我们必须时刻清醒地认识到这一点，并以此为前提来对待他们。对于古巴、委内瑞拉政权或朝鲜政权，你也同样需要知道自己面对的是什么。

再拿古巴来说，过去许多人会说，‘好吧，它只是个小国，所以我们不必担心。’然而，它虽是个小国，却极具破坏力，在西半球乃至其他地区严重损害了美国的利益。过去的态度往往是‘好吧，我们并不真正在乎他们在做什么’。但我们必须在乎，因为他们造成的破坏不仅波及西半球，还有非洲。顺便说一句，非洲有那么多国家至今仍未从古巴政权当年造成的破坏中恢复过来。显然，甚至在乌克兰，他们都有特工活动。而且它距离美国只有90英里。

因此，当然，我们对待古巴的方式会与对待一个距离遥远、拥有庞大军队和核武器的国家有所不同。但这并不意味着我们不应该理解并清醒地认识到——中国不是我们的盟友，中国是一个非常危险的独裁政权，朝鲜、伊朗以及距离美国仅90英里的古巴也同样如此。

**VOA：**让我们换个话题。我们都知道，中国国家主席习近平明天将抵达华盛顿与特朗普总统会晤。您认为他们的会晤取得怎样的成果才算成功？

**迪亚兹-巴拉特议员：**这很有意思，你必须清楚自己面对的是什么，对吧？中国是一个非常强大的国家，这一点必须承认。无论你愿不愿意，我们都必须与中国打交道。我知道，总统希望就人工智能问题与中方展开一些对话，我认为这非常关键。关于人工智能，很有趣的事实是它已发生，并且将长期存在。即使我们在美国完全停止发展人工智能，也无法阻止中国继续推进人工智能的工作。

问题在于，我们能否与中国达成一项具有约束力、并且可以核实的协议，对人工智能实施一定的管控，确保人工智能不会失控？我听说美国正在考虑的方案之一，是与中国建立某种直接沟通渠道，就像冷战时期我们与苏联建立的联系，类似于“红色电话”。这样一来，如果人工智能失控——无论是在中国，还是在美国的其他地方——双方都能够通过这些渠道直接沟通。我认为，这类举措都非常积极的。

但我必须提醒大家，人工智能是不会消失的。我们要么走在人工智能发展的最前沿，要么中国显然不会停止前进。我们能否采取一些措施，包括利用人工智能，来阻止中国采取真正恶劣的、危险的行动？如果我们能够在人工智能领域达成任何可核实的协议，就像里根总统过去谈到苏联时所说的，“信任，但要核实”。当我想到中国时，我会说，“不信任，但要核实”。所以，我们能否与中国达成一项可以得到核实的协议？如果能够做到这一点，那将是一项重大成果。

**VOA：**关于特朗普政府对台政策，各方一直有所讨论。作为国会众议院台湾连线小组主席，您是否看到台湾政策有什么变化？您是否仍然能看到国会对台湾的跨党派支持？

**迪亚兹-巴拉特议员：**我很高兴你提到了国会对台湾的态度。我们必须记住，美国与台湾之间的这种特殊关系，很大程度上建立在美国国会与台湾的关系之上。卡特政府时期，卡特总统——我不知道该说这是他的智慧，还是缺乏智慧——实际上与台湾断绝了外交关系，并承认了共产主义中国。顺便说一句，当时台湾这个盟友只提前大约两个小时才得到通知。国会随后以两党合作的方式介入。此后，国会一直以非常强有力的两党合作方式发挥领导作用，充分认识到台湾的重要性。

台湾是民主制，是美国的盟友，同时拥有强劲而充满活力的经济和民主制度。因此，这样的关系，这种特殊关系始于国会，而这一点从未改变。国会内部确实存在很多党派分歧，但在台湾问题上，两党一直拥有非常强有力的支持。我认为，这种两党支持是我们必须继续保持的重要基础。

**VOA：**议员先生，谢谢您。我们今天的访谈到这边就结束了。非常感谢您抽空接受美国之音采访。

Researchers suspect the hacker employed LLMs to develop custom tools.

 Published Sept. 21, 2026

 Cyber threat actors are physically breaching data centers to steal data and demand ransom from organizations, requiring bolstered security at these locations, according to the FBI. Getty Images

A Chinese-speaking threat actor has engaged in a hacking campaign at least since June, involving the theft of thousands of documents from, at minimum, one Western government, according to a [Monday blog post](https://www.greynoise.io/blog/open-season-on-kapibala-attacker-steals-government-records-wordpress-exploitation) from threat intelligence firm GreyNoise.

The hacker targeted critical vulnerabilities in multiple technologies, including WordPress, Zyxel and Ubiquiti, and is suspected of using a large language model to develop custom tools used in the attacks.

Researchers are still trying to ascertain the adversary’s specific motives beyond gathering large amounts of information.

“The actor is focused on creating access and stealing data,” Andrew Thompson, senior vice president of adversary operations at GreyNoise Intelligence, told Cybersecurity Dive. “The ultimate benefactor is not clear yet.”

### Critical flaws targeted

According to GreyNoise, the threat actor has targeted several vulnerabilities in recent months.

On June 12, the hacker tried to exploit a chain of vulnerabilities in Ubiquiti in order to achieve remote code execution. The vulnerabilities included [CVE-2026-34908](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-34908), [CVE-2026-34909](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-34909) and [CVE-2026-34910](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-34910). Those vulnerabilities were added to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/06/23/cisa-adds-four-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) catalog on June 23.

On July 20, the actor targeted an exploit chain in WordPress, called wp2shell, which includes [CVE-2026-63030](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-63030) and [CVE-2026-60137](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-60137). Hackers gained access to 49 organizations across 29 countries, mainly involving government agencies and small businesses.

More recently, the hacker targeted Zyxel GS1900 Smart Managed Switches using a novel exploit of [CVE-2026-7273](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-7273), GreyNoise said. Sensitive exploitation was confirmed in 996 switches across 48 countries, according to the researchers.

The researchers warned that the adversary is also using 17 different scripts to bypass Microsoft’s Antimalware Scan Interface. The actor is escalating privileges through token impersonation and creating a local administrator account.

The suspected hacker shares overlaps with an adversary known as Red Heron. Earlier this month, [researchers at Acronis tracked Red Heron](https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/red-heron-exploits-gitea-n-day-flaw-in-multinational-campaign-exposing-new-linux-rootkit/)exploiting [CVE-2026-60004](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-60004), a critical vulnerability in Gitea, a self-hosted source code management platform.

title: US to open two new military bases in Greenland, sources say
summary: COPENHAGEN/WASHINGTON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - The US plans to re-establish a Cold War-era military base in southern Greenland and set up ​another on the east coast, now used by the Danish dog sled patrol, under ‌a deal to be signed with Denmar
content:
COPENHAGEN/WASHINGTON, Sept 21 (Reuters) - The US plans to re-establish a Cold War-era military base in southern Greenland and set up ​another on the east coast, now used by the Danish dog sled patrol, under ‌a deal to be signed with Denmark and Greenland on Tuesday, according to three people familiar with the matter.

The sites are Narsarsuaq, whose population has dwindled to a few dozen people since the US closed its Bluie ​West One military base in the 1950s, and Mestersvig, a military outpost used by ​the Sirius Dog Sled Patrol, a Danish special forces unit, said two of ⁠the people.

Get a look at the day ahead in European and global markets with the Morning Bid Europe newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/morning-bid-europe/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Feurope%2Fus-open-two-new-military-bases-greenland-sources-say-2026-09-21%2F)

Denmark, Greenland and the United States are expected to sign their new agreement at the ​United Nations General Assembly in New York City at 10:30 a.m. ET (1430 GMT) on Tuesday.

The text ​of the agreement has not been made public and the three people familiar with the deal, speaking on condition of anonymity, said its details will not be finalized until it is signed.

The governments of Denmark and Greenland did ​not immediately respond to a request by Reuters for comment.

Item 1 of 2 General view of Mestersvig military outpost in Mestersvig, Greenland, September 18, 2025. REUTERS/Guglielmo Mangiapane/File Photo

**[1/2]**General view of Mestersvig military outpost in Mestersvig, Greenland, September 18, 2025. REUTERS/Guglielmo Mangiapane/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/mestersvig-military-outpost-in-greenland/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX1JDMkRVR0FMWklGRQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

A White House spokesperson declined to comment ​on the details of the agreement, repeating an earlier statement that its signing on Tuesday would "secure and defend ‌the security ⁠of Greenland and the United States."

Denmark says the agreement puts Arctic security under the watch of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, the military defense alliance, rather than leaving it solely to the US and Denmark.

The deal follows months of [pressure](https://www.reuters.com/world/trumps-push-greenland-hangs-over-danish-election-2026-09-21/) from US President Donald Trump, who has long said he ​wants the US to ​control Greenland and has ⁠at times refused to rule out military or economic force to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish territory. The idea has been rejected by an overwhelming ​majority of Greenlanders, polling shows.

Trump's threats, which peaked in January, triggered a ​diplomatic crisis ⁠within NATO and pushed Denmark and Greenland into negotiations with Washington aimed at defusing the pressure.

During the Cold War, the US maintained 17 military installations and more than 10,000 personnel in Greenland. Today only Pituffik ⁠Space ​Base remains, with some 150 US military personnel.

Reporting by Stine ​Jacobsen in Copenhagen and Gram Slattery and Erin Banco in Washington; Additional reporting by Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen in Copenhagen, and Phil ​Stewart and Steve Holland in Washington; Writing by Jonathan Allen; Editing by Don Durfee and Nia Williams

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

Stine Jacobsen is a Senior Correspondent at Reuters, where she has worked for more than a decade. Currently based in Copenhagen, she reports on politics and business across the Nordic and Baltic regions. Coverage spans major Danish companies including Novo Nordisk, Orsted, Vestas, Maersk and Lego, as well as Arctic affairs and regional security. She serves on the board of the International Press Centre in Copenhagen.

Erin Banco is a national security correspondent focusing on the intelligence community. She covers everything from the wars in Ukraine and Gaza to U.S. covert operations overseas. She previously worked at POLITICO as a national security reporter. Banco has a long history covering the Middle East region, from Cairo to Baghdad to Aleppo where she’s reported on the Arab Spring and its aftermath, including the civil war in Syria and the rise of ISIS. Her 2017 book, Pipe Dreams, focuses on the development of the oil and gas industry in the northern Kurdistan region of Iraq. Banco attended The University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she majored in Arabic and journalism. She earned a master’s in public administration from Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs in 2014.

Gram Slattery is a White House correspondent in Washington, focusing on national security, intelligence and foreign affairs. His work covers how key U.S. foreign policy decisions are debated, shaped and executed. He was previously a national political correspondent, covering the 2024 presidential campaign. From 2015 to 2022, he held postings in Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo and Santiago, Chile, and he has reported extensively throughout Latin America.

title: China & Global Trade Regulations: August–September 2026
summary: This roundup covers the key trade rules that take effect or enter the implementation phase in China and across major export markets in August and September 2026 — including China’s new consumption tax on batteries, electronic documentation
content:
This roundup covers the key trade rules that take effect or enter the implementation phase in China and across major export markets in August and September 2026 — including China’s new consumption tax on batteries, electronic documentation rules, export controls, and a wave of tariff and compliance changes in the US, the EU, Canada, Southeast Asia and beyond. Exporters and cross-border sellers are advised to review these changes closely.

## Part 1. China Domestic Regulations

### 1. Consumption Tax Introduced on Certain Battery Products

Effective: September 1, 2026

Issued by: Ministry of Finance, General Administration of Customs (GACC) and State Taxation Administration (STA), Announcement No. 20 of 2026

Key points:

*   From September 1, 2026, mercury-free primary batteries, nickel-metal hydride (NiMH) batteries, lithium primary batteries, lithium-ion batteries and all-vanadium redox flow batteries are subject to a consumption tax of 2%, rising to 4% from September 1, 2027.
*   From April 1, 2027, photovoltaic (PV) cells are taxed at 2%, rising to 4% from April 1, 2028.
*   From September 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028, sodium-ion, solid-state and fuel cells, as well as perovskite, tandem and gallium arsenide cells within the PV category, are exempt.
*   Relief is conditional on compliance with national product standards; a test report from a CMA-accredited testing body must be obtained before the first declaration.

Impact: Manufacturers and exporters of battery cells, energy storage systems, power tools and consumer electronics should monitor upstream cost changes and adjust export pricing accordingly.

### 2. Measures on Promoting and Regulating the Application of Electronic Documents

Effective: September 1, 2026

Key points:

*   Covers electronic bills of lading, sea waybills, railway/air/road freight waybills and multimodal transport documents, as well as electronic warehouse receipts and electronic cargo insurance policies.
*   Grants electronic documents the same legal validity as paper documents, and standardizes issuance, storage, transfer, pledge and circulation — supporting end-to-end digitalization of cross-border trade and international mutual recognition.

Impact: Foreign trade and logistics companies should confirm in practice whether shipping lines, customers, banks and destination-country authorities accept the relevant electronic documents.

### 3. New Rules on Quarantine/Sanitary Treatment Supervision for Entry-Exit Goods

Effective: September 1, 2026

Issued by: General Administration of Customs (GACC Announcement No. 111 of 2026, among others)

Key points: The new Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Quarantine Treatment for Entry-Exit Animals and Plants and the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Entry-Exit Sanitary Treatment take effect, covering fumigation, disinfection, disinsection and pest-control treatment, as well as updated treatment requirements and supervisory procedures for animal and plant products, wooden packaging and containers.

Impact: Exporters of animal/plant products and wooden packaging, and customs brokers involved in container fumigation.

### 4. Adjusted Quarantine and Inspection Requirements for Fruit Exports to Hong Kong and Macao

Effective: September 1, 2026

Key points: Requirements for orchards, packing houses, product traceability and packaging/labeling are clarified. Cartons must indicate fruit type, place of origin, orchard and packing house. Quality and safety records should generally be retained for at least three years.

Impact: Companies exporting fruit to Hong Kong and Macao.

### 5. Cross-Border Centralized Operation of Multicurrency Funds for Multinational Companies

Effective: September 14, 2026

Issued by: People’s Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)

Key points: The updated policy on centralized cross-border operation of domestic and foreign currency funds by multinational companies takes effect, expanding eligibility and making it easier for multinationals to pool funds across borders, balance surpluses and shortfalls, and settle cross-border receipts and payments.

Impact: Exporters with overseas subsidiaries, branches or overseas warehouses will find cross-border fund management more convenient.

### 6. New State Council Regulations on Exit and Entry Administration

Effective: September 15, 2026

Key points: Compared with the 2013 Exit and Entry Administration Law, the new regulations address four areas: protecting Chinese citizens from overseas security risks, regulating the management of foreign nationals entering China, improving exit-entry restriction measures, and regulating exit-entry agency services.

Impact: Exporters that regularly send staff overseas for exhibitions, client visits or long-term postings should review exit and documentation requirements in advance.

### 7. New Customs Rules on Health and Quarantine of Special Entry-Exit Goods and Articles

Effective: August 1, 2026

Key points:

*   Scope expanded from “special articles” to “special goods and articles,” aligning with the revised Frontier Health and Quarantine Law.
*   Goods already regulated as pharmaceuticals, veterinary drugs or medical devices are no longer treated as special goods/articles; routine sanitary quarantine applies, which is expected to streamline clearance.
*   Declarants are clarified: consignors/consignees, senders/receivers, carriers or their agents are the statutory declarants.
*   New biosafety risk monitoring is introduced for special entry-exit goods/articles that could endanger public health within China. Blood and human tissues, pathogenic microorganisms and biological products require updated filing and approval procedures.

### 8. China–Uzbekistan Customs AEO Mutual Recognition Takes Effect

Effective: August 1, 2026

Key points:

*   Scope: Uzbekistan recognizes China’s Advanced Certified Enterprises (ACEs); China recognizes Uzbek companies holding Uzbek customs business and security certificates.
*   Exports: Chinese ACEs must share their AEO code (AEOCN + digits 9–17 of the Unified Social Credit Code) with their Uzbek importers.
*   Imports: when importing from Uzbekistan, enter the Uzbek AEO code (format: UZB/9-digit enterprise code/III) in the consignor code field of the customs declaration and the corresponding manifest field.
*   Four benefits: lower inspection rates, priority inspection when physical examination is required, a designated customs liaison officer, and priority clearance after recovery from international trade disruption.

### 9. MOFCOM Adds 14 EU Entities to the Export Control Restriction List

Effective: August 1, 2026

Issued by: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)

Key points: To safeguard national security and interests and fulfill international non-proliferation obligations, 14 EU entities, including Rafat Group, are added to the export control restriction list. Exporters are prohibited from exporting dual-use items to these entities, and foreign organizations and individuals are prohibited from transferring or supplying dual-use items of Chinese origin to them. Ongoing activities must cease immediately; exports in exceptional circumstances require application to MOFCOM.

Impact: Exporters of dual-use items must screen counterparties against the control list.

### 10. Tighter US Export Controls on Drone-Related Dual-Use Items

Effective: August 5, 2026 (upon announcement)

Issued by: MOFCOM

Key points: Exports to the US of drones and their key components and related technologies listed in China’s Dual-Use Items Export Control List will be reviewed case by case with stricter scrutiny; licensing facilitation measures do not apply.

Impact: Exporters of complete drones and drone components to the US.

## Part 2. Key Export Markets

### North America

**1. US Imposes New Tariffs of 10%–12.5% on 60 Economies**

Effective July 24, 2026 (full rollout in August)

A new Section 301 tariff regime replaces the temporary 150-day global 10% tariff, covering 60 economies that account for 99.4% of US imports. China, Australia, Vietnam and Thailand face a 12.5% rate; Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and the EU face 10%–12.5%. Canada, Mexico, India, Indonesia, the UK and Malaysia face an additional 10% on top of existing US tariffs. Exemptions cover oil, natural gas and resources from certain countries, USMCA-covered goods, and goods already subject to national-security-related tariffs.

Impact: Nearly all exporters to the US should re-calculate quotations and margins at the latest rates.

**2. US Tariffs of 10%–100% on Imported Drones and Components**

Effective September 3, 2026 — White House Section 232 Proclamation

A 100% ad valorem tariff applies to certain drones with maximum take-off weight exceeding 25 kg, drones with integrated thermal imaging, drone docking stations and certain critical components; a 25% tariff applies to certain drones of 25 kg or below. These stack on existing Section 301 tariffs on China, significantly raising the combined tariff burden on Chinese-origin drones.

Impact: Drone exporters should verify product HTS codes and scope of application.

**3. CBP to Tighten Scrutiny of Importer of Record (IOR) Records from September 18**

Effective September 18, 2026 — US Customs and Border Protection (CBP)

CBP will intensify verification of information submitted by new and existing IORs on CBP Form 5106 (Importer Identity). If IOR information is found incomplete or inaccurate, the corresponding IOR number may be cancelled, making it unusable for US import clearance.

Impact: Exporters to the US and freight forwarders/brokers must ensure IOR data is accurate and complete.

**4. New FCC Rules Affect Robots, Including Robot Vacuums**

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has added advanced robotic equipment manufactured overseas to its list of covered equipment and services. This affects humanoid robots, quadruped robots, robot vacuums and robotic lawn mowers, and restricts exports of new models to the US.

Impact: Exporters of robots and smart home appliances to the US.

**5. US Tariffs of up to 100% on Certain Patented Pharmaceuticals**

Effective September 29, 2026

Section 232 measures on patented drugs and related pharmaceutical ingredients are expanded. Patented drugs and ingredients falling within scope that have not obtained preferential arrangements may face tariffs of up to 100%. Generic drugs and related ingredients are not covered for now.

Impact: Exporters of patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients to the US.

**6. Canada Enters Phase 2 of the China EV Import Quota**

September 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

Canada’s China EV import quota enters the second phase of the first quota year, with a base quota of 24,500 vehicles plus any unused quota carried over from Phase 1. Eligible Chinese EVs with import permits may enter the Canadian market at the 6.1% most-favored-nation (MFN) rate.

Impact: Market access for new-energy vehicle exporters to Canada has improved notably.

**7. Canada Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on Nearly US$20 Billion of US Goods**

Effective September 8, 2026

Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on more than 700 US products worth C27.6billion(aboutUS20 billion), in three tiers — 15%, 25% and 50% — mainly covering steel and aluminum, dairy, home appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics and electronics.

Impact: Companies involved in US–Canada transshipment or with cross-border supply chain exposure should monitor cost changes.

### Europe

**1. EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) Rollout Begins**

Effective August 12, 2026

*   Heavy metals:Total lead, cadmium, mercury and hexavalent chromium content must not exceed 100 mg/kg.
*   PFAS (food-contact packaging):Individual PFAS substance < 25 ppb; sum of targeted PFAS substances < 250 ppb; total PFAS < 50 ppm.
*   Recyclability:All packaging placed on the EU market must be recyclabl

content:
**September 15, 2026 | WASHINGTON**: As Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares for his planned visit to Washington on September 24, a US congressional shadow hearing has brought the human-rights situation in Tibet, Xinjiang and Hong Kong into focus, with witnesses urging Washington not to allow human rights concerns to disappear from its China policy.

The hearing was jointly convened by Rep. Ro Khanna, Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and Rep. Jim McGovern, Ranking Member of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China. Titled **“The Void in China Policy: Why Human Rights Must Be on Trump’s Agenda with Xi at the White House,”** the hearing examined the state of human rights in China and sought recommendations for US policy ahead of Xi’s visit.

The witnesses brought perspectives from across China’s contested regions and communities. **Palden Gyal**, President of the International Tibet Media Organization, testified on Tibet; **Tahir Imin**, founder and director of _Uyghur Post_, addressed the Uyghur experience; **Jonathan Stivers**, US Director of the Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong and a Commissioner of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, represented concerns surrounding Hong Kong; and **Yaqiu Wang**, a fellow at the University of Pennsylvania’s Penn Project on the Future of US-China Relations, provided a broader China-policy perspective.

### Tibet: “A deliberate effort to erase identity”

For Tibet, the central testimony came from Palden Gyal, who spent decades reporting on Tibet, including 27 years with Radio Free Asia in Washington and five years with the Tibet Information Network in London.

Gyal described what he sees as a decades-long effort by the Chinese Communist Party to weaken Tibetan identity through restrictions on language, religion, culture and access to information.

He placed particular emphasis on China’s **Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law**, which came into force on July 1, 2026. Chinese authorities describe the legislation as a framework for promoting ethnic unity and development among China’s ethnic groups. Gyal, however, argued that the law could further institutionalize assimilationist policies in Tibet.

He specifically pointed to education and language, arguing that Tibetan children are increasingly separated from their linguistic and cultural environment through the state boarding-school system and Mandarin-dominated education.

His testimony also highlighted the information restrictions surrounding Tibet. According to Gyal, China’s restrictions on independent journalism and access to Tibet make it difficult for the outside world to independently document what is happening inside the region.

### A grandmother and her grandchildren

One of the most striking elements of Gyal’s testimony was a story about an **87-year-old Tibetan grandmother** who told him that she was grateful the Dalai Lama remained alive but saddened that her grandchildren spoke to her only in Chinese.

The story illustrated the concern at the heart of his testimony: that the consequences of language and education policies are being felt not only politically, but within Tibetan families themselves.

For Gyal, the issue is ultimately about whether Tibetan children will retain the language, religious traditions and cultural connections that have historically linked generations.

He urged Congress to support the **Assuring the Future of Tibet Act**, legislation introduced in 2026 that addresses US policy toward Tibet and the future of Tibetan political representation.

Gyal also called on President Donald Trump to raise Tibet directly with Xi during their September 24 meeting, including Tibetan human rights and religious freedom, and to press for renewed dialogue between Beijing and representatives of the Dalai Lama.

### The Uyghur question

The hearing also brought the situation of Uyghurs in Xinjiang into the same congressional discussion.

Tahir Imin, founder and director of _Uyghur Post_, testified alongside Gyal, placing Uyghur concerns directly before lawmakers as Washington prepares for Xi’s visit. The inclusion of a Uyghur witness reflects the broader scope of the hearing: China’s treatment of ethnic and religious minorities was considered as part of a wider assessment of Beijing’s human-rights policies.

Human Rights Watch has separately documented what it describes as systematic restrictions on freedom of expression, association, assembly and religion in China, as well as forced assimilation affecting Tibetans and Uyghurs and repression under Hong Kong’s national-security regime.

### Hong Kong also part of the testimony

Hong Kong was another major part of the hearing.

Jonathan Stivers, US Director of the Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong and a Commissioner of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, testified on Hong Kong alongside the witnesses addressing Tibet and Xinjiang.

His participation placed Hong Kong’s political freedoms and the consequences of Beijing’s expanding national-security framework within the same congressional examination of China’s human-rights record.

Together, the testimony from Tibet, Xinjiang and Hong Kong presented lawmakers with three different cases of how Beijing’s policies have affected communities with distinct political, cultural and religious identities.

### A debate over the direction of US China policy

The hearing came amid a broader debate in Washington about the place of human rights in US-China relations.

In announcing the hearing on September 10, Khanna and McGovern said human-rights abuses in China had traditionally attracted bipartisan concern in Congress. They argued that recent US policy had put that bipartisan approach under strain and said the hearing would provide an assessment and recommendations for US human-rights policy.

That debate now takes on added significance with Xi’s scheduled visit to Washington.

The hearing did not address China solely through the lens of trade, technology, security or geopolitical competition. Instead, it brought testimony from people directly focused on communities affected by Chinese government policies.

For Tibet, Palden Gyal’s message was that the issue cannot be separated from the future of Tibetan identity itself. For Uyghurs and Hong Kong, the testimony similarly ensured that their respective human-rights concerns remained part of the congressional conversation.

As Xi prepares to meet Trump, the September 15 hearing has placed a simple question before Washington: **what place will human rights have when the United States sits down with China’s leader?**

title: China creates Italy-sized no-fly zone around Beijing after rare crash
summary: The CITIC Tower, also known as China Zun, where damage is visible on a high floor of the exterior, in Beijing, China June 26, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/citic-
content:
The CITIC Tower, also known as China Zun, where damage is visible on a high floor of the exterior, in Beijing, China June 26, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/citic-tower-in-beijing/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMk4xTUE4SE40NQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

BEIJING, Sept 17 (Reuters) - China is establishing a vast airspace security zone roughly the size of Italy around Beijing, barring all but commercial, approved business and emergency flights, months after a [small aircraft crashed](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/beijing-steps-up-police-presence-around-citys-tallest-tower-reuters-witnesses-2026-06-26/) into the capital's tallest ​building.

A permanent 600-kilometre-wide circle of "Special Restricted Area" centred around Beijing will take effect from ‌September 20, an aviation notice attributed to Beijing airspace control authorities and available through the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's public NOTAM search system reviewed by Reuters showed.

Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/trading-day/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fasia-pacific%2Fchina-creates-italy-sized-no-fly-zone-around-beijing-after-rare-crash-2026-09-17%2F)

The entire airspace, from ground to unlimited altitude, will be closed for all ​flights except for commercial airline flights, approved business flights and military, customs, police and fire-rescue ​flights, the notice showed.

The over 280,000-square-kilometre zone encompasses Beijing and Tianjin, much of Hebei, ⁠and extends into parts of Inner Mongolia, Shanxi, Shandong, Liaoning and the Bohai Sea. By a ​rough geographic estimate, some 100 million people and dozens of airports and smaller airfields fall within its ​bounds.

The zone is among the largest permanent airspace restrictions imposed over a capital city. It follows a rare breach of Beijing's tightly controlled skies that raised questions about security gaps in the airspace around the Chinese capital.

A light sport aircraft ​crashed into the 108-storey CITIC Tower in Beijing's central business district on June 26. Local authorities ​said the crash killed the sole pilot and injured 13 others who were not on board.

The [66-year-old pilot](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/beijing-says-plane-crash-into-skyscraper-was-caused-by-personal-reasons-2026-07-02/), who authorities said ‌had ⁠repeatedly mentioned ending his life in his diary, deviated from his approved flight area and lost contact with a general aviation airport in Beijing's suburbs from which he took off, official reports said.

## CONTINUOUS SURVEILLANCE

All exempt flights operating inside the new restricted zone must strictly follow the pre-approved flight plan, report and obtain ​approval for any potential ​deviation, and maintain continuous ⁠two-way radio communication with air traffic control, the notice showed.

Aircraft are required to have surveillance and identification equipment on board that would allow air traffic ​controllers to identify and track them continuously and electronically. Pilots must also report "security ​status" before ⁠entering the restricted zone, the notice said.

Chinese state media [said](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/china-impose-no-fly-zone-over-beijing-after-light-aircraft-crashed-into-citys-2026-09-14/) over the weekend a "Capital No-Fly Zone" would be established over Beijing from September 20, without specifying the exact size and scope of the restricted area.

"To strengthen airspace ⁠security management ​in the capital region, maintain order in aerial operations, and ​protect important targets on the ground and the lives and property of the public ... China will designate a no-fly zone in ​and around the capital," the state-run Beijing Daily said on Sunday.

Reporting by Beijing Newsroom; Editing by Sanjeev Miglani

title: 北京香山论坛 中国持续与美军对话，但孤立日本；各国代表担忧AI风险
summary: 台北 — 北京香山论坛星期四(9月17日)闭幕。论坛期间，美中两军在两国元首即将会晤前持续对话；不过，日本官方代表的缺席引起外界注意，中国高级官员二度借反对军国主义复活暗批日本。与此同时，与会各国代表对人工智能(AI)可能带来的风险感到担忧。 **美中两军持续对话** 香山论坛为中国所举办年度防务论坛，近年来也被视为地缘政治晴雨表。美国战争部今年派出负责中国、台湾和蒙古事务的首席主任辛西娅·“赞西”·卡拉斯(Cynthia “Xanthi” Carras)代表出席，级别较去年
content:
台北 —

北京香山论坛星期四(9月17日)闭幕。论坛期间，美中两军在两国元首即将会晤前持续对话；不过，日本官方代表的缺席引起外界注意，中国高级官员二度借反对军国主义复活暗批日本。与此同时，与会各国代表对人工智能(AI)可能带来的风险感到担忧。

**美中两军持续对话**

香山论坛为中国所举办年度防务论坛，近年来也被视为地缘政治晴雨表。美国战争部今年派出负责中国、台湾和蒙古事务的首席主任辛西娅·“赞西”·卡拉斯(Cynthia “Xanthi” Carras)代表出席，级别较去年代表美方出席的驻华使馆武官有所提升。

中国官媒《环球时报》星期二(9月15日)社评指出，在中美元首会晤共识引领下，两国军方各层级对话在持续恢复。尽管美方这次参加香山论坛规格层级并没有突破惯例，但为双方开展政策层面的务实探讨创造了条件。

唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统预计于9月24日在白宫以国宴接待中国国家主席习近平，并将再次召开元首峰会。

台湾国防安全研究院研究员沈明室接受美国之音采访指出，从不久前美军太平洋司令部司令塞缪尔·帕帕罗(Samuel Paparo)和中国解放军东部战区司令员杨志斌的会晤，再到这一次战争部派团出席香山论坛，象征中国不再把断绝两军交流作为惩罚手段。

2022年，美国联邦众议院前议长南西·佩洛西(Nancy Pelosi)访问台湾后，引起中国强烈不满，一度切断美中军事热线作为抵制。

沈明室说：“美国参加的代表团，或者是带队的人的层级高低，也可以看出美中关系，或者军事交流的这种现况。”

台湾大学政治系副教授陈世民认为，对美国来说，香山论坛也是一个美军了解其最大竞争对手的场合，甚至有机会认识到未来可能掌握军中重要职位的军官。

他说，在习近平持续清洗解放军的背景下，尤其中共中央军委会趋近被掏空，这样的平台或许能提供美国一探解放军如今如何指挥运作。

解放军第二号人物、中央军委会副主席张又侠，以及负责作战筹划的联合参谋部参谋长刘振立，今年8月被拔除军职与人大代表资格。军委会目前仅剩身兼军委主席的习近平，以及政工体系出身、主责纪检与反贪腐的张升民。

陈世民告诉美国之音：“美国还是愿意派一些，战争部负责中国安全事务的重要的官员，去参加这个会议。那我相信美国的目的，当然就是要去了解，中国到底目前军方，未来(可能接任)重要军事职位的人会是谁。”

**日本被刻意排除**

相较美国出席香山论坛层级提升，反映美中两国逐步修复关系，日本官方则被刻意被排除，也象征日中关系依旧紧张。

日媒《共同社》报导，去年代表日本参加的防卫省防卫研究所人员此次未获邀请，派驻当地的武官也未能参加。

中国这次邀请日本前首相鸠山由纪夫参与论坛对话。鸠山在论坛上被问及日中关系现况时建议，日本首相高市早苗应该收回关于“台湾有事”的言论。

高市去年11月在国会答辩时表示，中国对台湾使用武力可能构成日本的“存亡危机事态”，暗示日本可能出动自卫队武力介入台海危机。这番言论随后掀起日中外交风波。

中国国家副主席韩正星期二在欢迎晚会上致词表示，中国反对一切复活军国主义、危害地区安全稳定的图谋和行径；中国国防部长董军翌日在开幕致词上强调，对一切潜藏的霸权主义、军国主义、历史修正主义变异，要保持高度警惕。上述致词虽未直接点名，但被外界视为针对日本。也有人解读是针对日本和美国。

陈世民指出，香山论坛原意是仿效新加坡的香格里拉对话，邀集各国军方以沟通接触降低冲突风险。不过前提是要开放、平等、透明，而中国却只邀请它想听到的声音，这样做是没办法达到原先目的。

他说：“你只邀请日本的亲中人士，然后对日本现在政府官方，不欢迎他来，那你这样怎么可能发挥你(香山论坛)作为一个安全机制，所能够发挥的一个用谈判取代战争的角色，因为你听不到日本正式官方的一个立场。”

日本秋田国际教养大学全球研究学程副教授陈宥桦电邮回复美国之音表示，日本防卫研究所作为过往都会收到香山论坛邀请的对象，今年却被排除在外，一来是中国要营造出孤立日本的情境，二来也是因为不久前该研究所才被中国商务部列为制裁对象。

他认为，中国跟日本的关系未来只会日趋紧张，压力的源头在中国而非日本。中国正在透过各个管道对日本施压，逼迫日本改变对台湾支持的立场，香山论坛只是其中之一，但是日本支持台湾的立场，因结构性因素是不可能改变的。

**与会各国代表担忧AI的发展**

香山论坛共有来自100多个国家、地区和国际组织的官方代表、专家学者和观察员。除了地缘政治情势，多国代表也对人工智能(AI)不受控制的发展和美中在此领域的竞争表达担忧。

路透社星期四报导，泰国国防部长阿敦(Adul Boonthumjaroen)指出，随着人工智能等技术改变战争形态，最紧迫是该如何建立一个国际秩序。巴基斯坦国防秘书阿里(Muhammad Ali)表示，人工智能加快了决策速度，而虚假与错误信息在政府能够有效应对之前，就可能摧毁公众信任。

此前，美国人工智能公司Anthropic联合创始人达里奥·阿莫迪(Dario Amodei)、OpenAI首席执行官塞姆·奥尔特曼(Sam Altman)、xAI创办人埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)等科技巨头齐声呼吁放缓AI发展。但特朗普总统则强调所谓的“AI末世论”是骗局。他说，如果美国放缓脚步，最高兴的会是中国。

中国顶尖AI企业高层大多未呼吁放慢AI发展脚步，中国政府则将AI视为驱动经济成长的力量。

美国海军分析中心研究员冯德威(David Finkelstein)在香山论坛场边接受媒体联访时表示，当AI应用于作战指挥体系、战争场景，乃至被纳入核指挥链条时，其所带来的风险值得高度警惕。在这个议题上，美中非常有必要开启对话。

AI治理预计将成为下周特朗普总统与中国领导人习近平会晤的议题之一。另据报道，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)9月20日在纽约接待中国国务院副总理何立峰率领的代表团，双方将先行讨论AI共同风险。

title: EU Commission proposes under-13s social media ban
summary: * Summary * Companies * Von der Leyen sets out proposal at press conference * Months of debate ahead before it could become law * Tech lobbying group warns of privacy risks STRASBOURG, France, Sept 17 (Reuters) - European Commission Preside
content:
*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Von der Leyen sets out proposal at press conference
*   Months of debate ahead before it could become law
*   Tech lobbying group warns of privacy risks

STRASBOURG, France, Sept 17 (Reuters) - European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen set out a ‌sweeping plan to keep children safe from online dangers on Thursday, proposing to ban under-13s from social media and require online services to design safe children's accounts.

The move follows [similar initiatives](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/australia-europe-countries-move-curb-childrens-social-media-access-2026-08-24/) in Australia, Britain, China, India, Turkey and several European Union countries ​over concerns about the impact Meta's

Facebook and Instagram, TikTok, Google's

YouTube and ChatGPT have on ​children's mental health and safety.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Feu-commission-proposes-social-media-ban-children-under-13-2026-09-17%2F)

[Australia's challenges](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/australia-defends-teen-social-media-ban-after-study-shows-most-still-online-2026-08-01/) in enforcing its world-first social media ban for ⁠children under 16 could see Europe facing an uphill battle as well.

"Today, our children are engaging with ​some of the most sophisticated technology ever created, and it was not created with children's well-being and development ​in mind," von der Leyen told a press conference.

She said the proposed EU Kids Act "will set clear boundaries in the digital world just as we do it on a daily basis in the real world".

## PARENTAL CONTROL

Under the proposal, which must ​be negotiated with EU countries and the European Parliament in the coming months before it can become ​law, accounts for children aged between 13 and 15 will be under parental control.

Teenagers pose for a picture while looking at a phone, in Bonn, Germany, February 20, 2026. REUTERS/Jana Rodenbusch [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/german-school-kids-react-to-germany-mulling-social-media-ban-for-minors/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMk9QSkFRSEQzVw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Social media and video-sharing services, online video ‌games, AI ⁠companions and chatbots for children below 18 will be subject to a list of dos and don'ts.

These include a ban on addictive features, profiling-based recommender feeds, infinite scroll, reward tricks and unsolicited contact from strangers. AI companions and chatbots must be turned off by default.

Online platforms must design algorithms safe for children and ​provide easy-to-use parental controls ​and tools to block ⁠and mute users.

The companies, which must verify users' age when they open an account via age assurance tools, risk fines as much as 6% of their global ​annual sales for non-compliance. They will also have to pay a supervisory ​fee to fund ⁠regulators' supervision.

Tech lobbying group CCIA Europe, whose members include Google and Meta, warned of the privacy risks arising from the proposal and conflicting requirements under other EU laws.

"Collecting age information, identity credentials, and data linking children with ⁠parents ​or guardians at this scale would undoubtedly create an attractive target ​for cybercriminals," CCIA head Daniel Friedlaender said.

"The Kids Act creates legal overlap and duplication that ultimately weaken protections for children and consumers," ​he said.

Reporting by Foo Yun Chee and Yves Herman, editing by Inti Landauro, Richard Lough and Timothy Heritage

Our Standards: [The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles., opens new tab](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/about-us/trust-principles.html)

An agenda-setting and market-moving journalist, Foo Yun Chee is a 21-year veteran at Reuters. Her stories on high profile mergers have pushed up the European telecoms index, lifted companies' shares and helped investors decide on their next move. Her knowledge and experience of European antitrust laws and developments helped her break stories on Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and Apple, numerous market-moving mergers and antitrust investigations. She has previously reported on Greek politics and companies, when Greece's entry into the eurozone meant it punched above its weight on the international stage, as well as on Dutch corporate giants and the quirks of Dutch society and culture that never fail to charm readers.

title: 国际刑警组织将于香港召开大会 英国律师警告中国可能借机“洗白”声誉

content:
伦敦 —

国际刑警组织(INTERPOL)第94届全体大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行。中国长期以来被指利用国际刑警组织追查政治目标，分析人士担心，中国可能借主办大会的机会，为自己的形象“洗白”。

“根据我们的经验，中国是滥用国际刑警组织规则最老练的国家之一”，英国上级审裁院移民和庇护庭副法官本·基思(Ben Keith)和在伦敦及海牙执业的大律师里斯·戴维斯(Rhys Davies)对美国之音表示。

两人长期处理红色通报、引渡及跨国镇压案件，并合作撰写刚发表的新书《国际刑警组织：法律与实务》（INTERPOL Law and Practice）。

**香港办大会，为中国洗白**

国际刑警组织在香港召开大会期间，将选举档案控制委员会(Commission for the Control of INTERPOL's Files, CCF)的全部七名成员。该委员会负责处理个人对自身数据的查询，也是唯一有权裁决并删除或修改红色通报(Red Notice)申请的机构。

基思说，他担心北京利用香港主办大会的机会，为自身形象“洗白”。“我们非常担心，中国正试图利用国际刑警组织为自己的声誉洗白。”他说。

香港警方近年对多名身处海外的民主活动人士、律师及倡议者发出国安法通缉令，部分案件附带100万港元悬赏。英国政府的香港半年报告说，截至2025年底，香港警方已对34名海外人士发出涉及国家安全罪名的通缉令。

基思把这些悬赏形容为“极其阴险”。他说，这不仅是提供现金线索，也是在鼓励他人寻找方法，把目标带回中国。

英国资深大律师、前香港大律师公会主席夏博义(Paul Harris SC)也对美国之音说，他对大会在香港举行“非常担忧”。

他说：“这是不合适的，因为中国已经违反《中英联合声明》，并以政治罪名监禁香港人。”

英国政府批评香港的海外通缉及悬赏是企图恐吓在英国合法行使言论自由的人士。

香港政府则表示，有关人士涉嫌危害国家安全，当局是在依法追捕逃犯，并非因为其政治立场或言论采取行动。香港政府也表示，《香港国安法》保障人权和自由，绝大多数居民及访港人士不会受到影响。

**政治案件披上刑事外衣**

戴维斯说，中国已成为国际刑警组织中的重要力量。他认为，一些由中国提出的红色通报表面涉及普通刑事罪名，实际上却带有政治动机。

他特别提到中国的“猎狐行动”和“天网行动”。北京将这些行动称为“追逃追赃及反腐败工作”，但基思说，他们接触了部分被中国当局锁定的目标，其中包括异议人士、记者及曾经批评中国政府的人。

基思还说，中国当局有时会扣留或威胁当事人在华亲属，再要求身处海外的目标回国“协助调查”；检察人员也可能向目标保证，回国后不会受到处罚。

中国政府表示，“猎狐”和“天网”旨在追捕涉嫌腐败及其他犯罪的外逃人员，并否认有关行动构成跨国镇压。中国外交部此前对国际调查记者同盟(ICIJ)表示，“中方严格遵守国际法及各国主权”。

戴维斯借用法律界的一个说法，把红色通报称为“独裁者的狙击步枪”，可以跨越国界，精准锁定个人。

他说，即使当事人没有旅行计划，红色通报仍可能导致银行终止服务、声誉受损及长期心理压力。

人权观察(Human Rights Watch)及其他人权机构多次指责中国滥用红色通缉令系统，将其作为打压海外异议人士、维权维稳以及强迫流亡公民回国的工具。

戴维斯认为，红色通报最隐蔽之处，是它为政治追捕披上一层法律外衣。请求国把指控提交国际刑警组织后，其他成员国的警务机关可能因为加入了这一体系而采取行动。

**国际刑警组织如何审查通报**

国际刑警组织章程第三条禁止该组织介入政治、军事、宗教或种族性质的活动。

该组织表示，所有红色通报均须经过专门工作组审查，已经发布的通报也会持续接受核查。当事人可以向档案控制委员会申请查阅或删除资料。

国际刑警组织此前回应国际调查记者同盟时表示，它拥有“稳健且持续接受评估”的审查制度，但最初决定只能依据提出申请时掌握的资料作出。

两名律师承认，国际刑警组织近年来加强了审查。然而，他们认为，如果政治案件被包装成诈骗、腐败或其他普通刑事案件，仍可能通过初步审查。

基思和戴维斯强调，国际刑警合作对于打击严重跨国犯罪不可或缺。但真正的问题是，当一项刑事指控进入全球警务系统后，谁能及时区分正常执法与政治追捕，以及谁来保护被错误锁定的人。

美国之音已就香港主办国际刑警组织全体大会和相关争议，分别向香港警务处和中国驻英国大使馆请求置评。截至发稿，尚未收到回复。

title: 特习会结束，台湾、日本反驳习近平叙事，专家：美或一年内落实对台军售
summary: 华盛顿 — 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)与中国国家主席习近平在华盛顿的峰会星期五(9月25日)落幕。美中元首会谈不仅事关两国关系，对全球经济及地区安全也带来重大影响。特朗普在台湾议题及对台军售问题上的表态因涉及第一岛链及印太地区的安全，美国印太盟友也关注峰会的结果。 在习近平对美国为期三天的国事访问结束后，外界一般认为，此次会面着较重于排场和礼仪，但实质性成果较为有效。前美国国务院亚太事务副助卿柯庆生(Thomas Christensen)星期五在美国智
content:
华盛顿 —

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)与中国国家主席习近平在华盛顿的峰会星期五(9月25日)落幕。美中元首会谈不仅事关两国关系，对全球经济及地区安全也带来重大影响。特朗普在台湾议题及对台军售问题上的表态因涉及第一岛链及印太地区的安全，美国印太盟友也关注峰会的结果。

在习近平对美国为期三天的国事访问结束后，外界一般认为，此次会面着较重于排场和礼仪，但实质性成果较为有效。前美国国务院亚太事务副助卿柯庆生(Thomas Christensen)星期五在美国智库战略与国际研究中心(CSIS)就此次峰会举行的线上讨论会上表示，从上一次特朗普与习近平5月份在北京峰会后的情况来看，从特朗普总统后来对媒体的发言才能更清楚知道，两人在会谈中真正的讨论话题与表态。

“我认为许多人都在想说我们已经在一个和解状态，这是美中关系一个重大改变。在我看来，这只是一个休兵或停火。我认为它非常脆弱。当我在看一年以后的情形时，我会预期，这个关系将有许多麻烦，”他说。

尽管北京的最终目标是要试图使特朗普停止对台军售，不过柯庆生表示，特朗普面对的国会的压力太大，两党参、众议员都要求他尽快批准已经延迟的140亿美元军售案，而且以他自己在国务院处理对台军售的经验，台湾立法院能通过300亿美元对美军事采购特别预算是极其不容易的，美国自己也有极大欲望要售台武器，未来一年这会是一个非常难以抗拒的机会。

“促使台湾采购如此大规模武器是一个极不寻常的机会，即便特朗普总统想要避免惹恼他的朋友习主席，那都会是未来12个月很难完全抗拒的机遇，”柯庆生说。

战略与研究中心中国实力项目主任林洋(Bonnie Lin)在讨论中提到，中国海警与海军这个星期再度阻止菲律宾向在第二托马斯浅滩(Second Thomas Shoal, 中国称仁爱礁，菲律宾称阿云津礁)的驻军运送补给，这是双方就仁爱礁补给问题达成临时协议两年来第一次发生同样问题，显示北京当局对美中元首的会面更有自信，因为通常在峰会前中国会尽量避免南中国海成为双方谈论的话题。

北京方面在特朗普和习近平的会谈后随即发布两人的谈话内容，除了两国双边关系和台湾议题外，双方也谈及中东局势、乌克兰危机及朝鲜半岛等议题，但在会谈后的24小时中，白宫却迟迟没有公布美方版本的会谈纪要，外界难以对峰会触及的更多面向做进一步解读。

白宫直到星期五下午才针对峰会发布声明说，正如特朗普总统所说，“这次会晤对中国和美国来说都是友谊、实力和成功的会晤……已经而且将会取得很多成就。”

除了提到多项关于峰会的仪式外，声明强调，特朗普也和习近平举行了“富有成效的双边讨论”。

特朗普说：“我认为我们的农场主和牧场主将会非常高兴--发生了很多积极的事情……对两国来说的大好事。会谈非常、非常富有成效。”

声明最后表示，此次国事访问展示了美国的实力、促进了美国的的经济利益，并明确揭示了一点：当美国凭借实力地位发挥领导作用时，和平与繁荣才最为稳固。

白宫在峰会后的初步声明没有提到特朗普与习近平会谈的实质内容，不过习近平在星期四白宫欢迎仪式上提及二战期间“中美并肩抗击法西斯侵略”，又在当天晚上的欢迎晚宴上说，“中美两国人民并肩作战，抗击日本军国主义侵略者”，同时引发了台湾和日本政府的反应。

台湾外交部更强烈驳斥中国外交部关于习近平在与特朗普的会谈中提及：“希望美方坚持反对‘台独’的正确立场，慎重处理台湾问题，为中美战略合作和两国关系发展奠定坚实基础”的叙述。

台湾外交部星期五在一个声明中说：“这是中方一贯透过扭曲事实，单方面传达其立场与主张的手法。”

台湾外交部重申：“中华民国与中华人民共和国互不隶属，台湾主权属于台湾人民，中共政权无权代表台湾，而台湾的未来只能由台湾人民以民主方式共同决定。”

台湾陆委会也发布声明指出，北京当局对二战的论述“完全是扭曲历史事实，1949年才成立的中华人民共和国，在二战期间根本不存在”，真正与美国并肩作战的是中华民国。

日本内阁官房长官，也是日本政府主要发言人木原稔星期五在记者会上表示，日本“高度关注”此次会谈，但没有立场评论美中两国元首的谈话。不过他提及日本与美国的关系表示，两国在战后达成和解并成为彼此最信任的盟友，也对亚太地区和全世界做出和平稳定的贡献。

日本放送协会(NHK)报道，木原稔强调，自二战后日本作为一个爱好和平的国家，始终致力于为世界和平繁荣做出贡献，并持续坚持此一方针和基本原则，对于习近平要求特朗普“坚持反对‘台独’”，木原稔表示，日本没有立场对此事发表评论，但他强调，台海和平稳定对整个国际社会至为重要，日本长期以来的立场就是希望涉台议题能通过对话和平解决。

title: 历史回顾：美国各届总统为到访的中国领导人准备的白宫国宴
summary: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普(Melania Trump)星期四(9月24日)在白宫为对美国进行国事访问的中国国家主席习近平和夫人彭丽媛举行举行了隆重的欢迎仪式之后，当晚又以国宴款待习近平主席夫妇。 这场国宴的筹备工作由梅拉尼娅亲自操盘，她的办公室在一份[公告](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2026/09/first-lady-melania-trump-rel
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普(Melania Trump)星期四(9月24日)在白宫为对美国进行国事访问的中国国家主席习近平和夫人彭丽媛举行举行了隆重的欢迎仪式之后，当晚又以国宴款待习近平主席夫妇。

这场国宴的筹备工作由梅拉尼娅亲自操盘，她的办公室在一份[公告](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2026/09/first-lady-melania-trump-releases-details-on-the-state-dinner-with-his-excellency-xi-jinping-president-of-the-peoples-republic-of-china-and-madame-peng-liyuan/)中表示，国宴的菜单“既展示了美国本土食材，又融入了微妙的中国风味，将两国的烹饪传统巧妙融合在了一起。”

首道菜品是一道黄南瓜天鹅绒浓汤(velouté)，配料包括野生蘑菇、新鲜香草和酥脆的意式培根(pancetta)，并淋有葱油。

宾客享用的第二道菜品是芝麻脆皮海鲈鱼，配菜包括炖小油菜、烤田园茄子以及绿酱(sauce verte)。

甜点方面，国宴提供香草奶油冻(crémeux)配酸樱桃蜜饯，两者均置于核桃杏仁奶油馅饼(frangipane)之上。这道甜点还将搭配一款冰淇淋，其原料蜂蜜采自第一夫人于今年4月在白宫庭院内设立的一个新的蜂箱。

特朗普总统在上午的欢迎仪式上致辞时特别指出，习近平是唯一一位两次对白宫进行国事访问的中国领导人。

而习近平上一次做客白宫是在2015年9月25日，由巴拉克·奥巴马(Barack Obama)总统和第一夫人米歇尔·奥巴马(Michelle Obama)招待。

当晚国宴的菜品包括配有黑松露和南瓜薄片的本地蘑菇清汤、黄油慢煮缅因龙虾配米粉卷、以及烤科罗拉多羊柳，佐以意式奶冻(裹有轻薄天妇罗面衣)和嫩西兰花。甜点则由带有淡淡黄油香气的面包搭配精致蛋奶冻组成，辅以迈耶柠檬酱(Meyer lemon curd)和荔枝雪葩。

第一位享受白宫国宴接待的中国领导人其实并不是国家元首，而是拥有绝对权威但职务只是国务院副总理的邓小平。

1979年1月29日，美中建交后不久，吉米·卡特(Jimmy Carter)总统和第一夫人罗莎琳·卡特(Rosalynn Carter)在白宫隆重接待了来美国进行正式访问的邓小平和夫人卓琳。这是自1943年已故中国前第一夫人蒋宋美龄访问白宫以来，到访白宫的最高级别中国访客。

根据《白宫历史协会》(White House Historical Association)的记载，卡特当天与邓小平举行了两场会谈，当晚举行国宴时，理查德·尼克松（Richard Nixon）总统辞职后首次返回白宫，与邓小平夫妇以及其他宾客享用了烧烤小牛腿、海鲜百花卷、芷红花香饭、翡翠甘蓝花与西洋菜沙拉以及奶油栗子冻，并配以香槟和白葡萄酒。

历史照片：1979年1月29日美国总统吉米·卡特(Jimmy Carter)及夫人罗塞琳·卡特(Rosalynn Carter)在白宫为时任中国国务院副总理邓小平及夫人卓琳举行晚宴时的菜单。(Credit: White House Historical Association/Courtesy of Henry & Carole Haller and Family)

1984年1月10日，首位中国政府首脑、国务院总理赵紫阳对美国进行国事访问。罗纳德·里根(Ronald Reagan)总统和第一夫人南希·里根(Nancy Reagan)在白宫设国宴招待赵紫阳，宾客们享用了酥皮酿牛肉、水煮多宝鱼以及石榴雪葩。

1985年7月23日，首位中国国家主席李先念对美国进行国事访问，里根总统和第一夫人南希·里根在白宫为李先念和中国第一夫人林佳楣举行国宴。当晚的菜品包括青柠萨巴雍(lime sabayon)、龙虾、夏南瓜和小牛里脊肉。

在比尔·克林顿(Bill Clinton)担任总统期间，曾有两位中国领导人前来美国进行国事访问。一位是中国国家主席江泽民和第一夫人王冶萍于1997年10月29日在白宫受到克林顿总统和第一夫人希拉里·克林顿(Hillary Clinton)隆重军礼欢迎。在当晚的白宫国宴上，江泽民夫妇和宾客们享用了配以青柠叶、香茅及玉米韭葱佐料的水煮龙虾、胡椒脆皮俄勒冈牛肉、柑橘茶味塔、杏仁膏熊猫造型甜点以及螺旋纹橙味雪葩。

1999年4月8日，中国国务院总理朱镕基对美国进行国事访问。克林顿总统夫妇在白宫以全套军礼为他举行欢迎仪式。当晚的国宴上，主菜是配以焦糖茴香和菊苣的烤鲑鱼；甜点则包括橙子雪葩、茶味芭菲(parfait)以及覆盆子和金橘小塔。

2006年4月20日，中国国家主席胡锦涛与夫人刘永清访美，但此次美国之行未被定位为国事访问，因此尽管他仍获享白宫南草坪鸣放21响礼炮的礼遇，并检阅了身着殖民时期服饰的笛鼓仪仗队，但是乔治·W·布什(George W. Bush)总统并未为他举行国宴，而是举办了一场午宴，菜品包括阿拉斯加比目鱼配蘑菇精华汁、黄油传家宝玉米浓汤及姜香饺子。

2011年1月19日，胡锦涛再次访美，此次访问被定性为国事访问，因此奥巴马总统为他在白宫举行隆重正式的欢迎仪式，获得包括21响礼炮在内的全套军礼礼遇。当晚国宴的菜品包括采用白宫花园蜂蜜调味的香草菜肴、山羊奶酪配梨沙拉、水煮缅因龙虾、肉眼牛排，以及作为甜点的苹果派配香草冰淇淋。

习近平似乎是唯一一位两次对美国进行国事访问的中国国家主席。但是如果他依照邓小平等老一代领导人设立的规矩，最高领导人的任期不超过两个五年任期的话，今天来白宫做客的人就应该不是他了。

title: China Still Has What America Needs: The Trump-Xi Summit Gives Washington a Chance to Buy Time
summary: The Trump administration approached its summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in October 2025 projecting confidence, asserting that it held leverage over China as the trade deficit country in the bilateral relationship. As U.S. Treasury Sec
content:
The Trump administration approached its summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in October 2025 projecting confidence, asserting that it held leverage over China as the trade deficit country in the bilateral relationship. As U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put it, “What do we lose by the Chinese raising tariffs on us? We export one-fifth to them of what they export to us, so that is a losing hand for them.” This was quickly shown to be folly. As I argued [in _Foreign Affairs_](https://www.foreignaffairs.com/united-states/tariffs-trade-wars-are-easy-lose), trade wars are easy to lose when countries depend upon an exporter for hard-to-replace inputs, yet still conceive of trade as a zero-sum game. China has escalation dominance over the United States, meaning that at any level of threat, the Chinese government has the ability to inflict more pain on the United States than vice versa. To ease Beijing’s restrictions on rare-earth elements, for example, which allow China to control 80 to 90 percent of production, the United States has conceded on tariffs, technology controls, and visa policies during various [negotiations](https://www.foreignaffairs.com/united-states/how-america-can-stop-getting-played-china).

But Washington’s inability to immediately decouple, let alone extract concessions, from China through tariff threats should not mean giving up on economic diplomacy. For centuries, lesser powers in the world economy subject to escalation dominance have navigated relations with their more powerful adversaries by bargaining while avoiding confrontation. In fact, until recently, that is how China—and essentially all other countries—have viewed their economic interactions with the United States, to the occasional frustration of U.S. officials.

Economic relationships are not all or nothing; they have room for resistance and cooperation, even if one side would clearly lose if it came down to outright conflict. Despite the high distrust and strategic rivalry between the two countries, the U.S.-Chinese economic relationship does not have to be played as a zero-sum game. The benefits from trade and diversification for both economies remain substantial, and China’s escalation dominance would not spare its own economy pain if it were forced into a tit-for-tat conflict with Washington. Indeed, Beijing, comfortable with the status quo, has little interest in such escalation.

At the upcoming summit between Xi and President Donald Trump, the U.S. government should initiate a different approach to the economic relationship by pursuing increased imports of key strategic goods as well as increased foreign direct investment from China. This should be only one part of a broader economic strategy, of course. Cooperation with allies will be necessary to encourage any sustained changes in Chinese commercial behavior and to diversify sources of supply over the longer term. A more complex assessment of Xi’s strategic goals and China’s vulnerabilities will also be needed for longer-term strategic success. But this meeting—and any that follow—give Washington a valuable opportunity to buy time to address the country’s acute needs.

### START WITH STOCKPILING

Despite a decade of denouncing the threat of Chinese imports and investment, under both the Trump and the Biden administrations, the U.S. government has failed to meaningfully decouple even the most sensitive industries from China. As the economists Mary Lovely and Christine Wan have shown, declining direct U.S. imports from China have simply resulted in supply chains becoming more attenuated and less transparent. China remains the source of rare earths, specialized magnets, and the lower-end semiconductors used in autos and appliances, even if intermediate steps of production now take place elsewhere. In the critical area of pharmaceuticals, for example, the United States may import numerous generic drugs from India, but India relies on China for the feedstocks and components to produce them.

This situation is precisely why industrial decoupling is such an uphill battle: strong economic fundamentals drove these commercial arrangements and unwinding them is slow and costly. For now, Washington’s most important priority should be to build up short-term inventories of those strategic goods ultimately sourced from China. In an ideal world, the United States would immediately get them from elsewhere, but the Trump administration, like the Biden administration before it, has not made significant progress on this front. Both tried, but failed, to incentivize the creation of alternative sourcing through wider access to the U.S. market or other compensation. And at their worst, in some benighted attempt to spontaneously create U.S. production through deprivation, both tried to force American businesses to do without Chinese inputs through tariffs and restrictions.

Meanwhile, U.S. officials have wasted past summits and negotiations by trying to convince their counterparts in Beijing to increase Chinese imports of various nonstrategic goods, none of which China values most. These efforts may be rationalized by current and former officials as a bank shot to make China more dependent on U.S. goods and gain leverage in future negotiations. But exports of American airliners and soybeans neither alleviate the immediate security vulnerability nor improve U.S. macroeconomic fundamentals. In fact, to the degree that such prioritization on export promotion allows China to pit the United States and its allies against each other—for example, inducing government-led bilateral deals to increase sales of Boeing versus Airbus airliners and vice versa—it weakens Washington’s ability to line up a unified front against economic coercion.

At the upcoming summit, the Trump administration should take a different tack. At the October 2025 meeting between Trump and Xi, the United States and Beijing struck a deal to temporarily reduce tariffs in exchange for partially relaxing limits on the exports of critical materials from China. In doing so, the administration, in essence, gave up on any strategic goals as soon as its bluster was revealed to be hiding weakness.And with the agreement set to expire in November, Washington may be tempted to simply renew its terms. Instead, the Trump administration should seek a more ambitious deal that includes multiyear, large-scale purchasing agreements for the critical goods whose production is currently heavily concentrated in China (or whose critical components are produced in China for supply chains elsewhere). The United States could use government guarantees and even purchases to create strategic reserves until alternative domestic or reliable allied sources emerge. In exchange, it should allow China to import more of some sought-after technologies in which the United States still has a lead.

> The threat of a sustained cutoff by China, while real, is exaggerated.

Such an agreement is both more attainable and more sustainable than many opponents may think. Even during the Cold War, in the 1970s and 1980s, the Soviet Union and the United States concluded a series of grain deals that allowed the Soviets to import American wheat, corn, and soybeans. Despite the constant temptation to exploit Soviet dependence—President Jimmy Carter would embargo trade with the Soviet Union in 1979 after its invasion of Afghanistan—the deals were renewed and expanded by Presidents Ronald Reagan and George H. W. Bush.

China could, of course, renege on such agreements at any time. It has already set the terms of its exports of rare earths and associated products in a way that discourages resale and accumulation, precisely to maintain the leverage it has built up. The direct cash value of rare-earth export sales by China is small and, in isolation, an insufficient incentive to give up that leverage.

Yet the threat of a sustained cutoff by China, while real, is exaggerated. For its part, China has an interest in selling more exports to offset its persistently weak domestic [demand](https://www.foreignaffairs.com/china/end-china-economic-miracle-beijing-washington) and industrial overcapacity. Furthermore, heavy use of export bans is costly, provokes retaliation, and ultimately encourages the development of hostile alternative systems. Washington should understand these risks all too well:U.S. overuse of financial sanctions have encouraged movement out of the dollar and into Chinese-led payments systems over the last five years.It is more likely that a U.S. offer of sufficient commercial benefit would induce China to export more freely.

Historically, even rivals approaching the cusp of war have successfully pursued stockpiling and continued trade. Before World War II, Japan did everything it could to import energy, rubber, and other critical supplies, getting as much as 40 percent of its war supplies from the United States as late as 1941, when Washington banned trade with Tokyo. Germany and the Soviet Union, meanwhile, were trading militarily useful technology and petroleum products through their respective invasions of Poland in 1939. And trade between France and Germany was largely stable in the decade leading up to World War I.

The same incentives that have governed strategic rivals throughout modern history apply to China and the United States today. The Trump administration and its more hawkish critics should thus recognize that greater flexibility on U.S. export controls—combined with opening of investment opportunities in the United States in a broader commercial relationship—is worth exercising for the benefits of more reliable access to Chinese goods for which Washington currently lacks any alternative. This is simply recognizing reality, rather than just giving up or insisting on using a tool that will not work. The smart move for the U.S. government is to import and stockpile as much as it can from China for as long as it can. Doing so should not discourage the creation of domestic or reliable allied supply any more than the United States cutting itself off from Chinese supply has encouraged it.

### INVESTED IN SUCCESS

Since ancient times, potential enemies have engaged in a form of hostage exchange, sending nobles or royal family members to live—and be at risk—in the opposing side’s metropole. This was not an absolute deterrent to conflict, but it did serve as a disincentive to attacks and slowed down precipitous escalations. Some hostages even proved to be useful envoys, enhancing understanding between both sides through public diplomacy, intelligence gathering, or both.

The modern economic form of the hostage exchange is foreign direct investment (FDI). Leading companies establish presences in rival countries, transferring technologies and management practices across borders. Much like the nobles of antiquity, this presence is symbolically valuable, since the companies are often closely tied to the elites at home and the practice puts their investment at risk.

But contemporary two-way FDI flows also generate substantially more economic benefits than the exchange of individual nobles ever did. FDI investments are statistically associated with the creation of jobs that pay well relative to local average wages, increases in local research and development spending, and diminished supply volatility through geographic diversification. This kind of exchange was a key component of successive economic deals between the United States and Europe, Japan, and Korea when the latter group saw relative gains of industrial competitiveness vis-à-vis American industry in the 1960 through the early 2000s. FDI reduced the occurrence of punitive tariffs and export controls, both by directly decreasing the need for them and by creating political constituencies with an economic interest in integration.

> The net benefits to the United States of Chinese FDI have gone up in recent years.

The U.S.-Chinese relationship, of course, is quite different

 Attendees gather at the Global South Modernization Forum in Cairo, Egypt, on Wednesday. XINHUA

CAIRO — The 2026 Global South Modernization Forum was held in Cairo on Wednesday under the theme "The Rise of Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges for Modernization in the Global South."

More than 100 experts and scholars from nearly 30 countries and regions attended the forum.

Participants said innovation in AI technology presents enormous opportunities while also posing governance challenges.

At the 18th BRICS Summit earlier this month, President Xi Jinping put forward important initiatives to empower new industrialization with AI and promote open-source and inclusive AI development, outlining a direction for AI development that serves the common good, they said.

Modernization in the Global South is at a crucial stage of overcoming development constraints, addressing capacity gaps and transforming growth drivers, they said, calling for effective use of AI to continually strengthen the internal drivers of development.

Participants said AI is a shared asset of all humanity and urged Global South countries to seize this historic opportunity to use AI to empower a wide range of industries and improve people's well-being.

They called for improving global AI governance, practicing genuine multilateralism, bridging the AI divide and ensuring that development and security reinforce each other.

They also urged greater exchanges and mutual learning in AI, a commitment to open-source development, openness, cooperation and sharing, and deeper theoretical and practical research to ensure that AI better benefits humanity.

The forum was jointly hosted by the State Council Information Office of China, the Party School of the Communist Party of China Central Committee (National Academy of Governance), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Peking University, Renmin University of China and Cairo University.

The event featured four parallel forums. "The Rise of the Global South: An Atlas of Academic Research on Modernization in the Global South" and "Top 10 Buzzwords in Global South Modernization Research of 2026" were released at the forum.

Academic exhibitions, youth exchanges and think tank seminars were also held before and after the forum.

title: A pilot brawl, then a rapid descent: passengers recount chaos on flydubai flight
summary: * Summary * Companies * Passenger describes incident on flydubai flight FZ1073 * Plane plunged sharply, wounded captain lay on the floor * A passenger subdued co-pilot who had stabbed the captain * Wounded captain managed to unlock cockpit
content:
*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Passenger describes incident on flydubai flight FZ1073
*   Plane plunged sharply, wounded captain lay on the floor
*   A passenger subdued co-pilot who had stabbed the captain
*   Wounded captain managed to unlock cockpit door
*   Reserve crew on board landed plane in Saudi Arabia

JERUSALEM, Sept 30 - When [flydubai flight](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/) FZ1073 suddenly plunged from ​over 30,000 feet on Wednesday, passenger Almog Italie said it felt like the plane was passing through "massive turbulence" before he ‌realised a life-or-death struggle had unfolded in the cockpit.

Italie described passengers running to the front of the cabin and commotion in front of the cockpit, where Israeli officials said the co-pilot had stabbed the captain to try to crash the plane flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with more than 170 Israelis on board.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fpilot-brawl-then-rapid-descent-passengers-recount-chaos-flydubai-flight-2026-09-30%2F)

"It was dropping like for 20, ​30 seconds, and then balanced, and then started dropping again, and balanced again, and then we saw that (there) are people in the front, ​directly (in front of ) the cockpit," he told Reuters. "Crew members and passengers from the front of the airplane took over ⁠and got control of the two pilots."

Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister’s office, said the wounded captain, bloodied and lying on the ​floor, had drawn on "the last moments of his energy" to click open the release on the cockpit door.

"At that moment, some of the passengers that ​realised something was happening raced forward, entered the pilot's cabin. They saw the injured pilot on the ground, and the other … the attacking pilot was standing over the control panel, bashing the control panel," he said.

A passenger subdued the attacker, he said.

A video filmed on board and verified by Reuters captured the aftermath.

In it, two wounded men are seen ​lying on the floor, both bloodied. A voice speaking in Hebrew off camera says one of them is the pilot "they tried to murder". A ​voice off camera identifies the other as the attacker, lying on his side with three stripes on his epaulette, indicating that he is a co-pilot.

"We were attacked now, on ‌this airplane, ⁠they tried to murder the pilot, and we took control of the team/staff," a man in a black shirt with blood on his face says.

A plane, carrying passengers who were on the FlyDubai aircraft bound for Israel from the United Arab Emirates, which was diverted to Saudi Arabia following an emergency signal, on the tarmac as it arrives at the Ben Gurion International Airport, in Lod, near Tel Aviv, Israel, September 30, 2026. REUTERS/Ammar Awad [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/passengers-from-a-flydubai-flight-to-israel-from-united-arab-emirates-that-was-diverted-to-saudi-arabia-after-an-emergency-signal-arrive-at-ben-gurion-international-airport/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlJUTkEzUlU2VQ%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Another man says: "We're standing here, no one is going to pass through the pilot's door."

## RESERVE CREW

A reserve flydubai crew that had been on board took control of the plane and landed it safely at Tabuk Airport (TUU), a flydubai spokesperson said.

A playback of the flight posted on flight-tracking website flightradar24 showed the plane cruising ​at 34,000 feet heading westwards over ​Saudi Arabia when it dropped more ⁠than 14,000 feet in 30 seconds, before veering northwest. It briefly crossed into Jordan, then returned to Saudi airspace and flew to Tabuk.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said the attempted attack "was thwarted solely thanks to the heroism of ​several Israeli passengers who stormed the cockpit, subdued the terrorist, and — with their own hands — restored control of ​the aircraft to an ⁠additional flight crew present on board".

"According to our preliminary information, the terrorist had a single objective: to crash the plane," he said in a statement.

Flydubai said in a statement that the underlying reasons for the event remained unknown and warned against "premature speculation".

Italie said the reserve crew "took over the airplane and balanced it".

"It was ⁠quite scary, but ​not for long. Most of the passengers kept calm and were very supportive to each ​other. And when then we landed in Saudi Arabia, which we got a very very warm welcome with a lot of medical staff and food and anything we needed, and we're ​waiting for the flight back to Tel Aviv," he said.

Additional reporting by Edward James Carron and Marine Delrue, Writing by Tom Perry, Editing by Timothy Heritage
