Alexander has over a decade of international reporting experience. He is currently a senior correspondent in Jerusalem covering Israel & the Palestinian Territories and was formerly in Dubai where he covered the Arabian Peninsula, including the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Yemen, often writing about foreign policy, security and economic-related issues.

title: Do I need a visa for France? Entry rules by nationality, purpose and length of stay
summary: ## Border modernisation: EES and ETIAS in 2026 Two new systems now apply at the Schengen border, and neither of them is a visa. They sit alongside the visa rules rather than replacing them. **The Entry/Exit System (EES) is**an automated bor
content:
## Border modernisation: EES and ETIAS in 2026

Two new systems now apply at the Schengen border, and neither of them is a visa. They sit alongside the visa rules rather than replacing them.

**The Entry/Exit System (EES) is**an automated border system that records non-EU travellers entering and leaving the Schengen area. It began a phased rollout on 12 October 2025 and, according to the European Commission, has been fully operational since 10 April 2026. It captures a facial image and fingerprints on first entry and replaces the manual stamping of passports with a digital record. Because biometric enrolment takes place at the border, travellers should allow extra time on their first crossing.

**ETIAS is**a travel authorisation that visa-exempt nationals will need from the last quarter of 2026 to enter France and the wider Schengen area. It is not a visa. The European Union has confirmed a fee of €20 (with exemptions for applicants under 18 or over 70), validity of up to three years or until the passport expires, and multiple entries within the same 90 days in 180 limit. Visa-exempt nationals, including British and American citizens, will need to hold a valid ETIAS before they board, while visa-required nationals continue to apply for a Schengen visa as before.

## Visa-free short stays and the 90/180-day rule

If your nationality is visa-exempt, you can stay in the Schengen area without a visa for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The 180-day window is a rolling one, counted backwards from each day you are present, which makes it easy to miscount without careful tracking.

A short stay covers tourism, business meetings, academic conferences, university entrance examinations and short courses lasting under three months. It does not allow salaried employment, and it does not allow you to follow a degree programme that runs beyond 90 days.

Because France is part of the Schengen area, time spent in other Schengen countries counts towards the same 90-day total. A fortnight in Spain and three weeks in Italy reduce the days you have left for France within the rolling window. Overstaying the limit can lead to fines, removal and a future entry ban, so the count should be treated as a hard ceiling rather than a guideline.

## When you need a Schengen short-stay visa (Type C)

If your nationality is on the visa-required list, you need a Schengen short-stay visa, known as a Type C visa, for any visit of 90 days or less. This applies to tourism, family visits and short business trips alike.

According to France-Visas, the standard fee is €90 for applicants over 12, €45 for children aged 6 to 12, and €35 where a visa facilitation agreement applies, with no charge for children under 6 or for family members of EU citizens. Applicants generally need travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000 for emergency treatment, hospitalisation and repatriation across the Schengen area. A Type C visa authorises a short visit only. It grants neither residence nor the right to work, and it cannot be converted into a study permit once you are in France.

## When you need a long-stay visa or residence permit (over 90 days)

Any stay of more than 90 days requires a long-stay visa, whatever your nationality outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland, including the nationalities that are visa-exempt for short trips. Permission to enter and permission to reside are two different things, and a long stay calls for the second.

**A long-stay visa is**a Type D visa issued for between three months and one year for a defined purpose, such as study, work or joining family. France issues it in two forms. The first is the long-stay visa that serves as a residence permit, the

visa de long séjour valant titre de séjour

(VLS-TS), which removes the need for a separate residence card during the first year but must be validated online shortly after arrival. The second is a long-stay visa that requires you to apply for a residence permit at your local prefecture within the first months of your stay. Students almost always fall under the first form.

## Do you need a visa to study in France?

You need a student visa to study in France if you are a non-European national on a course lasting more than 90 days. EU, EEA and Swiss students do not, whatever the length of their programme. France hosts a large international student population, with around 443,500 enrolled in 2024-2025 according to Campus France, and the rules below apply equally to public universities and to private institutions such as SKEMA.

### EU, EEA and Swiss students versus non-EU students

Students from the EU, the EEA and Switzerland enter France on a valid passport or national identity card and need neither a visa nor a residence permit. Non-European students enrolling on a course of more than 90 days need a long-stay student visa, obtained before they leave home. This holds true whether they join a [degree programme taught in France](https://www.skema.edu/en/programmes) at a public or a private institution.

### UK students after Brexit

British nationals are now third-country nationals for the purposes of French immigration. For a short course of under 90 days they remain visa-exempt, subject to EES registration and, from late 2026, to ETIAS. For a full degree, which by definition runs beyond 90 days, they have needed a long-stay student visa since 1 January 2021. UK applicants also complete the Campus France procedure before applying, a clear change from the pre-Brexit position that warrants early preparation. British citizens who were legally resident in France before 31 December 2020 fall under the EU Withdrawal Agreement instead.

### The student long-stay visa and the "Études en France" procedure

Non-European students apply for the long-stay visa that serves as a residence permit for students, the VLS-TS _**étudiant**_, which is issued for courses lasting 4 to 12 months. Several elements define the application:

*   **Proof of funds:**you must show access to at least 877,50€ and 10,530€ for a twelve-month year. Bank statements, a sponsor's guarantee, or a scholarship award letter are all accepted, and [a scholarship can count as accepted proof of funds](https://www.skema.edu/en/financial-support).
*   **Consular fee:**the long-stay student visa costs €50 for applicants going through the Campus France procedure and €99 otherwise, according to France-Visas, plus a handling fee capped at €40 where an external provider takes the appointment.
*   **The "Études en France" procedure:**Campus France runs a compulsory pre-consular process for students resident in one of 73 designated countries, including the UK, the US, India, China, Brazil and Morocco. Platform fees vary by country, for example £90 in the UK and $270 in the US. The certificate it produces is then required for the visa application.
*   **Validation after arrival:**once in France, you validate your VLS-TS online on the ANEF platform within three months of arriving. Since 1 May 2026 this validation costs €150, made up of a €100 reduced tax and a €50 stamp duty, payable on the platform. Missing the three-month deadline makes your stay irregular and suspends your right to re-enter the Schengen area.

Students admitted to a programme taught on a French campus fall within this regime. SKEMA provides [support for international students before and after they arrive](https://www.skema.edu/en/international-students) on its French campuses, and teaches courses such as the [Master in Management programme](https://www.skema.edu/en/programmes/grande-ecolemaster-management) there. The full application sequence, from the Campus France file through the France-Visas portal to the consular appointment, is set out on those official portals.

## Visa, exemption and residence permit: what is the difference?

These four terms are easy to confuse, and the distinctions decide what you can and cannot do.

*   **A short-stay visa**authorises a visit of up to 90 days. It does not allow residence or work.
*   **A long-stay visa**authorises a stay of more than 90 days for a defined purpose, and for students it also serves as the first-year residence permit once validated.
*   **A residence permit**is the document that authorises you to reside in France beyond your visa. It is issued in France and is not the same thing as a visa.
*   **A visa exemption**means you may enter without applying for a visa. It does not remove the conditions of entry, and from late 2026 visa-exempt nationals still need an ETIAS authorisation.

## Passport, documents and entry requirements at the French border

A valid travel document and supporting evidence can decide whether you are admitted, even when you do not need a visa. Border officers may ask any traveller to justify the purpose and conditions of their stay.

Your passport should have been issued within the last ten years, contain at least two blank pages, and remain valid for at least three months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen area. Depending on your situation you may also be asked for proof of accommodation, evidence of sufficient funds, a return or onward ticket, and travel medical insurance. Students should carry their enrolment certificate and, where relevant, their Campus France confirmation, together with proof of housing for their first months, which they can secure through SKEMA's guidance on [finding student accommodation in France](https://www.skema.edu/en/accommodation). Keeping certified copies alongside the originals avoids delays at the border.

## Do I need a visa for France? Examples by profile

The same nationality can lead to different requirements depending on why and how long you are coming.

*   A tourist staying under 90 days needs no visa if their nationality is visa-exempt, an ETIAS from late 2026, and a Schengen visa if their nationality is visa-required.
*   An international student staying several months needs a long-stay student visa, whatever their non-European nationality, obtained before departure, whether they study at the [Paris campus](https://www.skema.edu/en/campus/paris), the [Lille campus](https://www.skema.edu/en/campus/lille) or the [Sophia Antipolis campus](https://www.skema.edu/en/campus/sophia-antipolis).
*   A visitor staying with family or friends follows short-stay rules, often with a formal accommodation certificate from the host.
*   Someone moving to France long term needs a long-stay visa matched to their purpose, followed by a residence permit or by online validation of a VLS-TS.

## Official sources and a pre-travel checklist

Before departure, run through a short checklist:

*   Confirm your visa need on France-Visas for your exact nationality, purpose and duration.
*   Secure your visa or, if you are visa-exempt, your ETIAS authorisation once it is required.
*   Gather your supporting documents: passport, proof of funds, accommodation and insurance.
*   For a student stay, complete the Campus France procedure where it applies, then plan to validate your VLS-TS on the ANEF platform within three months and to pay the €105 student life contribution (CVEC).
*   Keep track of your days against the 90/180 limit if you travel on a visa-free basis.

If you are coming to France to study, take the steps in order: confirm your place, complete the visa procedure before you travel, then validate your status within three months of arriving. You can begin by [applying to a SKEMA programme in France](https://www.skema.edu/en/apply).

Visa requirements change by nationality and by date, so the official source is the authority on each point. France-Visas (france-visas.gouv.fr), including its "Check your visa need" tool, gives the visa requirement, the Schengen short-stay (Type C) fees and the document list. Service-Public.fr covers the residence rules and the VLS-TS. Campus France (campusfrance.org) runs the Études en France procedure and publishes the country platform fees. title: VOA专访：余茂春称美中峰会高规格背后是战略较量，展示美国实力与价值观
summary: 中国国家主席习近平为期三天的国事访问星期五(9月25日)划下句点，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统全程高规格接待，从亲自前往安德鲁斯联合基地接机，到白宫南草坪的欢迎仪式、东厅的国宴、红厅的茶叙，以及一同参观美国国家档案馆。 曾在特朗普总统第一任政府任职的哈德逊研究所中国中心主任余茂春教授在接受美国之音专访时表示，习近平此次访美高规格礼遇的背后其实是美中之间全方位的战略较量。 **特朗普向习近平展示美实力** 余茂春以1959年美国总统艾森豪威尔高规格接待前苏联领
content:
中国国家主席习近平为期三天的国事访问星期五(9月25日)划下句点，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统全程高规格接待，从亲自前往安德鲁斯联合基地接机，到白宫南草坪的欢迎仪式、东厅的国宴、红厅的茶叙，以及一同参观美国国家档案馆。

曾在特朗普总统第一任政府任职的哈德逊研究所中国中心主任余茂春教授在接受美国之音专访时表示，习近平此次访美高规格礼遇的背后其实是美中之间全方位的战略较量。

**特朗普向习近平展示美实力**

余茂春以1959年美国总统艾森豪威尔高规格接待前苏联领导人赫鲁晓夫为例说明，高规格的外交礼仪本身并不意味着美中关系取得实质性进展。在他看来，礼仪与实力展示恰恰可能反映出双方在缺乏实质突破的情况下，试图通过外交场面传递各自的战略讯息。

余茂春指出，今年5月习近平访问中国时，中方同样给予特朗普高规格接待，因此美方这次的安排在外交礼仪上具有对等性质。不过，他也以特朗普总统此前在阿拉斯加会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)时在F-22战机旁握手的安排作为对照，点出一个细节，特朗普总统选择在安德鲁斯联合基地以及白宫欢迎仪式中展示先进美军装备，包括战斗机与轰炸机在上空飞跃，是在向北京传递一个明确的讯息：那就是，美国可以高规格接待中共的领导人，但双方的实力对比仍然是美方需要突出强调的一环。

熟悉特朗普总统思维的余茂春认为，特朗普重视外交场合的视觉效果，希望在表达尊重的同时，让对方感受到美国的实力。

**四个“T”之外，贸易休战是核心**

此次美中峰会可能涉及的议题广泛。除了此前受到关注的贸易、台湾以及伊朗问题之外，人工智能和科技竞争也成为新的重要议题。

这些议题被概括为多个“T”，包括贸易(Trade)、台湾(Taiwan)、德黑兰/伊朗(Tehran)以及科技(Technology)。余茂春认为这些问题都涉及美中双方长期的战略利益，因此很难在一次元首会晤中彻底解决。

在他看来，这次美中峰会具体的成果反而是这四个T之外的另一个T--贸易休战，也就是“Truce”的延长。

余茂春强调，习近平希望美国延长贸易休战，而特朗普则更加关注中方此前承诺的落实情况，特别是稀土供应以及购买美国农产品等问题。他认为，美国方面持续关注这些承诺是否真正落实，而不仅仅是双方在峰会上作出口头表态。

**得AI者得天下**

至于人工智能议题，在特朗普总统日前提出：“得AI者得天下”的说法之后，成为美中科技竞争最激烈的战场。余茂春表示，随着特朗普提出“超级智能”(super intelligence)等概念，人工智能的安全与管控可能成为美中双方需要讨论的问题。

他认为，AI既可能给人类带来巨大益处，也可能产生重大安全风险，因此美中之间建立某种管控机制具有重要意义。但他同时指出，人工智能领域的竞争涉及技术、网络和国家安全利益，双方是否能够真正执行任何形式的协议，将是一个重要挑战。

**中国“明目张胆”支持伊朗**

特朗普总统星期五在和习近平一同参观国家档案馆时亲自向媒体证实，两人谈到了伊朗问题。余茂春认为，中国“明目张胆”支持俄罗斯与伊朗是美国长期关注的问题。他表示，美国近年来通过包括“二级制裁”在内的政策，对与俄罗斯、伊朗等国开展相关活动的国家施加压力，因此中国与这些国家的经贸关系可能成为美方关注的对象。

他认为，特朗普政府可能会继续要求北京在相关问题上作出更加具体的承诺，而美国最终是否采取进一步措施，则取决于北京的实际行动。

**军售时程不代表美对台政策改变**

美中元首峰会举行之际，美国在亚洲的盟友和伙伴如何看待华盛顿与北京的高层互动，也是外界关注的问题。

余茂春认为，每次美中元首峰会都可能让美国部分盟友产生疑虑，包括日本、韩国、菲律宾以及台湾。他指出，特朗普在联合国大会期间与日本、韩国领导人保持互动，可以被视为向盟友释放讯息，强调美中峰会并不意味着美国将削弱与盟友的关系。

在台湾问题上，余茂春认为，台湾可能仍然是美中关系中的重要议题，但不一定成为此次元首会谈的核心。

针对外界有关美国对台军售可能因美中峰会而延后的讨论，余茂春认为，军售时间安排本身并不必然代表美国对台政策发生重大改变。他表示，美国对台军售长期以来与两岸军事态势以及台湾自身的防务需求有关。

美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)在习近平访问前在纽约回应记者的相关提问时表示，140亿美元的对台军售依然在审议中，美国在出售武器时也必须权衡自身的需求。

余茂春表示，台湾近年来已经获得大量美国武器，但台湾自身的国防体系与美国军事体系之间仍需要进一步整合，因此武器采购的速度与规模也需要考虑实际吸收和运用能力。

**美中峰会向中国人民传递美国价值观**

除了贸易休战、人工智能、支持伊朗与台湾军售之外，余茂春也特别提到了人权议题。他她习近平这次访美引起了很多人的愤怒。全美国几乎各个层次、各个集团，都向白宫表示，希望向习近平传达一种抗议、不满的声音。国会里面也有，民间组织更多。所以，成千上万的人都对习近平表达了抗议的决心和愿望。特朗普总统也已经通过他的发言人表示，他会向习近平提出这些要求。这些东西形成了一种巨大的压力，当然是不可避免的。

至于特朗普总统如何通过美中峰会向中国人民直接传达信息。余茂春认为，美国领导人向中国人民传达美国的价值观，并不见得需要明确的政策表态。美国政府的行动很多，也可以通过政府自身的行为，对中国大陆形成巨大的影响。比如在对伊朗的战争中，中国老百姓当然对这件事情很关心，但对中国老百姓最有震撼力的，是美国军队动用了几千人、花费了几亿美元，去拯救两名受伤的美军飞行员。这件事情在中国老百姓当中被谈论得非常多，也体现了一个国家的价值观。比如，一个国家为了自己的人员不受到虐待，以及对军人的尊重，这些都是非常有震撼力的。

“像这些非常细微的影响，对中国的作用，我想一种是隐性的、间接的。另外，当然还有很多逐渐发展的软实力工具，包括像美国之音所做的工作就非常好。很多中国的听众、观众，也可以通过你们的渠道了解美国真正的走向以及美国领导人的政治表述。这些东西都是潜移默化的。要改变中国对美国的理解，我觉得需要美国和中国人民做出很多努力。”余茂春说。

**峰会成果：关键不在签署什么，而在落实多少**

对于如何衡量此次美中峰会最终成果，余茂春认为，不能仅仅根据峰会现场的气氛、国宴规格或者领导人发表的声明来判断。他强调，真正重要的是中方此前作出的承诺能否落实，美国政府也需要持续监督和核实相关承诺的执行情况。

余茂春认为，美中之间过去存在口头承诺与实际执行之间的落差，因此此次峰会之后，双方是否建立更加具体的落实和核查机制，将是观察峰会成效的重要指标。在他看来，峰会本身可能带来短期的外交稳定，但美中之间长期的战略竞争并不会因为一次高规格的元首会晤而消失。

**特朗普2.0的对华政策演进**

最后，余茂春也比较了特朗普总统第二任期与第一任期的对华政策，余茂春认为，两者之间存在相当程度的连续性。他认为，特朗普第一任期期间，美国对中国的战略定位发生了重大变化，而这一基本判断并没有因为拜登政府执政而根本改变。他认为，特朗普第二任期虽然在公开措辞上更多强调与中国保持沟通、避免冲突以及寻求“战略稳定”，但美国在科技、安全、产业政策和盟友体系等领域的政策仍然体现出对中国战略竞争的重视。

余茂春指出，特朗普第二任期的政策重点包括强化美国国内安全、重建工业基础、要求盟友增加国防投入，以及加强对先进技术的保护。他认为，这些政策虽然未必直接以“对抗中国”的形式出现，但与美中长期战略竞争存在密切联系。

title: Manila blames Chinese aggression for aborted South China Sea mission
summary: The Philippine Navy tank landing ship BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands, July 27, 2023. The ship was deliberately grounded on the shoal in 1999 and has since remained there as a forward outpost to support Manila
content:
The Philippine Navy tank landing ship BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands, July 27, 2023. The ship was deliberately grounded on the shoal in 1999 and has since remained there as a forward outpost to support Manila's territorial claim in the area.Armed Forces of the Philippines

[![Image 1: Reuters](https://media.assettype.com/bairdmaritime%2F2024-12-02%2F7e0yqzaz%2Freuters_logo_icon_170782.png?w=48&auto=format%2Ccompress)](https://www.bairdmaritime.com/author/reuters)

Published on:

25 Sep 2026, 10:12 am

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) accused China on Friday of obstructing a resupply mission to troops on board a grounded World War Two-era warship in the South China Sea, saying dangerous manoeuvres by Chinese vessels, "put Filipino personnel at risk," and prevented the mission from being completed.

"There was no collision, and no one was injured, but the dangerous manoeuvres of the China Coast Guard created a serious risk of collision," said Jay Tarriela, a PCG spokesperson on South China Sea issues.

The PCG said the China Coast Guard and the People's Liberation Army Navy, "obstructed a legitimate humanitarian and sustainment operation," to Second Thomas Shoal on Thursday.

It said China's actions were inconsistent with international law and a 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated Beijing's sweeping claims in the South China Sea.

The Philippines called on China to stop interfering with its lawful resupply missions.

The PCG said it would continue its lawful operations in the South China Sea and exercise Manila's sovereign rights and jurisdiction in the waterway.

The Chinese embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In 2024, Manila and Beijing reached a provisional arrangement on resupply missions to Second Thomas Shoal, which the Philippine foreign ministry has said helped prevent confrontations between the two sides.

In July, Manila accused the China Coast Guard of firing water cannon at government vessels near Scarborough Shoal and striking a Philippine navy staff member with a wooden baton during a separate encounter near Second Thomas Shoal.

_(Reporting by Nestor Corrales; Editing by David Stanway)_

content:
中国国家主席习近平此次对美国的国事访问可以说是继已故政治强人邓小平美国之行后，中国领导人访美历史上最为风光的一次。不过，有分析人士认为，此次元首峰会侧重排场与礼仪，尚未见到实质性的内容。

唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统不仅和第一夫人梅拉妮娅·特朗普(Melania Trump)一道于星期三(9月23日)傍晚罕见地亲自前往华盛顿郊外安德鲁斯联合基地接机，打破自1962年以来美方接待外国元首的惯例，让习近平和夫人彭丽媛在美国一落地就有宾至如归的感觉，还于星期四在白宫为习近平夫妇举行了包括21响礼炮在内的全套军礼欢迎仪式。

特朗普总统在欢迎仪式上表示，他和习近平已经建立了深厚的友谊，“这段友谊建立在相互尊重和两国人民的共同利益之上，”特朗普说。

习近平在致辞中也表示，他与特朗普彼此尊重，“已建立良好关系，保持经常性沟通。”习近平还宣布恢复熊猫外交，近期内将有一对中国大熊猫前往亚特兰大动物园落户。

盛大的欢迎仪式结束后，习近平与特朗普在白宫分别举行了大小范围的两轮会谈。但截至报道截稿前，白宫仍未发布有关峰会成果的声明或说明。中国官媒则报道了一些中国官方的反应，但是内容上除了重申北京的一贯立场外，并没有谈及任何重大的共识或成果。

美国智库德国马歇尔基金会印太计划执行主任葛来仪(Bonnie Glaser)在峰会结束后接受美国之音采访时表示，特朗普与习近平的此次峰会侧重于排场与礼仪，而不是实质性的内容。

“我认为具体成果包括：向亚特兰大动物园提供两只大熊猫，以及将釜山达成的贸易休战协议延长两个月，”葛来仪说。

葛来仪向美国之音表示，习近平星期三抵达华盛顿郊外的安德鲁斯联合基地时，特朗普总统十分罕见地亲自前往接机，“这是自1962年以来外国领导人未曾享有的礼遇。(习近平)被视为与特朗普地位平等的领导人”。

“中方将能够展示许多体现其领导人备受尊崇形象的画面，”葛来仪又说。

习近平在白宫的欢迎仪式上致辞时，特别谈到两国在二次大战期间并肩抗击法西斯侵略的历史，强调对于这段历史，中国和美国两国人民都不会忘记。

“中美关系希望在人民、未来在青年。在这里，我愿宣布，未来5年，中方将邀请10万名美国青少年来华交流学习，”习近平说。

不过曾经在中国留学和工作多年的前《时代周刊》(Time)驻北京记者、风险咨询公司“战略风险”(Strategy Risks)执行长石宇(Isaac Stone Fish)听完习近平的发言后在X平台上贴文说，他不建议美国青少年接受习近平的邀请，前往中国交流学习。

“与我当年在那里求学时相比，如今的中国管控更严，对外国人的接纳度也降低了。异见空间和言论自由的空间都已大幅缩减，”石宇说。

“对于身为同性恋或非白人的美国学生来说，情况更为糟糕。华裔美国人往往被期望‘更懂规矩’，而非洲裔美国人有时则会被视为二等公民，”石宇说。

石宇在大学时主修的是中国文学。他对如今无法建议年轻的美国人和他当年一样前往中国求学感到遗憾。

“一旦美中关系紧张局势加剧，这些学生实际上可能会沦为人质，”石宇指出。

美国国会中有些议员反对习近平访美，认为他作为一位独裁者，与他达成的交易完全都不可信。也有议员认为，由于美中关系很重要，因此特朗普邀请习近平来访无可厚非，但是可能不需给他如此高规格的待遇。

美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)本周在回应记者提问有关这些来自国会的批评声音时表示，美中两国拥有世界上最强大的两支军事力量，“美国必须这样做”。卢比奥说，“认为我们不应与他们进行最高层接触的想法是不负责任的。这简直荒谬。”

美国众议院中国问题特设委员会成员、南达科塔州共和党联邦众议员达斯蒂·约翰逊(Dusty Johnson)在接受美国有线电视新闻网(CNN)采访时表示，无论是哪一个政党的总统入主白宫，国会应该将如何从事外交的裁量权交给总统，因此他对特朗普在白宫接待习近平不持异议。

“如果总统做得不对，我会说出来。但是政治人物基本上应该让总统去从事外交，”约翰逊说。

不过他指出，习近平会说谎，而且善于操控人。因此特朗普与习近平打交道需要小心。

“我们必须确保，他不会操控本届政府达成不符合美国利益的交易，”约翰逊说。

德国马歇尔基金会的葛来仪指出，特朗普和习近平都寻求在美中双边关系中维持某种程度的稳定，“而此次峰会恰好实现了这一目标。”

“然而，与此同时，两位领导人也都在争取时间，以降低自身在面对对方时的脆弱性，并增强本国的实力，”葛来仪说。

title: Far-left leader pushing to lead Berlin says city has voted for change
summary: * Summary * Companies * Left wants to expropriate thousands of housing units from corporate landlords * Eralp drew support from young voters and thousands who had previously abstained * SPD and Greens want antisemitism allegations in local
content:
*   Summary
*   Companies

*   Left wants to expropriate thousands of housing units from corporate landlords
*   Eralp drew support from young voters and thousands who had previously abstained
*   SPD and Greens want antisemitism allegations in local party branches addressed first

BERLIN, Sept 21 (Reuters) - The far-left leader pushing to take over as mayor of Berlin promised on Monday to tackle unaffordable ​rents in the German capital, but faced early pressure to take action over accusations of antisemitism in parts of the local party.

Elif ‌Eralp led the Left Party to their best result in Berlin where they displaced Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative party in the mayor's office and look set to head a coalition governing the city for the first time.

The Misinformation Monitor newsletter rounds up international misinformation narratives, with a "Real or Fake?" quiz in every edition. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/misinformation-monitor/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Ffar-left-leader-pushing-lead-berlin-says-city-has-voted-change-2026-09-21%2F)

"Berlin has clearly voted in favour of a change in policy, for an affordable Berlin where everyone can live with dignity, regardless of income or background, and for ​the rent crisis to be tackled consistently at long last," she said on Monday.

## PLAN TARGETS CORPORATE LANDLORDS

Famously described by former mayor Klaus Wowereit as "poor ​but sexy", Berlin has become increasingly expensive and its once famously cheap rents are now a thing of the past.

Eralp has ⁠pledged to expropriate more than 200,000 housing units from corporate landlords in a campaign which saw the party, whose roots lie in the former East German communist ​party, make gains in central and western areas of the city as well as its traditional strongholds in the east.

"I still stand by that," she said on Monday, ​despite questions about how to finance a move the centre-left Social Democrats estimated would cost some €20 billion ($22.94 billion).

She said she aimed to reduce the influence of corporate landlords such as Deutsche Wohnen

and Vonovia

. Vonovia Chief Executive Luka Mucic said the group was ready to discuss solutions to Berlin's housing shortage but that "socialisation doesn't create any new housing".

Merz, who said the policy would ​have "devastating effects" on foreign investment if it were ever implemented, said he expected swift legislation to prevent expropriations.

## MAMDANI AN EXAMPLE

Item 1 of 3 Die Linke (the Left) party's top candidate for Berlin, Elif Eralp, reacts on the day of a press conference, after the state elections, in Berlin, Germany, September 21, 2026. REUTERS/Liesa Johannssen

**[1/3]**Die Linke (the Left) party's top candidate for Berlin, Elif Eralp, reacts on the day of a press conference, after the state elections, in Berlin, Germany, September 21, 2026. REUTERS/Liesa Johannssen [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/die-linke-the-left-party-leaders-react-after-state-elections-in-berlin/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMk9OTkFZWFhIVg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Compared by some to New York mayor Zohran ​Mamdani, whose campaign to make the city more affordable saw him win an unexpected victory last year, the 45-year-old Eralp is the child of left-wing Turkish parents who sought asylum ‌in Germany ⁠after a military coup in 1980.

Like Mamdani, her campaign focused heavily on personal campaigning and social media and she scored particularly strongly among the young, while winning support from thousands of Berliners who previously did not vote.

"As a woman, I'm reluctant to compare myself to a man. But naturally Mamdani's success was a big example for us," she said. "And we were very happy about it, because that election victory sent a very clear signal — not just to New York, but to the entire world."

Little ​known outside left-wing circles before the campaign, ​she now stands poised to lead ⁠the German capital at a time when the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has made increasing gains across the country and posted its best-ever result in liberal Berlin.

Potential coalition partners in the centre-left Social Democrats and the environmental Greens have indicated they ​are ready to talk about forming a government.

But both have demanded Eralp address the longstanding accusations over antisemitism that have ​been levelled against some ⁠local branches of the Berlin party, often in connection with criticism of Israel.

The issue has been extremely sensitive in Germany, which has seen a surge in antisemitic incidents since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by the militant group Hamas and the Israeli campaign that has laid waste to Gaza and killed tens of thousands.

Merz said the ⁠rise in antisemitism ​was a "disgrace for Germany" and pledged action to combat incidents in Berlin that he said had ​caused concern to European partners.

Eralp said it was her "absolute priority" to ensure that Jewish people in Berlin along with Muslims and all other groups "feel safe and can lead a good life here".

"It is absolutely ​clear to me that the glorification of violence and terrorism is completely unacceptable," Eralp told a news conference.

($1 = 0.8718 euros)

Additional reporting by Christian Kraemer; Editing by Andrew Heavens

*   Djibouti base may aid monitoring of rival militaries
*   Middle East tensions raise value of base's intelligence role

WASHINGTON, Sept 17 (Reuters) - China has made upgrades to its military base at Djibouti that should significantly enhance ‌its ability to monitor military activity across the Middle East and Africa, a report by a US think tank released on Thursday said.

Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank said commercial satellite imagery showed that China's military had installed ​new antennas, satellite communications equipment and other assets at its only formally acknowledged overseas military base.

Conflicts ​involving the Houthis, Iran, the US and Israel have brought substantial military activity ⁠into the region, increasing the potential value of intelligence collection from the base, the report said.

CSIS said ​two new communications compounds that had appeared at the base since mid-2024 likely form part of a broader ​intelligence and military command architecture and would strengthen communications between Chinese forces operating in the Middle East and Africa and military headquarters in China.

"The type and orientation of the base's new equipment is varied, enabling transmission and detection across a wide ​range of signals and frequencies," the report said.

The facilities would provide China with "a much more robust picture ​of the operating environment in the region," the report said.

China's Washington embassy did not immediately respond to a request for ‌comment on ⁠the report.

The report said the base in Djibouti opened in 2017 and serves as a key hub for Chinese naval operations in the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea. The facility sits near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, one of the world's most important choke points for maritime trade.

"The base's capabilities have continued ​to evolve over time to ​enable increasingly sophisticated operations, ⁠helping the PLAN establish a growing foothold in the region," the report said, referring to China's People's Liberation Army Navy.

It said the facilities would likely enable the ​Chinese military to monitor the activities of other militaries operating nearby, although it ​was not ⁠possible to determine whether they were actively intercepting communications.

The report said The United States, France, Italy and Japan all operate bases less than 10 miles (16 km) from China's.

It said China could potentially derive useful information even from encrypted ⁠military ​communications and "draw valuable insights into U.S. and other militaries' operations by ​observing the direction, origin, frequency, and pace of their signals."

It said the facility could support Chinese efforts to expand its footprint in ​Africa, where Beijing has steadily increased both economic and security engagement.

(This story has been refiled to fix the order of the words to 'People's Liberation Army Navy' in paragraph 9.)

title: Saudis and Houthis exchange strikes, Yemenis take to boats to flee as Middle East war spreads
summary: * Summary * Houthis release video of charred wreckage said to show Saudi warplane they shot down * Fleeing Yemeni refugees arrive in Africa across the Red Sea * Houthi leader calls for end of Saudi 'blockade and occupation' * Trump says he
content:
*   Summary

*   Houthis release video of charred wreckage said to show Saudi warplane they shot down
*   Fleeing Yemeni refugees arrive in Africa across the Red Sea
*   Houthi leader calls for end of Saudi 'blockade and occupation'
*   Trump says he hopes war will end soon, Iranians want a deal

DUBAI, Sept 17 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia ​and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis exchanged fresh strikes across their border on Thursday and Yemenis took to boats in the Red Sea to escape fighting, as the [spreading Middle ‌East war](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/how-yemens-houthis-went-small-mountain-militia-big-regional-threat-2026-09-17/) created new threats to global oil supplies.

Houthi-controlled television reported fresh Saudi air strikes on Thursday in Hajjah province close to the Saudi border near the Red Sea coast, and the vicinity of Taiz further inland to the south.

Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Ftrump-hopes-iran-war-nearing-end-houthi-saudi-fighting-escalates-2026-09-17%2F)

Report Ad![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

Saudi Arabia's civil defence said a Yemeni living in Saudi Arabia [had been killed](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/one-killed-saudi-arabia-intercepts-drone-launched-by-yemens-houthis-2026-09-17/) by debris from a drone intercepted over the western city of Taif, the first death Riyadh has announced in repeated Houthi attacks since ​fighting escalated last week. It has previously said more than 80 people were wounded.

In Djibouti on the African shore of the Red Sea, Wahida Omer, 50, reached land after ​fleeing on a small boat across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Yemen when her home village of Dhubab came under attack as the Houthis swept ⁠into the area. Her husband had been left behind and she had no idea if he was alive, dead or captured by the Houthis.

"The sea was frightening, difficult," she said in ​an interview filmed by the International Organization for Migration. Those on the boat were "crying the whole way, and we arrived still crying" with nothing to eat.

The IOM says more than 100,000 Yemenis have ​been displaced by the latest fighting, mostly within Yemen.

The Houthis, who have seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast since last week in a lightning advance, say the Saudi Air Force has conducted hundreds of airstrikes in recent days. They in turn have fired missiles and drones at targets across the border.

On Wednesday, the Houthis said they had shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. Video they released overnight showed fighters shouting "Allahu Akbar" in the charred ​wreckage of a crash site and holding up a piece of a military aircraft wing bearing Saudi insignia.

"We want the Saudis to cease their blockade and occupation of our country, and to ​stop their aggression against us. This is our demand!" Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi said in a televised speech, seated with a traditional dagger in his belt. Slogans on the wall behind him read: "Death to America, ‌death to ⁠Israel, a curse upon the Jews, victory for Islam."

## TRUMP HOPES WAR WILL END SOON

The spread of the Middle East war to Yemen and Saudi Arabia threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February.

[Global crude prices](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-prices-extend-losses-fears-middle-east-supply-disruptions-ease-2026-09-17/) eased slightly on Thursday but remain well above $100 a barrel after shooting to the highest levels since May. The cost of fuel for consumers has risen even more sharply, with the average retail price for diesel in the United States setting a new all-time record on Thursday just shy of $6.40 a gallon.

U.S. President ​Donald Trump has so far rebuffed pleas from ​the Saudis for military support fighting the ⁠Houthis, who agreed a ceasefire with the United States last year after Washington bombed the group for two months.

"Well, hopefully we are towards the end of the war," Trump told reporters on Wednesday. He said the Iranians "want to make a deal. We'll see how that works out."

No negotiations between ​the United States and Iran to end the war have been held since an interim agreement reached in June collapsed within weeks.

The U.S. ​Navy is trying to guide ⁠ships through the Strait of Hormuz, the outlet to the Gulf along Iran's coast, where a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas passed before the war, and is also imposing a blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran says the strait is closed and will remain shut until Washington lifts the blockade. It is seeking an agreement with neighbouring Gulf states that would let it collect fees from ships passing ⁠through the strait.

War ​in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia have jeopardised the main alternative route for Gulf oil, with the Houthis ​capturing the Red Sea coast and islands inside the Bab el-Mandeb, or "Gate of Tears", the strait at its mouth.

Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, which allowed it to pump oil across the Arabian Peninsula and ship it from the Red Sea, has ​been shut since it was struck last week in an attack Riyadh said came from Iraq, where Iran-backed militias also operate.

Reporting by Reuters bureaux Writing by Peter Graff Editing by Alexandra Hudson and Andrew Heavens

title: 部分火灾遇难者家属需支付数千美元费用以取回幸存财物

content: 受火灾影响的客户将被迫支付数千美元，否则他们的珍贵物品将被倾倒在三个月前墨尔本一处仓储设施遭受火灾破坏之后。 7 月 3 日，位于墨尔本东区 Scoresby 的 Koornang Road 的公共自助仓储（PSS）设施发生了一场大火——然而三个月过去了，争议仍在继续，一些客户抨击高昂的取回费用，因为该区域的一部分即将面临拆除命令。 然而，最近的无人机 footage 显示，火灾影响区的一些单元已经清理完毕。 PSS 管理层告诉 news.com.au，一些被火灾完全摧毁且高度污染的单元，其物品已被清理，客户已提前被告知这一举措。 PSS 设施有近 1000 个储物单元，客户 Holly Dr Vries 收到了令人心碎的照片，展示了火灾如何穿过她的单元。 里面存放着她的家庭用品、她 12 岁儿子的学校照片、他在幼儿园制作的工艺品以及她已故祖母的画作和中国餐具。 “然后我制作了一个装有所有医院文件和类似物品的婴儿箱，我打算把它给我的儿子，”她告诉 news.com.au。 “他的祖母几年前去世了，她死于肺癌，所以我有很多东西，她在他出生时给他的婴儿用品。” 这位 42 岁的妇女自 2025 年以来，在一段关系破裂和搬入小房子后，一直按月租赁该储物单元，费用约为 190 美元。 Holly Dr Vries lost almost everything in the fire. Picture: Supplied Photos sent to Ms Dr Vries showing the fire damage to her storage unit. Picture: Supplied 她最初在得知 7 月火灾后感到难过，但现在感到愤怒——在收到设施的照片后，她相信一些她的纪念品可能可以取回。 PSS 最初告诉她几乎什么都无法取回，然后寄回了一张圈出可见物品的照片。 “他们会让卫生专家进入我的单元，看看是否有任何东西可以取回……但是，据我……单元持有者所说，他们被收取了……千美元来清理他们的物品，只有微小的机会可以将其归还，”她说。 De Vries 女士说 PSS 告诉她，火灾造成了健康危害，因为可能暴露于烟雾、烟灰、化学品和阻燃剂。 “他们提到了化学品之类的东西，但是设施上方有无人机 footage，有人在火灾区被看到而没有佩戴适当的个人防护装备（PPE），”她补充道。 “所以，对我来说，如果他们这样做，危害性有多大？” PSS 管理层告诉 news.com.au，没有人在没有佩戴适合其工作区域的防护装备的情况下被允许进入现场。 “该场地是一个受控的工作现场，仅由授权承包商参加。专家为该场地的每个部分规定了所需的防护装备，总承包商负责确保遵循这些要求，”PSS 说。 “我们无法评论我们尚未看到的 footage。污染是不可见的：一个人穿过一个区域并不能说明那里存储的物品上有什么；只有检查和测试才能说明。” Photos sent by PSS to impacted storage unit customers. Picture: Supplied 包括 De Vries 女士单元在内的该区域拆除计划于 10 月 1 日完成，但 PSS 管理层告诉 news.com.au，已向议会申请延期。 De Vries 女士必须在 9 月 29 日之前决定是否让一家公司检查她的物品，并且必须签署一份赔偿协议，但她对这份法律文件感到不舒服。 “我为了可能只是拿回几件东西，就要放弃我所有的权利，”她说。 与此同时，另一位 PSS 客户 Mark Bugeja 的储物单元没有被火灾摧毁——但如果他想看到价值约 50,000 美元的模型套件收藏品，他将面临一笔可能巨大的账单，这是他花了 50 年积累的。 这位计算机程序员在 5 月存储了大约 5000 件物品，就在火灾爆发前两个月。 Mark Bugeja is facing potentially a huge bill if he ever wants his collection of model kits, worth around $50,000, back. Picture: Supplied 根据 PSS，包括 Mr Bugeja 在内的 36 个单元需要付费进行修复和清理工作，如果客户想取回他们的物品——或者他们可以免费被摧毁。 这是基于该公司获得的一份卫生专家报告，尽管 Mr Bugeja 要求，PSS 拒绝发布，PSS 管理层表示它是一份“包含有关其他客户单元信息的整个隔间文件，我们无论如何都无法披露”。 他最初得到的报价在 6000 美元到 8800 美元之间，用于修复物品。 后来改为初步报价 3300 美元，仅将他的物品从储物柜中取出并检查，不知道会产生什么进一步的费用。 在 news.com.au 看到的信中，Mr Bugeja 被告知，基于大量物品，还将收取 2500 美元的修复后验证费用，其中包括卫生专家重新测试的样品。 “但这一切的 kicker 是，如果我同意，我就必须签署一份豁免书，其中包括一份赔偿协议，这基本上会将任何风险或责任从 PSS 身上移开，”他说。 Pictures showing the contents of Mark Bugeja’s storage unit. Picture: Supplied 他的律师建议他不要签署赔偿协议，因为它可能会阻止未来对公司的任何行动，放弃他作为消费者的权利，并将责任重新放在他身上，他说。 “如果我同意支付费用并清理我的物品，但不同意免除他们或赔偿他们任何责任或风险，从现在和未来，那么我无论如何都拿不回我的物品，”他说。 He is concerned the saga is dragging out and potentially causing more damage to goods. Picture: Supplied The letters Mark Bugeja received about costs to regain his goods. Picture: Supplied PSS 管理层告诉 news.com.au，这 36 个客户的物品修复具有最高级别的污染，这是专业工作。 “费用取决于客户选择修复什么以及损坏的程度，”PSS 说。 “修复物品的费用仅在实际保存物品的范围内支付，验证费用是提前披露的固定金额。声称 2500 美元的验证费用是错误的和虚假的：任何文件都没有出现这样的数字，无论是我们的还是修复公司的。公共自助仓储不收取其中任何部分。” Consumer Action Law Centre CEO Stephanie Tonkin. Picture: Kylie Else Mark Bugeja wants to get his own cleaning quote. Picture: Supplied The photo one customer received of her unit. Picture: Supplied Chrystal Jelena had packed her whole life in the storage facility. Picture: Supplied Chrystal Jelena had goods to start her spice business in the facility. Picture: Supplied Chrystal Jelena used a unit due to being made homeless in May and believes there would have been no option to insure her goods. Picture: Supplied PSS 管理层补充说，无法保存或客户选择处置的物品，由授权承包商移除，并通过许可设施作为受火灾影响的废物进行处置。 “污染正是这些物品不能归还或作为普通垃圾扔掉的原因，”它补充道。 Consumer Action Law Centre 首席执行官 Stephanie Tonkin 说，该组织交谈过的客户经历了一段可怕的时间。 “我们希望 PSS 能为他们提供切实可行的解决方案，”她说。 目前，De Vries 女士“非常担心”她的物品将被 PSS 倾倒，她将再也见不到它们。 “我对 Public Self Storage 的反应，我想，是，如果我不必将其密封在塑料中直到生命的其余部分，我仍然希望拿回它们，”她补充道。 PSS 管理层表示，它真诚地为火灾对客户造成的影响感到抱歉，并表示该公司自第一天起就努力工作，确保没有人受到比情况不可避免的影响更大的伤害。 “公共自助仓储不为客户的物品提供保险。物品由客户自行承担风险，保险是客户的责任，每个客户在注册时都承认这一点，这是澳大利亚自助仓储的基础，”PSS 说。 “我们所做的是全额退还每个客户的预付费用，自 7 月 3 日起暂停所有费用，免费提供每个中心区单元的 photographic record，建立了一个无需选择即可修复路径，并为任何客户在其保险公司要求时提供一封信。” 7 月，维多利亚州警察说，一名 33 岁的人因鲁莽行为危及严重火灾而被起诉，但当 news.com.au 联系时，拒绝进一步评论。 Knox City Council 下令进行整改工程，以防止该场地进一步坍塌，本月将安排更多检查。 Knox City Council 发言人表示，已听到许多受困扰和担忧的单元持有者的消息，并理解这种情况造成的不确定性。 “建筑业主完全负责管理租户的用品，议会正将相关调查转交给业主，”他们说。 “议会的角色是确保建筑物适合居住。我们已经下令业主进行使建筑安全的工作，并提供一份火灾后环境评估报告，证明建筑物可以安全重新占用。” Consumer Affairs Victoria 发言人表示，他们不评论个别企业或调查，但在可能的情况下协助受影响的消费者。 “所有企业，包括那些在自助仓储行业的企业，必须确保其合同符合澳大利亚消费者法，”他们说。 “Consumer Affairs Victoria 认真对待不当行为的报告，并将进行调查并在必要时采取进一步行动。”

content: Lani Pallister 本周在悉尼赢得了四枚金牌和一枚银牌。（供稿：游泳澳大利亚/Delly Carr） Lani Pallister 有什么做不到的吗？ 周五晚上，Pallister 以 800 米自由泳的第四枚金牌结束了澳大利亚短池锦标赛，并成功锁定了参加世界锦标赛的 24 人阵容席位。 随后，这位 24 岁的运动员在周六清晨从凌晨 4 点醒来后，前往昆士兰州阳光海岸，在亚历山大头兰的 1.2 公里布洛夫至巴海洋游泳赛中夺得了荣誉。 “我会产生非常强烈的错失恐惧症（FOMO），”Pallister 在接受采访时被问及为何要踏上旅程时说道。 “回馈很重要……亚历山大头兰冲浪俱乐部帮助我成为了今天的运动员。” Lani Pallister 赢得了她连续第三次的布洛夫至巴游泳赛。（供稿：亚历山大头兰救生俱乐部） Pallister 对冲浪俱乐部的奉献精神不容置疑，她在 Instagram 上发布了一条故事，标记时间为凌晨 4 点 38 分，以便参加上午 11 点 20 分的阳光海岸比赛。 巴黎奥运冠军确保这次早起是值得的，她从始至终带领着实力强劲的选手群，赢得了该赛事的连续第三次胜利。 参加点对点海洋游泳比赛与过去四天在悉尼奥林匹克公园水上中心完成的 125 个转身相比，截然不同。 Pallister 参加了从 100 米到 1500 米的所有自由泳项目，除了 100 米外赢得了所有金牌，她在 100 米比赛中获得第二名。 这确保了她将作为北京世界锦标赛（12 月 1 日至 6 日）海豚队的首席选手。 该阵容包括六名新秀：Amelie Smith、Mark Nikolaev、Marcus Da Silva、Emily Jones、Cameron Bladen 和 Alex Quach。 Lani Pallister（左）和 Jenna Forrester 都获得了出色的锦标赛成绩。（供稿：游泳澳大利亚/Delly Carr） 海豚队主教练 Rohan Taylor 指出，Pallister 在悉尼的表现尤为突出，Sam Short 在 400 米、800 米和 1500 米自由泳项目上的全胜，以及 Jenna Forrester 的四枚银牌和一枚金牌也值得提及。 “那三个人毫无疑问是这里的亮点，”Taylor 说道。 “但也很高兴看到像 Amelie Smith 和 Marcus Da Silva 这样的选手脱颖而出并带来改变。 “也要为 Mark Nikolaev 点赞；他凭借一致性和毅力赢得了今晚的 Dolphin 号码，这本身就是值得称道的。 “北京的国际曝光是一个机会，让我们聚在一起，为洛杉矶 2028 做准备，这次比赛也为我们的年轻游泳者提供了向资深海豚选手学习的机会。” Lani Pallister 赢得了澳大利亚短池锦标赛的 200 米、400 米、800 米和 1500 米自由泳项目。（供稿：游泳澳大利亚/Delly Carr） 说到经验丰富的海豚选手，Cam McEvoy 也将加入北京的中国队，尽管他本周没有参加全国锦标赛。 世界泳联为在世界杯系列赛个人决赛中获得领奖台位置的任何游泳者提供世界锦标赛的 wildcard 名额。 这位 32 岁的长池世界纪录保持者随后在周五于阿塞拜疆巴库举行的 2026 年世界杯系列赛开幕夜上，以 50 米自由泳 20.22 秒的成绩打破了新的全国短池纪录，赢得了金牌。 Pallister 将前往美国 Flagstaff 参加海拔训练营，随后参加世界锦标赛，这代表她第九次入选澳大利亚海豚队。 “几周后要去海拔训练，然后基本上恢复全训练，全力以赴，目标是世界锦标赛，”Pallister 在短池锦标赛期间说道。 “我并没有预料到本周会有这么快游。我对 200 米加上 0.2 的成绩感到相当惊讶，所以我很高兴。” 海豚队世界锦标赛阵容 Iona Anderson, Ben Armbruster, Cameron Bladen*, Brittany Castelluzzo, Josh Collett, Isaac Cooper, Marcus Da Silva*, Jenna Forrester, Max Giuliani, Emily Jones*, Tara Kinder, Mark Nikolaev*, Lani Pallister, Alexandria Perkins, William Petric, Alex Quach*, David Schlicht, Sam Short, Amelie Smith*, Flynn Southam, Stuart Swinburn, Matt Temple, Olivia Wunsch, Josh Yong. *首次入选海豚队

title: 美共和党议员：美中应避免脱钩，台湾政策应维持现在路线
summary: 资料照片：共和党联邦参议员史蒂夫·戴恩斯在华盛顿举行的2026年基础设施峰会上发表讲话。(2026年3月11日) 华盛顿 — 美国共和党联邦参议员史蒂夫·戴恩斯(Steve Daines)表示，美国不应寻求与中国全面脱钩，而应在保持接触的同时降低风险。他强调，美国需要保持经济和军事力量，并通过外交沟通避免美中关系进一步升级。在台湾议题上，戴恩斯主张“保持现有路线”。 来自蒙大拿州的共和党联邦参议员戴恩斯星期四(10月1日)在尼克松基金会举行的“大国战略峰会”上谈到上星期举行的
content: 资料照片：共和党联邦参议员史蒂夫·戴恩斯在华盛顿举行的2026年基础设施峰会上发表讲话。(2026年3月11日) 华盛顿 — 美国共和党联邦参议员史蒂夫·戴恩斯(Steve Daines)表示，美国不应寻求与中国全面脱钩，而应在保持接触的同时降低风险。他强调，美国需要保持经济和军事力量，并通过外交沟通避免美中关系进一步升级。在台湾议题上，戴恩斯主张“保持现有路线”。 来自蒙大拿州的共和党联邦参议员戴恩斯星期四(10月1日)在尼克松基金会举行的“大国战略峰会”上谈到上星期举行的美中领导人峰会时说，这次会晤的主要意义在于稳定和缓和两国关系，而不是立即解决所有具体问题。 “就(峰会)结果而言，我认为，中国方面应该松了一大口气，因为此次访问期间没有发生任何不愉快的事，总统对习近平表现出了极大的礼遇和尊重，”戴恩斯说。 他指出，在中国文化中，“面子”是一个非常重要的问题，而习近平在此次访问中得到了尊重。 “我认为，这72小时的整个过程更多是一种礼仪性和仪式性的安排，实质性的内容相对少一些。不过，说实话，我本来也没有期待这次访问能取得太多实质性成果。我们只是想确保，在关税和言辞等方面，这种关系能够继续降温、缓和，而目前看来，我们处在一个更好的状态。” 谈到乌克兰和伊朗等议题，戴恩斯表示，美中双方曾进行“相当激烈的讨论”，但这些讨论主要是在闭门场合进行，公开场合的讨论相对较少。 针对外界认为美国政府对北京的立场不够强硬的批评，戴恩斯说，无论是在商业环境还是外交场合，根据他与中方打交道的经验，如果目标是推动问题取得实际结果，“坦诚而激烈的对话、艰难的对话”最好在闭门场合进行。 “相信我，双方私下正在进行一些非常强硬的对话。但总的来说，如果把这些强硬立场变成公开的言辞，通常只会把中方推向错误的方向，”戴恩斯说。 现年64岁的戴恩斯近年来被视为华盛顿与北京之间一个重要的非正式沟通渠道。在华盛顿的美中峰会之前，戴恩斯参议员今年8月底访问了广州和浙江等地，并参访当地科技企业。今年5月，在美国总统特朗普访问北京前夕，戴恩斯还率领一个跨党派国会议员代表团访问上海和北京。 戴恩斯也是上周唯一出席特朗普总统与中国国家主席习近平白宫晚宴的美国参议员。 戴恩斯在星期四的会上表示，美国不应寻求与中国全面脱钩，而应在保持接触的同时降低风险。 “我认为贝森特部长的说法非常准确，我们不能与中国脱钩，但我们需要去风险，” 戴恩斯说，“当然，我们可以进一步分析，从战术和战略层面来看，这究竟意味着什么，但我认为，我们首先应该确立这样一个基本前提：我们必须继续与中国保持接触。” 戴恩斯说，美中关系能否保持稳定，一方面取决于美国自身的经济和军事力量，另一方面也取决于双方是否保持沟通。他特别强调了两国最高领导人之间保持直接沟通的重要性。 “这些外交沟通渠道至关重要。我认为，美中关系中一个没有得到充分关注的事实是，特朗普总统和习近平主席保持着频繁沟通，两人会通过电话交谈，” 戴恩斯说。 戴恩斯于2015年进入美国参议院，此前曾于2013年至2015年担任众议员。他也是美国国会少数具有在中国长期工作和生活经历的议员之一。1991年至1997年任职于宝洁公司(P&G)期间，他曾被派驻广州和香港，参与公司在中国的业务拓展，并协助建立生产设施。 戴恩斯在会上谈到自己的中国经历时说，他从1991年开始接触中国，后来与家人搬到广州，在中国生活和工作多年。他表示，过去几十年亲眼见证了中国经济和科技领域的巨大变化，这也是他认为美国政策制定者需要不断了解中国的原因。 戴恩斯说，中国变化迅速，美国官员需要通过实地访问不断更新对中国的认识。他回忆说，自己曾对前国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥(Mike Pompeo)表示：“唯一比从未去过中国的参议员更危险的，是五年前去过中国的参议员。” 在台湾问题上，戴恩斯强调美国应当“保持现有路线”，并维持对台政策的一致性。他认为，美国政策出现摇摆可能增加误判和冲突风险。 “简单来说，答案就是，不要改变路线，在台湾问题上保持坚定。如果中方察觉到我们开始有些腿软、立场出现动摇，那将极有可能迅速引发他们产生采取军事行动的可怕念头，”戴恩斯说。 特朗普与习近平上星期举行的峰会结束后，中美双方发布的会谈成果均没有提及台湾。特朗普星期六也表示，他与习近平并没有花太多时间讨论台湾问题。此前，外界曾关注习近平是否会在峰会上要求美国在台湾问题上作出更多让步。路透社在峰会前曾报道，有消息人士称，中方可能要求特朗普依据1982年中美《八一七公报》停止对台军售。 不过，戴恩斯表示，他对台湾海峡未来短期和中期局势持相对乐观的看法。 “事实上，我对台湾问题的看法相对更加乐观一些，”戴恩斯说，“至少就我个人的判断而言，我认为，至少在短期和中期内，中国不太愿意冒险对台湾采取可能造成动荡的某种行动。他们已经看到了俄罗斯在乌克兰的遭遇。”

title: 俄罗斯袭击导致基辅桥梁关闭，首都交通瘫痪

content:
基辅市政府说，俄罗斯星期五(10月2日)的袭击迫使乌克兰首都第聂伯罗河上的三座桥梁关闭或部分关闭，造成严重的交通拥堵，一些居民不得不涉水过河。

基辅市军事管理局在电报(Telegram)平台上说，基辅公路和地铁共用的南桥(Southern Bridge)星期四多次遇袭，夜间又被袭击，这座桥梁双向封闭。

市长维塔利·克利奇科(Vitali Klitschko)说，地铁桥(Metro Bridge)的通行仅限于一条车道，帕顿桥(Paton Bridge)单向封闭。几条巴士和无轨电车线路都被改道。据乌克兰媒体报道，交通在中午前后恢复。

官员们说，在乌克兰首都的其它地方，无人机夜袭导致一栋公寓楼高层起火，造成一人死亡，两人受伤。

哈尔科夫市市长伊戈尔·捷列霍夫(Ihor Terekhov)在电报上说，制导炸弹星期五袭击了哈尔科夫的居民区，造成一人死亡，九人受伤，包括儿童。

俄罗斯国防部说，俄军无人机袭击了基辅的一座桥梁、周边地区的一座发电站、伊兹梅尔港和一艘货船，所有这些目标都用于军事目的。俄国防部说，防空部队夜间击落646架乌克兰无人机。

在外交方面，乌克兰外交部长安德烈·西比哈(Andrii Sybiha)说，乌克兰已收到来自印度、土耳其、埃及和美国的四项停火建议。

他在基辅对记者说，“我们愿意在能源领域和黑海地区实现停火，但必须是这两个方面都停火。” 他说，印度的提议范围最广，华盛顿的提议只涵盖能源领域。他说，基辅方面仍然愿意在前线实现无条件停火。莫斯科拒绝了临时停火协议，称必须首先达成全面解决方案。

西比哈还说，乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基(Volodymyr Zelenskyy)9月22日在纽约会晤美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)时讨论了美方的建议。

泽连斯基在会谈后说，如果俄罗斯停止袭击，基辅愿意接受“任何形式的”能源停火，他还说，没有要乌克兰单方面停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂的要求。

美国总统特朗普9月26日说，他希望乌克兰领导人能够与普京达成协议。

特朗普说，“我希望他能与普京达成和解，我也希望普京能与他达成和解。”

普京星期四在莫斯科举行的瓦尔代(Valdai)论坛上讲话时，排除了俄罗斯停止在黑海地区发动袭击的可能性，同时承认乌克兰对俄罗斯炼油厂的袭击给俄罗斯造成了经济损失。

乌克兰外长还说，乌克兰冬季期间至少需要300枚“爱国者”(Patriot)拦截导弹，并称俄罗斯储备了600枚弹道导弹，每月生产120至140枚。

欧盟委员会星期五说，在基辅达到改革基准后，已向乌克兰拨付了33亿美元，这是欧盟向乌克兰支付的最新款项。

欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩(Ursula von der Leyen)说，这笔资金将有助于在乌克兰进行自卫的同时维护金融稳定。乌克兰总理谢尔盖·科列茨基(Sergii Koretskyi)星期三说，今年的战争成本将达到约1550亿美元，政府仍在努力填补270亿美元的资金缺口，以维持作战行动的资金到2027年初。

title: 军情五处点名之后，英国学者还能说“不知道”吗？
source: 新闻汇总 - 茉莉花新闻网
summary: 茉莉花深度报道 文 / 魏臻 国际事务撰稿人 英国军情五处9月30日第一次独立公开发布间谍活动警报，点名中国通用技术研究院替中国国家安全部资助学术研究，100多名与英国有联系的学者参与过它资助的项目。从这一天起，还和这家机构合作的英国学者再也不能说自己不知道它和国家安全部的关系；按《2023年国家安全法》第3条，理应知道也可能构成犯罪。 9月30日，英国军情五处发布了一份“间谍活动警报”，点名中国通用技术研究院。警报说，这家机构与中国国家安全部有“非常密切的联系”，它的主要目
content: 茉莉花深度报道 文 / 魏臻 国际事务撰稿人 英国军情五处9月30日第一次独立公开发布间谍活动警报，点名中国通用技术研究院替中国国家安全部资助学术研究，100多名与英国有联系的学者参与过它资助的项目。从这一天起，还和这家机构合作的英国学者再也不能说自己不知道它和国家安全部的关系；按《2023年国家安全法》第3条，理应知道也可能构成犯罪。 9月30日，英国军情五处发布了一份“间谍活动警报”，点名中国通用技术研究院。警报说，这家机构与中国国家安全部有“非常密切的联系”，它的主要目的是资助能直接提升国家安全部间谍技术能力的学术研究；100多名与英国有联系的学者参与过国家安全部通过它资助的项目，涉及人工智能、网络安全、隐蔽通信和隐写术，其中一些人可能并不知道这家机构在项目中的角色。这是军情五处第一次独立公开发布警报。这份警报对还在和这家机构合作的英国学者意味着什么？ 答案是：从警报公开那一天起，他们再也不能说自己不知道这家机构和国家安全部的关系。军情五处在警报里专门提醒大学和研究人员注意英国《2023年国家安全法》第3条。按这一条，一个人的行为可能实质性地协助外国情报机构开展与英国有关的活动，而他知道、或者根据他所知的其他情况理应知道这一点，就构成犯罪，最高可判14年。BBC中文网指出，这意味着没有立即采取行动的英国学者，最终可能触犯法律。 一家关系被刻意模糊的出资方 军情五处说，许多学术机构和个人是“出于善意”与这家机构合作的，因为它和国家安全部的联系被刻意弄得模糊不清。中国通用技术研究院和中国国家自然科学基金委员会从2015年起共同设立联合基金，这个联合基金2026年仍在发布项目指南；基金说明称，它要重点解决中国通用技术研究院“在服务国家、履行职能中的”重大科学问题和关键技术问题。 英国《每日电讯报》查明，剑桥大学生物物理学教授米凯莱·文德鲁斯科洛（Michele Vendruscolo）参与的一项2024年发表的研究，得到过这个联合基金的资助；文德鲁斯科洛对该报说，他本人和剑桥大学都没有拿到这笔钱，那项研究也不涉及情报、安全、人工智能、网络安全或隐蔽通信。这类资助可以经由国家自然科学基金的联合基金发出。军情五处建议学者和中国机构合作时查清最终的资金来源，并“强烈建议”各校立即审查与这家机构正在进行或计划中的合作。负责安全事务的大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）说，他已写信给各大学负责人，要求终止与这家机构的关系。 中国驻英国使馆发言人说，英国情报部门的指责“纯属捕风捉影、无中生有”，并敦促英国情报部门停止散布谣言、破坏中英教育交流和科研合作。 不必再证明中国是“敌人” 《2023年国家安全法》第1至第3部分在2023年12月20日生效。第3条规定，可能构成协助的行为，包括直接或间接提供信息、物品、服务或经济利益。警报还提醒大学注意第17条规定的从外国情报机构获取物质利益罪。这部法已有涉华的判例：在英国替中国监视香港民主派人士的Chi Leung Wai和Chung Biu Yuen，被裁定犯有协助外国情报机构罪，2026年6月被判入狱。 旧法下的一起涉华间谍案没能审下去。2023年3月被捕的克里斯托弗·卡什（Christopher Cash）和克里斯托弗·贝里（Christopher Berry），2024年4月被控违反《1911年官方保密法》，罪名是收集或传递可能对“敌人”有用的信息；2025年9月15日，皇家检控署撤销了指控。检察长帕金森（Stephen Parkinson）说，政府补充提供的证人陈述，没有一份说明中国在案发时对英国国家安全构成威胁。取代旧法的《2023年国家安全法》不再要求证明当事人是在替“敌人”国家工作。两件事都关系到英国人有没有为中国情报机构提供帮助，不同的是，那起案子要先证明中国是敌人，政府拿不出这样的证词；这次警报援引的第3条不问对方是不是敌人，问的是当事人知不知道、该不该知道自己的行为可能协助外国情报机构。 美国起诉个人，荷兰筛查所有人 美国司法部2018年11月1日启动“中国行动计划”。哈佛大学化学教授查尔斯·利伯2021年12月被裁定六项重罪成立，其中两项是就他与武汉理工大学和中国“千人计划”的关系作虚假陈述。据《麻省理工科技评论》2021年12月的统计，在这个计划下被起诉的个人和机构只有约四分之一被定罪；2022年2月23日，美国司法部宣布终止这个计划，主要原因是它被指对华裔进行种族定性。荷兰走的是另一条路：2025年4月公布的《知识安全筛查法》草案，要求接触人工智能、量子、芯片等敏感知识的研究人员和硕士生事先接受政府筛查，预计每年约8000人，荷兰人也在其中；2026年6月，教育部长莱切特致函议会说，大范围筛查不可行，暂不实施。 英国这次两样都没有做。和美国相比，它不必先证明哪一个学者隐瞒了什么；和荷兰相比，它不必去审查每一个研究人员。它点名一家出钱的机构，把查清资金来源的责任交给各校和学者本人。此前的警报，军情五处发给的是议会：2022年1月，它发出干预警报，指李贞驹为中共中央统战部从事政治干预活动，由下议院议长转发给议员，调查权力法庭2024年驳回了她对军情五处的全部诉讼请求；2025年11月，它又向议员发出警报，点名领英上替国家安全部活动的两名猎头。军情五处总监肯·麦卡勒姆在年度威胁评估讲话中说，在秘密技术转移方面，军情五处正在应对接连不断的引诱英国学术专家的企图。 大学的钱和政府自己的名单 从几项统计看，中国仍是英国大学最大的生源国之一，在读人数减少，申请人数增加。英国高等教育统计局的数据显示，2024/25学年在英国高校就读的中国大陆学生有143,200名，比上一学年少约4%，入学新生连续第二年减少；英国大学招生服务中心的数据显示，截至2026年1月，来自中国的本科申请人增加约10%，到34,380人；英国内政部的数据显示，截至2026年6月的一年里，中国公民仍是获批英国学生签证（主申请人）最多的国籍，共86,368份。2024-25年度，国际学生的学费收入占英国高校总收入的23%；英国学生事务办公室说，这一年超过三分之一（35.8%）的英格兰高校出现赤字，预计2025-26年度升到42.7%。情报公司Strider的一份报告说，2020年以来超过5,000名英国研究人员与解放军关联机构合著了超过8,000篇论文。英国大学联合会说，它正在研究这份警报，帮助各校评估对现有和未来合作的影响。 2006/07至2024/25学年进入英国高校的国际新生人数，按来源地：中国新生连续第二年减少 政府自己的做法和警报并不一致。贾维斯此前在下议院说，中国等国家正试图影响英国大学的独立研究；可是2025年生效的外国影响登记计划，加强级至今只列了俄罗斯和伊朗，中国不在其中。德国之声报道，英国政府还批准了中国在伦敦建设其在欧洲最大使馆的计划。在政府的名单上，中国还没有和俄罗斯、伊朗放在同一档；防范中国通用技术研究院，眼下靠的是一份警报和各校自查。 如果警报之后仍有学者继续与这家机构合作，检方却以无法证明当事人理应知道为由不起诉，就说明警报没能让学者失去“不知道”这个理由，本文的判断就错了。接下来有三件事要看。第一，如果英国政府把中国列入外国影响登记计划的加强级，就说明政府在法规上也把中国放到了和俄罗斯、伊朗同一档；如果加强级仍然只有俄罗斯和伊朗，就说明防范中国仍主要靠情报机关的警报和学者自查。第二，如果有学者因警报后继续与这家机构合作而依第3条被起诉，就说明这份警报就是起诉前的告知；如果一直没有人被起诉，就说明警报的作用主要是让各校自己切断合作。第三，如果有英国大学公开宣布终止或审查与这家机构的关系，就说明大学接受了查清资金来源是自己的责任；如果各校都不公开表态，就无法知道警报落实了多少。 军情五处的这份警报，改变的是每一位还在和这家机构合作的英国学者的处境：从9月30日起，他们再也不能说自己不知道这家机构和国家安全部的关系；按第3条，理应知道也可能构成犯罪，最高可判14年。 茉莉花深度报道独立调研、撰写。 参考报道：ICEF Monitor（数据来自英国高等教育统计局）（5月20日） · The Guardian（摄影：Peter Nicholls/Reuters）（9月30日） · The Guardian（摄影：Leon Neal/PA）（9月30日） · BBC中文网（9月30日） · 德国之声中文网（10月1日）

title: In the Online Age, PRC Foreign Intelligence Evolves
summary: Executive Summary: Chinese intelligence efforts are increasingly moving away from human intelligence (HUMINT) collection to digital operations launched from within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The Ministry of State Security (MSS),
content: Executive Summary: Chinese intelligence efforts are increasingly moving away from human intelligence (HUMINT) collection to digital operations launched from within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The Ministry of State Security (MSS), military intelligence, and others have started to employ online recruiting to replace face-to-face contact for foreign assets. Beijing likely adopted the new model in response to the 2018 arrest of Xu Yanjun—the first MSS officer to be tried and convicted in the United States—which highlighted counterintelligence risks facing officers operating outside PRC borders. The MSS is using LinkedIn en masse to recruit and develop assets overseas. These operations frequently involve headhunter-style approaches and commercial pretexts to collect resumes and gather intelligence. Traditional HUMINT remains an important component of MSS tradecraft. MSS agents have started to integrate face-to-face contact in the PRC for managing their overseas contacts while their assets abroad deploy digital tools to facilitate operations. Beijing’s intelligence services are increasingly using massive, scattershot methods amenable to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to recruit foreign sources without sending their own officers abroad. They rely largely but not exclusively on online platforms, commercial consulting arrangements, and third-country intermediaries to identify, assess, and recruit targets, all while reducing the risk of counterintelligence detection. Meanwhile, People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence officers and agents continue to employ traditional face-to-face human intelligence (HUMINT) methods outside of the PRC when they pose a better chance of success. Numerous cases have surfaced in the last few months that indicate the scale and breadth of these espionage efforts. On the digital side, these include the seizure by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) of 13 Internet domains used to target U.S. citizens, including those with security clearances, as well as of additional domains used to target U.S. critical infrastructure (DOJ, June 10 , August 26 ). On the HUMINT side, examples include the DOJ sentencing of a former senior adviser for the Federal Reserve Board of Governors to over three years in prison for “funneling sensitive Federal Reserve information to Chinese spies,” and a former U.S. Army soldier pleading guilty to sending information on U.S. weapon systems to the PRC (DOJ, July 15 , September 16 ; CNBC , September 30).  [1] Beijing may have perceived an inflection point beginning in 2018 when Xu Yanjun (徐延军), the first Ministry of State Security (MSS) officer to be extradited to the United States, was arrested ( Reuters , November 21, 2022; National Security Archive , accessed October 1). With advancements among foreign counterespionage services, the PRC’s intelligence services may have concluded that recruiting and handling assets are best conducted from within the PRC’s borders. Prisoner Exchanges Highlight Risk and Suggest Change Xu Yanjun was convicted in 2021, and his operative, Ji Chaoqun (季超群), was convicted shortly thereafter in 2022 ( CNA , March 9, 2023; Guancha , Nov 28, 2024). In November 2024, however, both men were released and repatriated to the PRC, well before the end of their sentences. This was the first known instance where Beijing negotiated to recover intelligence personnel captured by the United States ( Chicago Tribune , November 27, 2024; VOA Chinese , November 28, 2024) In exchange, Beijing released two U.S. citizens convicted of “espionage” and one under a death sentence for drug trafficking. The lack of evidence from the Chinese side about these cases raises the possibility that Beijing decided to take the three individuals as hostages to trade for their nationals in the United States.  [2] This swap was particularly notable as it marked the return of PRC intelligence personnel apprehended in the United States for the first time.  [3] As far as is publicly known, Beijing had previously eschewed efforts to recover its captured spies. In one prominent case, Chi Mak (麦大志), who ran a highly effective and longstanding technology theft operation in southern California for 20 years before he was apprehended, was ignored after his 2007 conviction. He died there in October 2022 at age 82 ( Substack/HUMINT , November 21, 2025; Sina.com , May 1, 2007).  [4] Commercial Platforms Keep Intelligence Officers at Home Since the U.S.–PRC negotiated swap, PRC intelligence techniques have emphasized technology-enabled recruitment and handling, suggesting that Beijing views prisoner swaps as a tool only to be used on rare occasions. The MSS has developed a workflow that allows officers to remain within the PRC’s borders, mitigating the risk of identification by hostile security services. As noted by the Belgian security service, the recruitment and handling of “individuals of interest” now “is often carried out in China or from China” ( VSSE , January 14, 2025). Five Eyes nation assessments covering cases across North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific between 2019–2026 describe a similar evolution in intelligence operations conducted by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA). Chinese services increasingly conduct spotting and assessment at industrial scale through LinkedIn and other professional networking platforms, encourage targets to undertake seemingly legitimate paid consulting work as an initial step, and employ third-country and private-sector intermediaries as operational cut-outs. In this form, they have adopted the semiconductor industry’s commercial talent-recruitment model ( Five Eyes , March 6). The U.K. Security Service (MI5) has separately and specifically attributed comparable LinkedIn headhunter-style tradecraft—including two accounts identified as “Amanda Qiu” and “Shirly Shen”—to the MSS itself, indicating the online-recruitment shift spans both the civilian and military intelligence services rather than being unique to either ( BBC , November 18, 2025). The recruitment of former CIA and Defence Intelligence Agency officer Kevin Mallory in 2017 by the MSS was a precursor. Mallory, who was in financial difficulty, was approached on LinkedIn by a contact posing as a representative of the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences—a think tank with documented ties to Chinese intelligence—and offered a paid “consulting” role. The relationship subsequently developed through in-person meetings in Shanghai rather than the United States ( DOJ , May 17, 2019). Although Mallory was arrested before he could establish a long-term espionage operation, the case appears to have inspired, rather than discouraged, Beijing’s confidence in remote recruitment methods. Security services across Europe report similar patterns. MI5 Director General Ken McCallum disclosed in 2023 that approximately 20,000 Britons had been approached through LinkedIn by Chinese recruiters, more than double the roughly 10,000 users MI5 had said were being targeted online by all foreign intelligence services and criminals two years earlier ( The Guardian , October 18, 2023). The Canadian Security Intelligence Service has separately warned that Chinese intelligence services advertise employment opportunities through front companies, leading applicants to unknowingly work on behalf of a hostile intelligence service. Comparable warnings have also been issued by Germany’s Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV), the Netherlands’ General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD), and Czechia’s Security Information Service (BIS) ( BfV , 2020; AIVD , February 8, 2022; Euronews , September 16, 2024; CSIS Public Report, 2025). Such approaches continued this year, as demonstrated by the 2026 Kevin Zhang/Oriental Consulting operation, which reportedly netted substantial NATO and EU intelligence information ( Hong Kong Free Press , March 28). These industrial-scale approaches are particularly amenable to the deployment of artificial intelligence. AI systems can search and classify large numbers of publicly available professional profiles, identify combinations of access, expertise, foreign travel and possible financial or career vulnerability, and rank prospective targets for human review. Generative AI can then draft individualized approaches in the target’s language, vary the supposed recruiter’s identity and commercial pretext, and sustain preliminary conversations with many candidates simultaneously. The U.K. National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) assesses that AI already provides a “capability uplift” in reconnaissance and social engineering, making both more effective; it also enables more convincing approaches without the linguistic mistakes that traditionally exposed foreign phishing and influence efforts ( NCSC , January 24, 2024). Human Recruiters Remain Valuable Despite this growing reliance on online recruitment—likely enhanced by AI—traditional human intelligence operations have by no means disappeared. Instead, they complement digital approaches and are employed when they present the best chance of success. Two recent cases show how human recruitment is fused with technology-enabled tradecraft. Singaporean academic Dickson Yeo was recruited by Chinese intelligence contacts he met while giving a talk in Beijing, then set up a fictitious political consulting firm and used LinkedIn’s contact-suggestion algorithm to identify and approach potential sources almost daily; he received more than 400 resumes, roughly 90 percent from people with U.S. military or government security clearances, before he was caught ( Straits Times , April 2, 2025). Estonian national Gerli Mutso travelled to the PRC for coordination with PLA intelligence officers who used the cover identity of a fictitious “Beijing Information Association”; she then returned to Europe and recruited Tarmo Kõuts, an Estonian scientist with access to NATO’s Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation, who subsequently supplied classified defense-research material to the PRC. Mutso was convicted in 2022 and sentenced to eight and a half years; Estonia’s Supreme Court upheld her sentence in 2023 while partially annulling other elements of the conviction ( ERR News , June 17, 2023). Even with the shared linguistic background between the PRC and Taiwan, PRC intelligence officers follow a comparable trajectory over time. The Ministry of National Defense (MND) has noted that PRC tradecraft moved from direct in-person contact to introductions via third parties met outside Taiwan, to an increasing recent focus on online recruitment ( CNA , April 22, 2025; MND , April 23, 2025). This suggests the shift toward remote, intermediary-based recruitment is a general trend rather than one confined to harder-target Western countries. Conclusion PRC intelligence officers increasingly direct foreign recruitment from the safety of the PRC, relying on online platforms, commercial intermediaries, and locally based facilitators to conduct much of the initial contact and relationship building that was traditionally done abroad. The result is a model that reduces, but does not necessarily eliminate, operational exposure for Chinese intelligence personnel while allowing recruitment efforts to expand simultaneously, even exponentially, across multiple countries. Notes [1] Other examples include an MI5 warning that over 100 U.K.-linked academics had contributed to research projects funded by the MSS via a proxy ( MI5 , September 30); the arrest by Belgian authorities of both a man suspected of stealing semiconductor technology and an intern at NATO headquarters for spying for the PRC ( CBC , July 29; Reuters , September 7); the arrest by Korean authorities of two PRC citizens accused of intercepting fighter jet communications and reportedly obtaining training materials from U.S. bases ( Korea JoonAng Daily , September 29); the indictment of a man in Taiwan for leaking classified documents to PRC spies, and of another three former military personnel for collecting military secrets since 2020 ( Taipei Times , August 18; Focus Taiwan , October 1); and the sentencing of an Australian businessman for compiling reports for PRC intelligence ( ABC , September 10). [2] Hostage taking is part and parcel of Beijing’s playbook when dealing with foreign governments and institutions ( China Brief , May 11, 2017; Substack/Strategic Narratives , July 31, 2025). [3] The only other known example since the CCP’s 1949 victory was a genuine spy swap in 2015 between the PRC and Taiwan. In an agreement enabled politically by the meeting that November between President Xi Jinping and Taiwan’s then president Ma Ying-jeou (馬英九), the PRC released two Taiwanese military intelligence officers, Colonels Chu Kung-hsun (朱恭訓) and Hsu Chang-kuo (徐章國) in exchange for a Chinese intelligence officer, Li Zhihao (李志豪) ( Taiwan Ministry of National Defense , November 30, 2015; China Taiwan Net , December 1, 2015). [4] Beijing similarly ignored Larry Wu-tai Chin (金无怠) and his wife. Having confessed to the FBI that he had spied for the PRC over the course of four decades, Chin allegedly committed suicide in jail before sentencing ( Sohu.com , August 19, 2024). Years later, unofficial mainland sources began to laud his achievements as a “mole” inside the U.S. Intelligence Community (Red Song Network, January 26, 2018 , October 27, 2025 ; Sina.com , April 8, 2020; Zhihu , March 26, 2024). The post In the Online Age, PRC Foreign Intelligence Evolves appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Taiwan’s First F-16 Block 70s Have Finally Arrived
summary: After nearly seven years of waiting, Taiwan has received the first two aircraft from its long-delayed purchase of 66 new-build F-16C/D Block 70 fighters from the United States. The two single-seat F-16Cs, serials 6727 and 6728, touched down
content: After nearly seven years of waiting, Taiwan has received the first two aircraft from its long-delayed purchase of 66 new-build F-16C/D Block 70 fighters from the United States. The two single-seat F-16Cs, serials 6727 and 6728, touched down at Chihhang Air Base near Taitung on October 2. They are the first factory-new fighter aircraft delivered to Taiwan in 25 years and mark the beginning of the aircraft acceptance and integration phase of the Republic of China Air Force’s (ROCAF) so-called Peace Phoenix Soaring project. The two jets have also had an unusually eventful trip to Taiwan. They began their journey to the island on August 17, flying from Lockheed Martin’s production facility in Greenville, South Carolina, to Hawaii. The aircraft were subsequently forced to remain there for more than a month after an unexpected issue prevented them from continuing across the Pacific as planned. The reasons for the delay have been the subject of considerable speculation, including weather and tanker availability. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6727 arrive in Taitung. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press The two jets finally departed Hawaii again on October 1, stopping in Guam before making the final leg to Taitung today. Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo said today that more of the aircraft will arrive before the end of the year, although he did not provide a specific number. Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70 fighter jets Taiwan took delivery Friday of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 fighter jets purchased from the United States, with the aircraft landing at Chihhang Air Base in the eastern county of Taitung at around noon. pic.twitter.com/hbqdV6io26 — Focus Taiwan (CNA English News) (@Focus_Taiwan) October 2, 2026 The 66-aircraft purchase is worth approximately $8 billion. Taiwan originally expected deliveries to begin much sooner, but production-line adjustments, supply-chain problems, and software issues contributed to delays. COVID, too, had an impact on the production line. The program’s delivery schedule has slipped repeatedly . Defense Minister Koo said in March, May, and again through his deputy in June that the first aircraft were expected to arrive by the end of September. That deadline passed without an F-16 reaching Taiwan. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6727 touches down earlier today. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense acknowledged in late September that development and production of the aircraft’s new electronic warfare self-protection system had also been a factor. The Block 70s are being equipped with L3Harris’ AN/ALQ-254(V)1 Viper Shield electronic warfare suite , and the system was not yet fully through its development and production process when the first aircraft were otherwise ready for delivery . L3Harris announced on September 3 that it had completed production of the first 35 Viper Shield systems, underscoring that the electronic warfare equipment was itself still moving into production as Taiwan’s fighters were approaching delivery. Taiwan chose to acquire the AN/ALQ-254 rather than the AN/ALQ-257 electronic warfare system used on U.S. Air Force F-16s. Lawmakers have questioned whether the system meets requirements associated with earlier work to modernize earlier F-16A/B Block 20 fighters to the F-16V standard . Meanwhile, Defense Minister Koo argued that those requirements applied to the earlier Block 20 upgrade rather than the new Block 70 purchase. Other international F-16 Block 70 operators are also using Viper Shield. Taiwanese officials have defended the decision, citing the specific requirements of Taiwan’s F-16 fleet and associated procurement considerations. The system is intended to provide the new fighters with a modern electronic warfare and self-protection capability against increasingly sophisticated radar and missile threats. There are also still questions about when the Viper Shield system itself will be fully ready. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6727. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press Weapons deliveries have also not kept pace with the aircraft themselves. Taiwan is receiving AIM-120C-8 AMRAAM air-to-air missiles as part of the F-16 package, with 200 ordered. The C-8 version incorporates upgrades from the U.S. Air Force’s Form, Fit, Function Refresh (F3R) effort, including new electronics and improved electronic-counter-countermeasures intended to make the missile more capable in a heavily contested electromagnetic environment. For Taiwan, the missile will provide the new F-16s with a modern beyond-visual-range air-to-air weapon that can be cued by the aircraft’s AN/APG-83 Scalable Agile Beam Radar (SABR), as well as other sources of targeting information through the F-16’s networked systems. An AIM-120 AMRAAM is prepared to be loaded onto an F-16V at Chiayi Air Base, in Chiayi on January 28, 2026. Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP The AIM-120C-8 is particularly relevant as Taiwan fields more F-16s against China’s increasingly capable fighter fleet, which includes aircraft equipped with long-range air-to-air missiles such as the PL-15 . Taiwan’s F-16 Block 70 package also includes the AGM-88 High-speed Anti-Radiation Missile (HARM), intended for attacks against enemy air defense systems. According to Roy Choo , a defense journalist and TWZ contributor, the first of the new AGM-88F missiles arrived in Taiwan back in 2022. The major gap is the AGM-154C Joint Standoff Weapon (JSOW). The precision glide weapon is intended to give Taiwan a longer-range strike capability against ground targets without requiring the launching aircraft to fly directly over heavily defended areas. According to the latest reporting from Taiwan, deliveries of the AGM-154C have been held up by delays on the U.S. production line and may not begin until 2027 or 2028 at the earliest. Existing stocks of these weapons were also heavily used in Operation Epic Fury . The two aircraft now sitting at Chihhang are significant for another reason. Unlike Taiwan’s existing F-16V fleet, they are new-production aircraft rather than older fighters that have been upgraded. Taiwan received 141 F-16A/B Block 20s that were upgraded to the F-16V configuration under a separate modernization program completed in 2023. The new Block 70s incorporate many of the same technologies — including the APG-83 — but are built from the ground up as new aircraft. A Taiwan Air Force F-16V taxis out during a spring military exercise at Chiayi Air Base, in Chiayi on January 28, 2026. Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP The Block 70s will also bring a significant new passive-sensing capability to Taiwan’s F-16 fleet. Under a $328.5-million U.S. Foreign Military Sales contract awarded to Lockheed Martin in February, Taiwan is receiving the company’s IRST21 Legion-ES infrared search and track system. Designed specifically for the F-16, the long-wave infrared sensor can passively detect and track airborne targets without emitting radar energy. That gives the aircraft another way to search for and track threats while reducing its own electromagnetic signature. The IRST21 also gives the F-16s a passive way to detect and track low-observable targets, potentially providing another means of finding Chinese stealth aircraft without relying solely on radar. In 2019, Lockheed Martin displayed a model of a Block 70 F-16 with what appeared to be a podded IRST system on one of its chin stations at the biennial Taipei Aerospace & Defense Technology Exhibition in Taiwan: The mysterious IRST pod at TADTE – https://t.co/avpx5djZMM pic.twitter.com/86lqxu6fN6 — Alert 5 (@alert5) August 16, 2019 The new fighters will therefore complement Taiwan’s upgraded F-16A/Bs while expanding the overall number of modern F-16s available to the ROCAF. The timing matters. People’s Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft operate around Taiwan on an increasingly routine basis, forcing the ROCAF to maintain a persistent air-defense posture. The additional F-16s will provide more aircraft for missions ranging from air defense and counter-air operations to maritime strike . Ground crew prepare to load AGM-84 Harpoon anti-ship missiles in front of an F-16V during a drill at Hualien Air Force base on August 17, 2022. Photo by SAM YEH/AFP via Getty Images The F-16V fleet is also being tested for a more specialized intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance role. The ROCAF has recently been conducting flight and systems integration testing of the MS-110 advanced reconnaissance pod, part of its Phoenix Scout project. The service plans to acquire six pods to replace older reconnaissance equipment . Based on the DB-110 digital sensor architecture, the system combines visible-light and infrared imaging with long-range, day-and-night reconnaissance, and real-time image transmission, allowing imagery to be passed more rapidly to ground command and intelligence elements. Integrating the pod with the F-16 and associated ground systems will give Taiwan another means of monitoring activity around the island and its surrounding waters. A ROCAF F-16V carrying an MS-110 reconnaissance pod. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press But Taiwan remains heavily outnumbered across the Taiwan Strait. China is fielding an increasingly sophisticated combat aircraft fleet that includes the J-20 and J-35 stealth fighter, large numbers of advanced fourth-generation fighters, airborne early warning and other force-multiplier aircraft , and a growing variety of uncrewed systems . A J-20 fighter during the Changchun Air Show on September 22, 2025 in Changchun, Jilin Province of China. Photo by Zhang Xiangyi/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images And the F-16s will face the same fundamental problem as Taiwan’s other combat aircraft in a major conflict: staying operational. China possesses extensive missile and air capabilities that could threaten Taiwan’s airbases, aircraft shelters, fuel supplies, command-and-control infrastructure, and other elements needed to keep fighters flying. You can read more about how the ROCAF would likely go to war with China in this previous in-depth feature. Basing the new F-16s at Chihhang Air Base, operated by the 7th Tactical Fighter Wing, is significant, Choo told us. “The basing of the aircraft at Chihhang allows the ROCAF to readily project air power south and eastwards, especially over the Bashi Channel , which is one avenue PLA can gain access to the Philippine Sea and beyond.” He explained. “Previously, ROCAF fighters from other bases maintain QRA detachments there” A new F-16C Block 70 lands at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung on October 2, 2026. Photo by CHENG Yu-chen / AFP The F-16 delivery today is only the beginning of a much larger effort to get all 66 aircraft into Taiwanese service. According to the latest information from the ROCAF, 63 F-16C/D Block 70s remain in various stages of production and delivery in the United States, with some already moving through the handover process. The remaining aircraft will be delivered according to production, flight-test, and acceptance milestones before being ferried to Taiwan. Once the full order is delivered, Taiwan will operate more than 200 F-16s when the new Block 70s are combined with its existing fleet. That will give the ROCAF a considerably larger force of modern F-16s, with substantial commonality between the upgraded F-16V fleet and the new-production Block 70s. The aircraft will still need to go through Taiwan’s acceptance procedures, while pilots and maintenance personnel complete the necessary conversion and training work. The new jets will then be progressively incorporated into the ROCAF’s operational units. Remarkably, the arrival of the first Block 70 fighters today marks the first delivery of new fighters to Taiwan since 2001, when the last of the 150 F-16A/B Block 20s were delivered. “The ROCAF’s surviving fleet of 139 F-16s, 53 Mirage 2000s , and 129 F-CK-1s was largely inducted in the 1990s, when Taiwan held the upper hand in the cross-Strait air-power balance,” Choo explined. “Even then, there remained a requirement for additional fighters, prompting the island’s first formal request to purchase 66 F-16C/Ds during the 2006 Monterey Talks.” F-CK-1s taxi for takeoff during a scramble as part of a combat readiness exercise at Ching Chuan Kang Air Base in Taichung on January 7, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP “By the late 2000s, these fighters were approaching the limits of their combat effectiveness as the PLA air fleet expanded in both size and capability. Fortunately, substantial upgrades began to be rolled out to the F-CK-1s and F-16s from the 2010s.” In the wake of the 2019 acquisition of the F-16C/D Block 70s, questions arose over the aircraft’s asymmetric value as the Taiwan military increasingly focused on developing a plan for asymmetric capabilities in response to the PLA’s growing combat power. “However, developments in recent years have underscored the continued importance of a capable fighter fleet not least for policing Taiwan’s airspace amid the PLA’s sustained gray-zone air operations around the island,” Choo added. ROCAF F-16C Block 70 serial 6728. Peter Ho, Formosa Aviation & Military Image Press The timing of today’s arrival is also notable. The aircraft reached Taiwan just days after U.S. President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. The delivery comes amid questions in Taipei about the future pace of U.S. arms transfers, after Trump said in May that a proposed $14-billion Taiwan arms package was being held in abeyance. He had approved an $11-billion package in December 2025. Washington continues to say that its policy toward Taiwan has not changed. Beijing, for its part, continues to oppose U.S. arms sales to Taiwan and regards the island as part of Chinese territory. It has taken nearly seven years to get the first two F-16C/D Block 70s, to Taiwan. But their arrival marks the first step in a major modernization of the ROCAF’s F-16 fleet, adding new-production fighters with improved radar, electronic warfare, sensors, and weapons to a force that is already operating upgraded F-16Vs. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Taiwan’s First F-16 Block 70s Have Finally Arrived appeared first on TWZ .

content: “李南央状告海关案”跟进报道（146） ——继续通知、继续跟进 上期 “跟进”中 ，我说中国国家图书馆没有对美国地方法院 “李锐资料归属案” 的裁决提起上诉，应该是主管此案 李锐资料134专案组（LimsTim134） 的决定。这个推测在本月以无论如何大开脑洞也想不到的方式得到了证实。 9月19日，在东欧游历半个多月后，我们从法兰克福乘美联航班机飞回旧金山。我的座位是一排靠窗，巴悌忠的座位在我后面。正在整理行囊，身后飘过一声有些犹疑的招呼： “ Ms. Li. ”我下意识地 回头寻声，简直不能相信自己的眼睛，咫尺相对的会是张玉珍/中国国家图书馆的美国代理律师福赛特。他的座位与我同排，在走道的另一侧。我看着他那双显然也有些不敢置信的眼睛脱口而出： “ 世界怎么会这么小！上天居然为我的书准备了如此精彩的情节！ ” 福赛特似乎仍处在错愕之中不知如何回应。我抓住了这不可思议的天赐良机，迅即提问： “ 我有个问题，你如果觉得不方便不必回答。 ” 他秒回： “什么问题？” 我秒接： “不上诉是谁的决定？是你建议他们那么做，还是他们自己决定这么做？” 没有些许的踌躇，他说： “ 跟我没有关系，是他们自己的决定。 ” 我的嘴角翘了起来： “谢谢你让我知道。” 对话间，我看到福赛特旁边座位有位女士一直站立着望向我们，脸拉得有点长。我问： “这位是你的夫人？” 福赛特侧过身，让我和那位女士直接相对，说： “是，她是我的妻子。” 我冲福赛特的妻子笑了笑：“很高兴遇到你。” 她却有些不悦地问福赛特： “她是谁呀？” 福赛特 只回答了两个字： “ Li Rui’s Daughter （李锐的女儿）。” 显然，她知道老公曾经手的案子，一脸的无法相信： “世界真是太小了！” 大约察觉到妻子的不悦，福赛特对我笑笑，低下头摆弄起座位上的枕头、毯子。我转向坐在我后面的悌忠，他说：“这简直是百万分之一的机率！不信有上帝之手都不成！” 有心的读者可能会记得我在“跟进144”中提到地方法院裁决的最后一条： “作为本案胜诉方斯坦福和李南央有权根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第 54(d)(1) 条追回其合理费用。”这里的“合理费用” 指的是我方聘请专家证人、取证证人等费用。斯坦福向中国国家图书馆提了支付请求吗？答案是 “没有。”作为胜诉一方斯坦福的立场是：“相对整个案件而言，这些费用数额相当有限。为了以非对抗性的方式推进事态，斯坦福/胡佛方面决定不提交相关申请。” 在 “李锐资料归属权案”的初始 ，我对斯坦福大学不愿因这个案件影响她在北京大学内的斯坦福中心的运作而举棋不定是完全不理解的。结案后的今天，斯坦福大学在我方完胜之后不对中国国家图书馆穷追猛打，这个选择我认同。 这次在欧洲游历，我们在波兰首都华沙参观了位于瓦津基公园的美希莱维茨基宫内曾经的中美华沙会谈厅。厅内的介绍牌子上写着： 1958年至1979年间，在瓦津基皇家公园梅西莱维茨基宫，中华人民共和国和美利坚合众国政府代表举行过数十次会谈。这是当时中美之间对话沟通的主要途径，对两国建立互信、维护和平发挥了重要作用。 可以说，没有中美华沙会谈，就不会有后来1971年的尼克松宣佈访华和最后1979年的中美建交。很难想象，在视资本主义为万恶之源、美帝国主义为中国人民头号敌人的毛泽东年代，中美之间会在一座波兰的前王宫中一间佈置的绝不无产阶级化的厅内举行过会谈，而且不是一次，是数十次。联想到几天前美国国务卿鲁比奥回答各方对总统川普高规格接待习近平的质疑的回复： “对于两个拥有庞大经济和军事体量的强国而言，直接沟通是必要的。”他将川普与习近平的会谈与 冷战时期美苏之间的会谈进行了类比。 在十多个小时的航行途中，我和张玉珍的律师福赛特没有再说过一句话，商务仓的小包座将乘客隔在互不打扰的各自空间。直到飞机平稳落地旧金山机场，乘客纷纷起身去取头顶行李舱内的箱子，我与福赛特不可避免地再次直面相对。 我微颔告别说： “很高兴遇到你。” 他颇真诚地回应： “我也是。” 我又说： “我正在写案子的书，书中当然提到了你。你若愿意看，出版后我会告知你。” 他说： “请一定，很期待。” 换到八年前，我想我能忍住不对张玉珍的美国代理律师怒目而视就不错了。现在，我对美国独立于政治之外的法律体系有了更多的理解，我也从斯坦福的律师那儿学会了看问题的不同视角。是的，世界上有那么多的国家，那么多的国家又有那么多不同的制度、信仰、意识形态、文化、历史……即使是无可避免、迫在眉睫的你死我活，留有沟通渠道、保持对话、不把事情做绝，似乎是持有常识的政府、抑或个人的睿智选择。 回到我的 “状告海关案” 。上期 “跟进” 发出后，一位读者来电说： 祝贺您，南央大姐！您终于胜利了，正义终于胜利了！ 但愿您还剩下的一个案件能够在您和我们的有生之年也得到胜利！！ 我回复说： 是真相胜利了。在美国真相是可以获胜的。在那边，真相是可以被伪造的。“海关案”若获开庭日，或许是“真相”可以不再被伪造或掩饰的开端。 9月10日，北京第三中级法院向我发出了第32次“延审通知”。他们继续“通知”，我继续“跟进”。 2026年9月30日
