content: 艾地声Edysen  X @KA594594 · Oct 1, 2026 从“国庆”争论说起：我们究竟在爱什么样的“国”？  十多年前，也是在十月一日。一位相识多年的朋友给我发来一句：“国庆快乐。”他是做公益的，博士学历，曾经经历过失独之痛。后来夫妻二人都取得了香港身份，但工作、生活以及主要的社会交往仍然在深圳。他热心公益，也一直有相当强烈的“爱国”情结。 我当时回了他一句：“我从不过这样的节日。”就这么一句话，没有长篇争论，也没有互相谩骂。可是从那以后，他基本不再理我，我们的友谊也就这样莫名其妙地断了。 坦率说，当年的我心里是有判断的，而且判断相当刻薄：一个读到博士的人，经历过人生如此巨大的苦难，也已经移居香港，为什么对于“国家”“政权”“国庆”这些概念仍然不加区分？我甚至在心里用了“高学历脑残”这样的词。 多年以后再回头看，我仍然不同意他的政治判断，却不再那么确信当年的自己就比他高明多少。我的那句“我从不过这样的节日”，其实同样带着一种决绝。它表达了我的政治立场，却没有给对方的情感经验留下多少余地。他所说的“国庆快乐”，在他的意识里，未必是在为某个党庆祝，也未必是在为某种政治制度背书。他想到的可能就是“中国”——故乡、亲人、语言、文化、民族以及他几十年生活于其中的共同体。而我听到“国庆”两个字，首先想到的，却是1949年以后建立起来的中华人民共和国及其政治制度。 我们使用的是同一个“国”字，心中所指的，却可能根本不是同一个东西。这段因“国庆”而失去的友谊，很多年以后仍然让我觉得遗憾。 一、薄瓜瓜的一段话，又把这个问题带了回来 今年十月一日，我看到薄瓜瓜的一段帖文。他说：“今天是国庆。从历史看，我们的‘国’与西方的国不同。它凝聚的，是一个民族的文明与血脉。”随后，他把这种理解继续推演到海外华人的命运：中国如果不强大，华人在海外无论混得多好，也“站不住腰板”；最后用了那句中国人耳熟能详的话：“皮之不存，毛将焉附。”很快就有人批评他，认为他把中华人民共和国与中华民族、中国文明混为一谈：“这个‘国’”只有77年，怎么能够代表数千年的中国？ 这场争论有意思的地方，不在于谁的“认知水平”更高。相反，我觉得争论双方实际上同时碰到了一个中国政治思想中长期没有得到充分清理的问题：我们天天说中国、国家、祖国、民族、中华文明、中华人民共和国乃至党和政府，可是这些词究竟是不是一回事？如果不是，它们之间的边界又在哪里？ 二、十月一日究竟是谁的生日？ 这个问题首先可以从最简单的历史事实说起。1949年12月2日，中央人民政府委员会通过《关于中华人民共和国国庆日的决议》，决定自1950年起，以每年10月1日，即中华人民共和国宣告成立之日，为“中华人民共和国的国庆日”。此前全国政协的建议案甚至明确使用了“以代替十月十日的旧国庆日”的表述。所以，从严格的历史意义上说，10月1日纪念的是中华人民共和国的建立，它不是中华文明的生日，不是中华民族的生日，当然更不是“中国”这个历史共同体开始存在的那一天。 截至2026年，中华人民共和国建立77年，这没有问题；但如果因此说“中国只有77年历史”，同样把“中国”与“中华人民共和国”混为一谈。我们今天所说的一个“国”字，实际上经常装着完全不同的东西。有时候它指的是故国——生我养我的土地；有时候是祖国——带有强烈情感归属的历史共同体；有时候是民族——共同的历史、文化和身份认同；有时候是文化文明——语言、文字、经典、习俗以及跨越王朝兴亡而延续的文明传统；有时候是现代国际政治意义上的国家；有时候则明确指向1949年以来的中华人民共和国；还有一些时候，人们在不知不觉中进一步把中华人民共和国、现行政权、中国共产党和“中国”叠加在一起。 一个“国”字，承担了太多东西。 三、为什么这些概念如此容易混在一起？ 这并不完全是普通人的逻辑能力问题。今天中国官方关于爱国主义的制度表达，本身就在有意识地建立这些概念之间的联系。2023年通过的《爱国主义教育法》一方面把爱国主义与“中华民族”“伟大祖国”“中华文化”等联系起来；另一方面又明确要求“坚持爱国和爱党、爱社会主义相统一”。这就是一个非常值得观察的政治现象。 爱土地，爱民族，爱文化，爱国家，爱一种政治制度，爱一个执政党——本来是六个可以分别讨论的问题，却被压缩进了一个“爱国”概念。一旦这种概念融合完成，政治判断就很容易变成身份判断。你反对共产党，于是有人说你反华；你批评政府，于是有人说你不爱国；你不认同中华人民共和国现行政治制度，于是进一步被理解成你否定中国。甚至像当年的我一样，仅仅说一句“我不过这个国庆节”，对方听到的也可能不是“我拒绝庆祝一个具体政治国家建立的纪念日。”他听见的可能是“我不爱中国。” 这两句话当然不是一回事。可是当“党—国—民族—文明”长期叠加以后，它们在人们的情感世界里确实可能变成一回事。现在回头看，我那位朋友与我的决裂，也许就发生在这个缝隙里。 四、薄瓜瓜真正提出了一个比他自己那段话更大的问题 我并不想简单嘲笑薄瓜瓜的那段话。他说“我们的国凝聚的是一个民族的文明与血脉”，这里实际上表达了一种古老而普遍的民族国家情感。问题在于：如果这里的“国”是中华文明，那么它显然不始于1949年；如果是中华民族，也不能由中华人民共和国垄断定义；如果指中华人民共和国，那么它又不能自动继承数千年文明的一切历史意义。三者可以具有历史连续性，却不能因此成为三个同义词。 更值得讨论的是他的下一步推论：中国不强大，海外华人便站不住腰板。这里面包含一部分现实经验。一个国家的国际地位、经济实力和外交能力，当然可能影响其国民的旅行便利、领事保护以及国际处境。但是海外华人的尊严显然不能只从“中国强不强”推导出来。一个生活在法国的华人是否能够挺直腰杆，还取决于法国的法治是否保护他；一个成为美国公民的华裔，其基本权利首先来自美国宪法和法律；一个取得香港身份的人，也可能同时拥有复杂的地方、民族、文化与国家认同。 人的尊严不能完全抵押给一个抽象国家的强弱，否则我们马上会碰到另一个问题：如果一个国家军事很强、经济很强、国际影响力很强，却不能充分保障其公民的权利，这个国家的人民是不是就因此更有尊严？“强国”与“强民”，从来不是天然的同义词。 五、“皮之不存，毛将焉附”：谁才是皮？ 所以薄瓜瓜那段话里，我最感兴趣的其实不是“文明与血脉”，而是最后这八个字：皮之不存，毛将焉附。这个比喻在中国国家主义叙事中极其自然：国家是皮，个人是毛；国家在，个人才在；国家强，个人才能强；国家没有了，个人也无所依附。 但为什么一定如此？现代国家理论完全可以提出相反的问题：如果没有一个个具体的人，国家又依附在哪里？甚至中华人民共和国现行宪法第二条自己写的也是：“中华人民共和国的一切权力属于人民。”如果国家权力来自人民，那么逻辑上的主体究竟是谁？人民是为了国家而存在，还是国家为了人民而建立？国家是目的，还是工具？如果把这些问题再推进一步，我们甚至会发现：也许人民才是皮，国家才是毛。 当然，个人也无法脱离共同体独自生存。语言是共同体给予我们的，文化是前人留下来的，安全需要公共权力维护，市场需要规则，权利也需要制度保障。所以现代宪政并不是消灭国家，而是重新安排国家与人的关系。国家很重要，但正因为国家拥有军队、警察、监狱、税收以及合法强制力，它才尤其需要回答一个问题：这些权力究竟为谁而存在？ 六、国家会亡，民族可以继续，文明甚至可能穿越所有政权 中国历史尤其适合帮助我们理解这一点。秦亡了，中国没有亡；汉亡了，中国没有亡；唐宋元明清一个个成为历史，中国文明仍然延续。1912年中华民国建立，中国并没有因此只有114年历史；1949年中华人民共和国建立，中国当然也没有因此只有77年历史。政治国家有具体的制度形态，政府有产生和更替，政权有兴亡，而民族、社会与文明具有另一种更漫长的连续性。 这也正是“谁是中国”这个问题真正困难的地方。国家不是政权，政权不是政府；民族不是国家，文明更不是任何一个执政党的私产。它们彼此交叠，却必须能够被概念地区分。如果不能区分，我们最终就很容易从“爱中国”一步一步推导出“必须爱某种制度”，再从“爱某种制度”推导到“必须拥护某个政党”，最终甚至把对掌权者的批评理解为对祖国的背叛。这时候，“爱国”便不再只是人的自然情感，而可能成为一种政治忠诚测试。 七、多年以后，我也重新审视当年的自己 写到这里，我又想起那个已经多年不再来往的朋友。年轻一些的时候，我喜欢迅速给人下判断。博士学历又如何？受过那么多教育，怎么连国家与政权都分不清？经历过那么多人生苦难，又已经移居香港，为什么还是那么热衷于“爱国”？于是我心里给出了那个很粗暴的判断：“高学历脑残。” 今天我不会这样写他。不是因为我改变了自己关于国家和政权的基本判断，是越来越觉得：一个人的国家认同从来不只是知识问题，里面有童年，有故乡，有父母，有语言，有创伤，有利益，有安全感，也有几十年政治社会化留下的痕迹。知识能够帮助我们分析这些东西，却不能自动消灭它们。 更何况，我当年的决绝何尝不是另一种简单化？我认为自己看穿了国家与政权的区别，于是便很容易认为没有看穿的人都是愚昧的。这种“真理在我手中，所以我有资格审判你”的姿态，与我一直批判的政治文化之间，也许并没有想象中那么遥远。这大概是流亡以后，我才慢慢懂得的一件事情：反对国家主义，并不意味着必须反对别人对故国的感情；批判一个政权，也不需要把所有与自己政治判断不同的人都逐出道德共同体。我们需要区分的，正是这些东西。 八、我们究竟在爱什么？ 再看到今年这场关于“国庆”的争论，我已经不太想追问谁更聪明、谁更爱国。我更愿意问：当一个人说“我爱中国”的时候，他究竟在爱什么？是武汉的一碗热干面，是四川的山河，是江南的雨，是母亲说话的乡音？是汉字、唐诗、《史记》和两千多年绵延不断的文化记忆？是生活在这片土地上的十几亿具体的人？是现代意义上的中国国家？是中华人民共和国？是社会主义制度？还是中国共产党？ 这些东西可以同时被一个人热爱，但它们不是一回事。同样，一个人也完全可能深爱自己的故乡、语言、文化和同胞，却反对一个具体政府、政党或者制度。把这些东西区分开来，不是为了让中国人变得“不爱国”，它也许能够使“爱国”重新成为一种不需要政治审查的自然感情。 十多年前，一个朋友对我说：“国庆快乐。”我回答：“我从不过这样的节日。”我们因此失去了彼此。多年以后再想起这件事，我仍然不会补上一句“国庆快乐”，因为那不是我的真实想法。但如果时光能够倒流，我大概不会再在心里骂他“脑残”。我会问他一句：你说的这个“国”，究竟是什么？然后也允许他反过来问我：你拒绝的那个“国”，又究竟是什么？也许真正值得一个民族庆幸的，不是所有人在同一天挥舞同一面旗帜，说出同一句话；是终于有一天，人们能够面对同一个“国”，拥有不同的理解，彼此争论，彼此批评，却不必因此绝交，更不必因此成为敌人。

title: 3 Hong Kong dog owners lose appeals against ‘fighting dog’ classifications
summary: Three dog owners have lost their appeal against the government’s decision to classify their pets as “fighting dogs,” designations that were made as authorities tightened regulations following fatal dog attacks in August. Bao Bao and Baku ou
content: Three dog owners have lost their appeal against the government’s decision to classify their pets as “fighting dogs,” designations that were made as authorities tightened regulations following fatal dog attacks in August. Bao Bao and Baku outside the Animal Management and Animal Welfare Building Complex on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Dogs and Cats Classification Board, an advisory board to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), held three back-to-back appeal hearings at the Kowloon Animal Management Centre on Wednesday. The owners told HKFP that after the hearings, they were handed a document stating that the board had determined their pets to be fighting dogs. The AFCD said earlier this month that since August 20, it had identified seven dogs as fighting dogs. The designation subjects these dogs to rules such as requiring them to wear a muzzle, and barring them from entering dog-friendly restaurants. Mr Ho, the owner of Bao Bao, told HKFP he did not have much hope for the appeal result, but decided to try anyway. Bao Bao outside the Animal Management and Animal Welfare Building Complex on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. His dog, which was previously listed as a Staffordshire Bull Terrier on its license, was taken by AFCD officers at a cafe in Stanley last month. The AFCD then re-classified him as a Pit Bull Terrier, one of the four dog types that fall under the “fighting dogs” category. The group also includes Dogo Argentinos, Japanese Tosas, and Fila Brasileiros. The department said Staffordshire Bull Terriers fall under the Pit Bull Terrier type. He said he showed the board members messages of support from residents in Stanley, where he and his wife live with their three dogs, attesting that Bao Bao was a friendly and gentle dog. “I feel helpless. There was no point to this hearing,” Mr Ho said in Cantonese, adding that the board members did not directly address his concerns. ‘Identified as a murderer’ Jacqueline Cheung, founder of the non-profit Love Adopt Animal Society, brought Bowie to the appeal hearing on Wednesday. Bowie outside the Animal Management and Animal Welfare Building Complex on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Her non-profit is now taking care of Bowie after her previous owner gave her up following the dog’s designation as a fighting dog when he brought her for a vaccine appointment at an AFCD centre. Bowie was registered as a Sharpei on her dog license. Jacqueline said the appeal hearing lasted around 20 minutes, during which she told the board that Bowie showed clear characteristics of a Sharpei. “She has the fur of a Sharpei. Her bristle-like hair pokes me,” she said in Cantonese. “She also has a ‘meat mouth,” she said, referring to the fleshy muzzle that Sharpeis are known for. A document stating that Bowie is a “fighting dog,“ taken outside the Animal Management and Animal Welfare Building on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Cheung said the board did not address her argument, adding that the appeal was a “waste of time.” “The entire process is unscientific. It lacks credibility, and it’s mind-boggling,” Cheung said. “It’s like she’s been identified as a murderer, like Yip Kai-foon,” Cheung said, referring to an infamous Hong Kong gangster said to have been involved in a number of murders. Bowie is now staying at a dog hotel, with the expenses being paid for by her organisation. She said that she feared Bowie would never be able to find a home, as people might not want to adopt her knowing she is a fighting dog. Another dog owner, Mrs Lai, said that she and her husband attended the hearing with a lawyer. Baku outside the Animal Management and Animal Welfare Building Complex on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. She adopted Baku, an eight-year-old licensed as a mongrel, around four years ago. The dog was taken from their home in late August, after the AFCD said it received a case regarding a “suspected unregistered fighting dog.” The board, too, upheld the earlier decision designating her as a fighting dog. Laws toughened Hong Kong authorities’ hardened regulations on dogs comes after fatal dog attacks last month made headlines and prompted authorities to review the city’s laws relating to canines. In August, a dog – reportedly a Spanish mastiff – killed two smaller dogs in separate incidents in Yuen Long. A woman working at a dog shelter in Ta Kwu Ling was also killed by a dog that the AFCD later said was a fighting dog. While veterinarians have criticised the AFCD’s approach of using breed to determine the danger posed by a dog, the department has defended its policies. The Animal Management and Animal Welfare Building Complex. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Fighting dogs may attack suddenly without warning due to their characteristics,” the AFCD told HKFP last month. See also: ‘Deed, not breed’: Owners and experts push back on stigma against ‘fighting dogs’ “Their well-developed musculature and powerful jaws, coupled with a tenacious biting tendency, often result in more severe injuries when attacks occur.” Dog owners whose pets are classified as a fighting dog can launch an appeal within 14 days. The board members include veterinarians, dog breeders, academics, and representatives from animal welfare organisations, according to the AFCD. Earlier this month, a woman was killed while cycling at night in Yuen Long after a suspected dog attack. Police said CCTV footage showed three dogs chasing her while she was riding a bike. After that, the AFCD and the police mounted an operation, capturing eight stray dogs in the area. Among them, three were microchipped but their licences had expired, the department said.

title: Beijing Makes Rapid Gains Toward Seed Self-Reliance
summary: Executive Summary: Beijing is now realizing its long-held goal of mastering core breeding technologies. Chinese-made genotyping chips have broken the longstanding monopoly of U.S. firms and entered the breeding pipelines of leading seed com
content: Executive Summary: Beijing is now realizing its long-held goal of mastering core breeding technologies. Chinese-made genotyping chips have broken the longstanding monopoly of U.S. firms and entered the breeding pipelines of leading seed companies in the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Genetically modified (GM) crops are currently undergoing large-scale demonstration planting. Chinese institutions and companies control nearly all the traits in use. Within the PRC, foreign investors are barred from GM breeding, and gene editing follows a shorter approval path, which has paved the way for domestic developers to bring products to market. Artificial intelligence (AI) breeding tools developed by state research institutes and universities are entering pilot use, with broad prospects ahead. Drawing on multi-location field data from the national variety trial network, these tools will see deeper and wider application. On September 4, at the 33rd China Beijing Seed Industry Conference, one demonstration saw a dual-arm robot pollinate tomatoes, holding a pollen tube in one hand and a pollination brush in the other ( China Daily , September 7). The robot, GEAIR 2.0, comes from the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS).  [1] The conference focused on smart breeding and featured presentations on gene editing and other frontier technologies. It exhibited 145 frontier technological achievements, including breeding chips, large artificial intelligence (AI) models, and smart phenotyping equipment with independent intellectual property rights (Xinhua, August 28 , September 6 ). The conference showed the latest progress in the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) push for seed self-reliance.  [2] Since the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform approved the “Seed Industry Revitalization Action Plan” (种业振兴行动方案) in 2021, the self-sufficiency rate of germplasm and staple varieties has kept rising ( Xinhua , July 9, 2021). Domestically bred varieties now cover more than 95 percent of the PRC’s crop area (Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs [MARA], December 17, 2025 , July 27 ). Over the past year, the PRC has continued to push at the technological frontier of the seed industry. In 2025, the State Council issued its “Opinions on Deepening the Implementation of the ‘AI+’ Initiative” (关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见), which called for efforts to accelerate innovation in AI-driven breeding; in 2026, the No. 1 Central Document went further, calling for commercialization of biotech seed breeding (生物育种产业化) and integrating AI into agricultural development ( State Council , August 26, 2025; China Brief , September 21, 2025; Xinhua , February 3). Beijing is working to master the core technologies of the seed industry, and it is succeeding. Chinese Gene Chips Challenge Foreign Suppliers For years, the PRC’s seed industry relied heavily on imported technology for determining genetic variation, also known as genotyping. Genotyping chips, for instance, allow scientists to simultaneously identify tens of thousands of parts of a plant’s DNA. Breeders use the results to select parents, predict traits, and identify varieties. U.S. products long dominated the market, with Illumina and Affymetrix (now part of Thermo Fisher Scientific) supplying a PRC industry held back by high procurement costs and the technology gap until as late as 2024 ( China Daily , May 14, 2024). In February 2025, the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) placed Illumina on the PRC’s Unreliable Entity List. The following month, the ministry banned the company from exporting gene sequencers to the PRC. The ban was lifted in November 2025, but Illumina remains on the list (MOFCOM, February 4, 2025 , March 4, 2025 , November 5, 2025 ). Around that time, import substitution for genotyping chips sped up markedly and extended to equipment and consumables. In May 2024, Suzhou Laso Biotech (Laso; 拉索生物), together with the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences, China Agricultural University, and other institutions, released a solid-phase wheat genotyping chip, claiming that the scanner, reagents, and software were all developed and produced in-house ( China Daily , May 14, 2024). In October 2025, Laso, along with the Jiangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences and Huazhong Agricultural University, released a rapeseed genotyping chip, mastering the bead-array assembly process for solid-phase chips, a process Laso’s chairman described as “long monopolized by a few U.S. companies” (长期被少数美国公司垄断) ( Science and Technology Daily , May 14). Liquid chips, which capture target DNA in solution for genotyping by target sequencing, had achieved their breakthrough earlier. Hebei-based MolBreeding (博瑞迪) says its products cover 156 species ( MolBreeding , accessed September 26). Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture (隆平高科), Syngenta, and Dabeinong (大北农) have used them at scale in commercial breeding ( Jiangsu Xinhua Daily , May 18, 2022). The industry’s depth was on display at September’s conference in Beijing, which showcased more than 50 breeding chips covering crops, livestock and poultry, aquatic species, and fruit trees ( Xinhua , August 28). Central government policy is also creating demand for genotyping chips. On July 27, MARA published an initial catalog of ten crops, including rice and wheat, that were covered under its “essentially derived variety” system (实质性派生品种制度), which allows for the modification of a seed variety for commercial purposes only with the consent of the holder of the original variety if the modification retains the essential characteristics of the original ( MARA , April 23, 2023; China News Service , July 27).  [3] As the catalog expands to more crops, seed companies will need high-throughput genotyping to settle variety-rights disputes, and domestic suppliers already established in the market stand to benefit ( MARA , July 27). Domestic Traits Dominate Beijing’s Biotech Crop Rollout Genetically modified (GM) crops are the area where Beijing has pushed furthest and where domestic traits are most widely planted. Chinese institutions and companies control nearly all the traits in use throughout the PRC. Since 2008, the State Council has cultivated domestic traits through a major science and technology program, with the stated goal of “obtaining a batch of genes with important application value and independent intellectual property rights” (获得一批具有重要应用价值和自主知识产权的基因) ( MARA , July 10, 2008). Since then, attention within the PRC’s seed industry has shifted from whether domestic traits exist to how well they perform. At the conference, one forum was devoted to the yields and returns of demonstration planting of domestic GM soybeans ( Beijing Daily , September 3). Cotton is an earlier example of successful import substitution in GM crops. In 1997, the PRC approved the commercialization of Bt cotton, which has built-in insect resistance. Varieties from Monsanto, as well as from Delta and Pine Land, were cleared for sale in Hebei, Shandong, Henan, and Anhui provinces.  [4] According to official media, foreign Bt cotton varieties held more than 95 percent of the PRC’s Bt cotton market in 1998; Chinese-bred varieties from the Cotton Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences (CAAS) then overtook them, reaching a 70 percent share by 2005 ( China Youth Daily , May 9, 2006). Today, PRC-bred Bt cotton varieties hold 99 percent of the PRC market ( Xinhua , August 24, 2023). For GM soybeans and corn—the two largest U.S. agricultural exports by value—foreign companies have been shut out of cultivation approvals from the start ( USDA , June 30). The only companies or institutions that have been able to obtain the biosafety certificate required for these crops to be planted in the PRC are Chinese ( MARA , January 21, 2020).  [5] Beijing also restricts foreign entry and crop imports through formal rules. Under the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) (2024 Edition) (外商投资准入特别管理措施（负面清单）[2024年版 ]), issued by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and MOFCOM, foreign investors may not “invest in the breeding of GM varieties of crops, breeding livestock and poultry, and aquatic seedlings, or in the production of their GM seeds (seedlings)” (投资农作物、种畜禽、水产苗种转基因品种选育及其转基因种子（苗）生产) ( NDRC , September 6, 2024). Foreign companies’ GM crops may be imported, but the certificates must state that the material “may be used only as processing raw material, may not be diverted to other uses, and may not be released into the environment” (只能用作加工原料，不能改变用途、不能进入环境) ( MARA , December 31, 2024). By contrast, the government supports seed companies going abroad to breed, produce, and sell seed ( MARA , August 30, 2021). Dabeinong’s GM soybean traits have been approved for cultivation in Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay ( MARA , May 20, 2025). PRC developers keep producing new GM traits, while MARA discloses less and less about them. In May 2026, a high-oil soybean event developed by the Oil Crops Research Institute of CAAS and partners received a biosafety certificate, reportedly “the first domestic soybean event approved with high oil content as its target trait” (国内首个以高油为目标性状获批的大豆转化体) ( China Science Daily , May 7). Meanwhile, the approval lists on MARA’s website stop at the end of 2024, making it harder for outsiders to see the true state of the PRC’s GM development. The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has noted that the move “may raise public concerns regarding the transparency” of the PRC’s GM regulation ( USDA , December 1, 2025). Gene editing, a newer breeding technology than GM, is another area Beijing is pushing forward quickly. MARA issued the Guidelines for the Safety Evaluation of Gene-Edited Plants for Agricultural Use (Trial) (农业用基因编辑植物安全评价指南 [试行]) in January 2022 and the Review Rules for Gene-Edited Plants for Agricultural Use (农业用基因编辑植物评审细则) in 2023 ( MARA , January 24, 2022). Under the rules, developers of an edited plant adding no environmental or food safety risk can apply for a production-and-application biosafety certificate directly after intermediate trials ( MARA , April 28, 2023). Within two years, MARA issued ten biosafety certificates through this streamlined path.  [6] On editing tools, MARA listed “Cas12-family gene-editing platform tools with independent intellectual property rights” (拥有自主知识产权的Cas12家族基因编辑底盘工具) among the scientific achievements of the 14th Five-Year Plan period, and such tools already have Western buyers: Germany’s KWS and France’s Limagrain have taken global licenses to editing tools from Shandong Shunfeng Biotechnology (舜丰生物) and Qi Biodesign (齐禾生科), respectively ( KWS , September 10, 2025; MARA , December 17, 2025; Limagrain , July 31). AI Use Accelerating in Crop Breeding AI, the theme of the September conference, is still at an early stage in breeding, but its scale and speed of advance are already striking. Among 12 seed-industry large AI models exhibited at the event, the leading examples came from the state research system: the SeedLLM model developed jointly by the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Yazhouwan National Laboratory, and China Agricultural University; the Shennong Breeding Studio (神农育种Studio) released by China Agricultural University; and the crop phenomics big-data factory built by the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences ( Beijing Municipal Bureau of Agriculture and Rural Affairs , September 5). These AI tools are evolving to develop automated analysis capabilities. When SeedLLM was released in 2024, it mainly answered questions about variety selection and cultivation techniques. GeneScientist, released on top of it in 2025, has since helped researchers discover dozens of previously unreported gene functions, later confirmed by experiments (Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, April 28, 2024 , July 31, 2025 ). Shennong Breeding Studio, released during the September conference, goes a step further, reportedly bringing germplasm data and breeding analysis tools together, so researchers can describe what they need in natural language and call up data and tools for parent screening and line evaluation ( Xinhua , September 8). Once such platforms spread, analytical capacity once limited to large institutions will be open to many more breeders. Beijing holds a vast store of variety trial data, which will help to refine these tools. Under the relevant rules, new varieties of major crops must pass trials and registration before they can be promoted. This national variety trial system generates field data from multiple locations and years across the country. Data from more than 1,000 regional crop variety trial stations nationwide flow into designated platforms each year ( Xinhua , September 8). The state organizes the trials and feeds the data into these platforms, unlike U.S. trial data, which remain scattered among many holders. As a result, the PRC’s models may be trained more quickly. Conclusion Beijing’s push for seed self-reliance has extended over the last few years from a focus on crop varieties to the technologies used in creating them. State research institutes and universities lead much of the frontier research and companies turn it into products and bring them to market, while rules such as the bar on foreign investment in GM breeding leave room in the market for domestic technology. For the foreign companies that have long supplied seed products to the PRC, the more mature the PRC’s import substitution becomes—and the more the country achieves its goal of self-reliance—the more they are likely to be squeezed out of the domestic market. They will also face increasing pressure in global markets, as the PRC’s leading seed companies follow the path set by their compatriots in the automobile, battery, and solar sectors. Notes [1] GEAIR is short for Genome Editing combined with AI-based Robotics; its Chinese name is “吉儿” ( University of Chinese Academy of Sciences , August 12, 2025). In an experiment, a team led by Xu Cao (许操) at the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology used gene editing to reshape tomato flowers so the stigma is exposed, which a robot was then trained to recognize and pollinate. This method has also been used, successfully, to create male-sterile soybean lines of the kind hybrid seed production requires, plants that cannot pollinate themselves and can only receive pollen from others ( Beijing Tongzhou Release , September 3). GEAIR 2.0 is now being tested and piloted in several agricultural industrial parks and may spread further ( Xinhua , September 8). See: Xie et al., “Engineering crop flower morphology facilitates robotization of cross-pollination and speed breeding,” Cell 188, no. 21 (2025): 5809–5830.e27, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2025.07.028 . [2] China Brief has covered the PRC’s pursuit of self-reliance in seed and grain production previously. See: China Brief, June 7, 2021 , June 17, 2022 , May 23, 2025 . [3] Under MARA’s guidance, identification of derived varieties “gives priority to high-throughput molecular testing technologies such as SNP and MNP” (优先采用高通量分子检测技术，比如SNP、MNP) ( MARA , July 27). [4] Carl E. Pray, Jikun Huang, Ruifa Hu, and Scott Rozelle, “Five Years of Bt Cotton in China – the Benefits Continue,” The Plant Journal 31, no. 4 (2002): 424, https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-313X.2002.01401.x . [5] Based on the approval lists MARA published for 2019–2024, counted by event, with stacked events counted separately and renewals and area expansions not double-counted: 25 corn events and 10 soybean events. China National Seed Group (中国种子集团) holds five corn events, four of them (Bt11, GA21, the MIR162 series, and MZIR260) Syngenta events; ChemChina acquired Syngenta in 2017, and Syngenta now belongs to Sinochem Holdings. The lists are in the approvals section of MARA’s GM information column ( MARA , accessed September 26). [6] Based on the approval lists MARA published for 2023–2024: ten production-and-application biosafety certificates for gene-edited crops, five for soybeans, two for corn, two for wheat, and one for rice. The first went in April 2023 to Shandong Shunfeng Biotechnology for a high-oleic soybean, and most are held by Shunfeng and Qi Biodesign (MARA, April 28, 2023 , January 18, 2024 , May 8, 2024 , December 31, 2024 ). The post Beijing Makes Rapid Gains Toward Seed Self-Reliance appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Beijing’s London Embassy as an Integrated Threat
summary: Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) proposed new embassy in London may serve as a hybrid warfare hub. The site will consolidate existing united front, influence, intelligence, and diplomatic operations under one roof,
content: Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) proposed new embassy in London may serve as a hybrid warfare hub. The site will consolidate existing united front, influence, intelligence, and diplomatic operations under one roof, potentially improving coordination among various Chinese government agencies. The scale of the new embassy, which spans 5.5 acres in central London, could expand the PRC’s gray-zone and hybrid warfare capabilities. The site will also be out of the reach of U.K. law enforcement authorities due to its diplomatic immunity. PRC diplomats and United Front Work Department personnel have a long history of exploiting diplomatic cover to conduct influence operations. The new embassy could also amplify Beijing’s transnational repression campaign against dissents and individuals perceived to be hostile to it. Recent incidents involving PRC embassy staff carrying weapons, ongoing threats against Hong Kong and Taiwanese citizens suggest this trend continuing with greater intensity. On July 31, the High Court in London rejected a legal challenge against the government’s approval of a new embassy for the People’s Republic of China (PRC) on the site of the former Royal Mint Court ( Reuters , July 31). The decision was based on whether the U.K. government acted unlawfully in the approval and whether other factors were improperly taken into account, rather than the broader geopolitical and national security implications. The proposed embassy represents an integrated threat, something that analysis of the plans has largely overlooked to date. Once up and running, it could function as a cross-domain architecture for hybrid warfare, co-locating, coordinating, and integrating existing united front work and exerting cognitive pressure on Chinese Communist Party (CCP) targets on British soil. Recent behavior of embassy staff has only fueled this cause for concern. On July 3, guards at the current embassy were accused of brandishing electroshock weapons—which are illegal in the United Kingdom—and threatening protesters with them ( The i Paper , August 27). Following the incident, footage from earlier in the year came to light, appearing to show guards outside the new embassy site carrying the same weapons ( The Telegraph, September 2). The Party’s united front work in the U.K. meanwhile continues apace. In September, Yang Wanming (杨万明), president of the Chinese People’s Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries (CPAFFC), a united front-linked organization, led a delegation to the United Kingdom, engaging a number of mayors, business organizations, and universities across Scotland and England ( People’s Daily , September 14). Later in the month, Ambassador Zheng Zeguang (郑泽光) told an audience of more than 500, including leaders of nearly 100 overseas Chinese associations from across the country, to “cultivate a deep sense of patriotism … continue to be contributors to Chinese-style modernization and promoters of China’s unification” (厚植家国情怀 … 继续做中国式现代化的贡献者、中国统一大业的促进者) ( PRC Embassy in the United Kingdom , September 22). New Embassy as Hybrid Warfare Hub The previous government under Keir Starmer framed the new embassy as a “security benefit,” as Beijing’s diplomatic presence will consolidate under the new embassy from seven buildings to one ( The Guardian , January 2). From another perspective, however, that consolidation could also benefit the PRC by bringing all its operations under one inviolable roof, on a site of unprecedented scale, covering 5.5 acres of central London. The PRC’s hybrid warfare strategies view operations in different domains as mutually reinforcing. PRC diplomats have long organized gray zone activities that support Beijing’s preferred narratives with the participation of known united front actors. Consular “pop-up” events that provide consular services in non-designated diplomatic facilities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and beyond are a textbook example (China Brief; June 7, 2025 , December 12, 2025 ). Bounty notices issued by the PRC Ministry of Public Security (MPS) targeting Hong Kong and Taiwanese citizens are another instance of combined lawfare, influence operations, and transnational repression ( China Brief , July 25, 2025). Beijing’s operations, however, are often fragmented at the operational level, especially when it comes to non-state-level directed initiatives. The Fuzhou municipal Public Security Bureau (PSB) established two of the now-closed Chinese police stations in London; the Shantou municipal government set up UCT (U.K.-China Training Ltd./UK-China Travel Ltd.) as an overseas talent acquisition station; embassies and consulates co-host pop-ups with united front groups; diplomats engage with universities’ Chinese Students and Scholars Association (CSSA) branches for surveillance and political mobilizations; and the United Front Work Department (UFWD) directs the Council for the Promotion of the Peaceful Reunification of China (CPPRC), the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese (ACFROC), and other organizations for counterprotests ( WeChat/Shantou Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau , September 30, 2017; WeChat/PRC Embassy in Canada , September 11, 2019; IRSEM , October 2021; China Daily , January 24, 2022; Yixian News , January 24, 2022; Southeast Net , April 30, 2022; WeChat/PRC Consulate in Fukuoka , June 20, 2023; U.S.-China Press , August 14, 2023; CPPRC , accessed July 31, 2024; UK-China Training Ltd , accessed September 29). In these cases, each actor operates from its own premises, with frequent duplication of—or even competition for—resources. Groups also compete for official recognition from the embassy or consulates. The new London embassy would likely heighten that competition, with different united front groups all seeking access while officials strengthen ties with the most useful proxies. Meanwhile, recent conferences in Beijing appear to signal the institutionalization of overseas united front work (China Brief, August 7 , August 19 ). Together, these developments likely compound the Party’s leverage and influence capabilities. At ten times the size of the current embassy, making it larger than any PRC diplomatic mission in Europe, it could potentially have a much more active and effective role in coordinating these disparate efforts. UFWD personnel have a history of operating under diplomatic cover ( ASPI , June 9, 2020). If Ministry of State Security operatives are posted to the embassy at the same time, the new embassy could facilitate direct cooperation between the two, as housing representatives of both organizations under one roof would remove structural barriers to information flows, especially for actors previously scattered across seven buildings. Whether such integration occurs may not be observable from outside; but the new embassy provides the conditions for it to occur, and it aligns with the PRC’s “whole-of-system” approach to hybrid operations,. Diplomatic Immunity as a Shield The consolidation of disparate functions in one diplomatic mission may also give the PRC greater freedom to engage in gray zone operations or even subversive activities under the cover of diplomatic immunity. Although the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations is universal and applies to every foreign mission and diplomat, malign states can often exploit its protections. For Beijing, this can mean treating the embassy as a space immune from intervention that can be used for cross-domain operations below the threshold of a kinetic confrontation. The High Court ruling references an illustrative case. In a 2020 case, Zhang Meifang (张美芳), the PRC’s consul general in Belfast, carried out construction work at the consulate—a listed building—without planning permission. According to the ruling, she “relied on the Vienna Convention in rejecting the applicability of planning law and the jurisdiction of the court” ( The High Court , July 31). The case was eventually resolved, but in a way that revealed part of the PRC’s operational logic: “cooperation” often comes with a precondition. In this case, the host state had to first concede its enforcement mechanisms. Although the Vienna Convention does not require that diplomats operate legally, from Beijing’s perspective, it serves exactly the opposite function, by allowing the weaponization and active exploitation of diplomatic immunity. The expanded diplomatic presence on the new embassy site would increase the risks of such impunity, with more diplomatic passports meaning that more personnel will cover more positions, all with diplomatic cover. PRC diplomats have a long-documented history of involvement in influence operations in collaboration with ACFROC, CSSAs, and other actors across the united front network ( USCC , August 24, 2018; ASPI , June 9, 2020). An increase in the volume of PRC actors strongly suggests that operational capacity will also increase. Unlike a Chinese overseas police station housed in a Chinese restaurant, one operating from within the embassy compound cannot be investigated and forced to shut down by local law enforcement and intelligence agencies. Scale and Symbolism as Cognitive Pressure In recent years, the so-called “wolf warrior” rhetoric of PRC diplomats has escalated to direct threats of physical violence, and in some cases actual physical assault—behavior that can be understood as part of a toolkit for cognitive warfare operations. Before this year’s allegation of embassy guards wielding prohibited weapons, in 2022, diplomats dragged a protester inside the grounds of the consulate in Manchester and proceeded to assault him physically ( Reuters , October 17, 2022). Ongoing transnational repression has also included the Hong Kong Police Force’s issuing of arrest warrants and bounties on individuals living in the United Kingdom. This behavior is not unique to the United Kingdom. In 2025, for instance, former Canadian member of Parliament Paul Chiang, suggested that people hand over his opponent—a Hong Kong activist with a HK$1 million bounty ($130,000) on his head—to the PRC consulate in Toronto ( Hong Kong Police Force , December 24, 2024; Globe and Mail , March 31, 2025). In November 2025, the PRC consul-general in Osaka made a veiled threat against Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae in a social media post criticizing her remarks on a potential Taiwan contingency, saying that “the dirty neck that sticks itself in must be cut off” ( UDN , November 10, 2025).  [1] Most recently, during General Secretary Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington, D.C. in September 2026, at least one PRC individual appears to have attacked peaceful protesters but was not detained, reportedly because he had diplomatic immunity ( X/Maya Wang , September 24; HRIC , September 29). The psychological effect these precedents set is chilling. A more formidable PRC presence in London, beyond the reach of U.K. law enforcement and therefore emboldened to act with impunity, may leave individuals blacklisted by Beijing—such as parliamentarians, government officials, and researchers—feeling unsafe in the U.K. capital. The symbolism of the site reinforces this psychological component. In the 19th century, the Royal Mint received deliveries of silver that the Qing was forced to pay under a series of “unequal treaties” that Beijing today regards as milestones in China’s “century of humiliation” ( South China Morning Post , March 26, 2019). By acquiring the site for itself, Beijing is overturning what it sees as a historical injustice: as then-ambassador Liu Xiaoming (刘晓明) said at the 2018 official transfer ceremony of new diplomatic premises, Royal Mint Court is the “right monument of China” (中国的不朽之作; literally “China’s immortal work”) at the “right moment of China” (属于中国的时刻) ( PRC MFA , May 18, 2018). Whether by design or not, the very presence of such a “monument” sitting at the heart of London exerts cognitive pressure on Beijing’s targets. Conclusion The new U.K. government under Andy Burnham has yet to announce a stance on the embassy or an approach to the PRC. The initial signs, however, do not suggest a tougher stance on Chinese aggression. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband’s speech at the Labour Party Conference spoke of “stand[ing] up for our security against those who would do us harm,” but made no mention of the PRC ( The Labour Party , September 28). Burnham similarly avoided reference to the PRC, despite promising to “stand up to threats wherever they come from. Whether Russia, Iran or anywhere” ( The Labour Party , September 29). Still, the approval for the embassy was made by the former government, and the Burnham administration does not have to stand by a decision that was flawed from the beginning. Given that the proposed embassy can be interpreted as a central coordination node in which Party officials can integrate various influence operations and actors and pursue gray zone activities with relative impunity, any mitigation measures can only be effective if the embassy is assessed holistically—not as a few isolated risks or an oversized diplomatic facility, but as an integrated hybrid warfare architecture on British soil. Notes [1] In the original Japanese, the consul general wrote, “勝手に突っ込んできたその汚い首は一瞬の躊躇もなく斬ってやるしかない.” The post Beijing’s London Embassy as an Integrated Threat appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Campaign Against ‘New Qing History’ Reinforces Ethnic Unity
summary: Executive Summary: The ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is engaged in an ongoing campaign to enforce greater assimilation of ethnic minority (i.e., non-Han) populations under programs of “Sinicization”—which are intended not just to ass
content: Executive Summary: The ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is engaged in an ongoing campaign to enforce greater assimilation of ethnic minority (i.e., non-Han) populations under programs of “Sinicization”—which are intended not just to assimilate these groups within Han culture, but also to assert firmer government control over these regions and peoples. As a component of this larger effort, the CCP is engaged in an ongoing propaganda campaign against “New Qing History” (NQH). In contrast with traditional scholarship that depicts the Manchu Qing rulers as themselves thoroughly assimilated by Chinese culture, NQH emphasizes that the Qing was a far more Manchu-centric state than previously understood—and that Han-heartland “China” was but one of the domains (also including Mongolia, Tibet, Taiwan, and much of Turkic-speaking Central Asia) conquered and incorporated into a Manchu-ruled, multinational empire. This view implicitly challenges CCP narratives of a united, multi-ethnic “Chinese nation” ( Zhonghua Minzu ), and of an unbroken succession of Chinese dynasties reaching back to antiquity. The CCP’s campaign against NQH amplified in summer 2026, with multiple municipal- and provincial-level branches of the United Front Work Department (UFWD) launching an apparently coordinated campaign to attack and refute the NQH interpretation of China’s last imperial dynasty. This has included specific accusations that NQH is a “theory weapon” crafted by separatist forces to divide China, and that this thinking represents a direct threat to China’s national security. This narrative campaign may be expected to continue, alongside other policy tools employed by the Party to promote further “Sinicization.” In 2026, the government of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has taken measures to further assert and codify its policies regarding the control and management of the PRC’s ethnic (i.e., non-Han) populations. The most prominent such step came at the meeting of the National People’s Congress in March, when that rubber stamp body approved the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress (民族团结进步促进法) ( “Ethnic Unity Law” ). The expressed purpose of the law is to speed up “Sinicization”(中国化), promoting the fuller integration of the PRC’s ethnic populations and regions into a homogenized, Han-centric “common community of the Chinese nation” (中华民族共同体) ( PRC Ministry of Justice , March 13; China Brief , May 30).  [1] Among the more salient points of the law are the asserted need to enhance “ideological education on the Chinese nation’s development history” (中华民族发展史宣传教育), and to strengthen Mandarin-language elementary school instruction (articles 12 and 15, respectively). Ominously, the law also claims sweeping extraterritorial authority to target critics of the regime’s policies, by decreeing that groups and individuals outside the PRC who “undertake efforts against [the PRC] to wreck progress in ethnic unity, to manufacture ethnic separatist actions” (针对中华人民共和国实施破坏民族团结进步, 制造民族分裂行为) will face legal consequences. State media commentary predictably praised the law for “promoting extensive exchanges, interactions and integration among all ethnic groups, and advancing their common development,” while “rais[ing] the level of law-based governance in ethnic affairs” ( Xinhua , July 2). Party Touts ‘Great Unity’ Narrative The language employed in the law mirrors broader Chinese Communist Party (CCP) discourse on ethnic policy—and many of the salient terms carry specific, weighted meanings. In this context, “Sinicization” (中国化) carries with it a strong connotation of state control, rather than mere cultural affiliation.  [2] The term “Chinese nation” (中华民族, Zhonghua Minzu ), by contrast, carries the connotation of a national identity, that of the “Chinese people.” Zhonghua Minzu is depicted as transcending ethnic groups or political boundaries—and therefore connects to the “common consciousness” and “common community” of a multi-ethnic but firmly united nation, living side-by-side under the leadership of the CCP. The Party’s prescribed take on the history of the Zhonghua Minzu is the “‘Great Unity’ Historical Perspective” (“大一统”历史观). This maintains that China has been a unified and ethnically harmonious country throughout the entirety of its history, even as centralized political authority may have waxed and waned at various periods ( Guangming Daily , June 10, 2019; Chinese Social Sciences News [CSSN] , July 20, 2020). Per a PRC Ethnic Affairs Commission commentary that cites the Han Dynasty text Records of the Grand Historian (史记), this dates all the way back to the Qin state’s conquest and establishment of a unified kingdom circa 221 BCE. The commentary notes that “when Qin Shihuang unified all under Heaven, the first true ‘Great Unity’ state of Chinese history entered into being” (秦始皇一统天下，中国历史上真正的“大一统”国家由此肇始). The Qin’s unification of China marked a time of “great fusion of harmonious peoples” (和睦各族的大融合), which was “an important period for becoming a unified multiethnic country, and developing and solidifying the structure of the many peoples of the Chinese nation becoming one whole” (成为统一多民族国家、中华民族多元一体格局发展巩固的重要时期) ( China’s Ethnic Groups Magazine , January 18, 2023). Coordinated Crusade Against ‘New Qing History’ Advances Ideological campaigns against targeted heterodox modes of thinking have a long history within the CCP.  [3] To outside observers, such doctrinal disputes over obscure points in art and scholarship may seem akin to the proverbial debates of medieval theologians about the number of angels that might dance on the head of a pin. However, these matters have real significance within CCP discourse, where they often serve as ideological stalking horses intended to signal and reinforce prioritized Party policies. The CCP has identified a sinister, foreign-born threat to the “Great Unity Historical Perspective”: namely, the “New Qing History” (NQH; 新清史) school of scholarship. The CCP sees a fundamental threat in this mode of historical research, and has directed a sustained propaganda effort against both it and other alternative views that it labels “historical nihilism” (历史虚无主义) ( China Brief , March 28, 2025). The history of China’s last imperial dynasty, the Qing (1644–1912), has proven to be a sore spot for the CCP. This topic is politically so sensitive that a massive, 106-volume history of the period, completed by a government commission in 2018, has reportedly been indefinitely withheld from publication due to its alleged corruption by elements of “NQH” thinking ( SingTao , November 8, 2023; South China Morning Post , February 13, 2024) . In the meantime, a compulsory textbook has been issued for university students that criticizes and rebuts the arguments of the new Qing historians ( China Brief , May 24, 2024). New Qing History Complicates CCP Historical Narratives The Qing Dynasty was established in the 17th century via a series of military conquests by the Manchus (滿人), a non-Han people originating in the present-day northeastern provinces of the PRC (“Manchuria”). These conquests ended the Han Chinese-ruled Ming Dynasty. Traditional historical scholarship has tended to depict continuity between the Qing and earlier Chinese dynasties, and emphasized the extent to which the dynasty’s Manchu rulers were themselves thoroughly assimilated by Han Chinese culture. By contrast, New Qing History, a school of historical analysis that emerged among Western scholars in the 1990s, has taken a dramatically revisionist interpretation of the Qing period. NQH scholars developed the proficiency to study Manchu language documents, and focused greater attention on the distinctive Manchu cultural identity and outlook of the Qing rulers. NQH scholarship has posited that the Qing was a far more Manchu-centric state than previously understood; and that Han-heartland “China” was but one of the domains (also including Mongolia, Tibet, Taiwan, and much of Turkic-speaking Central Asia) conquered and incorporated into a Manchu-ruled, multinational empire.  [4] The CCP’s propaganda apparatus is engaged in an ongoing ideological campaign against NQH, for reasons that connect to the Party’s drive to assert both its own sovereignty claims and its vision of greater “ethnic unity.” Commentary from Chinese state academic institutions has long criticized NQH: for example, on grounds of its alleged “misreading of the 5,000-year history of civilization of the Zhonghua Minzu ” (中华民族五千多年文明史的误读), and that it fails to understand how the Qing “advanced the structure of the common community of the Zhonghua Minzu ” (推动中华民族共同体建构) (CSSN, April 12, 2024 ; April 10 ). NQH has even been identified in Party-affiliated commentary as a direct threat to national security.  [5] The Party Combats the ‘1644 Historical Perspective’ In a similar fashion, over the past year state propaganda institutions have felt the need to weigh in on the “1644 Historical Perspective” (“1644史观”)—a school of mostly online commentary that describes the fall of the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644) as a disaster for China, and the beginning of a long period of foreign rule (under the Manchus). For reasons nearly identical to those underlying the campaign against NQH, the “1644” commentary has also been singled out for official criticism. For example, in late 2025 the Zhejiang Province CCP Propaganda Department published a commentary titled “Be on Guard Against the ‘1644 Historical Perspective’ Disrupting the Rhythm” (警惕“1644史观”带乱了节奏). The commentary stated: Recently, the so-called “1644 Historical Perspective” has continued to generate controversy online. The core of this viewpoint argues that the 1644 destruction of the Ming Dynasty by the entry of the Qing army [was] “a rupture of Chinese civilization,” depicting the Qing Dynasty as a “foreign colonial regime” … [But] we must stride past the confused thinking of this “1644 Historical Perspective” … Chinese history has been written together by many peoples, in continuous development. The Ming – Qing transition was like every dynastic change, all were parts of the long river of Chinese history, rather than breaks in civilization … The Qing Dynasty inherited foundations of the Ming political system [and] consolidated unification of the territories of a multi-ethnic country [巩固了统一多民族国家的疆域] , [and] promoted contacts and exchanges among peoples, establishing [both] the legal principles and actual circumstances of modern China as a unified multi-ethnic country ( Zhejiang Province CCP Propaganda Department , December 17, 2025). United Front Launches New Attack in Summer 2026 Official criticism of NQH kicked up a notch in summer 2026, with state ministries and media outlets joining in more directly—thereby suggesting a conscious, top-down effort to further spotlight NQH for criticism and refutation. Such commentary often emphasizes the American origins of NQH, with the insinuation that it represents a foreign attack on the PRC’s domestic stability. One prominent example of this messaging emerged in mid-August, promulgated by institutions linked to the CCP United Front Work Department (UFWD), which bears the most direct responsibility for implementing the Party’s policies relating to ethnic minorities. In mid-August, a number of municipal and provincial-level UFWDs began to promote a commentary titled “New Qing History, Why Must We Attack It?” (“新清史”, 为什么该打?).  [6] The fact that multiple UFWD offices around the country began to promote the article nearly simultaneously strongly suggests higher-level directives to promote its message. This piece, arguably more clearly than any other, lays bare the underlying anxieties behind the CCP’s attacks on this seemingly innocuous academic theory. NQH is described as a “political plot” (政治阴谋) and as a “theory weapon raised up by separatist forces” (分裂势力提供“理论弹药”). This “theory weapon,” by calling into question Qing Dynasty governance of maritime regions, “gives support to ‘Taiwan independence’ separatist forces” (为“台独”分裂势力张目). On August 19, the China News Service (中国新闻社), the media outlet of the UFWD, published what appeared to be a condensed version of this article, as “New Qing History Seriously Erodes the Historical Foundations of the Chinese Nation” (“新清史”严重侵蚀中华民族共同体历史根基) ( CNS , August 19). This abbreviated version was itself picked up and featured by other regional governments ( CNS , August 20). Conclusion As asserted in a speech given by CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping in August 2021, “Chinese culture is like the trunk of a tree, while individual ethnic cultures are like branches and leaves; only when the roots are deep and the trunk is strong can the branches and leaves grow well” ( Central Conference on Ethnic Affairs , August 27, 2021). This statement encapsulates the Party leadership’s view of both the supremacy of majority Han culture, and the dependent nature of minority cultures in the PRC’s peripheral regions. The metaphor also carries with it a strong hint of the CCP’s intentions to further “Sinicize” such populations under more rapid assimilation and tighter central government control. It is in this context that the Party’s ongoing ideological campaign against “New Qing History” should be understood. The CCP sees an imperative to craft a narrative of eternal harmony between the complex patchwork of ethnic groups who reside in PRC territory, as a predicate to greater assimilation. Against this background, “New Qing History” challenges the “Great Unity” narrative with a far more complex story: one in which the “China” of the Qing Dynasty was less a unitary and cohesive nation than a multinational empire. As the Qing imperial state preceded the PRC state that ultimately emerged in the mid-20th century, the PRC inherited Qing sovereignty claims over vast peripheral regions—which were populated by peoples ethnically, linguistically, and culturally distinct from the Han majority. The central tenets of NQH challenge the Party’s narrative of an eternally unified and harmonious Zhonghua Minzu . It also challenges the narrative of unbroken succession, from one dynasty to the next, of the authorities of an ancient and unitary Chinese state. And, perhaps most sinister of all, NQH is foreign in derivation, reviving the CCP’s perennial paranoia about ideological infiltration eroding the foundations of one-party rule. The CCP’s own commentaries linking NQH with Taiwan “separatism” tip its hand as to why it so fears this stream of historical scholarship: by clear implication, borders and state sovereignties forged by Manchu conquests in the 17th century lose their binding legitimacy if they are disassociated from direct dynastic succession, and from an ancient and semi-mystical Zhonghua Minzu . As the CCP regime proceeds with its drive for further ethnic assimilation, it will also double down on the propaganda narratives that undergird the assimilation process. In tandem with this, the coordinated attacks on “New Qing History,” and other heterodox schools of thought regarding China’s history, may be expected to continue. Notes [1] For previous analyses of the Ethnic Unity Law , see: China Brief, March 27 , April 2 , May 6 , May 15 . [2] The author has commented on the use of the term “ Zhongguohua ”(中国化) in a previous article: John Dotson, “Propaganda Themes at the CPPCC Stress the ‘Sinicization’ of Religion,” ( China Brief , April 9, 2019). Note that endnote [1] of that article states: “There are differences of interpretation regarding the translation of the key Chinese-language term ‘ Zhongguohua ’ (中国化)—which could be interpreted as ‘Sinicization’ (implying an effort to bring something more closely into line with Han Chinese culture); or as ‘China-fication’ (implying that the thing in question will be nationalized, and/or brought under firmer state control). English-language outlets of official PRC state media generally use the former translation; however, the latter translation arguably better captures the meaning behind the government’s drive to further ‘ Zhongguohua ’ the practice of religion in China. For an authoritative commentary on the issue published under the name of the director of the CCP United Front Work Department, see: ‘You Quan: Persist in the Party’s Leadership over Religion, Persist in Advancing the Sinicization of Religion’ [尤权：坚持党对宗教工作的领导, 持续推进我国宗教中国化], Xinhua , March 20, 2019, https://archive.ph/v2DM4 . [3] Examples of these include Mao Zedong’s 1942 campaign against “bourgeois literature and art” during the period that the CCP was headquartered in Yan’an; and the official criticisms of the “poisonous weed” drama Hai Rui Dismissed from Office ( Hai Rui Ba Guan , 海瑞罷官), an ideological campaign that helped seed the political environment for the subsequent Cultural Revolution (1966-1976). For Mao Zedong’s speech on art during the 1942 Yan’an Rectification Movement, see: Mao Zedong, “Talks at the Yenan Forum on Literature and Art” (May 2, 1942), Marxists.org , https://www.marxists.org/reference/archive/mao/selected-works/volume-3/mswv3_08.htm . For an early official criticism of the playwright Wu Han and his play about the Ming Dynasty official Hai Rui, see: Yao Wenyuan, “On the New Historical Play Dismissal of Hai Jui “, People’s Daily (November 30, 1965), Marxists.org , https://www.marxists.org/archive/yao-wenyuan/1965/november/10.htm . [4] For an overview discussion of NQH scholarship perspectives, see: Joanna Waley-Cohen, “The New Qing History,” Radical History Review , Issue 88 (Winter 2004). https://www.academia.edu/11464843/Joanna_Waley_Cohen_The_New_Qing_History_ . [5] Zhang Renfeng (张仁枫) (Sichuan University Academy of Marxism), “The National Security Threat of the West’s False Historical Theory and an Historical Materialist Critique in Response—Targeting ‘New Qing Dynasty History’ and the ‘Inland Asia Historical Perspective’” (西方伪史观的国家安全威胁与唯物史观批判应对——以“新清史”“内亚史观”为靶点), Tongyi Zhanxian Xue Yanjiu (统一战线学研究) (2025, No. 5). [6] Li Defeng (李德锋) and Zhang Yide (张懿德), “New Qing Dynasty History, Why Must We Attack It?” (“新清史”, 为什么该打?). Li and Zhang are identified as faculty members at the University of Inner Mongolia. To cite but two examples of regional UFWD departments that published the article, those from both Weihai City and Shenzhen City did so on August 17 and August 18, respectively ( Weihai Municipal CCP United Front Work Department , August 17; Dao Zhonghua Tongzhan Xinyu, August 18). title: U.S. Mimics “Decoupled” Nuclear Detonation By Blowing Up A Tunnel Conventionally
summary: The U.S. government set off conventional explosives inside a tunnel deep in the Nevada desert this week in a test designed to replicate a so-called “decoupled” nuclear detonation . Data collected is now being used to help improve methods fo
content: The U.S. government set off conventional explosives inside a tunnel deep in the Nevada desert this week in a test designed to replicate a so-called “decoupled” nuclear detonation . Data collected is now being used to help improve methods for detecting this kind of nuclear testing. Just earlier this year, American authorities accused China of using decoupling to conceal new nuclear tests despite the country’s stated moratorium on such activities. The test, which involved the use of chemical high-explosives and radiotracers, was conducted yesterday inside P Tunnel in Area 12 of the Nevada National Security Site (NNSA), according to a press release from the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). The NNSS, which is situated within the boundaries of the U.S. Air Force’s Nevada Test and Training Range (NTTR), is used for a wide variety of testing purposes today . An agency under the Department of Energy, NNSA’s main jobs are to oversee the development and production of nuclear weapons, as well as manage America’s nuclear deterrent stockpile. A map giving the general sense of the location of the NNSS with the NTTR. Center for Radiological Nuclear Training Another map showing the specific testing areas within the NNSS. Area 12 is at the northern end of the complex. United States Geological Survey “This experiment is especially focused on further enhancing the U.S. capabilities to detect a ‘decoupled’ explosion,” per NNSA’s release. “Data collected from the experiment will be used to validate scientific models and refine algorithms that are critical to U.S. nuclear explosion detection efforts.” “Just as a stealth aircraft looks smaller on radar, decoupling can greatly muffle the signals detected by nuclear detection sensors, making a large explosion appear smaller,” the release explains. “In a conventional, or ‘coupled,’ underground nuclear test, a device is placed deep in a hole in close contact with the rock, allowing much of the explosion’s shockwave to reach sensors. In a decoupled test, by contrast, the device is detonated inside a large underground chamber, substantially reducing the explosion’s seismic signature.” “In this experiment, researchers gathered measurements using a broad suite of advanced sensors, including accelerometers, seismometers, infrasound sensors, electromagnetic sensors, chemical and radiotracer samplers, and meteorological sensors,” it adds. ”Together, these measurements will improve scientists’ understanding of the signatures produced by underground explosions and strengthen the United States’ ability to detect and characterize nuclear explosive events.” The U.S. already maintains a U.S. Atomic Energy Detection Systems (USAEDS) network, which is overseen by the U.S. Air Force Technical Applications Center (AFTAC). USAEDS is made up of more than 3,600 sensors positioned around the world. USAEDS is also tied in with the International Monitoring System (IMS), which is managed by the organization responsible for overseeing the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT). AFTAC also supports the mission to monitor for potential nuclear testing globally using a fleet of specially configured WC-135R Constant Phoenix aircraft. In addition, those planes are used to help keep watch for unusual spikes in atmospheric radiation that could point to nuclear or radiological accidents or other incidents leading to the spread of potentially dangerous radioactive material. With regard to the USAEDS network specifically, “once a disturbance is detected underground, underwater, in the atmosphere or in space, the event is analyzed for nuclear identification, and the findings are reported to command authorities,” according to AFTAC’s website . As mentioned, the U.S. government has accused its Chinese counterparts of using decoupling to conceal new nuclear testing, and NNSA’s press release draws explicit attention to these allegations. At the annual Conference on Disarmament in Geneva, Switzerland, in February, Thomas DiNanno, Under Secretary of State for Arms Control and International Security, said that China had conducted at least one such test at Lop Nur on June 22, 2020 . The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization (CTBTO) subsequently said the IMS had not detected an event matching that description at that location on that date. For its part, the Chinese government has denied the accusation. The social media posts below include satellite imagery showing activity at Lop Nur that could point to new nuclear testing activities in recent years. 参考 Satellite Imagery Analysis of China’s Alleged 2020 Nuclear Test at Lop Nur https://t.co/aafvU5Szh7 CSIS 20260213 ROLES SAT ANALYSIS No.7 中国に核実験実施の動き ー Lop Nur核実験場の画像分析 ー https://t.co/n66yYk0hLg ROLES 20250522 — KAROTASU (@type36512) May 24, 2026 While China is a signatory to the CTBT, the country has never ratified it. The Chinese government last acknowledged a critical-level nuclear test in 1996, after which a self-imposed moratorium was put in place, at least publicly. As an aside, the United States has also signed, but never ratified, the CTBT, and has a similar self-imposed moratorium on nuclear testing since 1992. It is worth noting that the treaty does not ban so-called sub-critical testing, which involves fissile material, but does not result in a full-fledged nuclear reaction. Last week, The Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration has been holding new talks with the Chinese government regarding various aspects of the country’s massively and rapidly expanding nuclear arsenal , including the testing allegations. That story immediately preceded a state visit by China’s President Xi Jinping to Washington, D.C., to meet with Trump. President Donald Trump (at left) and President Xi Jinping (at right) walk together at the White House last week. White House/Joyce N. Boghosian “The discussions between American and Chinese officials have centered on measures to reduce nuclear risks and haven’t been aimed at negotiating a formal arms-control pact, an effort Beijing has sharply rebuffed in the past,” according to that report. “The Trump administration has begun to highlight the possibility of implementing new verification measures.” “Independent experts say seismic instruments might be placed on or near test sites,” The Journal ‘s story also noted. “Another possibility, which was floated during the Biden administration, is to install radiation-detection equipment at test sites.” NNSA’s announcement about the test at the Nevada National Security Site is certainly an example of the development underway already of new means of verification that could be deployed at sites around the world. The United States has separately accused Russia of conducting lower-yield nuclear testing in secret in the past. Russia is a signatory to the CTBT and had previously ratified it. In 2023, President Vladimir Putin revoked that ratification in line with the provisions of a law passed by the country’s parliament, or Duma. Russian President Vladimir Putin (at left) together with President Trump during their summit in Alaska in 2025. White House President Trump has also floated the idea of the resumption of U.S. nuclear testing in response to Russian and Chinese activities, though other U.S. officials have downplayed the possibility of doing so . The United States is otherwise in the midst of a huge nuclear modernization effort that impacts the air , sea , and land-based legs of the deterrent triad. American authorities are also now pursuing these efforts in an environment fully unbounded by relevant arms control agreements following the sunset of the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) earlier this year. The Russian government has said it is ready to conduct new nuclear tests if the United States pursues this course of action. The last official nuclear test in Russia came in 1990 right before the fall of the Soviet Union. “It takes nuclear expertise to detect nuclear activities and experiments like these [to] ensure America remains unmatched in detection,” NNSA Administrator Brandon Williams said in a statement yesterday in light of the test in Nevada. “The Trump Administration has made it clear that the United States will lead from a position of strength. You cannot evade American innovation. With this experiment, we are sending a clear message: under this administration, America will never be outmatched.” Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post U.S. Mimics “Decoupled” Nuclear Detonation By Blowing Up A Tunnel Conventionally appeared first on TWZ .

title: 吕洪来：中国共产党成为专制极权政党的六大因素
summary: 作者臉書 2026-10-1 一、中国共产党的鼻祖国际共产主义运动就是政治激进运动 国际共产主义运动产生于欧洲。1847年 6月在伦敦由正义者同盟改组成立的以德国工人为主体，吸收英、法、比利时等国工人参加的共产主义者同盟，是世界上第一个以“科学社会主义”为指导思想的“无产阶级革命”政党。它的成立标志着国际共产主义运动的诞生。1848年 2月发表的《共产党宣言》提出“全世界无产者，联合起来！”的战斗口号，国际共产主义运动有了一个明确的理论和实践的纲领。马克思担任共产主义者同盟布
content: 作者臉書 2026-10-1 一、中国共产党的鼻祖国际共产主义运动就是政治激进运动 国际共产主义运动产生于欧洲。1847年 6月在伦敦由正义者同盟改组成立的以德国工人为主体，吸收英、法、比利时等国工人参加的共产主义者同盟，是世界上第一个以“科学社会主义”为指导思想的“无产阶级革命”政党。它的成立标志着国际共产主义运动的诞生。1848年 2月发表的《共产党宣言》提出“全世界无产者，联合起来！”的战斗口号，国际共产主义运动有了一个明确的理论和实践的纲领。马克思担任共产主义者同盟布鲁塞尔区部领导人，1848年马克思受共产主义者同盟中央委员会委托在巴黎建立新的中央委员会﹐当选为主席。 资本主义制度建立之初，由于资本主义经济的高速发展与资本主义制度建设相脱节，产生了社会分配的不合理，对工人合法权益缺乏保护，对资本垄断缺乏有效制约；出现了资本主义生产的绝对垄断、资本主义生产过剩导致的周期性经济危机、资本主义社会工人阶级的绝对贫困化、和工人的高失业率等一系列社会问题。引发了各资本主义国家工人的普遍不满和反抗，资本主义国家的工人运动因此而爆发。国际共产主义运动就是起源于资本主义初期的工人运动。 资本主义社会初期的工人运动，是资本主义社会初期经济发展与制度建设互相脱节所引发的，是工人阶级为维护自身合法权益而进行的反抗和斗争，有些像我们今天的维权运动，工人运动对于维护和提高自身的生存条件，对于促进资本主义制度的不断发展完善起到了积极的推动和促进作用。 但是当资本主义各国的工人运动走向联合，形成国际共产主义运动后，各国的工人运动就成为了政治运动。特别是当马克思的《共产党宣言》成为国际共产主义运动的理论和纲领后，国际共产主义运动就将推翻资本主义制度做为了自己的政治纲领和目标。使一场各国工人抗争性质的维权运动转变成为一场以推翻资本主义制度的为目标的政治运动。本来资本主义制度建立初期出现一些社会问题，是发展中的问题，可以通过工人阶级的反抗斗争迫使资产阶级加以解决，促进资本主义制度的不断完善和发展，事实上历史也正是这样发展的。 但是在马克思主义的影响下：国际共产主义运动却将当时资本主义制度初期产生的一些社会问题绝对化，将资本主义制度妖魔化，主观的判定资本主义制度已经走向灭亡，无产阶级革命的时代已经到来，极端激进的提出要消灭资本、消灭阶级、消灭剥削、消灭私有制，以暴力推翻资本主义制度，实行无产阶级专政，建立公有制社会的极端化政治主张，历史的发展证明这是马克思主义和国际共产主义运动一个致命的错误！ 这种政治上的极端和激进，客观的反映出当时工人阶级做为一个整体在政治上的不成熟。历史无情的证明：那个时期无论是资产阶级还是工人阶级都不可能成熟，都还只能处于发展成熟阶段！当时的工人阶级没有也不可能认识到，资本主义制度还处于发展阶段，处于上升时期，只有资产阶级才是资本主义时代的政治代表。 应当说爆发于19世纪的工人运动，是资本主义制度初期爆发的一场工人阶级争取和维护合法权益的抗争性质的运动。但是由于历史的局限，在马克思主义极端激进思想的指导和鼓动下，演变成为一场以推翻新兴资本主义制度为政治目标的国际共产主义运动。共产党事实上成为了极端激进的政治团体，其提出的：以暴力手段消灭资本、消灭阶级、消灭剥削、消灭私有制，实行无产阶级专政、建立公有制的主张，不仅违背了时代的潮流，违背了历史发展的客观规律，而且必然给人类社会造成无法挽回的灾难！ 二、中国共产党的指导思想决定了其必然走向专制极权 马克思主义是中国共产党的指导思想，马克思主义产生于资本主义社会的初期。卡尔·马克思 (1818—1883) 是马克思主义的创始人，时国际共产主义运动的奠基者。马克思是一个理论家和政治活动家。马克思在哲学、政治经济学方面的研究应当说具有一定的学术价值。但是马克思的共产主义学说和无产阶级革命理论，由于其所处时代的局限，是建立在对资本主义社会初期认识的、以偏概全的荒谬的理论。其主要表现在： 1、由于马克思生活在资本主义社会初期，不可能对资本主义制度，特别是资本主义社会有全面和深刻的了解，更无法预见到资本主义社会后来的成熟和发展，因此马克思不可能对资本主义社会和资本主义制度做出全面、科学的合乎客观规律的科学阐述和论证。 2、马克思将自己所处的资本主义发展时期，误判为资本主义已经开始从鼎盛走向灭亡。这已经被历史的发展证明是对资本主义完全错误的认识，这是由于马克思所生活的时代和历史局限所造成的。马克思将资本主义初期出现的一些社会问题，主观的判定为是资本主义制度固有的问题和资本主义制度无法解决的问题，得出资本主义必然灭亡和必须进行无产阶级革命的错误结论，这同样已经被历史的发展证明是完全错误的！ 20世纪初的中国是一个刚刚摆脱封建专制独裁的社会，根本就没有经历过资本主义发展阶段，没有经历过市场经济和大工业化生存的封闭社会。那时的中国既没有真正成熟的民族资产阶级，也没有什么真正的无产阶级，更不存在资本主义社会制度的一切特征。 如果说当年共产国际（第三国际）扶植成立中国共产党的目的是要在半封建、半殖民地的中国社会进行所谓共产主义革命；那么是毛泽东进一步的将中国共产党的组织形式成功的与中国的封建小农运动相结合；是毛泽东将马列主义的暴力革命理论转变为痞子暴民运动的指导思想；是毛泽东将共产主义运动的绚丽外衣披在了中国痞子暴民运动的身上；中国小农佃农传统的封建思想意识、加上马列主义的暴力革命理论和共产党的严密残酷的组织形式，这三者的结合就成为中国共产党这个痞子暴民组织的精髓。 是毛泽东完成了将中共从一个最初以激进知识分子为主体的，崇尚乌托邦思想的的列宁主义组织，向封建农民为主体的痞子暴民组织的转变；如果说激进的乌托邦组织多少还具有一些理想成分，而痞子和暴民组织则完全是对历史的反动，是对社会秩序和规则的破坏。为什么今天欧洲等发达资本主义国家的工人运动都走上了社会民主道路，唯有北朝鲜、古巴、中国这些落后国家还在坚持共产党的领导和社会主义？就是因为这些招牌更有利于权力垄断和传承，更有利于实行专制极权统治和独裁。 六、中国共产党的国际背景和中国的社会、历史、文化决定了中国共产党必然成为专制极权政党 国际共产主义运动本身的历史局限性、马克思主义的极端和暴力性、列宁主义的政治投机和恐怖性，这些是决定了中国共产党必然成为专制极权政党的政治因素； 20世纪初的中国刚刚结束了长达两千多年的封建帝制，两千多年封建帝制统治，使得封建传统、封建文化、深入几亿中国人的骨髓，这是中国共产党必然成为专制极权政党的历史和文化因素； 由于长期的闭关锁国，当时中国所谓的知识分子就是一群刚刚摆脱了臣民奴隶身份的读书人，对西方现代文明缺乏起码的认知和了解，所谓无产阶级就是刚刚摆脱几千年封建专制束缚，满脑子封建意识的小农和愚民，根本就不懂得什么是民主，什么是民主制度，这是中国共产党必然会成为专制极权政党的社会因素。 刚刚摆脱了几千年封建专制束缚的小农和愚民，在一些激进的读书人带领下，打着极端激进暴力的马列主义旗号，靠着共产国际这个国际恐怖暴力组织的支持，用极端恐怖暴力的手段打土豪、分田地来赢得支持，靠谎言欺骗获得社会同情，在夺得天下后建立起一个一党专制极权统治的社会，这就是中国共产党所领导的中国新民主主义革命的真实写照！ 中国共产党的国际背景和中国的社会、历史、文化决定了中国共产党必然成为专制极权政党，这是一种客观的、历史发展的必然，不能否认中国共产党初创时期，确实有相当一批热血青年和理想主义者加入，这是中国共产党内不断出现政治路线斗争的深层原因，也是后来中共党内能够出现华国锋、胡耀邦、赵紫阳、任仲夷、等党内改革派的重要原因。 本来文化大革命后，一段时期内中国共产党有望回归第二国际路线，但是随着邓小平提出的四项基本原则，随着政治体质改革的破灭，随着改革派领导人的被逐步清洗，今天的中国共产党已经完全被权贵阶层和庞大的错综复杂既得利益集团所控制，因此今天中国共产党的专制极权不仅有其历史的背景和根源，而且又与现实的既得利益牢牢地捆绑了在一起。 中国共产党内部已经很难再出现向胡耀邦、赵紫阳式的理想型的改革派领人物 政治社会历史文化决定了中国共产党必然成为专制极权政党，因此中国共产党的性质即不是哪一个人造成的，也绝不是哪一个人所能改变的，中国共产党在中国的出现所折射的是整个中华民族的不成熟，是面对时髦的蛊惑所表现出来的民族狂热，因此在中国要真正结束中国共产党的统治，靠的不是救世主，而必须是中华民族的真正觉醒。 政治社会历史文化决定了中国共产党必然成为专制极权政党，这即包括中国历史和文化的积淀的因素，又有国际共产主义运动的政治背景，也与我们整个民族的不成熟密不可分；中国共产党成为专制独裁政党，其自身负有不可推卸的政治责任，我们的民族同样负有不可推卸历史责任！没有我们的民族就不会有中国共产党？！ 中国共产党做为一个产生于几千年封建专制统治土壤里的政党、一个由共产国际这样的激进、恐怖、暴力集团扶植的政党、一个由封建小农和暴民组成的政党、一个靠恐怖暴力起家的政党、一个政治目标和奋斗方向完全违背社会历史发展客观规律的乌托邦政党、一个嗜权如命的政党，怎么可能不专制？不独裁？不极权？血腥、残暴、专制、独裁、极权，可以说是中国共产党从一诞生就注定的本质。 今天的中国共产党在经历了几十年的瞎折腾之后，已经成为了一个没有任何理想和信念的政治躯壳，如果说毛泽东时代搞公私合营、大跃进、人民公社、大锅饭这样的瞎折腾，还有一点所谓理想主义的色彩，那么后来的所谓改革开放、发展民营经济、到今天的不搞多党轮流执政、不搞指导思想多元化、不搞“三权鼎立”和两院制、不搞联邦制、不搞私有化；与普世价值和人类文明世界为敌，则都纯粹是为了保住手中的权力和既得利益。 面对这样一个从根源上就是专制极权性质的政党，一个与将权力与既得利益完全捆绑在一起的党国一体的政权，国家和平转型的道路已经走不通，中国共产党内部已经很难再出现向胡耀邦、赵紫阳式的理想型的改革派领人物。中国社会要结束一党专制极权统治，既不可能指望中国共产党主动的放弃手中的权力，还权于民；也很难指望被手无寸铁赤手空拳的普通民众所推翻；要结束中国共产党的一党专制极权统治，中国的政治反对力量只能与世界民主阵营共同携手，走和平革命的道路。 # 香港国安处以“23条”拘捕网媒记者，与8.31事件相关

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2019年9月6日，人们在香港太子港铁站出入口处的悼念墙前献花。

Published 3 小时前

阅读时间: 2 分钟

9月30日有报导引述消息称，香港网媒“Boom News - 爆炸头”创办人邓浩荣被捕。

香港记者协会关注事件，指邓浩荣是首名在《维护国家安全条例》（俗称“23条”）生效后，于公众领域中因该例煽动罪被捕的新闻工作者。

邓浩荣是香港警方国案处近期拘捕行动的被捕者之一。

今年8月31日，有人在港铁太子站外手持花束站立并叫喊口号，警方采取多次执法行动，以涉嫌违反“23条”中“出于煽动意图作出具煽动意图的作为”罪，累计至今拘捕八人。

2019年同日，反修例示威者与乘客发生在地铁列车内发生冲突，大批警员到场执法过程受质疑，被称为“8·31事件”。

## 警方迄今拘捕累计八人

9月30日早上，《星岛日报》[率先报导](https://www.stheadline.com/breaking-news/3620845/%E8%AD%A6%E5%9C%8B%E5%AE%89%E8%99%95%E6%8B%98%E7%B6%B2%E5%AA%92%E4%BA%BA%E7%88%86%E7%82%B8%E9%A0%AD-%E6%B6%89%E7%99%BC%E4%BD%88%E5%81%87%E6%B6%88%E6%81%AF%E7%85%BD%E5%8B%95)邓浩荣被捕，指他涉嫌发布假消息煽动。报导附上多张穿着国安警（NSD，即National Security Department）背心警员押解邓浩荣的相片；相中的邓浩荣被锁上手扣，双手被反扣在背后。

至同日深夜，警方[发新闻稿](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202609/30/P2026093000849.htm)表示，有人于8月31日晚上在港铁太子站外手持花束站立，叫喊“具煽动性的口号”及涉嫌散播假消息。

9月30日，警方以涉嫌违反《维护国家安全条例》第24条，即“出于煽动意图作出具煽动意图的作为”罪，拘捕一男一女，并在行动前取得法庭搜查令，搜查其住所及检取证物。两人被扣留调查。

综合本地传媒引述的消息，被捕者是邓浩荣及牙医李盈姿。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2020年8月31日，在太子港铁站外，警员在现场驻守。

据报，邓浩荣毕业于香港中文大学电脑科学系。他营运网媒“Boom News 爆炸头”，活跃于 YouTube、Facebook、Instagram 及 Threads等社交平台，主要以独立记者直播及报导。

翻查社交平台片段，“Boom News 爆炸头”当晚曾访问被截查的李盈姿，并提到有市民“带花悼念”及“未明未知8·31真相”等。

警方国安处表示，早前已分别于9月3日、27日及28日采行动，以相关罪名共拘捕三男三女，全数已获保释候查。

据报，9月3日的被捕人士为“旺角鸠呜团”成员陈冠旭及前区议员冯竞文，另一人为谭姓男子。

警方强调，所谓“831事件”并无事实根据，形容有人藉此散播谎言、攻击港府及抹黑警队，企图以危害社会安宁的手段达致其政治目的；又指会继续拘捕行动。

## 记协关注事件

香港记者协会[发声明](https://www.facebook.com/HKJA.official/posts/pfbid02wJ9s6PADNJqZkXZrGFFeeCrVfmr9WvpadLDVUxbqejBubKksnqmSQNZKbL9S4LcNl)表示，有传媒引述消息人士透露，邓浩荣被捕与其直播“8·31”活动相关；相关指控令不少前线新闻工作者感忧虑，因直播是如实报道现场发生事态，而在公众地方记录及直播现况，是基本新闻工作。

记协指出，若记者仅因在现场报道，或报道内容与官方说法不同而被捕，所有前线记者日后采访公众活动时都会承受同样风险。

记协要求警方公开交代邓浩荣被指触犯法律的具体行为，以及拘捕是否与他的采访及报道工作有关。

BBC中文向警方提出相关查询，至截稿未有回覆。

title: Political Prisoners Watch: Five Democracy Advocates Targeted for Seeking Help Abroad
summary: Political Prisoners Watch: Five Democracy Advocates Targeted for Seeking Help Abroad zevans@freedom… Thu, 10/01/2026 - 15:28 Type Perspectives Image Countries Vietnam Hong Kong Iran Azerbaijan Egypt Issues Authoritarian Reach Authors (Perso
content: Political Prisoners Watch: Five Democracy Advocates Targeted for Seeking Help Abroad zevans@freedom… Thu, 10/01/2026 - 15:28 Type Perspectives Image Countries Vietnam Hong Kong Iran Azerbaijan Egypt Issues Authoritarian Reach Authors (Person reference) Brian Tronic Page blocks From left to right: Pham Chi Dung, Anar Mammadli, Joshua Wong, Mohammed Seifzadeh, Gasser Abdel Razek (Photo Credits: Pham Chi Dung Facebook, Wikimedia Commons, Center for Human Rights in Iran, Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights) On September 2, prominent Hong Kong democracy activist  Joshua Wong pleaded guilty to charges under the territory’s notorious National Security Act—the second time he has faced prison time under the Beijing-imposed law. Having already been imprisoned since November 2020, he now faces the possibility of another lengthy sentence simply for demanding that Hong Kongers have a voice in their own government. Joshua’s detention has been widely recognized as emblematic of the Chinese Communist Party’s increasing restrictions on freedom in and the autonomy of Hong Kong. However, his case is also an example of an important but less visible phenomenon: to hide truth about their abuses, dictatorial regimes are criminalizing the act of talking to the outside world. The allegations against Joshua included meetings in the United States with Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi and then Senator Marco Rubio. Unfortunately, activists around the globe are facing similar charges. The following cases highlight the efforts of repressive regimes to shut down engagement with foreign democracies and international bodies that have made protecting democracy part of their mission. Vietnamese journalist Pham Chi Dung was detained after petitioning members of the European Parliament (EP) to pressure Vietnam over its human rights record. In 2019, he  wrote to EP members asking them to postpone ratification of the EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement until Vietnamese authorities made human rights improvements, and made a similar appeal in a  video featured at an event hosted by a British EP member. Two days later, he was arrested. UN experts  noted that the arrest “appears to be an act of reprisal for his human rights advocacy.” Dung was later  sentenced to 15 years in prison for “conducting antistate propaganda,” and he remains imprisoned today. Mohammad Seifzadeh , a human rights lawyer in Iran, wrote a  letter with other human rights activists to UN Secretary General António Guterres in December 2022, asking him to respond to the Iranian regime’s execution of peaceful protesters. Just a few months later, as a result of the letter, he was convicted of “propaganda against the system” and “spreading false information” and sentenced to a year in prison (though his sentence was eventually  suspended for medical reasons). Azerbaijani activist Anar Mammadli , chair of the Election Monitoring and Democracy Studies Centre (EMDS), was arrested in 2024 a few weeks after  calling on Azerbaijani authorities to release political prisoners and respect fundamental rights at events hosted by the UN Human Rights Council and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE). A group of UN officials  expressed “serious concerns that Mammadli’s detention and prosecution may be in retaliation for his human rights work and his engagement with UN mechanisms.” In 2026, Anar was sentenced to 13 years in prison on a variety of baseless charges. In November 2020, three staff of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, including Executive Director Gasser Abdel Razek , were arrested a  few days after discussing human rights issues with 13 foreign ambassadors and diplomats. While they were released a few weeks later, they were  placed under a travel ban that  remains in place to this day.
