title: Moscow Tries to Tie Its Partners to Putin’s Worldview
summary: Executive Summary: A September article by the Valdai Discussion Club argues that non-alignment no longer exists and that the West treats neutrality and confrontation alike, leaving governments in the Global South no choice but to pick a sid
content: Executive Summary: A September article by the Valdai Discussion Club argues that non-alignment no longer exists and that the West treats neutrality and confrontation alike, leaving governments in the Global South no choice but to pick a side. The claim originates with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who attends Valdai’s annual meetings, and Russian officials have pressed the same argument on a number of countries including Armenia, Serbia, India, and the United Arab Emirates. Moscow has little to offer the countries it courts. Russia plays a secondary role even within BRICS, depends on the People’s Republic of China and Iran, and cannot match the benefits of trade with the West. On September 10, Russian political scientist and Valdai Discussion Club Program Director Timofei Bordachev penned an article titled “Non-alignment no longer exists” ( Valdai Club , September 10). He argues that even insignificant manifestations of independence by governments of the “Global South” are “strikes against the interests of the United States and Europe,” which the West tolerates only because “at this time it simply is not strong enough to regain control of the world economy and politics.” He concludes that “there is no reason to think that the West’s policy toward those who have entered into confrontation with it and those who talk about their neutrality is structurally different” ( Valdai Club , September 10). The argument carries institutional weight because Valdai is not an independent research institution. Russian President Vladimir Putin attends its annual meetings, where his keynote addresses are published on the Kremlin’s official website ( President of Russia , October 2, 2025). Independent Russian and Western journalists describe the club as a showcase for Kremlin foreign policy and note its ties to the Presidential Administration ( Istories Media, September 15). The pattern follows Putin setting out a narrative, Valdai analysts giving it an analytical framing, and Russian officials repeating it in diplomatic form (see EDM , June 5, 2023). Bordachev’s argument rests on a conflation of concepts. The Valdai analysts acknowledge that economic competition is inescapable in relations between large countries. From this, they draw two conclusions. First, that the West treats competitors as enemies. Second, that it will suppress any manifestations of independence by these “enemies” regardless of their conduct, simply because they are sovereign. The view originates with Putin. The concept of the “unconditional enemy” seeking to destroy Russia because of its very existence was one of the main justifications for his aggression, which he can then present as “defense.” At the end of August, Putin declared that killer whales in the Arctic are eating bears and that this explains “why we are conducting the special military operation” ( Meduza , August 29). He had earlier made similar but less metaphorical claims, asserting that the West has a single goal—to dismantle Russia and “lord it over its constituent parts and bring them under the Western control” ( Kommersant , February 26, 2023). The concept serves two purposes. Domestically, it justifies expansionist wars. In foreign policy, it serves to convince allies to “choose a side” in the confrontation between Russia and the West. Since, by Russian logic, the West is prepared to destroy its competitors regardless of their actions, those countries have no alternative but to choose Russia. Russian officials advance the same argument in practice. In May, Russian Presidential Aide Yuri Ushakov criticized Armenia for continuing to “sit on two chairs,” presenting its balancing act as an obstacle to relations with Moscow ( Interfax , May 7). More often, officials follow the Valdai line and blame the West. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has argued that the European Union turns Serbia against Russia and forces Belgrade into an artificial choice between East and West ( Daily Storm , February 19, 2018). The claim is that the West, not Moscow, leaves these states no alternative. Valdai authors apply this logic directly to India and the United Arab Emirates. Brazilian political scientist and Valdai Club author Fabiano Melnichuk affirms that it is precisely “American assertiveness and associated neo-colonial practices that make it necessary for traditionally pragmatic countries to choose a side.” According to him, “the optimal way for both India and the UAE to restore strategic maneuverability and balance their relations with the West is to strengthen their commitment to BRICS,” particularly “in sectors where a partnership with the West appears most attractive” ( Valdai Club , September 9). [1] This is not the first time the Kremlin has attempted to force India and other countries to take Russia’s side and determine “which direction they take and with whom” ( Argumenty i fakty , October 22, 2022). Kremlin strategists do not hide that they are trying to manipulate their foreign counterparts by playing on their colonial past ( Valdai Club , April 14, 2022). Moscow cannot offer its partners any real alternatives. The same analysts admit that BRICS today confronts myriad crises, particularly in relations between the UAE and Iran ( Valdai Club , September 9). The People’s Republic of China (PRC), not Russia, leads BRICS, and Moscow is growing more dependent on Beijing (see EDM , November 13, 2024; The Big Asia , September 14). The PRC has proven a less-than-reliable partner for Moscow. Following Putin’s meeting with PRC President Xi Jinping at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit, the contract for the construction of the Power of Siberia 2  gas pipeline was not signed, while a major fire at the Amur gas chemical complex underscored the risks for PRC companies investing in Russian projects (see EDM , September 8). Moscow’s reliance on even such odious partners as Iran is also growing. As early as 2023, independent analysts noted that multi-billion-dollar investments by Gazprom in Iran were not paying off ( Carnegie Politika , May 22, 2023). This has not prevented the Valdai Club from publishing odes to Iran dedicated to “understanding the legacy” of the late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in relations with Russia. The text abounds in complimentary rhetoric and declarations regarding “joint efforts to combat unipolar hegemony, counter unilateral coercive measures, and establish an independent financial infrastructure” ( Valdai Club , September 2). Cooperation is primarily evident in the military sphere, and even there the direction is reversed. According to Western journalists, Iran is not so much supplying weaponry to Russia as asking Moscow to sell it advanced Geran strike drones for use in the war against Israel and the United States ( Financial Times , September 14). The Kremlin has virtually no investment projects capable of outweighing the benefits of trade with the West in the eyes of its partners. Sanctions create additional problems in cooperation with Russia. Against this background, Moscow’s persistent calls for partners to “choose a side” might backfire. The leaders of India and other states are unlikely to believe the West seeks to destroy them at any cost. If the choice becomes unavoidable, most of Russia’s current partners might opt for a completely different side. Note: [1] BRICS is a loose political-economic grouping originally comprised of Brazil, Russia, India, the People’s Republic of China, and South Africa, but now comprising 11 member states ( BRICS Info , accessed September 9). The post Moscow Tries to Tie Its Partners to Putin’s Worldview appeared first on Jamestown .

title: 蔡楚：我心中的李建华（一平）
summary: 《又是一年秋风凉》 “阿柴作曲、沙哑大叔作词” 又是一年秋色染上夕阳 我们也渐渐变了模样 人的一生总有相逢 也有散场 总有几个人一辈子难忘 李建华（笔名一平，1952年－2024年12月30日）知名诗人、散文家、编辑、文化评论家以及人权活动家。他是独立中文笔会的31位共同创办人之一，长期致力于文学创作与推动言论自由亊业。 文革中，他于1968年初中毕业，1969年被下放到黑龙江建设兵团，当了六年“知识青年”。1975－1979年，他在北京师范学院中文系学习，毕业后在北京外贸学
content: 《又是一年秋风凉》 “阿柴作曲、沙哑大叔作词” 又是一年秋色染上夕阳 我们也渐渐变了模样 人的一生总有相逢 也有散场 总有几个人一辈子难忘   李建华（笔名一平，1952年－2024年12月30日）知名诗人、散文家、编辑、文化评论家以及人权活动家。他是独立中文笔会的31位共同创办人之一，长期致力于文学创作与推动言论自由亊业。 文革中，他于1968年初中毕业，1969年被下放到黑龙江建设兵团，当了六年“知识青年”。1975－1979年，他在北京师范学院中文系学习，毕业后在北京外贸学院教中文。1989年后，李建华先生因“六四事件”失去高级讲师教职，被迫先后流亡波兰和美国，曾在波兰亚当密斯凯维支大学（Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań）和美国康奈尔大学（Cornell University）教授中文。2001年笔会创会后，他於2003-2005年任首届财务秘书，2011年起仼狱中作家委员会顾问直至逝世，其间于2016-2018年岀任本会理事兼自由写作和文学交流委员会主任。2004－2020年，他还在美国“中国人权”的副刊“人与人权”担仼编辑。 2024年12月30日，一平在美国纽约州伊萨卡市突发重疾，不幸逝世，享年72岁。 一平在半个世纪的创作生涯中，留下了诗歌、散文、文学评论、剧本等各类作品数百篇。他的写作风格被评价为诚实、清醒、内敛，拒绝虚饰，多关注历史的沉重与流亡者的精神世界。 2004年，因笔会在美国申请非营利组织的法律注册及建立银行账户的过程需要，我受时任会长刘晓波的委托，曾与李洁一起先后三次到纽约州，与一平、李进进和Jennifer会面，共同完成了这项工作。具体而言，一平和李进进律师完成了法律签署与注册登记。而Jennifer和李洁协助处理了文书，包括撰写复杂的全英文、美国国税局（IRS）非营利组织免税申请表格、整理组织材料和追踪审批进度，最终得到美国国税局的批准。这反映了当时笔会在海外推动组织正式法律注册过程中的分工合作。一平也因在注册工作中的踏实认真风格，受到会员们的尊敬，被文友们称为笔会的“注册人“。 2004年11月14日，我接到笔会义工Jennifer的电子邮件，同时抄送了万之、一平和李洁。Jennifer在邮件组中说：“收到了一封来自美国国税局（IRS）的信，内容涉及 ICPC 的非营利组织资格。负责处理 ICPC 档案的官员肯尼迪先生（Mr. Kennedy）提出了6个问题，我们需要在 2004 年 12 月 1 日之前予以答复。“Jennifer提出了回复意见，我们五人立即在邮件组中展开了讨论，并及时回复了肯尼迪先生（Mr. Kennedy）提出的问题。Jennifer还说：”我认为，我们距离最终获得 ICPC 的非营利组织资格已越来越近了。“果然Jennifer在年底前通知我和一平去纽约，为笔会在纽约的银行建立了账户。记得那年冬天，纽约的街道很滑，一平和我都几次几乎滑倒，但是总算完成了刘晓波的委托。 2005年1月21日，一平作为笔会财务秘书，曾给会长刘晓波写信说：“希望你能提醒大家，支出费用一定需要单据，没有单据不能报销。这一条，我们必须坚持，否则没法保证财务清楚，希望大家给以支持，自觉遵守。大家的生活都不稳定，许多事情顾及不上，非常可以谅解。但事情涉及资金来源，也涉及保障财务规则，因此需要大家多麻烦一点。为保障财务规则，如果今后开销没有单据，财务不给报销，请大家能谅解。如同意此建议，希望加上你的意见，转发给有关人员。“ 晓波回复说：“对不起给你带来工作的不便。下不为例。上次开会的餐费是特殊情况，那个画家村本来不经营餐馆，所以最后没有发票。也应该让他们写个手写的收据。至于理事们的旅行费用没有单据，显然是王怡或老廖二人把机票弄丢了。你可以正式通知各位以及理事会，以后无发票不给报销。这要成为财务上严格的规定。“此事说明一平坚守财务凭证清楚，保障财务规则必须遵守的踏实认真态度，为笔会初期，督促理事遵守财务规则，起到了表率作用。 2005年3日10日，贝岭给笔会理事和会员写信，要求写e信或打电话关心当时流亡美国的会员张慧敏，张慧敏不仅失业，还因她怀疑遭到中方的电磁波攻击，终日陷於恐惧之中。贝岭因此希望，在她出现危急的情形下，找到钱或捐钱帮助她、安排她的住处，等等。 由于当时晓波在中国大陆常被警方传唤，因此委托我任理事会网络会议的召集人兼任组织秘书，所以3日11日，晓波回复我说：“她现在的精神状态能胜任什么工作，还是私人募捐帮助她吧。如果你和迈平觉得她可以做点什么，你们在外面，更了解情况，只要你俩觉得可以，就行。” 3日12日，一平给贝岭写信说：“昨天给你发了我和蔡楚帮助张慧敏的倡议，征求你的意见，因为我们对张慧敏的情况不是很了解。先几次是乱码，之后我用另外的信箱再发，没接到回音，想你读到了。晚上给你打过电话，但没有人接。今天早上看到你给理事会和会员的信，谢谢你转给我。你提出在张慧敏危急的时候，给以经济帮助；根据你所谈的情况，和你所说帮助她到“好大学教书”，“读博士学位”等，说明现在张慧敏还没有到危急的状态。因此，我们的捐助倡议暂时就不做了，我们都看一看能否帮助她到到大学找到工作。我和张慧敏只通了2次电话，我对她的情况不很了解。感谢你对她的关心、帮助。我也会继续关注她的情况，也希望更多的人关心她。 当时，给张慧敏打电话的有我、万之、孟浪、一平、朱学渊，等等。这件事是一平与我的再次合作，不仅表现了一平办事的一贯踏实认真态度，还表现了他对会员的尊重和爱心。一平因此而受到会员的普遍尊敬，后来他相继当选理事并兼自由写作和文学交流委员会主任，成为独立中文笔会的骨干成员。 2008年2月14日， 一平给笔会理事会写信推荐李进进和李江琳入会，由于开始把李江琳的推荐人错填成当时的会长郑义，一平又去信纠正。此事同样说明一平的认真态度，为笔会在纽约地区的发展引入了新的人才。 翻阅近百封我与一平生前的电子邮件，并拜读了一平与高尔泰老师、郑义、北明、王康等文友们的几百封电子邮件，使我进一步理解了一平。虽然我身居美国南方，又常年陷入事务性工作中，自然缺乏与一平切磋诗歌的机会，但我这次从电子邮件中，看到一平思想中的不少闪光点，他同文友们对爱和美与文学、艺术、宗教、科技、政治及社会等领域之间的关系探讨，使我眼界大开，为之赞叹。 比如，一平说：“思考是文明的活力“，又说：“我的体会，美是文明的终极实现，但文明也由此盛极而衰，因为生命背离其存在的本真。“ 这个洞察极其深刻，直指现代文明的核心危机：当代文明正在陷入一种由“技术与消费主义异化”带来的“盛极而衰”，其根本原因确实在于生命背离了它最本真的存在状态。 是的，思考是文明的活力，而“保持独立思考，在自己的位置上呼唤‘重返本真’。”就是我们共同的选择和心声。 望着一平并未远去的背影，我用一首俄罗斯电影插曲《朋友》来为喜爱俄罗斯文学的一平送别：“我亲爱的手风琴你轻轻的唱，让我们来回忆少年的时光，春天驾着鹤群的翅膀，飞到了遥远的地方……温暖我们的心，那道路引导我们奔向前方……” 一位做事踏实认真又慧眼独具的一平，永远活在蔡楚心中。 2026年7月13日

title: Open brief aan Donald Trump van een Oeigoers slachtoffer dat 19 familieleden verloor door de Chinese genocide
summary: Aan de President van de Verenigde Staten, Donald Trump: Waarom heeft het Court of the Citizens of the World een arrestatiebevel uitgevaardigd tegen Xi Jinping? “De wereld wordt niet vernietigd door degenen die kwaad doen, maar door degenen
content: Aan de President van de Verenigde Staten, Donald Trump: Waarom heeft het Court of the Citizens of the World een arrestatiebevel uitgevaardigd tegen Xi Jinping? “De wereld wordt niet vernietigd door degenen die kwaad doen, maar door degenen die toeschouwen zonder iets te doen.” — Albert Einstein Geachte President Donald Trump, Mijn naam is Abdurehim Gheni Uyghur. Ik ben een Oeigoer die 19 familieleden heeft verloren als gevolg van het systematische genocidebeleid van de Chinese overheid in bezet Oost-Turkestan. In juli 2024 heb ik in Den Haag getuigd tegen de misdaden van Xi Jinping voor het "Court of the Citizens of the World" (Volkstribunaal). Nu u zich voorbereidt om in Washington aan de onderhandelingstafel te zitten met Xi Jinping, de president van de Volksrepubliek China, beschouw ik het als mijn menselijke plicht om u en de Amerikaanse beleidsmakers te herinneren aan een cruciale historische waarheid — een waarheid die rechtstreeks raakt aan internationale gerechtigheid, menselijke waardigheid en de toekomst van de vrije wereld. De prijs van gerechtigheid: Politiebedreigingen en mijn vader die werd doodgemotterd in een concentratiekamp Op 6 juli 2024 — slechts twee dagen voordat ik op 8 juli getuigde voor het Volkstribunaal in Den Haag — haalde de Chinese politie mijn vader en broer uit een concentratiekamp in het district Wushu (Wushi), prefectuur Aksu, in bezet Oost-Turkestan. Onder extreme druk dwongen ze hen om mij te bellen en uitten ze directe dreigementen om te voorkomen dat ik zou getuigen. Ik liet mij niet intimideren, stond voor de rechters en presenteerde het bewijsmateriaal dat de misdaden van Xi Jinping onthulde. De prijs voor het laten horen van de stem van gerechtigheid was echter verwoestend hoog. Als vergelding wierp het Chinese regime mijn vader en broer opnieuw in het concentratiekamp. Op 16 september 2024 bezweek mijn vader aan de gevolgen van folteringen en overleed hij in het kamp. Zijn overlijden werd onafhankelijk onderzocht en bevestigd door journalist Shohret Hoshur van Radio Free Asia. Dit is niet alleen de persoonlijke tragedie van mijn familie; het is een levende momentopname van de miljoenen Oeigoeren die lijden en sterven door martelingen in concentratiekampen. Het is het keiharde bewijs van hoe wreed, meedogenloos en minachtend tegenover het internationaal recht het communistische regime onder leiding van Xi Jinping werkelijk is. Xi Jinping: Een aangeklaagde misdadiger in het arrestatiebevel van het Court of the Citizens of the World Onder voorzitterschap van Zak Yacoob, voormalig rechter aan het Constitutioneel Hof van Zuid-Afrika, en samen met vooraanstaande internationale aanklagers en juristen waaronder ambassadeur Stephen J. Rapp, voormalig buitengewoon ambassadeur van de VS voor Oorlogsmisdaden, onderzocht het tribunaal in Den Haag honderden getuigenissen. Op 12 juli 2024 vaardigde het tribunaal op grond van het Statuut van Rome van het Internationaal Strafhof formeel een arrestatiebevel uit tegen Xi Jinping, met de volgende verklaring: "Het Court of the Citizens of the World heeft voldoende wettige gronden gevonden om Xi Jinping te beschuldigen en een arrestatiebevel tegen hem uit te vaardigen voor de volgende misdrijven: Misdaden tegen de menselijkheid in Tibet, te weten: 1. Gedwongen overdracht van kinderen 2. Gevangenzetting of andere ernstige beroving van de lichamelijke vrijheid 3. Vervolging van de Tibetaanse bevolking; En genocide en misdaden tegen de menselijkheid begaan tegen de Oeigoerse bevolking in de Autonome Oeigoerse Regio Xinjiang (XUAR), te weten: 1. Genocide 2. Gevangenzetting of ernstige beroving van de vrijheid 3. Foltering 4. Verkrachting en seksueel geweld (inclusief gedwongen sterilisatie) 5. Gedwongen overdracht van Oeigoerse kinderen 6. Gedwongen verplaatsing en dwangarbeid 7. Systematische vervolging 8. Gedwongen verdwijning. Het Court of the Citizens of the World roept de internationale gemeenschap en alle overheden op om een arrestatiebevel uit te vaardigen tegen de president van de Volksrepubliek China, een formele gerechtelijke procedure te starten en maatregelen te nemen om de dader aan te houden." Een waarschuwing aan de wereld vanuit een tragedie van 70 jaar Wij, het Oeigoerse volk, ondergaan al meer dan 70 jaar de onderdrukking van de Chinese Communistische Partij, de bezetting van ons vaderland en grootschalige schendingen van de mensenrechten. De tragedie waar de Oeigoeren vandaag de dag voor staan, is niet alleen het lijden van één enkel volk — het is een dringende waarschuwing aan de gehele wereld. Als China's hoogtechnologische autoritarisme en door de staat geïnitieerde genocide vandaag niet worden gestopt, zal het bittere lot van de Oeigoeren morgen de toekomst worden van vele andere naties en democratische samenlevingen. Een oproep aan President Trump en westerse democratieën Mijnheer de President, ik dring er bij u op aan om de westerse democratieën te verenigen tot een vastberaden front tegen de existentiële dreiging die uitgaat van het Chinese communistische regime, en zo de wereldwijde vrede en veiligheid te waarborgen. Een machtige natie zoals de Verenigde Staten toont haar ware grootheid pas wanneer zij rotsvast aan de kant van gerechtigheid en menselijke waardigheid staat. Tijdens uw aanstaande ontmoeting doe ik een respectvol beroep op u om: 1. Niet te vergeten dat Xi Jinping een pleger van genocide is, zoals oordeelde een internationaal tribunaal, en dat achter het Haagse arrestatiebevel de stemmen schuilgaan van miljoenen slachtoffers; 2. De Oeigoerse Genocide tot een niet-onderhandelbare prioriteit te maken op uw diplomatieke agenda, en krachtig de sluiting van alle concentratiekampen, de onmiddellijke vrijlating van onschuldige Oeigoeren en het beëindigen van staatsdwangarbeid te eisen; 3. Daadkrachtig leiderschap te tonen om de wereld te beschermen tegen China's expansiedrift en totalitaire wreedheden. De wereld van vandaag staat voor een ernstige historische test tussen hen die de gerechtigheid verdedigen en hen die zwijgen voor het aangezicht van de gruwelen. Omwille van de gerechtigheid en de menselijkheid: vergeet nooit dat Xi Jinping een formeel aangeklaagde genocidemisdadiger is! Met hoogachting, Abdurehim Gheni Uyghur 23 september 2026 | Nederland 中文版本

title: F-35 Canopy And Weapons-Bay Door Loss To China: Separating Fact From Fiction
summary: Chinese authorities have reportedly taken possession of an F-35 cockpit canopy and weapons-bay door that were inexplicably diverted to Hong Kong while being shipped from Australia to the United States. The incident appears to have left phys
content: Chinese authorities have reportedly taken possession of an F-35 cockpit canopy and weapons-bay door that were inexplicably diverted to Hong Kong while being shipped from Australia to the United States. The incident appears to have left physical components that incorporate aspects of the fighter’s low-observable design in the hands of a country that has spent years doing whatever it could to gain information on the aircraft and America’s stealth technology secrets in general. So, what does all this mean? Let’s put it in perspective. The parts in question were being shipped by UPS from Australia to the United States in late May, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg . The components from a Royal Australian Air Force F-35A were being sent to the United States for inspection and possible repair or disposal. A Royal Australian Air Force F-35A from 75 Squadron taxiing at RAAF Base Tindal, Northern Territory. Australian Defense Force F-35 sustainment procedures explicitly cover the movement of F-35 parts, including unserviceable components, through the program’s logistics network. The U.S. Air Force’s transportation guidance directs F-35 shipments outside the Defense Transportation System to follow approved Joint Program Office procedures. In other words, moving an unserviceable Australian F-35 component to the United States for inspection, repair, or disposition is consistent with the normal sustainment process. What is highly unusual is where this particular shipment ended up. F-35 components moving through an established international logistics system apparently stopped in South Korea, and were then routed to Hong Kong. Chinese authorities subsequently took possession of the parts and have not returned them, according to the sources cited by Bloomberg . F-35 canopy component replacement at Luke Air Force Base, Arizona. U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Ridge Shan Secretary of War Pete Hegseth autographs the weapons bay door of an F-35 at Lockheed Martin Air Force Plant 4, in Fort Worth, Texas. DoW photo by U.S. Navy Petty Officer 1st Class Alexander Kubitza “For security reasons, we can’t discuss the status of specific shipments or our shipping procedures,” Lockheed Martin told us in response to a request for clarification about the incident. The company added that it “follows all U.S. regulations established by the Department of War and regulated by the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) regarding the shipment of aircraft components. Our teams handle every shipment with the utmost diligence and safeguards to ensure the integrity of the F-35 program and the security of our allied partners.” The Pentagon’s F-35 Joint Program Office has acknowledged a “shipment issue” involving F-35 components and said U.S. authorities and industry partners are working to recover them and investigate what happened. Lockheed Martin, UPS, and the Pentagon have not publicly provided a detailed account of how the shipment was diverted or what happened to the parts after they reached Hong Kong. Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles also confirmed that Canberra was aware of the incident and was working with the United States and Lockheed Martin. Acting Prime Minister and Minister for Defense, Richard Marles, accompanied by Chief of Air Force Air Marshal Stephen Chappell at RAAF Base Edinburgh, South Australia. Australian Defense Force Marles has sought to play down the potential security implications of the components, saying his understanding was that the shipment did not contain sensitive equipment or sensitive parts. That does not by itself answer the more specific question of what could potentially be learned from these particular pieces of an F-35. After all, not every physical component of an F-35 is necessarily highly classified or capable of revealing meaningful information about the aircraft’s design. At the same time, a cockpit canopy and weapons-bay door involve structures, materials, interfaces, tolerances, and treatments that all have to work within the aircraft’s low-observable design. If radar-absorbing material or other specialized treatments remain on the components, that could potentially make them far more sensitive from a technological exploitation standpoint. The condition of the parts is also unknown. We do not know how much of their coatings or other treatments remain intact, whether Chinese authorities have examined them, or what information could actually be extracted from them in their current state. Above all else, there is little specific information in the public domain about what F-35-related technical information Chinese intelligence already has acquired over the years, what physical components or materials it may already possess, or what additional information could be gained through espionage, cyber operations, industrial access, observation of deployed aircraft, or other means. Without these facts, it is impossible to gauge what damage could have been done by this loss. Still, viewed in a vacuum of those unknowns, simply having an F-35 canopy and weapons-bay door in Chinese possession represents a significant loss of control over sensitive physical hardware — there is no way around that reality — and the severity of that loss could be substantial depending on the physical state of the parts. The circumstances are particularly sensitive because, as we mentioned in the opening of this article, China has pursued multiple avenues for acquiring information on the F-35 for many years , with publicly documented cases involving cyber operations, technical information, supply chains, and human expertise. Some aspects of China’s subsequent stealth aircraft designs have also prompted comparisons with U.S. aircraft, although claims that China simply ‘cloned’ entire aircraft are not supported by the available evidence. China And The F- 35 : A History Of Espionage In 2014, U.S. authorities charged Chinese businessman Su Bin with conspiring with two other Chinese hackers to break into the computer systems of U.S. defense contractors. Prosecutors alleged that the group targeted information on aircraft including the F-35 and F-22 . The alleged hacking campaign ran from 2009 to 2013. Su Bin later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to nearly four years in prison. The Justice Department’s 2026 case against former Air Force fighter pilot Gerald “Runner” Brown connects the two cases . Prosecutors allege that Brown used a co-conspirator to negotiate his work training Chinese military pilots with Su Bin. Brown, a retired U.S. Air Force major who spent more than 24 years in the service, subsequently worked as a contract simulator instructor training U.S. military pilots on the A-10 and F-35. In February 2026, the Justice Department charged him with providing and conspiring to provide unauthorized defense services to Chinese military pilots. CASE UPDATE from @NewYorkFBI : Former U.S. Air Force Pilot Arrested for Providing Defense Services to the Chinese Military https://t.co/JhwhJHS83v @FBILouisville @FBIIndianapolis and @FBILosAngeles provided assistance in this case. pic.twitter.com/3KElqci05y — FBI (@FBI) February 25, 2026 According to the criminal complaint, Brown traveled to China in December 2023, where he allegedly began training People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) personnel. Prosecutors say he also answered questions about the U.S. Air Force for three hours on his first day in China. Brown has been charged, and the allegations have not been adjudicated. He is one of multiple former Western aviators alleged to have provided training services and/or intelligence to Beijing . The Honeywell case provides yet another example, this time involving the defense industry’s supply of technical information. In 2021, the State Department reached a $13-million administrative settlement with Honeywell over alleged violations of the Arms Export Control Act and International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Honeywell had voluntarily disclosed alleged unauthorized exports and retransfers of ITAR-controlled technical data. The case involved 71 engineering drawings containing dimensions, geometries and layouts for manufacturing castings and finished parts used across multiple aircraft, engines and military systems. The State Department said the unauthorized exports and retransfers involved Canada, Ireland, Mexico, China, and Taiwan. Among the systems covered by the drawings were components associated with the F-35 and F-22. The case did not allege that Honeywell deliberately sought to provide China with sensitive military technology; rather, it concerned alleged violations of export-control requirements. A U.S. Air Force F-22 (nearest camera) flies alongside an F-35A. U.S. Air Force photo by Lt. Sam Eckholm There has also been a physical supply-chain precedent. In 2022, F-35 deliveries were temporarily halted after the Pentagon discovered that a magnet in the aircraft’s Honeywell-built turbomachine pumps —which provide critical power functions to the jet — contained a cobalt and samarium alloy produced in China. The material itself was not considered a security or flight-safety threat, but the discovery demonstrated how difficult it can be to maintain complete visibility over a global supply chain involving thousands of companies and multiple tiers of subcontractors. Taken together, these cases demonstrate several different pathways through which China has appeared in the F-35 security story: cyber theft, unauthorized technical-data transfers, supply-chain exposure, and alleged exploitation of former Western military expertise. The Hong Kong incident would add another major category: physical access to actual F-35 components. These are only some of the publicly documented examples. There is no public way to know the full extent of information or physical material Chinese intelligence may have acquired over the years, but is very likely far larger in scope than what is available in the open source. Chinese Access Concerns Have Shaped F-35 Export Policy The security issues surrounding the F-35 are significant enough that concerns about China have affected not only how the United States protects F-35 technology, but where Washington is willing to export the aircraft in the first place . The proposed sale of F-35s to the United Arab Emirates became deeply entangled in U.S. concerns about Abu Dhabi’s growing military and technology relationship with China. A 34th Expeditionary Fighter Squadron F-35A conducts inflight refueling above the United Arab Emirates. U.S. Air Force photo by Tech. Sgt. Kat Justen Washington had approved a potential package involving 50 F-35As, but U.S. officials and lawmakers expressed concerns about Chinese intelligence activity and technology in the UAE. Among the broader concerns were Chinese telecommunications infrastructure and the possibility of Chinese military or intelligence access to facilities associated with advanced U.S. weapons. A Congressional U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission report later cited the potential presence of Chinese intelligence collection capabilities and military facilities in the UAE as risks to the proposed F-35 sale. The issue has now resurfaced with Saudi Arabia . The State Department recently approved a potential $24.3-billion sale to the Kingdom involving 48 F-35s and associated equipment. But U.S. intelligence agencies have reportedly warned that China’s military and technology relationship with Saudi Arabia could create opportunities for Beijing to obtain sensitive F-35 information. According to reporting based on U.S. officials familiar with intelligence assessments, a Defense Intelligence Agency report raised concerns about Chinese military access to Saudi bases, Chinese technology in Saudi telecommunications infrastructure, and whether secure facilities could be maintained for F-35 operations. The assessments also questioned whether Saudi Arabia would limit contact between Chinese military and intelligence personnel and F-35-related sites. What Could The Components Reveal? As we noted earlier, there is no way to gauge the intelligence impact of the loss at this stage. The central unknown of what China already knows about the F-35, and what it may already have in its possession — especially related to these components — is the key variable here. Regardless, an F-35 canopy and weapons-bay door can provide information that cannot otherwise be easily obtained and gives a different level of fidelity in terms of material exploitation than what construction data and blueprints alone could. The F-35’s low observability is the product of an extremely complex combination of airframe shaping, construction materials, external coatings, manufacturing tolerances, speciality apertures, and more. U.S. Air Force 325th Maintenance Squadron low-observable maintainers work on an F-35A at Tyndall Air Force Base, Florida, in August 2024. U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Victoria Moehlman A canopy is a particularly demanding part of any stealth aircraft. It has to satisfy optical and structural requirements while also controlling radar reflections. The cockpit is historically a major source of radar reflectivity, including the pilot’s helmet. Therefore the canopy’s materials, construction, interfaces, and specialized treatments can be critical to the aircraft’s overall low-observable performance, and especially from the critical frontal aspect. The F-35’s canopy has been an ongoing work in progress for many years. It has had chronic material issues , especially when it comes to delamination . Multiple iterations spread over two decades have recently resulted in a major improvement of the issue. The tight balancing act of keeping the canopy transparent enough, while controlling the F-35’s stealthy signature and having that mix of materials be robust enough to last for a reasonable amount of time has been a major investment for the program. If the canopy is of a later variation, that loss alone could be substantial and could help China with their own low-observable canopy development programs even if they already had original information on the F-35’s canopy original design dating back years. Evidence of the F-35’s canopy delamination issue on an early example of the F-35B. Crown Copyright The F-35’s canopy has been a notorious work in progress, specifically the low observable coating/delamination issue which has improved a lot in recent years with new materials and processes. So no, you do NOT want to lose that in to China! https://t.co/9V0jdRAiwA — Tyler Rogoway (@Aviation_Intel) September 19, 2026 The F-35’s weapons-bay door has its own sensitivity issues. It is effectively a major section of the aircraft’s outer shell, with its structure, edges, interfaces, tolerances and treatments all having to function without creating unacceptable radar signatures. Its construction and material attributes can be reasonably extrapolated for the rest of much of the F-35’s outer mold-line. Above all else, if the radar absorbent material remained intact on the door, that would signify a major loss when viewed without any understanding of what China already knows about the F-35’s radar absorbing surface treatments. Historically speaking, RAM technology is among America’s closely guarded material sciences secrets. A Belgian Air Force service member inspects the open weapons bay of an F-35A at Luke AFB, Arizona. U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Tekorey Watkins For the time being, Australian officials have said they do not understand the parts to be sensitive. The investigation will ultimately have to establish what the components actually contain and what could be learned from them. The incident comes at a moment when China’s own stealth fighter efforts are undergoing an extraordinary expansion. The PLAAF is now operating the J-20 , China’s first operational fifth-generation stealth fighter, in increasingly large numbers . The smaller J-35 is also moving toward broader service, including a carrier role for the People’s Liberation Army Navy. Aircraft maintainers clean the fuselage of a J-20 fighter during the Changchun Air Show in the Jilin Province of China, in September 2025. Photo by Zhang Xiangyi/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images China has also moved into what Western observers generally describe as sixth-generation fighter development. Two new tailless combat-aircraft designs emerged publicly in December 2024. One is the large Chengdu aircraft commonly referred to as the J-36 , while the other is associated with Shenyang and is variously called the J-XDS or J-50 . Both have continued flight testing and yielded several prototypes with individual refinements . The exact capabilities and eventual operational roles of these aircraft remain uncertain. They are developmental designs, not established operational equivalents of the F-35 or other sixth-generation systems. However, China is clearly building an increasingly broad ecosystem of fifth- and next-generation low-observable combat aircraft, both crewed and uncrewed . In the latter category is a growing number of stealthy drones, including long-endurance types. A satellite image taken last month shows the WZ-X very large, low-observable, flying-wing drone undergoing testing. PHOTO © 2026 PLANET LABS INC. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. REPRINTED BY PERMISSION China didn’t likely need physical access to an F-35 canopy or weapons-bay door to develop the J-20, J-35, or its next-generation aircraft. But additional information about how a mature Western stealth aircraft handles materials, coatings, interfaces, manufacturing, and the integration of those elements can still have great potential value to an industry developing its own systems. This includes technologies intended to counter the U.S. combat aircraft and their low-observable characteristics. The F-35 has been produced in large numbers, is operated by a growing coalition of countries, and has been subjected to years of testing and operational experience. Its low-observable design represents decades of accumulated U.S. research and industrial know-how. At the same time, the global scale of the program inevitably makes control over sensitive information more complicated. More aircraft, more maintainers, more industrial partners, and more international logistics mean more points at which information and physical hardware have to be controlled. Over time, a program of this size will see an erosion in its secrets, but a major loss can drastically accelerate what should be a more gradual and controlled decline in security. The Lockheed Martin F-35 production line at Fort Worth, Texas. Lockheed Martin photo by Alexander H Groves The potential intelligence value of the components also has to be considered in the context of foreign material exploitation , or FME. Major military powers maintain dedicated capabilities to recover, examine and characterize foreign weapons, aircraft, sensors, materials and other equipment. The objective is not necessarily to reproduce an entire system . More important is determining how something is built, what materials and manufacturing techniques are used, how individual components perform, and where industrial strengths or limitations may lie. That is why countries have historically gone to extraordinary lengths to recover even crashed or damaged pieces of sensitive military hardware. The bigger the prize, the more risk an intelligence service would be willing to take in order to realize a recovery. The sensitivity surrounding the physical remnants of an F-35 is not new. When a Japan Air Self-Defense Force F-35A disappeared over the Pacific in 2019, the search quickly became more than a rescue operation. U.S. and Japanese forces mounted an extensive effort to locate the wreckage, with U.S. Navy P-8A aircraft and a destroyer joining the search. TWZ noted at the time that even scattered F-35 wreckage could expose valuable technological secrets, while the aircraft’s location on the seabed raised the prospect of an underwater espionage and recovery operation. USFJ is supporting @MoDJapan_en search & rescue efforts for missing F-35A w/ @US7thFleet P-8A aircraft & @air_fifth coord. @USForcesJapan continues to hope for the safe recovery of the pilot @JASDF_PAO pic.twitter.com/9E7x6QZxpY — U.S. Forces Japan (@USForcesJapan) April 10, 2019 That concern has also been evident in subsequent F-35 recovery operations. In 2022, the U.S. Navy recovered an F-35C from roughly 12,400 feet in the South China Sea after a carrier landing accident, removing the possibility that the aircraft could be accessed by another country. pic.twitter.com/JvQZErAAK0 — OedoSoldier (@OedoSoldier) January 27, 2022 Unanswered Security Questions At this point, there is no public evidence that the Hong Kong diversion was a deliberate Chinese intelligence operation, although it is certainly possible. It is also unclear whether Chinese authorities have examined the F-35 parts or what level of new and useful information has been recovered from them. If, as reported, Chinese authorities have taken possession of the parts and have not returned them, that would be an extraordinary development. If the diversion was genuinely the result of a shipping or logistics error, the outcome would itself be extraordinary. It would raise serious questions about the security controls surrounding the movement of F-35 hardware even without evidence of deliberate interference. The timing is also notable. Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington this week for a state visit with President Donald Trump, with the two leaders meeting amid broader disputes involving technology, security, and the future of U.S.-China relations. Whether the F-35 shipment comes up directly in those discussions is not known, but it would be an obvious subject for U.S. and Chinese officials to address through diplomatic channels. "Ladies and gentlemen, the President of the United States Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump, accompanied by the President of the People's Republic of China Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan." pic.twitter.com/hyPHOBC99Q — Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) September 24, 2026 For now, however, the central question remains how the parts got there. Until that is answered, we won’t know if this was a simple logistics failure or a deliberate intelligence operation. And beyond that, what China already knew about the components it now may have in its possession — a question we may never truly get an answer to. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post F-35 Canopy And Weapons-Bay Door Loss To China: Separating Fact From Fiction appeared first on TWZ .

title: 习特会：中美贸易休战再延期 路透社盘点两国贸易战重要时间线

content: 中国国家主席习近平正在对华盛顿进行为期三天的国事访问，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于周四（9月24号）在白宫接待习近平夫妇。这是今年世界两大经济体领导人之间的第二次会晤，也是习近平十多年来首次访问华盛顿。 路透社报道，此次访问预计将十分隆重，但双方预计不会达成任何重大协议。分析认为，尽管两国之间存在着根深蒂固的竞争关系，但两位领导人都急于强调两国关系的稳定。 周三，当习近平主席夫妇抵达华盛顿附近时，特朗普总统和第一夫人梅拉尼娅在红毯上迎接了他们。两位总统面带微笑，握手并进行了简短的交谈，军乐队奏乐并鸣放礼炮。随后，他们各自离开。 据美国有线电视公共事务网（C-SPAN）报道，这是自2015年教皇方济各访问以来，美国总统首次在安德鲁斯空军基地接待外国领导人。当时，教皇方济各受到了奥巴马总统的接待。 中国官媒新华社援引习近平抵达时发表的声明称，习近平主席希望与美国建立更加稳定的关系，强调北京和华盛顿应该是“伙伴而不是对手”，两国“和平共处的历史逻辑”没有改变。 特朗普计划以一场盛大的欢迎仪式来回馈中国，力求给习近平主席留下深刻印象。这场仪式将于格林尼治标准时间下午2点在白宫南草坪、国事厅和玫瑰园举行。两国元首将于下午举行双边会晤，之后将举行盛大的国宴，届时多位美国科技界领袖将出席。 贸易休战延期 路透社报道，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特告诉福克斯新闻，他和中国国务院副总理何立峰已同意将两国间的贸易休战期延长两个月，至1月10日。该休战期原定于11月10日到期。 周四上午，唐纳德·特朗普在其“真相社交”平台（Truth Social）上发布消息称，他将与习近平讨论“超级智能”（他用来指代人工智能的术语），同时明确表示他不期望达成任何实质性决定。 斯科特·贝森特上周末与何立峰讨论了人工智能问题。美国国务卿马可·卢比奥表示，双方正在讨论建立“类似于冷战时期的直接沟通渠道”，以防止“可能影响经济或社会，甚至导致国家间冲突”的事件发生。 总体而言，由于北京和华盛顿在阿片类药物和稀土元素等诸多问题上仍存在分歧，预计中国国家主席此次访问不会取得重大突破。 尽管如此，定于周四举行的会谈仍有可能达成旨在降低某些行业关税、合作打击毒品走私以及扩大两国军队对话的协议。预计唐纳德·特朗普还将呼吁释放被中国拘留的美国公民和其他人士。 路透社周四视频回顾了过去一年中美贸易战的重要时间点。 2025年1月21日 唐纳德·特朗普宣布就职，再次入主白宫。 2月1日，特朗普下令对来自墨西哥、加拿大和中国的商品加征关税，要求他们阻止芬太尼流入美国，加拿大和墨西哥还被要求阻止非法移民流入美国，此举引发了一场可能会削弱全球经济增长并重新引发通货膨胀的全球贸易战。 在特朗普多次警告北京方面在阻止非法毒品流入美国方面做得不够之后，对所有中国输美商品加征10%的额外关税于美国东部时间2月4日凌晨0点01分生效。 2025年2月4日，中国对美国进口商品加征关税，以回应美国对中国商品加征的新关税，此举再次引发世界两大经济体之间的贸易战。尽管特朗普总统向墨西哥和加拿大提供了暂缓措施，但贸易战依然持续。 特朗普于2025年4月2日表示，他将对其他国家对美国商品加征的关税进行对等征收，此举加剧了他重返白宫后发起的贸易战。他签署了对等关税的行政命令，以及另一项旨在堵住所谓“最低限度”漏洞的行政命令，该漏洞允许从中国进口的低价值包裹免税。 2025年4月4日，中国宣布对美国商品加征一系列关税和限制措施，将从4月10日起对所有美国商品加征34%的关税。 4月9日，特朗普宣布对许多国家暂停加征关税90天，立即生效。当天下午，特朗普宣布将对中国进口商品的关税提高至125%。数十个贸易伙伴暂停加征关税的举措，距离关税生效不到24小时。 特朗普4月9号宣布，“我给了那些没有进行报复的国家90天的暂停期，因为我告诉他们，如果你们进行报复，我们将加倍报复。我对中国就是这么做的，因为他们进行了报复。” 中国外交部于4月10日表示，中国不希望发生贸易战，但如果美国继续以关税相威胁，中国也不会畏惧。 5月7日，特朗普于表示，他不会为了让中国回到谈判桌前而取消关税。 5月9日，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 抵达日内瓦，与中国经济主管贺立峰和瑞士官员举行首次贸易会谈。5月以来，由贝森特和中国国务院副总理何立峰率领的代表团一直在欧洲各城市举行会晤，试图解决这场贸易战。 5月12日，美国和中国宣布达成协议，暂时削减相互关税。作为世界两大经济体，双方希望结束这场扰乱全球经济前景、令金融市场动荡不安的贸易战。 6月11日，美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克于2025年表示，在伦敦与中国达成的贸易框架和实施计划应能解决稀土和磁体贸易限制问题。 7月29日，中国首席贸易谈判代表李成刚在斯德哥尔摩表示，中美双方达成共识，将继续推动美国暂停对中国商品加征对等关税，以及中国的反制措施。 8月11日，特朗普回避了是否会延长原定于8月12日生效的对华加征关税期限的问题，他告诉记者“我们拭目以待”，同时赞扬了中国在与美国的谈判中展现出的合作精神。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，作为9月15日在马德里结束的关于关税和经济政策的更广泛谈判的一部分，美中两国就短视频应用TikTok达成了一项框架协议。 10月10日，特朗普在Truth Social上发帖，重启了对北京的贸易战，结束了这两个最大经济体之间脆弱的休战局面。他承诺大幅提高关税，以应对中国限制其关键矿产出口的行为。 美国总统宣布 对中国输美商品加征100%的额外关税，并对“所有关键软件”实施新的出口管制，这些措施将于11月1日生效，比现有关税减免到期日提前9天。 特朗普在10月21日表示，他认为他将与中国国家主席习近平举行“非常成功的会晤”，但也表示也许……这次会面不会发生。他说，“ 两周后，我将前往韩国，与习近平主席会面。我们将在韩国会晤。我们将讨论很多事情。他们想讨论他们被征收157%关税的问题；这比他们预想的要高一些。” 2025年10月25日 ，美中两国高级经济官员在马来西亚首都吉隆坡谈判 ，努力缓和贸易战，为下周特习会做好准备 。 2025年10月30日，APEC峰会期间，特朗普和习近平在釜山空军基地举行了关键的面对面会谈。特朗普在与习近平握手时表示，中美贸易协议可能签署 。特朗普与习近平在韩国釜山举行的会谈是自2019年以来的首次会晤，标志着他旋风式亚洲之行的结束。在此次亚洲之行中，他还大力宣传了与韩国、日本和东南亚国家在贸易方面取得的突破。 特朗普在峰会结束后表示，他已与习近平达成协议，削减对华关税，以换取北京方面打击非法芬太尼贸易、恢复美国大豆采购以及保持稀土出口畅通。 2026年1月16日加拿大总理卡尼访华，称中国是“可靠且可预测的伙伴”，并在达沃斯论坛上鼓励欧洲领导人寻求来自中国的投资。 1月24日，特朗普表示，如果加拿大与中国达成贸易协议，他将对加拿大征收100%的关税，并警告这样的协议将危及加拿大。

title: 赵晓：从“改变中国”到“长期竞争” ——美国对华战略与“文明持久战”的形成

content: 作者：赵晓 2026-9-23 万维博客 中美峰会在即。 美国一方面加征关税、限制高端芯片、强化第一岛链；另一方面又在最新战略文件中表示，美国不寻求“主宰、扼杀或羞辱中国”，而是希望获得稳定和平、公平贸易与相互尊重。 这两者矛盾吗？ 并不矛盾。 美国没有放弃与中国竞争，而是在重新限定竞争的目标： 不是从竞争走向和解，而是从“如何改变中国”，转向“如何同一个不会消失的中国长期竞争”。 我把这种关系称为： 文明持久战。 所谓“文明持久战”，不是两个民族的生死决战，也不是必须消灭对方文明，而是两个文明型大国在无法改造对方、无法摆脱对方、也无法承受全面战争的条件下，围绕实力、制度、科技与国际秩序展开的长期竞争。 它的内核只有三句话： 不能速胜。 不能退出。 不能失控。   一、旧战略：通过接触改变中国 1972年尼克松访华，直接目标是联手制衡苏联。 1979年中美建交，两国关系开始制度化。 2001年中国加入世界贸易组织，中美进入经济大融合时代。 在这段时期，美国对华战略背后一直存在一个隐含假设： 随着中国进入全球市场、发展民营经济、形成中产阶级并接触西方社会，中国最终会在经济、法律乃至政治制度上向西方靠拢。 贸易不只是贸易。 贸易还被寄望成为改变中国的力量。 这个战略创造了巨大的经济成果。 美国企业获得了市场和供应链，美国消费者获得了大量廉价商品；中国则获得资本、技术、订单、管理经验和高速增长。 但最后出现了一个美国没有充分预料的结果： 中国加入了这个体系，却没有变成美国所期待的中国；中国利用这个体系迅速强大，却没有接受美国预设的政治终点。 川普带来的第一个变化，不是关税，而是推翻了美国对华战略的一个旧前提： 经济接触未必带来政治趋同。 一个国家可以进入全球体系，也可以借助这个体系发展自己，同时保持自己的制度与文明传统。   二、川普1.0：从接触转向防范 2017年，川普政府发布《国家安全战略》，将中国称为挑战美国力量、影响力和利益的“修正主义力量”。 这是美国对华战略的正式转折。 中国不再主要被视为一个可以通过接触逐渐改变的国家，而被视为一个拥有经济、科技和军事力量的长期竞争者。 2019年，美国国务院政策规划事务主任斯金纳又提出，美国正在面对一个“真正不同的文明”，并称这是美国第一次面对一个“非白种人的大国竞争对手”。 这番话充满争议，也不能代表美国完整的官方战略。 但它暴露出美国战略界一度出现的“文明冲突诱惑”： 既然中国没有因接触而发生美国期待的改变，那么中美竞争会不会演变成一场不可调和的文明较量？ 问题是，中国不是苏联。 中国有超大规模人口、完整的工业体系、广泛的贸易网络和悠久的文明连续性。美国可以限制中国，压制中国，给中国制造巨大困难，却很难期待中国轻易退出历史舞台。 中国研究专家白鲁恂（Lucian Pye）曾说： 中国是一个伪装成民族国家的文明。 这句话未必严谨，却点出了一个事实： 中国不仅是现代国际体系中的一个国家，也是一个具有深厚历史记忆和强大延续能力的文明共同体。 中国不是美国可以轻易改变的对象。 也不是美国能够承担“失去”的国家。   三、拜登时期：竞争被制度化 拜登上台后，并没有回到过去的接触政策。 川普改变了美国对中国的基本判断，拜登则把这一判断制度化、联盟化。 拜登政府的对华战略可以概括为三个词： 投资、联合、竞争。 投资，是重建美国的基础设施、产业能力、半导体和科技创新。 联合，是重新整合欧洲、日本、韩国、澳大利亚、印度和菲律宾等盟友伙伴。 竞争，则是在技术、产业、军事、规则与国际影响力上同中国展开长期较量。 川普主要依靠关税和单边压力。 拜登更重视联盟、规则、供应链“去风险”和精准技术限制。 方法不同，方向却高度连续： 美国已经不再相信中国会自动趋同，而是开始为长期竞争作准备。 美国对华战略由“内部改变”，转向“外部塑造”： 中国可以继续发展，但美国要努力阻止中国凭借自身发展，改变美国所希望维持的亚洲秩序。   四、川普2.0：竞争目标开始收缩 到了川普第二任期，美国的判断又向前走了一步。 2025年《美国国家安全战略》将今天的中美商业关系描述为“近乎对等者之间的关系”（near-peers）。 这并不是说，中美已经在军事、金融、科技和全球影响力上全面平起平坐。 但它意味着： 美国已经不能再把中国视为等待毕业的学生、等待转型的对象，或者可以任意安排的次等力量。 中国已经强大到美国不能绕开，但还没有强大到美国必须全面退让；美国仍然强大到可以给中国制造巨大压力，但也没有强大到可以命令中国。 2026年《美国国家防务战略》进一步表示： 美国的目标不是主宰中国，也不是扼杀或羞辱中国；美国寻求的是稳定和平、公平贸易，以及建立在实力基础之上的相互尊重。 这当然不是美国放弃竞争。 美国仍在强化第一岛链，限制中国获得最先进的芯片和军事技术，重建关键产业链，并要求盟友承担更多防务责任。 真正改变的是竞争目标： 过去的冲动，是赢得一场终结竞争的最后胜利。 现在的目标，是让任何一方都无法迅速打破地区均势。 这就是美国对华战略从“胜利战略”转向“均势战略”。 不是消灭对手，而是阻止对手支配关键地区；不是寻求最后决战，而是维持长期平衡。   五、未必是温和，而是现实主义 美国为什么收缩战略目标？ 不是因为突然友善，而是因为成本太高。 第一，中国是核大国。 任何以彻底击败对方为目标的战争，都可能走向无法控制的毁灭。 第二，中美经济仍然深度联系。 全面脱钩的代价不仅由中国承担，也会落在美国消费者、企业、农民和金融市场身上。 第三，中国拥有庞大的工业体系、市场规模和国家动员能力，不会因为几轮关税和出口限制迅速失去竞争能力。 第四，美国同时面对欧洲、中东、拉丁美洲和国内财政压力，不可能把全部资源无限期投入亚洲。 第五，美国的盟友愿意防范中国，却未必愿意参加一场以彻底击败中国为目标的全面对抗。 所以，美国今天的战略比早期的文明冲突论更加克制，却未必更加软弱。 它减少了宏大的意识形态目标，反而可能因此变得更加集中、持久和现实。 一个不再幻想迅速改变中国的美国，可能成为一个更有耐心的竞争者。   六、文明持久战 中美关系因此正在进入一种新的历史状态。 双方无法改变对方。 无法摆脱对方。 也无法承受全面战争。 因此，两国竞争将越来越像一场没有明确终局的重复博弈。 今天的关税，会影响明天的供应链。 今天的技术限制，会推动明天的自主替代。 今天的军事部署，会改变明天的安全判断。 今天留下的信用，也会影响后天的合作空间。 在这种竞争中，真正重要的不是一时输赢，而是谁所代表的文明更有韧性，谁更能创新，谁的制度更能纠错，谁能让自己的人民保持信心，也让更多国家愿意与自己合作。 这就是“文明持久战”的真正含义。 它不是战争动员。 而是承认：两个文明型大国将长期共处、长期竞争，也必须长期管理彼此之间的危险。   七、中国最需要避免两个误判 第一个误判是： 美国仍然要像当年对付苏联那样，彻底击败中国。因此，中国除了全面对抗，没有别的选择。 这种判断会把所有分歧都解释为生存斗争，最终制造自我实现的敌意。 第二个误判是： 美国开始谈“相互尊重”，意味着美国已经退缩，中国可以迅速扩大战略空间。 这种判断则可能诱发冒险。 更接近现实的判断是： 美国开始接受中国将长期存在，却不会接受中国主导亚洲；中国无法把美国赶出全球体系，美国也无法把中国从世界经济和国际政治中剔除。 两国将继续竞争。 而且可能竞争很久。 结语 过去，美国对华政策的潜台词是： 中国最终会改变。 川普第一任期的转折是： 中国如果不会改变，美国就必须全面防范。 拜登政府的回答是： 依靠国内投资、技术优势和盟友体系，长期塑造中国的外部行为。 到了川普第二任期，一个新的现实主义判断逐渐清晰： 中国不会按照美国的期待被改造，也不可能被轻易击垮；美国真正能够做的，是保持自己的经济、科技和军事优势，阻止中国支配印太，同时维持必要的贸易、禁毒与危机管理合作。 这不是和解。 也不是决战。 这是美国从改造世界的雄心，退回到力量政治的边界；从追求历史终局，转向管理一场没有明确终局的长期竞争。 最后，可以用三句话概括： 美国已经放弃“中国必然被改变”的幻想，但没有放弃维护自身优势。 美国开始承认中国不会消失，但不会因此接受中国主导亚洲。 中美关系真正进入的，不是和平时代，也不是决战时刻，而是竞争性共存的漫长年代。

title: 赵晓：“文明持久战”的背后——美国对华战略的四次心理转换
summary: 作者： 赵晓 万维博客 2026-9-24 《 从“改变中国”到“长期竞争” ——美国对华战略与“文明持久战”的形成 》发表后，得到不少朋友的回应和鼓励。一些朋友特别注意到我提出的“文明持久战”这个概念。 需要说明的是，这里的“文明”是描述性概念，不是价值判断。它不要求一个国家已经进入尊重生命、自由与尊严的现代文明，而是沿用亨廷顿式的用法，指一个社会长期形成并相对稳定延续的语言文字、生活方式、政治传统与集体认同。“是一个文明”，不等于“已经现代文明化”；前者描述历史文化共同体
content: 作者： 赵晓 万维博客 2026-9-24 《 从“改变中国”到“长期竞争” ——美国对华战略与“文明持久战”的形成 》发表后，得到不少朋友的回应和鼓励。一些朋友特别注意到我提出的“文明持久战”这个概念。 需要说明的是，这里的“文明”是描述性概念，不是价值判断。它不要求一个国家已经进入尊重生命、自由与尊严的现代文明，而是沿用亨廷顿式的用法，指一个社会长期形成并相对稳定延续的语言文字、生活方式、政治传统与集体认同。“是一个文明”，不等于“已经现代文明化”；前者描述历史文化共同体，后者判断制度与价值。称中美“文明持久战”，是说明中美面对的是两个具有深厚历史记忆与强烈自我认同的共同体。 所谓“文明持久战”，也非指两个民族的生死决战，更不是要消灭对方的文明，而是两个文明型大国在无法改造对方、无法摆脱对方、也无法承受全面战争的条件下，围绕实力、制度、科技与国际秩序展开的长期竞争。 它的内核是三句话： 不能速胜。不能退出。不能失控。 但“文明持久战”不是突然出现的。它的背后，是美国对华认知近八十年来的一场心理去魅，需专文论述。 这场去魅，可以用四个动词串起来： 从仿佛可以“拥有”中国，到相信可以“塑造”中国；从一度出现“击败”中国的冲动，到今天准备“管理”同中国的竞争。 四步走完，美国才逐渐认识到一件事： 它不能决定中国如何改变，也不能把“中国必然按照美国的期待改变”，作为对华战略成立的前提。 这，或许是理解今天中美关系最重要的一把钥匙。 一、第一次转换：从“拥有中国”到承认中国不属于美国 1949年，中华人民共和国成立。美国政界随即爆发了一场持续多年的政治风暴： “谁失去了中国？” 杜鲁门政府、国务院里的“中国通”以及主张同中共接触的外交官，都被指责为软弱、失职，甚至“出卖中国”。 然而，这个问题本身包含着一个未经反省的前提： 中国原本是美国可以拥有、保住或者安排的。 如果中国不是美国的，何来“失去中国”？ 1949年，国务卿艾奇逊在《中美关系白皮书》的送交函中写道：中国内战的结局超出了美国政府的控制；在美国能力的合理限度内，无论美国已经做什么或可能做什么，都无法改变这一结果。它是中国内部力量作用的产物，美国曾试图影响这些力量，却没有做到。 艾奇逊不是说外部力量对中国毫无影响，也不是说美国此前的政策没有得失。他指出的是一个更根本的事实： 中国的历史方向，最终不可能由华盛顿决定。 只有曾经拥有，才谈得上失去。 美国可以失去在中国的影响力，失去市场、盟友或地区优势，却不可能“失去中国”，因为中国从来不属于美国。 然而，艾奇逊的清醒并没有真正成为美国对华政策的长期基础。“失去中国”的焦虑退潮之后，另一种更加温和、也更加隐蔽的期待出现了： 美国未必需要控制中国，却可以通过接触、贸易和全球化，逐渐塑造中国。 二、第二次转换：从“拥有中国”到“塑造中国” 1972年尼克松访华，1979年中美建交，2001年中国加入世界贸易组织。 在这个过程中，美国对华政策逐渐形成了一个强大的隐含假设： 随着中国进入全球市场，民营经济不断发展，中产阶层不断扩大，中国最终会在经济、法律乃至政治制度上向西方靠拢。 这套逻辑可以简化为一句话： 贸易带来市场化，市场化造就中产阶级，中产阶级推动政治开放。 贸易因此不只是贸易。 市场也不只是市场。 它们还被寄望成为推动中国制度转型的力量。 当然，不能把冷战后的接触政策简单理解为“以贸易改变制度”。接触还有许多现实目标：避免中美重新敌对，推动中国融入国际体系，开拓中国市场，并在朝鲜半岛、全球经济和气候变化等问题上寻求合作。 但是，期待经济开放最终带来政治趋同，的确构成了美国精英对华想象的重要部分。 这种想象背后，仍然延续着一种美国中心主义： 美国不仅代表一种国家利益，也代表历史前进的方向；其他国家一旦进入美国主导的世界体系，最终就会越来越像美国。 美国不能“拥有中国”，却仍然相信自己能够“塑造中国”。 接触政策当然不是毫无成果。中美双方都从中获得了巨大的经济收益，中国社会也被改革开放、国际贸易和互联网深刻改变。 但美国没有充分预料到的是： 中国进入了美国主导的国际体系，却没有变成美国所期待的中国。 这里必须辨明一点。 问题不在于接触没有改变中国，而在于： 中国发生了巨大改变，却没有按照华盛顿预想的方向和速度改变。 中国既没有拒绝全球化，也没有因为全球化而完全西方化；既融入了国际秩序，又不断扩大自己在国际秩序中的发言权。 美国战略界由此不得不面对一个过去不愿面对的问题： 如果中国不会因为经济接触而自动趋同，美国的对华战略怎么办？ 三、第三次转换：从“塑造中国”到“击败中国”的冲动 2018年，坎贝尔与拉特纳在《外交事务》发表《对华清算：北京如何打破华盛顿的预期》。 这篇文章的重要性，不在于它第一次主张对华强硬，而在于它系统反思了美国对华政策背后的旧假设。 两位作者承认，美国长期高估了自己改变中国内部发展轨迹的能力。无论是贸易、接触和国际制度的吸纳，还是制裁、外交压力和价值倡议，都没有使中国沿着美国期待的方向发展。 这不是说中国永远不会改变。 任何国家都会改变，中国也一直在改变。 真正破产的是另一个判断： 美国可以通过自身政策，决定中国改变的基本方向。 这里有一个非常重要的区别： 说“中国不会改变”，是一种静态的文明决定论；说“美国不能决定中国如何改变”，则是一种现实主义的能力判断。 前者未必正确，后者却越来越成为美国战略界的共识。 川普第一任期的历史作用，首先不是发动了贸易战，而是公开推翻了美国对华战略的旧前提。 2017年《国家安全战略》将中国称为挑战美国力量、影响力和利益的“修正主义力量”。美国对华战略的重心由此发生变化：不再主要关注中国内部会不会转型，而更加关注中国力量的增长会不会改变亚洲乃至全球的力量分布。 接触政策的预期落空后，美国战略界一度出现一种更激进的冲动： 既然不能通过接触改变中国，是否可以通过全面竞争压倒中国？ 2019年，美国国务院一位高级官员甚至把中美竞争同“文明差异”联系起来。这种带有种族色彩的说法引起巨大争议，也没有成为美国完整的官方战略，却暴露出一种“文明冲突”的诱惑： 既然中国没有被接触改变，中美竞争是否注定是一场只能由一方获胜的文明决战？ 然而，中国毕竟不是苏联。 中国拥有超大规模人口、完整的工业体系、广泛的贸易网络、核武器和悠久的文化文明连续性。美国可以限制中国，遏制中国，给中国制造巨大困难，却很难期待中国突然退出历史舞台，更无法保证一个陷入混乱的中国符合美国利益。 美国不得不同时面对两个现实： 中国很难被改造，也很难被击垮。 这正是“文明持久战”形成的现实基础。 四、第四次转换：从“击败中国”到“管理竞争” 2 019年，坎贝尔与沙利文在《外交事务》发表《避免灾难的竞争》。 这篇文章比一般的“对华强硬论”又向前走了一步。 两位作者提出，美国不应追求类似冷战结束那样的 “决定性终局” ，而应寻求一种符合美国利益和价值观的 “清醒共存的稳定状态” 。 换句话说，中美竞争不再被理解为一个必须彻底解决的问题，而是一种需要长期管理的国际现实。 这篇文章后来显出特殊分量：两位作者中，一位随后出任美国国家安全顾问，另一位后来出任常务副国务卿。 2019年提出的“竞争性共存”，此后成为拜登政府对华战略的重要思想来源。理论倡导者亲自进入决策中枢，也成为这一观念从政策主张走向国家战略的重要标志。 美国对华战略由此出现第二次重大转向。 第一次，是从“接触改变中国”转向“防范中国”。 第二次，是从“击败中国”转向“管理竞争”。 这不是和解，也不是放弃竞争，而是重新限定竞争的目标： 不是消灭对手，不是迫使对手投降，也不是等待某个历史终局，而是防止对方获得支配性优势，同时避免竞争滑向全面战争。 五、从“内部趋同”转向“外部约束” 2022年，国务卿布林肯在阐述拜登政府对华政策时说： 美国不能依赖北京改变自身轨迹，因此，美国将塑造北京周围的战略环境。 这句话很重要，但也容易被过度解读。 它不是说美国从此不再关心中国内部的发展，也不是说美国完全放弃对中国施加影响。 美国真正放弃的，是把“中国最终按照美国期待发生转型”，当作对华战略成立的前提和胜利标准。 布林肯的意思是： 即使中国不改变，美国的战略也必须能够成立。 由此有了“投资、联合、竞争”： 投资美国自己的产业、科技和基础设施； 联合盟友伙伴； 在科技、供应链、军事安全和国际规则上同中国展开长期竞争。 美国战略从期待“内部趋同”，转向构筑“外部约束”： 从等待中国改变，转向限制中国扩张；从制度改造，转向力量拒止。 到了川普第二任期，这种战略收缩变得更加明确。 2026年《美国国防战略》表示，美国的目标不是主宰、羞辱或扼杀中国，而是确保中国不能支配美国及其盟友；实现这一目标，并不需要改变中国内部制度，也不需要把中美关系变成一场生存性斗争。 这意味着，美国开始把对华竞争的目标进一步收缩为： 维持印太地区的力量平衡，防止中国取得地区主导地位，同时从实力地位出发，同中国保持贸易、外交和必要的战略沟通。 这当然不意味着美国变得温和。 美国仍会强化第一岛链，限制中国获得最先进的技术，重建关键产业链，并要求盟友承担更多防务责任。 但美国越来越清楚地把“竞争”与“改变中国”区别开来，把“拒止性威慑” （deterrence by denial）与“文明决战”区别开来。 过去的冲动，是赢得一场可以终结竞争的最后胜利； 现在的目标，是让任何一方都无法迅速打破地区均势。 美国正在从“胜利战略”转向“均势战略”。 六、美国真的放弃改变中国了吗？ 这个问题必须严谨回答。 答案是： 既是，也不是。 说“是”，是因为美国越来越不相信自己能够按照自身形象重塑中国，也不再把中国必然实现西方式转型作为国家战略的前提。 说“不是”，是因为美国仍然希望中国在市场规则、地区行为和国际秩序等方面发生有利于美国的变化，也仍会通过贸易、技术、外交和联盟体系施加影响。 因此，更准确的表述不是： “美国终于认识到中国不可改变。” 而是： 美国终于认识到，它不能决定中国如何改变，更不能把中国必然按照美国的期待改变，作为对华战略成立的前提。 同样，“不存在失去中国的问题”，也不意味着美国不再争夺对中国的影响力。 它意味着： 中国从来不是任何外国可以拥有或失去的对象。美国可能失去对华影响力，失去中国市场，失去地区优势，却不可能“失去中国”，因为中国的历史命运最终属于中国人民。 外部力量当然可以影响中国，改变中国发展的成本和环境，却不能代替中国人民完成中国自身的历史转型。 七、去魅之后，竞争可能更加冷酷 美国放下“改造中国”的执念，并不会使中美关系自动变得温和。 恰恰相反，一个不再幻想迅速改变中国的美国，可能成为一个更有耐心、更能集中资源，也更加难以对付的竞争者。 过去，美国常常把贸易、投资和国际交往同时当作改变中国的手段。 现在，它越来越倾向于把不同问题拆开处理： 关税就是关税，芯片就是芯片，海峡安全就是军事均势，稀土与供应链就是产业安全，禁毒与危机沟通则属于双方必须合作的有限领域。 意识形态的热度下降之后，剩下的是更加精确的成本计算、力量配置和边界谈判。 这种现实主义减少了救世主义的冲动，却可能使竞争更加持久。 因为一个把目标限定为维护均势、保存优势的国家，往往比一个追求彻底胜利的国家，更能承受长期博弈。 八、去魅必须是双向的 写到这里，一个问题绕不过去： 这场去魅只应发生在美国一边吗？ 当然不是。 美国需要放下的幻觉，是“中国必然按照美国的期待改变”；中国同样需要放下一个对称的幻觉，就是“美 国必然衰落，时间必然站在中国一边 ”。 两种幻觉的结构其实完全相同： 都预先宣布了对手的历史结局，都把自己的战略建立在对方“必然如何”之上。 艾奇逊早在1949年就承认，美国不能决定中国的历史方向；但美国此后绕了近八十年，才重新回到这一清醒。 中国如果以为只要等待，就必然等来一个衰落甚至退出亚洲的美国，实际上是在重复美国当年的错误，只是把方向颠倒了。 因此，对中国来说，真正需要警惕的，不只是误判美国的战略意图，也是误判时间本身。 持久竞争比的不是一时的爆发力，而是数十年里谁犯的错误更少、发现得更早、改得更快。 中国真正的危险，也不只是某一轮关税战或者芯片战失利，而是把一时的动员优势误认为长期的制度优势。 动员能力是集中体制的长项，纠错能力却往往是它最稀缺的东西：权力越集中，坏消息越难及时上达，错误越难被及时发现，代价也越容易被延后。 在速决战里，这个短板可能被强大的动员能力暂时掩盖；在持久竞争中，它却会被时间不断放大。 一场没有明确终局的竞争，对双方提出的是同一个要求： 不再以对方必然改变为前提，而以自己的持续纠错为根基。 九、“文明持久战”的真正含义 上一篇文章把美国的新认知概括为“文明现实主义”： 承认不同文明不会因为贸易而自动趋同，也不必因为不同而走向相互毁灭。 文明现实主义是一种认知，“文明持久战”则是由这种认知产生的历史状态。 中美关系正在进入这样一种状态： 双方无法按照自己的形象改造对方，无法把对方从世界体系中排除，也无法承受全面战争带来的毁灭性后果。 所以，中美竞争将越来越像一场没有明确终局的重复博弈： 今天的关税，会重塑明天的供应链； 今天的技术限制，会刺激明天的自主替代； 今天的军事部署，会改变明天的安全判断； 今天是否遵守承诺，也会影响后天的合作空间。 在这场竞争中，真正决定成败的，不只是哪一方拥有更多军舰、芯片和资本，还包括： 谁的文明更有韧性； 谁的制度更有纠错能力； 谁更能持续创新； 谁能让自己的人民保持信心； 谁能吸引更多国家自愿合作； 谁能在拥有力量时保持克制，在遭受压力时避免失控。 这就是“文明持久战”的真正含义。 它不是战争动员，更不是文明仇恨。 它承认竞争，却拒绝把竞争解释为两个民族只能活一个的生死斗争；它承认力量，却不相信力量能够任意改造另一个文明；它接受长期共存，同时警惕共存滑向全面冲突。 结语：从“历史终局”回到“历史之中” “谁失去了中国”，代表的是一种虚幻的拥有感。 “通过接触改变中国”，代表的是一种温和的塑造欲。 “击败中国”，代表的是接触预期落空后一度出现的对抗冲动。 而今天逐渐形成的“管理竞争”，意味着美国开始接受一个更加有限、也更加真实的战略目标： 中国不会按照美国的期待被改造，也不可能被轻易击垮；美国真正能够做的，是保持自身优势，联合盟友，塑造中国的外部环境，防止中国主导印太，同时维持必要的贸易、外交与危机管理合作。 这不是和解。 也不是决战。 这是美国从改造世界的雄心，退回到力量政治的边界；从追求历史终局，回到历史之中。 最终，可以把这场思想演变概括为三句话： 美国已经放弃“中国必然按照美国期待改变”的幻想，却没有放弃维护自己的优势。 美国开始承认中国不会消失，却不会因此接受中国主导亚洲。 中美关系真正进入的，不是和平时代，也不是决战时刻，而是竞争性共存的漫长年代。 这就是“文明持久战”的背后，也是它最值得双方警醒的地方： 不能速胜，不能退出，不能失控。 而对于任何把时间当作盟友的一方，还要再加一句： 时间不站在任何一方，它只站在犯错更少、纠错更快的一方。

content: 作者：曹长青 原载台湾《看》杂志 2026 年 9 月号 9 月 23 日，中国国家主席习近平访问美国。这是应今年 5 月川普总统访北京时对习近平邀请的回访。一年之内，两个世界大国领导人的相互正式访问，对中美关系的改善具有重要作用，尤其是，也潜在有利于台湾安全、促进台海局势稳定。因为这次习近平访美，中美之间的国际事务对抗点大幅降低，更易走向合作。   伊朗战争，没有影响中美关系   首先是当前的伊朗战争，中国虽然是德黑兰的老朋友，但这次没敢公开支持伊朗，不想损害和美国的关系，因为川普非常看重其它国家对伊朗的态度，连那个曾被川普视为盟友 / 朋友的意大利女总理梅洛尼，都因拒绝美国使用其军事基地（攻击伊朗）而遭川普公开批评并绝交。南韩总统李在明曾表示不愿帮忙，也被川普修理，并大幅降低美韩军事演习规模。所以这次中国没有公开支持伊朗得到川普赞赏，他公开提到北京没有给伊朗提供武器。所以在伊朗问题上，中美两国领导人更多是共识，而没有重大冲突。这是当今国际政治的重要一点。   俄乌战争，中美趋向共识   第二就是俄乌战争。在拜登时代，美国力挺乌克兰（提供了 3500 亿美元支持），中国支持俄国。这是当时中美关系恶化的一个重要触点。但现在局势改变，川普总统的美国不再像拜登那样一面倒支持泽林斯基，更希望推动乌战尽快停火谈判，俄乌签署和平协议。川普已经停止了对乌克兰的资金援助和军事支持，连泽林斯基想要的爱国者导弹拦截系统，川普也没有答应给。川普并与俄国总统普京在阿拉斯加举行高峰会谈，双方基本达成乌战结束的框架。泽林斯基不同意这个框架，那美国的态度就是，不再管，你们双方就继续打吧；而打的结果，就是乌克兰不仅没有胜利的可能，反而失去更多领土，尤其是生命。 乌战爆发以来，乌克兰已失去 20% 领土，伤亡过百万人，人口从战前的 4200 万降至今天的 2900 万（乌东地区和克里米亚失去近 1000 万人口，加上逃到欧洲的几百万乌克兰人，再不回来了。战场逃兵就有 20 万 —— 乌国防部长在国会证词）。所以，在乌战问题上，中美不仅没有重大分歧，川普还可能希望习近平帮助调解，促使俄罗斯在谈判问题上更加灵活。   北韩核武，中美都想和平解决   第三个国际焦点是北韩核武问题。原有的促使朝鲜半岛无核化的 “ 六方会谈 ” （美国，中国，俄国，日本，南韩，北韩）机制早已不复存在。因为乌战和欧美对俄罗斯的制裁，俄国与美国关系破裂，导致俄国与北韩结盟，双方签署了军事共同防御条约，莫斯科公开表示，理解北韩拥有核武的立场，等于变相支持，这是拜登政府用乌克兰打 “ 代理人战争 ” 、不惜美俄交恶的恶果之一。 中国采取默认态度，也不坚持原来的朝鲜半岛无核化立场，因为担心平壤和莫斯科走得更近，中国被边缘化、降低北京对平壤的影响力。在中俄两个大国都支持或默认北韩发展核武的情况下，美国就比较棘手。所以川普总统的策略是，与北韩改善关系、拆解中俄朝三角联盟（希望他们只保持松散联手）。川普总统决定大幅缩小美韩军演规模，并向北韩领导人金正恩喊话，说与他关系一向很好，并谋求今年 11 月的亚太经合会议（在中国深圳召开）期间与金正恩见面，都是这种策略的一部分。 从伊朗战争就可看出，仅仅靠轰炸，并不能解决根本问题。所以对北韩发展核武等，更不能用军事轰炸等解决。且不说北韩一旦动用核武，南韩首都首尔就在北韩的大炮射程之内（距三八线太近，所以韩国一直有迁都呼声），如果一旦美军轰炸，不能在第一时间摧毁全部的北韩核武基地和大炮，那北韩的报复、对首尔的摧毁会是难以估量的（大首都圈首尔的人口 2600 万，占南韩人口的一半）。所以，对北韩发展核武问题，无法用军事解决，只能通过外交等手段运作，保住和平最重要。川普总统被抨击的所谓 “ 亲独裁者 ” 背后，是有着捍卫世界和平为首任的重要背景和策略因素的。所以，在这种背景下，北韩问题更不会成为中美两国元首会谈的障碍。   台湾问题：川普私下对习近平说狠话   最后是中美之间的常规问题：台湾安全。双方其实心照不宣，都知道对方的想法，所以也会像以往那样，各自表述；尤其是美方，更可能一笔带过，不会多谈。虽然说美国的台海政策被专家们称为 “ 战略模糊 ” ，其实历来都是清楚的：不支持台湾宣布独立，更反对中共武力犯台。其根本点是保持台海局势稳定，保持现状，保住台湾 2300 万人民的生活方式和选择权利。 美国不会公开说 “ 支持台独 ” ，避免刺激中国造成台海局势紧张，因那不符合美国的国家利益和台湾的安全。同时美国更不会像白痴拜登总统那样，在乌战爆发之前高调公开宣布，对俄国入侵乌克兰，美国和北约不会出兵干预，等于开了绿灯。 对中国，川普的两手策略是：在公开场合，给足习近平面子；但在私下，则明确坚定地告诉习近平，只要我川普在白宫，中国就不要想武力犯台，因为 “ 在我这里不可以 ” 。后来有报导说，习近平也表态，只要川普当总统，中国就不会对台动武。所以，这次中美领导人再次会晤，台湾问题也不会成为焦点，美方甚至都不会把它作为重点谈判内容。   合作而不结盟、竞争而不脱钩   去掉国际焦点，这次中美领袖会晤，可能更多聚焦在双方经贸和危机管控问题上。而经贸交易等，是川普的强项。中美之间的关税战早已停火，税率问题已基本确定，所以这次也不存在交锋。只是在中国的稀土出口到美国、美国的高科技出口到中国等问题上，双方可能讨价还价。结果可能一如既往：中国购买美国更多大豆等农产品，缩小美国的贸易逆差，美国对一些限制出口的产品解禁。这些不是像伊朗战争、俄乌战争、台湾安全等那类重大原则问题双方难以让步，而是都有较大交易的空间。 今年五月川普总统访问北京时，中国方面就明确提出，希望把中美 “ 建设性战略稳定关系 ” 作为未来三年以上的框架。美国很可能接受这种建议，因为现在中美双方似乎都已经开始接受一个事实 —— 双方不可能消灭竞争，只能学习如何在竞争中共存，尤其是避免战争。所以 9 月的川普和习近平的中美峰会之后，中美关系的大概率是： “ 对抗降温但并不和解、合作但不结盟、竞争却不脱钩 ” 。   写于 2026 年 8 月 20 日

# New Zealand says China is its most persistent state-backed cyber threat

## New Zealand report identifies China as its most persistent state-backed cyber threat, with foreign espionage actively targeting key government, health, education, and IT infrastructure network.

[Follow us on **Google**](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.jpost.com/)![Image 4:  A LAPTOP with binary codes displayed in front of the Chinese flag. Individuals basically do not care if their personal data are stolen, unless the hacker personally locks them out of their accounts or the theft has some other major concrete negative impact on their lives.](https://images.jpost.com/image/upload/f_auto,fl_lossy/q_auto/c_fill,g_faces:center,h_720,w_1280/514979) A LAPTOP with binary codes displayed in front of the Chinese flag. Individuals basically do not care if their personal data are stolen, unless the hacker personally locks them out of their accounts or the theft has some other major concrete negative impact on their lives.(photo credit: DADO RUVIC/REUTERS)By REUTERS SEPTEMBER 24, 2026 00:21
New Zealand's cyber security agency said [China](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-909403) was the country's most persistent and capable state-backed cyber threat, as foreign actors targeted government agencies and organizations in sectors including health, education and information technology.

The National Cyber Security Center (NCSC), part of the [New Zealand](https://www.jpost.com/diaspora/antisemitism/article-908712) intelligence community, said it had identified activity suspected to originate from foreign state actors that put sensitive New Zealand information at risk.

It linked suspected state-sponsored cyber activity to actors from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, according to its annual Cyber Threat Report released on Thursday.

Advertisement

"Of these nations, the People's Republic of China is the most persistent and capable state actor undertaking cyber activity in New Zealand," the report said.

The assessment is the latest warning from a Western-aligned intelligence agency over alleged [Chinese cyber espionage](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-906925), which Beijing has routinely denied. It follows a report from New Zealand’s security agency in August that said that China was the only country New Zealand had detected conducting espionage "at ​scale."

New Zealand First leader Winston Peters reacts during an interview in his office at Parliament House in Wellington Tuesday, 22nd September 2026 (credit: REUTERS/Marty Melville)

### **Chinese state-backed actors accounted for 86 nationally significant cyber attacks**

The [Cyber Security](https://www.jpost.com/business-and-innovation/article-908500) report said 86 of 369 cyber incidents deemed to be of potential national significance in the year to June 2026 had suspected links to state-sponsored actors. The incidents included activity targeting government agencies, health and education organizations, and IT managed-service providers.

Advertisement

The agency warned that geopolitical competition was increasingly playing out in the South Pacific, where it was aware of state-backed cyber espionage targeting governments and infrastructure.

New Zealand has close family, cultural, political and economic ties across the Pacific, and such activity could affect citizens, businesses and civic institutions, it said.

State-backed actors were likely to target organizations that operate infrastructure or networks, provide essential public services, or hold information that could offer a strategic advantage, the NCSC said.

It warned that cyber espionage can be difficult to detect, with actors conducting reconnaissance and positioning access in systems over months or years before using it for intelligence gathering or disruption.

Long-running intrusions could lead to the compromise of operational technology and the loss of corporate and personal data, it said.

title: AI at the Trump-Xi summit + Taiwan + EV overcapacities
summary: AI at the Trump-Xi summit + Taiwan + EV overcapacities H.Seidl Wed, 09/23/2026 - 13:00 picture alliance / abaca | Pool/ABACA Download (pdf - 412.67 KB) MERICS Briefs MERICS China Essentials Sep 24, 2026 10 min read AI at the Trump-Xi summit
content: AI at the Trump-Xi summit + Taiwan + EV overcapacities H.Seidl Wed, 09/23/2026 - 13:00 picture alliance / abaca | Pool/ABACA Download (pdf - 412.67 KB) MERICS Briefs MERICS China Essentials Sep 24, 2026 10 min read AI at the Trump-Xi summit + Taiwan + EV overcapacities Top story Trump and Xi will talk AI, but don’t expect a major breakthrough Amid a wave of AI mishaps and calls for regulation, hopes are running high that Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump may find some consensus on AI regulation in their meeting this week. On key trade issues, top officials from both sides had already reached agreements before Trump personally welcomed Xi at the airport on Wednesday: The US extended the suspension of additional tariffs negotiated in the 2025 Busan Agreement until January 10; China will not further tighten export controls on rare earths for the time being. Meanwhile, in the race for advanced AI applications, mistrust between the two countries remains high, making significant agreements or accords on AI seem unlikely. Both governments are likely to focus on small but achievable results. One door-opener that may at least have a chance is the US pitch for a crisis hotline specifically focused on AI. With the two countries locked in a competitive spiral of distrust reminiscent of the Cold War, neither has sufficient incentive to put the brakes on its own AI development. Earlier attempts by the Biden administration to find a common approach were thwarted by Beijing’s demands for Washington to relax trade restrictions on technologies it lacks. From Beijing’s perspective, US government and corporate calls for a slowdown – which until now have remained mere rhetoric – are simply an excuse to “blunt China’s AI advance.” China, already number two in what both sides view as an arms race, faces US export controls on AI chips. It is of course concerned about the lack of controls over rogue AI tech in the US, while Washington worries that an increasingly assertive Beijing would not comply with a negotiated slowdown. China may, however, be more open to bilateral talks now than when Joe Biden was in office. In July, Xi publicly warned for the first time about the risk of “technological loss of control” in AI, and in September, the head of China’s intelligence enumerated concerns about increasingly sophisticated and autonomous AI systems. Last week, China’s most influential standard-setting body for AI released the third version of a framework for developing safety standards. Still, safety guardrails for China’s own AI industry are still lacking. A grand bargain between the US and China on AI safety is highly unlikely. Still, the fact that the world’s two major AI powers may be resuming some form of bilateral dialogue is encouraging. Even a seemingly small win like a crisis-communication channel could go a long way in averting or managing AI incidents before it is too late. Rebecca Arcesati , Head of Science, Technology and Innovation Program (Co-lead) MERICS Media coverage and sources: POLITICO: ‘The scientific, technical term is BS’: Inside the new Bessent-China AI hotline China Daily: 'Dr Frankenstein' alarm cries of US' AI elites a self-serving bid for profit: China Daily editorial Lianhe Zaobao (CN): 中国国安部长陈一新提AI六大风险：系统影响政治安全环境 (China’s Minister of National Security Chen Yixin mentions six major AI risks: AI systems affects the political security environment) Cyberspace Administration of China (CN): 《人工智能安全治理框架3.0》发布 (‘AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0’ published) DigiChina: Forum: Xi Jinping Headlines World AI Conference METRIX 110% This is the percentage by which the number of PhD graduates in China grew in the last decade, rising from around 54,000 in 2015 to almost 113,000 in 2025. Despite this jump, China still counts only 62 doctoral graduates per million people, one quarter of the rate of the US and Europe, where there are 240 and 230 PhDs per million, respectively. But, as PhD admissions jumped from around 74,000 in 2015 to more than 201,000 in 2025, China is likely to continue closing this gap. The question is, to what end? Academic and professional opportunities for PhDs are already failing to keep pace with the number of graduates. Anecdotal evidence suggests that elite secondary schools, for one, are becoming attractive alternatives. Shenzhen Middle School, for example, employs more than 100 teachers with doctoral degrees at its central campus, about one quarter of teaching staff there. (Source: Caixin /Ministry of Education Statistics)  Topics Washington and Beijing needle each other over Taiwan, despite May summit pledges Despite pledging to pursue “strategic stability” after Xi Jinping and Donald Trump’s last meeting in May, both the Chinese and US governments have continued to test each other over Taiwan – albeit in more low-key ways. In the spirit of what it has called “a constructive relationship of strategic stability”, the Trump administration has only twice ordered US warships to cross the Taiwan Strait since May 2025 and effectively halted foreign military sales to the self-ruled island since Trump’s visit to China. And Beijing, in its quest for what it calls “constructive strategic stability”, has refrained from major military exercises in the Strait since its 29-31 December 2025 drills, which were a reaction to Washington’s last weapons sale to Taiwan. But the security situation in the Asia-Pacific remains tense beneath the surface. China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) has continued to patrol the waters and skies near Taiwan in recent months. Meanwhile, US allies and other regional partners have remained engaged in sustaining the island and the fragile security order across the Strait. The Philippines reportedly will allow Taiwan to open a second representative office, as tensions with China over the South China Sea remain high; two Royal New Zealand Navy warships transited the Taiwan Strait on 18 September to demonstrate what Wellington called “continued interest and commitment to the region”; and Japan in March 2026 started deploying new cruise and hypersonic missiles, weapon systems capable of striking Chinese cities such as Shanghai and Nanjing. Developments in the Asia-Pacific suggest a novel dynamic in which other regional actors have partly compensated for growing uncertainty over US security engagement with Taiwan – a good, but also potentially fraught shift for the island, given the immense strain Trump has placed on US alliances and partnerships.” Aurelio Insisa , Senior Analyst, MERICS More on the topic: MERICS China Security and Risk Tracker 01/2026  Media coverage and sources: State Council of the People’s Republic of China: Xi steers China-U.S. relations towards stability Reuters: China's Xi expected to press Trump to halt Taiwan arms sales under 1982 agreement, sources say Nikkei Asia: Taiwan to open new Philippines mission in diplomatic push, sources say  Reuters: New Zealand naval ships transit contested Taiwan Strait China says it wants to curb EV overcapacity – but other priorities point the other way China’s latest five-year plan for the car industry calls for better control of production capacity – but the conflicting goals of maintaining global competitiveness, domestic employment and economic stability are likely to limit any positive effects for foreign car companies suffering under China’s electric vehicle (EV) export glut. The government’s 15th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the Intelligent Connected New Energy Vehicle Industry, released early September, seeks to entrench China’s global leadership in EV sales, supply chain integration and technological innovation for autonomous driving – and officials have explicitly invited more foreign firms to produce vehicles in China for the global market. Despite Beijing’s worries about overcapacity, European companies and policymakers should expect even more competition from Chinese manufacturers. The plan for the first time calls for better management of the car industry’s production capacity through investment supervision for new projects, market consolidation, and enhanced tech and safety standards, which could drive out underperforming players. This comes after repeated calls from regulators to address overcapacity, and particularly the destructive competition that results from it – aggressive price-cutting to gain market share that squeezes profits. But efforts to curb overcapacity are likely to encounter broader social and economic priorities. Local governments are, in particular, likely to resist shuttering factories to avoid increasing unemployment, taking responsibility for stranded assets and sunk costs – and conceding defeat in the race between regions to produce the nation’s next EV or autonomous-driving champion.   The Chinese government has been calling for an end to cutthroat competition driven by overcapacity in the auto sector. But conflicting political goals and techno-industrial ambitions are likely to keep officials from disrupting the status quo, leaving Chinese companies with little choice but to seek further expansion abroad.” Sophia Pradels , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (CN): 工业和信息化部等九部门关于印发《智能网联新能源汽车产业发展“十五五”规划》的通知 (MIIT and Eight Other Departments Release the “15th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the Intelligent Connected New Energy Vehicle Industry”) Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (CN): 工业和信息化部举行新闻发布会 介绍智能网联新能源汽车产业高质量发展情况 (MIIT Holds Press Briefing on the High-Quality Development of the Intelligent Connected New Energy Vehicle Industry) State Council (EN): Intelligent connected NEVs set to boost China's auto industry upgrade Automotive World: China targets 70% NEV sales and mass self-driving by 2030 New immigration rules help Beijing enforce supply chain and tech security New cross-border travel rules in effect since September 15 are now helping Beijing restrict entry and exit if travelers fail to comply with China’s expanding economic and technological security regime. This raises new risks for both Chinese and foreign nationals. Exit bans in the case of criminal investigations and debt disputes have long been possible, but the new rules significantly expand the possible grounds for restrictions on visitors and citizens alike. The new conditions now tie travel into or out of the country closely to China’s growing supply chain security, countersanctions and export controls. This allows Chinese authorities to block Chinese citizens from exiting if they have special expertise in strategic fields such as AI, engineering, advanced manufacturing or rare-earth processing or have worked in a sensitive industry such as defense.  China may also prevent foreigners from entering or leaving the country if they or their employer are under investigation or have been placed on a countermeasures, unreliable entry or sanctions list or if they are deemed a threat to China’s supply chain security and broader national security interests. This means substantial new risks for international residents or visitors if they or their companies engage in supply chain diversification, due diligence, or anything that can lead to penalties or placement on one of these lists. Recent years have seen a significant easing of travel regulations to draw international visitors, with offers of visa-free entry and streamlined access to services on the ground. But political and business representatives visiting China should not be blinded by the open-door policies and keep this new addition to the laundry list of geopolitical risks in mind.
