title: Human Rights Council reprisals debate highlights growing trend of transnational repression - ISHR
summary: On 23 and 24 September, the UN Human Rights Council discussed the 2026 report of the UN Secretary-general on reprisals against persons or groups working with the United Nations. The [report](https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documen
content:
On 23 and 24 September, the UN Human Rights Council discussed the 2026 report of the UN Secretary-general on reprisals against persons or groups working with the United Nations.

The [report](https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/hrbodies/hrcouncil/sessions-regular/session63/a-hrc-63-62-aev.pdf) cited 32 States, while flagging that it omitted ‘verified claims’ that involved four other countries out of security concerns for the victims. Eight of the countries named are current members of the Human Rights Council – Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Egypt, France, China, India, Pakistan and Viet Nam. Another – Germany – is seeking election to the body in October, while Burundi is running for reelection.

The Secretary-General’s report highlighted the trend of transnational repression tactics deployed in acts of reprisals against exiled activists and groups related to their work with UN mechanisms, citing ‘at least 43 individuals and four organisations’ affected in 15 of the 32 States mentioned overall.

> 'Because human rights activists on the ground are those best equipped to inform the UN and about the challenges it should address, it is paramount that they be able to access the UN safely and freely. No one should face retaliation for defending their community and their rights on the global stage. States need to do better to protect those who expose violations at home or abroad.'

Madeleine Sinclair, Director of ISHR’s New York office and long time expert on reprisals

ISHR has long fought to denounce the practice of States taking retaliatory action against human rights defenders and organisations that engage with the UN. This year, our annual campaign to [#EndReprisals](https://ishr.ch/campaigns/endreprisals2026/) sought to highlight the plight of six activists that have had to seek refuge outside their countries as a result of their work, but who remain at risk or have been targeted through transnational repression tactics.

Transnational repression involves governments attempting to silence, intimidate, or punish people or organisations based abroad because of their work, including engaging with UN mechanisms, or of real or perceived acts of political or social dissent. Transnational repression can take the form of extrajudicial killings, torture, harassment, arbitrary detention, travel bans, expulsions, deprivation of nationality, misuse of international law enforcement mechanisms, including INTERPOL Red Notices, intimidation of family members and associates, and more.

Exiled Hong Kong pro-democracy activist **Anna Kwok**, who was cited in the report, read a statement during the Council debate urging States to support victims of transnational repression and prevent governments from resorting to it.

Kwok was one of six defenders highlighted in ISHR’s campaign alongside the four Burundian lawyers **Armel Niyongere, Dieudonné Bashirahishize, Vital Nshimirimana** and **Lambert Nigarura**, and exiled Egyptian journalist **Basma Mostafa**

> 'In this global fight to defend human rights, no matter where we are, feeling safe is a privilege. I, a Hong Konger pro-democracy activist, am among many global rights defenders who live every single day knowing we are being watched and threatened.'

Anna Kwok

Ten States also took the floor to highlight individual cases of reprisals and urge perpetrators to resolve them, including those of defenders highlighted in ISHR’s current and past campaign to end reprisals.

Speaking on behalf of Canada and New Zealand, Australia’s representative called for the protection of Nicaraguan human rights defenders in exile, and the release of pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong and of Russian Indigenous rights activist Daria Egereva. Representing the Benelux States, Belgium raised the cases of Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Chow Hang-Tung, Vietnamese journalist Pham Doan Trang, Cuban political prisoner Roberto Pérez Fonseca and Russian activist Alexey Gorinov.

Liechtenstein named Russian lawyer Violetta Fitzner, the Belarus Human Rights Lawyers association and of the Human Rights House Foundation organisation, also mentioning the cases of Anna Kwok and her fellow Hong Kong activist Carmen Lau. Germany raised the cases of Daria Egereva, her fellow Russian Indigenous rights activist Natalia Leongardt, and Chow Hang-Tung, while Denmark spoke about imprisoned Bahraini activist Abdulhadi Al-Khawaja. Finally, the United Kingdom spoke about Carmen Lau, Violetta Fitzner, and of the four Burundian lawyers Armel Niyongere, Dieudonné Bashirahishize, Vital Nshimirimana and Lambert Nigarura.

On 23 September, over 130 UN Special Procedures mandate holders and members of Treaty Bodies endorsed an [unprecedented statement](https://ishr.ch/latest-updates/over-130-human-rights-experts-issue-global-call-for-states-to-end-transnational-repression/) pointing to the ‘growing challenge’ that transnational repression poses to human rights. They called on all States to take steps to bolster their national legislation to punish and prevent such acts, and called for greater protection for the individual activists and groups that are being targeted by cross-border campaigns that violate human rights and fundamental freedoms.

**We urge States to continue publicly raising cases of individuals and groups that are victims of reprisals; call on the UN and States to work to ensure safe and unhindered access to the United Nations for those who need it most; and call on governments to take coordinated action to deter the spread of transnational repression tactics and offer better protection to those at risk.**

UN human rights experts released a landmark statement urging States, businesses, INTERPOL and international organisations to prevent and combat the spread of transnational repression, warning of its increasing impacts on human rights, democracy and the rule of law and those who take action to defend them.

In a joint statement published today, 21 civil society organisations - including ISHR - called for the renewal of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela.

Ahead of the expected release of feminist journalist and prominent #MeToo activist Sophia Huang Xueqin on 18 September, ISHR and 59 other civil society organisations urge Chinese authorities to ensure her release and guarantee that she can exercise her human rights without surveillance, harassment, retaliation or other arbitrary restrictions.

title: 十一年后，秦伟平再致习近平：请开启政治改革、恢复与达赖喇嘛对话、重新审视政治表达案件

content: —— 习近平访美之际，秦伟平再次公开呼吁中国走向改革与和解 习近平主席： 今天是2026年9月24日。 此刻，您正在美国华盛顿访问。这是您自2015年以来再次对美国进行国事访问。 十一年前的2015年9月，在您首次访美前夕，我曾发表《十问习近平》公开信，就中国政治改革、公民权利、互联网自由、选举、环境、反腐等问题向您提出询问，也曾表达希望能够与您进行公开对话的愿望。 那封信后来在中国大陆互联网受到封锁。 十一年过去了。 今天，当您再次来到美国，我想再次给您写一封信。 这一次，我不再提出十个问题。 我只想提出三个请求： 请开启中国政治改革。 请恢复与达赖喇嘛的直接对话。 请重新审视因政治表达和公民权利活动而被判刑的案件。 一、请开启中国政治改革 习近平主席，中国过去十多年发生了巨大的变化。 中国的经济、科技、军事和国际影响力都有了显著发展。 但在我看来，一个国家的现代化，不应只体现在经济实力和国家力量上，也应该体现在一个社会能否通过制度、法律和公共讨论，和平地处理不同意见与政治分歧。 我并不认为中国必须照搬任何其他国家的政治制度。 中国有自己的历史、文化和现实，中国完全可以探索一条适合自身国情的政治改革道路。 但我仍然相信，中国不能永远回避政治改革。 一个社会不可能永远只有一种声音。 不同意见也不应该自动意味着敌我关系。 和平批评政府、表达不同政治观点，应当拥有更大的法律和公共讨论空间，而不应被简单等同于对国家安全的威胁。 因此，我希望您能够推动中国逐步扩大公民参与和公共讨论的空间，进一步保障公民基本权利，让政治分歧更多通过制度、法律和对话来解决。 中国需要的不是混乱，也不是暴力革命。 我更希望中国能够通过和平、理性、渐进的方式完成政治改革。 在我看来，改革并不意味着削弱中国。相反，一个能够允许不同意见通过制度表达和竞争的社会，可能拥有更加持久的稳定与活力。 二、请恢复与达赖喇嘛的直接对话 习近平主席，第二件事情，我想谈西藏。 过去十三年里，我曾四次见到达赖喇嘛尊者。2016年，我曾与他进行过大约一个小时的交流； 就在两周前，我又在达兰萨拉见到了91岁的达赖喇嘛尊者。 这些经历让我更加相信： 西藏问题不应该成为中国人和藏人之间永远无法跨越的鸿沟。 北京有自己的立场，达赖喇嘛方面也有自己的立场。 双方存在分歧并不可怕。 真正令人遗憾的是，如果双方因为存在分歧，而长期失去直接沟通的渠道。 历史上，中方与达赖喇嘛方面并非从未有过接触。2002年至2010年间，双方曾举行九轮正式对话，最后一轮于2010年1月举行，此后正式对话长期没有恢复。 与此同时，达赖喇嘛方面长期提出的“中间道路”并不以西藏独立为目标，而是主张在中华人民共和国框架内寻求真正的自治。中方对此有不同的立场和解释。 正因为双方存在如此长期而复杂的分歧，我才更加认为，对话本身具有意义。 对话不等于投降。 坐到谈判桌前，也不意味着任何一方必须事先接受对方的全部主张。 恰恰因为存在分歧，才更需要沟通。 因此，我希望习近平主席能够采取实际行动： 与达赖喇嘛恢复直接接触和对话。 第一步甚至不需要解决所有问题。 可以先恢复沟通，先让双方坐下来谈。 如果未来能够通过和平对话逐步处理西藏问题，这不仅可能改善藏人与中央政府之间的关系，也可能成为中国政治进程中的一次重要突破。 有时候，真正重要的第一步，并不是找到最终答案，而是重新开始谈话。 三、请重新审视因政治表达和公民权利活动而被判刑的案件 第三件事情，是我长期以来一直关注的问题。 我希望中国能够进一步扩大和平表达政治观点、参与公共事务和进行公民活动的空间，也希望能够重新审视那些因相关活动而长期失去自由的案件。 其中，我特别希望您能够关注 许志永、丁家喜 两人的案件。 2023年4月10日，山东法院以“颠覆国家政权罪”判处许志永14年有期徒刑、丁家喜12年有期徒刑。美国国务院随后公开要求中国释放两人，并认为相关案件涉及对表达、集会等基本自由的限制。与此同时，中国政府则表示，两人的行为构成相关犯罪，案件依法审理，丁家喜的上诉也于2023年11月被驳回。 我今天再次提出他们的名字，并不是要否认任何国家维护公共秩序和国家安全的权利。 我只是希望，在涉及政治表达、公民活动和国家安全的案件中，能够有更加充分、透明和具有公信力的法律程序，也能够给社会留下通过法律、讨论和对话解决政治分歧的空间。 政府可以不同意一个人的观点。 一个人也可以批评政府。 但一个社会如何对待持不同意见的人，往往能够反映这个社会对自身制度和未来的信心。 因此，我呼吁： 重新审视许志永、丁家喜等因政治表达或公民权利活动而长期失去自由的案件，并在符合法律和实际情况的前提下，考虑释放、减刑或采取其他能够减少长期羁押及其家庭代价的措施。 我尤其希望，他们能够有一天重新回到家人身边。 这不仅关系到两个人的个人命运，也关系到中国社会未来如何面对不同意见。 我也希望有一天，能够自由回到故乡 这也是我今天必须谈到的一件个人事情。 我出生在中国。 我的成长经历、人生记忆和家庭联系，都与中国密不可分。 如今我生活在美国，但我与中国的联系从未中断。 我希望有一天，像我这样长期生活在海外、曾经公开表达过不同政治观点的人，也能够安全、自由、体面地回到自己的故乡。 我希望能够回湖北看看，看看这些年中国发生了什么变化，探望家人，也可以和不同政治观点的人坐在一起吃饭、聊天。 我同样希望，那些与我政治观点不同的人，也拥有这样的自由。 一个人的政治观点，不应该决定他能不能回到自己的故乡。 我相信，一个真正有自信的中国，可以允许不同观点的人回来，可以允许不同意见存在，也可以允许曾经批评政府的人与自己的国家重新建立联系。 如果有一天，一个曾经批评过政府的人能够自由回到自己的故乡，而一个与他观点完全不同的人也能够坐下来与他喝茶、聊天，那么我想，这本身就是一种政治成熟。 十一年后，我仍然愿意对话 2015年，我发表《十问习近平》的时候，中国互联网封锁了这封公开信。 这些年来，我也一直没有停止对中国问题的思考。 十一年过去，我的生活发生了变化，中国也发生了变化，世界同样发生了变化。 但我一直没有改变的一点，是我仍然相信： 中国的问题，需要中国人自己面对；中国的未来，也需要中国人自己讨论。 我知道，一封来自海外的公开信，不可能解决中国复杂的政治和社会问题。 我也知道，政治改革、西藏问题以及政治表达相关案件，都不是简单的问题。 但是，我仍然相信，面对问题本身，比回避问题更加重要；保持对话，也比彼此对立更加重要。 所以，十一年后的今天，我再次选择公开写下这些话。 不是因为我认为自己拥有改变中国的力量。 而是因为我相信： 中国的未来值得每一个中国人关心，也值得每一个与中国有联系的人表达自己的看法。 十一年以前，我曾以《十问习近平》的方式向您提出问题；今天，我不再重复那些问题，只想把这封信中的三个请求留给您，也留给这个时代： 让政治改革重新成为中国可以讨论的话题，让对话重新成为解决分歧的方式，让那些因为表达不同意见而失去自由的人，重新拥有回到家人身边的可能。 我希望有一天，中国能够以对话代替对立，以改革化解分歧，以宽容面对不同声音。 也希望有一天，我能够自由地回到自己的故乡。 十一年过去，我仍然愿意把这些话公开写给您。 因为我仍然相信，对话并不意味着放弃立场，而是给未来留下可能。 习近平主席，期待有一天，我们能够真正坐下来对话。   秦伟平 美国 2026年9月24日

title: America Is Losing the Ability to Train Tomorrow’s China Experts. The Trump-Xi Summit Can Help.
summary: Long-standing educational programs such as Fulbright, Boren, and the Critical Language Scholarship are all suspended. A leader-level deal could bring them back and protect the students who take part. ## By experts and staff Published Septem
content:
Long-standing educational programs such as Fulbright, Boren, and the Critical Language Scholarship are all suspended. A leader-level deal could bring them back and protect the students who take part.

## By experts and staff

Published September 23, 2026 1:02 p.m.

*   ![Image 1](https://assets.cfr.org/images/t_cfr_1_1/f_auto/w_1024/v1772033537/0020_Rush-Doshi-079-copy/0020_Rush-Doshi-079-copy.png)

Derk Bodde set out for Beijing in 1948 expecting to spend a quiet year translating an esoteric work of Chinese philosophy. Instead, as the first recipient of the newly created Fulbright fellowship in China, he found himself an eyewitness to the Chinese Communist Party’s takeover, and his account of what he saw became a rare firsthand record for policymakers, academics, and the American public. When China closed to foreign contact for the next quarter-century, Bodde’s expertise didn’t just remain useful: it was irreplaceable.

Bodde’s story is a clear example of the ways in which in-country research is a proven and often indispensable tool to strengthen American expertise of foreign countries—and not only with friendly nations. But as Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping prepare to meet tomorrow in Washington, DC, only around two thousand Americans are studying in China, down from fifteen thousand a decade ago, and the public and private ecosystem that once supported deep American study of China is collapsing precisely when it is needed most.

That decline is due both to funding cuts and legitimate concerns that students may face risks of arbitrary detention in China. Currently, two American academics have been [designated](https://www.state.gov/releases/office-of-the-spokesperson/2026/08/statement-from-assistant-secretary-dylan-johnson-on-wrongful-detention-designation-for-u-s-citizen-min-zin) as wrongfully detained after traveling to China for academic purposes, creating risks that must be addressed by Beijing. Such cases are rare—the vast majority of Americans who study in China do so without incident—but they are real, and their chilling effect reaches far beyond the individuals involved. At the upcoming summit, Presidents Trump and President Xi should elevate specific programs like Fulbright into leader-level deliverables, with President Xi’s high-profile support for them at the summit providing implicit assurances that participants will not face undue risks from China’s security services.

This approach has some precedent. Exchange programs sometimes receive broad protections from leaders. Indeed, even at the height of the Cold War, the United States established the International Research and Exchanges Board (IREX) in 1968 as a formalized, bilateral academic exchange mechanism, sending generations of American Sovietologists into the Soviet Union, even as the two countries remained locked in rivalry. IREX and its successors, including the Committee on Scholarly Communication with the People’s Republic of China, which managed similar style exchanges with China before diplomatic normalization, were established to lend U.S. government protection to academic exchanges deemed essential to the national interest.

By contrast, the China programs that built a generation of expertise are now defunct. The Fulbright Program has been [suspended](https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2020/07/16/trump-targets-fulbright-china-hong-kong) in China since 2020, partly over risks that participating students and researchers might be detained by China. Alongside Fulbright, less well-known but essential U.S. government–funded programs specifically designed to encourage greater foreign area expertise in government have been suspended to mainland China, including the Boren Awards, the Critical Language Scholarship, the National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y), and more.

At home, the area studies infrastructure in U.S. universities that was built in the 1950s, including the National Resource Centers, Title VI funding, and Foreign Language and Area Studies (FLAS) fellowships, has been gutted amid cuts at the Department of Education. In recent weeks, new unclear federal restrictions on higher education’s ties to China have pushed some universities to conclude that even nonsensitive academic engagement—undergraduate study abroad included—carries too much risk: the University of North Carolina is the latest institution to [pull down](https://www.insidehighered.com/news/quick-takes/2026/08/31/unc-ends-study-abroad-program-china) its study abroad program.

Critics of travel to China argue that Taiwan offers a safer alternative for Mandarin language study, and that the extent of state surveillance makes the risk of visiting China not worth the potential benefits. But Taiwan’s educational opportunities, while excellent, cannot fully substitute for the loss of access to China’s economy, society, and culture.

America needs a much deeper supply of China experts to handle a fast-changing relationship. In closed-door meetings compiled for the U.S.-China Education Trust’s 2026 report, [_America’s China Talent Challenge_](https://uscet.org/a-uscet-working-group-report-americas-china-talent-challenge-investing-in-deeper-american-understanding-of-china/), stakeholders across the U.S. government, business, and academia described how their sectors depend on American expertise to interpret China’s actions—from geopolitics and security, to trade and supply chains—and to keep the United States competitive. The working group concluded that China expertise must be considered a national resource.

As Trump and Xi meet in Washington, progress on people-to-people diplomacy may be less challenging than in other domains. But both sides can take steps to improve the situation.

First, the Trump administration should negotiate with Beijing to elevate specific programs, from named legacy programs—including the Fulbright, Boren, Critical Language Scholarship, and NSLI-Y—to new initiatives, into summit deliverables. President Xi’s endorsement of these programs would provide implicit protection for those students who participate in them. President Trump could privately push to formalize assurances that participants will face no risks from China’s security services. And to make that gesture credible, Beijing should release detained academics.

Second, in tandem with these negotiations, the United States should reverse cuts to funding programs, which are in many cases entirely unrelated to China. The area studies infrastructure built nearly eighty years ago, to include National Resource Centers, Title VI funding, and FLAS fellowships, has been gutted and should be restored. Congress should also fund new programs, purpose-built for today’s U.S.-China relationship. Scrutiny of university ties to China is in some cases warranted, but it should be scoped so that nonsensitive academic engagement, such as undergraduate study abroad and language programs, are able to proceed with appropriate safeguards.

To some, these proposals may seem unrealistic. But they are rooted in history and pragmatism. Washington has long had educational programs in countries with competitors and adversaries. Those programs were often sustained by leader-level understandings that they would be insulated from competitive dynamics in the relationship. Improving mutual understanding is inherently valuable. For both Washington and Beijing, it also reduces the risk of miscalculation. If the next generation of policymakers has no China experience, both countries will suffer.

A United States that no longer trains people who can read Chinese primary sources, sit in Chinese classrooms, or track policy implementation on the ground is hardly more secure and is substantially less capable. Rebuilding China expertise is not an act of goodwill toward Beijing. It is a hard-nosed investment in the United States’ atrophying ability to understand and compete with its most consequential rival.

The United States and China have few bright spots in the bilateral relationship, and fewer still that could be elevated into summit deliverables. Naming and insulating a handful of exchange programs from political and security pressures is in fact one of the most straightforward areas for cooperation that exists between the two countries.

title: Explainer: Why new war in Ethiopia’s Tigray threatens to trigger wider conflict
summary: Ethiopia’s Prime Minister, Abiy Ahmed, addresses the commencement of construction of the Bishoftu International Airport in Abusera, Ethiopia, January 10, 2026. REUTERS/Tiksa Negeri/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https
content:
Ethiopia’s Prime Minister, Abiy Ahmed, addresses the commencement of construction of the Bishoftu International Airport in Abusera, Ethiopia, January 10, 2026. REUTERS/Tiksa Negeri/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/ethiopia-begins-125-billion-construction-of-africas-biggest-airport/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjhZSUE1SE80Sg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

LONDON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - Regional forces in northern Ethiopia's Tigray on Wednesday seized control of three airports and clashed in multiple locations with federal troops, signalling the start of a [major offensive](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopian-airlines-suspends-flights-tigray-region-2026-01-07/) after months of growing tensions.

The move shatters a peace deal that ended the 2020-2022 conflict between ​the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and federal forces, and comes amid a backdrop of deteriorating ties between Ethiopia and Eritrea, ‌Sudan's civil war, tensions over Red Sea access, and the Horn of Africa being dragged into Middle East conflicts.

Report Ad![Image 2](blob:http://localhost/a2f9abce2c7bd7e72f7c1065e8e25533)

## WHY DOES NEW FIGHTING IN TIGRAY THREATEN A WIDER WAR IN ETHIOPIA?

The Pretoria Agreement, which formally ended a conflict that killed hundreds of thousands of people, has been under strain for months, each side accusing the other of violating ​the deal.

The peace process began to unravel after [splits](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopias-pm-abiy-appoints-new-leader-tigray-administration-2025-04-08/) emerged within the TPLF, and a hardline faction of the party [reasserted control](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tigray-party-restores-pre-war-government-threat-northern-ethiopia-peace-2026-05-05/) over the ​region, kicking out an interim administration.

Most recently, the TPLF formed an [alliance](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/seven-ethiopian-armed-groups-announce-anti-government-alliance-2026-09-21/) with six other armed groups from across ⁠Ethiopia, including former enemies from the war, aimed at overthrowing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

It is not clear how many members of the alliance ​were involved in clashes on Wednesday but Ethiopia is home to many heavily armed regional groups.

Abiy's government has accused Eritrea of financially backing members of ​the alliance, allegations Asmara has denied.

## WHAT ROLE WILL ERITREA PLAY?

As the situation unfolds, all eyes will be on Asmara, which has endured a turbulent relationship with Addis Ababa since independence in 1993.

Soon after coming to power, Abiy [won the Nobel Peace Prize](https://www.reuters.com/article/world/ethiopias-abiy-wins-nobel-peace-prize-for-resolving-conflict-with-eritrea-idUSKBN1WQ12X/) in 2019 for ending two decades of hostility between Ethiopia and Eritrea.

When the civil war erupted ​the following year, Eritrean forces then supported Ethiopia's federal army. Relations have deteriorated since the Pretoria peace agreement, which Eritrea was not party ​to despite having fought in the war.

Access to the Red Sea is another flash point.

Landlocked Ethiopia had a coastline for decades until Eritrea broke away. Since then, Addis ‌Ababa has ⁠repeatedly argued that restoring access to the sea - specifically the port of Assab - is vital for its long term security and economic development. Asmara has said it fears Addis Ababa will try to take Assab by force.

Earlier this month, the US government [lifted sanctions](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-removes-sanctions-eritrean-defense-forces-treasury-website-shows-2026-09-18/) on Eritrean Defense Forces and other entities.

It is not clear what impact removing sanctions would have on any conflict in Ethiopia, but the move is seen as a nod by the ​Trump administration to Eritrea’s [strategic coastline](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-lift-eritrea-sanctions-red-sea-tensions-reshape-alliances-document-says-2026-05-05/) opposite ​Saudi Arabia, and warning Ethiopia not ⁠to go to war with Asmara.

## WHICH REGIONAL RISKS RAISE THE STAKES THIS TIME AROUND?

Diplomats warn that a renewed Tigray war would no longer be a largely isolated Ethiopian conflict.

Instead, it would unfold as the Horn of Africa ​faces its most volatile security environment in years, with war raging in Sudan, persistent instability in Somalia, ​tensions over the Nile ⁠and expanding war and geopolitics from the Middle East spilling into the region.

Ethiopia has been accused of [backing](https://www.reuters.com/investigations/ethiopia-builds-secret-camp-train-sudan-rsf-fighters-sources-say-2026-02-10/) the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary group, which is fighting Sudan’s army in one of the world’s deadliest conflicts.

This support, which Ethiopia denies, is in line with its close relationship with the United Arab Emirates, the ⁠most active ​Gulf power in the region which UN experts say is also supporting the RSF. ​The UAE has denied the accusations.

For its part, Eritrea is closer to Sudan and has cultivated relatively close ties with Egypt, which is a long-time rival of Ethiopia. Egypt and Sudan ​both see Ethiopia's Grand Ethiopian [Renaissance Dam,](https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/ethiopia-opens-africas-largest-hydroelectric-dam-egyptian-protest-2025-09-09/) built on a tributary of the Nile, as a serious threat to their vital water supplies.

Editing by Alexandra Hudson

title: Communist Party names new Tibet party chief in regional leadership reshuffle
summary: Beijing has appointed a new party chief in Tibet as the Communist Party shuffles regional leaders ahead of its [21st national congress](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3341249/china-warns-against-do-nothing-officials-ahead-
content:
Beijing has appointed a new party chief in Tibet as the Communist Party shuffles regional leaders ahead of its [21st national congress](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3341249/china-warns-against-do-nothing-officials-ahead-2027-leadership-reshuffle?module=inline&pgtype=article).

Hu Changsheng, 62, will serve as the party secretary of [Tibet autonomous region](https://www.scmp.com/topics/tibet?module=inline&pgtype=article), leaving his post as party secretary of Gansu province to Wu Xiaojun, 60, currently the party chief of Qinghai province.

Meanwhile, Luo Dongchuan, 60, Qinghai’s governor, will succeed Wu as party secretary of the province.

The 21st party congress is expected to be held next year and will shape the leadership line-up for the next five years. Leadership changes at the provincial level ahead of the congress could offer clues about the party’s broader personnel arrangements and political line-up.

Hu spent the early years of his career in Sichuan province before transferring to Qinghai in 2015. In 2017, he was reassigned to Fujian province, where he headed the provincial party organisation department. He was appointed party secretary of the city of Xiamen in 2019 and was promoted to deputy party secretary of Fujian in 2020 while continuing as Xiamen’s party secretary.

President Xi Jinping spent more than a decade working in Fujian, where he served as party secretary of the provincial capital Fuzhou from 1990 to 1996, and as the province’s deputy party secretary from 1995 to 2002.

Hu became governor of Heilongjiang province in 2021 and party chief of Gansu in 2022.

Luo, who holds a doctorate in law, has extensive experience within the judicial system, having served in Beijing’s local courts and the Supreme People’s Court. In 2015, he was transferred to the Communist Party’s [Central Commission for Discipline Inspection](https://www.scmp.com/topics/central-commission-discipline-inspection?module=inline&pgtype=article), where he assumed the role of director of the case trial office.

After his tenure as head of the regional commission for discipline inspection in Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region from 2017 to 2018, he returned to the Supreme People’s Court as vice-president, later assuming an additional role as president of its Intellectual Property Court.

Luo also worked in Fujian as chief of the provincial political and legal affairs commission from 2020 to 2021, and as the provincial deputy party secretary from 2021 to 2024.

Luo was transferred to Qinghai where he was appointed deputy party secretary in 2024 and as governor last year.

Wu spent most of his career in Jiangxi province until being relocated to Qinghai in 2021. He was appointed governor of Qinghai in 2022 and party secretary in 2024.

content: 虽然 One Nation 已公布计划限制移民，但似乎没有任何政治家能够阻止的“外国入侵”——是不断涌入澳大利亚车道的进口双排座 SUV。 随着福特 Ranger 和丰田 HiLux 的“豪华”版售价超过 7 万美元，而预算型中国双排座车型充斥市场，三菱 Triton 则悄然在澳大利亚开辟了最务实的中间地带。 三菱于今年 5 月更新了 Triton，但这不仅仅是调整配置清单。 日本品牌升级了底盘，采用更低的前弹簧率、橡胶车身衬套和高响应减震阀，以防止空载时车厢像失控的蹦床一样颠簸。引擎舱内搭载的是相同的 150kW/470Nm 2.4 升双涡轮增压柴油发动机。 我们的测试车型为 GLS 版本，目前 MY25 版本有真皮座椅从 56,990 澳元起价的优惠，但新车型现价为 57,490 澳元起价，优惠将持续至 9 月 30 日。 简评 你最讨厌什么？ Kel● 双排座尺寸难以适应狭窄的购物中心停车场● 仪表盘设计显得过时● 空载时的行驶质感对日常活动来说仍然太硬 Grant● 双涡轮增压柴油发动机在高负荷下噪音较大● 驾驶员监控系统会在你长时间注视侧后视镜时发出警告——但它确实有所改进● 从首发定价开始就有定期折扣……但二手车保值率依然令人惊讶地坚挺 你最喜爱什么？ Kel● 新增的仪表盘弹出式杯架● 市场领先的 10 年质保带来的安心感● 运动套件物超所值 Grant● 起价优势● 易于访问车内仪表和操控按钮● 凭借良好的经销商网络享有品牌长期价值 你得到了什么？ 三菱 Triton 一直是我们在双排座市场中为那些希望保留经典可靠车标而选择的性价比之选。 选择中配 GLS 版本正好处于双排座市场的理想位置。外部亮点包括 18 英寸灰色合金轮毂、重型床栏、LED 大灯，以及 2026 款式的哑光黑色动态盾格栅搭配黑色后视镜盖。 车内采用软质包裹表面，带有银色对比缝线，配备双区自动空调、无线智能手机充电板、无钥匙进入及一键启动功能，以及自动防眩目内后视镜。信息娱乐系统由 9.0 英寸中央触摸屏控制，支持无线 Apple CarPlay 和有线 Android Auto，搭配 7.0 英寸驾驶员显示屏。 此外，还新增了两个仪表盘弹出式杯架——这是一项小小的工程成就，会让任何手持早晨冰拿铁的人感到由衷的喜悦。 我们的测试车配备了可选运动套件（$3244），包括黑色运动杠、底盘防护、挡泥板、软质车篷盖和黑色格栅徽标。我们还选择了豪华内饰选项，真皮座椅和前排加热额外收费 1500 澳元。 在所有权方面，三菱在该细分市场领先，提供 10 年/20 万公里质保，只要你按经销商网络要求保养车辆，即可享受道路救援服务。 Mitsubishi Triton GLS 可选真皮内饰的车厢功能。 驾驶体验如何？ 涡轮增压柴油发动机动力表现合理，提供充沛的中段扭矩，让你轻松加速至高速公路速度而不费吹灰之力。 在右脚大力踩踏油门的情况下，发动机变得异常喧闹，伴随着工业柴油发电机陷入恐慌的轰鸣声。 三菱 Super Select 四驱系统非常出色。与某些分时四驱系统不同，它允许你在干燥沥青路面上直接切换全时四驱，而不会卡滞传动系统，在拖车或暴雨驾驶时提供安心保障。 2026 款底盘更新在澳洲道路上带来了真正的胜利。得益于更软的前弹簧、高响应减震阀和新型橡胶车身衬套，Triton 不再试图将你的肾脏从尖锐坑洼或郊区减速带上甩出去。虽然空载时的行驶质感仍保留了作为载重型工作车的固有硬朗特性，但它比前代车型更加平滑且不那么苛刻。 至于它是否优于同平台的日产 Navara，这存在争议——Navara 拥有专为澳洲路况定制的悬挂系统。 即使是臭名昭著的驾驶员监控系统这次也感觉更好了。只要你分神几秒钟调整空调温度或查看侧后视镜，方向盘上方的摄像头就会立即像长途旅行中的后排乘客一样，用无尽的唠叨提醒你。 抛开电子保姆不谈，调校的转向和更优的车身控制让 Triton 在长途乡村公路上行驶起来异常稳定、可预测且轻松自如。 我们的城市、乡村和高速公路混合使用场景使 Triton 实现了 8.1L/100km 的合理燃油经济性。 我们对三菱 Triton GLS 的测试显示平均燃油消耗为 8.1L/100km。 你会购买吗？ Kel：我确实能欣赏高坐姿和拥有能装载半个 Bunnings 货物的托盘的粗犷魅力，但 Triton 对我来说并不合适。即使悬挂系统已升级，空载时的行驶质感对日常郊区驾驶来说仍然太硬，而试图将这位宽肩巨兽塞进狭窄的购物中心停车场，简直是一场高风险的几何学练习。 Grant：在一个高端双排座车型轻松超过 8 万美元的市场中，Triton GLS 是一个出色的价值主张。提供全时四驱能力、3.5 吨拖拽能力，以及三菱 10 年/20 万公里质保带来的无与伦比的安心感，售价低于 6 万美元，对于任何重视长期安心感和财务理性而非单纯车标地位的人来说，绝对是必须考虑的选择。 一览无余 三菱 Triton GLS 价格 57,490 澳元起价引擎 2.4 升 4 缸双涡轮增压柴油，150kW 和 470Nm，四轮驱动，6 速自动变速箱质保 10 年 20 万公里（含经销商保养），否则为 5 年 10 万公里及同等期限的道路救援服务保养封顶价格 5 次 2705 澳元/次，间隔每年或 15,000 公里安全 8 个安全气囊，前向和反向自动紧急制动，自适应巡航控制，盲区预警带车道变更辅助，驾驶员监控系统，前后驻车雷达，交通标志识别拖拽 3500kg 刹车拖拽，350kg 拖车球载荷，载重 1071kg油耗 7.7L/100km备胎全尺寸

title: 澳洲机场突击检查，4 名中国旅客遭遣返，大批航班罢工与高温天气接踵而至
summary: 马上！澳洲出行季要来了！机场、航班、天气接连出状况！ 刚查获14.5万支香烟， 澳洲一家航空公司传来消息，地勤员工准备罢工24小时。 与此同时，悉尼、墨尔本周末突然大升温： 最高气温将冲到33℃， 随后又迎来明显降温！ 而现在，学校假期马上开始，圣诞、新年也正在逼近，对于准备出门的华人来说，接下来这段时间真的要多留意了。 被查出14.5万支香烟 墨尔本机场近期再次查获大批非法烟草，澳洲边境执法局（ABF）表示，4名中国籍旅客从上海飞抵墨尔本后，被工作人员选中进行行李检查。 结
content: 马上！澳洲出行季要来了！机场、航班、天气接连出状况！ 刚查获14.5万支香烟， 澳洲一家航空公司传来消息，地勤员工准备罢工24小时。 与此同时，悉尼、墨尔本周末突然大升温： 最高气温将冲到33℃， 随后又迎来明显降温！ 而现在，学校假期马上开始，圣诞、新年也正在逼近，对于准备出门的华人来说，接下来这段时间真的要多留意了。 被查出14.5万支香烟 墨尔本机场近期再次查获大批非法烟草，澳洲边境执法局（ABF）表示，4名中国籍旅客从上海飞抵墨尔本后，被工作人员选中进行行李检查。 结果一查，在4人的行李和箱包中发现了大量香烟： 总数量达到145,529支！ 按照相关税费计算，这批香烟涉及的逃避关税金额约为25万澳元。 其中一名旅客的行李中，还发现了2320个被禁止的加热烟草产品以及电子烟相关配件。 值得注意的是，这起案件中，相关人员并没有因为这次烟草案件被起诉，但签证被取消并遣返。 而这并不是墨尔本机场近期第一次查获大批非法烟草，ABF数据显示，在上一个财年，墨尔本方面查获了： 超过21.4万支非法香烟， 以及约3.4吨散装烟草！ 今年4月，还有3名女性在墨尔本机场被查出携带约160公斤散装烟草。 ABF表示，机场方面会通过行李检查等方式，针对非法烟草及其他违禁品进行查缉。 对于经常往返澳洲和中国的华人来说，这里有一个很重要的提醒，回澳洲时，千万不要把“带了但不申报”和“带了以后主动申报”混为一谈。 很多人以为澳洲机场主要检查的是现金、香烟和违禁品，实际上，生物安全检查同样非常严格。 如果从海外坐飞机回澳洲，行李中常见的肉类、食品、种子、植物材料、木制品等，都可能涉及澳洲的生物安全规定，并不是说这些东西全部都不能带，关键在于： 有些需要符合特定条件， 有些则不能带入澳洲！ 澳洲农业、渔业和林业部明确提醒，旅客需要如实申报相关物品，并接受生物安全人员检查。 尤其需要注意的是，从2026年7月1日开始，澳洲一个penalty unit： 已经提高到364澳元！ 对于机场生物安全违规，最低的infringement notice可以是2个penalty units，也就是728澳元。 如果涉及被认定为高生物安全风险的物品，罚款金额可能提高到6个penalty units$2,184，或者12个penalty units：$4,368。 如果涉及为了逃避检查而藏匿相关物品，infringement notice金额最高可以达到： 20个penalty units， 也就是$7,280！ 所以真正需要注意的，并不是只要行李里有食品就会被罚，而是明明带了，却没有申报，或者工作人员询问时，没有如实说明。 澳洲农业部门明确说明，如果旅客主动申报并接受检查，即使最后工作人员判断某件物品不能带入澳洲，单纯因为如实申报该物品，并不会因此受到相应的生物安全处罚。 换句话说，不确定能不能带的时候，申报比隐瞒更重要，机场工作人员检查之后，如果物品确实不能入境，可能要求旅客将其丢弃或者采取其他处理方式。 但如果选择不申报，被查出来之后，情况就完全不同了，而这次墨尔本机场查获大批香烟，也再次提醒大家。 澳洲入境检查并不是只看护照和行李是否超重，烟草、电子烟以及生物安全相关物品，都可能成为检查重点。 而除了入境检查之外，近期准备坐飞机出行的人，还要留意另外一个变化： Qantas部分地勤员工 Qantas地勤大罢工来了 墨尔本悉尼华人出行注意！ 根据最新消息显示，最多约650名Qantas地勤员工： 准备进行24小时工业行动！ 根据工会公布的安排，维州的相关工作人员将在下周三进行24小时行动，随后，其他州的相关工作人员将在周四跟进。 这场劳资纠纷已经持续了11个月，Transport Workers’ Union（TWU）表示，员工希望改善包括工资、工作保障以及安全条件在内的问题。 此前，约350名参与投票的相关员工中，有97%支持采取工业行动，Qantas方面则表示，双方仍然通过Fair Work Commission进行谈判，公司希望最终协议能够包括年度加薪以及更多全职岗位机会。 同时，Qantas已经准备了应急方案，以尽量降低工业行动对乘客和运营造成的影响。 目前，这批参与工业行动的地勤人员，主要负责的是Qantas Freight货运业务，以及QantasLink部分区域航班的地勤服务。 其中大约650名员工里，绝大多数负责Qantas Freight，另外一部分负责悉尼机场的QantasLink航班。 悉尼旅客需要特别留意 QantasLink区域航班！ 如果你的行程是从悉尼机场搭乘QantasLink前往部分区域城市，就需要提前确认具体航班是否受到影响。 而对于墨尔本来说，这次工业行动的重点是维州相关地勤工作人员在周三进行行动。 不过，最新资料同时显示，这些参与行动的工作人员不负责Qantas国内干线和国际航班，也不负责其他机场的QantasLink航班。 因此，大家不要简单理解成，墨尔本周三Qantas全面停飞，悉尼周四也全面停飞，实际受到影响的范围要小得多。 但如果你的行程涉及相关地勤服务，尤其是区域航班、悉尼QantasLink以及货运业务，还是需要提前确认。 这次工业行动之所以受到关注，还有一个原因： 学校假期马上开始了！ 维州、昆州和北领地的学校假期即将到来，正好也是不少家庭开始出行的时候。如果相关航班受到影响，一些前往区域地区的旅客可能需要调整行程。 与此同时，由于大部分参与行动的员工负责Qantas Freight， 货运也可能受到影响！ TWU表示，如果货运受到影响，包括Australia Post包裹运输出现延误，责任应该由Qantas承担。 Australia Post则表示，如果工业行动最终发生，已经准备了详细的应急方案，并会与货运合作伙伴合作，尽量减少对客户和配送服务的影响。 所以，对于最近准备从墨尔本或悉尼坐Qantas出行的人来说，现在最重要的并不是把它理解成Qantas全面停飞。 而是看清楚自己的航班是什么类型，是否涉及相关QantasLink服务，以及出发机场和行程有没有受到影响。 尤其是学校假期马上开始，如果近期已经买好了机票，最好提前查看Qantas的最新航班信息： 相关QantasLink航班！ 这样比到了机场之后才发现行程发生变化要稳妥得多。 所以，近期准备出行的华人，除了提前查看航班状态之外，其实还有一个很容易被忽略的因素，就是天气。 毕竟现在已经进入春季，学校假期和周末出游的人越来越多，天气变化也会直接影响自驾、航班以及户外活动安排。 而这几天的澳洲天气， 一次非常明显的反转！ 悉尼墨尔本周末一起热起来！ 最高比平均高12℃！ 澳洲天气最近又开始变脸了，就在前几天，东南澳还受到冷空气影响，不少地方明显降温，部分地区甚至出现霜冻。 最新预报显示，悉尼、墨尔本周末都将明显升温，部分东南澳地区气温甚至会： 墨尔本周六最高约26℃，周日进一步升至27℃，以晴朗天气为主，不过周日风力会明显增强，有望成为当地近三年来最热的9月天气之一。 悉尼则更加热，周六最高约31℃，周日西区可能达到33℃，市区也会达到接近30℃的水平。 但这波高温不会持续太久！ 墨尔本周日27℃，周一直接降到15℃，悉尼周日33℃，周二也可能跌至19℃… 所以最近在墨尔本、悉尼生活的华人，衣服真的还不能完全换季。 墨尔本未来7天天气： 周六（9月19日）｜25℃ / 13℃ 大部分晴朗，阳光充足，午后体感温暖，是一周最舒服的出行日之一。 周日（9月20日）｜27℃ / 14℃ 本周最热的一天，大部分晴朗，但风力明显增强，下午外出会感觉偏干燥、偏大风。 周一（9月21日）｜15℃ / 11℃ 冷空气杀到！最高温暴跌至15℃，白天有阵雨，随后天气逐渐放晴，出门记得带伞和外套。 周二（9月22日）｜17℃ / 7℃ 雨停转晴，天空晴朗，不过清晨只有7℃，昼夜温差达到10℃以上。 周三（9月23日）｜20℃ / 7℃ 阳光回归，气温缓慢回升，早晚依旧偏冷。 周四（9月24日）｜25℃ / 10℃ 再次回暖到25℃，大部分时间多云到晴，春天的感觉重新回来。 周五（9月25日）｜26℃ / 17℃ 白天温暖舒适，傍晚开始云量增多，晚间有阵雨可能。 总结来说，从周日27℃，到周一只剩15℃，短短24小时骤降12℃，墨尔本人又要经历一天过两季。 悉尼则是典型的先热后凉，周末到周一连续三天维持28℃，几乎就是初夏体感，但随后一股降温天气接棒，阵雨也会陆续出现。 周六（9月19日）｜28℃ / 14℃ 晴空万里，白天阳光猛烈，紫外线较强，外出注意防晒。 周日（9月20日）｜28℃ / 15℃ 继续晴朗，高温稳定在28℃，非常适合海边、野餐和户外活动。 周一（9月21日）｜28℃ / 19℃ 白天依旧炎热，到了下午至夜间天气开始转变，阵雨概率大幅增加。 周二（9月22日）｜19℃ / 14℃ 本周变化最大的一天，最高温直接跌到19℃，全天有阵雨，体感比前一天凉了近10℃。 周三（9月23日）｜22℃ / 14℃ 天气依旧不稳定，可能出现间歇性阵雨，外出最好备一把折叠伞。 周四（9月24日）｜23℃ / 16℃ 局部仍有阵雨，不过白天比周二稍暖一些。 周五（9月25日）｜26℃ / 15℃ 雨水退场，阳光重新上线，最高温回升至26℃，迎来新一轮好天气。 总结来说，悉尼将连续三天28℃，但周二将突然降到19℃，夏天体验卡很快就到期了。 所以这几天如果准备周末出门，墨尔本可以抓紧享受一下27℃的暖天气，悉尼尤其是西区则要注意周末高温和较强紫外线。 但别急着把厚外套全部收起来，这轮升温来得快，降温也来得快。 对于在澳洲生活的华人来说，一年里最容易出门的几个时间，马上又要到了，有人准备趁假期带家人出去玩，有人准备坐飞机回家，也有人已经开始计划圣诞、新年的旅行。 可能和往年不太一样， 局部仍有阵雨，不过白天比周二稍暖一些。 周五（9月25日）｜26℃ / 15℃ 雨水退场，阳光重新上线，最高温回升至26℃，迎来新一轮好天气。 总结来说，悉尼将连续三天28℃，但周二将突然降到19℃，夏天体验卡很快就到期了。 # Yemen conflict displaces 112,000 people inside country, thousands flee to Djibouti, UN migration agency says

By [Olivia Le Poidevin](https://www.reuters.com/authors/olivia-le-poidevin/)

September 18, 2026 9:31 AM UTC Updated 2 hours ago

*
*
*

*
*
*
*
*

GENEVA, Sept 18 (Reuters) - At least 112,000 people have been displaced inside Yemen within the last two weeks as fighting continues along the country's west ​coast amid a renewed [conflict,](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthis-strike-saudi-targets-anew-talks-over-strait-hormuz-stall-2026-09-15/) while nearly 3,000 have fled by sea to ‌Djibouti, the United Nations migration agency said on Friday.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure while advancing along Yemen's Red Sea coast towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a ​key shipping route. Responding to the Houthi offensive, the Saudi and Yemeni air ​forces have bombarded Houthi targets.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Fyemen-conflict-displaces-112000-people-inside-country-thousands-flee-djibouti-un-2026-09-18%2F)

Nearly 3,000 people have crossed the Gulf of ⁠Aden to Djibouti in the Horn of Africa in less than a week as ​escalating violence have forced more families to flee, Sandrine Desamours, the representative for the UN’s ​refugee agency, UNHCR, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Djibouti.

The government of Djibouti is preparing for the arrival of up to 10,000 refugees - which will add acute pressure on the country’s health ​care and education services, she said.

Item 1 of 3 People rest outside a tent at a new camp for displaced people, following clashes between Iran-aligned Houthi fighters and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces, near Aden, Yemen, September 13, 2026. Picture taken with a mobile phone. REUTERS/Stringer

**[1/3]**People rest outside a tent at a new camp for displaced people, following clashes between Iran-aligned Houthi fighters and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces, near Aden, Yemen, September 13, 2026. Picture taken with a mobile phone. REUTERS/Stringer [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/escaped-with-only-our-lives-yemenis-flee-houthi-clashes-to-overcrowded-displacement-camps/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkdJTkFEWldGSA%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

The UN International Organization for Migration said people are ​fleeing on overcrowded boats and arriving with very limited food and water. Most fleeing are Yemeni families ‌seeking ⁠refuge in Djibouti, but IOM is also beginning to see a small number of migrants, mainly from Ethiopia, heading in the same direction.

Additionally, authorities in Somaliland and Puntland have also reported increased arrivals from Yemen, including Yemeni refugees and Somali refugee returnees, though numbers ​remain in the hundreds ​for now, UNHCR ⁠said.

UN agencies described the latest fighting as being a crisis on top of multiple crises as the country’s health services and economy ​have been shattered amid a long [civil war](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/who-is-fighting-yemen-2026-09-10/) between forces of the ​internationally recognised, ⁠Saudi-backed administration and the Houthis created one of the world's biggest humanitarian crises.

The Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast is bolstering Tehran’s hand in its conflict with the US, as the group tightens its ⁠control of ​the [Bab el-Mandeb Strait](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/why-is-bab-el-mandeb-strait-so-important-2026-09-10/), a strategic chokepoint for global ​oil and commodities shipping, more than six months after US and Israeli attacks on Iran.

title: Lost in tabulation: Diverging US-China trade data point to tariff evasion
summary: The United States and China share one of the world's largest and most closely monitored bilateral trading relationships. Yet the official statistics used to assess that relationship are sending sharply different signals. China reports expor
content:
The United States and China share one of the world's largest and most closely monitored bilateral trading relationships. Yet the official statistics used to assess that relationship are sending sharply different signals. China reports exporting more goods to America than the United States says it imports—particularly since early 2025, when the Trump administration sharply increased tariffs on China. Among possible reasons for the gap, the evasion of US tariffs appears to be an important contributor. As a consequence, US bilateral import data for China appear to have become less reliable. The reported decline in US imports from China should not be treated as a clean measure of either economic decoupling or the effectiveness of US tariffs.

From January through July 2026, the US Census Bureau recorded $158.3 billion in merchandise imports from China (including Hong Kong). Over the same period, China reported $258.1 billion in merchandise exports to the United States. The $99.8 billion difference was equivalent to 63 percent of reported US imports from China. This share was nearly five times its 2021–24 average. If the average monthly gap observed from January through July persists for the rest of the year, the cumulative gap for 2026 will exceed $170 billion.

Figure 1 shows how China's reported goods exports to the United States compare with America's reported goods imports from China since early 2024: Both declined sharply starting in February 2025 following US tariff increases.[[1]](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftn1) Their subsequent trajectories diverged. By July 2026, China reported monthly exports to the United States about 4 percent below their 2024 average. By contrast, US-reported imports from China were 26 percent below their 2024 average, indicating a more persistent contraction in bilateral trade.

## Why have US-China trade statistics diverged?

US-China bilateral trade statistics have never fully aligned. Before 2020, the gap was negative: The United States generally reported more imports than China reported as exports to the United States. The pattern reversed in 2020. The gap became positive and averaged roughly 13 percent of US imports during 2021–24. Federal Reserve researchers [estimated](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/did-the-us-bilateral-goods-deficit-with-china-increase-or-decrease-during-the-us-china-trade-conflict-20210621.html) that tariff evasion accounted for about $55 billion of the $88 billion shift in the reporting gap between 2018 and 2020. The tariffs [imposed](https://www.piie.com/research/piie-charts/2019/us-china-trade-war-tariffs-date-chart) in 2025 were substantially higher and covered more goods than the 2018–20 measures.

Tariff evasion can take several forms. Firms may misstate a shipment's country of origin to take advantage of lower bilateral tariff rates or reclassify goods when rates differ across product categories. They may also understate the reported value or quantity of imports. Because import and export declarations are filed separately, underinvoicing can create a gap between reported exports and imports. A recent _New York Times_[analysis](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/07/us/politics/tariffs-trade-import-fraud.html) found that the average value of merchandise per shipping container from China fell by around 40 percent between January 2025 and February 2026. In some cases, Chinese exporters may be responsible for the US customs entries. For example, a Nikkei Asia [investigation](https://asia.nikkei.com/spotlight/policy-asia/china-s-formidable-logistics-sector-challenges-trump-tariff-enforcers) describes allegations that logistics providers used shell companies as importers of record and manipulated invoices to reduce the duties owed. Nikkei separately [reports](https://asia.nikkei.com/economy/trade-war/trump-tariffs/us-scrutiny-deters-some-chinese-tariff-refund-claims-as-others-cash-in) that some Chinese companies have been reluctant to claim US tariff refunds because renewed scrutiny could expose irregularities in the underlying entries.

The effects of tariff evasion are not confined to US-China trade data. False declarations of origin create two gaps in bilateral trade data: a positive gap for the true country of origin, as observed with China, and an offsetting negative gap for the false country of origin. Relabeling of Chinese exports through Vietnam appears substantial. As New York Federal Reserve researchers [note](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/05/in-what-ways-has-u-s-trade-with-china-changed/), its reporting gap runs in the opposite direction from China's (figure 2). From January through July 2026, the United States recorded $149.6 billion in imports from Vietnam, while Vietnam's customs agency reported $105.0 billion in exports to the United States. The resulting $44.6 billion discrepancy is consistent with some Chinese goods being relabeled as Vietnamese, although aggregate data cannot establish exactly how much relabeling occurred.[[2]](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftn2)

## Do other factors explain the current US-China gap?

Other developments have contributed to the gap, but they appear much less significant than tariff evasion. First, the emergence of a positive gap in 2020 coincided with rapid growth in low-value shipments entering under the US _de minimis_ exemption, which [allowed](https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/national-media-release/de-minimis-value-increases-800) eligible imports valued at $800 or less to enter duty free with reduced documentation. China and Hong Kong accounted for roughly two-thirds of US _de minimis_ shipments around this time, [according](https://gava.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/FY2018-2021_De-Minimis-Statistics-update.pdf) to US Customs and Border Protection (CBP). The Congressional Research Service [estimates](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/IF12891.html) that Chinese low-value e-commerce exports to the United States rose from $1.4 billion in 2018 to $22.9 billion in 2024. Since these exports were [more likely](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2025/02/u-s-imports-from-china-have-fallen-by-less-than-u-s-data-indicate/) to appear in Chinese than US reporting, they contributed to the gap.[[3]](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftn3)

However, the United States [ended](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202500424/pdf/DCPD-202500424.pdf) duty-free _de minimis_ treatment for shipments from China in May 2025 and [suspended](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/eo-14324.pdf) it globally that August. China's Ministry of Commerce also issued [guidance](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zwgk/zcfb/art/2024/art_6261fd8d73e745368da54e2b37022514.html) in June 2024 encouraging e-commerce retailers to use overseas warehouses for fulfillment, shifting goods from individual parcels into bulk shipments subject to ordinary customs reporting. The value of global imports entering the United States under the _de minimis_ exemption [fell 26 percent](https://www.cbp.gov/trade/basic-import-export/e-commerce) in fiscal year 2025. This should have narrowed the reporting gap.

Chinese customs data through 2026 reinforce this conclusion. Although the categories shown in figure 3 cover a narrower range of goods than the CBP estimates, their trend remains informative. Chinese exports to the United States in these categories peaked in 2024 and declined thereafter. The US series for low-value imports from China requires a different interpretation. It shows a clear structural break in May 2025, when the _de minimis_ exemption ended and additional entry and reporting requirements took effect. Its subsequent rise likely reflects improved coverage rather than growth in low-value trade. Convergence with the Chinese series should have further narrowed the portion of the overall gap attributable to low-value shipments.

A second possible cause of the US-China reporting gap stems from Chinese exporters artificially inflating export values to claim tax rebates from the Chinese government. The Fed [analysis](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/did-the-us-bilateral-goods-deficit-with-china-increase-or-decrease-during-the-us-china-trade-conflict-20210621.html) cited earlier estimated that changes in Chinese tax incentives accounted for about $12 billion of the $88 billion shift in the reporting gap between 2018 and 2020. There are two reasons to think this was not a major contributor to the gap's recent growth. First, China [eliminated or reduced](https://www.china-briefing.com/news/navigating-chinas-latest-export-tax-rebate-adjustments-implications/) export rebates for selected products beginning in December 2024 and [announced](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/global/china-cut-export-tax-rebates-ease-global-trade-tensions) further cuts in January 2026. This contrasts with the 2018 episode, when it increased rebates to offset US tariffs. Second, Chinese authorities have [intensified](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202604/17/WS69e216b7a310d6866eb44173.html) tax enforcement since 2024, inspecting more than 130,000 firms suspected of fraudulent invoicing.

## Conclusion

The exact causes of the reporting gap remain uncertain. Still, tariff evasion appears the most likely explanation for its recent growth. To better counter tariff evasion and tax fraud, more systematic sharing and matching of transaction-level customs data could benefit both the United States and China. A [framework](https://www.state.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/13029-China-Law-Enforcement-Customs-4.9.1999-1.pdf) for such cooperation already exists, but implementation appears limited. More broadly, the episode illustrates the limits of using discriminatory tariffs to address bilateral trade imbalances. As argued in a recent PIIE [Policy Brief](https://www.piie.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/pb26-12.pdf) by Mary E. Lovely and Christine Y. Wan, such tariffs can redirect trade through third countries without substantially reducing US reliance on Chinese content or China's role in global production. Addressing trade imbalances instead requires [domestic adjustment](https://www.imf.org/en/blogs/articles/2026/07/30/rising-global-imbalances-underscore-need-to-confront-domestic-distortions) on both sides: The United States needs to rein in its large fiscal deficits, which contribute to its trade deficit, while China needs to stimulate domestic consumption and reduce industrial overcapacity.

In 2025, the [average effective tariff rate](https://www.piie.com/research/piie-charts/2025/trumps-tariff-revenue-tracker-how-much-us-collecting-which-imports-are) on US merchandise imports from China and Hong Kong was 30 percent. It remained elevated at 24 percent in 2026, through July, compared with a 6 percent average effective rate for imports from other countries.

[2](https://www.piie.com/blogs/realtime-economics/2026/lost-tabulation-diverging-us-china-trade-data-point-tariff-evasion#_ftnref2). Subtracting the 2021–24 average monthly gap from subsequent observations (through July 2026) leaves a cumulative gap of $109.7 billion for China and Hong Kong and a negative $62.5 billion gap for Vietnam. If Vietnam's gap entirely reflected relabeled Chinese exports, such relabeling would account for 57 percent of the adjusted US-China gap.

title: 菲律宾出动最大型船只和飞机驱离在巴丹群岛海域活动的中国科考船
summary: 菲律宾海岸警卫队星期四(10月1日)表示，菲方通过部署其拥有的一艘最大型船只以及一架飞机，成功驱离一艘在临近台湾的巴丹群岛(Batanes)省北部海域活动的中国科考船。 在菲方船只和飞机驱离中方科考船的过程中，中方一艘海警船曾赶到现场并与菲方船只一度发生对峙，但是并未阻止科考船的离去。 巴丹群岛是菲律宾最北端的省份，北隔巴士海峡与台湾的兰屿相望，两者相距约99公里。 “(菲方的行动)打断了该船未经授权的海洋科学考察活动，并迫使其离开其滞留位置,” 负责南海事务的菲律宾海岸警卫
content:
菲律宾海岸警卫队星期四(10月1日)表示，菲方通过部署其拥有的一艘最大型船只以及一架飞机，成功驱离一艘在临近台湾的巴丹群岛(Batanes)省北部海域活动的中国科考船。

在菲方船只和飞机驱离中方科考船的过程中，中方一艘海警船曾赶到现场并与菲方船只一度发生对峙，但是并未阻止科考船的离去。

巴丹群岛是菲律宾最北端的省份，北隔巴士海峡与台湾的兰屿相望，两者相距约99公里。

“(菲方的行动)打断了该船未经授权的海洋科学考察活动，并迫使其离开其滞留位置,” 负责南海事务的菲律宾海岸警卫队发言人杰伊·塔里埃拉(Jay Tarriela)指出。

中方科考船名为“嘉海科7号”，此前在巴丹群岛附近海域滞留期间，曾被菲海岸警卫队指控伪造位置信息。

菲律宾海岸警卫队表示，他们出动的是长达97米的“特蕾莎·马格巴努阿”号(BRP Teresa Magbanua)巡逻舰和一架飞机。他们指控这艘中国船只自9月28日以来一直停留在伊特巴亚特岛(Itbayat Island)西北约37海里处。

路透社援引菲律宾海岸警卫队的话说，“特蕾莎·马格巴努阿”号驶近至距离“嘉海科7号”不到100码（约91米）处，并放下一艘硬壳充气艇绕行该科考船数圈，同时通过无线电发出质询。

根据菲方的说法，在行动过程中，中方科考船多次改变航向以规避菲律宾船只。一艘中国海警船随后抵达现场，试图掩护这艘调查船，并向菲律宾船只发出了无线电质询。

菲律宾海岸警卫队指出，“嘉海科7号”号称属于私营船只，而中国海警船的介入引发了外界对其与中国政府关系的质疑。菲方认为，这也让人担忧科考船可能在巴丹群岛和吕宋海峡附近海底电缆通道收集数据以及这些数据的用途。

菲律宾海岸警卫队表示，其驱离行动仍在进行中，但目前已迫使“嘉海科7号”离开滞留位置。“特蕾莎·马格巴努阿”号仍继续监视该船，以确保其离开菲律宾的专属经济区。

塔里埃拉在社媒上发文指出，海岸警卫队的“Islander 251”号飞机在低空多次盘旋以支援水上行动，并誓言将继续“挑战、干扰并驱离该调查船，直至其离开菲律宾海域”。

中国驻马尼拉大使馆副发言人郭伟星期四在社媒上贴文称，中方科考船当时正在“中国管辖海域进行正常作业”，并指责菲律宾进行骚扰。郭伟敦促菲律宾停止“对中国正常科学研究活动的挑衅性干扰”。

塔里埃拉随即在社交媒体上予以回击，表示菲律宾海岸警卫队“将继续反对并驱逐那些未经许可、无权在我们海域进行考察的中国科考船！”

菲中两国在南中国海的主权争议由来已久，菲律宾和日本今年5月决定就划定重叠的专属经济区和大陆架展开正式谈判，激怒了北京。中方不仅向菲方和日方提出强烈抗议，还声称菲日双边举措“非法且无效”，理由是这些海域属于由台湾延伸出的中国管辖海域。

一些中国研究人员今年6月提出，巴丹群岛是台湾的自然地理延伸，因此属于中国主权范围之后，围绕这一海域的纠纷和冲突就格外引人注目，尽管这一主张并未得到北京官方的正式认可。

美国驻菲律宾大使李·利普顿(Lee Lipton)上周日就中国阻挠菲律宾向第二托马斯浅滩(中国称“仁爱礁”)执行补给任务发表声明，谴责中国海警和解放军海军采取“危险的阻挡及其他不负责任的动作”。

“美国强烈谴责中国海警和中国人民解放军海军采取危险阻挡及其他不负责任的动作。这些行为对一艘菲律宾船只构成碰撞威胁，并阻止了9月24日一次合法、例行的第二托马斯浅滩补给任务，”利普顿说。

“我们与菲律宾盟友站在一起，并赞扬他们表现出的专业和克制，”利普顿又说。

title: AI: Let’s Not Pause Progress
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: AI bots hide mistakes. They make up data and move files without permission. In response, some call for a ban on superintelligence, while others demand a pause or slowdown. Either move would be a mistake. Despite genuine fears about safety,
content: AI bots hide mistakes. They make up data and move files without permission. In response, some call for a ban on superintelligence, while others demand a pause or slowdown.  Either move would be a mistake. Despite genuine fears about safety, an AI slowdown will prove unworkable.  Consider the challenge of global action. Even if one views a ban, pause, or slowdown as desirable, ask yourself what China will do? Beijing called Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s “ We must pace the frontier ” warning “ fearmongering ,” suggesting that the alarm about AI was a US plot to hinder China’s own innovation.  If China isn’t on board, capable AI models will be available regardless of what the US does. The recent summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump underlined this impasse. No deal to slow or pause AI progress emerged. Instead, Trump said the two leaders “didn’t spend that much time talking about it” and that he had little interest in working with China on AI because “we’re leading by a lot.” A deal with China might even prove counterproductive. Pausing AI development risks accentuating asymmetry between able defenders and rogue actors, whether they be nation states, criminals, terrorists, or simply misaligned models. AI defense can reduce or offset the risk of AI offense. If we delay access to the most capable models, defenders’ hands would be tied.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. When OpenAI bots recently attacked the AI platform Hugging Face, an open-weight Chinese AI model helped  diagnose  the danger. Chinese and American AI models play a crucial role in hardening software systems. For nations under attack, they help identify vulnerabilities.  OpenAI’s Daybreak  cyber defense has been made available to Ukraine and was used by the EU’s cyber agency, ENISA, to identify software vulnerabilities in EU institutions, all of which have been defused.  A catastrophic event is not good for business; companies themselves have a strong incentive to support AI defenders. Post-Hugging Face, OpenAI made a billion-dollar commitment to support frontline defenders of critical infrastructure. Other leading labs are delaying model releases to allow more time for testing. Regulation risks boomeranging. It could slow researchers’ attempts to identify and address safety challenges.  Markets seem to believe AI safety risks are overblown. A good measure of cybersecurity risk is cyber-insurance premiums. Despite the recent alarms, these premiums  declined  by about 4% globally in Q2 of this year, the 12th consecutive quarter in which they’ve declined.  Some specific fields may offer a less clear balance between offense and defence. Could AI spark a new COVID-style pandemic? Not on its own. Bottlenecks such as DNA synthesis and access to a biolab would constrain intelligence, while the incremental gains using AI may remain modest. We should improve control of physical bottlenecks, pathogen detection, and pandemic preparedness. AI may help reduce risks to large-scale threats from asteroids, volcanos, solar storms, floods, and wildfires by improving prediction and detection. The economic growth dividend from AI could also be used to manage and help society adapt and respond.   We should harden critical infrastructure against cyber threats and increase pathogen monitoring. We should not ban “superintelligence” by pausing or slowing AI development, which could put defenders at a disadvantage and hold back AI’s potential to reduce risk. title: ​​Competing WWII Narratives Add To Taiwan Strait Tensions
summary: * [No Comments](https://theowp.org/competing-wwii-narratives-add-to-taiwan-strait-tensions/#respond) History has become a source of disagreement across the Taiwan Strait, as China and Taiwan clash over how China’s role in World War II shoul
content:
*   [No Comments](https://theowp.org/competing-wwii-narratives-add-to-taiwan-strait-tensions/#respond)

History has become a source of disagreement across the Taiwan Strait, as China and Taiwan clash over how China’s role in World War II should be portrayed. Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump met this past week in Washington, D.C. During Xi’s visit, both leaders emphasized the history of the wartime alliance between China and the United States. The White House stated that the countries fought as allies in World War II. Since then, Taiwan has pushed back against this narrative, arguing that it was the Republic of China (ROC), rather than the People’s Republic of China (PRC), that was the formal U.S. ally representing China during World War II.

This disagreement is bigger than simply a debate over the historical accuracy of each side’s claims. Mainland Affairs Council Deputy Minister Shen Yu-chung stated that Taiwan would work through appropriate channels to ensure Washington understands the ROC’s wartime relationship with the United States. China, on the other hand, has connected its interpretation of history to its broader position on Taiwan. During President Xi’s D.C. visit, Xi called on Washington, according to a Chinese government account of the meeting, to take the “correct position” of opposing Taiwanese independence. However, Taiwan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi has stated Taipei received reassurances that U.S. policy toward Taiwan has not changed following the summit.

History should be remembered and taught accurately. Beijing and Taipei therefore have legitimate reasons to care about how their respective histories are being portrayed, but allowing competing narratives strengthens existing political tensions. The Taiwan Strait already faces significant conflict over sovereignty, military activity, and diplomatic recognition. Adding disputes over historical representation could further widen the divide and create more misunderstanding. Both sides should recognize their differing historical interpretations without allowing those disagreements to become another barrier to peaceful dialogue.

This disagreement stretches back over half a century and is rooted in a complicated history that continues to shape Taiwan Strait relations. The ROC governed China during World War II, and both Nationalist and Communist forces fought against Japan. After the Chinese Communist Party defeated the Nationalist government in the Chinese Civil War, Mao Zedong established the People’s Republic of China in 1949, and the ROC relocated to Taiwan. Currently, China claims Taiwan as part of its nation and has maintained that it rejects Taiwan’s sovereignty. Taiwan’s government rejects this. The United States recognizes the PRC, but maintains unofficial relations with Taiwan and, under the Taiwan Relations Act, provides Taiwan with the means to maintain a sufficient self-defense capability.

China and the United States are still engaging in diplomacy, which is a positive development. Despite their disagreements, direct communication provides an opportunity to prevent political disputes from escalating into larger conflicts. The same principle should apply across the Taiwan Strait. China and Taiwan do not need to agree on every detail of their shared and contested histories; instead, they need to communicate about their future. Clearer communication and restraint in using history to advance political claims could reduce the chance of escalation. While the past will always shape cross-Strait relations, it does not have to determine whether their future is defined by conflict or peaceful dialogue.

title: Hong Kong gov’t says it will not appeal court ruling overturning Fanling Golf Course housing approval
summary: The Hong Kong government has said it will not appeal a court ruling that overturned approval for building 12,000 public rental flats on part of the historic Fanling Golf Course. The Fanling Golf Course. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The government
content: The Hong Kong government has said it will not appeal a court ruling that overturned approval for building 12,000 public rental flats on part of the historic Fanling Golf Course. The Fanling Golf Course. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The government said on Thursday that it would not launch a further appeal “having holistically considered legal advice and conducted a cautious assessment,” after losing the case at the Court of First Instance in 2024 and again at the Court of Appeal last month . It will review the proposed public housing plan on a 9.5-hectare plot of land within the 32 hectares that the government took back from the 172-hectare Fanling Golf Course in 2023. “The Government will announce the way forward at an appropriate time,” a spokesperson said in a statement. The case stemmed from a legal challenge launched by the Hong Kong Golf Club, which operates the Fanling Golf Course, against the government’s approval of an environmental impact assessment (EIA) report that greenlighted the public housing development. The Hong Kong Golf Club argued that there was a lack of public consultation when the authorities included additional information in the EIA report, and in 2024 the High Court ruled in favour of the private golf club. Fanling golf course. Photo: Wikicommons. The government launched an appeal against the ruling but lost again at the Court of Appeal last month , with a three-judge panel saying that there was “unfairness” in the consultation process. “[The new information]… was material that ought to have been but was not included in the EIA report for public inspection,” the Court of Appeal judgement read. “The failure to remedy this deficiency by holding a further consultation meant that there was unfairness in the consultation overall,” it added. The government said on Thursday that the ruling had clarified that not all information added to an EIA report necessitates further public consultation – rather, it will be determined on a case-by-case basis. The Environmental Protection Department will study the ruling and maintain the “reasonableness, legality, transparency and credibility” of the EIA regime, it added. Chief Executive John Lee had said that the setback with the Fanling Golf Course public housing plan would not significantly impact supply. Housing chief Winnie Ho said on Wednesday that the government was confident that the average waiting time for a public rental flat could be reduced to 4.5 years before the current administration’s term ends in June next year. The average waiting time for a public rental flat stood at 4.8 years as of last month, according to official figures.

title: Hong Kong child sexual abuse cases surge 60% as NGO urges evidence-based prevention measures
summary: Hong Kong has seen a 60 per cent increase in child sexual abuse cases over the past six years amid a broader upward trend in the maltreatment of minors, a local group has said, calling for evidence-based prevention measures to be strengthen
content: Hong Kong has seen a 60 per cent increase in child sexual abuse cases over the past six years amid a broader upward trend in the maltreatment of minors, a local group has said, calling for evidence-based prevention measures to be strengthened. NGO Against Child Abuse (ACA) holds a press conference calling for the strengthening of evidence-based child protection measures on September 23, 2026. From left: Maple Lau, director of ACA; Patrick Ip, clinical professor at the University of Hong Kong; Patrick Cheung, chairperson of ACA; Rosa Wong, assistant professor at Education University of Hong Kong; Keith Tung, assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong. Photo: Supplied. NGO Against Child Abuse said on Wednesday that the rate of child abuse soared from 0.92 per 1,000 children in 2020 to 1.54 in 2025 – a 67 per cent increase over the six-year period – citing data from the Social Welfare Department’s Child Protection Registry. For the first time in more than two decades, the number of child sexual abuse cases matched that of physical abuse cases against minors, with 501 cases recorded in 2025, the organisation said, calling the situation “concerning.” Physical abuse had long been the most common form of child maltreatment. Patrick Cheung, chairperson of Against Child Abuse, attributed the sharp increase to a myriad of factors, including the Covid-19 pandemic, economic downturn, parenting style changes, as well as recent legislation such as the Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse Ordinance, which was enacted in January. In particular, Cheung said the rise of child sexual abuse was related to internet activities and highlighted the increasing problem of online sexual grooming targeting minors. “A lot of the times we see that the perpetrators of child sexual abuse are peers and people met on the internet,” Cheung said in Cantonese during a press conference. Long-term harm Patrick Ip, clinical professor at the University of Hong Kong’s Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, said studies over the past decade had found that child abuse could inflict long-term harm on children across their social, psychological, behavioural, and biological development. Children play in Hong Kong’s Dino Park located in Shatin in April 2025. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. One 2024 study showed that child abuse survivors exhibited a higher chance of obesity – potentially due to impairment to the brain’s prefrontal lobe, which specialises in self-regulation – while a study in 2022 found that victims reported higher inflammatory responses years after the maltreatment took place, Ip said. Ip also noted that “family dysfunction” has become a severe problem in recent years, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic, when children had to stay home for schooling due to prolonged class suspensions. “Not only does [family dysfunction] diminish familial bonding, it also makes parents incapable and unwilling to maintain quality interactions with their children,” Ip said in Cantonese. “It creates a scenario in which children become used to facing their problems alone. And when there isn’t a good buffering system or support system for struggling children and parents alike, the risk of abuse increases,” he added. Multi-pronged measures But Ip also pointed to a 2022 study that found “positive parenting intervention” – meaning professional support regarding parenting style and emotion management – can improve parent-child interactions in low-income households. The results showed that parenting outcomes are modifiable with the appropriate intervention, which also lowers the risk of child abuse, he said. Children in Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The NGO called on society as a whole to raise awareness around the long-term consequences of child abuse and to increase sensitivity about high-risk families, enabling early identification and support. It also supported calls on authorities to introduce an offence of persistent child sexual abuse in upcoming sex law reforms, which have been championed by rights groups. Asked whether the city should follow countries such as Australia in banning children from social media, Cheung said the city should adopt a multi-pronged approach to prevent online sexual abuse against minors. Society needs to step up education for children regarding how to ensure safety online, while social media platforms should implement measures protecting minors from predators, he said.

content:
Item 1 of 2 Rear Admiral Bob Little, Commander of the US Coast Guard Arctic District, poses for a picture in Oslo, Norway, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Gwladys Fouche

**[1/2]**Rear Admiral Bob Little, Commander of the US Coast Guard Arctic District, poses for a picture in Oslo, Norway, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Gwladys Fouche [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/rear-admiral-bob-little-poses-for-a-photo-in-oslo/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjNMTkFPNzNWVw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

*   Summary

*   Four Chinese research vessels have sailed in offshore US Arctic so far in 2026
*   Compares with a total of five vessels in 2025
*   Ships stayed in international waters but gave no advance notice

OSLO, Sept 21 (Reuters) - The ​United States is watching China's presence in its Arctic zone "very closely" amid concerns regarding the ‌security of the US homeland, a senior US Arctic military official said.

So far in 2026, four Chinese research vessels have conducted work offshore in the US Arctic, compared to a total of five in 2025, Rear Admiral Bob Little, Commander of the ​US Coast Guard's Arctic District, told Reuters.

Sign up[here.](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/undefined?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fchina%2Fus-watching-chinese-marine-presence-off-alaska-arctic-coast-guard-chief-says-2026-09-21%2F)

The Chinese ships sailed in the maritime zones off the US ​state of Alaska, including the Aleutian Islands, into the Bering Strait and as far ⁠north as the North Pole, he said during a visit to Oslo to speak at a conference on ​Arctic security.

"Where I have responsibility, interest and concern is when they are operating in and around US sovereign ​space," said Little.

"So inside of our exclusive economic zones, or over our extended continental shelf, we certainly have a security concern. And so those are the types of activities that we see that we're watching very closely."

The ships remained in international waters ​but had not notified the US of their presence in advance through diplomatic channels, as would be the ​usual practice.

"When we challenge them and query them as to the purpose of their activities, their response typically is either 'we are ‌conducting ⁠operations in international waters' or 'we are conducting scientific research'," he said.

## CONCERNS

The concern is two-fold. One is that China may be involved in scientific research focused on the mineral exploitation of the seabed in an area that belongs to the US, Little said.

The other is that these vessels conduct activity that might "provide them (the Chinese) with a military ​advantage or pose a security ​threat to the United ⁠States", said Little, whose area of operations is nearly as vast as Europe.

China, which calls itself a "near-Arctic" state and wants to create a "Polar Silk Road" in the ​Arctic, has stepped up its presence in the polar region in recent years, sometimes ​in joint ⁠operations with Russia and sometimes alone.

While in Norway, Little discussed with international colleagues how they were dealing with similar activities by Russian research vessels.

"Whether it's the Barents (Sea) or the Baltic (Sea), it's easy to find examples of hybrid threats and ⁠activities," ​he said.

"So I certainly watch that very carefully, because it's the ​same nation-state that's my neighbour on the western side of the Arctic," he said, referring to Russia.

Moscow denies that its research vessels conduct ​illegal activity or that it poses any threat to US interests.

Reporting by Gwladys Fouche in Oslo Editing by Gareth Jones

title: 美中峰会：“大”到不容有失, 也“小”到不容有失
