content: 2026-9-20  Jinhuasan的博客 这是斯科特 · 肯尼迪（ Scott Kennedy ）上周五 9 月 18 日发表在《战略与国际研究中心》杂志关于即将到来的美中峰会的评论。肯尼迪先生是 华盛顿战略与国际问题研究中心 高级顾问兼中国商业与经济研究讲席主任。请读他的评论： 下周川普总统与中国领导人习近平的峰会将是两人今年的第二次会晤，此后可能还会有两次会面。世界上两个最强大国家的领导人能够坐下来讨论双边关系和国际事务，本身就是一项值得肯定的成就。但是，一方面是他们在可能讨论的议题和成果方面有限的雄心，另一方面是世界面临的挑战，两者之间的差距表明，全球领导力正出现一个日益扩大的真空。 太重要，不能允许失败 美国和中国都有强烈的自身利益，需要让两国关系至少在表面上保持平静。美国经济拥有显著优势，主要由人工智能领域的投资推动，但也存在明显弱点，其中包括持续的通货膨胀、不断上升的失业率以及急剧膨胀的债务。债券市场已经摇摆不定，收益率继续上升，这表明人们对于经济基础中根深蒂固的风险越来越感到不安。随着中期选举临近，川普政府此时制造一场双边关系危机并不符合自身利益。 北京很可能也在进行类似的盘算。尽管 —— 或者也许正是因为 —— 中国取得了技术进步，其宏观经济前景同样不稳定，甚至更加不稳定。习近平正处于筹划 2027 年秋季举行的中国共产党第二十一次全国代表大会的最初几个月，这次大会很可能会让他获得第四个五年任期，继续担任中国共产党领导人。与川普一样，一个稳定的国际环境将有助于改善他的政治处境，而这种环境在很大程度上取决于与华盛顿保持和平。 因此，观察人士可以预期，目前的商业休战将得到延长，中国将允许更多稀土流向美国和其他国家（日本获得稀土也是华盛顿高度重视的问题），而川普政府则不会对中国征收累计税率高于 2025 年 10 月釜山会晤时水平的关税。据报道，北京寻求把目前的安排一直延长到川普政府任期结束，而美国则倾向于只延长六个月。显而易见的折中方案将是再延长一年。 目标太小，不会达不到预期 这次峰会不会失败的另一个原因是，人们的预期已经被削减到几乎为零。北京可能希望达成一长串具体成果，而华盛顿则希望清单更短，但双方都没有太大雄心去达成具有突破性的安排和妥协。相反，可以预期的是一些有限的协议、进展和成果，例如双方同意把对对方价值 300 亿美元出口商品的关税降低到标准水平；在波音飞机、飞机零部件和农产品方面达成更多交易；开始讨论人工智能安全问题；在试图结束乌克兰和波斯湾冲突的措辞上作出细微调整；以及强调亚太经济合作组织和二十国集团的重要性。川普和习近平很可能将在 11 月于深圳、 12 月于迈阿密再次会晤，讨论更多类似内容。 不是 “ 两国集团 ” 尽管川普和习近平表面上会相处融洽，但这并不是一个 “ 两国集团 ” 。他们正在寻找管理双边关系的办法，但他们绝不是在作为国际秩序的共同管理者展开合作。任何一方也都没有兴趣提供大量公共产品，为更加持久的稳定创造条件。这是一场受到相互依存、大致均衡的力量对比以及双方处理国内挑战的需要所约束的大国竞争。 鉴于全球力量分布日益广泛、联盟的衰落以及非国家行为体的重要地位，一个 “ 两国集团 ” 从来都无法准确反映美中关系的重要性。尽管如此，这次会晤仍然是一次解决根本性挑战的错失机会，例如宏观经济失衡造成的国际影响、人工智能带来的日益增长的风险、乌克兰和中东的战争以及气候变化。 但是，川普政府本身受到限制，无法采取更多行动。它正在奉行一种帝国式外交政策，主要建立在对主权、硬实力和双边互动的严格强调之上。对于国际合法性以及为负责任行为制定准则、并约束包括美国自身在内所有国家的多边规范的关注，已经不在考虑范围之内。它也不像其他方面那样认为气候变化或人工智能安全构成同等程度的危险。此外，跨部门决策程序的瓦解意味着，川普政府通常是在一个问题与另一个问题之间不断跳转，并没有为长期处理复杂挑战做好充分准备。 因此，政府的战略正在贸易和安全两个方面遭遇障碍，一个领域的问题 —— 例如与北京之间不稳定的休战 —— 正在妨碍其他领域取得成功 —— 例如争取北京在乌克兰和伊朗问题上的帮助。华盛顿越来越发现自己正在多个战线上同时采取守势。 相反，北京完全有可能采取更多行动，但它满足于等待川普政府任期结束，同时阻挡来自欧盟和其他方面的压力，并逐步在其主导的各种论坛中推进自己的全球治理方式，例如上海合作组织和世界人工智能合作组织。尽管习近平很可能会带来一批令人印象深刻的中国领先高科技企业高管，但如果过去可以预示未来，他们不太可能获得展示自己企业和专业能力的空间，这意味着中国将错失向一个重要受众展现其社会更加细致复杂面貌的机会。 错失的机会 每当地球上两个最强大国家的领导人 —— 以及它们的一些顶尖企业 —— 聚在一起时，就存在成就大事的机会。但是，这需要双方持续投入，而目前在任何一个首都，这似乎都不太可能实现。如果没有发生任何严重的问题 —— 而且习近平对川普白宫的新直升机停机坪表达一番表面上的赞赏 —— 双方就会把这次聚会视为一次成功。但其他人不应该这样认为。

title: 为何新的巴基斯坦 – 中国边境协议令印度感到愤懑
summary: 中国士兵在靠近巴基斯坦的克勒扎拉山口附近进行雪地野外演习 多年来，印度一直拒绝承认巴基斯坦和中国在印度声称为其领土的领土上的边界。 上周，巴基斯坦和中国着手将这一边界制度化，引发了新德里的强烈反应。 两国启动了巴基斯坦 – 中国边界联合委员会，巴基斯坦将其描述为“重要里程碑”，这将深化在边境管理、联合勘测、贸易和人员往来方面的合作。 印度反应强烈，拒绝这一举措，称其没有任何法律依据，并表示不承认任何涉及印度声称领土的巴基斯坦 – 中国边界。 这一声明出现在一个特别敏感的时机。
content: 中国士兵在靠近巴基斯坦的克勒扎拉山口附近进行雪地野外演习 多年来，印度一直拒绝承认巴基斯坦和中国在印度声称为其领土的领土上的边界。 上周，巴基斯坦和中国着手将这一边界制度化，引发了新德里的强烈反应。 两国启动了巴基斯坦 – 中国边界联合委员会，巴基斯坦将其描述为“重要里程碑”，这将深化在边境管理、联合勘测、贸易和人员往来方面的合作。 印度反应强烈，拒绝这一举措，称其没有任何法律依据，并表示不承认任何涉及印度声称领土的巴基斯坦 – 中国边界。 这一声明出现在一个特别敏感的时机。 印度和中国正在寻求稳定其关系，此前两国在实际控制线（LAC）沿线经历了多年的军事紧张局势，这条争议线分隔了他们在喜马拉雅边境的大部分地区。与此同时，北京和伊斯兰堡正在深化在印度也声称的边境另一段区域的合作。 “巴基斯坦和中国之间没有边界。我们拒绝所谓的联合委员会，因为它没有任何法律依据，”印度外交部发言人 Randhir Jaiswal 表示。 该委员会涉及巴基斯坦 – 中国边境，包括夏克萨姆谷 该委员会涉及巴基斯坦 – 中国边境，包括夏克萨姆谷，这是一个大约 5,180 平方公里的区域，巴基斯坦于 1963 年割让给中国，但印度声称这是其领土拉达克的一部分。 印度称该领土曾是前邦联国查谟和克什米尔的一部分，被巴基斯坦非法占领后割让给中国。印度政府从未承认该协议，认为其非法无效。 这段历史解释了周三宣布的特别敏感性。 “巴基斯坦无权就其非法和武力占领的印度领土进入相关安排，”印度外交部表示。 巴基斯坦称查谟和克什米尔仍是争议领土，并认为因此印度无权挑战其 1963 年与中国达成的边界协议。它认为该协议有效。 德里·希瓦·纳拉·大学国际关系与治理研究系的 Jabin T Jacob 教授表示，这一新发展代表了一个旧机制的复兴，而非一个全新的安排。 “联合边界委员会在 1963 年中巴协议中有所规定，唯一的问题是将其启动的时机，”他告诉 BBC。 他说时机可能有几个原因，包括中国更广泛的划定边界努力，以及希望在巴基斯坦其他边境经历冲突和不稳定的时期，制度化沿边境的交流和通行。 一辆印度军队车队在靠近中国的公路上驶向列城 Jacob 表示，印度应该对这一发展感到“担忧”。更重要的是，他表示，这一举措似乎忽视了 1963 条约本身的一项规定。 该协议第 6 条规定，一旦克什米尔争端得到解决，无论最终控制该领土的是哪个国家，都将重新谈判，Jacob 表示。 对于印度来说，Jacob 表示，问题因国际信息环境而加剧。 “中国在国际媒体和信息景观中的相对主导地位 – [包括] CGTN、CRI、社交媒体存在 – 相对于印度，使其能够向全球提出其叙事和地图，而印度则局限于那些其他世界首都可能忽略的抨击，”他表示。 印度军队车辆在印度拉达克地区的一座山口附近的道路上行驶 这一担忧与边境本身的实际管理不同。巴基斯坦和中国已经在该地区拥有广泛的基础设施和连通性联系，包括中巴经济走廊（CPEC）和喀喇昆仑公路。 前巴基斯坦驻美大使 Husain Haqqani，现为 Anwar Gargash 外交学院和胡德研究所高级研究员，表示新委员会既具有实用性又具有政治性。 “它是两者的结合，”Haqqani 告诉 BBC。“它是一种增强边境和边界合作、防止非法穿越和保护与 CPEC 相关的战略基础设施的机制。” 他说，这也向印度发出了一个信号，表明北京继续从巴基斯坦的角度看待克什米尔。 “中国从未接受印度关于克什米尔的立场，中国从巴基斯坦而不是印度的角度看待吉尔吉特 – 巴尔蒂斯坦，”Haqqani 表示，指的是巴基斯坦控制的克什米尔地区，该地区与中国接壤，印度声称是其领土的一部分。 Haqqani 表示，伊斯兰堡的立场是根据印度控制下的克什米尔的发展而演变的。 “巴基斯坦仍然坚持查谟和克什米尔的最终地位尚未决定，”他说。“但由于印度在其克什米尔部分进行了内部变化——例如废除第 370 条——巴基斯坦认为没有什么问题，可以简单地制度化自 1963 年以来与中国的既定事实。” 卡拉奇以西的瓜达尔港是中巴经济走廊的关键部分 对于北京来说，这一安排也符合利用与邻国的关系来管理和向印度发出其立场的更广泛模式。 Haqqani 表示，对巴基斯坦在克什米尔方面的保证对北京具有战略和地缘政治价值。 “在战略方面，它进一步加深了与巴基斯坦的联系，在地缘战略方面，它强化了印度对中国和巴基斯坦两面威胁的恐惧，这取悦了巴基斯坦，也造福了中国，” 专家说，声明的时机也很重要。 “中国总是提前数月，甚至数年计划其决定，所以启动联合边界委员会的决定必须是在一段时间前做出的，”Haqqani 表示。 “这一信息的发布是为了在习近平主席最近的金砖国家峰会之旅后，向巴基斯坦发送战略伙伴关系方面的保证信息，并向印度提醒，多边参与并不能转化为中国对南亚的任何愿景的改变，” 但 Jacob 告诫不要将这一发展的每一个方面都解释为针对印度的直接军事行动。 “目前对 LAC 没有任何立即或明显的影响，”他说。 这表明，上周宣布的意义可能更多地在于逐步制度化印度一直拒绝的安排，而不是对争议喜马拉雅边境的立即改变。 印度的立场，Jaiswal 表示，仍然“清晰且一致”：任何试图使德里认为巴基斯坦非法占领印度领土的行为合法化的尝试都是不可接受的，与印度的主权无关。 但 Haqqani 认为，争端超出了边境的法律性。 “印度和中国关于边境和边界的根本分歧是地缘战略性的，而不是地图学上的，”他说。“因此，边境谈判和边境管理机制所能实现的是有限的。” 他还补充说，巴基斯坦仍然是“中国对印度的次要威慑”，而北京与伊斯兰堡的接触将继续向德里发送这一信息。

title: Visa Important Notices
summary: Visa Important Notices -All individuals applying for an A-3, C-3 (if a domestic worker), G-5, H1-B, H-3, H-4 dependent of H-1B and H-3, F, I, J, M, K-1, K-2, K-3, Q, R-1, R-2, S, T, TN, TD, or U nonimmigrant visa are instructed to adjust th
content: Visa Important Notices -All individuals applying for an A-3, C-3 (if a domestic worker), G-5, H1-B, H-3, H-4 dependent of H-1B and H-3, F, I, J, M, K-1, K-2, K-3, Q, R-1, R-2, S, T, TN, TD, or U nonimmigrant visa are instructed to adjust the privacy setting on all social media accounts to “public” or “open” to facilitate vetting necessary to establish their identity and admissibility to the United States under U.S. law. More information is available at Announcement of Expanded Screening and Vetting for Visa Applicants . (Last updated on September 18, 2026) -Read more about diversity visa processing at Diversity Visa Issuance Updated Guidance . (Last updated on August 31, 2026) -Read more about immigrant visa processing at travel.state.gov . (Last updated on August 28, 2026) -AIT/Taipei will be closed due to Typhoon BAVI Due to Typhoon BAVI, the AIT Taipei offices will be closed on Friday, July 10, 2026. Individuals who had nonimmigrant visa interview appointments scheduled for July 10 should wait for further notice from AIT’s Nonimmigrant Visa (NIV) Unit. The NIV Unit will send email notifications to individuals for new appointments soon. Please check your mailbox, including inbox and junk folders. (Posted on July 9, 2026) -Please note that, effective January 1, 2026, the local customer service center number will change. If you are calling from Taiwan, please call 02 7703 4494. If you are calling outside Taiwan, please dial +886 2 7703 4494. (Posted on December 31, 2025) -Pursuant to Presidential Proclamation 10998 on Restricting and Limiting the Entry of Foreign Nationals to Protect the Security of the United States, which takes effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Standard Time on January 1, 2026, the United States is suspending or limiting entry and visa issuance to nationals of 39 countries as well as individuals applying using travel documents issued or endorsed by the Palestinian Authority. Applicants who are subject to Presidential Proclamation 10998 may still submit visa applications and attend scheduled interviews, but they may be ineligible for visa issuance or admission to the United States. For additional details, visit travel.state.gov here . (Last updated on February 2, 2026) -Nonimmigrant visa appointments from December 18th have been rescheduled to the same time on December 19th. If applicants cannot make their visa appointment on December 19th, please reschedule on our visa appointment website starting December 19th afternoon. Additional interview slots will be made available on other days. (Posted on December 18, 2025) -Effective November 27, 2025, all visa issuances to Afghan nationals applying with an Afghan passport are paused until further notice. (Posted on December 10, 2025) -Presidential Proclamation Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers , issued on September 19, 2025, restricts the entry of aliens into the United States as H-1B nonimmigrants if they are seeking to perform services in a specialty occupation. This restriction only applies to H-1B petitions filed with USCIS after the Proclamation’s effective date of September 21, 2025, at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT). For additional details, visit the Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers webpage. (Posted on September 21, 2025) -Applicants for U.S. nonimmigrant visas should schedule their visa interview appointments at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate in their country of residence or nationality. Visa application fees are non-refundable and non-transferable. For more information, go to https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/News/visas-news/adjudicating-nonimmigrant-visa-applicants-in-their-country-of-residence-sep-6-2025.html (Posted on September 7, 2025) -Immigrant visa applicants are now generally required to interview in the consular district designated for their place of residence, or in their country of nationality if requested, with limited exceptions. Beginning November 1, 2025, the National Visa Center will schedule applicants in their place of residence or alternatively, their country of nationality, if requested. If an applicant requests to interview in a location other than the applicant’s assigned consular district or country of nationality, the National Visa Center may request additional information to confirm that location is an applicant’s place of residence, or to confirm whether an exception may be appropriate. For more information, go to Travel.State.Gov – Adjudicating Applicants in Their Country of Residence . (Posted on September 2, 2025) -Pursuant to the Presidential Proclamation on Restricting the Entry of Foreign Nationals to Protect the United States from Foreign Terrorists and Other National Security and Public Safety Threats, which takes effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on June 9, 2025, the United States is suspending or limiting entry and visa issuance to nationals of certain countries. Applicants who are subject to this Presidential Proclamation may still submit visa applications and attend scheduled interviews, but they may be ineligible for visa issuance or admission to the United States. For additional details, visit travel.state.gov . (Posted on June 6, 2025) The post Visa Important Notices appeared first on American Institute in Taiwan .

title: How Yemen's Houthis went from a small mountain militia to a big regional threat
summary: LONDON, September 17 - A lightning advance by Yemen's [Houthi group](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/why-havent-houthis-irans-allies-yemen-stepped-into-war-2026-09-08/) has brought the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait under its control,
content:
LONDON, September 17 - A lightning advance by Yemen's [Houthi group](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/why-havent-houthis-irans-allies-yemen-stepped-into-war-2026-09-08/) has brought the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait under its control, making the once ragged highland militia a regional player with global clout.

This is how the group evolved into a formidable fighting force [with Iranian support](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/trump-says-iran-war-end-after-us-midterm-elections-threatens-attack-pickaxe-2026-09-10/) that can disrupt vital shipping and strike critical oil and gas facilities in neighbouring Saudi Arabia.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/reuters-iran-briefing/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fworld%2Fmiddle-east%2Fhow-yemens-houthis-went-small-mountain-militia-big-regional-threat-2026-09-17%2F)

## WHO ARE THE HOUTHIS?

Starting out in the late 1990s as a Zaydi Shi'ite Muslim revival movement in ​north Yemen under the [Houthi family](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthi-red-sea-offensive-elevates-enigmatic-yemeni-commanders-standing-2026-09-16/), the group waged six wars against the government, building a strong local militia.

When Yemen's central state disintegrated during the 2011 Arab Spring, the Houthis took advantage, ‌gaining more ground and developing a relationship with [Iran](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran/) and its Lebanese ally Hezbollah.

In 2014 they seized the capital Sanaa, ousting the government, and halting a Gulf-backed political transition.

That prompted a Saudi-led military intervention to support the government, leading to years of civil war that ground to a stalemate and a 2022 ceasefire.

The Houthis fired missiles and drones at Israel and international shipping in the Red Sea during Israel's [war in Gaza](https://www.reuters.com/world/israel-hamas/) from 2023-25 in what they said was solidarity with Palestinians.

With their closest ally Iran under attack by the United States ​since February 28, the Houthis have again been firing on Red Sea shipping as well as energy facilities inside Saudi Arabia.

## WHAT IS THE MILITARY SITUATION INSIDE YEMEN?

The ceasefire collapsed over recent weeks and fighting resumed ​along the old front lines: Marib and Jawf governorates in the north, the city of Taiz in the southern highlands, Dhale in central Yemen and the Red Sea ⁠coastal strip known as the Tihama.

Last week the Houthis [rapidly advanced](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/yemens-houthis-reach-strategic-island-mouth-vital-shipping-lane-2026-09-11/) into the southern Tihama, seizing first the port city of Mocha and then the rest of the Red Sea coastline and islands, putting their guns along the whole ​shore of the 12-mile-wide (19-km-wide) [Bab el-Mandeb](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/why-is-bab-el-mandeb-strait-so-important-2026-09-10/) Strait.

Those territorial gains make it easier to block shipping on the Red Sea, a key route for Saudi oil exports to Asia, and set up a potential launchpad for a new ground thrust towards ​Aden.

Saudi Arabia has conducted airstrikes in support of government-aligned forces.

## WHAT DO WE KNOW ABOUT HOUTHI MISSILES AND DRONES?

The group's ability to strike at distance with growing accuracy is why it now matters far beyond Yemen.

Houthi ballistic missiles have reached as far as Israel, more than 1,000 miles (1,800 km) away, and one struck the perimeter of Israel's main airport in 2025. They have struck more frequently in Saudi Arabia, targeting [cities and infrastructure](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/saudi-coalition-says-houthi-drone-destroyed-near-mecca-2026-09-16/). And Houthi missiles have been fired at ships in the [Red Sea](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/yemens-houthis-say-they-fired-missiles-saudi-oil-tanker-red-sea-2026-07-28/), halting traffic in the waterway.

Item 1 of 4 Iran-aligned Houthi fighters pose next to a captured vehicle following what the source described as an attack on Saudi-backed forces in the location given by the source as al Jawf governorate, Yemen, in this screengrab taken from a video released by Houthi Military Media on September 15, 2026. HOUTHI MILITARY MEDIA/Handout via REUTERS

**[1/4]**Iran-aligned Houthi fighters pose next to a captured vehicle following what the source described as an attack on Saudi-backed forces in the location given by the source as al Jawf governorate, Yemen, in this screengrab taken from a video released by Houthi Military Media on September 15, 2026.... [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/battle-between-iran-aligned-houthi-fighters-and-saudi-backed-forces-in-al-jawf-governate/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMlVKTkFDUUUwRg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)Read more

Houthi drones have ​also struck repeatedly at Saudi targets and are now increasingly deployed on the battlefield — a big change from the last bout of civil-war fighting before the 2022 ceasefire.

## WHAT EQUIPMENT HAVE THE HOUTHIS BEEN SEEN USING?

The Houthis have posted ​videos online since the start of September that show some of the military equipment they are using.

Videos show drones dropping different types of mortar and other bombs onto vehicles and opposition fighters, a rocket or missile launching, and precise munition hits on ‌buildings and trucks ⁠at a camp, filmed by a high-resolution drone.

Other videos show Houthi forces on the ground including in pick-up trucks, some mounted with weapons, and on foot. Many fighters are shown in Arab robes rather than uniforms and carrying assault rifles. One video also showed a small group of fighters in camouflage uniforms. In some videos, fighters are shown with light and heavy machine guns and scoped rifles.

Videos showed them parading equipment captured from the Saudi-backed forces in the Tihama including armoured and combat vehicles, a tank, an artillery gun, satellite dish, small arms and a drone jamming device. But the videos do not generally show the captured hardware in action.

## HOW DO THE HOUTHIS GET THEIR WEAPONS?

A United Nations ​panel of experts' report in 2025 said the Houthis ​had developed missile and drone technologies through both ⁠technical assistance and domestic manufacturing.

It found there had been widespread arms smuggling despite a U.N. arms embargo, including overland shipments across the Omani border as well as seaborne smuggling.

Items seized included drone control devices, equipment to receive ships' navigational data, drone engines and missile components. A 2023 U.N. report noted seizures of entire drones, ballistic missile components such ​as chemical precursors and Iranian-made anti-tank missiles.

Iranian sources have said Tehran has supplied its Houthi allies with both weapons and experts. However, Iran has officially denied arming the ​Houthis in violation of the ⁠U.N. arms embargo.

A 2025 assessment by the International Institute for Strategic Studies think tank found that while the Houthis had made advances in domestic arms production, they remained dependent on Iran for key technologies and advanced capabilities.

## IN WHAT OTHER WAYS HAVE THE HOUTHIS DEVELOPED MILITARILY?

The U.N. panel of experts' report described Houthi military tactics as being focused on infiltration, drone attacks and shelling along front lines, and the laying of mines and other explosive devices.

They assessed that the Houthis had 350,000 fighters, ⁠partly through the ​recruitment of fighters under 18.

Training by Iran and Hezbollah has been critical for the Houthis, according to Yemen analysts. Baraa Shiban, an associate ​fellow at the Royal United Services Institute in London, said such training had begun soon after the Arab Spring and had helped the Houthis transform from a militia to a more organised military force with changes to their structure and movements.

Hezbollah missile and drone operatives were present with ​the Houthis in 2025, the U.N. experts said. Iranian Qods Force general Abdolreza Shahlaei was also present in Yemen for some time working with the Houthis, the experts said.

Compiled by Angus McDowall and Edward Carron, Editing by Timothy Heritage

title: 国会指出美中科研合作的国家安全隐患后，NASA暂停4千万美元拨款项目
summary: 众议院中国问题特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)星期五(10月2日)赞扬美国国家航空航天局(NASA)加强科研安全执法。在该委员会今年发布一份报告后，NASA最近采取重大步骤，加强对《沃尔夫修正案》(Wolf Amendment)的执行力度，并暂停总计4000万美元的40个拨款项目，以着手处理报告指出的安全隐患问题。 这位密歇根州共和党籍联邦众议员在声明中说：“NASA采取重要步骤保护美国的科研与创新，理应受到肯定。” 今年5月，穆勒纳尔领导的众议院
content:
众议院中国问题特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)星期五(10月2日)赞扬美国国家航空航天局(NASA)加强科研安全执法。在该委员会今年发布一份报告后，NASA最近采取重大步骤，加强对《沃尔夫修正案》(Wolf Amendment)的执行力度，并暂停总计4000万美元的40个拨款项目，以着手处理报告指出的安全隐患问题。

这位密歇根州共和党籍联邦众议员在声明中说：“NASA采取重要步骤保护美国的科研与创新，理应受到肯定。”

今年5月，穆勒纳尔领导的众议院中国问题特设委员会公布了一份报告，题为《美国太空未来的研究安全：NASA对《沃尔夫修正案》的执法情况》(Research Security for America's Future in Space: NASA's Enforcement of the Wolf Amendment)，检查NASA的安全合规问题以及对《沃尔夫修正案》的执行情况。

《沃尔夫修正案》是2011年通过的法律，禁止NASA在没有国会和联邦调查局批准的情况下出资与中国展开双边研究与活动。

该报告发现有几百个NASA支持或资助的出版文献有美中人员共同署名或机构合作，有可能违反《沃尔夫修正案》。

前弗吉尼亚州共和党籍联邦众议员弗兰克·沃尔夫(Frank Wolf)是《沃尔夫修正案》的推出者。他在那份报告的前言中写道，美国科研环境的开放促进创新，加强美国领导力，“然而，开放并不意味着没有规则。当纳税人资助的研究与国家安全风险发生交集时，美国既有权威也有义务划定明确的界限。《沃尔夫修正案》确立了这些界限。本报告表明，必须采取更多举措来坚守这些界限。”

中国问题特设委员会主席、来自密歇根州的共和党籍联邦众议员穆勒纳尔(左)和来自艾奥瓦州的共和党籍联邦参议员格拉斯利(右)。

今年2月，穆勒纳尔与艾奥瓦州的共和党籍联邦参议员查克·格拉斯利(Chuck Grassley)曾联名致函NASA负责人，对这家美国宇航机构可能资助了“与中国实体的双边合作”提出质疑。众议院中国问题特设委员会还在当时发表声明说，“NASA资助的研究永远也不应依赖与中国军工综合体有关联的实体。”

在该委员会5月份发布那份报告后，NASA对总额超过4000万美元的40个正在进行的研究拨款项目进行审议，检查与中国机构开展双边研究合作时可能存在的违反《沃尔夫修正案》规定的问题，在审议期间，这些拨款项目被暂停。

NASA还启动了行政执法行动，并在其研究安全办公室与监察长办公室之间建立了一项协调机制，以便将经证实的违规行为移交有关机构作进一步调查，而且有可能移交司法部采取执法行动。

此外，NASA制定并实施了一项自动化流程，以主动识别可能涉及违禁或高风险合作的论文成果，并对接受拨款的人员制定了额外的审查程序，以确保合规。

穆勒纳尔在声明中说：“这对主动识别违禁合作并将其移交进行适当执法至关重要。我赞赏NASA领导层和特朗普政府采取这些必要的具体步骤，以保护由纳税人资助的研究工作。”

在众议院中国问题特设委员会对美中科技合作问题提出关切后，美国战争部今年1月采取措施，阻止在美运营的被列为“中国军事企业”的实体接受该部资助的基础研究资金，美国国家科学基金会(NSF)则在今年7月推出新政策，禁止将其科研资金用于与被纳入美国政府各个受限制清单的实体开展合作。

title: Trump denies offering to sell arms to China’s Xi, but says ‘maybe it’s a good idea’
summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday denied asking Xi Jinping if he wanted to buy American weapons, countering his own envoy’s claim that Trump made the offer to his Chinese counterpart. A newspaper featuring a front page photo of the meetin
content: US President Donald Trump on Monday denied asking Xi Jinping if he wanted to buy American weapons, countering his own envoy’s claim that Trump made the offer to his Chinese counterpart. A newspaper featuring a front page photo of the meeting between Chinas President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump is seen at a news stand in Beijing on September 25, 2026. Photo: Greg Baker/AFP. US Ambassador to China David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday that Trump made the extraordinary offer to sell arms to the rival superpower. “I’ve never heard of that one, I’m going to have to ask him,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Purdue’s comments. “They’d probably like to buy it because we do make better equipment than them, so maybe it’s a good idea. But we didn’t discuss it.” Purdue had said Trump made the offer during Xi’s state visit to the White House last week in response to Chinese concerns over US weapons sales to Taiwan. “President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world.’ He actually asked President Xi — would he like to buy some? — at one point,” Perdue said in an interview with Fox News. “There are continuing conversations about other sales, (Trump) and President Xi talk about that every time they get together,” Perdue said, adding that the US position has not changed. A US official told AFP earlier that “the US government has no plans to sell weapons to China”, when asked about Purdue’s remarks. Chinese President Xi Jinping (right) ​paid a state visit ‌to the US between September 23 and 25 at the invitation of President Donald Trump (right). Photo: White House. US arms sales to Taiwan, a self-ruled island which China claims is part of its territory and has threatened to seize by force, have long been a thorny issue between Washington and Beijing. The United States is required by law to supply Taiwan, which has a democratically elected president and legislature, with weapons for its defense. ‘Negotiating chip’ The US State Department said in a statement to The New York Times that “US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.” The Chinese foreign ministry did not directly answer when asked about the comments on Monday. But it said China has “always strengthened its national defense capabilities based on its own needs, and remains committed to maintaining world peace and stability.” Trump has maintained a strategically ambiguous stance over Taiwan, refusing to say directly whether the US would come to its aid if China invades, while continuing to approve weapons sales. Beijing warned Taiwan in June that seeking independence “by relying on the United States or through military means is a dead end.” Washington approved a $11.1 billion arms sale to Taiwan in December, which Perdue said was a sale of “more arms to Taiwan than any other president since 1979.” The US paused a $14 billion weapons purchase by Taiwan in May, with Trump calling it a “very good negotiating chip” in dealings with China, raising fears that Taiwan’s security could be traded away. Taiwan’s annual Han Kuang military exercise on July 9, 2025. Photo: Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense, via X. During his Washington trip, Xi repeated his warning that Trump should show “prudence” over Taiwan, and went further to urge the United States to oppose Taiwan independence explicitly. Trump has declined to say whether he discussed Taiwan with Xi during the visit, preferring to stress what he says is his good relationship with the Chinese leader as the two countries seek to manage their tensions. The two leaders have met twice already this year, with Trump having traveled to Beijing in May. They have confirmed they will meet for a third and fourth time at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, in November and the G20 forum at Trump’s Doral resort in Miami in December.

title: 第二十四篇 信心与交托

content:
**第二十四篇 信心与交托**

**——将一切忧虑卸给神，因为祂顾念我们**

**壹、读经**

**彼得前书五章六至七节：“所以你们要谦卑，服在神大能的手下，使祂到了时候，可以叫你们升高。你们要将一切的忧虑卸给神，因为祂顾念你们。”**

**诗篇三十七篇五节：“当将你的道路交托耶和华，并信靠祂，祂就必行事。”**

**提摩太后书一章十二节：“因为知道我所信的是谁，也深信祂能保守我所托付的，直到那日。”**

**腓立比书四章六至七节：“应当一无挂虑，只要凡事借着祷告、祈求，带着感谢，将你们所要的告诉神；神那超越人所能理解的平安，必在基督耶稣里，保卫你们的心怀意念。”**

**贰、真正的信心必定产生交托**

弟兄姊妹，信心如果是真实的，最终一定会产生一个结果：交托。我们为什么能够把事情交给神？因为我们相信祂。如果我们不认识一个人，就很难把重要的东西交给他。

所以保罗不是说：“我知道我所相信的是什么。”他乃说：“知道我所信的是谁。”信心的中心不是一套道理，乃是一位活的人位——**神自己。**

我们越认识神，就越能信靠神；越信靠神，就越能把自己交给神。所以交托不是一种心理技巧。交托乃是信心所产生的结果。

**叁、为什么我们这么难交托？**

因为我们天然的人喜欢控制。我们希望知道：明天会怎样？事情会怎样发展？别人会怎样反应？我的家庭会怎样？我的工作会怎样？我的身体会怎样？当我们不能控制的时候，忧虑就进来了。所以许多时候，忧虑的背后隐藏着一个问题：我们想控制自己实际上不能控制的事情。但主从来没有叫我们控制明天。

主乃要我们：今天信靠祂。马太福音六章三十四节说：“所以你们不要为明天忧虑，因为明天自有明天的忧虑。”信心使我们把未知的明天，交给已知、可信靠的神。

**肆、“将一切的忧虑卸给神”**

彼得前书五章七节用了一个非常生动的字：“卸给神。”好像一个人背着很重的担子，现在把担子卸下来。这就是交托。有时候我们来到主面前祷告：“主啊，我把这件事交给你。”祷告结束以后，却马上又把它背回来。

一整天继续思想：“怎么办？”“如果这样怎么办？”“如果那样怎么办？”这说明我们虽然祷告了，却还没有完全卸下。所以我们需要学习在祷告中说：“主，这件事我已经告诉你。现在我把它交给你。”当忧虑再回来时，再转向主：“主，我已经交给你，我选择信靠你。”

**伍、为什么我们能够交托？——因为祂顾念我们**

彼得前书五章七节没有只说：“将一切的忧虑卸给神。”后面还有一个非常甜美的原因：“因为祂顾念你们。”这就是我们交托的根据。我们不是把自己交给一位冷漠的神。乃是交给一位顾念我们的父神。

主耶稣在马太福音六章告诉我们：天上的飞鸟，父尚且养活；野地的百合花，神也给它妆饰。然后主说：“你们的天父原知道你们需要这一切。”（太六32）所以我们能够交托，不只是因为神有能力，更因为：祂顾念我们。神有能力，却又爱我们；神有智慧，也知道我们真正的需要。因此我们可以放心把自己交给祂。

**陆、交托不是不负责任**

这里需要有一个重要的平衡。有人可能说：“既然交给神，我就什么都不作。”这不是圣经所说的交托。农夫把收成交给神，却仍然需要撒种、浇灌、劳苦。我们把家庭交给神，仍需要尽家庭的责任；把工作交给神，仍要忠信工作；

把服事交给神，仍需要祷告、预备并尽功用。所以：交托不是把责任推给神；交托乃是尽我们的责任，却把结果交给神。我们负责忠信，神负责结果。这是信心生活非常重要的原则。

**柒、交托与服在神大能的手下**

彼得前书五章六至七节其实是连在一起的：“你们要谦卑，服在神大能的手下……”接着才说：“将一切的忧虑卸给神。”这给我们看见，真正的交托里面包含着：接受神主宰的安排。

我们有时愿意把难处交给神，却附带一个条件：“主啊，你一定要照我的方法解决。”这还不是完全的交托。真正的交托乃是：“主啊，我把需要告诉你，也把结果交给你；你怎样带领，我愿意接受你的旨意。”这需要谦卑。因为我们承认：神比我们更有智慧。

**捌、保罗说：“我知道我所信的是谁”**

提摩太后书一章十二节是信心与交托非常宝贵的一节：“因为知道我所信的是谁，也深信祂能保守我所托付的，直到那日。”保罗能够交托，因为他**认识神。**所以解决忧虑最深的方法，不只是告诉自己：“不要忧虑。”乃是更多认识主。当我们认识祂的信实，认识祂的慈爱，认识祂的智慧，认识祂的主宰，认识祂的能力，我们自然就能说：“主，我可以把自己交给你。”所以真正信心的增长，就是对神认识的增长。

**玖、交托以后，要学习安息**

腓立比书四章六至七节给我们看见一个属灵的次序：忧虑 → 祷告 → 交托 → 平安。经节说：“应当一无挂虑，只要凡事借着祷告、祈求，带着感谢，将你们所要的告诉神。”

接着：“神那超越人所能理解的平安，必在基督耶稣里，保卫你们的心怀意念。”请注意：经节没有说，祷告以后环境立刻改变。却说：神的平安先来保卫我们的心怀意念。这就是交托的一个记号：事情可能还没有解决，我们里面却开始有安息。为什么？因为事情已经从我们的手中，交到了神的手中。

**拾、最高的交托不是交托事情，乃是交托自己**

我们开始学习交托时，通常是交托一些事情：“主啊，我把这个难处交给你。”“我把这个家庭问题交给你。”“我把这个工作交给你。”这些都很好。但神最终所要的，比这些更深。祂要我们说：“主啊，我把我自己交给你。”

罗马书十二章一节说：“将身体献上，当作圣别并讨神喜悦的活祭。”这就是最高的交托——**奉献。**不是只把问题交给主，乃把我们这个人交给主。不是只说：“主，求你处理我的事情。”乃是说：“主，我属于你。”我的时间属于你，我的家庭属于你，我的前途属于你，我的财物属于你，我的服事属于你，我的一生属于你。

**拾壹、交托使我们从自己转向基督**

为什么交托这么重要？因为只要事情一直抓在我们手里，我们的心就一直被事情霸占。当我们把事情交给神，里面就释放出来，可以更多转向基督。

因此：忧虑临到 →我们转向主 →借着祷告交托 →停止倚靠自己 →接受神作平安 →享受基督作供应 →基督更多分赐到我们里面。这样，原来使我们忧虑的事情，反而成为我们经历基督的机会。这就是神圣的分赐。

**拾贰、交托乃是为着神经纶的完成**

我们最终需要看见：神不是只要解决我们人生中的问题。神乃要得着：一个完全向祂敞开、让祂作生命并让祂掌权的人。当我们一直抓住自己，神在我们里面就受到限制。

但当我们说：“主，我把自己交给你。”神就有路更多把自己作到我们里面。于是：信靠 →交托 →敞开 神圣分赐 →生命长大 →性情变化 →与众圣徒同被建造 →基督身体得着实际 →新妇预备整齐。所以交托不是消极的放弃。交托乃是把主权让给神，使神能够在我们身上完成祂的经纶。

**拾叁、结束的话**

弟兄姊妹，第四大段“如何过信心的生活”，我们已经看见一条非常实际的路：凭信而活，不凭眼见；信靠神，不倚靠自己；在祷告中操练信心；在环境中学习信靠神；在等候中相信神的时间；最终，把一切交托给神。

彼得前书五章七节是我们每天都可以经历的话：“将一切的忧虑卸给神，因为祂顾念你们。”当忧虑来的时候，不要一直与忧虑争战。乃要把忧虑变成祷告。每一个忧虑，都可以成为一个交托；每一个交托，都可以成为一次经历基督的机会。所以我们可以简单地告诉主：“主，我不知道明天如何，但我知道你是谁。”“我不能控制环境，但我相信你仍然掌权。”“我不知道结果怎样，但我知道你顾念我。”“所以主啊，我把这一切交给你，也把我自己交给你。”这就是信心与交托。

**应用祷告**

主耶稣，谢谢你，因为你是可信靠的主，也是顾念我的神。主，我承认我常常把许多重担背在自己身上，想控制环境、控制结果，也为明天忧虑。今天我再来到你面前。我愿意将一切的忧虑卸给你，因为你顾念我。主，我把我的家庭交给你，把我的工作交给你，把我的身体交给你，把我的前途交给你，把我的服事交给你，把我所爱、所挂心的人交给你，也把一切我不能控制的事交给你。使我尽我今天该尽的责任，却不把结果抓在自己手中。

主，我相信你的能力，也相信你的智慧；相信你的爱，也相信你的时间。更深地说，主啊，我不只把事情交给你，我把我自己重新奉献给你。我的一生属于你。求你在我里面得着完全的地位，把基督更多分赐并构成到我里面，使我在生命里长大、被变化，与众圣徒同被建造成为基督的身体。愿我们都成为预备好的新妇，使你的经纶得着完成，并终极完成于新耶路撒冷，作三一神与蒙救赎、重生、变化并得荣之人永远团体的彰显。阿们。

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期三(9月23日)将在华盛顿欢迎中国国家主席习近平的到访，两位大国领导人的会谈预计将聚焦贸易、科技、伊朗等议题。在白宫准备以国事访问的最高规格之一迎接习近平之际，台湾也在密切观察这场峰会可能释放的政策信号。

**华盛顿为习近平准备了什么？**

习近平夫妇将在美国华盛顿当地时间星期三傍晚抵达安德鲁斯联合基地(Joint Base Andrews)，这是习近平近三年来第一次访问美国。特朗普总统打破通常在白宫迎接外国领导人的惯例，将亲赴安德鲁斯基地迎接习近平。

星期四，特朗普总统将在白宫为习近平夫妇举行国事访问欢迎仪式。将有479名美军官兵参加仪式，海军陆战队乐团演奏两国国歌，特朗普与习近平将分别致辞。两位领导人还将在白宫玫瑰园检阅军事仪仗队，欢迎仪式的最后是由一架B2“幽灵”轰炸机和四架F-22“猛禽”战斗机进行飞行表演。

星期四的活动还包括一场与美国科技界重量级人物的国宴。

星期五，特朗普总统夫妇将与习近平夫妇进行茶叙，随后参观收藏着美国《独立宣言》和《宪法》原件的国家档案馆，查阅历史上对美中关系意义重大的记录和文献。习近平夫妇随后将离开华盛顿，结束三天的国事访问。

[路透社](https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/world/trump-plans-grand-spectacle-for-potentially-tense-xi-talks/ar-AA2cOJDz?ocid=BingNewsSerp)报道，尽管双方存在严重分歧，但双边依然推进了峰会，分析人士表示，此次峰会意在展示世界最大工厂和最大消费国之间的稳定关系，但各界对习近平此次访问能带来突破的期望不大。

**抗议人士的迎接方式**

与此同时，在华盛顿街头，宾夕法尼亚大道通往白宫方向已经架起围栏，特勤局人员和华盛顿警方明显加强安保，预计将有大批抗议者聚集华盛顿抗议习近平的到访，包括西藏、维吾尔、香港、法轮功、中国民运及人权团体和台湾侨团都计划举行示威。

**台湾国防部：继续与五角大楼保持密切联系**

就在华盛顿以高规格礼仪迎接习近平之际，数千公里之外的台湾，也在密切观察这场访问，尤其关注特朗普与习近平会谈是否触及台湾以及美国对台军售问题。

华盛顿智库战略与国际研究中心(CSIS)费和中国研究项目顾问，曾任白宫国家安全委员会东亚和大洋洲事务高级主任的埃德加·卡根(Edgard Kagan)星期二在该智库发布的一篇[问答文章](https://www.csis.org/analysis/xi-jinpings-return-washington-state-visit-build-stability?utm_source=chatgpt.com)中表示，他认为，台湾会密切关注三个方面。

首先，美国对台湾政策的措辞是否有变化，特别观察美国是否继续使用“不支持台湾独立”，还是出现北京希望的更强措辞“反对台湾独立”；其次，台湾方面也关注特朗普是否向习近平做出涉及台湾的具体承诺，如推迟对台军售或者限制台湾领导人过境美国。最后，卡根认为，台湾方面也会从华盛顿的礼遇规格，特习两人互动和特朗普的公开表述来判断美中关系的走向。

[路透社](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/taiwan-to-maintain-close-contact-with-us-on-arms-sales/ar-AA2cO3HI?ocid=BingNewsSerp)报道，台湾国防部副发言人乔福骏星期三表示，美国政府和国会已经多次表示支持台湾自我防卫的能力，台湾将继续与美国国防部保持密切联系，继续推动依计划执行的军售。

特朗普总统在2025年12月批准了111亿美元的对台军售，今年5月特朗普与习近平在北京举行峰会后，推迟了批准另一笔140亿美元新的对台军售。一名白宫发言人本星期在答复美国之音的提问时表示，“正如特朗普总统说过，他将在短时间内针对一个新的对台军售方案作出决定。”

title: ‘Soft resistance’ is the ‘most malicious’ threat to nat. security in Hong Kong – security chief
summary: Hong Kong’s security chief has named “soft resistance” the “most malicious” threat to national security in the city. Secretary for Security Chris Tang announces the beginning of the public consultation period for Hong Kong’s homegrown secur
content: Hong Kong’s security chief has named “soft resistance” the “most malicious” threat to national security in the city. Secretary for Security Chris Tang announces the beginning of the public consultation period for Hong Kong’s homegrown security law, Article 23, on January 30, 2024. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “The evil of soft resistance lies in the fact that you may not know it is evil,” Secretary for Security Chris Tang said in an interview with Commercial Radio on Monday. “You may even think it is [coming from] a good person.” Reiterating language introduced by the government last year, Tang listed “four great national security risks” in Hong Kong. These include interference by foreign forces, domestic terrorist activities, fugitives continuing to spread “Hong Kong independence ideology,” and “soft resistance.” Among the four, Tang said, “soft resistance” is the “most malicious” since its dangers are not as clear as the others’. China’s national flags and Hong Kong flags are displayed in the city on September 30, 2025, a day before the 76th anniversary of the People’s Republic of China. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “If it is not illegal, first consider its intentions,” Tang added. “If it is illegal, action should of course be taken.” Tang did not elaborate or provide any examples. ‘Undercurrents’ The term “soft resistance” was first mentioned in 2021 in a speech by Luo Huining, then-director of Beijing’s liaison office in Hong Kong. Since then, Hong Kong officials have cited “soft resistance” as a threat to national security, although they have not provided a clear definition of the term . After Luo’s speech, pro-establishment commentator Lau Siu-kai told HK01 that soft resistance focused on ideological work that was difficult to address in law, including “disseminating disinformation, creating panic, maliciously attacking the SAR government and the central authorities and distorting the Basic Law.” Explainer: What is ‘soft resistance’? Hong Kong officials vow to take a hard line against it, but provide no definition In his radio appearance, the security chief said that the “four great threats to national security” continue to operate primarily in the “undercurrents” of society. At a passing-out parade last week, national security police chief Andrew Kan told new recruits to the force that “national security challenges have become more invisible,” cautioning them to stay on guard against “external forces,” “soft resistance,” and “ideological infiltration.” “Oftentimes,” Kan said, “hidden dangers lurk in every corner of our communities.” Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest. It criminalised subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts – broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure. The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents , while dozens of civil society groups disappeared . The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners , the UN and NGOs .

title: North Korea says US-led arms buildup justifies expanding nuclear force
summary: North Korea's vice defence minister said on Thursday ​that a growing U.S.-led military buildup and what he called an expanding nuclear alliance among Washington, Seoul and Tokyo justified Pyongyang's efforts to strengthen and expand its nuc
content:
North Korea's vice defence minister said on Thursday ​that a growing U.S.-led military buildup and what he called an expanding nuclear alliance among Washington, Seoul and Tokyo justified Pyongyang's efforts to strengthen and expand its nuclear forces.

Speaking at the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, China's flagship international security conference, Vice Defence Minister Kim Kang Il said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was irreversible and pledged to continue expanding its nuclear arsenal.

"The ceaseless nuclear arms buildup of the enemy states fully justifies the building of a solid nuclear shield of the DPRK," Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea's formal name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

"As the enemy states' nuclear threat reaches the extreme level ... the ‌DPRK will firmly ‌defend the peace and stability in the Korean Peninsula and the region ​by ‌ceaselessly ⁠expanding and strengthening ​its ⁠self-defensive nuclear deterrent."

Kim blamed tensions on the Korean Peninsula on what he called Washington's "invariable" hostile policy toward North Korea and accused the United States of turning trilateral cooperation with South Korea and Japan into a nuclear alliance.

He said North Korea's constitutional status as a nuclear weapons state was "the line of no retreat" and urged other countries to abandon what he called the "daydream" of denuclearisation.

Kim's appearance at the Xiangshan Forum marked a rare high-profile showing by North Korea at an international security gathering in recent years and came as Pyongyang seeks closer ties with Beijing amid tensions ⁠with Washington and its allies.

Asked about the possibility of a meeting between ‌U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, ‌Kim said he was not in a position to discuss whether such ​a summit could take place.

Former U.S. Special Representative for ‌North Korea Stephen Biegun said at the Korea Risk Group's West Coast Exchange conference on Thursday that ‌North Korea's muted response to Trump's repeated claims of communication with Kim Jong Un suggested Pyongyang was "not closing the door" on potential future talks with Washington.

Biegun said it "would not be a surprise at all" if Trump were to propose a meeting with the North Korean leader following the APEC summit in China in November and that such a meeting could even take ‌place in Pyongyang.

DENUCLEARISATION REJECTED

The North Korean official's remarks followed a statement on Thursday morning from Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of Kim Jong Un, rejecting ⁠renewed international calls for ⁠North Korea's denuclearisation following discussions at the annual meeting of the International Atomic Energy Agency.

In a statement carried by state media KCNA, she said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was "absolute" and could not be reversed, dismissing repeated denuclearisation demands as annual "noise" and insisting Pyongyang's nuclear position had been permanently established "physically and legally".

Her comments echoed a separate statement on Wednesday by a North Korean defence ministry spokesman, who accused the United States and South Korea of escalating military confrontation through joint weapons-of-mass-destruction response planning and exercises.

The spokesman said recent U.S.-South Korean WMD response discussions amounted to an "open declaration of confrontation" and warned such actions could require Pyongyang to invoke provisions of its nuclear force policy law.

The statements appeared to form part of a broader messaging campaign by Pyongyang on its nuclear policy, according to Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies in ​Seoul.

The comments were aimed at cementing North Korea's ​claim that its nuclear status had reached an "irreversible stage", while creating justification for future military and nuclear activities in response to what it portrays as growing U.S. and South Korean pressure, Lim said.

Reuters

summary: CUS Press Release For Immediate Release October 1, 2026 Contact@uyghurstudy.org Uyghurstudy.org Washington, D.C. – Today marks the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China. For the government in Beijing, it is a da
content: CUS Press Release For Immediate Release October 1, 2026 Contact@uyghurstudy.org Uyghurstudy.org Washington, D.C. – Today marks the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China. For the government in Beijing, it is a day of celebration. For the Uyghur people, this date carries an entirely different meaning: a day of mourning for a people whose homeland was taken from them. In late 1949, the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) invaded East Turkistan. Only weeks earlier, the leaders of the independent East Turkistan Republic, founded in Ghulja in 1944, had died in a still-unexplained plane crash on their way to Beijing for talks arranged by Joseph Stalin. Six years later, on October 1, 1955, Beijing formally established East Turkistan as an “autonomous region,” naming it the “Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region.” The promise made to the Uyghur people was clear: in their own land, their language and faith would be protected, and they would decide their own future. Decades later, all that remains of that promise is a signboard. Uyghurs have been made refugees in their own homeland and prisoners deprived of their religious freedom. According to CUS research, the showcase position at the head of the regional government has been given to a Uyghur. Real power, however, lies with the regional Communist Party secretary, a post that for decades has been held by Han Chinese officials appointed by Beijing. One year before “autonomy” was declared, the paramilitary Production and Construction Corps (Bingtuan) was established in 1954. Together with planned migration policies, it has radically transformed the region’s demographics. In 1953, Han Chinese made up roughly 6 percent of the population; by the 2020 census, that share had exceeded 42 percent. Uyghur-language education has been systematically removed from schools. Children have been torn from their families and cut off from their mother tongue in boarding schools. Mosque domes and minarets have been torn down, and cemeteries have been bulldozed. Fasting, praying and teaching the Qur’an have been treated as signs of “extremism.” Since 2017, millions of Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims have been confined in concentration camps labeled “vocational training […] The post 77 Years of Occupation: Sham Autonomy, Religious Persecution and Genocide Against the Uyghurs appeared first on Center for Uyghur Studies .

content:
## China’s Military Power in 2025: Crossing a Strategic Threshold

In 2025, China stands at a pivotal juncture in its military evolution—transforming from a regional power into a near-peer competitor on the global stage through unprecedented modernization, strategic expansion, and integrated defense capabilities. Avec une force armée en pleine métamorphose, le pays déploie une posture militaire audacieuse, alliant dissuasion nucléaire, dominance aérienne et cyberguerre avancée. Prepared for high-intensity regional conflicts and increasingly capable of projecting influence beyond Asia, China’s military power by 2025 represents not just accumulation, but systemic readiness.

## The Scale and Scope of China’s Defensive Assets

By 2025, China’s military infrastructure reflects an estimated 2.3 million active personnel, the largest standing force in the world, augmented by a surge in reserve capabilities. The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) maintains over 5,000 combat control satellites, enabling precision targeting and real-time battlefield awareness across vast operational zones. Naval assets have expanded dramatically: the PLA Navy now fields 370 vessels, including 11 domestically built aircraft carriers—two operational, one under comprehensive trials—enhanced by stealthy destroyers and stealth submarines.

Air power has seen transformative growth as well. The PLA Air Force commands more than 3,200 combat aircraft, with fifth-generation fighters like the J-20 conductors forming the backbone of a growing stealth fleet. Unmanned systems, including over 1,200 combat drones, now integrate key roles in surveillance, strike, and electronic warfare.

Collectively, these assets form a layered, networked force designed for anti-access, area-denial, and rapid response—critical for safeguarding China’s near-seas and extending influence across the Indo-Pacific and beyond.

## Nuclear Modernization and Strategic Deterrence

China’s nuclear doctrine is evolving to match escalating global tensions. By 2025, estimates suggest the arsenal has grown to between 500 and 600 warheads, with investments concentrating on submarine-launched ballistic missiles (SLBMs) and strategic bombers.

The growth of the Dongfeng-41 ICBM and the birth of the hypersonic DF-17—capable of glide and maneuver—signals a shift toward survivable, second-strike capabilities. Strategic bombers, including the suffocating Venture-F (KJ-600 airborne early warning platform) and the emerging HK-3 stealth bomber prototype, enhance precision strike and persistent surveillance potential. “China is evolving from a minimal deterrent nuclear posture to one of credible strategic flexibility,” noted Dr.

Li Wei, defense analyst at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. “This modernization reduces reliance on early warning alone and prepares authorities for calibrated responses in a crisis.”

## Technology Integration and Joint Operations Mastery

Central to China’s leap in military capability is the deep fusion of artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and advanced communications into joint operations. The Central Theater Command leads efforts to break traditional service silos, enabling seamless integration of land, sea, air, space, and cyber domains.

AI-powered predictive analytics assist command decisions, while Shenzhou and Taichung UAVs demonstrate real-world effectiveness in battlefield coordination. Cyberwarfare units, strengthened by specialized units under the PLA’s Strategic Support Force, now conduct both defensive and offensive cyber missions with increasing precision. These units protect critical infrastructure while probing adversary networks—transforming cyberspace into a strategic battleground.

The 2025 PLA exercises showcased unprecedented synchronization, with naval strike forces, drone swarms, and electronic warfare platforms operating as a single, responsive system.

## Regional Ambitions and Global Reach

China’s military power in 2025 is not confined to Asia. Forward deploys in the South China Sea consolidate control over disputed zones through advanced anti-ship missiles and surveillance drones, deterring NATO-aligned freedom-of-navigation operations.

In the Indo-Pacific, naval task groups patrol critical shipping lanes and peer with Quad nations in joint drills. Looking further, docking agreements in Djibouti and growing logistical partnerships enable rotating presence in the Indian Ocean—extending power projection well beyond immediate periphery. Military diplomacy complements hardware: China’s arms exports and peacekeeping deployments enhance soft power while validating doctrinal superiority.

African and Southeast Asian nations increasingly undergo joint exercises, cementing Beijing as a strategic alternative to Western security architectures.

### Key Capabilities Shaping 2025 Force Posture

- **Naval Forces**: 370+ ships including 11 aircraft carriers, 60 modern destroyers, and a stealthy submarine fleet. - **Air Power**: 3,200+ combat aircraft featuring stealth fighters and drone support.

- **Strategic Deterrence**: Nuclear arsenal expanding to 500–600 warheads, focused on survivable platforms. - **Hypersonic Systems**: DF-17 glide vehicles and PF-21 missiles enabling rapid zone denial. - **Joint Abilities**: Integrated command systems enabling cross-domain operations.

- **Cyber & Space**: 5,000+ cyber specialists and a growing constellation of military satellites.

## Implications for Global Security and Strategic Balance

China’s 2025 military posture marks a qualitative shift in regional power dynamics, compelling neighbors and strategic competitors alike to recalibrate defense strategies. While Beijing emphasizes peaceful development, the sheer scale and accelerated modernization challenge assumptions of strategic equilibrium.

The U.S. and allies respond with enhanced forward patrols, indigenous advanced systems, and multilateral exercises aimed at containment and deterrence. Within this evolving landscape, China’s military evolution is not merely defensive—it is both a reflection of rising autonomy and a signal of global ambition.

As capabilities converge and strategic reach deepens, 2025 stands as a definitive benchmark in China’s journey toward full strategic parity and influence. In sum, China’s military power in 2025 is no longer defined by size alone, but by integration, innovation, and strategic assertiveness—ushering in an age where the PLA is both shield and sword on the world stage.

title: 余茂春：特朗普高規格接待習近平 背後凸顯美中全方位戰略較量

content: VOA樊东宁 脸书 2026-9-27 中國國家主席習近平為期三天的國事訪問於星期五（9月25日）畫下句點。美國總統川普全程以高規格接待，從親自前往安德魯斯聯合基地接機，到白宮南草坪的歡迎儀式、東廳的國宴、紅廳的茶敘，以及一同參觀美國國家檔案館，展現美方對此次訪問的重視。 曾在川普第一任政府任職的哈德遜研究所中國中心主任余茂春教授接受美國之音專訪時表示，習近平此次訪美獲得高規格禮遇的背後，其實反映出美中之間全方位的戰略較量。 川普向習近平展示美國實力 余茂春以1959年美國總統艾森豪高規格接待前蘇聯領導人赫魯雪夫（Nikita Khrushchev）為例指出，高規格的外交儀本身並不意味著美中關係取得實質性進展。在他看來，外交禮儀與實力展示，恰恰可能反映出雙方在缺乏實質突破的情況下，試圖透過外交場面傳遞各自的戰略訊息。 余茂春指出，今年5月川普訪問中國時，中方同樣給予川普高規格接待，因此美方這次的安排在外交禮儀上具有對等性質。 不過，他也以川普此前在阿拉斯加會見俄羅斯總統普京時，在F-22戰機旁握手的安排作為對照，指出其中一個值得注意的細節。川普選擇在安德魯斯聯合基地以及白宮歡迎儀式中展示美軍先進裝備，包括戰鬥機與轟炸機飛越上空，向北京傳遞一個明確訊息：美國可以高規格接待中共領導人，但雙方的實力對比，仍是美方希望凸顯的重要環節。 熟悉川普思維的余茂春認為，川普重視外交場合的視覺效果，希望在表達尊重的同時，也讓對方感受到美國的實力。 四個「T」之外，貿易休戰才是核心 此次美中峰會可能涉及的議題相當廣泛。除了此前備受關注的貿易、台灣以及伊朗問題之外，人工智慧與科技競爭也成為新的重要議題。 這些議題被概括為多個「T」，包括貿易（Trade）、台灣（Taiwan）、德黑蘭／伊朗（Tehran），以及科技（Technology）。余茂春認為，這些問題都涉及美中雙方的長期戰略利益，因此很難透過一次元首會晤徹底解決。 在他看來，此次美中峰會的具體成果，反而是這四個「T」之外的另一個「T」——貿易休戰（Truce）的延長。 余茂春強調，習近平希望美國延長貿易休戰，而川普則更加關注中方此前承諾的落實情況，特別是稀土供應以及採購美國農產品等問題。他認為，美方持續關注的是這些承諾是否真正落實，而不僅僅是雙方在峰會上作出口頭表態。 得AI者得天下 至於人工智慧議題，在川普日前提出「得AI者得天下」的說法後，已成為美中科技競爭最激烈的戰場之一。 余茂春表示，隨著川普提出「超級智慧」（Super Intelligence）等概念，人工智慧的安全與管控可能成為美中雙方需要討論的議題。 他認為，AI既可能為人類帶來巨大益處，也可能產生重大的安全風險，因此美中之間建立某種管控機制具有重要意義。不過，他同時指出，人工智慧領域的競爭涉及技術、網路及國家安全利益，雙方能否真正執行任何形式的協議，將是一項重要挑戰。 中國「明目張膽」支持伊朗 川普星期五與習近平一同參觀美國國家檔案館時，親自向媒體證實，兩人談到了伊朗問題。 余茂春認為，中國「明目張膽」地支持俄羅斯與伊朗，是美國長期關注的問題。他表示，美國近年來透過包括「次級制裁」在內的政策，對與俄羅斯、伊朗等國進行相關活動的國家施加壓力，因此中國與這些國家的經貿關係可能成為美方關注的對象。 他認為，川普政府可能會繼續要求北京在相關問題上作出更加具體的承諾，而美國最終是否採取進一步措施，則取決於北京的實際行動。 軍售時程不代表美國對台政策改變 美中元首峰會舉行之際，美國在亞洲的盟友與夥伴如何看待華盛頓與北京的高層互動，也是外界關注的焦點。 余茂春認為，每次美中元首峰會都可能讓美國部分盟友產生疑慮，包括日本、韓國、菲律賓以及台灣。他指出，川普在聯合國大會期間與日本、韓國領導人保持互動，可以被視為向盟友釋放訊息，強調美中峰會並不意味著美國將削弱與盟友的關係。 在台灣問題上，余茂春認為，台灣仍可能是美中關係中的重要議題，但不一定會成為此次元首會談的核心。 針對外界有關美國對台軍售可能因美中峰會而延後的討論，余茂春認為，軍售時間安排本身並不必然代表美國對台政策發生重大改變。他表示，美國對台軍售長期以來都與兩岸軍事態勢以及台灣自身的防務需求有關。 美國國務卿盧比奧在習近平訪美前於紐約回應記者相關提問時表示，總額140億美元的對台軍售案仍在審議中，美國在出售武器時也必須權衡自身的需求。 余茂春表示，台灣近年來已經獲得大量美國武器，但台灣自身的國防體系與美國軍事體系之間仍需要進一步整合，因此武器採購的速度與規模，也需要考量台灣實際吸收及運用武器的能力。 美中峰會向中國人民傳遞美國價值觀 除了貿易休戰、人工智慧、支持伊朗與對台軍售之外，余茂春也特別提到了人權議題。 他表示，習近平此次訪美引起了許多人的憤怒。美國幾乎各個層次、各個團體，都向白宮表達了希望向習近平傳達抗議與不滿的訴求。國會也有相關聲音，民間組織的反應則更多。因此，成千上萬的人都表達了抗議習近平的決心與意願。川普也已經透過發言人表示，將向習近平提出這些訴求。這些因素形成了巨大的壓力，當然也難以避免。 至於川普如何透過美中峰會直接向中國人民傳達訊息，余茂春認為，美國領導人向中國人民傳遞美國價值觀，未必需要透過明確的政策表態。美國政府的許多行動，也可以透過自身的作為，對中國大陸產生巨大的影響。 他舉例說，在對伊朗的戰爭中，中國民眾當然相當關注相關發展，但真正令中國民眾感到震撼的，是美軍動用數千人、耗費數億美元，營救兩名受傷的美軍飛行員。這件事在中國民間受到廣泛討論，也體現了一個國家的價值觀。 余茂春表示，一個國家為了確保自己的軍人不受到虐待，以及對軍人的尊重而採取行動，這些都具有相當大的震撼力。 他說：「像這些非常細微的影響，對中國所產生的作用，我想一種是隱性的、間接的。另外，當然還有很多逐漸發展的軟實力工具，包括像美國之音所做的工作就非常好。很多中國的聽眾、觀眾，也可以透過你們的管道，了解美國真正的走向以及美國領導人的政治表述。這些東西都是潛移默化的。要改變中國對美國的理解，我覺得需要美國和中國人民做出很多努力。」 峰會成果：關鍵不在簽署什麼，而在落實多少 對於如何衡量此次美中峰會的最終成果，余茂春認為，不能僅憑峰會現場的氣氛、國宴規格或領導人發表的聲明來判斷。他強調，真正重要的是中方此前作出的承諾能否落實，而美國政府也需要持續監督並核實相關承諾的執行情況。 余茂春認為，過去美中之間一直存在口頭承諾與實際執行之間的落差，因此，此次峰會結束後，雙方是否建立更加具體的落實與核查機制，將是觀察峰會成效的重要指標。 在他看來，峰會本身或許能帶來短期的外交穩定，但美中之間長期的戰略競爭，不會因為一次高規格的元首會晤而消失。 川普2.0對中政策的演變 最後，余茂春也比較了川普第二任期與第一任期的對中政策。他認為，兩者之間存在相當程度的延續性。 余茂春指出，川普第一任期期間，美國對中國的戰略定位發生了重大變化，而這項基本判斷並沒有因為拜登政府執政而出現根本性改變。 他認為，川普第二任期雖然在公開措辭上更加強調與中國保持溝通、避免衝突以及尋求「戰略穩定」，但美國在科技、安全、產業政策及盟友體系等領域的政策，仍然體現出對美中戰略競爭的重視。 余茂春指出，川普第二任期的政策重點包括強化美國國內安全、重建工業基礎、要求盟友增加國防投入，以及加強對先進技術的保護。 他認為，這些政策雖然未必直接以「對抗中國」的形式呈現，但都與美中長期戰略競爭存在密切關聯。

content:
The Bottom Line Up Front

**The same architecture of surveillance and control underpins China’s presence in Tibet, the Uyghur region, Inner Mongolia, and Hong Kong, built on procurement networks designed to stay a step ahead of sanctions and export controls.**

Using an original dataset built from government and corporate records, this report maps digital surveillance supply chains across four regions governed by China: the Tibet Autonomous Region (Tibet/TAR), the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR/ the Uyghur region), Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (Inner Mongolia), and Hong Kong. This data offers a novel lens on China’s surveillance apparatus because, unlike secondary reporting or victim testimony, government records document the state’s own purchasing decisions and reveal which companies and technologies underpin its infrastructure.

Analysis limited to a single region misses the pervasiveness of China’s digital surveillance architecture. While these four regions are not the only ones affected by China’s repressive surveillance system, this report focuses on them due to the acute impact that surveillance has had on those populations. Tibet is often recognized as the prototype and the Uyghur region as the scale-up for China’s repression of ethnic minorities and mass surveillance. These tools and tactics extended into Hong Kong under a nominally distinct legal system, and have also spread into Inner Mongolia, which has garnered significantly less attention.

China’s digital surveillance apparatus has evolved from Maoist-era grassroots social control to a high-tech infrastructure enabled by artificial intelligence (AI), consisting of high-resolution cameras, biometric data collection, and predictive policing platforms. The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) “Five Poisons” (五毒) framework designates ethnic and religious minority populations as well as pro-democracy activists as existential threats and provides the ideological foundation for targeted surveillance in China. State-led initiatives like “Sharp Eyes” (雪亮工程) enhance the reach and scale of targeted digital surveillance. Notably, the extent of Chinese state surveillance in Inner Mongolia documented by C4ADS shows that the CCP’s surveillance and repression patterns are not confined to the populations named in the Five Poisons framework. However, the Five Poisons designation still identifies the populations Beijing views as posing the greatest threat to its national security.

Chinese government records show four recurring elements in the state’s repressive surveillance apparatus: (1) public security bureaus (PSBs) are the primary procurers of surveillance equipment, (2) PSBs are acquiring AI-enabled biometric technology, (3) projects rely largely on domestic distributors (especially the three largest telecommunications companies), and (4) U.S.-sanctioned manufacturers such as Uniview and Hikvision remain major manufacturers of surveillance equipment supplied to China.

China’s surveillance technology capacity was built by leveraging Western technology and partnerships, but a large domestic industry now exists comprising the world’s largest surveillance manufacturers and exporters. This report’s findings show that as domestic capacity grows, it increasingly limits the reach of sanctions and export controls that target only named foreign manufacturers, creating a need to leverage additional tools aimed at distributors and end users, discussed further in the Recommendations. However, foreign companies remain embedded in the supply chain.

Through government acquisition systems, global supply chains may still be more widely complicit in the repression of ethnic minority groups and political dissidents. Mapping these supply chains and understanding the patterns of how China continues to power its repressive surveillance apparatus is a precondition for financial, legal, and reputational accountability. Disruption requires knowing which actors to target, how they are connected, and the ways they operate. This report identifies the leading domestic suppliers of surveillance hardware named in relevant contracts across the four regions, offering an initial snapshot of the companies most central to this market. Because the U.S.-sanctioned manufacturers discussed in this report operate on a global scale, corporate due diligence and know-your-customer (KYC) standards are essential tools for preventing further complicity in state-sponsored repression.

title: Hong Kong authorities hail scheme for reducing sodium levels in bread by average of up to 17%
summary: Hong Kong authorities have hailed a health scheme that encouraged bread manufacturers to cut sodium levels by an average of up to 17 per cent, following a report that found most adults in the city consume more salt than the recommended dail
content: Hong Kong authorities have hailed a health scheme that encouraged bread manufacturers to cut sodium levels by an average of up to 17 per cent, following a report that found most adults in the city consume more salt than the recommended daily intake. Hong Kong bread products. File photo: Daisy Tam. The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) said on Tuesday that, since the scheme was rolled out in 2019, all participating bread manufacturers have met the voluntary sodium reduction targets for their white and wholemeal bread products. They include seven manufacturers of pre-packaged bread and 19 manufacturers of non-packaged bread, which together produce about 80 types of white and wholemeal bread products, according to the CFS, an agency under the Food and Environmental Department. Under the scheme, manufacturers are encouraged to keep the level of sodium in white bread at below 380 milligrams for every 100 grams of white bread, with a cap of 490 milligrams. For every 100 grams of wholemeal bread, the average sodium level should not exceed 380 milligrams. The maximum level is 470 milligrams, according to the guidelines. “After the implementation of the Scheme, the average sodium content of related bread products decreased by 10 per cent to 17 per cent, with some manufacturers successfully reducing the sodium content of their products by more than 40 per cent,” a spokesperson for the CFS said in the statement on Tuesday, which is World Heart Day. A restaurant in Hong Kong. Photo: via Pexels.com The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended that an adult should not exceed five grams of salt intake per day, equivalent to 2000 milligrams of sodium. According to a survey conducted by the Department of Health between 2020 and 2022, Hongkongers aged 15 to 84 had a daily salt intake of 8.4 grams. The survey also found that more than 80 per cent of Hongkongers aged 15 to 84 had a salt intake above the WHO recommended daily limit. High salt intake increases the risk of cardiovascular disease and stroke by raising blood pressure. “As we observe World Heart Day, the CFS reminds the public of the importance of reducing sodium intake in lowering the risk of high blood pressure, thereby promoting heart health and preventing cardiovascular diseases,” the government agency said. It added that it had provided training and testing for bread manufacturers to reformulate their products to reduce sodium levels.

title: Trump and Xi Agree on “Constructive Strategic Stability,” But Differ on What It Means
source: 芝加哥全球事务委员会
summary: Trump and Xi Agree on “Constructive Strategic Stability,” But Differ on What It Means ccolon Mon, 09/28/2026 - 17:47 US President Donald Trump pulled out all the stops last week to give Chinese President Xi Jinping a lavish reception in Was
content: Trump and Xi Agree on “Constructive Strategic Stability,” But Differ on What It Means ccolon Mon, 09/28/2026 - 17:47 US President Donald Trump pulled out all the stops last week to give Chinese President Xi Jinping a lavish reception in Washington. Although substantive discussions were limited, the two leaders agreed to extend the US-China “trade truce” for two months, established a dialogue process on artificial intelligence (AI), and confirmed they will meet in November when China hosts the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting and again in December for the US-led Group of 20 summit in Florida. Throughout, Trump’s primary goal appeared to be to sustain and deepen what he claims is a “great friendship” with Xi. Still, Trump’s almost sycophantic treatment of Xi raised eyebrows among some observers, who thought he showed Xi more hospitality than a communist dictator deserved. Many also complained that Trump’s behavior may have validated Xi’s supposed view that he holds the upper hand in the strategic competition between China and the United States. That strategic competition has become the inescapable prism through which all US-China interactions are now viewed and made it difficult to see a path forward to the “ constructive relationship of strategic stability ” Trump and Xi rhetorically embraced in Beijing in May and reaffirmed in Washington. But it is the competition itself that prevents the two sides from making any progress on how to define and pursue that goal. Since the phrase “constructive strategic stability” emerged this spring, Beijing has tried to capitalize on Trump’s endorsement and lock it in as a framework for stabilizing US-China relations. Xi invoked it repeatedly during his meetings in Washington, stressing that the countries should turn the “vision into action” and “strive to take their relationship where cooperation is the mainstay.” He added that the word “competition” need not be avoided but that such “competition should be a healthy one and should be kept within bounds.” Yet many US commentators have described the approach as a Chinese trap, speculating that Beijing will subsequently hold Washington accountable for abiding by China’s own interpretation of the framework. Perhaps in response to that, the Trump administration has invoked the phrase only occasionally and given few indications that much thought has been given on how to operationalize it. According to official Chinese media , it was only during a breakfast tea meeting on the last morning of the summit that Xi secured Trump’s reiteration of the phrase. The divergence is emblematic of the underlying competitiveness that belies the rosy characterization of Xi’s visit. Beneath the surface—and even above the surface—both Washington and Beijing are still approaching the relationship as a zero-sum contest for global influence, with both sides insisting that the other side has made it so. Moreover, both sides appear to believe that they have the leverage in the relationship. And both believe that time is on their side. This is clearly not a sturdy foundation on which to pursue “constructive strategic stability” in US-China relations. Rather than continue to argue over the proper mix of competition and cooperation in the relationship, both Washington and Beijing need to recognize the constraints imposed by interdependence and dispense with the notion that either side could ever sustainably “win.” They should engage in working out the terms of peaceful coexistence—for their benefit and that of the rest of the world, which wants Washington and Beijing to do so. Two issues in the bilateral relationship will be key indicators going forward. The first is Taiwan. As most experts anticipated, there was no substantial movement on the issue of Taiwan during Xi’s Washington visit. Xi again urged Trump not to resume arms sales to Taiwan, with the focus of attention now on whether Trump will authorize the sale he suspended after the Beijing summit. But arms sales—and a focus on military deterrence in the Taiwan Strait—ultimately diverts attention from the real core dilemma that Washington faces with regard to Taiwan: the continuing erosion of the United States’ “one China policy.” The bigger question now is what Trump’s bottom line is on “one China” and Taiwan’s strategic importance. The second key indicator to watch is artificial intelligence, which is probably the issue on which strategic cooperation between China and the United States is most imperative. Unfortunately, AI has now also become central to the strategic competition, with the Trump administration explicitly stating that the United States needs to “win” over China. Whether the dialogue process that was announced in Washington can redirect the two sides away from zero-sum confrontation and toward collaboration on the rapidly advancing technology will be a key bellwether for the future of the bilateral relationship—and for global security. Trump and Xi have the opportunity in their November and December meetings to get more into the substance of these and other key bilateral issues. But the prospects for positive breakthroughs and stabilization of the relationship will remain limited as long as the two sides are focused more on maneuvering for advantage than on working together to define “constructive strategic stability.” And as long as Trump remains an impulsive, rather than strategic, decisionmaker. September 28, 2026 Paul Heer China US Foreign Policy Jacquelyn Martin / AP The Chicago Council on Global Affairs is an independent, nonpartisan organization and does not take institutional positions. The views and opinions expressed in this commentary are solely those of the author. About the Author Paul Heer Senior Nonresident Fellow, Lester Crown Center on US Foreign Policy, Chicago Council on Global Affairs Prior to joining the Council as a senior nonresident fellow, Paul Heer served for 30 years as a specialist on East Asian affairs in the US intelligence community. He also served on the staff of the president's daily brief and as a member of the senior analytic service at the CIA before becoming the national intelligence officer for East Asia. Reviewer ccolon

title: 抱薪者不可使其冻毙于风雪
source: 中国民主党洛杉矶委员会
summary: 作者：张伟军 编辑：吕聪 皮乔海，湖北鄂州人。此前，他一直生活在洛杉矶，在洛杉矶的抗议活动中，我经常能看到他忙碌的身影。这一次，他特意乘飞机来到华盛顿特区，参加和平集会和抗议习近平活动。 9月22日，在众议院门前草坪的活动中，他扛着一口棺材，兴奋地对我说：“伟军，你看这多有趣啊！包子这口棺材，我能抬一天，十里山路不换肩都没问题！” 我笑着调侃他：“希望你有机会扛200斤小麦的时候，也能这么说。” 当时的我们，谁也没有想到，短短两天之后，这竟成了我和老乡最后一次见面前的轻松回忆
content: 作者：张伟军 编辑：吕聪 皮乔海，湖北鄂州人。此前，他一直生活在洛杉矶，在洛杉矶的抗议活动中，我经常能看到他忙碌的身影。这一次，他特意乘飞机来到华盛顿特区，参加和平集会和抗议习近平活动。 9月22日，在众议院门前草坪的活动中，他扛着一口棺材，兴奋地对我说：“伟军，你看这多有趣啊！包子这口棺材，我能抬一天，十里山路不换肩都没问题！” 我笑着调侃他：“希望你有机会扛200斤小麦的时候，也能这么说。” 当时的我们，谁也没有想到，短短两天之后，这竟成了我和老乡最后一次见面前的轻松回忆。 9月23日下午，我们一同前往安德鲁斯空军基地，因为习近平当天预计最先抵达这里。 为了避免被粉红阵营巨大的旗帜遮挡，我们提前分散到几个不同的据点，包括车道左右两侧以及人行横道的三角区域。 然而，冲突还是发生了。 几名粉红看到皮乔海手中的讽刺性人像道具后，情绪激动地冲上来抢夺。双拳难敌四手，在混乱中，皮乔海胸口被中共特务特制雨伞捅伤，手指也被打出了血。 面对这一切，现场警察只是和稀泥，并没有对涉事中共特务采取任何处罚措施。这让皮乔海十分郁闷和气恼。他怎么也没有想到，在美国众目睽睽之下遭到袭击，最后竟然如此潦草收场。 9月24日，我们跟随大部队来到白宫门口参加活动。谁也没有想到，这竟然成了我和老乡最后一次见面。 活动开始前，我特意问他：“身体还好吗？” 他给我看了受伤的地方：胸口还有被雨伞捅伤留下的淤青，手指也明显肿了起来。 活动快结束时，不知道从哪里突然跑出来一群中共派来的老粉红，气势汹汹地冲过来。 按理说，当天白宫围栏外人行道的抗议活动区域是魏京生老前辈申请下来的 Permit，属于我们和平集会抗议区域，而粉红阵营在另一侧街道。这样的举动明显带有攻击目的性。 我们这边有老人、有妇女，很可能成为他们袭击的对象。皮乔海上前阻拦了一群老粉红，与其中一名粉红发生肢体冲突。这一幕恰好被一名女警察看到，他很快就被警察按倒在地。 当晚，界立健等人前往警察局了解情况。警察告诉他们，晚上12点会有结果。 漫长的等待中，终于到了午夜，传来了一喜一忧的消息。 喜的是，其他四名在混乱中被按倒在地的人都获得了释放。 悲的是，皮乔海却被指控两项罪名：殴打他人和袭警。 在美国，袭警指控可能带来严重的法律后果。据我现场所见，整场冲突中，我并没有看到皮乔海实施袭警行为。这样的指控让我们难以理解，也让人不禁质疑：事情为什么会发展到这一步？ 后来，我们又通过移民监狱网站查到了他的相关信息。 就这样，皮乔海被留在了那里，没能和我们一起踏上返程的航班。 一个为自由奔走的人，如今身陷囹圄 皮乔海为人善良、正直、谦和。他独自一人抚养着十多岁的孩子，生活十分艰难。为了维持日常生活，有时连房租都需要向朋友借钱周转。即便如此，他依然没有放弃对自由与民主的追求，始终积极参与各类和平抗议活动和捐款。 这一次，为了参加华盛顿特区的和平集会和抗议活动，他再次倾尽所能。往返交通与食宿费用共计774美元，这笔钱也是他向香港自由民主党创始人廖文浩先生借来的。 他经常提起自己的愿望：希望邪恶的独裁统治终结，希望中国能够建立一个民主、自由的社会，让普通人像台湾民众一样，不再因为表达言论、参加集会而感到恐惧，能够享有基本的人权与自由。 他说，等到那一天，他就要回到自己魂牵梦绕的家乡。 然而，如今的他却被关押在异国他乡，面对刑事指控和移民羁押的双重压力。 我很难想象，在当前移民政策和庇护审理环境下，如果他最终被遣返回中国，又将面临怎样的遭遇？ 他会不会像季超、阎友信等民运人士一样，遭遇失联，甚至从此杳无音信？ 这些担忧并非凭空而来。对于一个曾经公开表达政治观点、参加抗议活动的人来说，未来充满了太多未知。 更令人揪心的是，他在洛杉矶还有一个独自抚养的十多岁孩子。原本就十分艰难的生活，如今又因为他的被捕而蒙上了更大的阴影。 一个连房租都需要向朋友借钱、连赴华盛顿参加抗议活动的774美元都要向朋友借来的人，如今却身陷囹圄。想到这里，我的心里充满了难以言说的沉重。对于一个连房租都需要向朋友借钱的人来说，774美元绝不是一笔小数目。但他还是义无反顾地踏上了前往华盛顿的旅程，只为亲自站出来，为自由与民主发声。 我在此呼吁海外民运人士和关心中国民主、人权事业的朋友们，关注皮乔海的处境，为他提供力所能及的帮助，包括法律援助以及必要的声援。 抱薪者不可使其冻毙于风雪，仗义者不应被孤立于困境。 一个为自由奔走的人，不应该在最需要帮助的时候，被所有人遗忘。 愿皮乔海早日获得公正的对待，平安归来。

title: Mystery Shoulder-Fired Surface-To-Air Missile Appears In Russian Service
summary: An unusual shoulder-fired air defense missile seen in Russian use may be of Chinese or Iranian origin, raising questions about the movement of foreign weapons through the increasingly interconnected military supply networks linking Moscow,
content: An unusual shoulder-fired air defense missile seen in Russian use may be of Chinese or Iranian origin, raising questions about the movement of foreign weapons through the increasingly interconnected military supply networks linking Moscow, Beijing, and Tehran. The man-portable air defense system (MANPADS) appeared in Russian television footage showing a mobile air defense group operating in the Rostov region, which borders Ukraine. The weapon was shown during an exercise said to have involved one of the elements of Russia’s 51st Air Defense Division. The footage was subsequently highlighted by the X account TheDeadDistrict. ruSSian's have developed a new “Iva” MANPADS. In the footage, it is in service with one of the mobile fire groups of the 51st Air Defense Division in Rostov Oblast. Although, no—it is most likely the Iranian Misagh-2 MANPADS. Imagine, they don't even have enough production… pic.twitter.com/aYrOtSmG6h — 𝔗𝔥𝔢 𝕯𝔢𝔞𝔡 𝕯𝔦𝔰𝔱𝔯𝔦𝔠𝔱 (@TheDeadDistrict) September 28, 2026 The system does not closely resemble any of the Russian-made MANPADS families otherwise used by the country’s armed forces. Russian personnel seen with the weapon reportedly referred to it as “Iva,” although that designation by itself does not establish the weapon’s origin or model. The word Iva is Russian for willow (a type of tree), of which one particular species is named Verba — also the name of the Russian-made 9K333 MANPADS. This weapon looks very different to the example shown, but the connection is unlikely to be a coincidence. An operator of the mystery MANPADS is interviewed by the Russia-1 TV channel. Russian State Media A visual analysis of the newly observed launcher reveals comparisons with both the Iranian Misagh-3 and Chinese QW-series systems, particularly the QW-18/QW-18A and QW-19. In particular, a closer examination of the imagery highlights an additional box-like component toward the front of the launcher. That feature appears more consistent with photographs of Chinese QW-series systems rather than the Misagh. The front part of the MANPADS launcher, with the distinctive box-like component below the tub. Russian State Media There is also a scarcity of publicly available imagery of later Iranian variants to completely exclude an Iranian system. At the same time, the Misagh series itself is understood to be derived, or at least heavily influenced by Chinese designs. An Iranian Misagh-3 MANPADS with its missile. Tasnim News Agency Iranian basij with QW-18/Misagh-2 MANPADS pic.twitter.com/xfc0nMe4f8 — Yuri Lyamin (@imp_navigator) March 26, 2026 Another possibility is that the weapon is a Russian-produced version or derivative of a Chinese or Iranian design, rather than an imported system. The possibility of foreign-made or foreign-designed equipment appearing in Russian service has to be viewed against the much broader transformation of Moscow’s military relationships since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Russia’s relationship with China has deepened substantially since the invasion, with Beijing becoming a critical source of machinery, electronics, and other components that Russia’s defense industry can no longer obtain as readily from Western suppliers. Moscow and Beijing had already declared a “no limits” partnership shortly before the invasion, and their military relationship has subsequently included exercises and expanding military-technical cooperation. U.S. officials have accused China of supplying Russia with components used in weapons production, including microelectronics. Beijing has rejected accusations that it is providing lethal military assistance to Russia. A close-up of the front end of the MANPADS. Russian State Media Iran has also become an important military partner . Russia has used Iranian-designed Shahed-series attack drones extensively in Ukraine and has worked with Tehran on local production and adaptation of those systems. Moscow and Tehran formalized their relationship further with a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty in January 2025, which includes provisions for military-technical cooperation and joint exercises. In return, Russia has supplied Iran with military technology and has cooperated with Tehran on sensitive weapons programs. The possible Chinese connection takes on additional significance in light of a major reported procurement deal between China and Iran. In July, Reuters reported that Iran was expected to receive the first shipment of a deal covering 300 to 400 Chinese-made MANPADS, with a reported value of $60 million to $70 million. The weapons identified by sources included the Chinese QW-12 and FN-16 systems. Chinese missiles the United States fears… an unsleeping eye against drones and low‑flying aircraft China’s QW‑12 and FN‑16 air‑defense systems intercept low‑altitude targets — including drones — forming a rapid defensive line against close‑range aerial threats. pic.twitter.com/kJZ6mnqmHg — China Now (@ChinaNow24) August 23, 2026 The reported contract was signed with a Hong Kong-based company that sources described as an intermediary between the Iranian side and the Chinese supplier. Reuters said the initial deliveries were planned from Urumqi in western China, with the weapons then transiting through Pakistan before reaching Iran. Pakistan’s military publicly denied any involvement in such transfers, while China’s Foreign Ministry called the report “groundless.” Reuters also reported that delivery schedules and quantities could still change. More significantly for the Russian sighting, a European security source told Reuters that authorities were aware of several contracts under discussion involving the potential sale of QW-12, QW-18, and QW-19 MANPADS to Iran. A Middle Eastern security source separately claimed that Iran had been seeking QW-18 systems. The operation was carried out using a MANPADS, likely the Chinese “QW-18” anti-aircraft missile or its Iranian copy, the “Misagh-3”. https://t.co/OnPgqHJmQ8 pic.twitter.com/BuKt1MoKp7 — OSINTWarfare (@OSINTWarfare) October 23, 2024 There is currently no evidence tying the launcher seen in Russian hands to the Iranian procurement from China. At the same time, the possibility of an Iranian connection should not be ruled out, especially since Chinese-designed MANPADS have a documented history of appearing outside conventional state inventories. Earlier TWZ reporting , drawing on research by the Small Arms Survey monitoring group, examined the illicit proliferation of Chinese-designed MANPADS and identified dozens of cases involving armed groups in multiple countries. That research included QW-series weapons and documented cases in which investigators linked Chinese-designed MANPADS to Iranian supply networks. Countries with reports of illicit possession of advanced MANPADS by armed groups, 2011-21. Small Arms Survey One particularly notable case involved the Jihan , a vessel intercepted in 2013 carrying weapons that investigators identified as including QW-18-pattern MANPADS. UN investigators, the U.S. government, and   Conflict Armament Research assessed Iran as the likely source of those weapons. It is also worth noting that Chinese MANPADS have already appeared on the Ukrainian side of the war. In late 2025 and 2026, Ukrainian units were photographed with Chinese-made FN-6 and FN-16 systems, including an FN-6 associated with an air defense team reportedly engaging a Russian cruise missile. Exactly how the weapons reached Ukraine remains unclear, with possible third-party transfers or diverted shipments among the possible explanations. A Chinese FN-6 MANPADS in service with the MFG of the 143rd JTC “Podillia.” It is reported that this MANPADS was used this morning to shoot down a ruSSian Kh-101 CM. The FN-6 was developed in 2000 and supplied, among others, to Sudan, from where it likely found its way to Ukraine pic.twitter.com/9zA012ue3j — 𝔗𝔥𝔢 𝕯𝔢𝔞𝔡 𝕯𝔦𝔰𝔱𝔯𝔦𝔠𝔱 (@TheDeadDistrict) November 19, 2025 Reported as the downing of an Kh-101 cruise missile this morning using a Chinese FN-6 MANPADS. There is no public information confirming that this system has been supplied to or used by Ukraine, making this a notable development. pic.twitter.com/pUujFB81aH — NOELREPORTS (@NOELreports) November 19, 2025 Incidents like these demonstrate that Chinese MANPADS can move through indirect supply networks, including networks associated with Tehran. Regardless of how it arrived in Russia, the appearance of a foreign or foreign-derived MANPADS there is notable. Mobile fire groups have become an increasingly visible component of Russia’s layered air defense effort, particularly as the war in Ukraine has placed enormous emphasis on countering low-altitude drones and other threats, including deep inside Russia. A Russian CUAS mobile fire group shown with a Courier UGV for additional counter-drone targeting. https://t.co/7yTPPZ47f0 pic.twitter.com/bDu6MbZLEZ — Samuel Bendett (@sambendett) September 2, 2026 MANPADS are well suited to this mission because they can be dispersed among small teams, rapidly repositioned, and deployed without the larger radar and vehicle infrastructure associated with conventional surface-to-air missile batteries. In particular, they can be deployed around military installations and other sensitive infrastructure. A foreign system appearing in a Russian mobile fire group might be an imported weapon, an Iranian-produced derivative, a Chinese system acquired for evaluation, a captured weapon, or even a previously unidentified Russian configuration. model, or even that it is a brand new Chinese-made variant (its possible that I just hadn't seen it, or seen it from these angles) but it is a notable new addition to Russia's MANPADS inventory. — Matt Schroeder (@MSchroeder77) September 28, 2026 Another possibility is that the MANPADS is North Korean in origin. Russia’s military relationship with Pyongyang has expanded significantly , including the provision of increasingly advanced military equipment and technology. There is no known North Korean MANPADS matching the configuration seen here, however, and the possibility remains speculative. North Korean weapons have also frequently incorporated or closely followed Chinese designs , meaning a Chinese-looking configuration would not necessarily rule out a North Korean origin. I was able to geolocate and thus confirm that the photo of North Korean M-1978/1989 Koksan 170mm SPGs was taken in Russia. 56.069386, 92.920244 Krasnoyarsk, central Russia https://t.co/BOaR44uLeS https://t.co/mC8solXVOv pic.twitter.com/LUHO2cllKZ — Status-6 (@Archer83Able) November 14, 2024 Russia has dramatically expanded defense production since 2022, but its industry remains under heavy wartime demand and sanctions-related constraints. Western restrictions have complicated access to advanced electronics, machine tools and other components, while Russia has increasingly relied on domestic substitutes and foreign suppliers. The mystery MANPADS launchers disassembled and in a container for transport. Russian State Media At the same time, Russia must replenish weapons consumed in Ukraine, meaning foreign supplies could supplement domestic production, fill specific gaps, or allow scarce industrial capacity to be directed elsewhere. For Russia, even a limited number of additional shoulder-fired systems could therefore have practical value as Ukrainian long-range strike capabilities continue to expand. For now, the exact model and provenance of the MANPADS in question remain unconfirmed, but the apparent Chinese or Iranian design characteristics are highly noteworthy. Further appearances of the system could provide the clues needed to determine what it is, where it came from, and whether this represents an isolated example or a more significant acquisition effort.
