content: Abstract This article examines how the rapid spread of aerial, surface, and subsurface uncrewed systems across the Pacific is creating new risks of miscalculation, particularly around Taiwan. It argues that existing mechanisms such as the Code for Unplanned Encounters at Sea (CUES) are poorly suited to autonomous and remotely operated platforms, leaving unresolved questions of identification, attribution, human control, and escalation. The article proposes supplementary regional encounter protocols to reduce the risk that an ambiguous drone incident becomes the opening move of a wider conflict. Introduction On June 16 , a small autonomous surface vessel operated by the California-based company Seasats moved close enough to a Chinese Type 052D guided-missile destroyer to record detailed footage of it. The encounter took place about 65 miles northwest of the Philippine Island of Luzon, inside the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone. No one was injured, no warning shots were fired, and no sailors faced off against each other. But the incident previewed a dilemma regional governments have just started to face: How to respond to an unmanned boat of unknown intent when it approaches a warship in a contested area? Ferdinand Magellan gave the Pacific Ocean its name during his expedition in 1520. Five hundred years later, the world’s largest ocean is seeing a storm brought on by military systems that carry neither pilots nor sailors. This change is more than just naval rivalry. The East Asia and Pacific region is home to 32% of global trade and has become the hub of global maritime activity. A crisis in the Pacific would thus not only threaten the forces themselves, but also ports, shipping routes, supply lines, and economies well beyond the ocean. The Pacific’s Drone Buildup The U.S., China, Australia, Japan, Taiwan, and others in the region are all developing their uncrewed capabilities. Washington’s Replicator program aims to deploy many small, expendable, autonomous systems, and the US Pacific Fleet has created a squadron of small uncrewed surface vessels. China has been showing increasingly advanced aerial, surface and underwater systems and has been using drones in exercises around Taiwan. Australia’s MQ-28 Ghost Bat flew in formation with a US F-15EX for Exercise Valiant Shield and conducted dispersed refueling from Rota in the Northern Mariana Islands. Japan is developing a defense system that combines uncrewed and manned aircraft, and Taiwan is increasing domestic drone manufacturing as part of its asymmetric defense policy. There are good reasons for this rush. Such systems can conduct surveillance, resupply isolated units, search for submarines, relay communications and expose hostile positions without risking the lives of human crews. They can be deployed in certain missions at lower cost than conventional aircraft or warships and can also be deployed in missions that are not possible with conventional equipment. Drones would make a Chinese blockade or amphibious assault of Taiwan more difficult. For China, they can expand surveillance , targeting, and pressure around the island. Lastly, for the U.S. and its allies, they offer means to spread military power out over a large maritime area. When Expendability Creates Risk This should make crises easier to contain at first glance. When an uncrewed aircraft or vessel is destroyed, no pilot or sailor is killed, providing governments with more leeway to take the loss without retaliating. But the same expendability can encourage risk-taking. States and even private operators could be more inclined to fly drones near enemy forces, contested areas, military bases, and sensitive shipping lanes, since there’s no one on the ground in danger. For a crewed platform, a mission that might otherwise be too provocative to authorize could be more easily authorized when no one is aboard. The real issue is uncertainty. An officer observing an oncoming uncrewed vessel may not be able to determine if it is taking photographs, gathering electronic intelligence, carrying a jammer, placing a sensor, or preparing an attack. An aircraft flying towards a warship could be remotely controlled on a pre-programmed course, under autonomous guidance, or simply be faulty. There are few clues about intention and fewer opportunities for direct communication before a decision needs to be made if there is no crew on board. In an even more harrowing scenario, an uncrewed system can misidentify a civilian settlement, vessel, or aircraft for a military target and act against it, leading to civilian loss of life and property and necessitating a strong military response from the nations involved. Taiwan and the Risk of Miscalculation Such danger and uncertainty could become especially dangerous around Taiwan. Chinese military aircraft and vessels are already present in the region, as are Taiwanese forces, heavy civilian maritime and air traffic, and occasional American and allied operations. China’s late-2025 Taiwan exercises featured ships, aircraft, missiles and drones, including scenarios of blockade and attacks on maritime targets. Meanwhile, Taiwan is also developing a “hornet’s nest” of air, surface and subsurface drones that could help fend off an invasion, according to American officials. The next crisis could then start with a sense of uncertainty as the following situation demonstrates. A reconnaissance drone enters a sensitive area during a major exercise. The other side jams it, captures it, or shoots it down. Other unmanned systems are dispatched to find it; ships start to move; planes take off, and both sides claim the other is escalating. The situation can be dangerous without anyone wanting a war. Leaders would still have to make quick decisions without knowing what the platform is doing, who is controlling the platform, and whether its behavior is intentional. Conflict is not inevitable, and it is possible these systems deter deliberate attacks. However, they will open up more avenues for surveillance, probing, interference and misunderstanding. The main threat is not that a machine will make its own decision to go to war. It is that uncrewed systems expand the number of encounters in which commanders must interpret intent without the usual human signals. The Rules Have Not Kept Pace Current regional regimes only partially address this issue. In 2014, navies in the region endorsed the Code for Unplanned Encounters at Sea. It offers voluntary means of communication and safe maneuvering during naval ship and aircraft encounters. Unfortunately, the non-binding agreement predates the current proliferation of autonomous military systems, and doesn’t offer any specifics on how to identify the operator of an increased platform, how to contact the remote controller, or how to respond if the platform ignores warnings. Civilian control is progressing, but it does not solve the military issue. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) approved its first global safety code for autonomous vessels in May 2026. The code covers navigation, remote operations, and cybersecurity, but is not mandatory and mostly for commercial shipping. It was not intended to regulate interactions between military drones and foreign warships in sensitive political waters. The Seasats incident off Luzon highlights another complicating factor: private ownership. A warship may not be aware of whether the drone it encounters is being used for a commercial client, to test technology, under a government contract, or as part of an intelligence mission. The platform might have little or no national markings, and the people operating it might be hundreds of kilometers away. The distinction between private and state activity will become harder to discern in a crisis as militaries increasingly depend on commercially developed systems. Regional governments need to start negotiating a supplementary code for uncrewed military encounters before a serious incident forces the issue. Such a framework need not settle sovereignty disputes or restrict lawful military operations. It should set up recognizable identification, verified contact information for a responsible human operator, minimum separation distances, common warning procedures and a clear escalation procedure before the platform is jammed, captured or destroyed. It should also make clear that states remain responsible for privately owned systems conducting military or security-related missions. No major power will disclose the full capabilities, payloads or autonomy software of their systems, nor should an agreement demand that. Rules should be about behavior that can be seen. A drone doesn’t have to reveal all of its sensors. Still, the operator should be held responsible for reacting to warnings, keeping safe distances and avoiding actions that another military might reasonably interpret as an imminent attack. Australia and Japan are in a good position to champion such an initiative. Both heavily invest in uncrewed systems, have close ties with the United States, and are members of regional forums that involve China and Southeast Asian countries. Australia played a role in the development of CUES, and Japan’s growing drone program means it has a vested interest in ensuring that autonomous platforms do not cause uncontrolled escalation. Regional or bilateral agreements may follow initial agreement under the Western Pacific Naval Symposium. Such rules will not eliminate the climate of mistrust in the South China Sea, nor will they solve any sovereignty issues or stop any intentional coercion. They are more specific in their role: to minimize the risk of a tactical engagement with an uncrewed platform being confused with the first phase of a larger attack. The post The Pacific Drone Arms Race Has No Rules appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

title: 中共整党正按其设计运转，一套独特的纪律体系助其长存至今
source: 中国民主转型研究所（每季度一次刊物）
summary: * 作者安德鲁·梅塔（Andrew Mertha）是约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院乔治与萨迪·海曼中国研究讲席教授。 * 本文系采编，作者观点不代表本刊立场。 * 原文链接： https://www.foreignaffairs.com/china/chinas-purges-are-working-designed 《外交事务》9月17日发文：中共整党正按其设计运转，一套独特的纪律体系助其长存至今 近年，多位解放军高级将领相继落马，有关“习近平大权独揽疑心重重、党内动
content: * 作者安德鲁·梅塔（Andrew Mertha）是约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院乔治与萨迪·海曼中国研究讲席教授。 * 本文系采编，作者观点不代表本刊立场。 * 原文链接： https://www.foreignaffairs.com/china/chinas-purges-are-working-designed 《外交事务》9月17日发文：中共整党正按其设计运转，一套独特的纪律体系助其长存至今 近年，多位解放军高级将领相继落马，有关“习近平大权独揽疑心重重、党内动荡不安”的说法在华盛顿颇为流行。据CSIS统计，自2022年以来，已有30名将官级军官被查处，另有更多人悄然消失于公众视野。 但华盛顿这种流行看法可能颠倒了因果。过去二十年，学界普遍认为中共之所以能在苏东剧变后屹立不倒，靠的是邓小平时代建立起来的一整套“制度化”安排——任期限制、集体领导、按能力提拔干部。 而习近平上台十余年来，几乎拆除了这套制度的每一根支柱：2018年取消国家主席任期限制、弱化集体领导、迟迟不指定接班人，并在军队等敏感领域随意撤换高层。 若制度真是中共韧性的根基，这些举动理应预示危机。然而现实却是，党并未因此分裂或削弱，反而在整党过程中显得更加稳固。 文章指出，这背后的关键，在于中共对待“犯错干部”的方式，本质上并非苏联式的清洗，而是一套已运行近百年的“整风”机制。 斯大林式清洗以肉体消灭或彻底逐出为目的，波尔布特则将异己者送进乱葬岗；中共的做法不同：目标是把人留在体制内、加以“改造”，而非简单除掉。 这一传统可追溯至1929年毛泽东在福建古田提出的《关于纠正党内的错误思想》，其中已将干部的思想偏差比作“病症”。到1942至1945年的延安整风运动，“惩前毖后、治病救人”正式成为党内纪律处理的指导原则——写检查、党内批评与自我批评、组织审查定级，一整套流程延续至今，从基层到政治局概莫能外。 文章指出，整风的真正作用不在于改变干部的思想——大量证据显示，多数人不过是按剧本表态、风头一过便故态复萌——而在于生成一份永久存档的“个人档案”。 这份档案记录着每个人的历史污点与政治表现，成为悬在干部头上的“达摩克利斯之剑”，既制造出普遍的自我约束，也让党组织获得了掌控近亿党员所需的信息优势。由于定性过程由工作组起草、同事联署、上级批准层层完成，责任被有意分散，个人或机构都难以单独承担“整人”的骂名，从而降低了此举引发反弹的风险；同时，纪律运动也成为协调庞大官僚体系、压倒地方山头利益的有效工具。 不过，文章也强调，这套自我净化机制并非无懈可击：它擅长维系纪律，却无法解决接班问题。整风的逻辑要求不允许任何下属积累独立权威，这恰恰使真正有资历、有威望的接班人难以浮现。 毛泽东、邓小平当年凭借革命元勋的历史地位化解了继承危机，此后的领导人则依赖任期制等制度性安排；而这些安排如今已被习近平本人拆除殆尽。 文章由此判断，中共大概率不会崩溃——其档案与整肃体系正是为防止精英分裂而设计，且行之有效——但由此形成的政权很可能是“军事上更弱、政治上更强”的形态，与外界许多主流分析相悖。真正值得关注的风险节点，不是将领接连落马之时，而是最高领导人本人年迈却仍未明确继承人选之日。   * 更多精彩内容，欢迎长期关注《中国民主季刊》：https://chinademocrats.org/?cat=8

title: Murder trial opens for ex-husband and in-laws of Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi
summary: A murder trial for the ex-husband and two former in-laws of Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi has opened, three and a half years after her killing and dismemberment shocked the city. Hong Kong model and influencer Abby Choi, whose dismembered b
content: A murder trial for the ex-husband and two former in-laws of Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi has opened, three and a half years after her killing and dismemberment shocked the city. Hong Kong model and influencer Abby Choi, whose dismembered body was found by police in a Tai Po house on February 24, 2023. Photo: @xxabbyc/Instagram. Alex Kwong, Choi’s ex-husband, his father Kwong Kau, and his brother Anthony Kwong stand accused of murdering Choi and preventing the lawful burial of a body. They face up to life behind bars if convicted by a jury. The trio appeared at the High Court on Monday before deputy judge Brian Keith, with the courtroom packed with members of the public hoping to observe the high-profile trial, according to local media reports. The killing of Choi stunned the city in February 2023 when parts of her body were discovered in a village house in Lung Mei Tsuen, Tai Po, days after she went missing. Police found her remains in the fridge and soup pots in the house, which was equipped with an electric saw and a meat grinder that had been used to mince human flesh. The High Court. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Choi, an influencer with over 100,000 followers on Instagram, had appeared on the cover of fashion magazine L’Officiel Monaco and posted about her trip to Dior fashion week in Paris days before her murder. 💡 If you are suffering from sexual or domestic violence, regardless of your age or gender, contact the police, Harmony House ( click for details ) and/or the Social Welfare Department on 28948896. Dial 999 in emergencies. Authorities had said that Choi, who was 28 years old, and her ex-husband’s family had financial disputes involving a luxury property. See also: ‘Murder victim, rape survivor, porn star’: How Hong Kong media treats women reveals a wider issue, scholars say Choi divorced Kwong, with whom she had two children, and subsequently married Chris Tam, the son of the founder of the popular chain TamJai Yunnan Mixian. Choi and Tam also had two children together. The court on Monday ordered media not to report on the proceedings before a jury is sworn in and forbade the disclosure of the identities of Choi’s four children. The trial is expected to last 45 working days.

title: China expels generals accused of graft from Communist Party: state media
summary: China expelled two high-ranking military officers from the ruling Communist Party on Monday, state media reported, months after it was announced they were being investigated for “serious violations of the law”. Zhang Youxia in a 2023 meetin
content: China expelled two high-ranking military officers from the ruling Communist Party on Monday, state media reported, months after it was announced they were being investigated for “serious violations of the law”. Zhang Youxia in a 2023 meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin. Photo: Kremlin. One of them, Zhang Youxia , held the position of the more senior of two vice chairmen on the Central Military Commission (CMC), making him China’s highest-ranked general. However, the defence ministry said in January that Zhang and the second officer, Liu Zhenli, were “suspected of serious violations of discipline and the law”, a common euphemism for corruption. The announcement fit into the sweeping anti-graft drive that has defined President Xi Jinping’s time in power — but Zhang’s fall from grace in particular shocked observers, given his seniority and the perception he was close to China’s leader. State news agency Xinhua shared details of their cases for the first time, saying they involved “exceptionally large sums of money”. ‘Disloyal to the Party’ Top officials meeting in Beijing on Monday “decided to expel” the two men from the Communist Party and transfer their cases to the military’s legal organs “for review and prosecution”, Xinhua said. An investigation found Zhang and Liu had “become disloyal to the Party… and crossed red lines” by engaging in a list of offences including forming cliques and accepting huge sums of money for personal gain, Xinhua said. The two men also “used their positions to help others in matters such as job promotion”, Xinhua reported, citing the investigation. Their expulsion is subject to ratification at a plenary session of the Party’s Central Committee. Monday’s decision “reaffirms the firm position that… there is absolutely no place for corrupt elements to hide within the military”, Xinhua said. Last month, Zhang and Liu were stripped of their positions in the state CMC.

title: 美财长贝森特周日在摩根大通纽约总部与贸易代表格里尔一起会晤中国副总理何立峰

content: 2026年9月20日，美国财政部长贝森特抵达摩根大通纽约总部，与中国国务院副总理何立峰举行会晤。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)、贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)美国东部时间星期日(9月20日)上午在纽约与中国副总理何立峰就贸易、人工智能安全和稀土供应等问题举行会谈，为唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统这个星期四与中国领导人习近平的会晤铺平道路。 路透社的实况视频显示，纽约当地时间10点多，美国贸易代表格里尔率先抵达摩根大通纽约总部，随后，何立峰带领中国代表团抵达。10点30分左右，贝森特也到达了摩根大通的大楼。 在会晤开始前，贝森特告诉记者，他期待着“有针对性的、内容详尽的、有建设性的会谈”，这将为即将在华盛顿举行的特朗普-习近平峰会铺平道路。预计会议会持续一整天。 贝森特随后在社媒平台X上发帖说：“在纽约，我和何立峰副总理继续就美中经贸关系进行磋商，为美国总统特朗普与习近平主席在华盛顿举行的历史性峰会做准备。这些会谈有助于为特朗普总统推进美国经济利益、为美国人民带来成果奠定基础。” 根据美国贸易代表办公室星期五 宣布 的消息，美中正在加深合作，以促进这两个世界最大经济体之间的互利贸易。“特朗普政府将继续通过监督近期承诺的落实情况、扩大非敏感商品的贸易以及改善美国农民、制造商和工人的市场准入，来推动与中国的贸易平衡。”格里尔在声明中说。 中国商务部发言人星期六在官网回复记者询问时，也证实何立峰将在9月19日至23日率团赴美与美方“就彼此关心的经贸问题开展磋商。” 贝森特和美国贸易代表办公室的声明都没有透露会议的详细议程，但路透社星期天的报道说，关键议题将包括将于11月10日到期的美中贸易休战协议、美国官员所称的中国稀土磁体和关键矿产的供应不足问题，以及在人工智能模型安全漏洞事件曝光后，人工智能领域可能存在的安全保障措施。 贝森特这个星期稍早接受美国媒体 Axios 采访时表示，“美国仍然是人工智能领域的领导者。我们愿意就避免共同风险、防止两国人工智能体系走向分裂(bifurcation)展开讨论。” 外界高度关注这场纽约会谈释放的信号，尤其希望观察华盛顿与北京能否在习近平访美前，就关税、稀土供应、人工智能及贸易休战等核心经贸议题缩小、管控分歧，并为两国元首会晤铺平道路。 与此同时，在习近平访美行程安排方面，美联社和路透社分别援引美国政府高级官员的消息报道，特朗普计划在安德鲁斯联合基地机场迎接抵达美国的习近平。不过，白宫尚未通过正式声明公布这一安排。

title: 贝森特、格里尔周日会晤何立峰，美中峰会进入最后准备
summary: 资料照片：美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(左一)、美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(左二)以及中国副总理何立峰(右一)2025年5月11日在日内瓦会面讨论美中贸易和关税问题。 在美中特习峰会前的最后一个周末，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)，贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)星期日(9月20日)将在纽约与中国副总理何立峰举行会谈。与此同时，美国对中国国家主席习近平的来访进入最后准备阶段。 美国贸易代表办公室星期五 宣布 ，贸易代表格里尔星期日
content: 资料照片：美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(左一)、美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(左二)以及中国副总理何立峰(右一)2025年5月11日在日内瓦会面讨论美中贸易和关税问题。 在美中特习峰会前的最后一个周末，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)，贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)星期日(9月20日)将在纽约与中国副总理何立峰举行会谈。与此同时，美国对中国国家主席习近平的来访进入最后准备阶段。 美国贸易代表办公室星期五 宣布 ，贸易代表格里尔星期日将与财政部长贝森特一同前往纽约，会晤中国副总理何立峰，为即将在华盛顿举行的美中峰会做准备。 格里尔在声明中表示，美中正在加深合作，以促进这两个世界最大经济体之间的互利贸易。“特朗普政府将继续通过监督近期承诺的落实情况、扩大非敏感商品的贸易以及改善美国农民、制造商和工人的市场准入，来推动与中国的贸易平衡。”格里尔说。 中国商务部发言人星期六在官网回复记者询问时，也证实何立峰将在9月19日至23日率团赴美与美方“就彼此关心的经贸问题开展磋商。” 英国《金融时报》资深记者德米特里·塞瓦斯托普洛(Demetri Sevastopulo)星期六上午在X 发文 透露，贝森特与何立峰将于纽约当地时间星期日上午10点30分在摩根大通纽约总部举行会晤，“摩根大通提供场地，但不参与谈判，”他说。 包括美国贸易代表办公室和美国财政部均未公开证实会谈举办地点。 美国贸易代表办公室星期五的声明并未透露周日会谈的具体议程。 路透社 星期五引述知情人士称，贝森特与何立峰周日会谈的可能议题主要包括人工智能、贸易、稀土供应及更广泛的经济关系。 双方预计将讨论人工智能风险管控，贸易方面则可能涉及延长将于11月到期的关税休战、落实既有经贸承诺，以及改善美国农产品和其他商品的市场准入。稀土议题也将是重点，美国希望中国增加稀土磁材和关键矿产供应。 贝森特这个星期稍早接受美国媒体 Axios 采访时表示，“美国仍然是人工智能领域的领导者。我们愿意就避免共同风险、防止两国人工智能体系走向分裂(bifurcation)展开讨论。” 目前，有关纽约会谈的细节仍然不多。外界预计，双方将探讨特朗普与习近平可能达成共识的领域。路透社援引消息人士的话说，会谈可能延续到下周一(9月21日)至技术或工作层面，议程将保持灵活，以便双方就“一系列相关问题展开实质性讨论”。 外界高度关注这场纽约会谈释放的信号，尤其希望观察华盛顿与北京能否在习近平访美前，就关税、稀土供应、人工智能及贸易休战等核心经贸议题缩小、管控分歧，并为两国元首会晤铺平道路。 与此同时，在习近平访美行程安排方面，美联社和路透社分别援引美国政府高级官员的消息报道，特朗普计划在安德鲁斯联合基地机场迎接抵达美国的习近平。不过，白宫尚未通过正式声明公布这一安排。

title: America’s Secret Weapon in the Nuclear Race
summary: America’s Secret Weapon in the Nuclear Race bbert@hudson.org Thu, 09/17/2026 - 10:17 SVG Commentary Sep 17, 2026 Washington Post America’s Secret Weapon in the Nuclear Race Washington can tap a unique advantage as Beijing races ahead on fus
content: America’s Secret Weapon in the Nuclear Race bbert@hudson.org Thu, 09/17/2026 - 10:17 SVG Commentary Sep 17, 2026 Washington Post America’s Secret Weapon in the Nuclear Race Washington can tap a unique advantage as Beijing races ahead on fusion: private enterprise.   Abigail Remler David Feith Senior Fellow Abigail Remler & David Feith Commentary Caption The Burning Plasma Experimental Superconducting Tokamak (BEST) facility, which will house a compact fusion experiment device, undergoes its first exterior lighting test on September 9, 2026, in Hefei, China. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print Chinese leader Xi Jinping isn’t dawdling when it comes to science. He has directed his country to build a network of enormous fusion-energy facilities that could strengthen its ability to design and validate nuclear weapons without explosive testing. The United States has no comparable program, but it does possess a unique advantage: Private companies are already financing and building essential next-generation fusion technologies. Beijing doesn’t benefit from such an ecosystem, and Washington still leads across much of nuclear-weapons science and development. The Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California, for example, is still the only facility in the world to achieve fusion ignition. But scientific leadership doesn’t guarantee the experimental capacity, industrial base or construction speed that the U.S. will need for effective deterrence. The U.S. National Nuclear Security Administration, or NNSA, knows that well. It faces the increasingly difficult mission of modernizing the nuclear stockpile, producing more warheads and keeping pace with China’s rapid buildup, all with limited resources. The private sector offers the agency a way to stretch its resources further. Rather than try to build every new fusion capability itself, the NNSA could create a competitive, milestone-based partnership with private firms, while reserving certain highly sensitive functions for the government-run national laboratories. The model has already proved effective before. In 2006, NASA selected two companies to create systems capable of delivering cargo to the International Space Station. One was a four-year-old start-up named SpaceX. In choosing it, NASA’s Commercial Orbital Transportation Services program departed from the usual contracting model. The agency paid the companies only as they achieved technical milestones. The firms put their own capital at risk but retained ownership of what they built, allowing the same systems to serve customers beyond NASA. The results were catalytic. NASA invested about $788 million in the program, a fraction of the billions that the agency estimated traditional procurement might have cost. The partnership helped produce two cargo-delivery systems and gave SpaceX the patient capital and demanding customer it needed to develop capabilities that later served both government and commercial markets. The NNSA now faces a comparable opportunity in what’s known as inertial confinement fusion (ICF). The process uses lasers, pulsed electricity or other so-called drivers to compress tiny fuel targets — usually hydrogen-filled capsules smaller than a grain of rice — and create fusion conditions. The resulting temperatures, pressures and radiation environments allow scientists to study weapons materials and validate stockpile models without explosive nuclear tests. Though these capabilities have traditionally resided at NNSA-run national labs a new generation of companies is pursuing similar technologies to produce commercial fusion energy. Such ventures are primed to help support the country’s weapons-science mission . China recognizes this dual-use potential. It is investing roughly $10 billion in new laser and pulsed-power projects across at least five major ICF facilities, three of them already under construction, that will support military and commercial energy ambitions . The U.S., meantime, remains heavily dependent on aging facilities inside national labs, with major improvements years away and no settled plan for next-generation successors. China is thus poised to gain an edge in nuclear designs, weapons simulations and testing the effects of nuclear weapons on military systems, while building a springboard into commercial fusion energy. Congress could direct and fund the NNSA to establish a five-year, dual-use ICF capabilities program on the NASA-SpaceX model. The agency and its labs would specify the necessary physical environments and security protections, then award competing companies as they successfully deliver. Industry would contribute the capital, engineering talent and construction capacity. This would complement, not duplicate, the Energy Department’s existing milestone program for commercial fusion. That effort focuses on pilot plants capable of generating electricity. Their products are essential but unfit for security purposes. A NASA-style program investing in distinctly weapons-related capabilities would ensure that private facilities are designed from the outset to pursue multiple objectives — civilian and military — with appropriate government access and security. Nor would this privatize stockpile stewardship or replace the national labs. Classified weapons designs, simulation tools and effects data must remain tightly controlled. Many experiments should occur only at government sites. Commercial approaches might fail, change direction or prove poorly matched to NNSA requirements. That’s why the agency should support multiple technologies, pay for demonstrated results and preserve core government nuclear-weapons science capacity . Keeping industry at arm’s length, however, would deprive our nuclear-weapons enterprise of vital American ingenuity and capital. It could leave the NNSA trying to retrofit privately financed facilities after their designs have hardened, while watching valuable capabilities develop without any connection to the nuclear-weapons mission. Early partnership would be cheaper, safer and more useful. The choice is between an integrated American system that combines public missions with private capital and a fragmented one facing off against China’s coordinated buildup. Twenty years ago, NASA understood that preserving U.S. leadership required changing how government worked with industry. The NNSA can make the same leap. China is building, but American companies are, too. Washington can unite the national labs and private fusion firms before the next generation of facilities is built without national security needs in mind. As SpaceX showed, commercial partnerships created to meet certain government needs can help unlock entire industries and strategic advantages. Read in The Washington Post. Enjoyed this analysis? **“工程师治国”：中国为何热衷于“超级工程”？**

Published 3 小时前

大型建设工程正在重塑中国——从巨型大坝、庞大的太阳能发电场，到覆盖全国的高铁网络。北京的“工程师思维”能否助其应对气候变化？

中国的高层领导层长期由工程师主导，国家主席习近平便是其中之一，他曾在1970年代接受过化学工程专业的训练。

从港珠澳大桥到“南水北调”工程，这种对基建的热狂已延伸至能源领域。作为全球最大碳排放国，中国已投入数万亿美元布局风电、核电与特高压输电网。

然而，中国至今仍高度依赖煤电，且大规模工程常破坏在地生态，并造成数百万居民被迫迁徙。那么，北京的这种做法对气候变化意味着什么？

title: 特朗普总统表示他并未与习近平讨论向北京出售武器的可能

content: 特朗普总统在白宫椭圆形办公室讲话。(2026年9月28日) 唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统星期一(9月28日)说，他在上星期的美中峰会期间并没有与中国领导人习近平讨论向中国出售武器的可能性。美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Perdue)星期日在接受电视台采访时曾说，特朗普总统曾询问习近平是否有兴趣购买美国武器，美国政府随后澄清美国并无向中国出售武器的计划。 星期一，特朗普总统在白宫椭圆形办公室举行的一次活动中被记者问到，庞德伟大使在接受福克斯新闻星期天(Fox News Sunday)节目的采访时说，特朗普曾示意美国将向中国出售军事装备，这种说法是否准确？他是否提出这样的建议？ 特朗普总统问记者是不是问“向台湾”出售武器。记者说，庞德伟说的是“向中国”出售武器。 特朗普回答说：“我从来没听说过这件事。我得去问问他。你的意思是我们要卖给他们？他们可能会想买，因为我们制造的装备确实比他们的好。所以也许这是个好主意。不过，我们并没有讨论过这件事。他们可能谈的是台湾。我想他说的可能是台湾。” 庞德伟在星期日的那段电视采访中被主持人香农·布里姆(Shannon Bream)问到价值140亿美元的台湾武器订单和安全援助项目据报遭到延迟的问题。庞德伟强调美国的台湾政策没有改变。 “特朗普总统在台湾问题上的立场，和我见过的任何人一样坚定，”他说，“他已经非常明确地表示，我们没有改变一个中国政策。我们支持《台湾关系法》、三个联合公报和六项保证。” 庞德伟说，特朗普之前已经批准了价值110亿美元的对台军售，美方还在继续讨论其他可能的军售项目。 “我们的支持没有改变，”他说，“我们不支持独立，也不支持胁迫。” 他在采访中提到，特朗普曾向习近平解释，美国向世界其他地方出售武器。 “特朗普总统一直说，‘嘿，我们向世界各地的其他人出售武器。’他实际上有一次还问习近平主席，他是否也想买一些，”庞德伟说。 一名美国国务院官员星期日晚回应美国之音(VOA)的置评请求时说：“美国法律禁止向中国出售武器，也不存在向中国出售武器的提议或计划。” 中国目前被列入美国《国际武器贸易条例》(ITAR)限制名单。美国对向中国出口国防物品和国防服务实行原则上拒绝批准的政策。 白宫公布的特朗普与习近平峰会成果文件也没有提及两人讨论向中国出售美国武器。 中国国家主席习近平上星期对美国进行了白宫所称赞的“历史性”的国事访问。 特朗普总统星期一说：“我们和习主席进行了很棒的会晤，我给它的评分–从0分到10分–我给它的评分是12分。非常尊重，非常好。很棒的会晤。”

title: 共产党从旧习俗死敌，摇身一变成了旧习俗拥护者

content: * 本文编译自《经济学人》茶馆专栏 * 原文地址： https://www.economist.com/china/2026/09/28/xi-jinping-uses-old-festivals-to-boost-the-partys-image 20世纪初，中国的改革者们猛烈抨击农历及其旧节庆，认为它们与现代格格不入。1912年清朝覆灭以后，中华民国政府采用了公历。中国共产党则走得更远，把许多节日斥为“封建迷信”。 中国共产党从旧习俗的死敌摇身一变，成了它们的推广者，这是比较戏剧化的一次立场大转变。春节在“文革”期间曾被取消，到1980年才得以恢复。不过，直到2005年，中共才发布文件，号召复兴传统节日，尤其是中秋节、清明节、端午节。 习近平赋予了这些节日更大的政治分量。他称这些节日是中华文化自信的体现，并由此暗示，党是“中国性”的保证。“同一轮明月”是中秋前后反复出现的宣传主题，被用来形容中国各民族之间的纽带、台海两岸共同的文化遗产，以及全人类的共同福祉。官方媒体借节日之机，大力宣扬习近平非常喜欢的一个老观念：国与家是交织在一起的。 中国的传统节日复兴远不只是一场自上而下的运动。诚然各地过节的热情参差不齐：在许多城市，人们只是享受放假而已。但在南方，尤其是福建，寺庙和宗祠比其他地方更完整地挺过了毛泽东时代动乱。古老的习俗是对抗现代失范感的锚，对许多人来说，家庭团聚的喜悦（和烦恼）远比国家统一这个抽象概念更重要。 对传统节日复兴的一种常见批评是：流于表面。中秋节有个戏谑的别称叫“月饼节”，因为过去许多人过这个节，唯一的方式就是吃月饼（另外，月饼礼盒也是贿赂官员的便利工具）。如今与中秋相关的活动如此丰富，说明传统在许多地方正在扎得更深，这在很大程度上是因为各个城市想吸引更多游客。漳州有踩高跷扮演民间人物的表演；在西安，演员们走上街头，邀游客比拼咏月诗词；水乡乌镇设起祭台，人们可以在台上为月亮女神嫦娥供奉食物。 问题在于，人们越是认真对待传统，官方规定与民间实际需要之间的摩擦就越明显。漳州寺庙林立，但任何扩建都须经宗教事务部门繁琐审批，教义要符合官方解释，场所还得悬挂国旗，有的寺庙院子里甚至立着颂扬习近平保护传统文化的展板。推崇以汉族为主的节日，也可能疏远少数民族。据活动人士说，一些信仰伊斯兰教的维吾尔人曾被施压在春节喝酒、吃猪肉饺子，以示过节。党还公开担心村民把寺庙和宗祠当作世俗权威来源。一位国学老师解释说，按儒家的道理，君主并不能为所欲为，百姓是否顺服，要看统治者是否施行仁政；但被问到当今领导人是否做到了，他抿着嘴，没有回答。 共产党如今成了它曾经贬低、甚至试图消灭的那些传统的守护者。可它唤回的这些传统，根扎得比党本身深得多，最终或许更有资格赢得人们的忠诚。

title: Hong Kong’s changing climate in 7 charts: from quadrupled ‘very hot days’ to record rainfall
summary: Hongkongers have long complained of the city’s summers getting hotter and longer – and the numbers show they’re not wrong. Hong Kong saw a record-breaking heatwave in summer 2026. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Data from the Hong Kong Observato
content: Hongkongers have long complained of the city’s summers getting hotter and longer – and the numbers show they’re not wrong. Hong Kong saw a record-breaking heatwave in summer 2026. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Data from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) shows that record after record is being broken, from the number of “hot nights” a year to the average temperature through August, the final month of summer. HKFP looks at the city’s warming climate over the decades in seven charts. 1. ‘Very hot days’ on the rise (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); In the 2000s, the city recorded a yearly average of 13.4 “very hot days” – when the daily maximum temperature reaches 33 degrees or above. Since the 2020s, there have been more than 50 very hot days a year. Records were set in 2021 and 2023, when Hong Kong experienced 54 very hot days. By the end of August, there had already been 30 very hot days so far this year. As of September 21, there have been four very hot days this month. The number of very hot days in August has generally risen in proportion with the annual figure. 2. Heat warnings in force more than ever (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); Annual hours under the HKO’s “very hot weather warning” have tripled since 2000 – climbing from 464 hours to a peak of over 1,400 hours in 2021. Since 2020, heat warnings have been in force for at least 13 per cent of every calendar year. In 2000, it was just over 5 per cent. The very hot weather warning is triggered not by a specific temperature, but by a heat index threshold that takes into account temperature, humidity, and airflow. 3. ‘Extremely hot days’ prevalent (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); The HKO defines extremely hot days as days when the maximum temperature reaches or exceeds 35 degrees. With the exception of one abnormally hot year in 1963, when there were five “extremely hot days,” the city had never seen a year with more than two such days until the past decade. Most years, in fact, had no extremely hot days. That’s changed since 2016. Hong Kong has recorded an average of 4.6 extremely hot days annually for the last 10 years. So far this year, there have been three , all of them in August. 4. Summers getting longer The city is not just seeing more “very hot days” – it’s also experiencing them across a wider timeframe, beyond the traditional summer months . Before the 2010s, very hot days were concentrated in June, July and August. In other months, they were rare. But over the past decade, very hot days have increasingly been starting as early as May, and spilling into September and October. Between 2021 and 2025, the city recorded a double-digit number of very hot days in September, compared to typical single-digit figures or even zero in previous years. Last year, there were four very hot days in October. Before 2021, there were usually none. 5. August temperatures soar above ‘normal’ (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); The mean temperature in August used to regularly sit below 28.7 degrees, which the HKO defines as the “normal” mean temperature for the month. But in the past decade, temperatures above that threshold have become the norm. Since 2016, there were only two years that the mean temperature in August dipped below the “normal” level – and not by much. In 2016, the mean August temperature was 28.4, and in 2018, it was 28.6. In comparison, across the 35-year span from 1980 to 2015, there were a total of 22 years in which the mean temperature was below normal. 6. Number of ‘hot nights’ doubles (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); The HKO defines “ hot nights ” as ones when the daily minimum temperature is 28 degrees or above. From 2015 onwards, there have been an average of 46 hot nights a year, with 2021 setting an all-time record of 61. In contrast, there were only around 20 hot nights annually from 2000 to 2009. As of the end of August, there have been 35 hot nights so far this year, putting it on par with last year. By the end of August 2025, there were 34 hot nights. But there have not been any hot nights in September so far. Last year, there were 13 – a historical record for that month. 7. Rainstorm warnings more frequent (function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})(); There have been 15 red rainstorm warnings and three black rainstorm warnings so far this year – both the second-highest numbers on record. Last year, the HKO issued 16 red rainstorm warnings and five black rainstorm warnings – a record for both. The 82 warnings issued so far this year – among which the vast majority are the lowest-level amber alerts – are the most in history. The city was particularly rainy in June, July and August, with July’s rainfall being the second-highest on record for the month. June also saw the HKO issue two black rainstorm warnings in one day for the first time.

title: Trump embraces Xi as he turns up attacks on American media
summary: Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors. **Jeffrey Goldberg:** I want to turn to the visit by President Xi to Washington for a state visit. There are flyovers, a lot of pl
content:
Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** I want to turn to the visit by President Xi to Washington for a state visit. There are flyovers, a lot of planes, and a lot of fancy dinners, but not much happened. I mean, unless I'm wrong, Adam.

**Adam Harris, Host, Radio Atlantic:** We got a lot of platitudes out of it. We got an extension of this sort of almost like ceasefire in the trade war temporarily, but I think --

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Like a two-month extension.

**Adam Harris:** A two-month extension, exactly right.

Well, we came into this week with the idea that they would be talking about A.I., right, all of the warnings that we've been getting from kind of across the political spectrum. You had Scott Bessent who said that he met with his counterpart in China and that they had discussed a potential sort of like red phone for A.I. and a warning system on the back end.

But, you know, several days on, what we have seen is that, you know, China didn't come with any of its CEOs in the same way that Trump came with CEOs to -- when he made his visit to China. So, it was almost as if they were in two different places, right, where Trump likes to move fast and negotiate and say, oh, we want to, we're going to get a deal done right now, where China's saying, well, we're still trying to thaw this relationship that has been sort of tense and, you know, you've, going through a series of retaliatory trade tariffs and --

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** I bet OpenAI is building that red phone right now. That'll be good. It'll be manned by a bot.

The -- and, Susan, I want to talk about the A.I. in China because that was the -- if there had been consequential outcomes here, that would have been a consequential outcome. This is what Xi said this week about A.I. Both China and the United States are leading nations in artificial intelligence. We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage A.I. for good and ensure that the development of A.I. is always under human control and serves the wellbeing of the people.

Trump, on the other hand, said this week at the U.N., the United States also totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control for the artificial intelligence being spoken of so much now. Hereinafter officially called super intelligence, changing the name and that the use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake. It makes it sound fake.

Okay, so we're in a weird situation, not the first time we've been in a weird situation, that the leader of the Communist Party dictatorship that rules China, rhetorically at least, sounds more with it, maybe than the president of the United States on this subject. Talk through their differing approaches.

**Susan Glasser, Staff Writer, The New Yorker:** Yes. No, Jeff, I mean, if anything, the quote that you read, you know, it's certainly eyebrow-raising if the president -- his A.I. approach is to say, I'd like to rebrand it. You know, it's not a branding problem that's causing these engineers to say that there's --

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** What's the expression? You know that expression in Washington, sometimes you have a P.R. problem and sometimes you just have a problem?

**Susan Glasser:** Yes, exactly.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** I think these companies have a problem.

**Susan Glasser:** Like, Houston, we have a problem, right?

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Yes.

**Susan Glasser:** I mean, you know, the people who are building A.I., you know, a good proportion of them are warning us that there's not a zero chance risk of them destroying humanity, as we know it. And, apparently, that has taken a second priority for the president of the United States to rebranding A.I. and also showing the leader of China his new helipad.

But, you know, if anything what I was going to say, Jeff, is that your quote is one of the less embarrassing quotes, if that's possible, that Donald Trump gave about artificial intelligence this week. At his speech at the United Nations General Assembly, he talked about rebranding A.I. He also talked about the fact that A.I. was just another hoax, like, quote, Russia, Russia, Russia, like climate change, and all the other things that they're trying to fool us with.

And so what's fascinating to me is that Donald Trump is now viewing the sort of A.I. doom warnings coming, again, from inside Silicon Valley itself. He's now saying that's some kind of a Democratic hoax, like his collusion with Russia in the 2016 campaign.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Right.

**Susan Glasser:** And it shows the extreme personalization of power. He came out after his first meetings with Xi the other day and he said, I don't want to do anything about Russia. Our guardrail -- sorry, about A.I., our guardrail for A.I. is the Department of Justice.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Our guard -- Vivian, what -- the personalization of power is interesting idea. Why is Trump slotting A.I. into this kind of reaction narrative? In other words, why is he taking the side of untrammeled A.I?

**Vivian Salama, Staff Writer, The Atlantic:**I mean, there's the argument that he doesn't quite understand how it works, and this is something that we hear a lot --

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** To be fair, that we share some of that. I mean, nobody really -- there's a few hundred people who might understand how it works.

**Vivian Salama:** No judgment. No judgment.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Yes, no judgment. Yes.

**Vivian Salama:** Just putting it out there is that, you know --

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Just being fair.

**Vivian Salama:** -- he's someone who doesn't use email and, like, you know, he's just maybe of a generation or just the type of man that he is, that he just doesn't really delve into these issues very deeply.

There's also the business side of it. I mean, we were just talking about the business opportunities, you know. Yes, Xi did not show up with CEOs, but the entire state dinner with Xi was packed with tech CEOs from the United States, who Trump very eager to kind of get them having a leg up in businesses and especially in China where there are opportunities for cooperation for American businesses to kind of take advantage of some, you know, of the market there. And I think he sees it as, you know, let's wait and see if this is going to be good for American business before we cast judgment too much on this technology.

And, of course, you have people like J.D. Vance and others who are younger and a little bit more -- I'm not ageist, but putting it out there, you know, he has came from Silicon Valley and kind of is a little bit more immersed in things like this and he's a little more cautious with his language.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:**Yes. I noticed at the state dinner, the head table, Trump and Xi, Jensen Huang, the NVIDIA chairman, who's quite bullish in that Trumpian kind of it's all going to be fine, and Elon Musk, by the way, always a surprise guest at the White House these days, who has been warning about A.I. And what a fascinating conversation that could have been because you have the Chinese -- we've been told in this country beware of China and its autocratic development of A.I., killer robots and killer everything. But then you have an American president who is taking a kind of extreme libertarian view. It's all very muddled now to try to make sense of this.

**Peter Baker, Chief White House Correspondent, The New York Times:** It also is sort of this kind of an arms race view of it as well.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Yes.

**Peter Baker:** Like, you know, if we don't do it, China will.

And, you know, look, there is an argument that, you know, could we trust China to restrain itself even if we did come to some sort of an international accord, right? Had they been good actors on the stage before? It's an open question.

But this reminds us of the early days of the Cold War when nuclear arms were still being developed by only a handful of countries, and we tried to figure out how do we keep that genie back in the bottle?

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Right. Vivian I noticed that -- as you have, that the summit ended in a kind of typical way with the Chinese ultimately coming back to the thing that obsesses them, Taiwan.

**Vivian Salama:** The Chinese put out a statement while President Trump was very keen to just put out that it was a great meeting, they did lots of great things. The Chinese put out a very flowery statement where they talked about cooperation and partnership and, you know, the need to enhance their strategic cooperation.

And then tucked in like paragraph number five was this very stern statement about the need to respect China's, you know, territorial claims over Taiwan. And basically in summary, the U.S. needs to stay out of it. And that is very keen, especially because of the fact that President Trump has never really been explicit about his views on Taiwan, and he's sort of taking a wait-and-see approach on what kind of positions invest with Xi.

There's been major concerns that he will kind of throw in the kitchen sink or Taiwan if he's to get a China deal. And so this has been a concern here in Washington, especially including among Republicans who don't want to see that.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:**So, at the end of this summit, we're back where we were before. We have no sense of whether -- we understand that China's preoccupied with taking Taiwan by force possibly. And we have no sense of whether the president of the United States will actually do what other presidents we think would have done, which is defend Taiwan.

**Vivian Salama:**And his advisers tell me, you know, there is no change in the U.S. policy toward Taiwan. And I say, well, why doesn't the president just say that? And they say, the president's going to do what he's going to do.

**Jeffrey Goldberg:** Well, I'm going to do what I'm going to do and pivot to -- well, it's all Trump, alas, here we are. But the press crisis that we're having, Adam, I wanted to show you a clip of President Trump addressing Kaitlan Collins from CNN.

title: The Coverage of the Uyghurs in Indonesian Media
source: 乔治华盛顿大学维吾尔族研究中心(每月1到2次）
summary: * Guest contribution by Ibrahim Abdulmajid In understanding an increasingly complex global landscape, the media plays a central role in shaping particular narratives and perspectives on various topics and issues, including the Uyghur issue
content: * Guest contribution by Ibrahim Abdulmajid In understanding an increasingly complex global landscape, the media plays a central role in shaping particular narratives and perspectives on various topics and issues, including the Uyghur issue in Indonesia. The Chinese government has invested heavily in influence operations that employ disinformation tactics and media propaganda. In this regard, particularly concerning Southeast Asia, the Center for Uyghur Studies has published a special report titled China’s Influence Operations in Southeast Asia and the Uyghur Crisis. Amid the Chinese government’s extensive disinformation and propaganda operations, Indonesia’s local media plays a crucial role in countering such efforts. But how exactly do Indonesian media outlets report on and frame issues concerning the plight of Uyghur Muslims? Several scholarly journal articles have examined this question. One of them is an article by Betha Dwi Octaviani comparing how Tempo and Antara frame the Uyghur issue. Tempo is a privately owned media outlet founded in 1971. It was temporarily shut down in 1982 because of its critical coverage of Indonesia’s authoritarian government at the time. In 1994, the Soeharto government shut down Tempo for a second time. Today, Tempo is known for its critical stance toward Indonesia’s domestic political affairs. Meanwhile, Antara is Indonesia’s national news agency, owned by the Indonesian government. Its origins date back to the colonial era, when it was founded in 1937. At that time, Antara was established as an alternative to the Dutch colonial government’s media, which Indonesian activists believed did not represent the interests of the country’s indigenous population in its reporting. Between Private and Government Media In the journal article cited above, Betha found differences in how Tempo and Antara presented news reports about the Uyghur issue. While Tempo covered the issue in the context of alleged human rights violations and drew upon survivor testimonies and reports by international human rights organizations, Antara positioned it within the context of bilateral relations between Indonesia and China. It tended to adopt a “safe” stance to preserve the stability of relations between the two countries. Drawing upon official reports from international bodies and organizations such as the […] The post The Coverage of the Uyghurs in Indonesian Media appeared first on Center for Uyghur Studies .

content: 一种用于感冒和流感补充剂的药用草本成分，因与严重过敏反应有关，将逐步退出澳洲货架。 澳洲治疗用品管理局（TGA）周一宣布，穿心莲（Andrographis paniculata）今后不得用于进入澳洲市场的新药。 不过，含穿心莲的现有药物不会立即下架，TGA已鼓励供应商召回相关产品。 穿心莲原产于印度和斯里兰卡，在阿育吠陀医学和中国传统医学中颇为常见，通常用于支持免疫力、对抗感冒及流感症状。 目前约有80种含穿心莲的产品列在澳洲市场，超市、保健食品店和药房均有售。 过去几年，业界对这一成分的忧虑不断升温。此前曾有过敏性休克反应报告，2024年6月还出现一宗死亡事件。 TGA表示：“我们持续收到与含穿心莲药物有关的过敏性休克报告。” TGA说：“我们决定从《允许使用成分认定》（Permissible Ingredients Determination）中移除穿心莲，因为在列名药物框架下，严重过敏反应（包括过敏性休克）的风险无法得到充分降低。” 这项决定源于今年4月完成的安全审查。审查认定，截至2025年12月，该药物被认定导致1368宗反应，其中近300宗属于过敏性休克病例。 TGA指出，穿心莲引发的过敏反应无法预测：有人第一次服用就会出现反应，也有人此前服用一直没有问题，后来仍可能发作。 目前仍不清楚穿心莲为何会导致过敏性休克，而大多数受影响者此前没有已知的过敏或哮喘病史。 行业主要倡导机构Complementary Medicines Australia批评这项禁令，主张像管理扑热息痛（paracetamol）和抗生素等其他药物一样，以警告方式管理穿心莲。 该机构说：“全面禁止并不是正确做法，因为这会让数十万澳洲民众无法继续获得一种他们一直安全使用的产品。大量证据显示，相当多消费者会转而购买网上产品，而这些产品甚至没有任何警告。” TGA强烈鼓励供应商自愿停产含有该成分的补充剂，并展开面向消费者的召回行动。 如果企业不自行召回产品并停止生产，TGA将从10月中旬起采取监管行动，停止这类药物的供应。 澳洲公司BioCeuticals表示，旗下ArmaForce和Clinical ImmuneForce补充剂都含有这一成分，公司已经停止发出相关库存，目前正与TGA沟通。 BioCeuticals说：“消费者的健康和安全是我们的最高优先事项。” 当局建议消费者检查自己的药物是否含有穿心莲，再考虑是否继续使用。 预计这一成分将转入注册药物途径。该途径监管更严格，并要求提供消费者用药信息。

title: HKFP Lens: Fans celebrate Hong Kong icon Leslie Cheung on what would have been his 70th birthday
summary: Exhibitions and events around Hong Kong have celebrated local icon Leslie Cheung on what would have been his 70th birthday on September 12. More than 23 years after his death, the events show how Cheung left his mark not only on the worlds
content: Exhibitions and events around Hong Kong have celebrated local icon Leslie Cheung on what would have been his 70th birthday on September 12. More than 23 years after his death, the events show how Cheung left his mark not only on the worlds of music and film, but also in the hearts of countless fans who still think of him as family. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” in Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. All across his hometown, venues were festooned with photographs of the Cantopop singer and movie star, plastered with posters for his films and artwork from his albums, and decorated with the costumes he wore on stage. A live tribute concert was also staged, and a drone show lit up the skies above Victoria Harbour in his honour. HKFP documented these events, which drew in fans of all different ages and backgrounds. An exhibition on the classic film “Days of Being Wild” in a Commercial Press store in Tsim Sha Tsui, September 16, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Born in Hong Kong on September 12, 1956, Cheung was a trailblazer in a relatively conservative era. He first made his name as a Cantopop singer but later made waves in the film industry as well, starring in classics such as Rouge, Days of Being Wild, Farewell My Concubine, and Happy Together. He was also famous for his distinctive sense of style, which reflected his androgyny and bisexuality and cemented his place as a queer icon in the Chinese-speaking world. A poster for the classic Hong Kong film “Days of Being Wild” displayed in Causeway Bay on September 16, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The star, who struggled with depression, died by suicide on April 1, 2003. To this day, fans still mark the date by leaving flowers at the Mandarin Oriental hotel in Central, where he fell to his death. To them, he is more than just a celebrity – he is “Gor Gor,” their Elder Brother. The “Leslie – Grace at 70 Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Design Institute in Tiu Keng Leng, September 16, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. 💡 If you are in need of support , please call: The Samaritans 2896 0000 (24-hour, multilingual), Suicide Prevention Centre 2382 0000 or the gov’ t mental health hotline on 18111. The Hong Kong Society of Counselling and Psychology provides a WhatsApp hotline in English and Chinese: 6218 1084. See also: HKFP’s mental health services guide. To mark Cheung’s 70th birthday, the Hong Kong Heritage Museum has opened an exhibition entitled “Miss You Much” that will run until May next year. Between now and November 15, the Hong Kong Design Institute in Tiu Keng Leng will also be home to a showcase called “Leslie・Grace at 70 Exhibition.” The Commercial Press in Tsim Sha Tsui, meanwhile, has curated an exhibition, open until October 11, spotlighting Wong Kar-wai’s 1990 film Days of Being Wild, which starred Cheung alongside a host of other Hong Kong icons. Vintage boutique offLINE STUDIO has also put together a display on the film in its Causeway Bay store. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On September 12 this year, the organiser of a tribute concert broadcast an audio message from Daffy Tong, Cheung’s longtime partner: Hello everyone. Today is Leslie’s 70th birthday, and we are here to wish him a happy birthday. After all these years, Leslie hasn’t changed at all – he remains as handsome and charming as ever. His movies are still wonderful to watch, and his songs are still beautiful to hear. What has changed is us: we have grown old, with hair full of grey and faces full of wrinkles. Yet our hearts for him have never changed. We still miss Gor Gor and love him dearly. The “Miss You Much Leslie 70th Birthday Exhibition” at the Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin, September 17, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Fashion display on the classic Hong Kong film “Days of Being Wild” in a vintage clothing store in Causeway Bay, September 16, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. content: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)将于星期二(9月22日)在纽约出席联合国大会的期间与前来纽约出席联合国大会的日本首相高市早苗(Sanea Takaichi)举行双边会晤。分析人士指出，这对美日两国在对华关系上，特别是关键矿产问题上保持更加紧密的一致提供了很好的机会。 由于特朗普星期四将在白宫招待前来美国进行国事访问的中国国家主席习近平，而中日关系由于高市有关台湾的发言持续恶化、跌入谷底，特朗普与高市的会晤和他与习近平举行的峰会同样引起各界的高度关注。 华盛顿智库德国马歇尔基金会“印太”计划主任葛来仪(Bonnie S. Glaser)星期天上午在X平台发帖说：“高市首相在纽约与特朗普的会晤，为强调美日两国在对华关系，特别是关键矿产/永磁体和台湾问题上需要更加紧密地保持一致提供了一个很好的机会。” 华盛顿奥尔布赖特石桥集团(Albright Stone Group)合伙人、技术以及亚洲及美洲政策主管 保罗 ·特廖洛(Paul Triolo)则在X上写道：“高市寻求在下周初在美中峰会前会晤特朗普，日本首相是希望让华盛顿继续保持对中国的威慑。” 美国常驻联合国代表迈克·沃尔兹(Mike Waltz)上星期五证实了上述消息。他说，特朗普总统将于星期一和星期二访问纽约两天，期间将在联合国大会上发表演说。特朗普在会议的间隙还将分别会晤日本首相高市早苗和英国首相安迪·伯纳姆(Andy Burnham)。高市首相也将从星期一开始对纽约进行为期四天的访问，并且也将在联合国大会发表演说。 日本是美国在亚洲的重要盟友。特朗普总统5月在结束对中国的访问，乘坐“空军一号”返美途中，主动致电高市早苗，向其详细介绍了“特习会”的会谈情况。 根据日本防卫省星期六公布的新闻稿，日本时间9月18日晚上，日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎与美国战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)举行了约10分钟的电话会谈。在会谈中，两防长一致表示将强化日美同盟的威慑力。 《日本时报》(Japan Times)在报道中指出，高市与习近平在与特朗普会谈时，可能都会提及或强调台湾问题。 中国政府一直声称对实施民主治理的台湾拥有主权，而且不惜动武也要实现中国大陆与台湾的统一。为了实现这一目标，北京方面不仅持续建军备战，而且持续增大对台湾的安全和军事压力。 高市早苗于2025年11月7日在国会众议院接受质询时表示，如果发生“台湾有事”，可能构成日本可行使集体自卫权的“存亡危机事态”，日本自卫队不排除进行武力干预。高市早苗的这番发言导致日中关系持续恶化、跌入谷底。 特朗普总统今年访问北京并与习近平举行峰会后曾提出美军“长途跋涉9500英里去打仗”是否合理的问题。特朗普还谈及将一项价值140亿美元的对台军售案作为与习近平打交道时的筹码，将其称为“非常好的谈判筹码”。特朗普的这番谈话不仅引起台湾方面，而且也导致东京方面的担忧。 另据多家日本媒体的报道，高市会晤特朗普时，双方可能也会讨论美国针对国际刑事法院(ICC)院长、日本籍人士赤根智子(Tomoko Akane)实施制裁的问题。 日本政府支持赤根智子和国际刑事法院，而美国则认为该机构应该解散。高市在会谈中将如何处理这一问题尚待观察。

title: In Pictures: Hong Kong sex work exhibition explores violence and bodily autonomy in an underground industry
summary: Boxes of condoms, AI-generated photos of sex workers, and a computer opened up to a part-time girlfriends website sit inside Heath, an event space in Tsim Sha Tsui. AI-generated posters of sex workers at A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition a
content: Boxes of condoms, AI-generated photos of sex workers, and a computer opened up to a part-time girlfriends website sit inside Heath, an event space in Tsim Sha Tsui. AI-generated posters of sex workers at A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The venue is perhaps a fitting one for A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition spotlighting the history of sex work in Hong Kong. Located in the basement of Chungking Mansions, it was once home to a string of nightclubs. The two-week exhibition is organised by three NGOs that support the city’s sex workers – Action for Reach Out, Teen’s Key, and Midnight Blue. A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wong Ka-ying, an artist and writer who curated the showcase, said the exhibition aimed not only to show pride in sex work, but also to explore themes such as violence, choice, and bodily autonomy. “Sex work is [one of] the oldest industries in the world, with over 3,000 years of history, yet the stigma around it remains pervasive,” Wong said in Cantonese during a media preview last Friday. (From left to right) Exhibition curator Wong Ka-ying, executive director of Teen’s Key Megan Yik, executive director of Action for Reach Out Cherry Chui, and director of Midnight Blue Ngai Tak-kin. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “But why, today, when human civilization has advanced so much, is our understanding and perspective on sex work still so narrow?” she said. “These are the questions we want to ask.” Wong will also lead exhibition tours this weekend, with English and Cantonese sessions available. A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. As part of the media preview, the exhibition’s organisers invited four people with experience in the sex work industry to share their stories. An online sex workers’ directory at A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Daphne, who describes herself as a “professional domme,” said she first got into rope play in 2022. This is her full time job, she said, adding that she also teaches rope bondage. Her interest in BDSM was first sparked when she was studying fashion design. She said she was “obsessed” with latex, and later learned through online research that she was a dominant. Daphne, a sex worker, at A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. She finds most of her clients through social media, where they send her a message. In return, she asks them what they are looking for, what their “hard limitations” are, and what their personal experience is. A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “I really like BDSM. I really enjoy the power exchange dynamic,” she said in Cantonese. “Some of my clients are very generous,” Daphne added. “They buy me a business class ticket or take me on overseas trips. They pay for everything.” A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Another woman, who asked to be called Captain, said she became a part-time girlfriend in 2017 when she was still a student because she had to help her family pay off a large debt. Scrawls reading “whore” and “STDs on the fourth floor” at A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “I heard that being a part-time girlfriend would allow me to make a lot of money quickly,” she said, adding that she created an Instagram account and searched the hashtag “part-time girlfriend.” Newspaper clippings about the Hong Kong Macau Sex Cultural Festival in 2008 at A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Now a single mother of two, she is still in the industry and works to pay off her family’s debt monthly. Unlike Daphne, she sees her work as purely for making money. She said she has had some unpleasant experiences, including being filmed in secret by a man and police raiding the spa she was working at. A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Asked how she protects herself, Captain said that when she meets clients, she checks in to hotel rooms with them together. “This way, I can make sure the client didn’t arrive first and install a camera,” she said. She said she does regular STD check-ups at Action for Reach Out. A Body of One’s Own, an exhibition about sex work in Hong Kong, at Heath in Tsim Sha Tsui. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Only my closest friends know that this is what I do,” she said. Running until September 27, the exhibition will also feature events including a life drawing session, sharings by sex workers, and a theatre workshop. A Body of One’s Own Address : The Garage @ Heath, Basement floor, 36-44 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong Date : September 12 to 27 Entry : Free

content:
路透社：美国限制对华商飞零件出口，防止中国囤货

10月1日，路透社援引多名知情人士称，美国商务部过去数周放慢了对华航空零件出口许可审批，并限制中国商飞获准进口的零件数量，防止其囤货。特朗普政府希望将中国对美国航空供应商的依赖，转化为贸易谈判筹码，争取在稀土供应等问题上获得让步。

这涉及国产大飞机的关键供应链。发动机制造商CFM在2026年5月26日发布的资料显示，C919使用其LEAP-1C发动机；CFM由美国GE与法国赛峰各持股50%。

据报道，中国还希望为同意购买的200架波音飞机取得数年所需的备件，但美方不愿作保证，希望保留零件供应作为换取未来让步的筹码。目前，这项备件要求的进展尚不明确。美国供应商的零件对中国航司运营的波音、空客飞机，以及商飞生产的客机都很关键。

美国官员还在考虑进一步限制起落架等航空零件出口，一份草案提出对航空液压油增加出口许可要求。这些新规定尚处于讨论或草案阶段，不能等同于已经全面禁运。

报道指出，习近平上周访美后，两国同意将贸易休战延长至2027年1月10日，但航空零件供应仍被美方保留为施压工具。报道发表时，美国商务部、白宫及中国驻美使馆均未立即回应。

title: 罗夏日记 | 别再吹中国“最安全”：警察国家给你安全感，法治国家才给你安全
summary: 罗 夏日记 X @Hh06554468Hh · October 2, 2026 《 别再吹中国“最安全”：警察国家给你安全感，法治国家才给你安全 》 前两天看老梁谈“中国是不是世界上最安全的国家”，有句话我觉得一针见血：安全感和安全，是两回事。 中国人经常把“安全”理解成治安：晚上敢不敢出门，有没有枪，会不会被抢。中国媒体又长期喜欢报道欧美的枪击、毒品、抢劫，于是很容易形成一种印象：国外乱，中国最安全。 可我在中国生活那么多年，我对中国式安全最大的体会就一句话：你别遇上事。
content: 罗 夏日记   X @Hh06554468Hh  · October 2, 2026 《 别再吹中国“最安全”：警察国家给你安全感，法治国家才给你安全 》 前两天看老梁谈“中国是不是世界上最安全的国家”，有句话我觉得一针见血：安全感和安全，是两回事。 中国人经常把“安全”理解成治安：晚上敢不敢出门，有没有枪，会不会被抢。中国媒体又长期喜欢报道欧美的枪击、毒品、抢劫，于是很容易形成一种印象：国外乱，中国最安全。 可我在中国生活那么多年，我对中国式安全最大的体会就一句话：你别遇上事。 没事的时候当然安全。上班、吃饭、逛街、晚上撸串，到处是摄像头、安检、警察，管得严得不得了。可问题是，管得严，就等于安全吗？ 一个真正安全的社会，不是只保证你晚上撸串的时候没人抢你，而是你倒霉的时候依然有人跟你讲理。 你被欠薪了怎么办？遇到冤屈怎么办？正常渠道解决不了，你想讨个说法怎么办？我在北京亲眼见过截访：一边设置信访部门让你反映问题，另一边现实中又长期存在地方人员拦截、带回赴京上访者的现象。门给你挂着，路却给你堵着。 生病、失业、孩子教育、35岁以后找工作，也都是一样。中国人为什么那么爱攒钱？很多时候不是因为多喜欢存钱，而是因为不敢不存。因为你知道自己不能轻易掉下去。一场大病、一次失业、一次家庭变故，都可能让一个普通家庭迅速感受到风险。我把这种东西叫作“中国式斩杀线”。 做生意也是一样。真正让人没有安全感的，不是哪一项具体政策，而是你不知道明天规则会不会突然变。一个行业今天还合法经营、正常投资，明天一纸政策下来，就可能大幅改变整个商业模式。2021年的“双减”就是最典型的例子：政策急转之后，大量教培机构退出市场。对一个做生意的人来说，最可怕的就是这种缺少充分可预期性、政策急转和“一刀切”式执行带来的风险——你不是输给市场，也不是输给竞争对手，而是可能突然发现：游戏规则变了。 一个连明天的规则都难以预期的社会，谈什么真正的安全？ 所以我为什么说中国给我的不是安全，而更多是一种警察国家制造出来的安全感？ 因为摄像头可以让小偷有所忌惮，安检可以降低某些治安风险，警察可以让街面看起来井然有序。但这些东西解决不了一个更根本的问题：当伤害你的恰恰是权力、政策或者不受有效约束的规则时，谁来保护你？ 这才是我理解的安全。 我到了加拿大以后，反而觉得更安全，并不是因为加拿大没有犯罪。这里当然有犯罪，也有各种社会问题。但真正让我觉得安全的，不是街上多站几个警察，而是我遇上事以后，规则还在那里。 所以我越来越不相信“警察多＝安全”“摄像头多＝安全”“管得严＝安全”这套逻辑。 警察国家可以靠监控、安检和强力管控，给你制造一种表面上的安全感；真正能够给一个普通人提供安全的，是法治，是稳定的规则，是权力本身也必须讲理。 一个国家如果不讲理，警察再多、摄像头再多，也只能让你在没出事的时候觉得安全。 警察可以让你没事的时候觉得安全。 法治，才能让你出事的时候依然安全。 ——文｜罗夏日记

title: How Beijing could throttle Taiwan without firing a shot
summary: Honour guards during a flag-lowering ceremony at the Liberty Square in Taipei, Taiwan (Daniel Ceng/Anadolu via Getty Images) Administrative quarantine sounds anodyne – for Taiwan, it is war by other means. 2 October 2026 3 min read An armed
content:
Honour guards during a flag-lowering ceremony at the Liberty Square in Taipei, Taiwan (Daniel Ceng/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Administrative quarantine sounds anodyne – for Taiwan, it is war by other means.

2 October 2026 3 min read

An armed naval blockade is categorised as an act of war under the [United Nations Charter (Opens in new window)](https://www.un.org/depts/los/convention_agreements/texts/unclos/UNCLOS-TOC.htm), establishing a clear _casus belli_ to activate collective self-defence commitments under Article 51.

To neutralise this trigger under international law in the case of Taiwan, China is operationalising legal warfare. Instruments including the _Coast Guard Law_, the revised _Maritime Traffic Safety Law_, and the _2024 Coast Guard Order No. 3_ grant Chinese maritime enforcement agencies domestic authority to board, inspect, and detain foreign vessels in claimed jurisdictional waters.

Beijing is substituting the traditional concept of a sovereign naval blockade with a civilian-led administrative quarantine.

The China Coast Guard’s routine incursions across Taiwan’s restricted offshore waters represent the operational testing of an asymmetric siege mechanism, one designed to bypass Western defence doctrines entirely. Over the next 12 to 24 months, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) may use domestic statutory mandates, customs safety declarations, and paramilitary assets to achieve the economic isolation of Taiwan without crossing the formal threshold of kinetic warfare.

Rather than deploying the PLA-Navy to seal Taiwan’s coasts, Beijing mandates advance customs manifests for vessels bound for ports such as Kaohsiung, which handles approximately 57% of Taiwan’s maritime trade value. Non-compliant commercial traffic faces interception under the administrative pretext of anti-smuggling, biosecurity, or maritime safety checks.

A law-enforcement quarantine of this type shifts the legal and operational burden of initiating military conflict onto Taipei and its partners, exploiting commercial risk structures to strangle the island’s economy from within.

> The operational effectiveness of a quarantine does not rely on sinking merchant vessels; it exploits the mechanics of global maritime finance.

Research from [CSIS (Opens in new window)](https://features.csis.org/chinapower/china-taiwan-series/) and the [Naval War College China Maritime Studies Institute (Opens in new window)](https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cmsi-maritime-reports/) demonstrates how the “Kinmen Model” – normalising Coast Guard and Maritime Safety Administration patrols within Taiwan’s contiguous waters – provides the template for wider commercial interdiction.

The operational effectiveness of a quarantine does not rely on sinking merchant vessels; it exploits the mechanics of global maritime finance. When civilian enforcement officers commence boarding operations in the Taiwan Strait, China may [reclassify these waters (Opens in new window)](https://cimsec.org/the-insurance-trigger-sovereign-guarantees-and-commercial-lawfare-as-deterrence-against-a-chinese-quarantine-of-taiwan/) as an enhanced risk area. This would lead insurers to levy prohibitive additional war risk premiums, making commercial transits economically unviable. Under standard maritime charter contracts, shipmasters _likely_ invoke safe-port clauses and voluntarily divert inbound cargo.

This dynamic creates an acute vulnerability for Taiwan’s energy security. Taiwan depends entirely on daily deliveries of LNG, maintaining operational[storage reserves of only 14 days (Opens in new window)](https://english.cw.com.tw/article/article.action?id=4993). Diverting just a handful of tankers may force immediate power rationing across civilian and semiconductor manufacturing sectors.

This scenario also presents Taipei with an operational dilemma. Interposing civilian Coast Guard Administration cutters concedes Beijing’s premise that the dispute is an internal administrative matter. Conversely, deploying Republic of China Navy warships to escort commercial tankers allows Beijing to claim Taiwan has militarised a peacetime customs operation, providing the pretext for PLA-Navy strike groups to intervene.

A China Coast Guard vessel patrols on 21 September 2026 near Qingdao, China (VCG via Getty Images)

Deterring an administrative quarantine requires Western defence doctrine to move beyond conventional naval defence planning through three multilateral measures.

First, the United States, Japan, and regional allies should construct a multinational marine reinsurance backstop. By underwriting commercial hull and cargo risk when private underwriters withdraw, partner nations can neutralise Beijing’s ability to use market insurance triggers as an economic weapon.

**Second, p**artner nations should deploy their own Coast Guard assets to conduct joint presence operations in the Taiwan Strait, challenging Beijing’s jurisdictional claims symmetrically without triggering military escalation.

Third, Taiwan may draw on its standing as an autonomous Separate Customs Territory within the [World Trade Organisation (Opens in new window)](https://www.wto.org/english/thewto_e/countries_e/chinese_taipei_e.htm) to challenge PRC interdictions under [General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade Articles X and XI (Opens in new window)](https://www.wto.org/english/docs_e/legal_e/gatt47_e.htm), backed by pre-packaged allied sanctions targeting China Coast Guard operational commands.

A coercive quarantine orchestrated by maritime law enforcement represents a form of grey-zone coercion designed to circumvent traditional allied defence treaties. By framing territorial coercion as domestic customs administration, Beijing exploits the sensitivities of global shipping and the fragility of Taiwan’s energy reserves. Deterrence in the Taiwan Strait can no longer focus solely on repelling an amphibious assault. Without integrated commercial insurance guarantees, multilateral law enforcement coordination, and assertive legal counter-measures, the international community risks allowing Beijing to achieve through administrative coercion what it cannot accomplish without war.

About the author

Christopher Eylward is an operations supervisor within the Royal Australian Navy, with over 15 years of leadership experience in maritime operations, tactical data networks, and operational intelligence.

content: 一家在英国资助研究的组织已被英国情报局 MI5 宣布正在支持北京的情报机构 英国情报局 MI5 警告称，超过 100 名与英国机构有关的学者无意中通过一家为其情报和安全服务机构工作的前哨公司，协助了中国针对英国的间谍活动。 在这次非常规的公开警报中，英国内部安全服务机构警告大学和学者称，继续与中国通用技术研究院（CGTRI）保持联系，最终可能导致因协助外国国家而受到刑事指控。 安全大臣 Dan Jarvis 表示，MI5 的警告暴露了中国情报机构试图利用英国学术研究来破坏英国国家安全的企图。 他表示，他已向所有大学校长写信，要求终止与该组织的合作关系。 今年 6 月，MI5 及其在美国、加拿大、澳大利亚和新西兰的密切合作伙伴发布联合警告，称中国军事情报机构正在针对专业社交网站和在线招聘平台。 这次针对英国的新警报更进一步，揭示了据称在英国学术机构内部日益增长的威胁。 MI5 表示，CGTRI，有时被译为“中国通用技术学院”（CAGT），与中国国家安全部（MSS）有着“非常紧密的联系”。 “MI5 已确定，CGTRI 的主要目的是资助直接提升 MSS 间谍技术能力的学术研究，”它表示。 “超过 100 名与英国有关的学者参与了 MSS 通过 CGTRI 资助的项目，”并指出，在某些情况下，研究人员可能不知道前哨公司在其项目中的作用。 英国学者参与了 CGTRI 资助的项目，主题包括人工智能、网络安全、秘密通信系统和隐写术，即隐藏秘密消息或文件在普通消息或物体中。 “这项活动支持国家安全部间谍活动，对英国国家安全构成威胁，”MI5 表示。 安全警报称，许多学术机构和个人将因与 CGTRI 的“善意”联系而参与，因为与中国的国家安全之间的联系已被“模糊化”。 它继续道：”英国学术机构强烈建议立即审查任何正在进行或计划中的与 CGTRI 的合作。这是为了确保国家安全部不会从英国大学或研究机构中获得任何进一步的好处。” 公开警报提出了这样一种可能性，即如果不立即采取行动，英国学者最终可能会触犯法律。 它强调，《国家安全法》是 2023 年通过的一项关键立法，旨在打击国家间谍活动，其中规定了一项新的罪行，即协助外国情报机构，前提是个人应当合理知道自己在做什么。 Jarvis 表示：””此警报暴露了中国情报机构试图秘密利用我们学者的专业知识和研究，破坏我们的国家安全以及我们盟友的安全的企图。”

title: 澳洲取消刷卡附加费，中国买家三年投入 50 亿，成最大海外购房群体
summary: 从10月1日起，澳洲消费者使用信用卡和借记卡付款时，将迎来一项重要变化：商家不得再向消费者收取刷卡附加费（card surcharge）。 这意味着，以后在餐厅、商店、服务机构等场所使用银行卡付款，消费者将不再需要额外承担这笔刷卡费用。 随着新规正式实施，澳洲日常支付方式也可能出现一些新的变化，现金、PayID以及其他支付方式的使用情况都受到关注。 澳洲联储（RBA）数据显示，2025年澳洲约有15%的支付仍通过现金完成，而在通常的一周里，大约一半澳洲居民使用过现金。 值得注
content: 从10月1日起，澳洲消费者使用信用卡和借记卡付款时，将迎来一项重要变化：商家不得再向消费者收取刷卡附加费（card surcharge）。 这意味着，以后在餐厅、商店、服务机构等场所使用银行卡付款，消费者将不再需要额外承担这笔刷卡费用。 随着新规正式实施，澳洲日常支付方式也可能出现一些新的变化，现金、PayID以及其他支付方式的使用情况都受到关注。 澳洲联储（RBA）数据显示，2025年澳洲约有15%的支付仍通过现金完成，而在通常的一周里，大约一半澳洲居民使用过现金。 值得注意的是，近年来现金使用情况也出现了一些变化。2022年约47%的澳洲人会携带现金，到2025年这一比例已经升至约50%。 随着刷卡附加费退出日常消费，一些商家可能会通过提供现金折扣、PayID优惠等方式，引导消费者选择不同的付款渠道。 澳洲联储此前也表示，商家可以通过提供折扣来鼓励消费者使用特定支付方式，而不是通过附加费增加消费者的付款成本。 刷卡附加费取消后，商家仍然需要承担支付处理成本，因此不同企业可能会根据自身经营情况调整支付安排。 一些商家可能将相关成本纳入整体定价体系，也有企业可能通过优化支付方式来降低交易成本。 随着刷卡附加费取消，现金支付可能进一步获得关注。 对于部分小型商户来说，如果现金支付能够降低支付处理成本，也可能通过“现金优惠”等方式吸引消费者。 未来在咖啡店、餐馆、社区商铺等场景中，消费者可能会看到更多不同的支付选择。 除了商家端，银行和支付行业同样会受到这项变化影响。 澳洲联储计划进一步限制交换费（interchange fee）。这类费用通常由商家的银行支付给消费者发卡机构，是银行卡支付体系中的一项重要成本。 随着支付规则调整，整个银行卡支付体系也将发生变化。 澳洲最大海外购房群体 最新数据显示，中国大陆买家仍是澳洲房地产市场最主要的海外买家群体之一。2026年上半年，中国大陆投资者对澳洲住宅房产的咨询量位居全球第二，仅次于泰国。 按照目前的咨询趋势，澳洲有望连续第三年成为中国大陆买家在亚洲以外市场中咨询量最高的目的地之一。 澳洲财政部及外国投资审查委员会（FIRB）数据显示，2025/26财年前6个月，获批购买澳洲房产的外国居民中，约27%涉及中国大陆买家，中国台湾和越南买家分别占12%和10%。 过去三年，中国大陆投资者在澳洲住宅市场的获批购房金额预计接近50亿澳元。 数据显示，2023/24财年，中国大陆投资者购房金额约26亿澳元；2024/25财年约14亿澳元。2025/26财年的全年数据尚未公布，如果下半年维持上半年水平，全年金额预计约10亿澳元。 业内人士表示，官方统计下降，与部分中国买家先获得澳洲永久居留身份、再以本地买家身份购房有关，因此并不能完全反映实际市场需求。 从购房目的地来看，中国大陆买家的关注重点正在发生变化。 Juwai IQI数据显示，过去几年墨尔本一直是中国买家咨询量最高的澳洲城市，但今年悉尼的咨询量首次超过墨尔本，成为最受关注的澳洲购房目的地。 目前悉尼和墨尔本两地合计占中国大陆买家需求的近62%。 与此同时，阿德莱德和黄金海岸的关注度也明显上升。其中，阿德莱德在中国大陆买家咨询中的占比已从一年前的2%升至8%，黄金海岸的占比则约为此前的5倍。 Juwai IQI联合创始人Daniel Ho表示，中国大陆买家的兴趣正在从传统热门城市进一步扩展至澳洲更多地区。 在购房资金方面，Daniel Ho表示，中国大陆买家的购房行为与依赖贷款的本地买家有所不同。 据其介绍，超过65%的中国大陆买家采用现金购房，因此澳洲利率变化对这一群体的直接影响相对有限。 他认为，对于不少中国家庭而言，购房更多与移居、子女教育、家庭规划等人生阶段有关，而不完全取决于短期市场走势。

title: 专家解析美中峰会：要面子更要里子
