content:
特朗普总统史无前例亲自到安德鲁斯联合基地欢迎到访的中国国家主席习近平，并在白宫举行隆重的欢迎仪式与国宴，传统基金会国安与印太事务研究员安德鲁·哈丁(Andrew Harding)告诉美国之音，特朗普总统台面上给足习近平面子，私底下卯足全劲在实质议题上过招，并确保中方履行承诺。

以下是专访摘要：

### **特朗普总统给足习近平面子 在实质议题上较劲？**

哈丁说：显然，他希望受到尊重，这当然非常重要。

即使回顾十年前，当时美国和中国无疑已经是竞争对手。但如今，中国在很多不同领域都已经大幅缩小了与美国之间的差距。因此，对习近平来说，此次访美能够受到非常高规格的礼遇非常重要。

这显示出两国之间存在相互平等、甚至更高程度的尊重。

但如果我们具体来看这次峰会可能达成的成果，我认为习近平可能会特别关注台湾问题。这一直是中国共产党高度重视的议题，也是一个核心问题。

今年5月，台湾问题被定义为最敏感的问题。如果美国在处理台湾问题时没有采取中国所期望的方式，中方已经表示，军事行动甚至战争都有可能发生。这是一条非常明确的红线。

因此，如果习近平希望看到美国在台湾问题上采取更加符合中方立场的政策，我不会感到意外。比如在战略清晰度方面，或者希望美国就台湾当前执政当局提出一些问题。

但我相信，特朗普总统以及身边的顾问不会陷入这样的局面。所以，我认为这可能是习近平希望推动的方向之一，但我还是会再次关注峰会的实质内容，确保美国不会在这些问题上作出这样的改变。

### **衡量美中峰会成功的关键为何？**

哈丁说：我认为，这次峰会是否成功，可以从两个关键方面来衡量。

第一，中国是否会落实今年5月北京峰会期间达成的承诺，以及更早时候，比如釜山峰会或之前达成的协议。我们知道，美中之间一直存在一些争议，尤其是中方签署协议之后是否能够切实履行承诺。

随着越来越多的信息在峰会前公布，比如稀土、波音飞机以及农产品采购等，这些都是双方此前已经达成共识的领域。但现在仍然存在一个问题，那就是中国是否会真正落实这些承诺。所以，我希望看到中方尽可能按照此前达成的协议切实履行。

如果没有做到，那么双方将采取什么措施，让相关承诺重新回到正轨。

第二个衡量峰会成功与否的标准，是美国能否在达成任何协议的同时，继续保持自身的战略筹码和优势。

换句话说，我们可能会看到双方就人工智能、贸易关税等问题达成一些协议或展开讨论。

但归根结底，美国不应该以出口管制等战略工具作为交换条件，也不应该让中国对美台关系产生任何形式的左右或影响。

这些只是两个例子。无论双方最终达成什么协议，我们都需要确保美国能够继续掌握这些领域的主动权。

### 美中峰会如何管控危机、防止误判？

哈丁表示：双方可能会建立一种机制，在出现国家安全问题，或者某个问题开始出现苗头时，能够发挥类似危机管控机制的作用。

也就是说，一旦出现问题，两国元首或双方领导人之间有一种沟通渠道，可以及时交换信息，确保彼此了解对方正在努力解决问题，更重要的是避免发生误判。

所以归根结底，在人工智能问题上，双方都希望建立一种能够防止局势升级的机制，也希望形成某种共识，因为建立这样的沟通和理解符合双方的共同利益。

更广泛来看，我认为最重要的是寻找双方能够达成共识的领域。我们可能会看到一些关税下调的协议，但应该不会涉及战略性商品，而可能集中在一些非战略性商品上，规模可能达到数十亿美元。

除此之外，我们不应该期待这里会有太多重大的宣布，因为两国领导人都希望维持双边关系的基本稳定，但与此同时，双方仍然是竞争对手。

美国和中国仍在持续竞争。因此，双方真正能够回旋和谈判的空间是有限的。我认为，我们可能会看到人工智能、贸易或者关税方面取得一些进展，但不太可能出现足以重新定义美中关系的重大突破。

### 美国如何确保盟友利益不受影响？

哈丁说：对盟友的安抚是非常重要的，全世界都在关注这次峰会，美国和中国是世界上最具影响力的两个国家，因此，各国都关心峰会将取得什么结果，也都希望了解美中关系未来将如何发展。我很高兴看到，总统将与日本首相高市早苗的会晤放在重要位置。

正如您提到的，他在离开北京、返美途中还专门打电话给她。这再次表明，总统非常重视美国与日本之间的关系以及美日同盟。

至于这对台湾意味着什么，我认为，这也应该表明，美国非常清楚，台湾在这次峰会中有许多重要利益受到影响。

特朗普政府团队与台湾一直保持着良好的关系。当然，军售问题也是一个重要议题。我认为，我们本周可能不会立即得到答案，这是有意为之，因为总统不希望这个问题影响峰会。但我仍然有信心，总统以及政府其他官员都认识到，美台关系对于美国的国家安全利益和经济利益具有极其重要的意义。

所以，我理解各方对这次峰会可能会有一些担忧。但我认为，总统团队正在向世界各地的盟友和伙伴传递一个信息：美国实力依然强大，总统手中拥有筹码。他会确保盟友和伙伴及时了解情况，让他们知道应该期待什么，也不会作出损害盟友利益的决定，更不会采取任何可能让中国更加有恃无恐、危及自由世界的行动。

title: US Allies Will Be Watching Xi Jinping’s Washington Visit Closely
summary: US Allies Will Be Watching Xi Jinping’s Washington Visit Closely bbert@hudson.org Mon, 09/21/2026 - 10:28 SVG Commentary Sep 18, 2026 National Interest US Allies Will Be Watching Xi Jinping’s Washington Visit Closely The US-China relationsh
content: US Allies Will Be Watching Xi Jinping’s Washington Visit Closely bbert@hudson.org Mon, 09/21/2026 - 10:28 SVG Commentary Sep 18, 2026 National Interest US Allies Will Be Watching Xi Jinping’s Washington Visit Closely The US-China relationship is no longer purely bilateral, and Washington should not signal that it is ignoring its allies’ concerns.   Liselotte Odgaard Senior Fellow (Nonresident) Liselotte Odgaard Commentary Caption United States President Donald Trump meets with China's President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of their visit to Zhongnanhai Garden in Beijing on May 15, 2026. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print As Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares to visit Washington next week, much of the commentary has focused on a familiar set of questions. Will he and US President Donald Trump stabilize relations? Can they reduce tensions over Taiwan ? Will trade disputes ease? Will military-to-military contacts improve? These questions matter. But they miss the most important strategic point. The real audience for a summit between President Xi and President Trump is not in Beijing or Washington. It is in Tokyo, Manila, Canberra, Seoul, and, increasingly, NATO capitals. The meeting’s strategic significance will be determined less by what it means for the bilateral US-China relationship than by what it signals to America’s allies.  This reflects a fundamental shift in the international security environment. For most of the post-Cold War period, US-China relations could largely be understood through a bilateral lens. Today, they cannot. Coalitions, rather than individual states, are increasingly shaping the balance of power in the Indo-Pacific .  The evidence is visible across the region. Japan is undertaking the most significant military capability buildup in decades. The Philippines has expanded military access for US forces under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement . South Korea and Japan have deepened security cooperation despite longstanding political tensions. AUKUS has deepened defense cooperation between Australia , the United Kingdom and the United States . Meanwhile, European allies have become more active in the Indo-Pacific through naval deployments, defense industrial cooperation and strategic coordination.  From Beijing’s perspective, these developments are more consequential than any individual summit. China ’s challenge is no longer the United States alone but an increasingly integrated network of allies and partners. The United States and Japan are improving command integration and operational planning. Washington, Tokyo, and Manila have expanded trilateral cooperation . Across the region, allies are investing in air and missile defense, maritime surveillance, and logistics resilience and autonomous systems. Together, these efforts are creating a coalition-based deterrence architecture. This reality should shape how we measure success if Xi visits Washington. A successful summit is not one that generates the warmest headlines or the most optimistic-sounding communiqué. Instead, we should judge its value by three questions.  First , will the summit reduce the risk of miscalculation without weakening deterrence? The United States and China have good reasons to maintain communication channels. Strategic competition will endure regardless of diplomatic atmospherics, and the danger of accidents or unintended escalation is real. Communication can reduce those risks. But stability rests on credible deterrence. Diplomacy works best when both sides understand the costs of coercion and military adventurism. Second , does the summit reassure allies rather than marginalize them? This question matters because US allies have long worried about major-power accommodation reached at their expense. Allied capitals watch every high-level engagement between Washington and Beijing closely. Allied policymakers will pay less attention to ceremonial symbolism than to whether the meeting reinforces confidence that their interests remain central to US strategy. This concern is not hypothetical. The credibility of American leadership depends not only on military capabilities but also on allied confidence that Washington will consult with them, take their interests seriously, and resist any temptation to pursue short-term stabilization with China at the expense of long-term coalition cohesion. In today’s Indo-Pacific, alliance reassurance is itself a strategic asset. Third , does the summit preserve momentum in allied defense cooperation? This may ultimately be the most important question. The most significant strategic development in the Indo-Pacific is not a single weapons platform, military exercise, or diplomatic initiative. It is the growing integration of allied capabilities across multiple domains. This includes intelligence sharing, logistics arrangements, and defense industrial cooperation. Through intelligence sharing, logistics cooperation, defense industrial ties, maritime domain awareness, and emerging technologies, allies are building practical links that are becoming deeper and more institutionalized.  Importantly, many of the initiatives are developing momentum of their own. They increasingly transcend individual governments and administrations. They are becoming embedded in military planning processes, bureaucratic structures and industrial partnerships. From Beijing’s perspective, this trend presents a difficult challenge. China can negotiate with one American administration. It is far more difficult to negotiate away a dense network of security relationships among states that increasingly perceive similar security risks and share common interests in maintaining regional stability.  That is why the success of a Xi summit should not be measured solely by whether US-China relations improve in the short term. The more consequential question is whether the meeting strengthens confidence among the countries whose cooperation will shape the future balance of power. A visit by Xi Jinping could help establish guardrails for competition and reduce the danger of crisis escalation. Those are worthwhile objectives. But policymakers should resist the temptation to treat dialogue itself as a strategic outcome. The long-term stability of the Indo-Pacific will depend less on summit diplomacy than on whether allies continue to strengthen the collective capabilities needed to deter conflict. In an era of strategic competition, alliance confidence is not a peripheral concern. It is the foundation of deterrence. Read in The National Interest. Enjoyed this analysis? title: Hong Kong authorities decline to comment on report that US fighter jet parts diverted to city
summary: Hong Kong authorities have declined to comment on a report that parts for F-35 fighter jets, a classified US aircraft targeted by Chinese intelligence, were diverted to the city. F-35B Lightning II aircraft at Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska
content: Hong Kong authorities have declined to comment on a report that parts for F-35 fighter jets, a classified US aircraft targeted by Chinese intelligence, were diverted to the city. F-35B Lightning II aircraft at Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska. Photo: F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office﻿, via Facebook. Media outlet Politico reported last week that a shipment of US-bound F-35 parts being flown from Australia this summer ended up in Hong Kong, citing anonymous sources. The alleged incident prompted a US government investigation amid concerns that China could gain access to the sensitive weapon system, the US news site reported. A spokesperson for the Hong Kong government said it “will not comment on individual incidents.” According to Politico, the parts – which included one of the jet’s canopies – were being transported by an intermediary on behalf of F-35 manufacturer Lockheed Martin . Sources told Politico that the canopies contain technology that only the US and its allies have. The US Congress. File photo: Wikimedia Commons. Lawmakers on the US House committee that oversees armed services are looking into the incident, House Armed Services Committee spokesperson Heather Vaughan told media outlets. “The committee is aware of this issue and we’ve received multiple briefings on it,” Vaughan said. The F-35 project is governed by the US government’s F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office. The office counts US allies, including the UK, Australia and Canada, among its partners purchasing the aircraft. A Beijing foreign ministry spokesperson said in 2022 that China had “no interest in the [US’s] aircraft.”

title: America and China are fighting for the future of AI — chips are the battlefield
summary: When President Donald Trump sits down with [Chinese President Xi Jinping](https://foxnews.com/category/person/xi-jinping) in Washington this week, the agenda will be crowded. Trade. Tariffs. Rare earth minerals. National security. Supply ch
content:
When President Donald Trump sits down with [Chinese President Xi Jinping](https://foxnews.com/category/person/xi-jinping) in Washington this week, the agenda will be crowded.

Trade. Tariffs. Rare earth minerals. National security. Supply chains.

But looming over all of it is a technological competition that could shape the balance of economic and military power for decades: [artificial intelligence](https://foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence). And increasingly, the battle isn’t simply about who builds the best AI model.

[**TRUMP-XI’S CHINA SUMMIT IS A DEFINING TEST FOR AMERICA IN THE NEW COLD WAR**](https://foxnews.com/opinion/trump-xis-china-summit-defining-test-america-new-cold-war)

It is about who controls the chips, computing infrastructure and technology ecosystem underneath it.

America remains the global leader in advanced AI technology and semiconductor design. But China is pushing aggressively to reduce its dependence on American technology, and Huawei has emerged as one of the most important companies in that effort. That should have Washington’s full attention.

For years, the United States has used export controls to restrict China’s access to advanced semiconductors and semiconductor-manufacturing technology, particularly technologies with potential military applications.

Those restrictions had a clear national-security objective: prevent America’s most sophisticated technology from strengthening a strategic competitor’s military capabilities. But there has also been an unintended consequence worth confronting. China accelerated its effort to build an AI ecosystem that doesn’t need America.

[**AI ‘DOOMERS’ RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK**](https://foxnews.com/politics/ai-doomers-risk-kneecapping-us-vs-china-ex-pentagon-vet-says-both-extremes-miss-mark)

Huawei expanded its Ascend AI-chip roadmap. Chinese developers adapted software and models to domestic hardware. Chinese companies poured resources into computing systems capable of compensating for some of the performance limitations of individual Chinese chips. And Huawei isn’t standing still.

The company recently said demand for its AI computing equipment in China is exceeding supply. It is accelerating future generations of its Ascend processors and developing enormous computing systems capable of connecting vast numbers of chips.

That means the strategic question facing Washington has changed.

[**AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL**](https://foxnews.com/opinion/america-runs-data-dont-build-infrastructure-china-will)

The question isn’t simply: How do we keep sensitive American technology away from China? It is also: How do we make sure the rest of the world continues choosing American technology instead of China’s? Those are related questions, but they aren’t identical.

If American technology becomes inaccessible across too much of the global market, China has an enormous incentive to develop substitutes. Huawei has an enormous incentive to sell them. And governments and companies around the world have an enormous incentive to build around whatever technology they can reliably obtain.

[**THE AI REVOLUTION COULD BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY DISASTER IF WE AREN’T CAREFUL**](https://foxnews.com/opinion/ai-revolution-could-become-national-security-disaster-if-we-arent-careful)

Once developers write software for an ecosystem, companies construct computing infrastructure around it and countries invest billions deploying it, switching becomes much harder. That’s why this isn’t merely a chip-sales competition. It is an ecosystem competition.

America wants a world running on American chips, American software, American standards and American innovation. China wants to build an alternative. It wants a world in which Huawei and other Chinese companies provide a technology stack that Beijing controls and America cannot easily influence.

[President Trump](https://foxnews.com/category/person/donald-trump) has taken a different approach from the Biden administration. His administration rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule while maintaining controls targeting technologies with serious national-security implications.

The administration has also allowed certain advanced chips to be considered for sale to approved Chinese customers under licensing requirements and security conditions. The theory is straightforward: protect the technologies most critical to national security without unnecessarily surrendering commercial markets to Chinese competitors. That distinction matters.

[**CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE**](https://foxnews.com/opinion/china-building-ai-war-machine-washington-must-wake-late)

Nobody serious is arguing that America should simply hand China unrestricted access to technology that could materially enhance advanced weapons, military AI, surveillance or other sensitive capabilities.

National security comes first. But there is a difference between protecting America’s crown-jewel technology and adopting restrictions so sweeping that they accelerate China’s determination to replace American technology throughout the commercial market. Because Huawei’s goal isn’t merely to survive American restrictions.

Huawei wants to compete. It wants Chinese chips powering Chinese AI. It wants Chinese computing infrastructure supporting Chinese models. And ultimately, Chinese technology companies want customers outside China using their systems.

That’s why the next phase of this competition will be fought over which chips countries buy, which computing systems they install, which software developers learn and which technology stack becomes the default infrastructure for the AI economy.

America has enormous advantages. We have extraordinary semiconductor designers, the world’s leading AI companies, deep capital markets, world-class universities, entrepreneurs and an innovation culture China has spent decades trying to replicate.

But technological leadership isn’t permanent. It has to be defended. And sometimes the greatest threat to American leadership isn’t that China suddenly invents something better. It’s that America creates policies that make its own technology harder for the world to use while Beijing aggressively offers an alternative.

There are already calls for the United States to [slow AI development](https://foxnews.com/opinion/sen-bernie-sanders-yes-we-must-hit-pause-button-ai-before-it-is-too-late) or impose broader restrictions in the name of safety and security. Those arguments deserve serious debate.

AI presents real risks. Advanced semiconductor technology has genuine military applications. Export controls can be an important national-security tool. But every restriction also has consequences.

The question should be whether a restriction actually improves American security without unnecessarily strengthening China’s competing technology ecosystem. Because China isn’t pausing. Huawei isn’t pausing. And global demand for AI computing certainly isn’t pausing.

Somebody will provide the chips. Somebody will provide the computing infrastructure. Somebody will provide the software. Somebody will establish the standards.

The United States has a direct strategic interest in American companies remaining central to that ecosystem.

The previous generation of American leaders watched too much manufacturing capacity and too many strategically important supply chains migrate overseas. We should not repeat that mistake with the infrastructure of artificial intelligence.

Semiconductors are no longer merely components inside computers. Compute is strategic power.

The nations and companies controlling advanced computing will possess enormous advantages in scientific discovery, medicine, manufacturing, intelligence, cybersecurity and military technology. That is why the [Trump-Xi meeting](https://foxnews.com/politics/china-rolls-out-red-carpet-trump-xi-meeting-tests-trade-taiwan-tensions) matters far beyond whatever trade agreement or diplomatic communiqué emerges from Washington.

The two presidents represent countries competing over something much larger: Who builds the technological infrastructure of the 21st century?

The United States should protect its most sensitive technology, its intellectual property and technologies with significant military applications. At the same time, American companies will continue competing for commercial markets around the world.

Design the chips here. Build the semiconductor infrastructure here. Develop the software here. Protect the technology that truly must be protected. And keep American technology innovative and competitive enough that countries around the world continue choosing the American ecosystem instead of Huawei’s.

The [AI Cold War](https://foxnews.com/opinion/chill-coming-trumps-summit-xi-proof-new-cold-war-china) is already underway. And the chips are the battlefield.

title: 美国情报官员：中国试图通过沙特获取F-35战斗机技术
summary: 美国官员表示，情报官员在内部报告中就中国可能针对向沙特阿拉伯出售数十架先进F-35战斗机一事进行间谍活动表达了担忧。这笔 待完成的军售 价值240亿美元。 这些美国官员说，情报分析人士指出，中国可能通过在沙特阿拉伯的间谍活动，或通过其与沙特的军事和安全伙伴关系获取F-35战机技术。 一名官员说，五角大楼国防情报局数月前发布了一份详细报告，讨论了中国军方进入沙特基地以及沙特在电信基础设施中使用中国技术的问题。这名官员说，报告还质疑美沙两国能否维持F-35技术所在设施的安全。 这
content: 美国官员表示，情报官员在内部报告中就中国可能针对向沙特阿拉伯出售数十架先进F-35战斗机一事进行间谍活动表达了担忧。这笔 待完成的军售 价值240亿美元。 这些美国官员说，情报分析人士指出，中国可能通过在沙特阿拉伯的间谍活动，或通过其与沙特的军事和安全伙伴关系获取F-35战机技术。 一名官员说，五角大楼国防情报局数月前发布了一份详细报告，讨论了中国军方进入沙特基地以及沙特在电信基础设施中使用中国技术的问题。这名官员说，报告还质疑美沙两国能否维持F-35技术所在设施的安全。 这份报告以及来自其他情报机构的评估已在几个政府机构和国会办公室之间传阅。2025年秋，在政府讨论这笔军售可能性时，国防情报局曾就类似风险发布过一份更笼统的报告，《纽约时报》当时对此进行了 报道 。 随后，特朗普总统在于11月在白宫接待沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼的前一天宣布了这笔军售。穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼是沙特事实上的领导人。 这笔军售现在已进入更深入阶段，而国防情报局较新的报告提出了更为强烈的担忧，包括技术方面的担忧。国务院已于6月将包括48架战机和一台备用发动机的拟议销售方案送交两个国会委员会，以寻求非正式批准。一些议员和国会工作人员一直就情报机构提出的担忧向政府施压。 由于间谍和军事事务的敏感性，这些美国官员在谈及情报官员的担忧时要求匿名。 美国国务院、五角大楼和沙特驻华盛顿大使馆拒绝置评。白宫和中国大使馆没有回应置评请求。 在特朗普第一个任期内，美国情报机构也曾在内部提出类似担忧。当时，特朗普于2020年同意向阿拉伯联合酋长国出售F-35战机，作为阿联酋与以色列 关系正常化 协议的一部分。 F-35战机由洛克希德·马丁公司生产，从生产到交付需要数年时间。因此，拜登政府在战机生产和交付之前很久就决定对这笔军售进行审查。当时，由于阿联酋正在 加强与中国在军事、情报和技术领域的联系 ，美国情报机构也提出了同样的问题。随后，美国官员 终止了这一军售进程 。 穆罕默德王储一直在努力提升沙特的军事实力。他曾在也门对胡塞武装发动一场灾难性的七年战争，沙特领导的部队在那场战争中使用美国炸弹 杀害平民 。在当前 美国和以色列对伊朗发动的战争 中，沙特军队也 未能阻止 来自伊朗的袭击，而沙特与伊朗支持的胡塞武装已 重新开始交战 。 穆罕默德王储长期以来一直寻求从美国购买F-35战斗机，特朗普最终于去年11月同意了这一要求。沙特和美国已经进行了数十年的军事合作，而沙特也是美国武器和防务装备的最大买家。但沙特同时也从中国购买弹道导弹，中国军方还在帮助沙特学习制造弹道导弹、建立生产设施以及改进导弹作战能力。 民主党议员曾于2022年6月 致信 拜登总统，阐述他们对这一项目的担忧。 一名美国官员说，五角大楼近期的情报报告指出，能进入存放F-35技术的设施的只有只有沙特和美国的军官及承包商。五角大楼官员尤其担心如何保护F-35先进的雷达和监视技术。 情报分析人士在报告中质疑沙特是否会进一步同意限制与中国军事和情报人员及相关实体的接触。 报告还质疑沙特官员是否会同意将华为和中兴这两家知名中国科技公司的设备从电信和路由器基础设施以及国防设施中移除。 一些以色列官员也对这笔军售表示担忧，就像特朗普当初提议向阿联酋出售F-35时一样。以色列是中东唯一拥有F-35战斗机的国家，近年来曾使用这些战机对伊朗发动空袭。自1973年阿以战争以来，美国政策制定者一直试图确保以色列在该地区保持国会所要求的“定性军事优势”。 历届美国政府都会通过一个高度机密、持续数月的审查程序，评估拟议中的中东地区武器销售是否符合这一要求。然而，特朗普第二届政府仍在推动向以色列 大规模军售 ，尽管美国政治光谱的各派都有人呼吁停止或大幅减少军事支持。 在过去的一些情况下，国务卿鲁比奥以地区紧急状态为由，绕过国会批准程序，加快向以色列运送武器。如果国会领导人不同意F-35战机销售，他可能会采取同样做法。 特朗普还同意 帮助沙特建立民用核项目 。该项目本身也引发了安全担忧，因为穆罕默德王储曾誓言，如果伊朗建造核武器，沙特也会这样做。

title: 八九学生集体声明：支联会不在了，我们还在
summary: 王丹     X  @wangdan1989   · Sep 6, 2026 9月11日，香港高等法院依据港版国安法，判处支联会前领导人李卓人、何俊仁、邹幸彤 “煽动颠覆国家” 罪名成立，三人分别被判刑5至7年。 作为1989年学生运动的亲历者，我们强烈谴责这一判决，这是中共当局掩盖六四屠杀罪行，否定历史的又一例证。 支联会于1989年学运期间成立，为支援北京学生做出了巨大贡献。六四屠杀之后，1990年至2019年，支联会连续30年坚持
content: 王丹     X  @wangdan1989   · Sep 6, 2026 9月11日，香港高等法院依据港版国安法，判处支联会前领导人李卓人、何俊仁、邹幸彤 “煽动颠覆国家” 罪名成立，三人分别被判刑5至7年。 作为1989年学生运动的亲历者，我们强烈谴责这一判决，这是中共当局掩盖六四屠杀罪行，否定历史的又一例证。 支联会于1989年学运期间成立，为支援北京学生做出了巨大贡献。六四屠杀之后，1990年至2019年，支联会连续30年坚持举办维园烛光集会，守护六四记忆，传承历史真相。2021年，港区国安法颁布之后，支联会在压力下被迫解散。 每年六月四日，维园数十万人的烛光，是对屠杀死难者最好的缅怀，八九学生永远感谢支联会为纪念六四付出的努力。 从1989年到今天，我们始终面对着一场记忆与遗忘的搏斗。六四已经过去三十七年了，但死难者的冤屈依然没有得到昭雪，正义依然没有得到伸张。只要真相一天没有大白于天下，我们就会坚持下去，守护这份历史记忆。支联会不在了，我们还在。 最后，我们呼吁中共香港当局：立刻无条件释放李卓人、邹幸彤、何俊仁。就像邹幸彤大律师法庭所言，追求民主无罪，他们所做的一切，一天牢也不应该坐！ 八九学生:  王丹 吾尔开希 郑旭光 张伯笠 王超华 童屹 方政 刘俊 李恒青 赵常青 李兰菊 陈破空 金岩 赵昕 唐恺 邬萍晖 余厚强 2026.9.15 几点说明: 1. 昨天与一位原八九同学交换意见, 我们都认为, 香港支联会三君子案, 最应该站出来声援的, 就是当年的八九学生. 因为三君子守护的, 正是我们自己亲身经历的历史. 某种程度上说, 他们的义举是八九精神的延续, 而几十年来支联会举办的维园晚会, 更是我们能够坚持下来的精神支柱之一. 今天他们为了声援我们而付出代价, 我们是最不能保持沉默的一群人. 2. 起草了声明稿之后, 我辗转难眠, 从凌晨2点开始, 一一跟一些联络较多的原八九同学联系, 征集联署. 到早晨9点, 就已经拿到十六位同学的签名, 没有人有半点犹豫, 可见大家的内心都有同样的愿望, 愿望也同样的迫切. 3. 由于时效关系, 也由于个人联络范围有限, 第一批联署名单如上. 在此, 我们也呼吁更多的当年参加过八九民运的同学们, 请你们继续联署! 希望有更多的人站出来, 向那些为了守护我们经历过的那段历史的记忆, 而付出巨大代价的香港人, 表达我们的敬意; 让他们知道, 我们永远与他们站在一起!

content: 作者臉書 2026-9-30 因為花千樹出版社宣佈結業，有人在報章撰文緬懷舒巷城和張五常，讓我回想起一些舊事，也值得一記。 在香港出版界，花千樹是一家特別的出版社，它是張五常獨資，基本上不以盈利為目的，主要出版張五常與舒巷城的作品，張五常系列是他在信報專欄的文章結集，舒巷城則是他的舊作整理出版。有一次我向張五常約稿，希望出版他的書，張五常婉拒了，說他的書都要給花千樹出版，賺一點錢，用來出版舒巷城的舊作。 據說張五常青少年時代，長時間跟在舒巷城身邊，舒巷城多才多藝，張五常深受他的影響。後來張五常學術上出彩，到港大經濟系任教授，他就把舒巷城請到自己身邊，給他一個助理的職位，領港大的薪水。當年舒巷城在中環寫字樓做一般文員，收入當然與港大職員不可比，可見張五常相當念舊，對老朋友舒巷城照顧有加。 張五常請舒巷城在身邊工作，主要是為他的中文文稿把關。舒巷城的文字當然沒話說，因此張五常在信報的文章，文字都是一流水平，清通有味，把一些財經大道理簡化成人人都看得懂的常識。 當然，我們不知道張五常的文章中，有多少成份是舒巷城手筆，不過舒巷城去世後，我再讀張五常的文章，不但仍保留原先那種指點江山揮斥人世的風格，也還保留文字那種隽永雅致的韻味，不知道是張五常本色如此，還是他又請了新的「槍手」。 舒巷城是老一輩香港本土作家，上世紀六七十年代已經成名，他的代表作長篇小說《鯉魚門的霧》，也是不少學院派教授的研究對象。他也寫詩和散文，詩風恬淡口語化，與當時年輕詩人熱衷的現代詩不同，有一次他寫一首詩，嘲弄現代詩的晦澀，字裡行間妙趣橫生。 當年我初來乍到，向新晚報和文滙報投稿，舒巷城也在那幾個左派文學園地發表作品，因此彼此有印象。後來曾敏之成立香港作家聯會，我們又都是會員，因此慢慢熟悉。 舒巷城是少見的有真性情的人，臉上永遠有一種孩童般天真的微笑，他性格隨和，也喜歡聊天，有時談興來了，會即席唱一段粵曲，一邊唱一邊在桌邊打拍子，自得其樂。他與妻子陳月明女士住在鰂魚涌一幢舊樓，我去過他家，家裡清簡無煙火氣，不知為什麼，有一點淒清。 舒巷城去世後，作聯會刊做了一個追思特輯，我也寫了一篇文章回憶與他的交往。後來花千樹出版舒巷城的文集，有一次他妻子約了我們幾個朋友，請我們幫手整理他的舊稿，我們也都應約，盡了一點力。舒巷城去世後，張五常安排他妻子到花千樹任編輯，用意大概是讓她有一份收入，生活不會有問題，足見張五常還是相當有人情味的。 我與張五常本來不會有什麼交集，他是大教授，彼此又在不同圈子，但本世紀初我與古劍和舒非得到藝發局資助，主編一份文學雜誌《文學世紀》，籌劃第一期內容時，我就想找張五常做一個訪問。 張五常不是文學界中人，但他的財經文章與林行止一樣，都很有文學味道，大可當作散文來讀。香港專業界別中，能寫好文章的人不多，張五常是其中之一，如果能採訪他，請他談談讀書心得和文學理念，不失為一個好的選題。 我寫信給他時本不抱太大希望，因為他根本不認識我，也不知道《文學世紀》是什麼雜誌，但他居然一口答應。我自己猜想，可能在作聯紀念舒巷城的特輯上，他有看過我的追懷文章，所以對我有點印象。 那天對他的採訪，印象最深的是從頭到尾，他兩隻腳都筆直架在辦公桌上，上身向後仰起，兩隻手交叉在肚皮上，鞋底對著我。在那一兩個鐘頭內，我就瞪眼看著他那污黑的鞋底，而他居然也沒有改變一下自己的坐姿。 我不知道他的同僚和學生來見他，他會不會都以兩隻鞋底招呼他們，也不知道港大校長和城中權貴來了，會不會也有同等待遇。我與他遠無冤近無仇，他犯不著特意浪費時間，約我去當面羞辱我，所以當時我只覺他是一個被人慣壞的、不懂檢點個人行為的狂狷之士。我曾經上山下鄉，什麼骯髒的東西沒見過？一雙鞋底遮住他的臉，那是他的損失。 訪問內容都忘記了，只記得他說一句話，說自己「有料到」，就可以躺在地上和別人說話，這句話在採訪稿給他過目時他刪掉了，大概覺得太狂妄突兀。在我看來，即使自己真的看別人不起，也大可不必躺到地上和別人說話，那樣豈不是把自己擺在別人腳下？ 與我接觸的林行止先生與張五常相比較，兩人的品行天差地別。林先生溫文爾雅，令人如沐春風，與張五常的目中無人，恰是兩個極端。兩人都是人中龍鳳，天姿聰穎，問學精進，事業成功，但個人品行之差別不可以道里計，這與天性有關，也與家庭教育有關，也與自我修養有關。 張五常才氣縱橫，他在國際財經界赫赫有名，他評論各國財經從來都居高臨下，口沫橫飛。我對財經是外行，但有時不得不承認，他真的有一些別出心裁的創見，看到別人看不到的東西。他的攝影作品風格強烈，後來又跟上海書法家周慧珺學書法，自稱書法成家了，我不懂，只能說他「八足咁多爪」，沾什麼都可以輕鬆上手。 張五常對中國改革開放的「貢獻」，是他很早就公開主張，中共應該適度容忍地方官的貪污，因為金錢好處對地方官的工作有激勵作用。隨著改革開放的深入，貪腐終究成為中共改革開放的副產品，自此尾大不掉，到今日還在作怪，關於這一點，中共不知應感謝他，還是要怪罪他才好。 因為恃才傲物，張五常也不將國家法規放在眼裡，他後來被美國政府通緝，罪名是串謀逃稅和藐視法庭，因為香港與美國有移交逃犯協定，他長期在大陸居住，自此與香港漸行漸遠。 在香港四十年，張五常是我見識過最狂傲的人。他有狂傲的資本，又念舊情，他學有專精，又興趣廣泛，他對社會有貢獻，又犯法被政府通緝。只能說，他是一個我行我素禀性複雜的人，把人性善惡都發揮到極致，他是香港殖民地時代的特產，這種人以後都不會有了。

title: Hong Kong man charged with voyeurism over hiding pinhole cameras in gym
summary: A Hong Kong man has been charged with voyeurism after he was arrested for allegedly installing hidden pinhole cameras in a gym changing room. Shatin Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. Fung Kwok-wang, a 34-year-old worksite foreman,
content: A Hong Kong man has been charged with voyeurism after he was arrested for allegedly installing hidden pinhole cameras in a gym changing room. Shatin Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. Fung Kwok-wang, a 34-year-old worksite foreman, left the Shatin Magistrates’ Courts on Tuesday morning after being granted bail. A pinhole camera found at a 24/7 Fitness Shatin. Photo: @4_matthew_15 via Threads screenshot. He was arrested on Sunday, after videos of a pinhole camera taped to a removable ceiling panel circulated on social media. The camera was discovered by a staff member at a 24/7 Fitness branch in Sha Tin, police said. According to a court document, Fung was charged with one count of voyeurism, alleging that he installed or operated a pinhole camera at the Sha Tin gym between September 24 and 25 to enable himself or any other person to commit a voyeurism offence under the city’s Crimes Ordinance. The gym chain has suspended Fung’s membership and stepped up checks across all branches. Storage devices seized Police said in a Monday press conference that three pinhole cameras were found in the changing rooms at the gym on Lek Yuen Street. Sha Tin District chief inspector Ng Yuk-pui said that the cameras were seized along with three memory cards found in three separate individual changing rooms at the gym. The gym has two female toilets, one male toilet, and four unisex individual changing rooms, each with a shower area and changing space, Ng said. Hard drives and other devices seized from the suspect’s residence, pictured at a police press conference on September 28, 2026. Photo: Hong Kong Police Force. Police identified the suspect after conducting digital forensic analysis of footage stored on the cards. Ng said the police were not able to reveal how many videos were stored on the cards as the case had entered legal proceedings. Officers also seized hard drives and other devices from Fung’s residence. Asked whether the police would take action against sellers of the pinhole cameras, Ng said that the suspect bought the cameras on a well-known mainland Chinese e-commerce platform, which would pose limitations on enforcement. According to local media reports, Fung was believed to have bought the cameras from Taobao.

title: Shein shares dive more than 11% after earnings disappoint
summary: Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results. Shein app. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprin
content: Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results. Shein app. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress. The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just one percent on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved. By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein’s share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9 percent at HK$31.44. Monday’s results were Shein’s first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company’s valuation at around $26.3 billion — well short of the nearly $100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022. Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9 percent to nearly $3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported. Exchange Square in Central, Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The decrease “reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending” in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said. Another key market, the United States, saw revenue drop six percent in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs. Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein’s share price has fallen more than 35 percent. The accelerating decline in Shein’s operating profit “clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands”, said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence. “Management plans to absorb freight and tariff costs rather than raise prices to protect the company’s competitive position,” she said, adding that localising stock in Europe will lead to higher logistics costs in the short term.

content: Bhavin Patel 希望他的妻子 Reshma 还活着。(ABC News: Hamish Harty) 这原本应该是她一生中最难忘的旅程。 Reshma Patel 一直梦想着去喜马拉雅山脉的冈仁波齐神山和玛旁雍措地区进行为期两周的朝圣之旅。 她不想乘坐直升机观光，而是决心徒步完成这次旅行，以免“年纪太大”。 她近 25 年的丈夫 Bhavin Patel 同意留在纽卡斯尔照顾他们的两个学龄儿童。 但在 Patel 女士于 8 月 26 日进行朝圣期间，一场毁灭性的洪水席卷了尼泊尔 – 西藏边境地区。 一个月过去了，超过 1,400 人死亡，超过 5,500 人下落不明，其中包括 Patel 女士和另外 33 名澳大利亚人。 Bhavin Patel（左）认为国际社会还可以做更多来帮助寻找失踪者，包括他的妻子 Reshma（右）。(来源：Bhavin Patel) Patel 先生呼吁采取更多行动，同时拒绝放弃妻子还活着的希望。 “我仍然抱有希望，”他说。 “我永远不会放弃希望她会在某个安全的地方，等待着某人或我自己。” 家庭面临的艰难时刻 Patel 先生说，他一直在从澳大利亚政府那里收到每日更新，但现在已经停止了。 在一份声明中，外交贸易部（DFAT）发言人表示，澳大利亚政府对仍失踪的 34 名澳大利亚人深感担忧。 “我们认识到，这对家庭和亲人来说是一段极度痛苦的时期，”他们表示。 “澳大利亚政府仍然致力于支持他们的福利，并确保他们获得准确和及时的信息。” 灾难发生第二天，Patel 先生前往尼泊尔寻找 Patel 女士和她同行的 Isha Foundation 旅游团。 他认为他们最有可能位于西藏一侧边境的偏远地区。 与其他人一起，他租了一架直升机从上方查看该区域，并观察了他认为在西藏山区有可能生存的地方。 Bhavin Patel 租用的直升机内部拍摄的两个视角，用于寻找他失踪的妻子。(来源：Bhavin Patel) 尽管早期报告称该旅游团可能位于西藏一侧边境的移民局大楼内，但洪水发生时旅游团的确切位置仍然不确定。 Patel 先生希望他的妻子和其他人可能身处一个安全的地方，只是因为灾难规模巨大和地理环境复杂而未被发现。 目前，尼泊尔和中国均未确认任何澳大利亚人死于此次事故。 需要更多援助 上周在纽约联合国大会上，尼泊尔总理 Balendra Shah 呼吁紧急资金以帮助他的国家在危机后重建。 尼泊尔政府的回应也备受关注，因为包括中国、美国和印度在内的国家提供的援助最初被拒绝，后来才被接受。 Patel 先生说，他计划返回西藏，并在能够实地进入该地区时继续搜寻。 “我们坚信她一定在西藏的某个地方，”Patel 先生说。 目前，Bhavin Patel（左）在纽卡斯尔家中照顾这对夫妇的两个学龄儿童。(来源：Bhavin Patel) 他说，国际社会还可以做更多，集体敦促尼泊尔和中国政府接受更多援助，并继续搜寻数千名下落不明的人。 “海外国家想要提供帮助，但那个政府不允许他们这样做，”他说。 “所有国家……都在推动尼泊尔政府和中国政府，也许他们可以做一些事情。”

title: US tariffs on China in 2026: what Chinese goods pay now and what changed
summary: ## What a US buyer pays on Chinese goods today US duties are owed by the importer of record, usually the US buyer, not the Chinese exporter. The liability is a personal debt of the importer to the United States.[[3]](https://airliftusa.com/
content:
## What a US buyer pays on Chinese goods today

US duties are owed by the importer of record, usually the US buyer, not the Chinese exporter. The liability is a personal debt of the importer to the United States.[[3]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cfr-141-1) Section 301 duties follow the country of origin, not the country of export, and every duty is set by the 10-digit HTS line of the goods.[[4]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-301-faq)

As of September 25, 2026, an entry of Chinese-origin goods is built from these layers. Which ones apply depends on the product.

*   **The normal (Column 1 General) duty** for the HTS line, from free upward.[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19)
*   **The Section 301 list duty** if the line is on one of the China lists: 25% on Lists 1 to 3, 7.5% on List 4A, and 25%, 50% or 100% on products raised in the 2024 four-year review.[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19)[[5]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2024-21217)
*   **The 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor duty** on products of China under 9903.05.31, since July 24, 2026, on top of any list duty, unless the goods fall in an exemption.[[1]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-15181)[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19)
*   **Section 232 duties** on covered goods such as steel, aluminum, copper, vehicles and parts, and wood products. Goods under the Section 232 headings listed in 9903.05.90 (metals, vehicles and parts, wood products, patented pharmaceuticals and semiconductors) are exempt from the forced-labor duty but not from the list duties; newer Section 232 programs, such as drones, are not on that list.[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19)
*   **Antidumping and countervailing duties** where a Commerce order covers the product.[[11]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-adcvd)
*   **Fees:** the merchandise processing fee and, for ocean freight, the harbor maintenance fee.[[40]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cfr-24-23)[[39]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cfr-24-24) See [customs clearance](https://airliftusa.com/service/custom-clearance-services) for the current fee limits.

## The US duty stack on goods from China, September 25, 2026

Rates are additional to the Column 1 duty unless the row says otherwise. The rows marked ended are listed because many 2025 and early 2026 landed-cost quotes still include them.

US duties on products of China, as of September 25, 2026| Measure | Rate | Chapter 99 heading | In force |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Column 1 General (MFN) duty | Set by HTS line[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | None (the 10-digit line itself) | In force |
| **Section 301, China Lists 1 and 2 (in force)** | 25%[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | 9903.88.01, 9903.88.02[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | Since July 6 and August 23, 2018[[6]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-08806) |
| **Section 301, China List 3 (in force)** | 25%[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | 9903.88.03, 9903.88.04[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | In force |
| **Section 301, China List 4A (in force)** | 7.5%[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | 9903.88.15[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | In force |
| **Section 301, four-year review products (in force)** | 25%, 50% or 100% by product group[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | 9903.91.01, 9903.91.02, 9903.91.03, 9903.91.05 and others[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | From September 27, 2024 or later dates by group[[5]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2024-21217)[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) |
| **Section 301, forced labor (in force)** | 12.5%[[1]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-15181) | 9903.05.31 (Hong Kong: 9903.05.43)[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | Since July 24, 2026[[1]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-15181) |
| **Section 232 (in force)** | Metals: 50% or 25% of full customs value by product list, lower for some goods; other programs vary[[8]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-procl-11021)[[9]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-procl-11032) | By program[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) | Metals on full value since April 6, 2026[[8]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-procl-11021) |
| Antidumping and countervailing duties | Set by each order[[11]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-adcvd) | None; case number on the entry | Order by order |
| Section 122 surcharge (ended) | 10%[[34]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-csms-67844987) | 9903.03.01[[34]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-csms-67844987) | February 24 to July 24, 2026[[34]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-csms-67844987) |
| IEEPA reciprocal tariff (ended) | 10% from April 5, 84% from April 9, 125% from April 10, then 10% from May 14, 2025[[23]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14257)[[24]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14259)[[25]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14266)[[26]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14298) | 9903.01.63, 9903.01.25[[25]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14266)[[26]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14298) | April 5, 2025 to February 23, 2026[[23]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14257)[[32]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-csms-67834313) |
| IEEPA fentanyl duty (ended) | 10%, then 20% from March 4, 2025, then 10% from November 10, 2025[[20]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14195)[[22]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-dhs-2025-03677)[[28]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14357) | 9903.01.24[[28]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14357) | February 4, 2025 to February 23, 2026[[20]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-eo-14195)[[32]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-csms-67834313) |

## Section 301: the China lists and the forced-labor duty

Section 301 is the main reason Chinese goods pay more than the same goods from elsewhere. There are two separate actions, and a product can pay both.

**The technology-transfer lists.** USTR's first China actions took effect on July 6 and August 23, 2018.[[6]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-08806) The HTS now carries 25% for Lists 1, 2 and 3 and 7.5% for List 4A.[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) The 2024 four-year review raised rates on named product groups, including 100% on electric vehicles (9903.91.03) and 50% on solar cells (9903.91.02), from September 27, 2024, with later steps for other groups.[[5]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2024-21217)[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19) USTR extended 178 product exclusions through 11:59 p.m. eastern daylight time on November 9, 2026.[[7]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2025-21671) It opened the second four-year review on May 6, 2026.[[6]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-08806) Our [Section 301 guide](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/section-301) covers each list, the exclusions and the review in detail.

**The forced-labor duty.** On July 28, 2026, USTR published actions in 60 Section 301 investigations of economies' failure to impose and effectively enforce a ban on imports made with forced labor. It set 12.5% on products of China and 12.5% on products of Hong Kong, for goods entered from 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026. Goods loaded before that time and entered before 12:01 a.m. on July 28, 2026 were exempt.[[1]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-15181) Under U.S. note 52, goods that pay this duty also pay any other additional duty in the same subchapter, which includes the China lists.[[1]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-ustr-2026-15181) The exemptions for China sit in 9903.05.85 to 9903.05.92 and cover goods in transit on July 24, listed HTS provisions and articles, civil aircraft, listed pharmaceutical articles, the Section 232 goods named in 9903.05.90, donations and informational materials. HTS Revision 19 has no China-specific exemption heading.[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19)

## Section 232 on Chinese goods

Section 232 duties apply by product, at the same rate for every origin unless a proclamation sets a partner rate. Since April 6, 2026, the metals duties apply to the full customs value, regardless of metal content: 50% for all aluminum and steel articles, most copper articles and certain derivatives, 25% for the copper articles and derivatives on a second list, and lower rates for some goods.[[8]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-procl-11021) Proclamation 11032 revised those product lists from June 8, 2026.[[9]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-procl-11032)

For Chinese goods the stacking matters. A product under one of the Section 232 headings named in 9903.05.90 (metals, vehicles and parts, wood products, patented pharmaceuticals and semiconductors) is exempt from the 12.5% forced-labor duty, but the China list duties still apply, and CBP's reporting order puts the Section 301 Chapter 99 number first and the Section 232 number after it.[[2]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-hts-rev19)[[10]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-reporting-order) Every 232 program, rate and date is in our [Section 232 guide](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/section-232).

## Antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese goods

When Commerce finds that goods were sold in the US at unfairly low or subsidized prices, it sets antidumping (AD) or countervailing (CVD) duties, and CBP collects them.[[11]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-cbp-adcvd) They come from product-specific orders, with rates set by exporter, and are paid on top of every duty above. Check whether an order covers the product before you place a purchase order.

A few long-standing orders on common Chinese exports, each with its scope, HTS numbers and notices on our AD/CVD pages:

*   Aluminum extrusions, [A-570-967](https://airliftusa.com/tools/ad-cvd/A-570-967) and [C-570-968](https://airliftusa.com/tools/ad-cvd/C-570-968), orders published May 26, 2011.[[12]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-doc-2011-13086)[[13]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-doc-2011-13103)
*   Solar cells and modules, [A-570-979](https://airliftusa.com/tools/ad-cvd/A-570-979) and [C-570-980](https://airliftusa.com/tools/ad-cvd/C-570-980), orders published December 7, 2012.[[14]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-doc-2012-29668)[[15]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-doc-2012-29669)
*   Wooden bedroom furniture, [A-570-890](https://airliftusa.com/tools/ad-cvd/A-570-890), order published January 4, 2005.[[16]](https://airliftusa.com/tariff-updates/china#source-doc-e4-3926)
*   Wooden cabinets and vanities, [A-570-106](https://airliftusa.com/tools/ad-cvd/A-570-106), order published April 21, 2020.[[17]](https://airliftusa.

title: 特朗普总统在为习近平主席举行的白宫国宴上的讲话(全文翻译)
summary: 唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普(Melania Trump)9月24日晚上在白宫设宴款待对美国进行国事访问的中国国家主席习近平和夫人彭丽媛。特朗普总统和习近平主席在国宴上发表了讲话。 **以下是特朗普总统讲话的全文翻译:** 非常荣幸，感谢各位。习主席，彭夫人，中国代表团的各位成员，梅拉尼娅和我很高兴再一次在白宫欢迎各位，你们确实是非常了不起的人。今年早些时候我访问北京时，中国人民的热情好客给我留下了深刻的印象。今晚，在你们十年来首次
content:
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普(Melania Trump)9月24日晚上在白宫设宴款待对美国进行国事访问的中国国家主席习近平和夫人彭丽媛。特朗普总统和习近平主席在国宴上发表了讲话。

**以下是特朗普总统讲话的全文翻译:**

非常荣幸，感谢各位。习主席，彭夫人，中国代表团的各位成员，梅拉尼娅和我很高兴再一次在白宫欢迎各位，你们确实是非常了不起的人。今年早些时候我访问北京时，中国人民的热情好客给我留下了深刻的印象。今晚，在你们十年来首次重返华盛顿之际，我们也希望以同样的礼遇款待各位。

很久以前，欧洲探险家在寻找通往东方的中国的新航路的时候，首次发现了美洲大陆。这场探寻造就了现代世界和这个美丽的国家，并最终催生了美中两国人民之间的长久情谊。这也是我们今天晚上所庆祝的这份情谊。

东西方此后最终在美国相会。158年前，第一个正式的中国外交使团访问了美国，在波士顿，他们会见了艾默生、梭罗等美国思想家。在纽约，他们与市长、州长以及华尔街的巨头共进晚餐。到了华盛顿，他们来到了白宫，出席了美中之间有史以来的第一次国宴。

今天晚上我们在美国的土地上重温那次初次相遇的精神，来自商界、文化界、政界的当代顶尖领袖齐聚于此。一方面，中国承载着五千年的历史与传统，从孙子一直到孙中山，而美国所继承的是源自耶路撒冷和罗马的信仰传统，古雅典的民主，斯巴达的赫赫战功，以及250年前在费城宣告的自由。

作为两国领导人，习主席和我都明白，我们代表不同的制度，但两国人民之间的纽带历久弥坚，我们的关系比起过去要更加地好。自从第一批商船驶离纽约港，到达珠江之滨以来，美中两国人民一直在交易商品，相互传递知识、习俗和思想。这是两国商业往来和相互尊重的基础，我们应携手继续培养这样的关系，为子孙后代带来繁荣与安全。

我现在要脱稿讲几句，必须要脱稿讲几句。

习主席、彭夫人，在我们身后，有一个帘子，帘子后面是通向我们全新的宴会厅。可以说这个宴会厅过去150年来，很多总统都希望能够建成，但是都没有做成功。宴会厅建成以后，将能够容纳1000名以上的宾客。今天很遗憾，我们当前的会议室只能容纳140个人，但建成以后，那个会议厅将能够容纳更多更多的人。所以，一会当我们吃完饭，表演结束以后，我想邀请习主席和彭夫人可以移步到我们的窗帘后面看一下我们已经打扫干净的工地，看一下工地里面是金碧辉煌。

秉承这份友谊的精神，我很荣幸向习主席赠送一份礼物。这一份礼物来自一位杰出的美国艺术家，可以说是当今最好的艺术家之一，也是由我和梅拉尼娅亲自参与设计。白头鹰，也称美洲雕，是美国的国家象征，体现了美国自由翱翔的精神，我们希望它在北京能够被放在一个彰显荣誉的地方。

习主席、彭夫人，梅拉尼娅和我感谢两位在美国建国250周年之际来访美国。现在我提议大家举杯，向习主席和彭夫人致敬，并为美中两国之间这份跨越数千里，绵延数百年的深厚友谊干杯，愿两国人民能有一个更好，更和谐，与和平的未来，让我们向您致敬。

title: Gov’t considers 12 hours’ annual family care leave for civil servants to boost fertility
summary: Hong Kong civil servants could receive up to 12 hours of family care leave annually from next year, the city’s civil service minister has announced, as part of a raft of new measures to boost fertility by promoting family-friendly employmen
content: Hong Kong civil servants could receive up to 12 hours of family care leave annually from next year, the city’s civil service minister has announced, as part of a raft of new measures to boost fertility by promoting family-friendly employment practices and offering financial incentives to reduce the burden of child-rearing. A caretaker walks with a little boy in Hong Kong. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung told a Legislative Council panel meeting on Wednesday that the proposed family care leave allowance is intended to allow civil servants to leave their posts briefly to deal with personal matters, such as a sudden school suspension or a gas leak at home. Responding to a lawmaker’s question on Wednesday about accompanying family members to medical appointments – one of the use cases Yeung had listed a day earlier – she suggested civil servants use their paid annual leave for this purpose instead, as it could take the better part of a day. Secretary for the Civil Service Ingrid Yeung. Photo: GovHK. Yeung said she expects the application process for family care leave to be simple, adding that she believes most civil servants will not abuse the arrangement. Following the announcement, some internet users commented that 10 to 12 hours were insufficient to care for relatives. Others criticised the government for only introducing benefits for civil servants and not private-sector employees. The city’s leader John Lee laid out plans to establish family care leave for all government employees in his 2026 Policy Address last week – part of a series of measures to promote fertility, including the extension of one-off baby bonuses and increased child tax allowances. Lee previously introduced childcare leave for civil servants in his 2024 Policy Address. Starting from early 2025, Hong Kong civil servants who have children under three years old have been eligible for up to three days’ childcare leave per year. Civil servants. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Countries and regions across East Asia are rolling out policies to tackle the problem of slumping birth rates . In August, Singapore announced a proposed bill that offers eight days of annual childcare leave for parents with a child aged six or below. Parents with two children stand to get 10 days’ leave, while parents with three children will enjoy 12 days of annual childcare leave.

content: David Tsai/ 蔡慎坤  X @cskun1989 · Sep 22, 2026 很多人不知道沈栋和他的《红色赌盘》这本书，这本书很大程度上让习近平拿到了对付温家宝和王岐山的更多筹码，沈栋出版这本书的目的是什么？沒有多少人去深思。 《红色赌盘》虽然是沈栋写的，真正的核心人物其实是他的前妻段伟红。整本书讲的，与其说是两个人如何经商致富，不如说是他们如何进入中国高层政商关系网，又如何随着政治环境变化而付出代价。 段伟红出身普通，沈栋把她描述为一个极其聪明、精力旺盛、尤其擅长经营人际关系的商人。沈栋有香港和海外教育背景，熟悉国际商业和金融规则；段伟红更了解中国大陆的政治和商业环境。两人结婚后既是夫妻，也是商业伙伴，逐渐参与北京机场物流、房地产等大型项目，积累了巨额财富。 书中最关键的一条关系，是段伟红与时任国务院总理温家宝的妻子张培莉之间的交往。沈栋称张培莉为“张阿姨”，并描述段伟红如何通过长期交往与她建立亲密关系。按照沈栋的叙述，这种关系并不是简单的送钱办事，而是长期形成的利益、人情和私人感情交织的网络。政治关系能够带来信息、信任和接触权力的机会，而商业上的成功又反过来维护这种关系。 沈栋并没有简单声称温家宝本人直接参与了他们的商业活动。温家宝即使不直接介入商业，一个企业家如果能够进入总理家庭的私人社交圈，本身就可以获得巨大的社会资本。 除了温家宝家庭，书中还出现王岐山、孙政才、令计划等政治人物，以及他们身边的秘书、助手和亲属。沈栋特别强调，真正重要的关系并不只是认识高级官员，还包括认识官员身边能够传递信息、安排见面和建立信任的人。中国政商关系在他的描述中不是简单的一条线，而是一张复杂的人际网络。 孙政才本来是十八大指定的接班人之一，曾经身居高位，2017年被习近平整肃，因受贿罪被判无期徒刑。沈栋认为，段伟红与一些后来失势的政治人物关系密切，这增加了她自身的政治风险。至于段伟红为什么被控制、具体涉及什么问题，很多细节主要来自沈栋本人解释，公开资料并不足以完全验证。 习近平2012年出任总书记以后，大规模反腐败运动改变了中国的政治和商业环境。沈栋认为，在过去，一个企业家与高级官员建立关系是一种重要资产；当政治格局发生变化后，同样的关系突然成为危险的关系。过去认识谁能够决定你获得什么机会，后来认识谁却决定你承担什么风险。 2017年，段伟红在北京失去自由并长期与外界失联。沈栋后来与儿子生活在英国，并写下《红色赌盘》。整本书实际上形成了一个完整的循环：段伟红通过经营关系进入权力核心附近，借助政商网络取得商业成功，又最终因为身处这张网络而陷入危险。 这也是书名“红色赌盘”的含义。沈栋眼中的中国精英商业世界很像一场赌博。企业家不仅是在投资项目，也是在投资关系，甚至是在押注某些政治人物和政治网络。押对的时候，关系可以带来巨大的财富和机会；一旦政治风向改变，原来的资产可能迅速变成风险。 《红色赌盘》最值得关注的不是某一个官员或某一桩秘闻，而是沈栋试图描述的一套运作逻辑。权力之外，还有官员家属、秘书、朋友和企业家组成的关系网络；政治权力通过这些人转化为商业机会，商业利益又反过来维系关系。 这本书是沈栋个人的回忆录。公开发生的政治事件和人物身份可以核实，书中大量私人谈话、幕后交易以及对人物动机的解释，很难得到独立验证。因此更合适把它看成一个曾经身处中国顶层政商圈的人，对自己所经历的财富、权力、关系和风险的一份第一手叙述，而不是中国政商勾结的全貌。

title: The AI Revolution Could Become a National Security Disaster If We Aren’t Careful
summary: The AI Revolution Could Become a National Security Disaster If We Aren’t Careful bbert@hudson.org Tue, 09/22/2026 - 09:57 SVG Commentary Sep 18, 2026 Fox News The AI Revolution Could Become a National Security Disaster If We Aren’t Careful
content: The AI Revolution Could Become a National Security Disaster If We Aren’t Careful bbert@hudson.org Tue, 09/22/2026 - 09:57 SVG Commentary Sep 18, 2026 Fox News The AI Revolution Could Become a National Security Disaster If We Aren’t Careful The US hosts 75 percent of global high-performance compute, but moratoriums risk ceding that advantage to China and other rivals.   Alexandra Seymour Senior Fellow (Nonresident) Alexandra Seymour Commentary Caption An intelligent data center of China Unicom in northwest China on September 11, 2026. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print Reindustrialization is alive in America. Yet the recent backlash on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers reveals we have not learned from our offshoring mistakes: creating dependencies that will not be easily reversed. Whether or not AI data centers are built in America, AI is here to stay. Either we choose to shape the trajectory of AI technology by embracing the AI data center buildout or cede this advantage to other nations that are eager to lead the AI race. China, for example, announced nearly $300 billion in data center investment through 2030, not including private sector spending. India is offering a 20-year tax holiday for foreign cloud operators and the Republic of Korea is offering regulatory relief. Meanwhile, many Americans are calling for moratoriums. The national security consequences of who hosts AI data centers go beyond competition with China. If we do not build AI data centers in the United States, we risk everything that is inside the data centers: the data, compute, and intellectual property (IP) that drive innovation, protect privacy, and enable sovereignty. We will also forfeit our ability to set the security standards for this critical infrastructure. If AI data centers are the engines of AI innovation, data is the fuel. A significant amount of data is required to make AI useful, all of which must pass through AI data centers. Data, therefore, must be handled carefully — especially for privacy reasons — and viewed as a national asset. Adversaries will view data routed through AI data centers as an opportunity to advance their own AI ambitions. Data may be collected for espionage purposes or to accelerate adversaries’ own AI models, as we have seen China do time and again in cyberspace and through adversarial distillation . Adversaries may also conduct adversarial attacks during model training, which could, without our knowledge, degrade and manipulate data that determines the performance of AI models. Either way, insecure or compromised data impacts everyone — from large businesses to individuals — and exposes potentially sensitive information. Then there is compute. America currently hosts 75% of global high performance compute , making it a true strategic advantage. Strong export controls on advanced compute enable us to widen America’s AI lead against adversaries and work with allies and partners to shape the trajectory of AI. Our commitment to increased domestic semiconductor production through implementation of the CHIPS and Science Act is reinforcing our lead with new U.S. capacity. But where do chips go once we have them? Many of them go to AI data centers. Today, China’s semiconductors are a few generations behind the leading-edge due to U.S. export controls on high-end chips and equipment. But if chips are increasingly housed overseas where we cannot enforce security standards, we may increase the ease of remote access instead of closing this loophole, further enabling China to accelerate its own AI development. Relying on overseas AI data centers will also kneecap us in the event of a global crisis because other nations–not the United States–will decide where to surge compute. There is no guarantee that America will receive any of that capacity, but what we do receive will be slow because it will not be on our shores. Compute capacity is already severely constrained and will only become more limited as demand grows for AI tools. This will impact our military, which already faces a potential compute bottleneck , and our innovators powering new breakthroughs, including researchers, students, and startups. Having AI data centers in America ensures we can comfortably prioritize access during a crisis while continuing to foster our innovation economy and technical workforce. Tying together data and compute is AI IP, which includes the AI models and model weights that have enabled America to stay at the frontier. IP is already a well-known target for the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) , and this extends to AI. China has already engaged in IP theft through adversarial distillation to compete with proprietary, American frontier models. Sending AI data centers overseas is like handing IP over to the CCP, which they will continue to use for their own market dominance and, presumably, their military advantage. Luckily, America currently hosts the most AI data centers. However, given about 60% of announced projects for this year have yet to begin construction, this lead cannot be taken for granted. As companies and policymakers seize this moment to reframe the narrative about resource use and benefit to local communities, three immediate actions can build public confidence and ensure America’s security interests. First, America should leverage federal land to start rapid AI data center buildout. In July 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to open up federal land and streamline permitting for commercial AI data centers. By using this authority, America can ensure AI is viewed as a common good instead of a local burden. It also puts the responsibility on the U.S. government, rather than local communities, to work with data center developers to scale AI using modest resources. Second, the Commerce Department should leverage the AI Exports Program to promote secure, global AI data center buildout with allies and partners. Allies and partners need AI capacity as much as the United States, and we should help enable their success. Standards for cyber and physical security of AI data centers are vital to securing and shaping AI use, but are still in development. The AI Exports Program, which aims to share the American tech stack with allies and partners, can be the enforcement mechanism to standardize safe and secure AI data center operations overseas. Through this program, we can mitigate the impact of insider threats and natural disasters; failures of interdependencies, such as water and energy; and compromise of data, compute, and IP. By setting these expectations through an established program, companies can confidently build and other countries will know how to leverage the American tech stack for their own advantage, reinforcing it as the secure alternative to China’s tech stack. Third, we must save room for AI data center improvements. Although we do not want to stall AI data center buildout, which erodes their value, it is worth asking if the pace of this buildout is necessary to stay ahead in AI. Not every data center proposed is expected to be built, but estimates project that we could reach $7 trillion in global AI data center investment by 2030. The domino effect of more compute is greater opportunity to innovate better methods to power AI that may not require a massive data center, or to improve AI models so that they do not need as much power. We must give innovators time to make these breakthroughs, and us the flexibility to adapt. America is poised to lead or lose the AI industrial revolution — a physical representation of its security interests. It must choose to lead by embracing AI data center buildout in the United States. title: 顏純鈎：出入古今跨越華洋，拓荒文學耕耘新聞——緬懷香港文化旗手胡菊人先生

content: 作者臉書  2026-9-17 許行先生喪禮結束後，有幸見到胡菊人先生的夫人劉美美女士，並得到她贈送一本菊人先生的著作《思潮與人物》，內心之欣喜無以言表。本書內容相當豐富，容當拜讀後再為文推薦，但因此事，倒回想起我與菊人先生一點淵源。 我與先生在香港時聯絡很少，可能彼此文化圈子不同，而菊人先生也不是喜歡應酬的人，所以少有機會親炙他的風采，但我對菊人先生，卻早在三十歲來港不久就聞名。 當年初來，知識領域一貧如洗，只能拚命補課，因對文學創作有興趣，四處找書來讀，胡先生的《小說技巧》一書，是我最早接觸的文學理論著作。這是我第一次接觸一本系統性介紹西方現代小說創作技巧的著作，菊人先生將西方現代小說的主要思想和技巧一一詳述，深入淺出，令一個懵懂摸索文學門徑的人受益極深，它也是香港眾多文學愛好者的啟蒙讀物。後來我嘗試寫小說，戰戰兢兢學用一些新技巧，都是從菊人先生這本書中學習得來。 八十年代初我寫了一個短篇小說《山路》，投稿參加當年的第八屆青年文學獎，竟幸運地得到小說高級組冠軍。當年三位評判之一，胡菊人先生之外，還有陳映真和香港老作家黃思騁，可能因為這樣，給菊人先生留下一點印象。 多年後薛興國主政《香港時報》副刊，邀請了一批香港作家共囊盛舉，菊人先生一開始就闢一個專欄，後來我也受邀不定期供稿。有一次大陸詩人顧城在新西蘭殺妻後自殺，我寫一篇短文評論此事，稱他是「極端的理想主義，極端的個人主義，極端的心理畸型」，菊人先生看到，還為文表示贊同，但稱我為「青年作家」。當時我早已步入中年，看到後覺得好笑，大概菊人先生還停留在青年文學獎印象，沒想到我也會變老。 菊人先生在香港時，我們很少交集，只是我也來到溫哥華後，才有機會在加華作協的聚會中見面，有幾次還同席，但因人多，也沒機會深入交談。後來有一次，我到菊人先生府上拜訪，才與他們夫婦多了一些交流。當時談什麼大都已不復記憶，但記得他說過自己的膝蓋有點問題，有一邊已做過手術，置換了一個金屬關節。 胡菊人先生在香港文化界的地位，很多年輕朋友都不太知道，他是香港文化的拓荒者。先生對香港本土文化的貢獻，要先從《中國學生周報》說起，這份雜誌附屬於美資的友聯出版社，其背景是美國中央情報局成立的亞洲基金會。菊人先生由資料室剪報員做起，勤奮進修，後來升任《中國學生周報》社長（首任總編輯為後來聞名國際學界的余英時教授）。 菊人先生主政雜誌期間，以開明、自由與包容的編輯方針，兼容並蓄，鼓勵創作交流，成為當年香港文學藝術的最重要園地。要問這份雜誌對香港文化的貢獻，只要看看它培養出來的一批香港文化人，包括西西、也斯、小思、陸離、蔡炎培、崑南、綠騎士等，後來都是香港文學史上有代表性的作家詩人，他們對後輩的影響，又一代代傳承下去，顯示《中國學生周報》的源遠流長。 沒有胡菊人先生的苦心經營，不會有這份周報，也不會有周報培養起來的一代香港文化重鎮，至於半個世紀以後的香港文化，也不會有後來繁榮昌盛的局面。 菊人先生的貢獻遠不只《中國學生周報》，他後來受金庸邀請，主編《明報月刊》十幾年。如果說《明報》是金庸的新聞理想，那麼《明報月刊》便是金庸的文化追求，前者為俗，後者為雅，前者為對家國大事的即時反應，後者則為對民族文化的執著重建。 菊人先生年代的《明報月刊》，公認是該雜誌歷史上最鼎盛時期，每月一出版，必受到社會和文化界的高度關注，很多話題在社會上發酵，很多觀照與反省，都成為反復討論的重心，對當年香港與大陸的政治經濟和文化，都產生深遠影響。 菊人先生為自己的文化思想，在《明報月刊》孜孜矻矻埋頭經營了十三年，後來因緣際會，經台灣報人傅朝樞遊說，離開《明報》參與創辦《中報》。本來，菊人先生有機會更進一步實現自己的文化理想，可惜傅朝樞始終是一個商人，他很快露出親中的真面目，以致與菊人先生產生衝突，最終兩人分道揚鑣，而中報也因此迅速殞滅。 我看《思潮與人物》書前的作者簡介，關於菊人先生生平，隱去了《中報》這一段，大概這是一次相當不快的經歷，以致菊人先生都「費事」重提，但《中報》生存的短短一年多時間，因胡菊人先生的關係，也廣受讀者歡迎和重視。 離開中報後，菊人先生與大陸老一輩新聞工作者陸鏗合作創辦了半月刊《百姓》，又成為當年香港時事雜誌的標杆。這份雜誌後來發表的陸鏗訪談胡耀邦記錄，成為鄧小平清算胡耀邦的罪證之一，間接導致後來的六四學生運動，大大影響了中國當代歷史進程。這些都與菊人先生的苦心孤詣分不開，他對香港新聞文化的貢獻，對中國當代歷史的影響，都是我們應該認真記取的。 香港本土文化不是平空產生的，是一代又一代香港文化人，辛苦遭逢下堅忍不拔披荊斬棘的結果。今日中共踐踏香港，愚弄香港人，也正是從偷挖香港傳統文化土壤入手。一批貪婪官商和無恥文人，正充當中共打手，把傳統香港文化連根拔起，在這種形勢下，緬懷我們的文化前輩胡菊人先生，更加有現實意義。 胡菊人先生一生堅持「獨立之精神，自由之思想」，出入古今，橫跨華洋，他與他們那一代的文化巨人，開創下來的香港文化局面，應該永遠保存下去，發揚光大，它是香港人安身立命的根基。 胡夫人劉美美女士在贈書中附了一張卡，上書「見書念故人」，令我閱之心酸。很多對我這一輩有影響的前輩文化人都已經不在了，他們開創的香港文化正遭遇前所未有的戕害，世道如此，令人歔欷。但我們仍不可輕言放棄，應記取前人的辛苦擔當，盡我們的能力，保存香港文化的一脈心香。

title: China imposes travel curbs to protect ‘national security’ amid superpower tech race
summary: China imposed sweeping travel restrictions on its citizens on Tuesday, including exit bans on those deemed to endanger the country’s “industrial or technological security”. File photo: Lukas Messmer/HKFP. Citizens who viol
content: China imposed sweeping travel restrictions on its citizens on Tuesday, including exit bans on those deemed to endanger the country’s “industrial or technological security”. File photo: Lukas Messmer/HKFP. Citizens who violate technology import and export regulations could be banned from leaving China, the State Council said. Those who engage in illegal activities abroad could be “prohibited from leaving the country for a period of six months to three years from the date of their return to China”. China and the United States have been locked in a tech race, with both sides accusing the other in recent months of stealing the capabilities of locally developed artificial intelligence models. The new rules, first released in July but in effect from Tuesday, were formulated to “safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests”, the State Council said. ‘Wide remit’ However, analysts warn that the travel rules give China a “wide remit”. A robot is displayed at the Hong Kong Productivity Council’s AI exhibition in Kowloon Tong on May 21, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Security and criminal activities “can be vaguely defined and easily adjusted”, Chong Ja Ian from the National University of Singapore told AFP. “The outside world will only know how it applies that remit after there are cases of implementation,” he said. Chong pointed to reports of exit bans on foreign nationals, including the recent case of US citizen Min Zin. The US government has said the political analyst was taken into Chinese custody in Yunnan province on June 3 and was held improperly. China refuted the accusations in August, saying Min Zin was suspected of violating Chinese law. “The case of Min Zin is a reminder that the range of people (that China) could restrict from exiting could be quite wide — and potentially arbitrary,” Chong said. Dylan Loh, an associate professor at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University, told AFP the travel restrictions “send a message” that China will take action to prevent “leaks in security or national interest-sensitive areas”.

title: 蔡英文下周访美 卸任总统后首次 将赴斯坦福大学演讲
summary: 路透社台北消息，台湾前总统蔡英文周五（10月2日）表示，她将于下周访问美国，在斯坦福大学安全会议上发表演讲，这将是她自2024年卸任以来首次访问美国。 台湾前总统蔡英文在柏林墙倒塌纪念日访柏林 2025年11月10日 © iingwen 作者： 夏榕 广告 蔡英文在脸书上发文称，她将出席斯坦福大学 DEFCON 2026 技术与国家安全会议并致开幕词。 她写道：“我将与学术界、政府和科技界的各位朋友分享台湾的经验，以及我们如何继续应对在平衡科技发展、民主韧性和国家安全方面面临
content: 路透社台北消息，台湾前总统蔡英文周五（10月2日）表示，她将于下周访问美国，在斯坦福大学安全会议上发表演讲，这将是她自2024年卸任以来首次访问美国。 台湾前总统蔡英文在柏林墙倒塌纪念日访柏林 2025年11月10日 © iingwen 作者： 夏榕 广告 蔡英文在脸书上发文称，她将出席斯坦福大学 DEFCON 2026 技术与国家安全会议并致开幕词。 她写道：“我将与学术界、政府和科技界的各位朋友分享台湾的经验，以及我们如何继续应对在平衡科技发展、民主韧性和国家安全方面面临的新挑战。” 中国政府视民主治理的台湾为其领土的一部分，通常反对台湾高级官员（包括前领导人）的任何外国访问。中国外交部尚未对此置评。 路透社注意到，蔡英文卸任后已访问过英国、法国、德国和加拿大等国家。 蔡英文在2016年当选总统后，以及2020年连任后，中国拒绝与她对话，认为她和她的民进党都是“分裂分子”。中国也拒绝与她的继任者、现任总统赖清德对话。 在特朗普总统的第二任期内，赖清德尚未入境过美国。美国与台湾没有正式外交关系，但却是台湾最重要的国际支持者和武器供应国。 台湾政府表示，它有权与世界其他地区接触，并拒绝接受北京的主权声索。 在路透社报道外，蔡英文办公室周五也证实，蔡英文受美国斯坦福大学「戈尔迪结国安创新中心」（Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation）邀请，将在10月7日出席「Stanford DEFCON 2026科技与国家安全研讨会」发表开幕演讲。 蔡英文办公室发言人蔡舒景表示，Stanford DEFCON 是由学界发起并主办的重要论坛，主要目的在搭建跨界对话平台，连结学术界、政府部门、国防军事领域以及科技产业的领袖与新锐人才。 蔡舒景指出，论坛聚焦人工智慧、自主载具、太空技术与商业情报等新兴科技，探讨科技发展如何影响国际安全情势，以及如何进一步将科技创新转化为促进国家安全的助力。 戈尔迪结国安创新中心透过LinkedIn指出，蔡英文是台湾首位女性总统，在她执政的8年期间，面对印太地区日益复杂的安全环境，台湾强化了在关键科技与半导体制造领域的全球地位，深化国际伙伴关系，并投入资源提升国防与国家韧性。 另据台媒报道，除了10月7日的DEFCON研讨会，斯坦福大学胡佛研究所也已向校内人士发出邀请函，邀请参加蔡英文10月8日在胡佛研究所的演说，主题将围绕民主、韧性与全球安全。 10月8日的演说由胡佛研究所「台湾在印太地区」（TIPR）计划与斯坦福大学学生组织Stanford in Government共同主办，前美国国务卿莱斯预计将进行开场引言并介绍演讲者，蔡英文则预计与胡佛研究所资深研究员戴雅门进行对谈。

title: 中国国庆77周年：北京对台立场措辞更加强硬 香港特首盛赞中国制造业

content: 今天是10月1日，是中国建国77周年的国庆日。像往常一样，头天晚上（9月30日），人民大会堂会举办国庆招待会，然后中国国家主席习近平发表长篇致辞讲话。 2026年9月30日，中国国家主席习近平在北京天安门广场参加烈士纪念日仪式，途经人民英雄纪念碑前的花篮。烈士纪念日是国庆节的前一天。（路透社/Florence Lo摄） REUTERS – Florence Lo 广告 今年的这篇致辞有些地方十分引人注目，尤其是在北京对台湾问题的立场上。 习近平称，要深化两岸交流合作，坚决打击“台独”分裂势力，反对外部势力干涉，推动两岸关系和平发展，推进祖国统一大业。这次的措辞比习近平去年的讲话要强硬得多，以往中国方面强调得比较多的是北京“坚决反对”台独活动。 更加值得注意的是，这一立场的转变发生在中美元首峰会刚刚结束之后。习近平在上周的国是访问期间，曾要求美国总统特朗普“审慎”处理台湾问题。他公开呼吁美国“反对”台湾独立，并改变长期以来“不支持”台独的立场。 还有一个很有意思的细节。据美国全国公共广播电台NPR 报导，在习近平访美期间，最后一天的行程是访问美国国家档案馆博物馆，但一位不愿透露姓名的中国外交官透露，由于活动“最后一刻”发生了变化，整个展览都被撤掉了。撤掉的原因是中国对美国计划展示的一份文件——1951 年的《旧金山条约》感到不满。该条约结束了二战期间日本与包括美国在内的盟军之间的敌对状态。《旧金山条约》没有明确规定台湾的主权地位，台湾领导人经常援引该条约来论证台湾应该对其主权拥有自决权。自去年底以来，北京加大了对《旧金山条约》的批评力度，它不承认该条约，并且据美国外交官称，北京私下里要求其他国家将该文件视为非法文件，因为中国政府和台湾政府都没有签署该文件。这一事件表明，台湾问题在中美关系中仍然十分敏感，美国在对待这个问题上也十分谨慎。 特朗普一直避免主动回应台湾问题，并且避免给出确切的回答。他甚至以“美国愿意向中国出售武器”这样的言辞来模糊台湾问题的界限，尤其是对台军售问题 。虽然中国一直强烈反对，并且在每一次的习特会上都会谈及该问题，但美国从未公开作出回应。而有美国官员指出，华盛顿曾在12月批准向台湾出售价值111亿美元的武器。这次的军售协议表明，特朗普政府向台湾出售的武器数量“超过了1979年以来的任何一位总统”。但从这次国庆致辞来看，中国在台湾问题上的立场可以说日益强硬。 除了台湾外，习近平的致辞中还提到了香港。他强调说，要支持香港、澳门更好融入和服务国家发展大局，保持长期繁荣稳定。而国庆日当天，香港特首李家超也积极回应，他盛赞港首个五年规划，还强调这是香港首份五年规划公布后迎来的第一个国庆日，意义非凡。作为五年计划的一部分，当局制定了 22 项指标，这些指标被标记为“预期性”或“约束性”，采用了北京的评估框架。而面对外界的质疑，李家超上个月公布该计划后，否认这项为期五年、与北京做法一致的政策蓝图标志着香港现有制度的转变。他表示，该方案将坚持香港的“资本主义制度”。在官方媒体新华社发布的报道中，这位特首还特别强调了中国已成为世界制造业第一大国，并称在国际事务中发挥着关键的影响力。 那么中国民众对这次的国庆日作何反应呢？对于假期较少的中国民众来说，大家对这次的国庆日可以说翘首以盼。因为民众将享有为期一周的公共假期。今年由于中秋节和国庆节之间只有三个工作日，所以请假的人可以将这两个假期合并，变成一个13天长假。 官方媒体称，10月1日当天，全国铁路预计发送旅客近2500万人次，客流保持高位运行。而据中国民用航空局预测，9月25日至10月7日期间，中国航空公司预计将运送旅客3119万人次，比去年同期增长3.6%。每年的国庆长假期间，社交网站上有不少视频显示多数国内景点都是人山人海的景象，因此出国旅游成了部分民众的选择。9月15日，中国刚刚开始执行出入境新规，不少民众担心出境受限。但中国民航局表示，截至9月24日，该期间国际航班预订量同比增长22.5%。 总的来说，在当前中国内需疲弱的背景下，节假日助推消费对国内经济来说尤为重要，对大部分普通民众来说这也是一次难得的休假机会。

title: 王丹：既没有“人民”，也没有“共和”
summary: 王丹 X @wangdan1989 十月一日，是中华人民共和国成立七十七周年，中共在北京大张旗鼓地庆祝，历数自己的所谓“丰功伟绩”。表面上，也有很多中国人，在爱国主义的旗帜下，表现出欢乐喜庆的样子。 首先我要说，中国这个概念，对我来说，绝对不是可以用“中华人民共和国”来完全代表和涵盖的。在我看来，中华人民共和国，是中国共产党用武装斗争打败政治对手，而自行建立的一个新政权的国号。作为一个国号，它跟我心目中的“中国”，其实并不是一回事。因此，坦率讲，一个国号被确认七十七周年，对我
content: 王丹   X @wangdan1989 十月一日，是中华人民共和国成立七十七周年，中共在北京大张旗鼓地庆祝，历数自己的所谓“丰功伟绩”。表面上，也有很多中国人，在爱国主义的旗帜下，表现出欢乐喜庆的样子。 首先我要说，中国这个概念，对我来说，绝对不是可以用“中华人民共和国”来完全代表和涵盖的。在我看来，中华人民共和国，是中国共产党用武装斗争打败政治对手，而自行建立的一个新政权的国号。作为一个国号，它跟我心目中的“中国”，其实并不是一回事。因此，坦率讲，一个国号被确认七十七周年，对我来说，或许是具有历史意义的一件事，但是真的没有什么可以庆祝的。我理解和尊重那些参与建立了这个国号的人和他们的后代的欢欣的心情，但在我看来， 这是他们的欢欣，与我无关。 其次，就这个国号所代表的政权，这七十年在中国执政所导致的功过而言，我认为十月一日的意义，在于我们可以用这个机会，回顾与反思一下这个政权带给中国人民的，到底是什么？在当局自己吹嘘的“丰功伟绩”的背后，还有哪些，是我们在这样的一个特殊的日子里，不应当忘记的？我认为这一点，比庆祝更为重要。 在我看来，在中共建政七十七周年的今天，我们必须了解一件事，那就是不管中共如何自我吹嘘，他们都不能掩盖一个可怕的事实：中国的五星红旗上面，其实沾满了人民的鲜血；从50年代的土改到镇压，从反右运动到“文革”，从举世震惊的“六四“屠杀到最近十几年对于维权运动的打压，中共的统治的基础之一，就是曾经导致无数人失去生命的赤裸裸的暴力。而对这一点，中共当然讳莫如深，但这是真实的历史，在他们建国77周年的今天，这样的历史，我们不应当忘记。 我们也必须看到，这个政权的产生，如同中国历史上无数的封建王朝一样，并没有经过中国人民一人一票的选举。换句话说，这个政权的合法性，其实是他们自己自封的，没有经由正规程序得到中国人的同意。他们号称得到全国拥护，但是其实半点证据都没有。要知道，没有反抗，并不代表拥护，人民可能只是服从而已。77年了，这个政权宣称自己得到人民的拥护，但他们完全不敢进行真正的选举，这正说明他们知道，一旦选举，人民不会选择他们。这也说明，77年的时间过去了，他们仍然没有建立起真正的自信。 我们还应当知道，最近几十年，中国的经济确实有所增长，人民生活水平确实有所提高，这就是中共吹嘘的那些所谓“丰功伟绩”的唯一内容。但是，这些生活的改善，在很大的程度上，其实是中国人民通过自己的创造力和勤奋产生的，把它完全归结为中共的领导，是对人民的努力的抹杀。相反，通过制度化了的，成体系的大规模腐败，中共的官员们从人民的努力成果中，不知道抢走了多少钱财，这笔帐，在七十七周年的今天，如果一定要讨论经济发展的成就这个问题的话，就必须也拿出来算一算。 中华人民共和国，这个称号听起来很美好，但是七十七年来，人民哪一天当家作主过？所谓的“共和”，又体现在哪里？既没有“人民”，也没有“共和”，这样的一个政权的建立，有什么可庆祝的呢？

title: 吴祚来：斯诺影响了罗斯福对华认知

content: 吴祚来 X @wuzuolai   · 斯诺影响了罗斯福对华认知 1943年11月24日早晨，罗斯福的儿子艾略特(Elliot)发 现父亲在床上用餐，问起昨晚的情形。罗答说:“发生好多事喔。我见到委员长了。”艾略特问他对这位中国领导人的印象如何，罗先耸耸肩，然后说:“昨晚和蒋氏夫妇交谈所学，胜过我和联合参谋长团开四 个小时的会。”固然蒋花了相当长时间叙述中国军队的困难处境，罗 斯福对儿子说，他还是对某些问题不解，如:“为什么蒋的部队不打 仗?” 为什么蒋“试图阻止史迪威训练中国部队”? 为什么他 “将数以千 计的精兵留守在共产中国的边界”? 罗斯福两大疑问，成为中美之间最大的隔阂，随之形成的缝隙，成为中共统战的空间，中共的重要大外宣人员斯诺却与罗斯福有三次面谈。 1945年3月中旬，罗斯福与斯诺有过一次长谈。斯诺在《复始之旅》一书中记述，罗斯福对国共谈判没有进展感到失望。他对斯诺说，蒋介石对共产党要求的某些类似人权法案的保证“提出了一些十分荒谬的反对意见”，而在他看来，共产党的要求是“完全合理的”。他认识到中共作为游击区的实际政府正在日益增长的力量，正在考虑直接帮助中共抗击日本，打算在美军更加接近日本本土时，将物资和联络官员运送到华北沿海地区。斯诺问他，“我设想，我们的立场是，只要我们承认蒋政府是唯一政府，我们就必须只通过他来向中国供应所有的物资，对吗？我们不能在中国支持两个政府，是吧？” 罗斯福回答：“我一直在那里同两个政府打交道，我打算继续这样做，直到我们能使他们双方联合起来。” 这段谈话往往被用来证实罗斯福有意援助中共，然而谈话给斯诺留下的印象，是罗斯福“显然无意抛弃蒋介石政权”，“可能想把中共当作对蒋介石施加压力的一种手段，以促使他走向革新他的政府，成为统一和进步的中国的核心”。 从上面一则关于左翼红色作家斯诺与罗斯福的长谈，我们不难发现背后的问题： 其一：斯诺是宋庆龄、周恩来安排、由鲁迅等左翼作家引导的中共大外宣作家，他的书能够影响美国主流社会，特别是能够进入白宫，进而斯诺本人能够与总统交流关于中国的『实况』，中共的大外宣的成功达到了极致，因为它已实质性的影响到美国核心决策机构与人物； 其二，斯诺看到了罗斯福对国民政府的支持，也看到了总统利用共产党来平衡国民政府，以促使其更新。美国的理想主义者在这里犯了另一个错误，就是用美国思维与现实，来要求战时的国民政府。当时的国民党政府所属的军队许多是旧军阀力量整合而成，政府腐败与军队没有战斗力不是战时政府能够及时解决的问题。而美国的亲共力量因此贬损甚至歧视国民政府，支持共产党的声音也因此高涨，而共产党是一支在野力量，对国家不负责，暴力掠夺社会财富以充军费，由于斯诺等人的美化宣传，屏蔽了中共力量的邪恶，而放大了它的民主与正义属性。 其三：罗斯福『看到了』共产党的力量在壮大，共产党为什么在后方做大？总统听信了斯诺等大外宣的见证，也看到了亲共外交人员与军方人员的报告，但总统犯了常识错误，只要看一眼国共双方在抗日战争中牺牲的将士，就知道国民政府的力量在抗日过程中消耗，而中共军队利用抗日战争在扩张地盘。将中共当成平衡国民政府的力量，甚至当成可以联合的力量，是左翼力量与亲共力量误导白宫的结果。 『两个政府论』，即将国民政府与共产党政权平等对待，是变相承认了中共的合法性，如同现在承认塔里班是合法的政权一样，它利于非法的中共是无疑的，而要求国民政府与红色恐怖组织进行和谈，建立联合政府，这是将水与火放在一起实现共和的美式幻想。美国的『好心美意』第二次祸害了中国宪政民主进程，第一次是一战后美国主导的西方中立，对北洋政府进行武器禁运十年，导致北洋政权溃败，而这一次，在国共战争中武器禁运了一年，国民政府遭受重创，从此形势逆转。 美国的延安考察组目的是联共，被赫尔利挫败，但亲共势力却强势存在着，战时通过容共来获得中共对抗日战争的支持，战后则是期冀中共成为正常的政党，脱离苏联控制，融入国民政府，成为独立国内政治力量，美国的战时设计可以理解 ，美国的战后在苏联强化对中共的战略与战争支持之时，仍然固守这一国家计划，无异于让水火共容为一体，结果是以国民政府与美国的失败而告终。美国的目标非常明确，那么苏联的目标呢？ 吴祚来：亲左亲共使美国失去中国（2）

content: Eric Chau   臉書  2026-9-21 時事評論員、中國事務專家劉銳紹（人稱「夫子」），其一生故事是一部跨越半世紀的華人新聞風雲史。 他從昔日的親中左派報人，轉變為堅守客觀理性的獨立評論家。在近年香港政治環境劇變、傳統電台節目全面停播的考驗下，目前他轉戰網路網台及專欄寫作，繼續以「與時俱退、笑看人寰」的儒雅幽默發聲。 夫子的故事：從左派記者到「六四」唯一被點名的香港記者 劉銳紹出生於 1954 年的香港灣仔，早年就讀聖璐琦書院 年輕時抱有強烈的愛國情懷，隨後加入當時的親共左派報章《文匯報》，曾長駐英國及北京。 他一生的命運轉折點發生在 1989 年北京「六四事件」。時任《文匯報》駐北京辦事處主任的劉銳紹親歷現場，並在天安門廣場運動期間參與了該報著名的「痛心疾首」社論運動。六四鎮壓後，他在北京的報導被指控洩露官方機密，成為中共官方「平亂報告」中唯一被指名道姓譴責的香港記者。 因為這份對新聞真相的堅持，他隨後與多名高層一同離開了《文匯報》。從此，他脫離了黨報體制，成為一名獨立的時事評論員。此後數十年，他頻繁在香港電台、商業電台等各大主流媒體發表對中國政治、兩岸關係及香港形勢的精闢見解。 近況：告別傳統電台，轉戰網台與文字世界 近年來，隨著香港媒體環境與評論空間的大幅收窄，劉銳紹的發聲渠道經歷了重大調整： 被迫「封咪」與「與時俱退」： 劉銳紹曾長年主持香港電台節目，2021 年遭到停播。而他在商業電台主持的最後一個時事節目《政好星期天》，也在2024 年最後一天正式劃下句號。對此，他在劉銳紹 Facebook上幽默地自嘲：「我的所有電台節目全部正式被『與時俱退』。此後聽我胡言亂語，看我荒誕狂文，請覓他途！」 開闢網路節目續講歷史： 雖然傳統大氣電波「封咪」，但劉銳紹並未停下腳步。他轉戰網路，在 D100 網台開設了《劉銳紹採訪風雲錄 穿越新聞烽火50年》及《萬獸寓言看人生》等音視頻節目，用寓言和五十多年的親身採訪見聞，繼續引領大眾解讀政局。 筆耕不輟，藉古諷今： 他依然活躍於文字專欄，在《明報》專欄「夫子自唱」等渠道持續寫作。在近年發表的文章中，他經常借由歷史事件（例如陳獨秀案）來對比與反思當下的社會現實，展現出他特有的理性與文人情懷。 劉銳紹在動盪的時代中，始終保持不亢不卑的態度。正如他所言：「時代規律，既要適應，也可創造」，卸下傳統電台主持光環的夫子，依然在香港用最堅韌、溫和的方式，實踐著一位新聞人的終身志業。

title: Sai Kung’s Po Pin Chau trail fully booked ahead of upcoming holidays, as Hong Kong expects 1.3m mainland visitors
summary: Sai Kung’s popular Po Pin Chau trail has been fully booked for part of the upcoming National Day holiday, when Hong Kong expects to see some 1.3 million arrivals from mainland China over the weeklong vacation. Po Pin Chau. Photo: AFCD. The
content: Sai Kung’s popular Po Pin Chau trail has been fully booked for part of the upcoming National Day holiday, when Hong Kong expects to see some 1.3 million arrivals from mainland China over the weeklong vacation. Po Pin Chau. Photo: AFCD. The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) said in a Facebook post on Thursday that no available time slots are left for the High Island Geo Trail – Po Pin Chau Section on Friday and Saturday next week. Bookings are also full for this Friday and Saturday during Mid-Autumn Festival, the country park managers added, although a small number of openings remain on other days of the mainland’s Golden Week break to celebrate the founding of the People’s Republic. The AFCD introduced a trial booking system last month for the site, which has seen a surge in visitors as views of the sea stack’s volcanic rock columns went viral on Chinese social media platforms like Xiaohongshu, turning the remote path into a magnet for tourists “checking-in” online. East Dam, High Island Reservoir. Photo: Wikicommons. Visitors are required to book in advance for all weekends and public holidays beginning in September and ending on October 7—measures intended to stem ecological damage from overtourism and prevent accidents like the one that took the life of a mainland visitor on New Year’s Eve last year. The AFCD recommends that hikers who fail to secure a spot on the Po Pin Chau trail go to the nearby Biu Tsim Kok viewing point instead, which offers similar views but does not require advance booking. Hong Kong’s Immigration Department projects that around 1.29 million mainland Chinese will visit the city over the National Day holiday, which begins October 1. That equates to about 184,286 visitors daily—five per cent more than last year. Lantern Spectacular extended Responding to “overwhelming public interest,” the Hong Kong Tourism Board has announced that its International Lantern Spectacular in Victoria Park will be extended through part of the National Day holiday. International Lantern Spectacular at Victoria Park. Photo: HKGov. The event, which brings giant lanterns from 20 countries to Causeway Bay for the Mid-Autumn Festival, will now run nightly until October 4. Installations will be lit daily from 6.30pm to 11pm, with extended lighting hours until midnight on Mid-Autumn Day on Friday.

content: ✊ Solidarity Against Dictatorship! – Joint Protest Marking 77 Years of CCP Rule For the past 77 years, the Chinese Communist Party has expanded its totalitarian regime and relentlessly suppressed human rights. From Tibet, East Turkestan, Southern Mongolia, Manchuria, Hong Kong, and Cantonia, to dissidents and religious groups within China, countless people have faced persecution and exile. Even abroad, many continue to face transnational repression and intimidation by the CCP. But we will not be silenced! This October 3rd, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Southern Mongolians, Manchus, Cantonese, along with Anti-CCP activists and persecuted Christians, will stand shoulder to shoulder once again at Dam Square, Amsterdam. A mobile podium will be set up at the square, where representatives from each community will take the stage to speak out. This rally is a powerful demonstration of our solidarity, diversity, and unyielding will to resist. We call on all friends who love freedom and oppose dictatorship to join us! 📅 Event Details: Date: Saturday, 3 October 2026 Time: 13:00 - 15:00 Location: Dam Square, Amsterdam Co-organized by: Tibet Support Group NL Stichting Support Uyghurs Voice of Anti-CCP NL Joined by: Tibetans, Uyghurs, Southern Mongolians, Manchus, Cantonese, Anti-CCP Dissidents & Christians. 📣 What to Bring: You are more than welcome to bring flags, banners, or signs representing your community. Let us send the strongest message to the world: Dictatorship will fall, freedom will prevail! ⚠️  Important Travel Update for Oct 3 Due to railway maintenance, there will be NO trains to, from, or via Amsterdam Centraal on Saturday, October 3. Please alight at Amsterdam Sloterdijk station and transfer to a tram to reach Dam Square. Please plan your trip in advance and allow an extra 40 minutes for your journey. We recommend checking the NS App for real-time travel advice before departure.

content: 中美对标    X @new_voa  ·   4h 妖妖醬：沈栋突然爆料：车祸前他见了令谷一面 沈栋昨晚突然开口了。 就在十几个小时前，《红色赌盘》作者沈栋发表长文，第一次公开讲述他认识的令计划独子令谷。 最抓人的，是两人最后一次见面。 令谷出事前一个多星期，两人在北京新荣记吃饭。饭后，令谷告诉沈栋，朋友刚刚给他“安排”了一辆新款法拉利，就停在楼下，想请沈栋过去看看。 沈栋当天有事，没有去，只和令谷约好，改天把望京附近的赛道包下来，两人一起试车。 没想到，那成了他们最后一次见面。 沈栋推测，那辆朋友安排的新车，很可能就是后来在保福寺桥撞毁的法拉利。 但这篇文章真正的新料，不只是车。 过去，人们记住的令谷，是一个开着法拉利、带着两名年轻女子深夜狂奔的权贵公子。沈栋笔下的令谷，却已经在认真经营自己的政治未来。 二十多岁的令谷想把官二代、红二代组织成一个紧密团契。他研究美国的骷髅会和大学兄弟会，筹办读书会，寻找活动场地，把自己的“小兄弟”带给沈栋和段伟红过目。 他甚至已经能够替这些年轻人规划仕途、疏通关系。有人不到三十岁，就被推上了正处级。 这很容易让人想到林立果。 令谷当然还没有林立果的“联合舰队”，也没有证据表明他参与任何政变。相似之处在于：两个最高权力身边的年轻人，都没有等待父辈交班，而是提前经营属于自己的年轻班底。 令谷还明白，政治不能没有钱。 他和富二代筹办基金；有人替他安排柏悦酒店公寓；有人给他送来法拉利。权贵圈里的昂贵资源，不一定需要登记在权贵子弟名下。今天投入的是跑车、公寓和现金，等待兑换的却是令家未来的权力。 车祸发生以后，故事从令谷转向了令计划。 按照沈栋听到的说法，令计划曾亲自查看现场，怀疑车辆被人动过手脚，儿子也可能在夜店被人下药。他还试图向胡锦涛隐瞒儿子的死亡。江泽民得知以后，当面质问胡锦涛，把这场私人悲剧变成了十八大人事谈判中的政治武器。 这部分属于沈栋的圈内听闻，不是已经证实的车祸调查结论。但它与2012年《纽约时报》报道的基本框架一致：令计划被指动用中央警卫资源掩盖车祸，江泽民一方借机发难，令计划失去晋升机会，胡锦涛的换届布局遭到重创。 三天之内，薄熙来和令谷先后出事。 薄熙来倒台，习近平少了一个拥有独立政治资本的红二代对手；令计划出局，胡锦涛失去了联络和维系旧部的关键人物。 一个削弱同辈竞争，一个削弱前任制约。 令谷原本想用读书会搭建自己的政治未来，最后却是一辆法拉利，为另一个人打开了通往个人集权的大门。 本期节目先完整朗读沈栋原文，再对照2012年以来的报道，区分哪些是亲历、哪些是听闻、哪些是沈栋十四年后的政治判断。 节目链接 ： https:// youtu.be/A829v0gfVJc

# 美国提出延长对伊朗核计划监督期限，中俄投票否决

ZANE IRWIN 2026年9月18日

中国常驻联合国代表傅聪今年早些时候在安理会会议上发言。Eduardo Munoz/Reuters

俄罗斯和中国周四在联合国安理会否决了美国提出的伊朗制裁委员会专家小组授权延期决议草案。此举加深了美国与其地缘政治对手中俄之间因特朗普政府试图孤立伊朗伊斯兰共和国而产生的紧张关系。

在纽约举行的安理会会议上，这些国家的驻联合国代表发表了针锋相对的言论，而就在不到一周后，中国国家主席习近平和美国总统特朗普将在华盛顿举行一场备受期待的会晤。

中国常驻联合国代表傅聪敦促安理会“避免双重标准、政治操弄、施压对抗”。

俄罗斯常驻联合国代表瓦西里·涅边贾谴责了他所称的“我们西方同事的破坏性道路，这完全由他们在向伊朗伊斯兰共和国施压时所追求的经济利益所决定”。

广告

伊朗官员没有立即就这次表决或否决作出回应。

这场冲突围绕美国提出的一项决议展开。该决议旨在延长一个专家小组的工作期限。这个小组负责监督伊朗的核计划及其规避国际制裁的行为。另一个联合国核监督机构——国际原子能机构——本月报告称，伊朗方面已[拒绝](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260918/un-iran-resolution-russia-china-veto/)该机构进入其核设施。

英国和法国以及八个非常任理事国投票支持美国提出的决议，两个国家弃权。但中俄这两个拥有否决权的常任理事国投票否决了这项措施，称相关制裁已经到期，因此这一问题不应再成为讨论议题。两国代表还敦促通过外交途径结束美国与伊朗之间的战争，并表示支持德黑兰发展民用核计划的权利。

美国常驻联合国副代表詹妮弗·洛切塔称俄罗斯和中国的否决是“阻挠行为”，并表示其目的是压制“揭露它们自己支持流氓政权活动”的报告。

她还说，否决将造成“监督真空，只会让伊朗政权以及那些从规避这些措施中获利的人受益”。

美国官员5月表示，[俄罗斯正通过里海向伊朗运送无人机部件](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/09/world/middleeast/caspian-sea-iran-russia.html)，帮助德黑兰在与美国的战争中重建进攻能力。此前，美国官员还表示，[俄罗斯在战争中向伊朗提供情报](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/09/world/middleeast/caspian-sea-iran-russia.html)，包括显示军舰和军事人员位置的卫星图像。

广告

这场战争始于2月底美国和以色列对伊朗发动的袭击，它还为中美之间的竞争[开辟了新战线](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260506/trump-china-iran-war/)。中国购买伊朗石油帮助维持了伊朗经济的运转。

8月，特朗普宣布针对伊朗发起新的、力度更大的制裁行动后，[中国作出强烈反应](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260826/us-bessent-china-iran/)，下令中国企业[不得遵守](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260506/us-china-iranian-oil-sanctions/)这些制裁措施。

傅聪周四表示，美国决定退出2015年与伊朗达成的核协议并于今年对伊朗发动战争是“当前危机的根源”。

周四，让美国处境更加复杂的是，一个联合国实况调查团[发布报告](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2026/09/iran-civilians-trapped-between-extreme-state-repression-and-violations?sub-site=HRC)称，它“有合理理由认为，美国发动无差别攻击，造成平民伤亡或民用物体受损，因而犯下战争罪”。报告列举了两起美国发动的袭击，其中包括2月对伊朗一所学校的导弹袭击，造成150多人死亡，其中大多数是儿童。

美国官员3月承认，五角大楼的一项初步调查认定，[美国应对这些袭击负责](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20260312/iran-school-missile-strike/)。特朗普政府否认美军以平民为攻击目标，但尚未公布调查结果。

联合国的最新一轮交锋发生在中伊两国外长在北京举行高级别会晤的第二天，而与此同时，特朗普似乎在伊朗问题上可用的[选项已经越来越少](https://cn.nytimes.com/china/20260917/iran-war-china-trump-summit/)。

title: 所谓“中国式强大”，只会让我们这些海外华人更丢脸、更直不起腰
